Plasma-facing limiter. NAMES.name: angle_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Second inclination angle (β) of the oblique trapezoidal cross-section of an ICRH antenna strap, giving the signed tilt of the beta-side lateral face relative to the directed strap base edge.
NAMES.long:
The oblique trapezoidal cross-section of an ICRH antenna strap is geometrically characterized by two lateral-face inclination angles, alpha (α) and beta (β). The beta angle is the signed inclination of the beta-side lateral face relative to the directed base edge of the trapezoid, complementing [alpha_angle_of_antenna_strap](name:alpha_angle_of_antenna_strap), which describes the inclination of the opposite lateral face.

Together with shape parameters such as length_of_antenna_strap and [height_of_antenna_strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), the pair of inclination angles (α, β) fully specifies the oblique trapezoidal cross-sectional geometry used to model the conducting strap element in RF antenna simulations. This angle is a fixed mechanical design parameter derived from engineering drawings and does not vary with plasma conditions.

The analogous second-inclination angle for passive structures is [angle_of_passive_loop](name:tilt_angle_of_passive_loop), which encodes the β angle of the passive loop cross-section in the same geometric convention.

NAMES.name: alpha_angle_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Signed inclination of the alpha-side lateral face of an oblique trapezoidal ICRH antenna-strap cross-section relative to the directed strap base edge.
NAMES.long:
The alpha angle is the oriented inclination of the alpha-side lateral face of an oblique trapezoidal ICRH antenna-strap cross-section, measured from the directed strap base edge. It specifies the alpha-side geometry complementary to the beta-side quantity represented by [angle of antenna strap](name:angle_of_antenna_strap).

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left(\hat{n}\cdot(\hat{b}\times\hat{a}),\,\hat{b}\cdot\hat{a}\right)
$$

where $\hat{b}$ is the unit vector along the directed strap base edge, $\hat{a}$ is the unit vector along the alpha-side lateral face, and $\hat{n}$ is the positive normal to the oriented cross-sectional plane. The angle is restricted to the alpha-side face and is distinct from the beta-side inclination.
NAMES.sign: Positive when rotation from the directed strap base edge toward the alpha-side lateral face follows the positive normal of the oriented strap cross-section.

NAMES.name: angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: Signed rotation angle of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror about its mechanical steering axis, measured from the launcher reference orientation and controlling the EC microwave beam injection direction.
NAMES.long:
The mirror angle quantifies the angular position of the steering mirror on an electron-cyclotron launcher, which redirects the millimeter-wave beam along the desired injection path into the plasma. By adjusting this angle, the beam can be directed at different magnetic flux surfaces, enabling localized electron heating or non-inductive current drive at a chosen plasma radius.

The accessible angular range is bounded by the mechanical travel limits of the actuator system: the lower bound is given by minimum_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror and the upper bound by [maximum_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:maximum_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), together defining the full range of injection directions available for the microwave beam. The resulting beam orientation after the mirror reflection is further characterized by angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam, which describes the beam direction in the plane transverse to propagation.

Mirror positioning is achieved through motorized actuators with angular position encoders; real-time feedback enables precise beam aiming during plasma operation. The spatial location of the mirror center is complemented by [radial_centroid_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:radial_centroid_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and [vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), which together define the mirror center position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: area_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Area of a neutral beam injector is the source cross-section of the active ion-source emission face that forms the extracted beam before neutralization. For a multi-aperture source, it is the sum of the contributing aperture areas.
NAMES.long:
Area of a neutral beam injector is the source cross-section of the active ion-source emission face that forms the extracted beam before neutralization. It represents the open or emitting part of the ion-extraction face through which extracted ions enter the beamline; for a multi-aperture source it aggregates only apertures that contribute to the extracted beam.

The area is defined as the projected geometric area of the active emitting or open aperture set onto the plane normal to the nominal extracted-beam direction:

$$
A_\mathrm{NBI} = \int_{S_\mathrm{open}} \left|\hat{\mathbf{b}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{r})\right| \, dS
$$

where $S_\mathrm{open}$ is the active open or emitting aperture surface on the ion-source extraction face, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the nominal extracted-beam direction, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local unit normal of that aperture surface, and $dS$ is the surface-area element.

This quantity is the geometric source area used to normalize extracted beam current density to total extracted current, as in $I_\mathrm{ext}=\langle j_\mathrm{ext}\rangle A_\mathrm{NBI}$ for area-averaged extracted current density $\langle j_\mathrm{ext}\rangle$ and extracted current $I_\mathrm{ext}$. It is not a downstream neutral-beam cross-section, propagated beam footprint, or an area of a neutralizer, duct, collimator, or target. The related [beam area of neutral beam injector](name:beam_area_of_neutral_beam_injector) denotes the same active beam-forming source cross-section from the beam side of the source, while aperture dimensions such as [neutral-beam aperture width](name:neutral_beam_width_of_aperture) specify component geometry rather than the aggregate active area.

NAMES.name: beam_area_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Geometric area of the ion-source emission surface from which a neutral beam injector extracts ions before downstream neutralization.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the geometric area of the ion-source emission surface that contributes to formation of the extracted neutral beam. It refers specifically to the source surface, not to downstream neutralization, transport, or beam-interception surfaces.

The area is defined by the surface integral

$$
A_{\mathrm{source}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{open}}} dS
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{source}}$ is the source-surface area and $dS$ is an infinitesimal surface element on the open emitting region $S_{\mathrm{open}}$.

For a multi-aperture source, the area is the sum of the open emitting aperture areas. It is the source-surface component of the geometric quantity [area of a neutral beam injector](name:area_of_neutral_beam_injector), whose definition uses the same pre-neutralization emission surface.

NAMES.name: capacitance
NAMES.short: Charge-storage coefficient relating incremental electrical charge to the voltage across an electrical component.
NAMES.long:
Electrical capacitance quantifies the charge stored by an electrical component per unit change in the voltage across its terminals.

$$
C = \frac{\mathrm{d}Q}{\mathrm{d}V}
$$

where $C$ is capacitance, $Q$ is the charge associated with the component, and $V$ is the terminal voltage difference. For a linear component, this relation reduces to $Q = CV$.

For a passive lumped element, capacitance is non-negative and represents electric-field energy storage. It is distinct from resistance, which describes dissipative loading; the antenna-specific instance is [capacitance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:capacitance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna).

NAMES.name: current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short: Electric current density attributable to non-inductive drive by plasma waves through wave–particle interactions, distinct from inductive and non-wave current contributions.
NAMES.long:
Wave-driven current density is the electric current-density contribution produced by wave–particle interactions that preferentially drive charged-particle motion. It is non-inductive and is distinct from the total [current density](name:current_density) and from non-inductive contributions not driven by waves.

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wave}} = \sum_s q_s\,\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,\mathrm{wave}}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the wave-driven current density, $q_s$ is the charge of particle species $s$, and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,\mathrm{wave}}$ is that species’ wave-driven particle flux. A resolved instance such as [per-toroidal-mode wave-driven current density](name:per_toroidal_mode_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive) attributes this contribution to an individual toroidal Fourier mode; the parent quantity does not impose that mode resolution.

NAMES.name: current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive
NAMES.short: Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by electron-cyclotron wave absorption and resonant wave–particle interactions, summed over all wave sources.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net toroidal plasma current attributable to electron-cyclotron wave-driven current generation. It excludes inductive current and current produced by other non-inductive mechanisms.

The total driven current is the toroidal projection of the driven current density integrated over a poloidal cross-section:

$$
I_{\mathrm{EC}} = \int_A j_{\phi,\mathrm{EC}}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{EC}}$ is the electron-cyclotron-driven current-density component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, $A$ is the plasma cross-sectional area in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $dA$ is its differential area. The quantity is a current contribution, not the absorbed electron-cyclotron wave power; its broader wave-driven-current counterpart is [current due to wave-driven current drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the driven current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Parallel current (IEC) driven by electron cyclotron (EC) waves in the ECRH/ECCD system. Represents the net toroidal current generated via the EC current drive mechanism, used for non-inductive current control.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by EC waves

NAMES.name: current_due_to_ion_cyclotron_current_drive
NAMES.short: Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by ion-cyclotron wave absorption and integrated over the plasma cross-section.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net plasma current driven by ion-cyclotron wave–particle interactions, excluding inductive and non-wave current contributions. It represents the toroidal component of the current generated by the absorbed ion-cyclotron power.

The current is obtained by integrating the driven toroidal current density over the plasma cross-section:

$$
I_{\mathrm{ICCD}} = \int_A j_{\phi,\mathrm{ICCD}}\,dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{ICCD}}$ is the driven current, $j_{\phi,\mathrm{ICCD}}$ is the ion-cyclotron-driven toroidal current density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $A$ is the plasma cross-sectional area. The quantity is a net current, so oppositely directed local contributions are algebraically summed. It is a source-specific component of [current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive) and is distinct from [current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the driven current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Parallel current (Ip) driven in the plasma by ion cyclotron (IC) waves from the ICRH launcher system. Part of the heating and current drive summary for the IC system.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by IC waves

NAMES.name: current_due_to_lower_hybrid_current_drive
NAMES.short: Net toroidal plasma current driven non-inductively by lower-hybrid slow waves through wave–particle interactions, contributing to the total non-inductive current.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net toroidal plasma current attributable to lower-hybrid current drive. It represents the lower-hybrid contribution to the plasma current and excludes inductive current and non-wave-driven non-inductive contributions.

$$
I_{\mathrm{LH}} = \int_{A_p} j_{\phi,\mathrm{LH}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{LH}}$ is the lower-hybrid-driven current, $j_{\phi,\mathrm{LH}}$ is the toroidal component of the lower-hybrid-driven current density, and $A_p$ is a poloidal cross-sectional area of the plasma. The quantity is a whole-plasma net current, so oppositely directed local contributions may partially cancel. It is a wave-driven contribution within [current due to wave-driven current drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive) and is distinct from [current due to electron cyclotron current drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the lower-hybrid-driven current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Parallel current driven by lower hybrid (LH) waves (LHCD), representing the non-inductive toroidal current generated by the LH heating and current drive system. A key figure of merit for current profile control scenarios.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by LH waves

NAMES.name: current_due_to_neutral_beam_injection
NAMES.short: Net toroidal plasma current driven by neutral-beam injection, combining the fast-ion current and collisional electron return current after beam ionization.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-beam-driven plasma current is the net toroidal current produced when injected neutrals ionize and their fast ions transfer momentum to the plasma. It includes both the directed fast-ion contribution and the associated collisional electron return-current contribution.

The current is defined by integrating the net neutral-beam-driven toroidal current density over the plasma cross-sectional area:

$$
I_{\mathrm{NBI}} = \int_{\mathcal{A}_{p}} j_{\phi,\mathrm{NBI}}(R,Z)\,d\mathcal{A}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{NBI}}$ is the neutral-beam-driven plasma current, $j_{\phi,\mathrm{NBI}}$ is its toroidal current-density contribution, and $\mathcal{A}_{p}$ is the plasma cross-sectional area in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This source contribution is distinct from [absorbed power of a neutral beam injector](name:absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector) and is combined with other current sources, including [plasma current due to ohmic induction](name:plasma_current_due_to_ohmic_induction) and [current due to electron-cyclotron current drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net toroidal current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Parallel current driven by a neutral beam injection (NBI) unit. Represents the non-inductive current drive contribution from the specified NBI beam, a key parameter for current profile control and advanced tokamak scenarios.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Parallel current driven by this NBI unit

NAMES.name: current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short: Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by wave–particle interactions, including cumulative and toroidal-mode-resolved representations.
NAMES.long:
Wave-driven current is the toroidal plasma current attributable to momentum transfer from externally applied electromagnetic waves through wave–particle interactions. It excludes inductive current and non-wave non-inductive current sources.

For a selected poloidal cross-sectional area, the current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{wd}} = \int_A j_{\mathrm{wd},\phi}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{wd}}$ is the wave-driven current, $A$ is the selected poloidal area, $j_{\mathrm{wd},\phi}$ is the toroidal component of the [wave-driven current density](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), and $(R,\phi,Z)$ is the right-handed cylindrical frame. For a flux-surface-enclosed area, this gives the cumulative quantity represented by [toroidal current due to wave-driven current drive](name:toroidal_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive); the same current may be decomposed into [per-toroidal-mode current](name:per_toroidal_mode_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the wave-driven plasma current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: electron_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to electron populations, integrated over the plasma volume and partitioned into thermal and fast-electron contributions.
NAMES.long:
Electron absorbed wave power is the total rate of energy transfer from coherent electromagnetic waves to the electron populations. It includes direct absorption by both bulk thermal electrons and fast non-thermal electrons.

The volume-integrated electron power is defined by

$$
P_e^{\mathrm{abs}} = \int_V p_e^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{abs}} + P_{e,\mathrm{thermal}}^{\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $P_e^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total electron absorbed wave power, $p_e^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local wave power deposition density to electrons, $V$ is the plasma volume, and the two terms are the [fast-electron absorbed wave power](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power) and [thermal-electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power). This quantity is the electron component of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), excluding power absorbed directly by ions or other channels; [ion absorbed wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power) represents the corresponding ion channel.

sources.enhanced_context: Global wave power absorbed by the thermal (bulk) electron population from a coherent wave. Represents the total heating power deposited into thermal electrons by the wave, excluding fast particle absorption.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: electron_energy
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated kinetic energy content of a specified electron population, encompassing bulk thermal and fast suprathermal electrons while excluding other plasma populations.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total kinetic energy contained in a selected electron population throughout the confined plasma volume. It is an extensive energy content, not a power or energy-transfer rate; the population scope determines which electron component is included.

$$
E_e = \int_{V_\mathrm{plasma}} u_e(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $E_e$ is the integrated electron energy, $u_e(\mathbf{r})$ is the local kinetic-energy density of the selected electron population, $V_\mathrm{plasma}$ is the confined plasma volume, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position. For the fast suprathermal component, [fast electron energy](name:fast_electron_energy) excludes the bulk thermal electron contribution. For the thermal component, [thermal electron energy](name:thermal_electron_energy) uses $u_e = 3p_e/2$, where $p_e$ is the local thermal electron pressure.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Fast electron power is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) electron population, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Fast electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power transferred to the fast, non-thermal electron population throughout the plasma volume. It is the fast-electron component of [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power).

The volume-integrated power is defined by

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_V p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-electron absorbed wave power, $p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local coherent-wave power density absorbed by fast electrons at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

This quantity excludes wave power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons, ions, and other populations, as well as wave power that is launched but not absorbed. Unlike [fast electron power at inside flux surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it represents the total plasma-volume integral rather than a cumulative value inside a specified flux surface. The population scope is complementary to [thermal electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

sources.enhanced_context: Wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) electron population from a given coherent wave. Represents the total (globally integrated) fraction of wave energy transferred to suprathermal electrons.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: fast_electron_energy
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated fast suprathermal energy content of the electron population, excluding the bulk thermal electron contribution.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated fast suprathermal energy content of the electron population is the total kinetic energy carried by electrons outside the bulk thermal population. It is the fast-population component of [electron_energy](name:electron_energy) and is distinct from [thermal_electron_energy](name:thermal_electron_energy).

The quantity is defined by

$$
E_{e,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{plasma}}} u_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $E_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the integrated fast-electron kinetic energy, $u_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local kinetic-energy density of the fast electron population at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the defined plasma volume. The integral excludes kinetic energy assigned to bulk thermal electrons. Unlike [fast_particle_energy](name:fast_particle_energy), this quantity is restricted specifically to suprathermal electrons.

sources.parent_definition: Fast particle energy content driven by LH waves

NAMES.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: First local tangential coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror is its signed displacement from the mirror-local origin along the first local tangential direction. That direction is the more horizontally directed in-plane mirror tangent oriented toward increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
First local tangential coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror is the signed scalar projection of the point displacement from the mirror-local origin onto the mirror's first local tangential axis. The mirror-local orthonormal triad $(\hat{\mathbf t}_1, \hat{\mathbf t}_2, \hat{\mathbf n})$ has $\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ and $\hat{\mathbf t}_2$ tangent to the mirror outline plane and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ as the plasma-facing normal. The first local tangential axis $\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ is the more horizontally directed in-plane tangent, oriented toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is defined by the Euclidean projection of the outline-point position relative to the mirror-local origin onto the first local tangential unit vector:

$$
\xi_1 = (\mathbf r - \mathbf r_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf t}_1
$$

where $\xi_1$ is the first local tangential coordinate of the mirror outline point, $\mathbf r$ is the position vector of the outline point, $\mathbf r_0$ is the mirror-local origin, and $\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ is the first local tangential unit vector.

This coordinate is paired with the [second local tangential coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), which uses $\hat{\mathbf t}_2$ in the same mirror-local tangential plane. The second local tangential direction is fixed by $\hat{\mathbf t}_2 = \hat{\mathbf n} \times \hat{\mathbf t}_1$, so $\hat{\mathbf t}_1 \times \hat{\mathbf t}_2 = \hat{\mathbf n}$. This local coordinate is distinct from locating the mirror in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame through quantities such as the [radial centroid of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:radial_centroid_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and the [vertical coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the displacement from the mirror-local origin to the outline point has a component in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf t}_1$.

sources.enhanced_context: Positions along the x1 axis of the irregular outline defining the EC launcher mirror geometry in its reference position, in the local (X1, X2) coordinate system. Forms part of the closed contour describing the mirror cross-sectional shape.
sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x1 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the object in the (X1, X2) coordinate system, used only if geometry_type/index=1. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

NAMES.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Signed coordinate of a neutral beam injector source-outline vertex along the injector’s first local tangential direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed first local tangential coordinate of a point on a neutral beam injector source outline. It belongs to the injector’s object-local frame and is paired with the [second local tangential coordinate](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector) to describe the outline in its tangent plane.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
x_1 = (\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_1
$$

where $x_1$ is the first local tangential coordinate, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position of the source-outline vertex, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the origin of the injector-local frame, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ is its positive first local tangential unit vector.

The origin and orientation are determined by the neutral beam injector’s local geometric convention; this quantity is not a coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and does not specify that convention by itself.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the outline vertex lies in the direction of the positive first local tangential basis vector from the local-frame origin.

sources.enhanced_context: Positions of NBI ion source outline vertices along the x1 axis of the local (X1, X2) coordinate system. Defines the geometry of the beam extraction surface outline.
sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x1 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system

NAMES.name: fraction_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short: Dimensionless fraction of the total launched wave-beam power carried by a specific electromagnetic polarization mode, ranging from zero (no power in that mode) to unity (entirely that mode).
NAMES.long:
In magnetized plasma wave heating, an electromagnetic beam injected into the plasma can be decomposed into orthogonal polarization eigenmodes whose power partition governs both the coupling efficiency and the spatial deposition profile. This quantity expresses the power fraction residing in one named eigenmode relative to the total beam power, providing a dimensionless measure of the modal purity of the launched beam.

For a beam composed of two complementary orthogonal modes, the mode fractions satisfy

$$
f_\mathrm{mode} = \frac{P_\mathrm{mode}}{P_\mathrm{total}}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{mode}$ is the power in the specified polarization mode and $P_\mathrm{total}$ is the total launched beam power, so fractions for complementary modes sum to unity.

For electron-cyclotron heating, the two principal eigenmodes are the ordinary mode (O-mode, with electric field parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field at perpendicular incidence) and the extraordinary mode (X-mode); the specific ordinary-mode case is captured by [ordinary_mode_fraction_of_wave_beam](name:ordinary_mode_fraction_of_wave_beam). The mode fraction is determined by the launch polarization state of the antenna or mirror system and is set as a launch parameter in ray-tracing or beam-tracing calculations.

Values span $[0, 1]$; a value of 1 indicates a purely single-mode launch, while intermediate values arise from imperfect polarization optics or intentional mixed-mode injection.

NAMES.name: frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Operating radio frequency of an electron-cyclotron heating antenna that sets the electron-cyclotron resonance conditions for its emitted electromagnetic wave.
NAMES.long:
The operating frequency is the temporal frequency of the electromagnetic wave generated by the antenna. It determines the magnetic-field strengths at which the wave can resonantly interact with electrons.

For the nonrelativistic electron-cyclotron harmonic condition,

$$
2\pi f_{\rm rf} = \omega_{\rm rf} = s\frac{eB}{m_e}
$$

where $f_{\rm rf}$ is the radio-frequency drive frequency, $\omega_{\rm rf}$ is the corresponding angular frequency, $s$ is the positive integer harmonic number, $e$ is the elementary-charge magnitude, $B$ is the local magnetic-field magnitude, and $m_e$ is the electron mass.

This quantity describes the antenna drive frequency, not its emitted power, feed voltage, or beam-steering angle. It is distinct from the [ion-cyclotron heating antenna frequency](name:frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), which selects ion-cyclotron rather than electron-cyclotron resonance conditions.

sources.enhanced_context: Frequency of the electron cyclotron (EC) beam, typically in the range 100–170 GHz. Determines which resonance layer in the plasma the wave is absorbed at, a key parameter for ECRH/ECCD targeting.
sources.leaf_definition: Frequency
sources.parent_definition: Set of Electron Cyclotron beams

sources.enhanced_context: Operating frequency of the electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) launcher, which determines the resonance layer location in the plasma for wave absorption. A key system parameter for ECRH/ECCD scenario design.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: ECRH frequency

NAMES.name: frequency_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Operating radio frequency of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna; a non-negative scalar that selects the ion cyclotron harmonic and constrains resonance to plasma locations with the corresponding magnetic-field magnitude.
NAMES.long:
Operating radio frequency of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the non-negative scalar oscillation frequency of the electromagnetic wave applied by the antenna for ion-cyclotron-range heating. It determines which ion cyclotron harmonic can resonate and constrains the resonance to locations where the magnetic-field magnitude gives the corresponding ion cyclotron frequency.

For an ion species with charge number $Z_i$ and mass $m_i$, resonance at harmonic $n$ satisfies:

$$
2\pi f = n\Omega_{ci} = n\frac{Z_i e B}{m_i}
$$

where $f$ is the antenna operating frequency, $n$ is a positive integer harmonic number, $\Omega_{ci}$ is the ion cyclotron angular frequency, $e$ is the elementary charge, and $B$ is the magnetic-field magnitude at the resonant location.

This quantity is the antenna operating frequency, not the launched power, antenna impedance, strap phase, or spatially varying local ion cyclotron frequency. The frequency alone does not identify a unique absorption channel when multiple ion species or harmonics can satisfy the resonance relation.

sources.enhanced_context: Operating frequency of an ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) antenna, averaged over its modules. Determines the resonance layer location and the target ion species for wave absorption in the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Frequency (average over modules)
sources.parent_definition: Set of Ion Cyclotron antennas

sources.enhanced_context: Operating frequency of an individual ICRH antenna module, time-resolved and recorded per module fed by a single transmission line. Determines the ion cyclotron resonance layer position in the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Frequency
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

sources.enhanced_context: Ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) wave frequency for a given launcher. This is the launched RF wave frequency that determines which ion species and harmonic are resonantly heated.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: ICRH frequency

NAMES.name: frequency_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Operating radio frequency of a lower-hybrid antenna is the non-negative carrier frequency assigned to that antenna. It sets the launched wave angular frequency and helps constrain lower-hybrid accessibility and electron parallel-resonance conditions.
NAMES.long:
Operating radio frequency of a lower-hybrid antenna is the non-negative carrier frequency assigned to that antenna. It sets the temporal oscillation rate of the lower-hybrid electromagnetic wave at launch and is one of the quantities that determines the wave dispersion, accessibility, and resonant interaction with electrons.

The frequency fixes the RF angular frequency and, with the launched parallel wave number, the parallel phase velocity sampled by Landau-resonant electrons:

$$
\omega_\mathrm{RF} = 2\pi f_\mathrm{LH,ant}, \qquad
v_{\parallel,\mathrm{ph}} = \frac{\omega_\mathrm{RF}}{k_\parallel} = \frac{c}{n_\parallel}
$$

where $f_\mathrm{LH,ant}$ is this antenna frequency, $\omega_\mathrm{RF}$ is the launched wave angular frequency, $k_\parallel$ is the launched parallel wave number, $n_\parallel$ is the launched parallel refractive index, and $c$ is the speed of light.

The lower-hybrid interpretation requires this carrier to be considered relative to the cold-plasma lower-hybrid resonance and accessibility conditions for the plasma composition, density, and magnetic field. It is distinct from launched wave-index components such as [toroidal launched wave index](name:toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and [poloidal launched wave index](name:poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna), which describe direction or phase spectrum, and from modulation, sideband, or bandwidth quantities.

sources.enhanced_context: Operating frequency of a lower hybrid (LH) antenna. Sets the wave frequency relative to the lower hybrid resonance, determining wave penetration depth and current drive efficiency in the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Frequency
sources.parent_definition: Set of Lower Hybrid antennas

sources.enhanced_context: Wave frequency of the lower hybrid (LH) wave used for heating and current drive (LHCD). Determines the wave propagation characteristics and accessibility conditions in the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: LH wave frequency

NAMES.name: gap_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Gap of an antenna strap is the nonnegative perpendicular clearance from the rear-facing surface of an ion-cyclotron-range antenna strap conductor to the conducting wall directly behind it, on the side facing away from the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Gap of an antenna strap is the scalar mechanical clearance between the rear-facing surface of an ion-cyclotron-range antenna strap conductor and the conducting wall directly behind it. It is defined on the side of the strap facing away from the plasma and represents the empty perpendicular separation, not a dimension of the conductor itself.

The clearance is the minimum perpendicular separation from the strap rear surface to the rear conducting wall:

$$
g = \min_{\mathbf{x}\in S_\mathrm{rear}} d_\perp(\mathbf{x}, W_\mathrm{back})
$$

where $g$ is the antenna-strap gap in meters, $S_\mathrm{rear}$ is the rear-facing surface of the strap conductor, $W_\mathrm{back}$ is the conducting wall directly behind the strap, and $d_\perp$ is the nonnegative perpendicular distance in meters from point $\mathbf{x}$ on $S_\mathrm{rear}$ to $W_\mathrm{back}$.

This name denotes the same rear-surface-to-back-wall clearance as [back_surface_gap_of_antenna_strap](name:back_surface_gap_of_antenna_strap), with shorter wording. It excludes strap body dimensions such as [thickness_of_antenna_strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap), [inner_radius_of_antenna_strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap), and [outer_radius_of_antenna_strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap), and it does not denote a signed displacement or a plasma-facing standoff distance.

sources.enhanced_context: Distance from an ICRH antenna strap to the conducting wall or conductor located behind it. This geometric parameter influences the antenna loading resistance and RF coupling efficiency to the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Distance to conducting wall or other conductor behind the antenna strap
sources.parent_definition: Set of IC antenna straps

NAMES.name: height_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Full vertical extent of an ICRH antenna strap conductor cross-section, measured parallel to the Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The antenna-strap height is the full vertical extent of the rectangular conductor cross-section, measured parallel to the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is a geometric cross-section dimension, not the antenna elevation or its distance from the plasma.

$$
H = Z_{\max} - Z_{\min}
$$

where $H$ is the strap height and $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the vertical coordinates of the upper and lower cross-section boundaries. The dimension is non-negative and complements the [toroidal width of the antenna strap](name:toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap) and [thickness of the antenna strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap), which describe the other conductor extents. For an annular cross-section, the radial boundaries are specified by the [inner radius of the antenna strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap) and [outer radius of the antenna strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap).

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical full height of the rectangular cross-section of an ICRH antenna strap element. Defines the vertical dimension of the rectangular strap geometry used in ion cyclotron antenna modelling.
sources.leaf_definition: Vertical full height
sources.parent_definition: Rectangular description of the element

NAMES.name: ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to ion populations, integrated over the plasma volume and partitioned into thermal and fast-ion contributions.
NAMES.long:
Ion absorbed wave power is the total rate of energy transfer from coherent electromagnetic waves to ion populations. It includes direct absorption by both bulk thermal ions and suprathermal fast ions.

The volume-integrated ion power is defined by

$$
P_i^{\mathrm{abs}} = \int_V p_i^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{abs}} + P_{i,\mathrm{thermal}}^{\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $P_i^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total ion absorbed wave power, $p_i^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local wave power deposition density to ions, $V$ is the plasma volume, and the two terms are the [fast-ion absorbed wave power](name:fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power) and [thermal-ion absorbed wave power](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power). This quantity is the ion component of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), excluding power transferred directly to electron populations; [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) represents the corresponding electron channel.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total coherent-wave power absorbed by the suprathermal ion population, integrated over the plasma volume and excluding thermal-ion absorption.
NAMES.long:
The fast ion absorbed wave power is the volume-integrated power delivered by coherent electromagnetic waves to the suprathermal, nonthermal ion population through wave-particle interactions.

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast\,ion}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs,fast\,ion}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast\,ion}}$ is the total absorbed power, $p_{\mathrm{abs,fast\,ion}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local power-absorption density for fast ions at position $\mathbf{r}$, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. This quantity is the fast-ion component of [ion absorbed wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power), excluding power absorbed by thermal ions and electrons. It is aggregated over the coherent-wave channels and toroidal modes represented by the global quantity; [per-toroidal-mode fast-ion absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power) and [fast-ion power at an inside flux surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) provide more resolved scopes.

sources.enhanced_context: Total wave power absorbed by the fast (suprathermal) ion population from a coherent wave, integrated over the plasma volume. Represents energy transfer from the RF wave to non-thermal ions for a given ion species.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Total coherent-wave power absorbed by a specified ion charge state is the direct wave-to-ion energy-transfer rate for that charge-state population, integrated over the plasma volume and excluding later collisional energy exchange.
NAMES.long:
Total coherent-wave power absorbed by a specified ion charge state is the volume-integrated rate at which coherent electromagnetic-wave fields transfer energy directly to ions in that charge-state population.

The defining volume integral is

$$
P_{i,\zeta}^{\mathrm{wave}} = \int_{V_\mathrm{plasma}} p_{i,\zeta}^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $P_{i,\zeta}^{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the absorbed wave power for ion charge state $\zeta$, $p_{i,\zeta}^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local coherent-wave power absorption density for ions in that charge state at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_\mathrm{plasma}$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is the volume element.

This quantity is resolved for one ion charge state; it is not the charge-state-summed [ion absorbed wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power) and it never includes [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power). More specific children may add an ion-population qualifier while retaining the same charge-state-resolved meaning, for example [fast ion charge-state absorbed wave power](name:fast_ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power). It excludes energy exchanged after absorption through Coulomb collisions or other inter-population relaxation.

sources.enhanced_context: Total wave power absorbed by the fast (suprathermal) ion population of a given ion charge state. Quantifies the fraction of RF wave energy deposited into energetic ions rather than the thermal bulk.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to fast ions in one specified ion charge state, excluding collisional energy exchange.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the direct electromagnetic-wave energy transfer rate to the fast, non-thermal ions belonging to one specified charge state, integrated over the full plasma volume.

The defining relation is

$$
P_{q,\mathrm{wave}} = \int_V p_{q,\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{q,\mathrm{wave}}$ is the absorbed wave power for charge state $q$, $p_{q,\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})$ is its local wave-power deposition density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $V$ is the full plasma volume.

This is a charge-state-resolved component of [ion charge-state absorbed wave power](name:ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power): it excludes power transferred subsequently through Coulomb collisions and is not the cumulative value inside a selected flux surface, which is represented by [fast ion charge-state power at inside flux surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

sources.enhanced_context: Total wave power absorbed by the fast (suprathermal) ion population of a given ion charge state. Quantifies the fraction of RF wave energy deposited into energetic ions rather than the thermal bulk.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated power transferred from a coherent electromagnetic wave to an ion population, with population resolution and mode aggregation defined by each specific instance.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total power absorbed directly from a coherent electromagnetic wave by a selected ion population over the plasma volume. It generalizes the charge-state-resolved thermal quantity represented by [thermal ion charge-state power](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power).

$$
P_{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs,ion}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the volume-integrated ion absorption power, $p_{\mathrm{abs,ion}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local electromagnetic-wave power absorbed by ions, $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element. Population selection, charge-state resolution, and toroidal-mode aggregation are specified by more specific instances. The quantity is an ion contribution to the broader [ion absorbed wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power), rather than power absorbed by electron populations.

sources.enhanced_context: Total wave power absorbed by the fast (suprathermal) ion population of a given ion charge state. Quantifies the fraction of RF wave energy deposited into energetic ions rather than the thermal bulk.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: length_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.short: Curvilinear distance accumulated along a beam-tracing ray from a designated reference point to a point on its vacuum or plasma trajectory.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the geometric distance accumulated along a beam-tracing ray from its designated reference point to a point on the ray. It follows the ray trajectory and therefore differs from the straight-line separation of the endpoints.

For a ray position $\mathbf{r}(\lambda)$ parameterized by a monotonically increasing path parameter $\lambda$, the arc length is

$$
s(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)=\int_{\lambda_0}^{\lambda_1}\left\lVert\frac{d\mathbf{r}}{d\lambda}\right\rVert\,d\lambda
$$

where $\lambda_0$ identifies the reference point, $\lambda_1$ identifies the endpoint, $\mathbf{r}$ is the ray position, and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ is the Euclidean norm. The resulting length is non-negative and may include segments in both vacuum and plasma. The electron-cyclotron-specific counterpart [length of electron-cyclotron beam](name:length_of_electron_cyclotron_beam) uses the same geometric path-length concept.

sources.enhanced_context: Curvilinear arc length along a ray or beam trajectory in beam tracing calculations. Parameterizes the propagation path of the wave beam through the plasma for EC, IC, LH, or other RF wave heating schemes.
sources.leaf_definition: Ray/beam curvilinear length
sources.parent_definition: Set of rays/beams describing the wave propagation

NAMES.name: maximum_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: Maximum allowed value of the signed rotation angle of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror within its mechanical travel range.
NAMES.long:
The upper mechanical travel limit is the greatest permitted value of the mirror’s signed rotation angle, bounding the accessible steering range of the launcher. It is a limit of the mechanical actuator, not the mirror angle during a particular operating condition.

Let $\theta$ denote the signed mirror angle defined by [angle of electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror). The upper limit $\theta_{\max}$ is defined by

$$
\theta_{\max} = \sup\{\theta \mid \theta\text{ is mechanically accessible}\}
$$

The quantity excludes the lower travel limit and does not describe the mirror’s position unless that position equals the upper boundary of the allowed range.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the mirror rotates in the positive sense defined for [angle of electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).

sources.enhanced_context: Maximum angular displacement (rotation angle) of the EC launcher mirror about its reference position, measured counter-clockwise around the movement direction vector. Defines the upper mechanical travel limit for the mirror steering degree of freedom.
sources.leaf_definition: Maximum angular displacement with respect to the reference position, counter-clockwise around the direction vector
sources.parent_definition: Set of degrees of freedom for this mirror, allowing the mirror to move around its reference position indicated in ../geometry. Can be cascaded for composite movements.

NAMES.name: neutral_beam_energy
NAMES.subject: neutral_beam
NAMES.short: Kinetic energy per atom of the full-energy neutral-beam component, set by the ion-source acceleration voltage before neutralization.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the kinetic energy carried by one atom in the full-energy component of an injected neutral beam. It represents the energy associated with the complete ion-source acceleration, rather than beam power or total injected energy.

The full-energy value is defined by the accelerating potential difference:

$$
E_{\mathrm{full}} = e V_{\mathrm{acc}}
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{full}}$ is the atom's kinetic energy in joules, $e$ is the elementary charge, and $V_{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the magnitude of the ion-source acceleration voltage in volts. Expressed in electron-volts, the numerical energy equals the numerical acceleration voltage in volts.

This quantity applies only to the full-energy component. It excludes half- and third-energy components produced by molecular dissociation and is not an abundance-weighted average over those components. The associated injector power is a separate quantity, [neutral beam injector power](name:power_of_neutral_beam_injector).

sources.enhanced_context: Full beam energy of the injected neutral beam species, corresponding to the kinetic energy gained by a single atom during acceleration. This is the characteristic injection energy for the NBI unit, determining penetration depth and heating profile.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Full energy of the injected species (acceleration of a single atom)

NAMES.name: ordinary_mode_fraction_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short: Fraction of the launched electron-cyclotron wave-beam power carried by the ordinary polarization mode.
NAMES.long:
The ordinary-mode fraction is the share of launched electron-cyclotron wave-beam power carried by the ordinary electromagnetic polarization eigenmode. It distinguishes this polarization component from the complementary mode contributions represented by the parent quantity [fraction of wave beam](name:fraction_of_wave_beam).

$$
f_O = \frac{P_O}{P_{\rm launch}}
$$

where $f_O$ is the ordinary-mode power fraction, $P_O$ is the launched power in the ordinary mode, and $P_{\rm launch}$ is the total launched wave-beam power. The fraction is bounded by zero and one when the polarization-mode powers are nonnegative and exhaust the launched power; it excludes power introduced or lost after launch.

sources.enhanced_context: Fraction of electron cyclotron (EC) beam power launched in ordinary (O) mode, where 1.0 indicates pure O-mode and 0.0 indicates pure X-mode. Characterizes the wave polarization state of the launched EC beam.
sources.leaf_definition: Fraction of EC beam power launched in ordinary (O) mode. If all power is launched in ordinary mode (O-mode), o_mode_fraction = 1.0. If all  power is launched in extraordinary mode (X-mode), o_mode_fraction = 0.0
sources.parent_definition: Wave polarization

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short: Non-inductive current density from wave-driven current drive resolved per toroidal Fourier mode number, quantifying the independent driven-current contribution of each toroidal harmonic.
NAMES.long:
Wave-driven current-drive schemes transfer directed parallel momentum to the plasma through resonant wave-particle interactions, producing a non-inductive current density. Decomposing the wave field into toroidal Fourier harmonics indexed by mode number $n_\phi$ yields this per-mode current density, whose sum over all $n_\phi$ recovers [current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive) and whose volume-integrated toroidal projection gives the total [current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive).

The field-aligned projection is the physically dominant contribution and is captured by [parallel_per_toroidal_mode_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive](name:parallel_per_toroidal_mode_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), which isolates the flux-surface-averaged driven current for each toroidal harmonic as a function of minor radius. The mode-resolved representation is particularly valuable for lower-hybrid and electron-cyclotron current-drive, where different $n_\phi$ values correspond to distinct parallel refractive indices, cyclotron resonance surfaces, and spatially separate deposition locations.

This quantity is computed from spectral ray-tracing or full-wave codes that resolve wave-plasma momentum exchange at each toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, and the components are expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the parallel (field-aligned) component of the driven current density points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: parallel_per_toroidal_mode_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short: Parallel per-toroidal-mode current density due to wave-driven current drive is the magnetic-field-aligned component of the non-inductive current-density contribution from a single toroidal Fourier harmonic.
NAMES.long:
Parallel per-toroidal-mode current density due to wave-driven current drive is the component of the current-density contribution from one toroidal Fourier harmonic that is parallel to the local magnetic field. It represents the field-aligned part of the non-inductive current generated by wave-driven current drive for the specified harmonic.

The defining projection is

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{wcd}}^{(n_\phi)} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{wcd}}^{(n_\phi)} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{wcd}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the parallel per-toroidal-mode current density due to wave-driven current drive, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{wcd}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the vector [per-toroidal-mode current density due to wave-driven current drive](name:per_toroidal_mode_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode index associated with variation in toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height.

This quantity is a field-aligned scalar projection, not the vector current density and not the $\hat{\phi}$ component that defines [toroidal current density](name:toroidal_current_density) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It includes only the wave-driven non-inductive contribution for the specified $n_\phi$; it excludes inductive, bootstrap, neutral-beam-driven, and other non-wave current-density contributions. It is distinct from the integrated [per-toroidal-mode current due to wave-driven current drive](name:per_toroidal_mode_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive) and the [toroidal current due to wave-driven current drive](name:toroidal_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the wave-driven current-density contribution from the specified toroidal harmonic points along $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

sources.enhanced_context: Flux-surface-averaged wave-driven parallel current density (J∥) per toroidal mode number (nφ), providing the spectral decomposition of RF-driven parallel current as a function of radius and mode index.
sources.leaf_definition: Flux surface averaged wave driven parallel current density, per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Source radial profiles (flux surface averaged quantities) for various time slices

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short: Toroidal mode current due to wave-driven current drive is the cumulative toroidal plasma current enclosed by a flux surface for one toroidal Fourier mode.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal mode current due to wave-driven current drive is the cumulative toroidal plasma current enclosed by a magnetic flux surface and attributed to one toroidal Fourier mode. It represents the wave-particle-interaction contribution only; inductive and non-wave non-inductive current sources are excluded.

The cumulative mode current inside the surface labeled by normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is defined by:

$$
I_{\mathrm{wcd},n}(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}) = \int_{S(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}})} \widetilde{\mathbf{j}}_{\mathrm{wcd},n}(R,Z) \cdot \hat{\phi}\,dR\,dZ
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{wcd},n}$ is the mode-resolved current, $n$ is the dimensionless toroidal Fourier mode number, $\widetilde{\mathbf{j}}_{\mathrm{wcd},n}$ is the corresponding wave-driven current-density coefficient in A m$^{-2}$, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $R$ is major radius in m, $Z$ is vertical height in m, and $S$ is the enclosed poloidal cross-section.

At the outer closed surface, this quantity is the single-mode contribution to [current due to wave-driven current drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive). Unlike [toroidal current due to wave-driven current drive](name:toroidal_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), it is not summed over toroidal Fourier modes; its local density counterpart is [per-toroidal-mode current density due to wave-driven current drive](name:per_toroidal_mode_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the specified mode's net current contribution flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Wave-driven toroidal current from a standalone calculation, resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Represents the toroidal current contribution from each phi-mode without self-consistent coupling to other sources.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave driven toroidal current from a stand alone calculation (not consistent with other sources) per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities for various time slices

sources.leaf_definition: Wave driven toroidal current, inside a flux surface, per toroidal mode number

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Wave power absorbed by fast suprathermal electrons, resolved into contributions from individual toroidal Fourier mode numbers.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the coherent-wave power transferred to the fast, suprathermal electron population for one toroidal Fourier mode. Summing the modal contributions gives the volume-integrated [fast electron absorbed wave power](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast}} = \sum_{n_\phi} P_{\mathrm{fast},n_\phi}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the total fast-electron absorbed wave power, $P_{\mathrm{fast},n_\phi}$ is its contribution for toroidal Fourier mode number $n_\phi$, and the sum covers the mode numbers in the decomposition. The quantity includes only fast electrons and excludes thermal-electron and ion absorption. It is distinct from [per-toroidal-mode thermal electron absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

sources.enhanced_context: Wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) electron population resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi) for a coherent wave. Captures the mode-number decomposition of fast-particle RF power absorption by electrons.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative radial profile of absorbed wave power on fast electrons inside a flux surface, resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Quantifies mode-resolved fast-electron wave absorption as a function of radius.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density), per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Cumulative coherent-wave power absorbed by the suprathermal ion population within a magnetic flux surface, resolved by toroidal Fourier mode number.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the power transferred from a coherent electromagnetic wave to suprathermal (fast) ions, cumulatively integrated inside a magnetic flux surface and separated by toroidal Fourier mode number.

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast\,ion}}(\rho,n_\phi)=\int_{V(\rho)}p_{\mathrm{abs,fast\,ion}}(\mathbf{x},n_\phi)\,dV
$$

Here, $\rho$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, $V(\rho)$ is the volume enclosed by that surface, and $p_{\mathrm{abs,fast\,ion}}$ is the local power density absorbed by fast ions in that mode.

The quantity excludes power absorbed by thermal ions or electrons and excludes wave power that is launched but not transferred to fast ions. Summing over toroidal modes at the full plasma volume recovers the total [fast-ion absorbed wave power](name:fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power); species-resolved thermal contributions are represented by [per-toroidal-mode thermal-ion absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power) and [per-toroidal-mode thermal-electron absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

sources.enhanced_context: Wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) ion population from a coherent RF wave, resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Quantifies RF energy deposition into the fast ion component as a function of toroidal mode index.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative absorbed wave power on thermal ion species inside a flux surface, resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Provides the toroidal mode decomposition of the radial power deposition profile for thermal ions.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density), per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal-Fourier-mode contribution to coherent-wave power directly absorbed by fast ions in a specified charge state, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the coherent-electromagnetic-wave power absorbed directly by fast ions in one specified charge state, resolved by toroidal Fourier mode and integrated over the plasma volume. It is a modal component of [fast-ion charge-state power](name:fast_ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power), excluding collisional energy exchange between plasma populations.

The volume-integrated modal power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast},q}(n_\phi)=\int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}}p_{\mathrm{abs,fast},q}(n_\phi,\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $n_\phi$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, $q$ is the ion charge state, $p_{\mathrm{abs,fast},q}$ is the corresponding local absorbed-power density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume.

Unlike [per-toroidal-mode fast-ion power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density), this quantity is volume-integrated and retains ion charge-state resolution; it is distinct from the corresponding thermal-ion modal power [per-toroidal-mode thermal-ion charge-state power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power).

sources.enhanced_context: Wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) ion population, decomposed per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Captures the mode-number-dependent RF heating contribution to fast ions for a specific ion charge state.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative absorbed wave power on fast (non-thermal) ion species inside a flux surface, resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Quantifies the toroidal-mode-resolved RF power deposition profile for fast ions.
