NAMES.name: perpendicular_wave_vector_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Non-negative magnitude of the RF wave-vector component perpendicular to the local equilibrium magnetic field launched by an ion-cyclotron heating antenna.
NAMES.long:
This quantity measures the transverse spatial variation of the radio-frequency wave launched by an ion-cyclotron heating antenna, relative to the local equilibrium magnetic field.

The perpendicular wave-vector magnitude is defined by

$$
k_\perp = \left|\mathbf{k} - (\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}})\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right|
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the local RF wave vector, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and vertical bars denote vector magnitude.

Only the component transverse to the magnetic field is included; the parallel component is excluded. The result is non-negative and has no propagation-direction sign. It is the antenna-specific counterpart of the general [perpendicular wave-vector magnitude](name:perpendicular_wave_vector_magnitude).

sources.enhanced_context: Main perpendicular wave number (k⊥) of ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) waves launched by an IC antenna. Characterizes the transverse spatial scale of the wave in the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Main perpendicular wave number of IC waves

NAMES.name: poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Signed dimensionless poloidal component of the launched lower-hybrid wave refractive-index vector, measured along increasing geometric poloidal angle about the antenna reference point.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal launched-wave index is the projection of the lower-hybrid launched wave refractive-index vector onto the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle about the antenna reference point. It describes the poloidal part of the launch spectrum and is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal launched-wave index](name:toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

The index is defined by

$$
N_\theta = \frac{\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta}{k_0} = \frac{k_\theta}{k_0}
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the launched wave vector, $\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle $\theta$, $k_\theta$ is the corresponding wave-vector projection, and $k_0 = \omega/c$ is the free-space wavenumber for angular frequency $\omega$ and speed of light $c$. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The quantity describes the launch condition only; it is not the local poloidal wave index after propagation or interaction with the plasma.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the launched wave-vector projection points in the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle $\theta$.

sources.enhanced_context: Poloidal refractive index (n_pol) of the lower hybrid wave spectrum launched by a row of LH antenna waveguides. Characterizes the poloidal wavenumber spectrum of the launched LH wave relative to the antenna reference point.
sources.leaf_definition: Refraction index in the poloidal direction. The poloidal angle is defined from the reference point; the angle at a point (R,Z) is given by atan((Z-Zref)/(R-Rref)), where Rref=reference_point/r and Zref=reference_point/z
sources.parent_definition: Set of horizontal rows of waveguides (corresponding to different poloidal positions). A power spectrum is provided for each row.

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_beam_tracing_point
NAMES.short: Signed poloidal magnetic flux function evaluated at a beam-tracing point, serving as the magnetic-surface label at that location.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal magnetic flux at a beam-tracing point is the value of the equilibrium flux function at the point where the ray or beam path intersects the plasma. In an axisymmetric equilibrium, it labels the nested magnetic surface passing through that point and is distinct from the normalized coordinate derived from axis and boundary values.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the flux function is defined by

$$
\psi(R,Z) = \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, $R'$ is the integration radius, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component. The beam-tracing point supplies the coordinates at which $\psi$ is evaluated. Its value is related to [poloidal magnetic flux at a flux surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface), while [normalized poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate) uses the magnetic-axis and plasma-boundary flux values for normalization.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $B_Z$ on the integration disk points in the $+Z$ direction.

sources.enhanced_context: Poloidal magnetic flux (ψ) at each position along a ray or beam path in the beam tracing calculation, providing the flux-surface label at each propagation step.
sources.leaf_definition: Poloidal flux
sources.parent_definition: Position of the ray/beam along its path

NAMES.name: power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Cumulative power associated with a specified plasma heating or energy-transfer channel, integrated over the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative power associated with one physically defined plasma heating or energy-transfer channel inside a specified magnetic flux surface. The parent does not by itself select a species, population, source, absorption mechanism, or whether the channel is absorbed power or net transferred power.

For a volumetric channel power density, the cumulative power is

$$
P_{\mathrm{ch}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ch}}(\psi)$ is the cumulative channel power, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux-surface label, $V(\psi)$ is the volume enclosed by that surface, $p_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is the corresponding volumetric power density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the volume element.

Species- and population-specific instances include [electron power at an inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), [ion power at an inside flux surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), and [ion charge-state power at an inside flux surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface). Absorbed-power channels count energy deposited in the recipient population, whereas net-transfer channels follow the specified transfer direction and may be signed.

NAMES.name: electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Cumulative wave power absorbed by all electron populations, thermal and fast, from a specified wave source or source set within the plasma volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The electron power at inside flux surface is the cumulative rate at which wave energy from a specified source or source set is deposited into the electron population, spanning both thermal bulk electrons and fast suprathermal electrons, within the plasma volume bounded by a closed magnetic flux surface. It is an enclosed-volume channel quantity: each bounding surface includes all electron wave absorption inside that surface.

For a local volumetric electron wave-power deposition density, the cumulative power is

$$
P_e(\psi_s) = \int_{V(\psi_s)} p_e^{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_e(\psi_s)$ is this cumulative electron wave power, $\psi_s$ is the magnetic-flux-surface label of the bounding surface, $V(\psi_s)$ is the plasma volume enclosed by that surface, $p_e^{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the local volumetric rate of wave energy deposition into the electron population, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the volume element.

For the same wave channel and enclosed volume, this quantity satisfies the population decomposition $P_e = P_{e,\mathrm{thermal}} + P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$, with components [thermal electron power at inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and [fast electron power at inside flux surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface). It is the electron counterpart of [ion power at inside flux surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and a species-specific instance of [power at inside flux surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface); it excludes ion absorption and non-wave loss or exchange channels.
NAMES.sign: Positive when wave energy is deposited into the electron population.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Cumulative wave power absorbed by the fast (suprathermal) electron population within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Fast electron power at an inside flux surface quantifies the total rate at which coherent wave energy is absorbed by the non-thermal fast electron population within the plasma volume bounded by a given magnetic flux surface. It is the fast-electron contribution to [electron power at an inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), distinct from the bulk thermal-electron contribution [thermal electron power at an inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

The quantity is obtained by integrating the flux-surface-averaged [fast electron power density](name:fast_electron_power_density) $p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}$ over the enclosed plasma volume:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho) = \int_0^\rho p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho') \frac{dV}{d\rho'} \, d\rho'
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast,e}}(\rho)$ is the cumulative absorbed power, $\rho$ labels the limiting flux surface, $\rho'$ is the integration variable, $p_{\mathrm{fast,e}}$ is the local fast-electron absorbed power density, and $dV/d\rho'$ is the differential enclosed volume per unit flux-surface label. Only absorption by fast electrons is included; thermal-electron and ion absorption, launched power, and power absorbed outside the enclosed volume are excluded. At the outermost closed flux surface, the quantity gives the total wave power absorbed by fast electrons.

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative absorbed wave power deposited on fast (non-thermal) electrons inside a given flux surface, computed by volume integration of the fast-electron power deposition density from the magnetic axis outward.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Cumulative power associated with wave absorption by a specified ion charge state, integrated over the plasma volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative power associated with one physically defined plasma heating or energy-transfer channel inside a specified magnetic flux surface. Here, the channel is wave power absorbed by a specified ion charge state, which may belong to either the thermal or fast ion population.

The cumulative absorbed power is

$$
P_q^{\mathrm{abs}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_q^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_q^{\mathrm{abs}}(\psi)$ is the cumulative absorbed power for charge state $q$, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux-surface label, $V(\psi)$ is the plasma volume enclosed by that surface, $p_q^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the corresponding local absorbed wave-power density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the volume element.

This quantity is resolved for one ion charge state and excludes absorption by other charge states and by non-ion populations. It is the charge-state-resolved counterpart of [ion power at an inside flux surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), while [fast ion charge state power at an inside flux surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and [thermal ion charge state power at an inside flux surface](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface) specify the fast and thermal realizations.

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative absorbed wave power on fast (non-thermal) ion species of a given charge state inside a flux surface, obtained by volume integration of the fast ion power absorption density from the plasma centre outward.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified fast (non-thermal) ion charge state within the plasma volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Charge-state-resolved cumulative wave power deposited into the fast (non-thermal) ion population enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface. It is obtained by integrating the local fast-ion charge-state power-deposition density over the plasma volume from the magnetic axis to the selected flux surface.

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast,cs}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_{\mathrm{fast,cs}}(\mathbf{r})\, dV
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{fast,cs}}$ is the local wave power deposited per unit volume into the specified fast-ion charge state and $V(\psi)$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the flux surface labeled by $\psi$.

This quantity is the fast-ion subset of [ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and the charge-state-resolved counterpart of [fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface). It excludes power absorbed by thermal ions of the same charge state; the thermal complement is [thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface). Summing over all charge states recovers the total fast-ion enclosed power.
NAMES.sign: Positive when net wave power flows from the electromagnetic field into the fast-ion charge state.

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative absorbed wave power on fast (non-thermal) ion species of a given charge state inside a flux surface, obtained by volume integration of the fast ion power absorption density from the plasma centre outward.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Cumulative wave power absorbed by all ion populations — thermal and fast — within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The ion power at inside flux surface is the cumulative rate at which wave energy is deposited into the ion population — spanning both thermal bulk ions and fast (non-thermal) ions — within the plasma volume bounded by a closed magnetic flux surface. It is the ion-channel component of the more general [power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface), separating ion energy absorption from the corresponding electron heating contribution.

The quantity is the volume integral of the total ion wave-power density $p_i(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\psi)$ enclosed by the flux surface labeled $\psi$:

$$
P_i(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_i(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_i$ is the ion volumetric heating power density in W m$^{-3}$ and $\psi$ is the chosen flux-surface label, such as the normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$.

The population-resolved breakdown is given by [thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) for the bulk ion channel and [fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface) for non-thermal beam or fusion-born ions. This cumulative radial profile enables power-balance analysis and is inferred from combining absorbed-power density profiles computed via wave ray-tracing or Monte Carlo beam-deposition codes with equilibrium flux-surface geometry.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Cumulative wave power absorbed by the fast (non-thermal) ion population within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion power at inside flux surface quantifies the running volume integral of RF wave power deposited into the suprathermal (non-thermal) ion population, profiling the radial distribution of enclosed fast-ion wave absorption. It forms the fast-ion component of [ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), which includes both this quantity and the complementary thermal-ion contribution captured by [thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

The enclosed fast-ion power is defined as:

$$
P_\mathrm{fast}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} Q_\mathrm{fast}(\mathbf{r})\, dV
$$

where $Q_\mathrm{fast}$ is the volumetric fast-ion wave power deposition density and $V(\psi)$ is the plasma volume enclosed within the flux surface at poloidal flux coordinate $\psi$.

This quantity arises primarily in scenarios such as ion cyclotron resonance heating, where waves resonantly accelerate minority ions to suprathermal energies and sustain a non-Maxwellian tail population. The profile of $P_\mathrm{fast}(\psi)$ accumulates with increasing enclosed volume, saturating at the total fast-ion absorbed power at the last closed flux surface. For the charge-state-resolved counterpart, see [fast_ion_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface); the local deposition density from which this integral is constructed is given by [fast_ion_power_density](name:fast_ion_power_density).

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative absorbed wave power on fast (non-thermal) ion species inside a given flux surface, computed as the volume integral of the fast-ion power deposition density. Profiles the enclosed fast-ion wave absorption as a function of radial coordinate.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short: Net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma through electron cyclotron heating, with source aggregation determined by scope and excluding launched or reflected power.
NAMES.long:
Electron-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which electron-cyclotron-range electromagnetic waves transfer energy to the plasma, principally through resonant electron absorption. It denotes deposited plasma heating power rather than generator, launched, transmitted, or reflected power.

The absorbed power is defined by the volume integral of the local electron-cyclotron heating density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{EC}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} Q_{\mathrm{EC}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the absorbed power, $Q_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the local power-transfer density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. Source aggregation is scope-dependent; the [total electron-cyclotron heating power](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating) sums the contributions from all electron-cyclotron wave sources. The quantity is non-negative for net absorption and is distinct from [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) when that quantity includes wave absorption without restricting the mechanism to electron cyclotron heating.

sources.enhanced_context: Electron cyclotron heating power (P_EC) coupled to the plasma from a specific ECRH/ECCD launcher. Represents the absorbed RF power delivered to the plasma electrons via electron cyclotron resonance.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron cyclotron heating power coupled to the plasma from this launcher

NAMES.name: power_due_to_first_orbit_loss
NAMES.short: Power carried out of the confined fast-ion population by particles whose first guiding-center orbit after birth or acceleration is unconfined; it is a positive loss magnitude.
NAMES.long:
First-orbit-loss power is the kinetic-energy loss rate carried away by fast ions whose first guiding-center orbit after birth or acceleration intersects the confining boundary. It represents the aggregate loss from the confined fast-ion population, rather than energy transferred by collisions or subsequent orbit evolution.

The volume-integrated loss power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{FOL}} = \int_V p_{\mathrm{FOL}}^{(1)}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{FOL}}$ is the first-orbit-loss power, $V$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $p_{\mathrm{FOL}}^{(1)}$ is the local kinetic-energy loss rate density from first-orbit-unconfined fast ions.

The quantity is a non-negative loss magnitude and excludes power losses specifically attributed to charge exchange, such as [fast-ion power due to charge exchange](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange).

sources.enhanced_context: Power loss due to first orbit losses, where newly born fast particles (e.g., from NBI or fusion reactions) escape before completing a full orbit. A global scalar power sink in the distribution function framework.
sources.leaf_definition: Power loss due to first orbit losses
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities (integrated over plasma volume for moments of the distribution, collisional exchange and source terms), for various time slices

NAMES.name: power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short: Net radio-frequency power coupled from ion-cyclotron heating launchers into the plasma, resolved per launcher or aggregated across the launcher system. It excludes reflected power and losses before the launcher–plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net radio-frequency wave power crossing the boundary between an ion-cyclotron heating launcher and the plasma. It may represent one launcher or the aggregate of multiple launchers.

The launcher-resolved coupled power is defined by the time-averaged Poynting flux through a surface separating the launcher from the plasma:

$$
P_{\mathrm{IC},a} = \oint_{S_a} \langle \mathbf{S}_a \rangle \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}} \, dA
$$

where $a$ labels the launcher, $S_a$ is a surface enclosing its plasma-facing aperture, $\langle \mathbf{S}_a \rangle$ is the time-averaged Poynting flux of its launched wave field, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the surface normal directed toward the plasma, and $dA$ is the surface-area element.

The quantity excludes reflected power and losses in transmission lines, launcher structures, and surrounding material. It is not reduced by incomplete absorption after the coupled wave field enters the plasma. Summing launcher-resolved values gives [total power due to ion cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating); it is distinct from [total power of the ion cyclotron heating antenna](name:total_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), which denotes launched rather than boundary-coupled power.

sources.enhanced_context: Ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) power coupled to the plasma from a specific launcher. Represents the net power absorbed by the plasma from the IC heating system.
sources.leaf_definition: Value

NAMES.name: power_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.short: Power of a beam-tracing beam is the residual electromagnetic wave power still carried by one coherent wave beam at the endpoint of its traced trajectory. It is distinct from initial launch power and from cumulative plasma-absorbed power.
NAMES.long:
Power of a beam-tracing beam is the residual electromagnetic wave power still carried by a single coherent beam at the endpoint of the traced trajectory. It represents power remaining in the wave after propagation and after modeled transfer of wave energy to the plasma.

The single-beam power balance relates the residual power to the initial and absorbed powers:

$$
P_{\mathrm{res}} = P_0 - P_{\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{res}}$ is [power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:power_of_beam_tracing_beam), $P_0$ is [initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam), and $P_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is [absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam) over the same beam trajectory.

This quantity excludes power already transferred to plasma particles; deposited power is represented by absorbed-power quantities, including species-resolved forms such as [electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam). The more general wave-beam power concept is [power_of_wave_beam](name:power_of_wave_beam).

sources.parent_definition: Set of rays/beams describing the wave propagation

sources.enhanced_context: Initial power carried by a ray or beam at the start of the beam tracing calculation. Used to normalize power flow along the ray or beam trajectory in RF wave propagation codes such as TORBEAM or GRAY.
sources.leaf_definition: Initial power in the ray/beam

NAMES.name: absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.short: Absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total electromagnetic wave power transferred from one coherent beam to the plasma along its trajectory.
NAMES.long:
Absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total electromagnetic wave power transferred from a single coherent beam to plasma particles along the beam trajectory. It is summed over the contributing plasma species and is distinct from the residual wave power represented by [power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:power_of_beam_tracing_beam).

Under the single-beam power balance, the absorbed power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs}} = P_0 - P_{\mathrm{res}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is this absorbed power, $P_0$ is the [initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam), and $P_{\mathrm{res}}$ is the residual power of the same beam at the trajectory endpoint. The total includes contributions represented by species-resolved quantities such as [electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam) and [ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam). It excludes power remaining in the wave and power assigned at launch but not transferred along the traced trajectory.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Wave power absorbed by ions of a specified charge state from a single coherent beam-tracing beam, giving the charge-state-resolved ion contribution to total path-integrated wave energy deposition for that beam.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total wave power transferred from a single traced coherent electromagnetic beam to the ionic population in a specified charge state over its computed propagation path. It is the charge-state-resolved ion contribution to the species-summed [absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam), complementing the electron channel provided by [electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam).

For a ray arc length $s$ increasing along the direction of wave propagation, the absorbed power for ion charge state $z$ is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs},z} = \int_{s_0}^{s_{\mathrm{end}}} 2\kappa_{i,z}(s)\,P(s)\,ds
$$

where $\kappa_{i,z}(s)$ is the spatial amplitude-damping coefficient for the specified ion charge state in m$^{-1}$, $P(s)$ is the remaining beam power in W at arc-length position $s$ in m, and $s_0$ and $s_{\mathrm{end}}$ are the start and end arc-length positions. The factor of 2 converts amplitude-damping to power-damping because wave power is proportional to squared wave-field amplitude, consistent with the parent formulation.

Summing over all charge states of all ion species and adding the electron contribution recovers [absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam) for that beam. The residual [power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:power_of_beam_tracing_beam) at the beam end equals the entering power minus the sum of all species- and charge-state-resolved absorbed powers.

NAMES.name: power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Radio-frequency power associated with ion-cyclotron heating antenna systems, covering incident, reflected, net launched, and antenna-summed contributions.
NAMES.long:
The quantity denotes radio-frequency wave power associated with an ion-cyclotron resonance heating antenna at the antenna reference plane. Depending on the specific quantity, it represents incident power traveling toward the antenna, reflected power returning toward the generator, net launched power, or an aggregate over antennas; it is distinct from power absorbed by the plasma.

For a single antenna and an antenna set, the net and total launched powers are related by

$$
P_{\mathrm{net}} = P_{\mathrm{fwd}} - P_{\mathrm{ref}}, \qquad P_{\mathrm{total}} = \sum_{a=1}^{N_{\mathrm{ant}}} P_{\mathrm{net},a}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is forward incident power, $P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is reflected power, $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is net launched power, $P_{\mathrm{net},a}$ is the net power from antenna $a$, and $N_{\mathrm{ant}}$ is the number of antennas. The [forward power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and [reflected power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) are directional components, while [total antenna power](name:total_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is the antenna sum. Launched power is not the absorbed heating power represented by [total power due to ion-cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating).

NAMES.name: forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Forward radio-frequency power traveling from the generator toward a single ion-cyclotron heating antenna at the antenna reference plane.
NAMES.long:
Forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the forward-traveling radio-frequency wave power at a defined reference plane on the feed line, directed toward the antenna. It is the incident component of the antenna-associated power represented by [power of ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), before accounting for power returning toward the generator.

For an antenna, the net launched power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{net}} = P_{\mathrm{fwd}} - P_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is forward power, $P_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is [reflected power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) traveling toward the generator, and $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is net power launched through the antenna. Forward power is distinct from net launched power and from power absorbed by the plasma; it is not reduced by reflection.

NAMES.name: power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Generic RF power at a single lower-hybrid antenna, encompassing the forward, reflected, and launched power components that collectively characterize the wave-power budget at the antenna interface.
NAMES.long:
RF power at a lower hybrid antenna encompasses the distinct power quantities that characterize the wave-power budget at the antenna interface, where RF energy carried by a transmission line is coupled into a phased waveguide array facing the plasma.

The three principal per-antenna power quantities are related by:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the [forward power](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) (incident RF power arriving at the antenna input reference plane), $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the [reflected power](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) (the fraction returning toward the transmission line due to impedance mismatch between the waveguide array and the plasma load), and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the [launched power](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) (the net power entering the vacuum vessel). Directional couplers installed on the transmission line simultaneously measure both forward and reflected power, from which launched power is derived. System-level aggregates — [total_launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and total_absorbed_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna — sum these per-antenna values over the full lower hybrid system and quantify, respectively, the total injected and deposited power.

NAMES.name: forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Forward power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the incident RF power traveling from the transmission line toward the antenna input reference plane.
NAMES.long:
Forward power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative RF power propagating toward the antenna input reference plane from the transmission line. It is one per-antenna component of the wave-power budget represented by [power of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

The per-antenna power components satisfy:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the incident power arriving at the reference plane, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the power returning toward the transmission line, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net power entering the vacuum vessel. Thus, forward power includes the portion subsequently reflected and is distinct from [reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and [launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). The quantity applies to one antenna and is not an aggregate over multiple antennas.

sources.enhanced_context: Forward power arriving at the back of a Lower Hybrid (LH) antenna. Measures the incident RF power delivered to the antenna structure before coupling into the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Forward power arriving at the back of the antenna

NAMES.name: launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Net RF power entering the vacuum vessel from one lower-hybrid antenna after reflected power is subtracted from incident forward power.
NAMES.long:
Launched power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative net RF power entering the vacuum vessel at the antenna interface. It is the per-antenna component of the wave-power budget represented by [power of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

The launched power is defined by:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the incident RF power propagating toward the antenna input reference plane and $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the RF power returning toward the transmission line from that plane. The resulting quantity is distinct from [forward power of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and is not summed over multiple antennas.

NAMES.name: power_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Power delivered by a single neutral beam injector at the vacuum vessel boundary, evaluated before plasma absorption, shine-through, and fast-ion orbit-loss corrections.
NAMES.long:
Power delivered by a single neutral beam injector at the vacuum vessel boundary is the launched kinetic power carried by neutral beam particles from that injector as they enter the vessel. It is a non-negative per-injector scalar defined before subsequent interaction of the beam with the plasma.

The kinetic-power flux crossing the vessel-entry surface defines the quantity as:

$$
P_j = \sum_\alpha \int_{S_j} \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_j>0} \frac{1}{2} m_\alpha |\mathbf{v}|^2 (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_j) f_{\alpha j}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\, d^3v\, dA
$$

where $P_j$ is the launched power of injector $j$, $S_j$ is the surface through which that injector's neutrals enter the vessel, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_j$ is the unit normal directed into the vessel, $\alpha$ indexes neutral particle species, $m_\alpha$ is particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is position on $S_j$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $t$ is time, $f_{\alpha j}$ is the neutral-particle distribution function, $dA$ is the surface element, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space element. The restriction $\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_j>0$ selects particles crossing into the vessel.

This quantity includes all neutral energy components delivered by the specified injector at the vessel boundary. The sum over injectors gives [total_power_of_neutral_beam_injector](name:total_power_of_neutral_beam_injector), and it differs from [absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector](name:absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector), which is evaluated after plasma absorption and loss processes are applied. It excludes source electrical input, power stopped upstream of the vessel boundary, and later corrections for ionization, shine-through, charge-exchange losses, fast-ion orbit losses, or other plasma-interaction effects.

sources.enhanced_context: NBI power coupled to the plasma by this unit (Pnbi), excluding shine-through and fast ion orbit losses. Represents the effective heating power delivered to the thermal plasma by neutral beam injection.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: NBI power coupled to the plasma by this unit (i.e. without shine-through and fast ion losses)

sources.enhanced_context: Neutral beam injection (NBI) power launched into the vacuum vessel from a given NBI unit. Represents the beam power delivered to the plasma vessel before accounting for shine-through or orbit losses.

NAMES.name: absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Power absorbed by the plasma from a single neutral beam injector after subtracting neutral-beam shine-through and fast-ion first-orbit losses from the launched injector power.
NAMES.long:
Power absorbed by the plasma from a single neutral beam injector is the portion of its launched neutral-beam kinetic power deposited through interaction with the plasma. It is a non-negative per-injector quantity, distinct from the boundary-delivered [power of the neutral beam injector](name:power_of_neutral_beam_injector), which is defined before absorption and loss corrections.

The absorbed power is defined by:

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs},j}=P_j-P_{\mathrm{ST},j}-P_{\mathrm{FO},j}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs},j}$ is the absorbed power for injector $j$, $P_j$ is its launched power at the vessel boundary, $P_{\mathrm{ST},j}$ is the [neutral-beam shine-through power](name:power_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough), and $P_{\mathrm{FO},j}$ is the power carried away by fast ions lost on their first orbit.

This quantity excludes source electrical input, losses upstream of the vessel boundary, residual shine-through, and fast-ion first-orbit losses. The all-injector launched aggregate is [total power of neutral beam injectors](name:total_power_of_neutral_beam_injector), whereas this quantity applies the plasma-interaction corrections to one injector.

NAMES.name: power_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short: Power of a wave beam is the cycle-averaged electromagnetic energy-flow rate of a coherent RF or microwave beam at a specified propagation or interaction stage.
NAMES.long:
Power of a wave beam is the cycle-averaged electromagnetic energy-flow rate of a coherent RF or microwave beam at a specified propagation or interaction stage. A carried-power instance is evaluated through an oriented beam cross-section whose positive normal is the local propagation direction; a transferred-power instance is the rate at which the beam loses energy to another physical system.

For harmonic fields represented by peak-amplitude phasors, the carried and transferred forms are defined by

$$
P_\mathrm{wave\,beam} =
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \int_A \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{H}^*\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,dA, & \text{carried through } A,\\[1ex]
\displaystyle P_\mathrm{in}-P_\mathrm{out}, & \text{transferred from the beam over an interaction region}
\end{cases}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{wave\,beam}$ is the wave-beam power, $A$ is the beam cross-section, $\mathbf{E}$ is the complex electric-field phasor, $\mathbf{H}^*$ is the complex conjugate of the complex magnetic-field-strength phasor, $\operatorname{Re}$ takes the real part, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ defines the positive oriented area element $d\mathbf{A}=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,dA$. $P_\mathrm{in}$ and $P_\mathrm{out}$ are carried wave-beam powers at the entry and exit of the interaction region, with both surfaces oriented along local beam propagation. The factor $1/2$ applies to peak-amplitude phasors; for rms phasors the cycle-averaged Poynting vector is formed without that factor.

The time integral over an interval is [wave-beam energy](name:wave_beam_energy). [Power of a beam-tracing beam](name:power_of_beam_tracing_beam) is the traced-beam specialization, with [initial power of a beam-tracing beam](name:initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam) its value at the initial tracing surface. A staged quantity such as [launched power of a wave beam](name:launched_power_of_wave_beam) identifies a particular power-flow location, while absorbed or species-resolved deposition, such as [absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam), [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power), or [electron absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam), is distinct from remaining carried power.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net cycle-averaged electromagnetic energy flux is in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ for carried power, or when $P_\mathrm{in}>P_\mathrm{out}$ for transferred power.

NAMES.name: launched_power_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short: Net RF or microwave power carried by one wave beam across the vacuum-vessel entry plane after transmission and returned-power losses.
NAMES.long:
Launched power is the net cycle-averaged electromagnetic power crossing the vacuum-vessel entry plane in the propagation direction of one coherent RF or microwave beam.

At the launch reference plane, it is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{launch}} = P_{\mathrm{forward}} - P_{\mathrm{return}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{forward}}$ is the forward beam power after transmission losses, and $P_{\mathrm{return}}$ is the power propagating back toward the launcher at that plane; both are cycle-averaged powers in W.

This quantity is a stage-specific form of [power of a wave beam](name:power_of_wave_beam). It excludes generator or source power, load power, and power subsequently absorbed by the plasma; therefore, it is distinct from plasma-absorbed power.
