NAMES.name: pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Pressure of an ion cyclotron heating antenna is the scalar absolute pressure of fluids contained in antenna-associated volumes or the nonnegative compressive normal pressure transmitted at antenna hardware interfaces. It excludes tensile normal stress, shear stress, and pressures not physically localized to the antenna assembly.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of an ion cyclotron heating antenna is the scalar normal pressure associated with material media contained within the antenna assembly or with compressive contact at antenna hardware interfaces. For a gas or liquid it denotes the absolute thermodynamic pressure of that medium; for a solid contact it denotes the nonnegative compressive part of the normal traction transmitted across the contact.

The common mechanical definition is the area-averaged compressive normal traction:

$$
p = \frac{1}{A}\int_A \max\!\left[-\mathbf{t}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}},\,0\right] \, dA
$$

where $p$ is this pressure, $A$ is the surface area over which it is defined, $\mathbf{t}=\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the traction vector acting on a surface with unit normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, and $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the Cauchy stress tensor of the medium or contacting body. For a static isotropic fluid, the compressive normal traction is independent of surface orientation, so this scalar equals the absolute thermodynamic pressure.

The locus is restricted to media volumes and mechanical interfaces that are part of, or mechanically intrinsic to, the ion cyclotron heating antenna assembly, including contained gas, contained liquid, seals, windows, supports, and current-carrying component contacts when the scalar represents their normal load. It excludes plasma pressure, vessel pressure not attributable to the antenna assembly, tensile normal stress, shear traction, and signed components of a stress tensor. The related [gas pressure of an ion cyclotron heating antenna](name:gas_pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is the subset restricted to neutral-gas thermodynamic pressure and excludes liquid-coolant and solid-contact pressure.

sources.enhanced_context: Amplitude of a pressure measurement on an ion cyclotron (IC) antenna module. Stores time-resolved pressure data for monitoring mechanical or gas pressure conditions at a specific sensor location on the module.
sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of pressure measurements

NAMES.name: gas_pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Absolute thermodynamic pressure of gas within or associated with an ion cyclotron heating antenna, excluding mechanical contact pressure in solid hardware.
NAMES.long:
The gas pressure of an ion cyclotron heating antenna is the absolute thermodynamic pressure of the neutral gas occupying an antenna volume or gas boundary. It is the gas-phase component of [pressure of an ion cyclotron heating antenna](name:pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), not a structural or contact load.

For a dilute gas in local thermodynamic equilibrium, the pressure is related to its state by

$$
p = n k_B T
$$

where $p$ is the gas pressure, $n$ is the neutral-gas number density, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, and $T$ is the thermodynamic temperature. For a nonideal gas, $p$ retains its thermodynamic meaning and is determined by the appropriate equation of state.

The quantity excludes pressure exerted by solid hardware interfaces and mechanical contact forces; zero corresponds to perfect vacuum.

sources.enhanced_context: Amplitude of a pressure measurement on an ion cyclotron (IC) antenna module. Stores time-resolved pressure data for monitoring mechanical or gas pressure conditions at a specific sensor location on the module.
sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of pressure measurements

NAMES.name: pressure_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Pressure of a lower-hybrid antenna is the scalar compressive stress associated with the antenna or a medium contained by its antenna volume. It includes thermodynamic gas or fluid pressure and mechanical contact pressure acting on antenna surfaces or structures, defined as an absolute, nonnegative quantity.
NAMES.long:
Pressure of a lower-hybrid antenna is the scalar compressive stress associated with the antenna or a medium contained by its antenna volume. It includes the thermodynamic pressure of gas or fluid within the antenna enclosure and the compressive normal contact pressure exerted on antenna surfaces or structural interfaces. The quantity is absolute and nonnegative: fluid pressure is referenced to ideal vacuum, and mechanical pressure denotes compressive normal stress only.

As a scalar reduction of the mechanical state, the pressure is the compressive isotropic part of the Cauchy stress tensor:

$$
p = -\frac{1}{3}\,\mathrm{tr}\,\boldsymbol{\sigma}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the Cauchy stress tensor of the medium or interface under consideration, with the convention that tensile normal stress is positive in $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ so that compression yields $p > 0$. For an isotropic fluid at rest this reduces to the absolute thermodynamic pressure of the fluid.

The quantity is restricted to pressure physically localized to the lower-hybrid antenna assembly and the media it contains or contacts. It excludes tensile normal stress, shear stress, and any pressure not physically localized to the antenna assembly, such as bulk plasma pressure or pressures in remote transmission-line or pumping systems. It is broader than a gas-only antenna pressure, which is restricted to the neutral-gas thermodynamic pressure of the antenna vacuum volume; the analogous quantities for ion-cyclotron systems are [pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna](name:pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and [gas_pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna](name:gas_pressure_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna).

sources.enhanced_context: Gas pressure inside the vacuum tank of a lower hybrid (LH) antenna. Monitors the vacuum condition of the antenna waveguide system, relevant for antenna conditioning and operational safety.
sources.leaf_definition: Pressure in the vacuum tank of the antenna
sources.parent_definition: Set of Lower Hybrid antennas

NAMES.name: radial_centroid_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: Major radius coordinate of the geometric center of an electron cyclotron launcher mirror, measured from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial centroid of an electron cyclotron launcher mirror is the perpendicular distance $R$ of the mirror's geometric center from the machine toroidal symmetry axis, defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is the major radius in meters. Together with [vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), it fully locates the mirror center in the meridional plane, establishing the geometric reference point from which EC beam injection angles and trajectories are computed.

The centroid position in the machine frame combines with the mirror rotation [angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and any mechanical offset_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror to define the complete launch geometry used in ray-tracing and beam-tracing models for electron cyclotron heating and current drive. The local boundary contour of the mirror surface is described separately in the mirror-fixed planar frame via x1_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror and x2_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the mirror centroid lies at a finite major radius from the toroidal symmetry axis ($R > 0$), which holds for all physical in-vessel launcher positions.

sources.enhanced_context: Major radius (R) coordinate of centre.
sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the object. This origin is located within the object area and should be the middle point of the object surface. If geometry_type=2, it's the centre of the circular object. If geometry_type=3, it's the centre of the rectangular object.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row
NAMES.short: The radial coordinate is the major-radius coordinate of the lower-hybrid antenna-row geometric reference point: its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate of a lower-hybrid antenna row is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of the row geometric reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The coordinate $R$ is the perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

When the same reference point is represented by Cartesian coordinates $(x, y, z)$ in a right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and origin on the toroidal symmetry axis, the major radius is

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates of the row reference point and $R$ is measured in meters.

This quantity is a position coordinate of the antenna-row reference point, not a local coordinate normal to the antenna mouth and not a plasma or wave-launching parameter. It should refer to the same geometric reference point as toroidal_angle_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row and [vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row).

sources.enhanced_context: Radial distance from the antenna mouth along the grid used for the electron density profile in front of the lower hybrid (LH) antenna. The coordinate origin is at the antenna mouth, increasing toward the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Radial distance to the antenna mouth (grid for the electron density profile). 0 at antenna mouth, increasing towards the plasma
sources.parent_definition: Set of Lower Hybrid antennas

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate R of the declared reference position of a neutral beam injector in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The major-radius coordinate locates the declared reference position of a neutral beam injector by its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.

$$
R_{\rm ref}=\sqrt{x_{\rm ref}^{2}+y_{\rm ref}^{2}}
$$

where $R_{\rm ref}$ is the major-radius coordinate and $x_{\rm ref}$ and $y_{\rm ref}$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates of the reference position in the right-handed $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this is the $R$ coordinate. Together with the [vertical coordinate of the neutral beam injector](name:vertical_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector), it locates the reference position in the horizontal-vertical plane.

sources.enhanced_context: Major radius (R) coordinate of position.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Major radius

NAMES.name: radial_normalized_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.short: Radial direction cosine of the electromagnetic wave vector along a beam-tracing ray, equal to the radial component k_R divided by the total wave-vector magnitude |k|.
NAMES.long:
The radial normalized wave vector is the direction cosine of the local wave vector projected onto the major-radius direction $\hat{R}$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, evaluated at each point along the beam or ray path in beam-tracing calculations. It encodes what fraction of the instantaneous wave propagation direction is oriented radially — outward from or inward toward the machine symmetry axis.

The quantity is defined as:

$$
k_{R,\text{norm}} = \frac{k_R}{|\mathbf{k}|}
$$

where $k_R$ is the [radial wave-vector component](name:radial_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam) and $|\mathbf{k}|$ is the total wave-vector magnitude. Together with the [toroidal normalized wave vector](name:toroidal_normalized_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam) and the [vertical normalized wave vector](name:vertical_normalized_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam), this component forms a unit direction vector satisfying $k_{R,\text{norm}}^2 + k_{\phi,\text{norm}}^2 + k_{Z,\text{norm}}^2 = 1$.

In beam-tracing or ray-tracing simulations for RF heating, the normalized wave-vector components track the instantaneous wave propagation direction as the ray refracts through an inhomogeneous magnetized plasma. Values are dimensionless and bounded to the interval $[-1, 1]$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $k_R$ points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$, away from the machine symmetry axis.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalized radial component of the wave vector (k_r/|k|) along the beam or ray path in beam tracing calculations. Represents the fraction of the total wave vector directed along the major radius direction.
sources.leaf_definition: Normalized wave vector component in the major radius direction = k_r / norm(k)
sources.parent_definition: Wave vector of the ray/beam along its path

NAMES.name: radial_offset_of_beamlet_group
NAMES.short: Signed major-radius displacement of a beamlet-group center from its nominal position, measured along the radial direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed radial displacement of a beamlet-group center from its nominal static position during a position variation. It describes only the major-radius component of the group's displacement, not the complete position vector or the injector's own reference position.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, the offset is defined by:

$$
\Delta R_{\mathrm{bg}} = R_{\mathrm{bg}} - R_{\mathrm{bg},0}
$$

Here $R_{\mathrm{bg}}$ is the beamlet-group center's major-radius coordinate and $R_{\mathrm{bg},0}$ is its nominal static reference coordinate; $R$ is measured from the machine symmetry axis and increases outward.

For dynamic beam tilting, the offset describes the group's positional variation and is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the neutral beam injector](name:radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector), which refers to the injector reference position. Related angular variation is described by the [perturbed beam tilt angle of the neutral beam injector](name:perturbed_beam_tilt_angle_of_neutral_beam_injector).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the beamlet-group center lies at larger major radius than its nominal reference position.

sources.enhanced_context: Major radius (R) coordinate of delta position.
sources.leaf_definition: Major radius
sources.parent_definition: Variation of the position of the beamlet group centre

NAMES.name: radius_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the strap conductor axis to a circular cylindrical boundary of its annular cross-section. The unqualified parent covers either boundary; inner and outer radii are the boundary-specific quantities.
NAMES.long:
Radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the strap conductor axis to a circular cylindrical boundary of its annular cross-section. The unqualified quantity identifies the common boundary-radius concept without selecting the inner or outer surface.

Use [inner radius of antenna strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap) and [outer radius of antenna strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap) when the selected annular boundary is part of the meaning; if $r_\mathrm{in}$ and $r_\mathrm{out}$ denote those two boundary radii, then $0 \le r_\mathrm{in} \le r_\mathrm{out}$. This quantity is distinct from [height of antenna strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), [toroidal width of antenna strap](name:toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap), and the major-radius coordinate $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: inner_radius_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Inner radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the strap conductor axis to the inner cylindrical boundary of its annular cross-section.
NAMES.long:
Inner radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the strap conductor axis to the inner cylindrical boundary of its annular cross-section. It identifies the inner boundary of the conductor material and is the smaller of the two annular boundary radii.

Use [radius of antenna strap](name:radius_of_antenna_strap) for the boundary-radius concept without selecting a surface, and [outer radius of antenna strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap) for the larger boundary radius. If $r_\mathrm{in}$ and $r_\mathrm{out}$ denote the inner and outer radii, respectively, then $0 \le r_\mathrm{in} \le r_\mathrm{out}$. This quantity is distinct from the [height of antenna strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), [toroidal width of antenna strap](name:toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap), and [thickness of antenna strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap).

sources.enhanced_context: Inner radius of the annular cross-section of an ICRH antenna strap element. Defines the inner boundary of the annular strap geometry used in ion cyclotron resonance heating antenna modelling.
sources.leaf_definition: Inner radius
sources.parent_definition: The element is an annulus of  center r, z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

NAMES.name: outer_radius_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Outer radial boundary of the annular cross-section of an ICRH antenna strap conductor, defining the larger of the two radii that bound the conductor annulus.
NAMES.long:
The outer radius of an ICRH antenna strap is the radial distance from the central axis of the strap conductor to the outer cylindrical surface of the annular cross-section. It marks the external boundary of the conductor material and, together with the [inner radius](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap), fully specifies the radial extent of the annular conductor.

For an annular cross-section, the radial conductor wall thickness follows $\Delta r = r_\mathrm{out} - r_\mathrm{in}$, where $r_\mathrm{out}$ is the outer radius and $r_\mathrm{in}$ is the inner radius. The nominal centerline radius reported by [radius_of_antenna_strap](name:radius_of_antenna_strap) is the mean $(r_\mathrm{out} + r_\mathrm{in})/2$.

This geometric parameter enters electromagnetic wave-coupling calculations and RF impedance modeling for ion cyclotron resonance heating systems. Together with the width, [height](name:height_of_antenna_strap), and [thickness](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap) of the conductor, it provides the complete geometric description needed for antenna strap simulations.
NAMES.sign: Positive when measured radially outward from the strap conductor axis.

sources.enhanced_context: Outer radius of the annular cross-section of an ICRH antenna strap element. Together with the inner radius and centre position, defines the annular strap geometry for wave coupling and electromagnetic modelling.
sources.leaf_definition: Outer radius
sources.parent_definition: The element is an annulus of  center r, z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

NAMES.name: reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Reflected RF power of a single ion cyclotron resonance heating antenna traveling backward toward the generator at the antenna reference plane.
NAMES.long:
Reflected power of an ion cyclotron heating antenna is the backward-traveling RF power at a defined reference plane on the feed line, directed from the antenna toward the generator. It is the component subtracted from forward power to obtain the net power launched through the antenna aperture.

The reflected power is related to the net launched power by:

$$
P_\mathrm{reflected} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{launched}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the incident traveling-wave power represented by [forward power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net power represented by [power of the ion cyclotron heating antenna](name:power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), with both quantities evaluated at the same reference plane.

This quantity describes returned RF power and is not plasma-absorbed power or net launched power.

sources.enhanced_context: Reflected RF power at an ICRH antenna module, i.e. the power travelling back from the antenna toward the transmission line source. A key quantity for assessing coupling efficiency and antenna matching.
sources.leaf_definition: Reflected power
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

sources.enhanced_context: Reflected power from an ion cyclotron (IC) antenna, representing the fraction of forward power not coupled into the plasma. Used to assess ICRH antenna-plasma coupling efficiency alongside forward and launched power measurements.
sources.leaf_definition: Reflected power
sources.parent_definition: Set of Ion Cyclotron antennas

NAMES.name: reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative RF power returning from the antenna input reference plane toward the transmission line because of incomplete coupling to the plasma load.
NAMES.long:
Reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna is the nonnegative RF power propagating from the antenna input reference plane back toward the transmission line because of incomplete coupling to the antenna-plasma load. It is one per-antenna component of the RF power budget, distinct from [forward power](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) and [launched power](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

For a single antenna, the net launched power is defined by:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the incident power arriving at the antenna input reference plane, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the power returning toward the transmission line, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net power entering the vacuum vessel. The quantity is per antenna and is not a system-wide sum; its role within the complete RF budget is given by [power of a lower-hybrid antenna](name:power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

sources.enhanced_context: Reflected RF power from a lower hybrid (LH) antenna, representing the fraction of forward power not coupled into the plasma. High reflected power indicates poor coupling efficiency and is monitored for antenna coupling optimisation.
sources.leaf_definition: Reflected power
sources.parent_definition: Set of Lower Hybrid antennas

NAMES.name: resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the real part of the effective radio-frequency loading impedance at the antenna feed reference plane. It represents the resistive component associated with power coupled to the plasma and dissipative antenna losses.
NAMES.long:
Resistance of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the real part of the effective radio-frequency loading impedance presented by the antenna at its feed reference plane. It characterizes the component of the antenna load that absorbs radio-frequency power, including plasma loading and intrinsic dissipative losses, distinct from the reactive energy storage represented by antenna capacitance or inductance.

The antenna loading impedance is decomposed into resistive and reactive parts as:

$$
Z_\mathrm{ant} = R_\mathrm{ant} + i X_\mathrm{ant}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{ant}$ is the complex antenna loading impedance, $R_\mathrm{ant}$ is the antenna resistance in ohms, $X_\mathrm{ant}$ is the antenna reactance in ohms, and $i^2=-1$.

For a sinusoidal strap current, the resistive power associated with this load is $P_\mathrm{res}=R_\mathrm{ant} I_\mathrm{rms}^2$, where $P_\mathrm{res}$ is in watts and $I_\mathrm{rms}$ is the [root-mean-square wave current of the antenna strap](name:root_mean_square_of_wave_current_of_antenna_strap) in amperes. This quantity is a feed-plane impedance component and is not itself a forward, reflected, or net power; those powers describe traveling-wave energy flow in the connected radio-frequency circuit.

sources.enhanced_context: Coupling resistance of an ion cyclotron (IC) antenna module, characterizing the resistive part of the antenna loading impedance seen by the transmission line. A key RF coupling efficiency parameter relating launched power to antenna current.
sources.leaf_definition: Coupling resistance
sources.parent_definition: Set of antenna modules (each module is fed by a single transmission line)

NAMES.name: root_mean_square_of_wave_current_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: The root-mean-square wave current of an antenna strap is the non-negative effective value of the radio-frequency current flowing through an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna strap during wave excitation.
NAMES.long:
The root-mean-square wave current of an antenna strap is the effective value of the time-varying radio-frequency current flowing through an antenna strap conductor during wave excitation. It represents the current magnitude associated with RF wave launching and excludes static bias current and non-RF current components.

It is defined over an averaging interval $\tau$ as the square root of the time average of the squared instantaneous RF current:

$$
I_\mathrm{rms} = \left(\frac{1}{\tau}\int_{t_0}^{t_0+\tau} i_\mathrm{RF}^2(t)\,dt\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $i_\mathrm{RF}(t)$ is the instantaneous RF current in amperes, $t$ and $t_0$ are times in seconds, and $\tau$ is the averaging interval in seconds; for a periodic waveform, $\tau$ is an integer number of RF periods, and for a sinusoid with peak current $I_0$, $I_\mathrm{rms}=I_0/\sqrt{2}$.

Because the instantaneous current is squared before averaging, $I_\mathrm{rms}$ is non-negative and contains no phase information. The companion [strap RF phase](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap) is required with this RMS current to specify the complex strap-current excitation.

When the [antenna loading resistance](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) $R_\mathrm{load}$ is the resistive part of the driving-point load associated with the strap current, the accepted RF power at that reference plane satisfies $P_\mathrm{acc}=I_\mathrm{rms}^2 R_\mathrm{load}$; equivalently, it is the [forward RF power](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) less the [reflected RF power](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) at the same reference plane.

sources.enhanced_context: Root mean square (RMS) current flowing along an ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) antenna strap, characterizing the RF current amplitude used to excite the electromagnetic wave field for plasma heating.
sources.leaf_definition: Root mean square current flowing along the strap
sources.parent_definition: Set of IC antenna straps

NAMES.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: Signed coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along its second local tangential axis in its object-local planar frame, measured from the mirror-local origin.
NAMES.long:
Signed coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along its second local tangential axis in its object-local planar frame, measured from the mirror-local origin, is the scalar projection of that point's displacement onto the mirror's second local tangential direction. The mirror-local triad is $(\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1,\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2,\hat{\mathbf{n}})$, where $\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$ is the more-horizontal tangential direction directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height; $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the plasma-facing unit normal; and $\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\times\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$ completes the right-handed triad.

For an outline point with position vector $\mathbf{r}$ and mirror-local origin $\mathbf{r}_0$, the coordinate is defined by

$$
x_2 = \left(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_0\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2
$$

where $x_2$ is the second local tangential coordinate of the outline point.

This coordinate specifies the second in-plane component of the mirror outline and complements the [first local tangential coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror). It is not the cylindrical radial coordinate $R$, toroidal angle $\phi$, or vertical coordinate $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the displacement from the mirror-local origin to the outline point has a component in the direction $\hat{\mathbf{t}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\times\hat{\mathbf{t}}_1$.

sources.enhanced_context: Positions of the EC launcher mirror outline along the x2 axis in the local (X1, X2) coordinate system. Defines the irregular 2D contour of the mirror geometry at its reference position.
sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x2 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the object in the (X1, X2) coordinate system, used only if geometry_type/index=1. Repeat the first point since this is a closed contour

NAMES.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Signed second local-tangential coordinate of a neutral beam injector outline vertex, measured in the injector-local frame and paired with the first coordinate to locate that vertex.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed position of an outline vertex along the neutral beam injector's second local tangential axis. It is paired with the [first local-tangential coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector) to locate the same vertex in the injector-local frame.

The coordinate is defined by:

$$
x_2 = (\mathbf{r}_v-\mathbf{r}_0)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2
$$

where $x_2$ is this coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the vertex position, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the local origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ is the second local tangential unit vector. The local orthonormal basis $(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3)$ is right-handed; $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3$ is the plasma-facing normal, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The coordinate applies to outline vertices associated with the neutral beam injector and is distinct from the first local-tangential coordinate and from global cylindrical coordinates.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the vertex displacement has a positive projection along $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3\times\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ from the local origin.

sources.enhanced_context: Positions of the NBI ion source outline vertices along the x2 axis of the local (X1, X2) coordinate system. Defines the irregular geometry of the beam extraction surface in the x2 direction.
sources.leaf_definition: Positions along x2 axis
sources.parent_definition: Irregular outline of the detector/aperture in the (X1, X2) coordinate system

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the plasma-volume integral of the local coherent-wave power deposition density into the bulk thermal electron population. It is the thermal-electron component of [electron absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power), rather than the total absorbed power across all plasma channels.

The defining volume integral is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal electron power density](name:thermal_electron_power_density), $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is differential volume.

The integral includes only power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons and excludes deposition into fast electrons, ions, and other channels. Unlike [thermal electron power at inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it covers the complete plasma volume rather than a specified enclosed region.

sources.enhanced_context: Global wave power absorbed by the thermal (bulk) electron population from a coherent wave. Represents the total heating power deposited into thermal electrons by the wave, excluding fast particle absorption.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Toroidal-Fourier-mode contribution to coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population, excluding fast-electron and non-electron absorption.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the power transferred from a coherent electromagnetic wave to the bulk thermal electron population, resolved into a single toroidal Fourier mode. Summed over all toroidal modes, it gives the volume-integrated [thermal electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power), while excluding the fast-electron contribution represented by [per toroidal mode fast electron absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

The modal contributions satisfy

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{abs}} = \sum_{n_\phi} P_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{abs}}(n_\phi)
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by thermal electrons, $P_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{abs}}(n_\phi)$ is its contribution for toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, and the sum uses the adopted modal normalization. The quantity concerns bulk thermal electrons only; absorption by fast electrons, ions, or other channels is excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Wave power absorbed by the thermal electron population, resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Gives the mode-number spectrum of thermal electron heating from a coherent wave.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative absorbed wave power on thermal electrons inside a flux surface (volume-integrated power density), resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Captures the radial deposition profile contribution from each toroidal harmonic for thermal electron heating.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density), per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Cumulative wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron power at an inside flux surface quantifies the total rate at which coherent wave energy is absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population within the plasma volume bounded by a given magnetic flux surface. It is the thermal-electron contribution to [electron power at an inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), distinct from the suprathermal contribution [fast electron power at an inside flux surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

The quantity is obtained by integrating the flux-surface-averaged thermal-electron power density $p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}$ over the enclosed plasma volume:

$$
P_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho) = \int_0^\rho p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho') \frac{dV}{d\rho'} \, d\rho'
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho)$ is the cumulative absorbed power, $\rho$ labels the limiting magnetic flux surface, $\rho'$ is the integration variable, $p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}$ is the local thermal-electron absorbed power density, and $dV/d\rho'$ is the differential enclosed volume per unit flux-surface label. Only absorption by bulk thermal electrons is included; fast-electron and ion absorption, launched power, and absorption outside the enclosed volume are excluded. At the outermost closed flux surface, it gives the total wave power absorbed by thermal electrons.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal (Maxwellian) ion population, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The thermal ion absorbed wave power is the volume-integrated power delivered by coherent electromagnetic waves to the bulk thermal (approximately Maxwellian) ion population via wave-particle resonance interactions. It is the thermal-ion component of [ion_absorbed_wave_power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power), which spans all ion populations.

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,i}} = \int_{V} p_{\mathrm{th,i}}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th,i}}$ is the local wave power density absorbed by thermal ions and $V$ is the total plasma volume. The associated spatial deposition profile is described by [thermal_ion_power_density](name:thermal_ion_power_density).

This quantity excludes power deposited into suprathermal (fast) ions. No ion-species qualifier is carried: it aggregates over all thermal ion species present in the plasma. Charge-state-resolved contributions are provided by [thermal_ion_charge_state_power](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power); summing over all charge states and species recovers this global value.

sources.enhanced_context: Total RF wave power absorbed by the thermal (bulk) ion population of a given species from a coherent wave. Represents the heating power deposited into the Maxwellian ion distribution, distinct from fast-ion absorption.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal-mode-resolved contribution to coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal ion population, retaining the cumulative power associated with each mode.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal Fourier-mode contribution to [thermal ion absorbed wave power](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power), representing coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred to the bulk thermal ion population. It is volume-integrated over the same physical domain as the parent quantity and summed over all thermal-ion charge states.

$$
P_{\mathrm{th\,ion}}(n_\phi)=\int_V q_{\mathrm{abs,th\,ion}}(n_\phi,\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th\,ion}}(n_\phi)$ is the absorbed power for toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, $q_{\mathrm{abs,th\,ion}}$ is the corresponding local absorbed-wave power density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $dV$ is the volume element, and $V$ is the integration volume. Under the adopted Fourier normalization, summing modal contributions over toroidal mode number recovers the parent power. Unlike [per-toroidal-mode thermal-ion power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_power_density), this quantity is volume-integrated; unlike [per-toroidal-mode thermal-ion charge-state power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power), it is not resolved by charge state.

sources.enhanced_context: Wave power absorbed by the thermal ion population resolved per toroidal mode number (n_phi). Captures the RF heating power deposition spectrum over toroidal Fourier harmonics for thermal ions in coherent wave interactions.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population per toroidal mode number
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Power transferred from a coherent electromagnetic wave to the bulk thermal ions of a specified charge state, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated power absorbed by the bulk thermal ion population in a specified charge state from a coherent electromagnetic wave. It is the thermal component of ion charge-state power and excludes nonthermal ions and collisional energy exchange between plasma populations.

The total absorbed power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{th},q} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs},\mathrm{th},q}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th},q}$ is the thermal-ion power for charge state $q$, $p_{\mathrm{abs},\mathrm{th},q}$ is the corresponding local coherent-wave power-transfer density, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. The total includes all toroidal Fourier modes; [per-toroidal-mode thermal ion charge-state power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power) resolves the same quantity by mode. It contributes to the broader [ion absorbed wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power) and is a charge-state-resolved component of ion charge-state power.

sources.enhanced_context: Total wave power absorbed by the thermal ion population for a specific ion charge state, integrated over all toroidal mode numbers. Quantifies the net thermal ion heating from wave-particle interaction for this species state.
sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Power transferred from a coherent electromagnetic wave to bulk thermal ions of a specified charge state, resolved per toroidal Fourier mode number.
NAMES.long:
The quantity $P_{n,\mathrm{th},Z}$ is the wave power absorbed by thermal bulk ions of a specified charge state $Z$, attributed to toroidal Fourier harmonic $n$ of the coherent driving wave field. It is the toroidal-mode-resolved component of [thermal_ion_charge_state_power](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power); summing over all resolved toroidal mode numbers $n$ recovers the charge-state-resolved total:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th},Z} = \sum_{n} P_{n,\mathrm{th},Z}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th},Z}$ is the volume-integrated absorbed power for the specified charge state over all modes. The quantity is charge-state-resolved rather than summed over all states of the ion species, in contrast to [per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power), which aggregates over all thermal ion charge states. For the analogous quantity in the fast, non-thermal ion population, see [per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power).

sources.leaf_definition: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population per toroidal mode number

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified thermal ion charge state within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified thermal ion charge state within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface. It is the portion of wave power transferred to thermal ions in that charge state, accumulated over the volume inside the chosen surface.

The cumulative power is defined by integrating the local absorbed-wave-power density for that thermal ion charge state over the enclosed plasma volume:

$$
P_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\lambda) = \int_{V(\lambda)} p_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\lambda)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power for thermal ion charge state $q$ inside the magnetic flux surface labeled by $\lambda$, $p_q^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local absorbed-wave-power density for that thermal ion charge state, and $V(\lambda)$ is the plasma volume enclosed by that magnetic flux surface.

This quantity is charge-state resolved and includes only absorption by the thermal ion population; it excludes absorption by electrons, fast or non-thermal ions, neutrals, and non-wave power exchange. Because power is extensive, the sum over all thermal-ion charge states gives [thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface). It is the thermal-population contribution to [ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface); the corresponding fast-ion contribution is [fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative absorbed wave power on thermal ion species inside a flux surface, obtained by volume integration of the absorbed power density from the magnetic axis outward. Provides the radial profile of total wave power deposited on thermal ions.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Cumulative wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal ion population within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The thermal-ion power at inside flux surface is the running volume integral of wave power deposited into the bulk thermal ion population, giving the radial distribution of enclosed thermal-ion wave absorption. It is the bulk-ion component of [ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), separated from both fast-ion and electron heating channels.

The quantity is the volume integral of the thermal-ion wave-power density $p_{\mathrm{th},i}(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\chi)$ enclosed by the flux surface labeled $\chi$:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th},i}(\chi) = \int_{V(\chi)} p_{\mathrm{th},i}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the thermal-ion volumetric wave-power density in W m$^{-3}$, $dV$ is the volume element in m$^3$, $P_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the enclosed thermal-ion wave power in W, and $\chi$ is the chosen flux-surface label, such as the normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$.

This quantity includes only wave energy absorbed by bulk thermal ions inside the selected closed magnetic flux surface. Wave energy absorbed by thermal electrons is [thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), wave energy absorbed by suprathermal ions is [fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), and the sum over thermal and fast ion populations is [ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

sources.enhanced_context: Absorbed wave power on thermal ion species inside a flux surface, computed as the cumulative volume integral of the thermal ion power absorption density. Represents total RF heating deposited within a given radial location for thermal ions.
sources.leaf_definition: Absorbed wave power on thermal species inside a flux surface (cumulative volume integral of the absorbed power density)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species

NAMES.name: thickness_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Thickness of an ICRH antenna strap is the full, non-negative depth of the strap conductor cross-section, measured along the local normal to its broad plasma-facing surface. It is a length distinct from the in-plane strap width, height, or length.
NAMES.long:
Thickness of an ICRH antenna strap is the geometric extent of the strap conductor in the direction normal to its broad plasma-facing surface. It is a full separation distance across the conductor cross-section, so it is non-negative and is not an oriented displacement.

For a conductor cross-section $C$ and a dimensionless unit normal vector $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ to the broad plasma-facing surface, the thickness $t$ may be defined by the range of projected positions:

$$
t = \max_{\mathbf{r}\in C}\left(\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right) - \min_{\mathbf{r}\in C}\left(\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right)
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is a position vector with components of length, so each projection $\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ has units of meters. This definition is independent of the arbitrary origin used for $\mathbf{r}$ and returns the complete non-negative depth of the conductor along the local normal direction.

In antenna geometry models, the thickness is taken from the physical strap design or from a simplified cross-section used for electromagnetic and engineering calculations. It helps determine conductor volume, surface placement, self-inductance, resistance, thermal capacity, and the geometric clearance between the strap and neighboring antenna structures. It complements in-plane dimensions such as width_of_antenna_strap, [height_of_antenna_strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), and length_of_antenna_strap.

For order-of-magnitude checks, ICRH strap thicknesses are usually millimeter-to-centimeter engineering dimensions, roughly 0.001-0.1 m, but the appropriate value is design-specific and the standard name imposes no universal numerical bounds.

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular coordinate locating points of an antenna strap around the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal angle of an antenna strap is the azimuthal coordinate of a point defining the strap geometry about the machine symmetry axis. It locates the strap around the torus and is distinct from the cross-sectional inclination [angle of the antenna strap](name:angle_of_antenna_strap).

For Cartesian coordinates $x$ and $y$ in meters in the right-handed $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ vertical, the toroidal angle is defined by

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(y,x)
$$

where $\phi$ is measured from the facility-defined zero-angle direction and increases in the toroidal direction. The quantity applies to the specified strap reference point or outline point; it is not the strap width or an inclination angle.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the angular displacement follows increasing $\phi$ about $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal steering angle of an electron-cyclotron beam, obtained from the toroidal wave-vector direction cosine in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal steering angle specifies the signed component of an electron-cyclotron beam's propagation direction along the geometric toroidal direction. It describes beam orientation, not the toroidal position of the launcher.

The angle is defined from the toroidal wave-vector component as

$$
\alpha_\phi = \arcsin\left(\frac{k_\phi}{|\mathbf{k}|}\right)
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the wave vector, $k_\phi = \mathbf{k} \cdot \hat{\phi}$ is its component along the toroidal unit vector, and $|\mathbf{k}|$ is its magnitude. The normalized ratio is the toroidal direction cosine represented by [toroidal_normalized_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:toroidal_normalized_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam); the corresponding poloidal steering quantity is [poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam](name:poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the beam wave vector has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Toroidal steering angle of an EC beam, defined as arcsin(k_φ/k) where k_φ is the toroidal component of the mean wave vector. Determines the toroidal launch direction, driven current, and parallel refractive index N∥ of the injected EC wave.

Here the term wave vector refers to the mean wave vector in the EC beam

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_launching_position
NAMES.short: Toroidal angle of launching position is the azimuthal coordinate of the physical point where a heating wave or particle beam is launched, measured in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame with R major radius, φ toroidal angle, and Z vertical height.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal angle of launching position is the azimuthal coordinate of the physical point where a heating wave or particle beam is launched. It is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a launch point whose horizontal Cartesian coordinates are expressed in a right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and $+\hat{x}$ defining $\phi=0$, the toroidal angle is

$$
\phi_\mathrm{launch} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_\mathrm{launch}, x_\mathrm{launch}) \bmod 2\pi
$$

where $x_\mathrm{launch}$ and $y_\mathrm{launch}$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates of the launch point, in meters, and $\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the quadrant-resolved azimuth.

This quantity specifies only the toroidal location of the launch point. The vertical coordinate of the same point is [vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position), while steering or propagation orientation is represented by direction quantities such as [toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam](name:toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam); this quantity is not a beam direction or wave-vector angle. Values differing by integer multiples of $2\pi$ identify the same toroidal locus.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the angular displacement from the $\phi=0$ direction is counter-clockwise as viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ side looking toward decreasing $Z$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal angle

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
NAMES.short: Toroidal current due to wave-driven current drive is the cumulative toroidal plasma current enclosed by a magnetic flux surface and attributable to wave-particle interactions. It is the total wave-driven contribution, not a single toroidal Fourier harmonic.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current due to wave-driven current drive is the cumulative toroidal plasma current enclosed by a magnetic flux surface and attributable to wave-particle interactions. It represents the wave-particle-interaction contribution to the enclosed toroidal current, excluding inductive, bootstrap, neutral-beam-driven, and other non-wave current sources.

For a magnetic flux surface labeled by the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) $\psi$, the enclosed current is defined by the poloidal-area integral of the toroidal component of the wave-driven current density:

$$
I_{\phi,\mathrm{wcd}}(\psi) = \int_{A(\psi)} j_{\mathrm{wcd},\phi}(R,Z)\, dA
$$

where $I_{\phi,\mathrm{wcd}}$ is the toroidal current due to wave-driven current drive, $A(\psi)$ is the poloidal cross-sectional area inside the $\psi=\mathrm{constant}$ contour at fixed toroidal angle, $j_{\mathrm{wcd},\phi}$ is the toroidal component of the [wave-driven current density](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive), $dA$ is the physical area element on that poloidal cross-section, and $(R, \phi, Z)$ is the right-handed cylindrical frame with $R$ major radius, $\phi$ toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ vertical height.

This is an enclosed-current quantity: $I_{\phi,\mathrm{wcd}}(\psi)$ depends on the selected flux surface, and at the outer closed flux surface it equals the net [current due to wave-driven current drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive). When a toroidal Fourier decomposition of the wave field is used, this quantity is the sum over harmonics; [per-toroidal-mode current due to wave-driven current drive](name:per_toroidal_mode_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive) is the corresponding single-harmonic contribution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the wave-driven toroidal plasma current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal component of the refractive-index vector for a lower-hybrid wave launched by a lower-hybrid antenna.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal launched-wave index is the signed projection of the refractive-index vector of a wave launched by a lower-hybrid antenna onto the toroidal direction. It characterizes toroidal phase variation and is distinct from the dimensional [toroidal wave vector](name:toroidal_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam).

The index is defined by

$$
n_\phi = \frac{\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{k_0} = \frac{k_\phi}{k_0}
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the launched-wave vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $k_\phi$ is the toroidal projection of $\mathbf{k}$, and $k_0$ is the free-space wavenumber. The corresponding poloidal quantity is the [poloidal launched-wave index](name:poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the launched-wave vector has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Refraction index in the toroidal direction
sources.parent_definition: Set of horizontal rows of waveguides (corresponding to different poloidal positions). A power spectrum is provided for each row.

NAMES.name: toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Full toroidal width of the rectangular cross-section of an ICRH antenna strap conductor element, measured along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Full toroidal width of the rectangular cross-section of an ICRH antenna strap conductor element, measured along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the edge-to-edge extent between the two toroidally separated sides of the strap conductor.

For a strap represented at a characteristic major radius, the toroidal width is related to the angular separation of the two toroidal edges by:

$$
w_\phi = R_\mathrm{strap}\,\Delta\phi
$$

where $w_\phi$ is the toroidal width, $R_\mathrm{strap}$ is the representative major radius of the strap, and $\Delta\phi$ is the smaller non-wrapping angular separation between the two toroidal edges.

This is a full width, not a half-width or a signed coordinate difference. It is distinct from the poloidal extent [height_of_antenna_strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap) and from the local-normal extent [thickness_of_antenna_strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap) of the same strap conductor.

NAMES.name: total_external_heating_power
NAMES.short: Aggregate zero-or-positive non-inductive auxiliary heating power absorbed or deposited in the plasma, including neutral-beam and radio-frequency heating contributions and excluding Ohmic inductive heating.
NAMES.long:
Total external heating power is the aggregate zero-or-positive auxiliary heating power absorbed or deposited in the plasma by external non-inductive heating systems. It includes plasma-coupled contributions from neutral-beam injection and radio-frequency systems such as electron-cyclotron, ion-cyclotron, and lower-hybrid heating, and excludes Ohmic inductive heating. It is zero when no external auxiliary heating power is absorbed or deposited in the plasma.

The aggregate is defined as the scalar sum of absorbed auxiliary-heating contributions:

$$
P_\mathrm{ext} = \sum_i P_{i,\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{ext}$ and each $P_{i,\mathrm{abs}}$ are powers expressed in watts, and $i$ indexes the auxiliary heating systems included in the aggregate.

This quantity represents absorbed or deposited plasma power, not source electrical input, generator power, launched radio-frequency power, transmitted-line power, or neutral-beam power before plasma absorption. Component contributions include quantities such as [total power due to electron cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating), [total power due to ion cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating), and [absorbed power of neutral beam injector](name:absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector). The launched neutral-beam quantity [total power of neutral beam injector](name:total_power_of_neutral_beam_injector) is distinct because it is defined before absorption losses, whereas this aggregate includes only the absorbed contribution.

sources.enhanced_context: Total additional external heating power coupled to the plasma, summing all auxiliary heating systems (NBI, EC, IC, and LH) excluding Ohmic power. Represents the total non-inductive power input driving plasma heating and current drive.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total additional external power (NBI+EC+IC+LH, without ohmic) coupled to the plasma

NAMES.name: total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short: Total power due to electron cyclotron heating is the net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma from all electron-cyclotron wave sources through resonant electron-cyclotron interactions. It excludes launched, transmitted, reflected, and unabsorbed shine-through power.
NAMES.long:
Total power due to electron cyclotron heating is the net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma from all electron-cyclotron wave sources through resonant interaction with electrons at the electron cyclotron frequency or its harmonics. It is an absorbed heating power, not the generated, launched, transmitted, reflected, or unabsorbed radiofrequency power.

The total absorbed electron-cyclotron heating power is the sum of the net absorbed powers from the contributing electron-cyclotron sources:

$$
P_\mathrm{EC} = \sum_{s=1}^{N_\mathrm{EC}} P_{\mathrm{EC},s}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{EC}$ is the number of contributing electron-cyclotron sources, $P_{\mathrm{EC},s}$ is the net electron-cyclotron power absorbed by the plasma from source $s$ expressed in watts, and $P_\mathrm{EC}$ is the total absorbed electron-cyclotron heating power expressed in watts.

The per-source contribution is [power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating](name:power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating). This quantity is non-negative and is zero when no electron-cyclotron power is absorbed by the plasma; it is a component of [total_external_heating_power](name:total_external_heating_power) when total external heating is formed over all auxiliary heating methods.

sources.enhanced_context: Total electron cyclotron (EC) heating power coupled to the plasma. Represents the absorbed RF power delivered to the plasma by ECRH systems, a key global energy input parameter.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total EC power coupled to the plasma

NAMES.name: total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
NAMES.short: Total net radio-frequency power absorbed by the plasma through ion cyclotron resonance heating, summed over all ion-cyclotron launchers or antenna systems. It excludes power that is launched but reflected or lost before coupling to the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Total power due to ion cyclotron heating is the total rate at which electromagnetic wave power in the ion-cyclotron frequency range is coupled from all launchers to the plasma.

The total coupled power is

$$
P_{IC} = \sum_a P_{IC,a}
$$

where $P_{IC,a}$ is the power coupled to the plasma from launcher $a$, given per launcher by [power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating](name:power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating). Coupled power is the net wave power crossing the antenna–plasma boundary: it excludes generator output, reflected power, and transmission and antenna losses, and it is not reduced by any subsequent incomplete absorption of the coupled wave field within the plasma.

sources.enhanced_context: Total IC power coupled to the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total IC power coupled to the plasma

NAMES.name: total_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Total power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the net launched radio-frequency power from the antenna set, summed over all ion-cyclotron heating antennas. It excludes reflected power and is distinct from power absorbed by the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Total power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the antenna-summed net launched radio-frequency wave power at the antenna reference planes. It is the aggregate of the net power associated with each ion-cyclotron heating antenna and is distinct from the power ultimately absorbed by the plasma.

The total launched antenna power is defined by summing the net contribution from each antenna:

$$
P_{\mathrm{total}} = \sum_{a=1}^{N_{\mathrm{ant}}} \left(P_{\mathrm{fwd},a} - P_{\mathrm{ref},a}\right)
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{total}}$, $P_{\mathrm{fwd},a}$, and $P_{\mathrm{ref},a}$ are powers expressed in watts, $P_{\mathrm{fwd},a}$ is the forward incident power traveling toward antenna $a$, $P_{\mathrm{ref},a}$ is the reflected power returning from antenna $a$, and $N_{\mathrm{ant}}$ is the number of antennas included in the sum.

This quantity represents launched antenna power, not absorbed heating power. The corresponding single-antenna net power is [power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna); its directional components are [forward power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) and [reflected power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), while plasma absorption is represented by [total power due to ion-cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net radio-frequency power flow is from the antenna set toward the plasma-facing launch side.

sources.enhanced_context: Total RF power launched into the vacuum vessel by the entire ICRH antenna system, summed over all antennas. A key global measure of power coupled from the antenna array to the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Power launched into the vacuum vessel by the whole ICRH system (sum over antennas)

NAMES.name: total_power_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Power delivered by all neutral beam injectors at the vacuum vessel boundary, evaluated before plasma absorption, shine-through, and fast-ion first-orbit loss corrections. It is the non-negative sum of launched kinetic powers over the injectors.
NAMES.long:
Power delivered by all neutral beam injectors at the vacuum vessel boundary is the aggregate launched kinetic power carried by neutral beam particles as they enter the vessel. It is a non-negative scalar defined before subsequent interaction of the beams with the plasma.

The sum of per-injector launched powers defines the quantity as:

$$
P_{\mathrm{NBI}} = \sum_{j \in \mathcal{J}} P_j
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{NBI}}$ is the total launched neutral-beam-injector power, $\mathcal{J}$ is the set of neutral beam injectors included in the aggregate, and $P_j$ is the launched power of injector $j$ crossing its vessel-entry surface into the vessel. Injectors that do not launch neutral particles contribute zero.

This quantity includes all neutral energy components delivered by the aggregated injectors at the vessel boundary. It is the sum over [power_of_neutral_beam_injector](name:power_of_neutral_beam_injector) and differs from [absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector](name:absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector), which is evaluated after subtracting neutral-beam shine-through and fast-ion first-orbit losses from launched power. It excludes source electrical input and power stopped upstream of the vessel boundary, but no plasma-interaction loss or absorption term is subtracted from this launched total.

sources.enhanced_context: Total neutral beam injection (NBI) power launched from injectors into the vacuum vessel. A summary scalar representing the injected beam power used for global heating power accounting.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total NBI power launched from neutral beam injectors into the vacuum vessel

sources.enhanced_context: Total neutral beam injection (NBI) power coupled to the plasma, representing the fraction of the launched NBI power that is deposited into the plasma through beam ionization and thermalization.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total NBI power coupled to the plasma

NAMES.name: vertical_angle_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Vertical inclination angle of the central beamlet of a neutral beam injector, measured from the horizontal plane to the beamlet axis.
NAMES.long:
The vertical angle of a neutral beam injector characterizes the elevation of the central beamlet axis with respect to the horizontal plane, encoding the upward or downward tilt component of the beam's injection direction. Together with the toroidal pointing geometry described by angle_of_neutral_beam_injector and the tangency major radius beam_major_radius_of_neutral_beam_injector, this angle fully specifies the 3D trajectory of the central beam axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The angle $\alpha_v$ is the elevation of the central beamlet unit direction vector $\hat{b}$ above the horizontal plane:

$$
\alpha_v = \arcsin\!\left(\hat{b} \cdot \hat{Z}\right)
$$

where $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector and $\hat{b}$ is the unit vector along the central beamlet axis, with $\alpha_v = 0$ for a perfectly horizontal beam and $|\alpha_v| < \pi/2$ for any physical configuration.

This geometric parameter is fixed by the physical design and alignment of the injector unit and its duct orientation, established from engineering design specifications and optical survey measurements. The vertical_width_of_neutral_beam_injector describes the vertical spatial extent of the full beamlet group at the injector aperture, complementing this directional quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the central beamlet is directed upward, in the $+Z$ direction above the horizontal plane.

sources.enhanced_context: Angle of inclination of a beamlet at the centre of the NBI injection unit surface relative to the horizontal plane. Characterises the vertical pointing geometry of the neutral beam injection unit.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Angle of inclination between a beamlet at the centre of the injection unit surface and the horiontal plane

NAMES.name: vertical_centroid_of_coil_conductor_element
NAMES.short: Vertical Z-coordinate of the geometric centroid of a rectangular coil conductor element cross-section, measured in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical centroid coordinate locates the geometric center of a rectangular coil conductor element cross-section along the $Z$-axis of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major-radius distance from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is the vertical height.

For a rectangular cross-section with lower edge at $Z_\text{min}$ and upper edge at $Z_\text{max}$, the centroid is:

$$
Z_c = \frac{Z_\text{min} + Z_\text{max}}{2}
$$

where $Z_c$ is in meters and coincides with the midpoint between the two horizontal bounding edges of the rectangle.

This geometric parameter is specified in engineering design documentation for coil, antenna, and passive-structure assemblies, and may be confirmed by physical survey measurements before or during machine operation. Paired with the corresponding major-radius centroid, it fully characterizes the planar position of each sub-element within the poloidal cross-section, providing the input required for Biot–Savart magnetic field calculations from individual current-carrying segments. The analogous coordinate for the parent coil conductor is captured by [vertical_coordinate_of_coil_conductor](name:vertical_coordinate_of_coil_conductor), the generic conductor cross-section center by [vertical_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section](name:vertical_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section), and the ion cyclotron antenna strap center by [vertical_coordinate_of_antenna_strap](name:vertical_coordinate_of_antenna_strap).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the centroid lies above the machine midplane in the direction of increasing $Z$.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of rectangle.
sources.leaf_definition: Geometric centre Z
sources.parent_definition: Rectangular description of the element

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Vertical location of an antenna strap’s geometric center, expressed as the Z coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the vertical coordinate of the geometric center of an antenna strap, locating the strap relative to the machine midplane. It is a geometric position, not the strap’s height, thickness, or vertical extent.

For a strap occupying volume $V$, its geometric-center coordinate is defined by

$$
Z_c = \frac{1}{V}\int_V Z\,dV
$$

where $Z_c$ is the center coordinate, $Z$ is vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $V$ is the strap volume, and $dV$ is the volume element. This quantity is analogous to the [vertical coordinate of a diagnostic antenna](name:vertical_coordinate_of_diagnostic_antenna), but applies specifically to the antenna strap.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the strap’s geometric center lies in the $+Z$ direction, above the machine midplane.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of annulus.
sources.leaf_definition: Centre height
sources.parent_definition: The element is an annulus of  center r, z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of outline.
sources.leaf_definition: Height
