NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_aperture
NAMES.short: Vertical Z coordinate of the geometric center of an aperture in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long: The vertical coordinate $Z$ locates the geometric center of an aperture along the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is measured upward from the machine midplane. Apertures appear across a wide range of fusion-relevant hardware — neutral beam injectors, electron cyclotron launcher ports, optical diagnostic slits, and detector entrance windows — and their vertical positions are essential inputs for sight-line reconstruction, ray-tracing, and geometric alignment with plasma-facing components. For a given component, this quantity is paired with the corresponding radial coordinate to fully specify the 2-D cross-sectional location of the aperture center; the analogous quantity for optical elements is [vertical_coordinate_of_optical_element](name:vertical_coordinate_of_optical_element), which follows an identical convention. Aperture center positions are fixed geometric descriptors of the hardware configuration, determined from engineering drawings or in-situ survey measurements and updated only when hardware is modified.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aperture center lies above the machine midplane in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of centre.
sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: If geometry_type=2, coordinates of the centre of the circle. If geometry_type=1 or 3, coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the plane detector/aperture. This origin is located within the detector/aperture area.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_coil_conductor
NAMES.short: Signed vertical position of a point on a coil conductor, expressed as the Z coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed vertical coordinate of a specified point on a coil conductor, rather than the coordinate of its geometric centroid. It is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, whose basis satisfies $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.

$$
Z_P = \mathbf{r}_P \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_P$ is the position vector of point $P$ and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector; $Z_P$ is the corresponding vertical coordinate. The point-specific quantity is distinct from the [vertical centroid of a coil conductor element](name:vertical_centroid_of_coil_conductor_element), which applies only to a defined conductor-element centroid.
NAMES.sign: Positive when point $P$ is displaced in the direction of increasing $Z$, along $+\hat{Z}$.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of arcs of circle.
sources.leaf_definition: Height of the start point of each arc of circle
sources.parent_definition: Description of the element contour by a set of arcs of circle. For each of these, the position of the start point is given together with the curvature radius. The end point is given by the start point of the next arc of circle.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: Vertical Z coordinate of the geometric center of an electron cyclotron launcher mirror, measured along the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate $Z$ locates the geometric center of an EC launcher mirror along the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z = 0$ denotes the machine midplane. Together with the major-radius coordinate [radial_centroid_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:radial_centroid_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and the toroidal angle, it fully specifies the three-dimensional position of the mirror center in the machine.

The vertical position is determined by the port assignment in the vacuum vessel and is established during machine assembly or optical survey, with uncertainties of order millimeters. The coordinate serves as a boundary condition for beam-tracing calculations that compute EC wave power deposition and current-drive profiles; small changes in $Z$ shift the injection height and alter which resonance layer the beam intercepts.

EC launchers installed in equatorial ports have mirror $Z$ values near the midplane, while upper-port launchers occupy elevated $Z$ positions depending on machine geometry and plasma shaping requirements. The [angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) parametrizes the mirror rotation that steers the beam poloidally, while the mirror boundary in its local planar frame is described by x1_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror and x2_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror. For an analogous position coordinate of a different heating system, see [vertical_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector](name:vertical_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the mirror center is located above the machine midplane in the direction of increasing $Z$.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of centre.
sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Coordinates of the origin of the local coordinate system (X1,X2,X3) describing the object. This origin is located within the object area and should be the middle point of the object surface. If geometry_type=2, it's the centre of the circular object. If geometry_type=3, it's the centre of the rectangular object.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
NAMES.short: Vertical coordinate of the reference point of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna, measured from the machine equatorial midplane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed vertical coordinate of the reference point of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna. It locates that reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, and does not describe the antenna's dimensions or emitting surface.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{ref}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the position vector of the antenna reference point, $\hat{Z}$ is the upward vertical unit vector, and $Z_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is a length coordinate expressed in m. The analogous location quantity for another radio-frequency antenna is the [vertical coordinate of a lower hybrid antenna](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the reference point lies in the $+Z$ direction from the machine equatorial midplane.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of reference point.
sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Reference point used to define the poloidal angle, e.g. the geometrical centre of the vacuum vessel. Used to define the poloidal mode numbers under antenna/surface_current

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position
NAMES.short: Vertical Z coordinate of the physical point from which a heating beam or wave is launched, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate $Z$ of the launching position locates the spatial origin of a beam or electromagnetic wave's propagation trajectory within the tokamak vessel, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $Z$ is the height along the machine symmetry axis.

For electron cyclotron heating systems, this coordinate specifies the height at which the EC beam exits the launcher and enters the plasma. Together with the major-radius and toroidal-angle components, it fully defines the three-dimensional launch-point geometry needed for beam-tracing and current-drive modeling. The [angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror](name:angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) determines the beam injection direction from this spatial origin, while [vertical_coordinate_of_beam_tracing_point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_beam_tracing_point) gives $Z$ at discrete computed points along the propagating ray rather than at its origin.

The launch height is set by the mechanical installation of the launcher on the vacuum vessel and is determined by engineering survey. For equatorial-port launchers, $Z$ is close to 0 m; upper-port or top-launch geometries place the origin at $Z \approx 0.5$–$1.5$ m in medium-to-large tokamaks.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the launching position lies above the geometric midplane ($Z > 0$) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Launching position of the beam

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
NAMES.short: Vertical Z-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate locates the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna along the vertical direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation is:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{ant}} = Z(P_{\mathrm{ant}})
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ant}}$ is the antenna reference point and $Z(P_{\mathrm{ant}})$ is its vertical coordinate. This quantity refers to the antenna reference point; the [vertical coordinate of a lower-hybrid antenna row](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row) refers instead to a row reference point.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the antenna reference point lies in the direction of increasing $Z$.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of reference point.
sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Reference point used to define the poloidal angle, e.g. the geometrical centre of the vacuum vessel. Used to define the poloidal refraction index under antenna/row

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row
NAMES.short: Vertical Z-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna row in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
Vertical $Z$-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna row is the projection of that row reference point onto $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a row reference point with position vector $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref,row}}$, the coordinate is defined by:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{row}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ref,row}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This is a row-level coordinate and is distinct from the antenna-level [vertical coordinate of the lower-hybrid antenna](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). It is distinct from the row vertical extent.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the row reference point lies in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame from the $Z=0$ plane.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of position.
sources.leaf_definition: Height
sources.parent_definition: Position of the middle on the row

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
NAMES.short: Vertical coordinate Z of the declared reference position of a neutral beam injector is the signed height of that point from the equatorial plane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical coordinate $Z$ of the declared reference position of a neutral beam injector is the signed height of that point relative to the equatorial plane in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It identifies only the vertical component of the injector reference-point position.

The coordinate is the projection of the reference-point displacement onto the vertical basis vector:

$$
Z_\mathrm{NBI} = \mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ is the displacement of the declared reference position from an origin on the symmetry axis in the equatorial plane, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

For an extended injector, this quantity locates only the declared reference point; it does not define the injector aperture, beam-axis direction, beam footprint, or full beam geometry. A complementary position coordinate is [radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector](name:radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector) when defined for the same reference point.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the declared reference position lies above the equatorial plane in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of position.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Height

NAMES.name: voltage_amplitude
NAMES.short: Maximum absolute instantaneous radio-frequency voltage at the transmission-line feed of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna module during one waveform cycle.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the peak magnitude of the radio-frequency voltage applied at the transmission-line feed of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna module. It describes the voltage waveform amplitude at the module interface, not the voltage at the generator or along the antenna strap.

$$
V_{\mathrm{peak}} = \max_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \left|v_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)\right|
$$

where $v_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ is the instantaneous feed voltage in volts, $t$ is time, and $\mathcal{T}$ spans one complete radio-frequency waveform cycle. The magnitude is non-negative and is independent of the voltage polarity. It is distinct from [forward power of the ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:forward_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), which describes traveling power toward the antenna, and from the antenna's [resistance](name:resistance_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), which describes its resistive RF loading.

sources.enhanced_context: Amplitude of the voltage signal on an IC antenna module transmission line feed. Represents the peak voltage magnitude used for power and reflection analysis of the ICRH system.
sources.leaf_definition: Amplitude of the measurement
sources.parent_definition: Set of voltage measurements

NAMES.name: wave_frequency
NAMES.short: Temporal carrier frequency of a coherent electromagnetic wave used to characterize its oscillation rate in plasma heating and current drive.
NAMES.long:
Wave frequency is the non-negative temporal carrier frequency of a coherent electromagnetic wave interacting with a plasma. It describes the rate of phase oscillation and applies to waves at launch or during propagation, independent of the wave amplitude or absorbed power.

The frequency $f$ is related to the angular frequency by

$$
f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}
$$

where $f$ is frequency in hertz and $\omega$ is angular frequency in radians per second. The launch-specific quantity [launched wave frequency](name:launched_wave_frequency) uses this same definition as the absolute reference for a launched wave, while [frequency of electron cyclotron heating antenna](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is a device-specific instance.

sources.enhanced_context: Wave frequency (f) of a coherent electromagnetic wave in the plasma. Determines resonance conditions for wave-particle interactions and selects the relevant heating regime (EC, IC, LH).
sources.leaf_definition: Wave frequency
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities for various time slices

NAMES.name: wave_phase_of_antenna_strap
NAMES.short: Relative RF wave phase assigned to one ion-cyclotron heating antenna strap, used with other strap phases to determine the launcher's toroidal wave spectrum.
NAMES.long:
The wave phase of an antenna strap is the phase offset of its RF excitation relative to a defined launcher reference signal or reference strap. It describes relative phasing between straps rather than the strap's geometric location or RF amplitude.

$$
\phi_s = \arg\left(\frac{C_s}{C_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right)
$$

where $C_s$ is the complex RF phasor associated with the strap, $C_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the complex phasor of the reference signal, and $\phi_s$ is the resulting phase angle in radians. The phase origin and positive phase direction are set by the launcher phase-reference convention; an absolute phase has no meaning without that convention. Phase differences between straps determine the launched wave spectral content, while the [toroidal angle of the antenna strap](name:toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap) describes geometric position and [voltage amplitude](name:voltage_amplitude) describes excitation magnitude.

sources.enhanced_context: Phase between antenna straps (φ) for an ICRH launcher, summarizing the relative phasing used to control wave spectral content and current drive efficiency.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Phase between straps

NAMES.name: wave_vector
NAMES.short: Wave-vector quantity giving the spatial gradient of wave phase; its magnitude is the local wavenumber and its components describe phase variation along specified directions.
NAMES.long:
The wave vector is the spatial phase-gradient vector of a propagating or fluctuating wave. It specifies the rate and direction of phase variation, while its magnitude is the local wavenumber.

For a local phase field $\Phi(\mathbf{r},t)$, the wave vector $\mathbf{k}$ is defined by

$$
\mathbf{k} = \nabla \Phi
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $t$ is time, and $\Phi$ is the wave phase. Components may be resolved along geometric directions, as in [vertical_wave_vector](name:vertical_wave_vector), or relative to the local equilibrium magnetic field, as in [perpendicular_wave_vector](name:perpendicular_wave_vector). Dimensionless forms such as [normalized_wave_vector](name:normalized_wave_vector) and [product_of_wave_vector_and_reference_larmor_radius](name:product_of_wave_vector_and_reference_larmor_radius) are scaled representations obtained by multiplying the wave vector or one of its components by a reference Larmor radius; they retain the underlying spatial-scale information without being additional directional components.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) component of the unit wavevector (k_z) at the launch point of an electron cyclotron (EC) beam. Defines the vertical direction of beam propagation at the launcher for ray-tracing calculations.
sources.leaf_definition: Component along the vertical direction
sources.parent_definition: Wavevector at launch point

NAMES.name: width_of_aperture
NAMES.short: Aperture width is the non-negative clear opening extent along the first local tangential direction in a right-handed aperture-local frame (first tangential, second tangential, normal). The second local tangential direction also lies in the aperture plane, and the normal is orthogonal to that plane.
NAMES.long:
Aperture width is the non-negative clear extent of an aperture along its first local tangential direction. The aperture is described in a right-handed aperture-local frame $(\hat{t}_1, \hat{t}_2, \hat{n})$, where $\hat{t}_1$ and $\hat{t}_2$ are the first and second local tangential unit vectors in the aperture plane, $\hat{n}$ is the local normal, and $\hat{t}_1 \times \hat{t}_2 = \hat{n}$.

For a clear opening region $\mathcal{A}$, the width is the maximum-minus-minimum span of the first-local-tangential coordinate:

$$
w = x_{1,\max} - x_{1,\min}
$$

where $w$ is the aperture width, $x_{1,\max}=\max_{\mathbf{r}\in\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{t}_1)$ and $x_{1,\min}=\min_{\mathbf{r}\in\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{r}\cdot\hat{t}_1)$ are the maximum and minimum first-local-tangential length coordinates over the clear opening, $\mathbf{r}$ is a position vector relative to any fixed origin in the aperture plane, and $\mathcal{A}$ is the clear opening region.

This quantity is a full aperture span, not a radius, semi-width, material width, support-structure dimension, or beam-envelope width. It uses only the first local tangential direction; the orthogonal in-plane extent along $\hat{t}_2$ is a different aperture dimension. For a circular aperture, this full span is the diameter and is twice the [radius of aperture].

NAMES.name: x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: Signed x-axis component of the unit vector defining an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation or rotation axis at its home position in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) basis.
NAMES.long:
Signed x-axis component of the unit vector defining an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's translation or rotation axis at its home position is the projection of that mirror-axis unit vector onto the $\hat{x}$ basis direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The vector direction is evaluated for the mirror at its home position.

The component is defined by the scalar projection

$$
d_x = \hat{\mathbf{d}} \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $d_x$ is this x-axis component, $\hat{\mathbf{d}}$ is the unit vector along the mirror translation or rotation axis at the home position, and $\hat{x}$ is the x basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

Together with the [y-axis component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and [z-axis component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), this quantity specifies the orientation of the mirror movement axis and satisfies $d_x^2 + d_y^2 + d_z^2 = 1$. It is an orientation component, not a mirror position, displacement, or rotation angle.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the mirror-axis unit vector has a component in the $+\hat{x}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: X coordinate of direction.
sources.leaf_definition: Component along X axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector indicating the direction of the translation or the rotation axis at "home" position (i.e. ../../geometry/centre)

NAMES.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: Y-axis component of the unit vector defining an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation or rotation axis at its home position.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the y component of the unit direction vector defining an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation direction or rotation axis at its home position. It is a directional cosine, not a displacement or steering angle.

The component is defined by

$$
d_y = \mathbf{d} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $\mathbf{d}$ is the mirror direction unit vector and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the y-axis unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$, with $\hat{z}$ vertical. The unit-vector condition gives $-1 \leq d_y \leq 1$. The corresponding [x-axis direction component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and [z-axis direction component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) complete the Cartesian direction description.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the mirror direction vector has a component toward increasing Cartesian y coordinate, that is, $d_y > 0$.

sources.enhanced_context: Y coordinate of direction.
sources.leaf_definition: Component along Y axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector indicating the direction of the translation or the rotation axis at "home" position (i.e. ../../geometry/centre)

NAMES.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
NAMES.short: Signed z-axis component of the unit vector defining the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation or rotation axis at its home position.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the z-axis component of the unit direction vector that defines the translation direction or rotation axis of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror at its home position. The corresponding [x-axis component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and [y-axis component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) complete the Cartesian direction vector.

For unit direction vector $\mathbf{u}$, the component is defined by:

$$
u_z = \mathbf{u} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}, \qquad \lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert = 1
$$

where $u_z$ is the z-axis component, $\mathbf{u}$ is the mirror direction unit vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the positive z-axis unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ frame, with $\hat{z}$ aligned with the vertical $+Z$ direction. The vector describes the mirror movement direction or rotation axis at its home position.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the mirror direction vector has a component along the positive $\hat{z}$ axis, corresponding to the vertical $+Z$ direction.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of direction.
sources.leaf_definition: Component along Z axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector indicating the direction of the translation or the rotation axis at "home" position (i.e. ../../geometry/centre)

NAMES.name: fast_electron_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volumetric coherent-wave power density absorbed by the fast (suprathermal) electron population. It is the local rate of coherent-wave energy deposition into fast electrons per unit plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Fast electron power density is the time-averaged volumetric rate at which a coherent wave transfers energy to the fast (suprathermal) electron population. It represents electron heating by wave absorption, distinct from power deposited into the bulk thermal electron population.

A kinetic energy-moment definition for the fast component is:

$$
Q_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{\alpha}\left\langle \int \frac{1}{2} m_e v^2\, \mathcal{C}_{\alpha}[f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\, d^3v \right\rangle_t
$$

where $Q_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast electron power density, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $v$ is particle speed, $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-electron distribution function, $\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}$ is the wave-induced part of its kinetic evolution due to coherent-wave component or mode $\alpha$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes averaging over the relevant wave or beat period.

This quantity is a local density, not cumulative absorbed power over a volume and not launched or field power before absorption. It is a sub-contribution to [electron_power_density](name:electron_power_density) and excludes [thermal_electron_power_density](name:thermal_electron_power_density); fast denotes the modeled non-thermal part of the electron distribution rather than a universal sharp energy threshold.
NAMES.sign: Positive when coherent-wave energy is transferred to the fast electron population.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: RF-wave power deposited per unit volume in suprathermal electrons for each toroidal Fourier mode, with the modal sum recovering total fast-electron power density.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local RF-wave energy deposition rate assigned to the suprathermal electron population for an individual toroidal Fourier mode. It is a modal decomposition of [fast electron power density](name:fast_electron_power_density), excluding thermal-electron absorption and volume-integrated fast-electron power.

The modal contributions are defined by their closure to the total local deposition rate:

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{n_\phi} P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}, n_\phi)
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the total fast-electron power density at position $\mathbf{x}$, $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}, n_\phi)$ is its contribution from toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, and the sum spans all represented toroidal modes. The quantity is a local deposition rate, not the volume-integrated [fast electron absorbed wave power](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net non-transport volumetric energy source rate for the fast-ion channel, giving local RF-wave power deposited into nonthermal fast ions and summed over included species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Fast ion power density is the local rate per unit volume at which coherent RF wave-particle interactions add energy to the nonthermal fast-ion channel. It is the absorbed-wave contribution associated with the broader [ion power density](name:ion_power_density), while excluding energy deposited into bulk thermal ions or electrons and spatial transport terms.

The species- and charge-state-summed quantity is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fi}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{F}} \sum_{Z \in \mathcal{Z}_a} P_{\mathrm{fi},a,Z}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fi}}$ and $P_{\mathrm{fi},a,Z}$ are local power densities in W m$^{-3}$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathcal{F}$ is the set of included fast-ion species, and $\mathcal{Z}_a$ is the set of included charge states for species $a$.

The quantity represents the total local wave-energy transfer to fast ions, without resolution by toroidal harmonic. Its mode-resolved counterpart, [per-toroidal-mode fast ion power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density), partitions this transfer by toroidal mode number.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Coherent-wave power absorbed per unit volume by the nonthermal fast-ion population for one toroidal Fourier mode, summed over all included fast-ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Per-toroidal-mode fast-ion power density is the local rate of energy transfer from a coherent electromagnetic wave to the nonthermal fast-ion population, resolved by toroidal Fourier mode and aggregated over included charge states. It is a modal component of the [fast-ion power density](name:fast_ion_power_density), distinct from power transferred to thermal ions, electrons, or other channels.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast},n_\phi}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_q P_{\mathrm{fast},q,n_\phi}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast},n_\phi}(\mathbf{x})$ is the modal power density, $P_{\mathrm{fast},q,n_\phi}(\mathbf{x})$ is the corresponding quantity for charge state $q$, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, and $\mathbf{x}$ is the local plasma position. The charge-state-resolved contribution is represented by [per-toroidal-mode fast-ion charge-state power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density). Under the adopted Fourier normalization, summing the modal contributions over $n_\phi$ recovers the [fast-ion power density](name:fast_ion_power_density).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric rate of wave energy absorbed by ions in a specified charge state, covering both thermal and fast ion populations.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state power density is the local rate at which wave energy is absorbed by ions in a specified charge state per unit plasma volume. It is the ion-population specialization of [power density](name:power_density) and applies to both thermal and fast ions, represented by [thermal ion charge-state power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density) and [fast ion charge-state power density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density).

For a differential plasma volume, the absorbed-wave power density is defined by

$$
p_{i,q}^{\mathrm{abs}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{wave}}^{i,q}}{dt\,dV}
$$

where $p_{i,q}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the absorbed wave power density, $E_{\mathrm{wave}}^{i,q}$ is the wave energy transferred to ion population $i$ in charge state $q$, $t$ is time, and $V$ is plasma volume.

This quantity denotes local wave-power deposition rather than a volume-integrated power or an unrelated collisional or transport source. Integrating it over the plasma volume gives the corresponding [ion charge-state power](name:ion_charge_state_power), while integration inside a flux surface gives [ion charge-state power at inside flux surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Absorbed wave power density deposited on fast (non-thermal) ions in a specified charge state, expressed per unit plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Local volumetric rate at which coherent wave energy is deposited into fast (non-thermal) ions of a single ion charge state. It is the fast-ion, charge-state-resolved component of [ion charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density).

The local density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{fast},q}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{fast},q}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{fast},q}(\mathbf{x})$ is the deposited power density at spatial position $\mathbf{x}$, $q$ identifies the ion charge state, $P_{\mathrm{fast},q}$ is the corresponding absorbed wave power, and $dV$ is a differential plasma volume.

This quantity includes only the specified fast-ion charge state and excludes thermal ions and other charge states. Integrating it over a plasma volume gives the corresponding cumulative quantity, such as [fast-ion charge-state power inside a flux surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface). It is distinct from [thermal-ion charge-state power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density), which describes deposition into bulk thermal ions.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Absorbed wave power density deposited on fast (non-thermal) ions of a specified charge state, resolved per toroidal Fourier mode number.
NAMES.long:
The local volumetric rate of wave energy deposition on fast (non-thermal) ions of a specific charge state $q$, attributed to a single toroidal Fourier mode number $n_\phi$. It is the charge-state-resolved and mode-resolved form of the fast-ion wave absorption.

Summing over all toroidal mode numbers and integrating over the plasma volume recovers the total charge-state-specific absorbed power:

$$
P_{abs}^{q} = \sum_{n_\phi} \int p_{n_\phi,q}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_{n_\phi,q}(\mathbf{r})$ is this quantity at spatial coordinate $\mathbf{r}$ for toroidal mode $n_\phi$ and charge state $q$.

Summing over all charge states $q$ yields [per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density), the charge-state-integrated counterpart. The mode-summed parent quantity is [fast_ion_charge_state_power_density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density). The thermal-ion analog at the same charge-state and mode resolution is [per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density).

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Absorbed wave power density deposited on thermal (bulk) ions in a specified charge state, expressed per unit plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Local volumetric rate at which coherent wave energy is deposited into thermal (bulk) ions of a single ion charge state. It is the thermal-ion, charge-state-resolved component of [ion_charge_state_power_density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), restricted to the bulk Maxwellian ion population and excluding fast suprathermal ions.

The quantity $p_{\mathrm{th,cs}}$ relates to the volume-integrated absorbed power by

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,cs}} = \int_V p_{\mathrm{th,cs}} \, dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th,cs}}$ is the total wave power absorbed by thermal ions of the charge state and $V$ is the plasma volume.

The collisional energy-exchange contribution to the same population is resolved separately by [thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions). The fast-ion counterpart for the same charge state is [fast_ion_charge_state_power_density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density). The toroidal-mode-resolved decomposition is provided by [per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density).

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Coherent-wave power density absorbed by bulk thermal ions of one specified charge state, resolved by toroidal Fourier mode number in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the toroidal-mode contribution to the charge-state-resolved thermal-ion heating density.
NAMES.long:
Coherent-wave power density absorbed by bulk thermal ions of one specified charge state, resolved by toroidal Fourier mode number in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, is the local density of coherent-wave energy absorption by that thermal ion charge-state population for a single toroidal mode label. The charge state is fixed; the quantity is neither summed over ion charge states nor over toroidal modes.

The corresponding [per-toroidal-mode thermal-ion charge-state power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power) is the volume integral of this density for the same mode and charge state:

$$
P_{n,c}^{\mathrm{th\,i}} = \int_V p_{n,c}^{\mathrm{th\,i}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $p_{n,c}^{\mathrm{th\,i}}$ is this coherent-wave power density, $P_{n,c}^{\mathrm{th\,i}}$ is the [per-toroidal-mode thermal-ion charge-state power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power), $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, $c$ is the specified ion charge state, the superscript $\mathrm{th\,i}$ denotes bulk thermal ions, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element over the plasma volume $V$.

The toroidal mode number $n$ is the integer Fourier label associated with coherent-wave dependence $\exp(i n\phi)$; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. The modal normalization must make the modal densities additive: summing $p_{n,c}^{\mathrm{th\,i}}$ over the retained toroidal mode labels reconstructs the [thermal-ion charge-state power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density) for the same charge state, with no additional toroidal or volume factor. Only the real physical contribution assigned to the mode label is represented; any complex Fourier-coefficient normalization is already absorbed into the modal partition.

It excludes power absorbed by electrons, fast ions, other ion charge states, and the charge-state-summed [per-toroidal-mode thermal-ion power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_power_density). As absorbed auxiliary-heating power density, each modal contribution is non-negative; a signed wave-particle exchange representing energy returned from the selected thermal ion charge-state population to the wave is outside this deposited-power quantity.

NAMES.name: left_hand_circularly_polarized_electric_field
NAMES.short: Left-hand circularly polarized electric field is the complex scalar phasor obtained by projecting the electric-field phasor onto the left-hand circular polarization basis perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction. It is the component that co-rotates with positive-ion gyromotion.
NAMES.long:
The left-hand circularly polarized electric field $E_+$ is the complex scalar phasor obtained by projecting an electric-field phasor onto the left-hand circular polarization basis perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction. It represents the perpendicular component whose instantaneous electric-field vector co-rotates with positive-ion gyromotion about the magnetic field.

Let $(\hat{e}_1, \hat{e}_2, \hat{b})$ be a local right-handed orthonormal basis with $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ along the local magnetic-field direction and $\hat{e}_1\times\hat{e}_2=\hat{b}$. For complex amplitudes defined by $\mathbf{E}(t)=\Re\{\tilde{\mathbf{E}}\exp(-i\omega t)\}$, the left-hand component is

$$
E_+ = \frac{\tilde{\mathbf{E}}\cdot\hat{e}_1 + i\,\tilde{\mathbf{E}}\cdot\hat{e}_2}{\sqrt{2}}
$$

where $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}$ is the complex electric-field phasor, $i$ is the imaginary unit, and $\omega$ is the angular frequency. Only the components perpendicular to $\hat{b}$ enter this projection.

This scalar is the circular-polarization projection of an electric-field phasor, not the full vector [electric field](name:electric_field) or the vector [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field). When the phasor is specifically a wave field, this is the same local left-hand projection represented by [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field); the complementary polarization is [right-hand circularly polarized electric field]. Its modulus and rectangular decompositions are [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field amplitude], [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field real part](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part), and [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field imaginary part](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the zero-phase instantaneous perpendicular electric field of a pure real $E_+$ phasor points along $+\hat{e}_1$ and subsequently rotates toward $-\hat{e}_2$ as time increases in the local right-handed orthonormal basis $(\hat{e}_1,\hat{e}_2,\hat{b})$, with $\hat{b}$ along the local magnetic-field direction.

sources.enhanced_context: Array of values for plus.
sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Left hand circularly polarised component of the perpendicular (to the static magnetic field) electric field, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude
NAMES.short: Non-negative amplitude of the complex wave electric-field phasor projected along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction, with phase information discarded.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the magnitude of the complex wave electric-field phasor parallel to the local equilibrium magnetic field. It retains the strength of the parallel component while discarding its phase.

$$
E_{\parallel,\mathrm{amp}} = \left|E_{\parallel}\right| = \sqrt{\left(\operatorname{Re} E_{\parallel}\right)^2 + \left(\operatorname{Im} E_{\parallel}\right)^2}
$$

Here $E_{\parallel}$ is the complex [parallel wave electric field](name:parallel_wave_electric_field), and $\operatorname{Re} E_{\parallel}$ and $\operatorname{Im} E_{\parallel}$ are its real and imaginary quadrature components. The amplitude is non-negative and must not be interpreted as a signed field component; the phase-resolved information remains in the parent phasor.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_electric_field
NAMES.short: Local vector electric field phasor resolved into a single toroidal Fourier mode, retaining the coherent wave's amplitude, radio-frequency phase, and polarization.
NAMES.long:
The per-toroidal-mode electric field is the complex vector Fourier coefficient of a coherent electromagnetic wave's electric field, retaining its local amplitude, phase, and polarization for one toroidal mode. It is a mode-resolved component of the complete [electric field](name:electric_field) vector.

For the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the coefficient is defined by

$$
\tilde{\mathbf{E}}_n(R,Z)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\tilde{\mathbf{E}}(R,\phi,Z)e^{-in\phi}\,d\phi
$$

where $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}_n$ is the per-toroidal-mode coefficient, $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}$ is the local [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field) phasor, $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The coefficient includes all vector projections; the [parallel per-toroidal-mode electric field](name:parallel_per_toroidal_mode_electric_field) is its field-parallel projection, while polarization-resolved quantities provide specialized components.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved cylindrical component points toward increasing $R$, $\phi$, or $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: parallel_per_toroidal_mode_electric_field
NAMES.short: Complex toroidal-mode Fourier coefficient of the wave electric field projected along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction, retaining amplitude and radiofrequency phase.
NAMES.long:
The per-toroidal-mode parallel wave electric field is the complex Fourier phasor obtained by projecting the mode-resolved wave electric-field vector onto the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction. It retains the signed parallel component and its radiofrequency phase.

$$
\tilde{E}_{\parallel,n}=\tilde{\mathbf{E}}_n\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}_0}{\lvert\mathbf{B}_0\rvert}
$$

Here $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}_n$ is the complex vector phasor defined by [per_toroidal_mode_electric_field](name:per_toroidal_mode_electric_field), $\mathbf{B}_0$ is the local equilibrium magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit vector. This complex projection is distinct from the nonnegative modulus represented by [parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude](name:parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projected electric-field component is directed along the local equilibrium magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field
NAMES.short: Power-deposition-weighted flux-surface average of the complex left-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field phasor for one toroidal Fourier mode, retaining its referenced phase.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the complex left-hand circular polarization electric-field phasor for one toroidal Fourier mode, averaged over a magnetic flux surface with local wave-power deposition as the weighting function. It is a weighted component of the [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), not a separate polarization state.

The defining weighted average is

$$
\mathcal{E}_{+,P}^{(n)}(\psi)=
\frac{\left\langle P_{\mathrm{dep}}^{(n)} E_{+}^{(n)}\right\rangle_{\psi}}
{\left\langle P_{\mathrm{dep}}^{(n)}\right\rangle_{\psi}}
$$

where $\mathcal{E}_{+,P}^{(n)}$ is the requested phasor, $E_{+}^{(n)}$ is the left-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field phasor, $P_{\mathrm{dep}}^{(n)}$ is the local deposition weight for toroidal mode number $n$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average on the surface labeled by $\psi$. The denominator must be nonzero.

The result retains amplitude and phase. Its phase is referenced to the selected zero-phase toroidal location, with toroidal angle $\phi$ defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame and represented on the interval $(-\pi,\pi]$. It differs from the unweighted [per-toroidal-mode left-hand circularly polarized electric field](name:per_toroidal_mode_left_hand_circularly_polarized_electric_field) through the deposition weighting.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field
NAMES.short: Complex toroidal Fourier coefficient of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus wave-electric-field component for a single toroidal mode.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the complex Fourier coefficient of the right-hand circularly polarized E-minus component of the wave electric field for one toroidal mode. It preserves the circular-polarization projection defined by the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field) while resolving its toroidal dependence.

$$
\widetilde{E}_{-}(n_\phi)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi}E_{-}(\phi)e^{-i n_\phi\phi}\,d\phi
$$

Here $E_{-}(\phi)$ is the parent complex electric-field phasor, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in radians, and $n_\phi$ is the dimensionless integer toroidal mode number. The result is a single-mode coefficient, not a sum over modes and not necessarily the real part of the phasor.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_particle_energy
NAMES.short: Perpendicular fast-particle energy is the part of the suprathermal particle kinetic energy associated with motion perpendicular to the local magnetic field, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular fast-particle energy is the part of the kinetic energy of the suprathermal particle population associated with motion perpendicular to the local magnetic field. It complements [parallel fast-particle energy](name:parallel_fast_particle_energy) within the total [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy).

It is defined by

$$
W_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_{\mathcal{V}} \int \frac{1}{2} m v_\perp^2 f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\,d^3r
$$

where $\mathcal{V}$ is the plasma volume, $f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})$ is the fast-particle phase-space distribution, $m$ is particle mass, and $v_\perp$ is the speed component perpendicular to the local magnetic field. For a gyrotropic distribution, the corresponding energy density is the perpendicular pressure, so the quantity equals the volume integral of [perpendicular fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), summed over the included fast-particle species.

sources.enhanced_context: Perpendicular energy content of fast (non-thermal) particles, defined as 3/2 times the volume integral of the fast perpendicular pressure. Quantifies the energy stored in the perpendicular degree of freedom of the fast particle population.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fast particles perpendicular energy content = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the fast perpendicular pressure

NAMES.name: poloidal_angle_of_beam_tracing_beam
NAMES.short: Poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam point in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, locating each trajectory position angularly about the magnetic axis.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam is the geometric angular coordinate of each successive point along a wave propagation trajectory in the poloidal $(R, Z)$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This spatial position angle locates where the beam lies in the poloidal cross-section at each step along its path, in contrast to [poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam](name:poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), which encodes the wave-vector propagation direction rather than the geometric beam location.

For a beam-tracing point at coordinates $(R, Z)$ with the magnetic axis at $(R_\mathrm{axis}, Z_\mathrm{axis})$, the angle follows the general [poloidal_angle](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface) construction:

$$
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}(Z - Z_\mathrm{axis},\; R - R_\mathrm{axis})
$$

where $R$, $Z$, $R_\mathrm{axis}$, and $Z_\mathrm{axis}$ are in meters and $\operatorname{atan2}(y, x)$ is the quadrant-aware arctangent.

In beam-tracing calculations, $\theta$ is evaluated at each discrete point along the computed ray path, allowing the beam deposition profile to be mapped onto poloidal-angle coordinates for comparison with profiles sampled at similar [poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position](name:poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position) values. Values span $(-\pi, \pi]$ rad, with $\theta = 0$ at the outboard midplane, $\theta = \pi/2$ rad at the top of the plasma, and $\theta = \pm\pi$ rad at the inboard midplane.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the beam-tracing point is above the horizontal plane through the magnetic axis ($Z > Z_\mathrm{axis}$).

sources.enhanced_context: Poloidal angle (θ) coordinate at each point along a ray or beam propagation path in the beam tracing calculation. Locates the beam trace in poloidal space within the wave propagation geometry.
sources.leaf_definition: Poloidal angle
sources.parent_definition: Position of the ray/beam along its path

NAMES.name: poloidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
NAMES.short: Poloidal angle of an electron-cyclotron beam is the steering angular coordinate of its mean wave-vector direction in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured from inward radial toward downward vertical.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal angle of an electron-cyclotron beam is the steering angular coordinate of the beam mean wave-vector direction at launch, projected into a poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the [poloidal angle](name:poloidal_angle) of the projected propagation direction, not the poloidal coordinate of a spatial point.

For a beam mean wave vector with radial and vertical components $k_R$ and $k_Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the angle is

$$
\theta_\mathrm{pol}=\operatorname{atan2}(-k_Z,\,-k_R)
$$

where $\theta_\mathrm{pol}$ is the poloidal angle, $k_R$ is the [radial wave-vector component], $k_Z$ is the [vertical wave-vector component](name:vertical_wave_vector), and $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ returns the quadrant-resolved principal value for the ordered pair $(x,y)$. The angle is zero for a projected beam direction along inward $-\hat{R}$ and equals $\pi/2$ for a projected beam direction along downward $-\hat{Z}$.

This quantity describes the electron-cyclotron beam steering direction at the launch point and does not locate a point on the beam trajectory. It is distinct from [poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam](name:poloidal_angle_of_beam_tracing_beam), which is the angular coordinate of successive trajectory positions, and complementary to [toroidal angle of the electron cyclotron beam](name:toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), which describes the toroidal component of the same steering direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the poloidal projection of the beam mean wave vector is rotated from the inward radial direction $-\hat{R}$ toward the downward vertical direction $-\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_wave_electric_field
NAMES.short: Complex phasor of the wave electric field projected onto a magnetic flux-surface normal directed toward increasing flux label, preserving local amplitude, phase, and normal polarization.
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-normal wave electric field is the complex phasor obtained by projecting the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the unit normal of a local magnetic flux surface. It preserves the local amplitude, phase, and polarization associated with that normal direction.

The defining projection is

$$
\tilde E_{\psi}(\mathbf r)=\tilde{\mathbf E}(\mathbf r)\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}_{\psi}(\mathbf r),\qquad \hat{\mathbf n}_{\psi}(\mathbf r)=\frac{\nabla\psi(\mathbf r)}{|\nabla\psi(\mathbf r)|}
$$

where $\tilde E_{\psi}$ and $\tilde{\mathbf E}$ are electric-field phasors in V m$^{-1}$, $\mathbf r$ is position in m, $\psi$ is a scalar magnetic flux-surface label, and $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\psi}$ is a dimensionless unit normal.

This projection is geometric and is not the major-radius component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is a component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field) and differs from the field-aligned [parallel wave electric field](name:parallel_wave_electric_field).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projection is along $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\psi}$, directed toward increasing flux label.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volumetric coherent-wave power density absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population. It is the local rate of coherent-wave energy deposition into thermal electrons per unit plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron power density is the time-averaged volumetric rate at which a coherent wave transfers energy to the bulk thermal electron population. It represents electron heating by wave absorption, distinct from power deposited directly into fast electrons, ions, or other nonthermal populations.

For a monochromatic wave, the cycle-averaged absorbed power density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{th},e}=\left\langle \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{th},e}(t)\cdot\mathbf{E}(t)\right\rangle_t = \frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{Re}\!\left[\tilde{\mathbf{J}}_{\mathrm{th},e}\cdot\tilde{\mathbf{E}}^{*}\right]
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},e}$ is the thermal electron power density, $\mathbf{E}$ is the wave electric field, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{th},e}$ is the induced current density associated with thermal electrons, $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes an average over a wave period, tildes denote peak-amplitude phasors, and $^{*}$ denotes complex conjugation. If rms phasor amplitudes are used instead, the factor $1/2$ is omitted.

This quantity is the thermal-electron channel of coherent-wave power absorption and is a component of the aggregate [electron power density](name:electron_power_density) when the energy balance includes coherent-wave transfer to thermal electrons. It excludes coherent-wave power deposited directly into [fast electron power density](name:fast_electron_power_density), ions, or non-electron species. The cumulative thermal-electron wave power in a plasma volume is the volume integral of $p_{\mathrm{th},e}$; for a flux-surface-bounded volume this corresponds to [thermal electron power at inside flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).
NAMES.sign: Positive when coherent-wave energy is transferred from the wave field to the bulk thermal electron population.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Toroidal Fourier-mode component of the coherent-wave power density absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal Fourier component of the [thermal electron power density](name:thermal_electron_power_density), representing coherent-wave energy deposition into bulk thermal electrons for one toroidal mode number. It excludes absorption by ions, fast particles, and other nonthermal populations.

At fixed position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the component is defined by

$$
\tilde{p}_{e,n_\phi}(R,Z)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi}p_e(R,\phi,Z)\,e^{-i n_\phi\phi}\,d\phi
$$

where $p_e$ is the thermal-electron absorbed power density, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal mode number, $R$ is major radius, and $Z$ is vertical height. The Fourier normalization and inverse-mode summation must be consistent with this definition; a single mode is not the toroidally integrated absorbed power.

sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the electrons

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net non-transport volumetric energy source rate for the thermal-ion channel, giving local coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk Maxwellian ion population and summed over included thermal-ion species and all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Thermal ion power density is the net non-transport volumetric energy source rate for the thermal-ion channel, giving the local coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk Maxwellian ion population. It is the absorbed-wave contribution associated with [ion power density](name:ion_power_density) for thermal ions, not the full ion thermal-channel source term from all heating and loss mechanisms.

For a complex-amplitude wave representation, the local time-averaged absorbed-wave density is the toroidal-mode sum of the electromagnetic work on the thermal-ion response:

$$
P_i^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_n P_{i,n}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}), \qquad P_{i,n}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{Re}\!\left[\mathbf{J}_{i,n}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \mathbf{E}_n^*(\mathbf{x})\right]
$$

where $P_i^{\mathrm{th}}$ is this thermal ion power density and $P_{i,n}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is its $n$th toroidal-mode contribution, each in W m$^{-3}$; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode index for angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\mathbf{E}_n$ is the complex wave electric-field amplitude; $\mathbf{J}_{i,n}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the induced current density associated with the thermal-ion response; $^*$ denotes complex conjugation; and $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the real part.

This quantity is extensive in the ion population: it is summed over included thermal-ion species and, for each species, over all charge states; [thermal ion charge-state power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density) denotes the corresponding charge-state-resolved density. It excludes power deposited directly into electrons or nonthermal fast ions, subsequent collisional energy transfer into thermal ions, and transport-flux divergence. The corresponding volume integral is [thermal ion absorbed wave power](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power), and the toroidal-mode contribution is [per-toroidal-mode thermal ion power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_power_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when coherent-wave energy is converted into thermal-ion internal energy.

NAMES.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal-Fourier-mode-resolved coherent-wave power density absorbed by the bulk thermal-ion population, with modal contributions partitioning total thermal-ion absorption.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the contribution associated with one toroidal Fourier mode to the local coherent-wave power density absorbed by bulk thermal ions. It resolves [thermal ion power density](name:thermal_ion_power_density) by toroidal mode number while retaining the same spatial convention.

The modal contributions are defined to reconstruct the total thermal-ion absorption:

$$
p_{\mathrm{th},i}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_n p_{\mathrm{th},i,n}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the total thermal-ion absorbed-wave power density, $p_{\mathrm{th},i,n}$ is the contribution from toroidal mode number $n$, and $\mathbf{x}$ denotes the evaluation position or spatial averaging domain. The toroidal mode number $n$ labels Fourier harmonics in the toroidal angle $\phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Only energy deposited in the bulk Maxwellian ion population is included; direct absorption by electrons and fast ions is excluded. Charge-state-resolved contributions are represented separately by [per-toroidal-mode thermal ion charge-state power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density), while fast-ion deposition is distinct from [per-toroidal-mode fast ion power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density).

NAMES.name: wave_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Magnetic-field perturbation carried by a coherent electromagnetic wave, distinct from equilibrium and static plasma or external-coil magnetic fields.
NAMES.long:
The wave magnetic field designates the oscillatory magnetic-field perturbation associated with a coherent electromagnetic wave. It is distinct from the equilibrium and static contributions included in the complete [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field), and provides the parent quantity for directional components such as the [parallel wave magnetic field](name:parallel_wave_magnetic_field).

For a harmonic wave, the physical field is represented by

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},t)=\operatorname{Re}\left\{\widetilde{\mathbf{B}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)e^{-i\omega t}\right\}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $t$ is time, $\omega$ is angular frequency, and $\widetilde{\mathbf{B}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex magnetic-field amplitude; the field has tesla units. Real- and imaginary-part quantities are separate phase-resolved representations, not alternate definitions of this field.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved wave magnetic-field component points along its declared positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Array of values for normal.
sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Magnitude of wave magnetic field normal to a flux surface, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: parallel_wave_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Signed component of the oscillatory electromagnetic-wave magnetic perturbation along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction, distinct from the total parallel magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the field-aligned component of the oscillatory magnetic perturbation carried by a coherent electromagnetic wave. It excludes equilibrium and other static magnetic-field contributions.

The component is defined by

$$
B_{\rm parallel}^{\rm wave} = \delta\mathbf{B}_{\rm wave} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_{\rm wave}$ is the wave magnetic-field perturbation and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq} = \mathbf{B}_{\rm eq}/|\mathbf{B}_{\rm eq}|$ is the local unit vector along the equilibrium magnetic field. It is a component of the parent [wave magnetic field](name:wave_magnetic_field), not its magnitude or a complex-quadrature part. Unlike [parallel magnetic field](name:parallel_magnetic_field), it does not include the equilibrium field.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the wave magnetic-field perturbation points in the direction of the local equilibrium magnetic-field unit vector.

sources.enhanced_context: Array of values for parallel.
sources.leaf_definition: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Parallel (to the static magnetic field) component of the wave magnetic field, given on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: absorbed_radiated_power_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Net photon power deposited on one divertor target surface after subtracting radiative power reflected from that surface.
NAMES.long:
Absorbed radiated power at a divertor target is the net photon-energy rate deposited on one specified target surface. It includes incident radiative energy absorbed by the target and excludes the reflected portion.

The net absorbed radiative power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}} = P_{\mathrm{inc,rad}} - P_{\mathrm{ref,rad}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}}$ is the absorbed radiated power, $P_{\mathrm{inc,rad}}$ is the incident radiative power reaching the target, and $P_{\mathrm{ref,rad}}$ is the radiative power reflected from the target.

This quantity applies to one divertor target and excludes conductive, convective, charged-particle, and other nonradiative deposition channels. Summation over all divertor targets gives [power of the divertor due to radiation](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_radiation); the broader radiative deposition concept is described by [power due to radiation](name:power_due_to_radiation).

sources.enhanced_context: Net radiated power deposited on a divertor target, defined as incident radiative power minus the reflected fraction. Used in divertor power balance and radiation load assessments.
sources.leaf_definition: Net radiated power on this divertor target (incident - reflected)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: charge_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of the second to first ionic charge moments, measuring impurity content relative to the electron population in a quasineutral plasma.
NAMES.long:
Effective charge is the charge-squared-weighted ionic content of a plasma, normalized by its total positive charge. It equals unity for a pure singly charged hydrogenic plasma and increases when higher-charge ions contribute.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{\sum_i n_i Z_i} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{n_e}
$$

Here, $n_i$ is the number density of ion species or charge state $i$, $Z_i$ is its positive integer charge number, and $n_e$ is the free-electron number density; the second equality uses quasineutrality. The sums include charged ion populations evaluated at the same location, while neutral atoms and molecules are excluded.

The [effective charge at the divertor target](name:effective_charge_at_divertor_target) is a spatially specialized instance of this general effective-charge quantity.

NAMES.name: current_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Net conventional electric current delivered by the plasma to one divertor target surface, integrated over the wetted strike zone.
NAMES.long:
Current at a divertor target is the net conventional electric current delivered to one divertor target by charged particles crossing the plasma sheath and striking the wetted strike zone. It is a surface-integrated signed charge flux, not a local current density, and represents the per-target contribution to the divertor and wall-current balance.

For a local target surface normal chosen from the plasma toward the material surface, the sheath-edge current integrated over the wetted area can be written as:

$$
I_{\mathrm{div,target}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wet}}} \left(j_{i,n} - j_{e,n}\right)\,dA
$$

where $j_{i,n}$ is the ion conventional-current density normal to the target surface in A m$^{-2}$, $j_{e,n}$ is the magnitude of the electron collection current density normal to the target surface in A m$^{-2}$, $dA$ is the differential target area in m$^2$, and $A_{\mathrm{wet}}$ is the wetted strike-zone area in m$^2$. The resulting integrated current is in A; the electron term is subtracted because electrons moving from the plasma to the target carry conventional current opposite to their particle motion.

The current may be measured with embedded Langmuir probes, segmented target current shunts, or Rogowski-coil arrangements around target structures, and may also be inferred from sheath models using local target plasma conditions such as [electron density at divertor target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target) and [electron temperature at divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target). It is closely related to deposited divertor power because the same sheath and strike-zone conditions govern both charge and energy fluxes, as represented by [power at divertor target](name:deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current) and [power of divertor].

For an electrically floating target in steady conditions, the net integrated current is expected to be near 0 A because ion and electron current contributions balance through the sheath. Non-zero values occur with target biasing, transient edge events, current-sharing between conducting structures, or disruption halo-current phases; the single-target value is not the total plasma current $I_p$ but may be assessed relative to $|I_p|$ when evaluating global current closure. No device-independent numerical range is implied, because the magnitude depends strongly on target geometry, electrical connection, plasma regime, and transient scenario.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net conventional current flows from the plasma into the divertor target surface.

NAMES.name: current_of_divertor
NAMES.short: Net conventional electric current carried by charged particles into all divertor target surfaces, including signed electron and ion contributions.
NAMES.long:
The total divertor current is the algebraic conventional current delivered by charged particles crossing the plasma-facing surfaces of the complete divertor assembly. It includes ion and electron contributions and excludes neutral-particle flux and displacement current.

The current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \sum_s q_s\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the total current in A, $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of divertor target surfaces, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is conventional charged-particle current density in A m$^{-2}$, $q_s$ is the signed charge of species $s$ in C, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s$ is its particle flux density in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ points from the plasma toward the material.

This assembly-integrated quantity differs from [current at a divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target), which applies to one target, and [current of a divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile), which applies to an individual tile.
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional charged-particle current flows from the plasma into the divertor material.

sources.enhanced_context: Total electric current (I) incident on a divertor, summed over all targets. Represents the net current carried by charged particles striking the divertor surfaces, relevant to divertor plasma-wall interaction studies.

NAMES.name: current_of_divertor_tile
NAMES.short: Net electric current flowing from the plasma across the electrostatic sheath onto the plasma-facing surface of an individual divertor tile.
NAMES.long:
The current of a divertor tile is the net electric current flowing from the plasma across the electrostatic sheath onto the plasma-facing surface of a single tile. It provides tile-resolved resolution of the current distribution across the divertor strike zone, complementing the target-integrated quantity [current_at_divertor_target](name:current_at_divertor_target).

The tile current integrates the local net sheath current density $j_s$ over the plasma-facing tile area $A_\mathrm{tile}$:

$$
I_\mathrm{tile} = \int_{A_\mathrm{tile}} j_s \, dA
$$

where $j_s$ depends on the local ion saturation current density, the tile-to-plasma sheath potential, and the local [electron temperature at the divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target). Dividing by the tile area, available from [surface_area_of_divertor_tile](name:surface_area_of_divertor_tile), converts this quantity to a mean incident current density.

Tile currents are measured using isolated tile circuits or embedded Langmuir probes whose signals are routed through the mechanical tile support structure, enabling time-resolved acquisition during plasma operation including transient ELM events.

Summing contributions from all tiles on a given target recovers [current_at_divertor_target](name:current_at_divertor_target), and summing over all targets gives [current_of_divertor](name:current_of_divertor). Tile-level current data are used to diagnose thermoelectric current loops, local erosion hot spots, and strike-zone asymmetries driven by 3D magnetic perturbations.
NAMES.sign: Positive when net electric current flows from the plasma onto the tile surface.

NAMES.name: density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Number density of a specified plasma species or species group at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume immediately upstream of the sheath at the target-facing plasma boundary. For ionic species it is summed over all positive ionization states; neutrals are excluded unless explicitly named.
NAMES.long:
Number density of a specified plasma species or species group at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the divertor-target instance of [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

The local number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_\alpha = \frac{dN_\alpha}{dV}
$$

where $N_\alpha$ is the number of particles belonging to species or species group $\alpha$ in a small plasma volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the divertor target.

For an ionic species-level subject, $N_\alpha$ is summed over all positive ionization states of that species; neutral atoms and molecules are excluded unless the subject explicitly denotes neutrals. [ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:ion_density_at_divertor_target) is the ionic specialization of this quantity, while [total_ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:total_ion_density_at_divertor_target) aggregates the particle densities of all ion species without charge-state weighting. This quantity is a particle number density, not a charge density.

NAMES.name: argon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Argon density at the divertor target is the local number density of argon ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is summed over Ar1+ through Ar18+ and excludes neutral argon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Argon density at the divertor target is the local number density of argon ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the argon-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local number density is defined by the differential particle count summed over argon charge states:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{q=1}^{18} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number of argon ions in charge state $q+$ in a small plasma volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the divertor target.

This quantity includes the positive argon ionization stages $\mathrm{Ar}^{1+}$ through $\mathrm{Ar}^{18+}$ and excludes neutral argon atoms. It is a particle number density, not a charge density; charge states are counted by particles rather than weighted by ionic charge.

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Local number density of beryllium ions evaluated in the plasma adjacent to the divertor target surface, summed over Be1+ through Be4+ and excluding neutral beryllium atoms.
NAMES.long:
Beryllium density at the divertor target is the local number density of beryllium ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to the divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is a species-specific component of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target), with neutral beryllium excluded.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}} = \sum_{Z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{Z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the total beryllium-ion number density and $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{Z+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions with charge state $Z+$; the sum includes Be1+ through Be4+. This species-specific quantity complements [boron_density_at_divertor_target](name:boron_density_at_divertor_target) and the local [beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density).
