NAMES.name: boron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Number density of boron ions at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume immediately upstream of the sheath, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral boron.
NAMES.long:
Number density of boron ions at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the boron-specific instance of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the number of boron ions in all positive ionization states and $V$ is a small plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the divertor target.

Neutral boron atoms are excluded, and the quantity does not include other ion species. This species-specific scope distinguishes it from [total_ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:total_ion_density_at_divertor_target); the same target-locus convention is used by [argon_density_at_divertor_target](name:argon_density_at_divertor_target) for argon ions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the local boron ion population contributes particles to the plasma volume.

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Carbon density at the divertor target is the local number density of carbon ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is summed over C1+ through C6+ and excludes neutral carbon atoms and carbon-bearing neutral molecules.
NAMES.long:
Carbon density at the divertor target is the local number density of carbon ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the carbon-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) and the carbon ionic specialization of [ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:ion_density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed carbon ion density is defined by summing the densities of the positive carbon ionization states:

$$
n_{\mathrm{C},t} = \sum_{q=1}^{6} n_{\mathrm{C}^{q+},t}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{C},t}$ is the carbon ion density at the divertor target, $n_{\mathrm{C}^{q+},t}$ is the density of carbon ions with charge state $q$ at the same locus, and $q=1$ and $q=6$ denote singly ionized and fully stripped carbon, respectively.

The sum includes carbon ions from $\mathrm{C}^{1+}$ through $\mathrm{C}^{6+}$, excludes neutral carbon atoms and carbon-bearing neutral molecules, and counts particles rather than ionic charge. It contributes as a species-resolved component of [total_ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:total_ion_density_at_divertor_target), which aggregates ion particle densities over species without charge-state weighting.

NAMES.name: deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current
NAMES.short: Deposited power at a divertor target due to halo current is the electrical work rate delivered to one divertor target by halo current crossing its plasma-facing surface.
NAMES.long:
Deposited power at a divertor target due to halo current is the electrical work rate delivered to one divertor target by halo current crossing the plasma-facing target surface. Halo current is current in the edge or scrape-off-layer plasma that closes through conducting plasma-facing structures; this quantity selects only its contribution to current-driven target loading.

For a target surface with defined local current density and potential drop, the target-surface definition is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{halo},t} = \int_{A_t} j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}(\mathbf{r})\,\Delta\Phi_t(\mathbf{r})\,dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{halo},t}$ is this deposited power, $A_t$ is the portion of the plasma-facing target surface intercepted by halo current, $dA$ is a target-surface area element, $j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}$ is the conventional halo-current density projected on the local unit normal directed from the plasma into the target material, and $\Delta\Phi_t = \Phi_{\mathrm{plasma}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the local plasma-to-target potential drop.

The surface integral of $j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}$ over $A_t$ is the halo-current contribution to [current at divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target). This quantity excludes the conductive, convective, radiative, and neutral-particle target-power channels, and excludes current-driven target power not produced by halo current; together with other current-driven components it is part of [power at divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target), while sums over divertor targets contribute to [power of divertor](name:power_of_divertor). It is zero when no halo-current electrical work is deposited on the target; positive values denote net energy deposition on that target.
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional halo current crosses from the plasma into the target along the plasma-to-material surface normal across a positive plasma-to-target potential drop.

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Deuterium density at the divertor target is the local number density of deuterium ions in the plasma adjacent to the target surface, summed over positive atomic charge states and excluding neutral deuterium.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium density at the divertor target is the local number density of deuterium ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the deuterium-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_D = \frac{dN_D}{dV}
$$

where $N_D$ is the number of deuterium ions in a small plasma volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side. The deuterium ion population is summed over positive atomic deuterium charge states, which reduces to the singly charged D+ population; neutral deuterium atoms and molecules are excluded. [hydrogen_density_at_divertor_target](name:hydrogen_density_at_divertor_target) provides the analogous hydrogen-isotope quantity.

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Deuterium-tritium density at the divertor target is the local number density of deuterium and tritium fuel ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is summed over the positive atomic ionization states of both isotopes, D+ and T+, and excludes neutral atoms and molecules.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-tritium density at the divertor target is the local number density of deuterium and tritium fuel ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the deuterium-tritium-specific member of [density at the divertor target](name:density_at_divertor_target) and the corresponding species-group instance of [ion density at the divertor target](name:ion_density_at_divertor_target).

The combined target fuel-ion density is defined by the differential particle count of the deuterium and tritium atomic ion populations at the same target location:

$$
n_{\mathrm{DT},t} = \frac{d\left(N_{\mathrm{D}^+}+N_{\mathrm{T}^+}\right)}{dV} = n_{\mathrm{D}^+,t}+n_{\mathrm{T}^+,t}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{D}^+}$ and $N_{\mathrm{T}^+}$ are the numbers of deuterium and tritium atomic ions in a small plasma volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the divertor target, $n_{\mathrm{D}^+,t}$ is the [deuterium density at the divertor target](name:deuterium_density_at_divertor_target), and $n_{\mathrm{T}^+,t}$ is the [tritium density at the divertor target](name:tritium_density_at_divertor_target).

For the atomic deuterium and tritium species, summing over all positive ionization states reduces to the singly ionized states $\mathrm{D}^+$ and $\mathrm{T}^+$. Neutral deuterium or tritium atoms, neutral molecules, and explicitly molecule-specific populations are excluded. This quantity contributes additively to [total ion density at the divertor target](name:total_ion_density_at_divertor_target) together with other positive-ion species, and it is a particle number density rather than a charge density. Its limiter counterpart is [deuterium-tritium density at the limiter](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter).

NAMES.name: effective_charge_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Effective ionic charge of the plasma immediately upstream of a divertor-target sheath, combining all positive ion species through charge moments.
NAMES.long:
Effective charge at a divertor target is the local charge-squared-weighted ionic content of the plasma adjacent to the target, evaluated at the sheath entrance. It characterizes impurity content relative to the total positive charge density.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{\sum_i n_i Z_i}
$$

where $n_i$ is the local number density of positive-ion species $i$ and $Z_i$ is its positive integer charge state. The sums include all positive ion species and charge states represented in the local plasma. The quantity equals unity for a pure singly charged hydrogenic plasma and increases when higher-charge ions contribute.

This effective-charge interpretation is the charge-moment form of [charge at the divertor target](name:charge_at_divertor_target), with the same target-local plasma scope; it is not a density or a charge-state-specific abundance.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron density at the divertor target is the local number density of free electrons in the plasma immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath.
NAMES.long:
Electron density at the divertor target is the local number density of free electrons in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the electron-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local electron number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_e = \frac{dN_e}{dV}
$$

where $N_e$ is the number of free electrons and $V$ is the enclosing plasma volume. The volume approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity includes free electrons in the plasma and excludes electrons bound in neutral atoms or molecules and electrons in the target material. It complements [electron_temperature_at_divertor_target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), which characterizes the electron energy distribution at the same sheath entrance.

NAMES.name: fluence_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Cumulative particle dose delivered to a divertor target surface over a specified time interval, equal to the time integral of the incident normal particle flux density summed over all contributing particle species.
NAMES.long:
Fluence at the divertor target is the total accumulated particle dose on the target surface over a time interval $[t_1, t_2]$, defined as:

$$
\Phi = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \Gamma_\perp \, dt
$$

where $\Gamma_\perp$ is the particle flux density incident normal to the target surface and $t_1$, $t_2$ are the start and end of the exposure window. The result represents the total number of particles arriving per unit target area during that interval.

[Ion fluence at the divertor target](name:ion_fluence_at_divertor_target) is the primary child quantity, accumulating the ion particle dose summed over all ion species and charge states. Other particle populations — electrons and fast neutrals — constitute additional child quantities within this parent scope.

This quantity is a surface-normal-integrated particle dose and carries no energy weighting; for instantaneous energy deposition per unit area see [energy_flux_at_divertor_target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: flux_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Flux at a divertor target is the local scalar surface density of power deposited on a divertor target surface, independent of how the incident energy carriers are decomposed.
NAMES.long:
Flux at a divertor target is the local scalar surface density of power deposited on a divertor target surface. It represents the target-surface load itself, without assigning that load to a particular carrier species, radiation component, or transport mechanism.

The target-surface flux is defined as the surface-area density of deposited power:

$$
F_{\mathrm{t}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{dep}}}{dA_{\mathrm{t}}}
$$

where $F_{\mathrm{t}}$ is the flux at surface point $\mathbf{x}$, $P_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the power deposited into the divertor target material, and $A_{\mathrm{t}}$ is area on the divertor target surface.

This name is an umbrella for scalar divertor-target deposited-flux quantities; the explicit energy-load specialization is [energy flux at divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target). It excludes upstream fluxes, volume power densities, and signed vector flux components. Channel-resolved contributions are distinct quantities unless a more specific standard name states that decomposition.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Energy flux at the divertor target is the local energy deposition rate per unit target-surface area from electron and ion conductive heat transport, charged-particle convective enthalpy, neutral-particle bombardment, and locally absorbed radiation.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at the divertor target is the local rate of energy deposition per unit area on a divertor target surface by incident particles and radiation. It combines electron and ion conductive heat transfer, charged-particle convective enthalpy, neutral-particle energy deposition, and radiation absorbed locally at the surface.

The total deposited energy flux is the algebraic sum of the contributing surface energy-flux channels:

$$
q_\mathrm{tgt} = q_\mathrm{cond} + q_\mathrm{conv} + q_\mathrm{neut} + q_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $q_\mathrm{tgt}$ is the energy flux at the divertor target, $q_\mathrm{cond}$ is the [conductive contribution], $q_\mathrm{conv}$ is the [convective contribution], $q_\mathrm{neut}$ is the neutral-particle bombardment contribution, and $q_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{abs}}$ is the [locally absorbed radiation contribution].

This quantity is a local surface flux density, not an area-integrated divertor-target power; integration over a specified target surface gives [power at the divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target), and the largest local value is [maximum energy flux at the divertor target](name:maximum_of_energy_flux_at_divertor_target). It excludes energy lost before reaching the target and incident particles or radiation that do not transfer energy to the target material.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the surface-normal energy flux points along the target-surface normal directed from the incident plasma toward the target material.

NAMES.name: flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling
NAMES.short: Rate at which recycling at divertor plasma-facing surfaces returns a transported quantity to the plasma, with the channel specified by a more specific quantity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the divertor-local contribution to the recycling flux: the rate at which recycling at divertor plasma-facing surfaces returns a channel-specific transported amount to the plasma. The channel may be particle content, energy, momentum, or another quantity defined by a more specific standard name such as [particle flux of divertor due to recycling](name:particle_flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling).

For a scalar transported amount $Q$, the divertor recycling rate is defined by

$$
\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{div,rec}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \mathbf{j}_{Q,\mathrm{return}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{plasma}}\,\mathrm{d}S
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the divertor plasma-facing surface, $\mathbf{j}_{Q,\mathrm{return}}$ is the returning surface flux of $Q$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ points from the surface toward the plasma. It is the divertor-specific component of [flux due to recycling](name:flux_due_to_recycling), and is distinct from a total recycling rate summed over all divertor targets.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Number density of helium-3 ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target, summed over both ionization stages (singly ionized and fully stripped) and excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.
NAMES.long:
Helium-3 density at a divertor target is the local number density of ionized helium-3 in the plasma adjacent to a plasma-facing divertor surface. It covers both helium-3 ionization stages — the singly ionized ($\mathrm{He3}^{1+}$) and the fully stripped ($\mathrm{He3}^{2+}$) — and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms. This quantity is a species-resolved instance of the [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) family, which abstracts over all species present at the target.

The total helium-3 ion density is defined as:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He3}} = \sum_{z=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He3}}^{z+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He3}}^{z+}$ is the local density of helium-3 in charge state $z+$ in the plasma layer immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath entrance at the target surface.

This quantity is inferred from spectroscopic measurements of characteristic helium-3 line emission combined with local ionization-balance calculations, or from edge-transport simulations constrained by particle-balance diagnostics. Helium-3 reaches the divertor target following transport through the scrape-off layer, originating either from advanced D-He3 fuel-cycle scenarios or from injected tracer gas. The helium-4 analog is [helium_4_density_at_divertor_target](name:helium_4_density_at_divertor_target); the spatial profile of the same species across the confined plasma is represented by [helium_3_density](name:helium_3_density).

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Number density of helium-4 ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target, summed over singly and doubly ionized helium-4 charge states and excluding neutral helium-4 atoms.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 density at the divertor target is the local number density of ionized helium with mass number 4 in the plasma immediately adjacent to the material target surface. It is summed over the two ionization stages — singly ionized $\text{He}^{1+}$ and fully stripped $\text{He}^{2+}$ — and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms, consistent with the [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) convention that ionic species are summed over all charge states.

The charge-state-summed density is defined as:

$$
n_{\text{He-4}} = n_{\text{He}^{1+}} + n_{\text{He}^{2+}}
$$

where $n_{\text{He}^{1+}}$ and $n_{\text{He}^{2+}}$ are the number densities of the individual charge states. In deuterium–tritium burning plasmas, helium-4 is the dominant fusion ash originating from thermalized alpha particles; its concentration at the divertor target directly reflects the efficiency of ash exhaust by the divertor pumping system. Insufficient helium removal causes ash accumulation and progressive fuel dilution in the core. The quantity is inferred from spectroscopic or charge-exchange recombination measurements in the divertor region. The analogous helium isotope quantity at this surface is [helium_3_density_at_divertor_target](name:helium_3_density_at_divertor_target); complementary helium-4 profiles at other locations are given by [helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis) and [helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary).

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Local number density of hydrogen ions evaluated in the plasma adjacent to the divertor target surface, summed over all positive hydrogen ionization charge states and excluding neutral hydrogen atoms and molecules.
NAMES.long:
Hydrogen density at the divertor target is the local number density of hydrogen ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the hydrogen-specific member of [density at the divertor target](name:density_at_divertor_target), with an isotope-specific scope analogous to [deuterium density at the divertor target](name:deuterium_density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}} = \sum_{Z>0} n_{\mathrm{H}}^{(Z)}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen-ion density and $n_{\mathrm{H}}^{(Z)}$ is the density of hydrogen ions with positive ionization charge number $Z$. For hydrogen, the sum contains only the singly ionized state $\mathrm{H}^{+}$.

Neutral hydrogen atoms and hydrogen molecules are excluded; consequently, this quantity is not the total density of hydrogen nuclei in all charge and molecular states.

NAMES.name: ion_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion density at the divertor target is the local number density of a specified positive-ion population near the target, summed over its included charge states at the electrostatic sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Ion density at the divertor target is the local number density of a specified positive-ion population in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the ionic component of [density at the divertor target](name:density_at_divertor_target), excluding neutral atoms, molecules, and free electrons.

For an included population $P$, the charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_P = \sum_{s \in P} \sum_{z=1}^{Z_s} n_{s,z}
$$

where $n_P$ is the ion density, $s$ indexes the included ion species, $z$ is the positive ionization charge state, $Z_s$ is the highest included charge state of species $s$, and $n_{s,z}$ is its local number density.

A species-specific member fixes $P$ to one element, while [total ion density at the divertor target](name:total_ion_density_at_divertor_target) includes all ionic species present locally.

NAMES.name: ion_fluence_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Cumulative incident ion-particle dose delivered to a divertor target, with each ion counted once across all species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Ion fluence at a divertor target is the cumulative number of incident ions per unit target area over a specified time interval. It is the ion-only component of [fluence at the divertor target](name:fluence_at_divertor_target), including all ionic species and charge states while counting each incident ion once.

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \left[\sum_{s\in\mathcal{I}} \Gamma_{\perp,s}(t)\right] \, dt
$$

Here, $\Phi_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the ion fluence, $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the interval endpoints in seconds, $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of included ion species and charge states, and $\Gamma_{\perp,s}$ is the incident normal particle-flux density for state $s$, in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$. The flux is directed from the plasma toward the target surface. Neutral atoms, molecules, and nonparticle channels are excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Positive charge fluence normal to an ideal axisymmetric divertor surface, estimated at the embedded Langmuir probe location. Represents the time-integrated ion charge flux incident on the plasma-facing component.
sources.leaf_definition: Positive charge fluence normal to an ideal axisymmetric surface of the divertor (assuming no shaping), estimated at the probe location.

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Iron density at the divertor target is the local number density of iron ions at the sheath entrance, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral iron.
NAMES.long:
Iron density at the divertor target is the local number density of iron ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the iron-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local iron number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of iron ions and $V$ is a small plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

All positive iron ionization states are included in $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$, while neutral iron atoms are excluded. [ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:ion_density_at_divertor_target) is the corresponding general positive-ion quantity, whereas [iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis) specifies the same iron population at the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Number density of krypton ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target, summed over all krypton ionization charge states from Kr1+ through Kr36+ and excluding neutral krypton atoms.
NAMES.long:
Krypton density at the divertor target is the local number density of ionized krypton in the plasma immediately adjacent to the material target surface, evaluated upstream of the electrostatic sheath entrance. It is the charge-state-summed krypton ion population at that location, excluding neutral krypton atoms, and is a species-resolved instance of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The total krypton ion number density aggregates all 36 bound-electron configurations:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr}} = \sum_{z=1}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}$ is the local number density of krypton ions carrying charge state $z$.

Krypton (atomic number 36) is a noble gas used as a heavy radiative seeding impurity; it radiates efficiently across a broad electron temperature range, redistributing power away from the strike zone and facilitating plasma detachment. The local density at the target reflects the balance between krypton injection, ionization and recombination, cross-field diffusion in the scrape-off layer, parallel transport along field lines, and surface recycling. In attached divertor conditions the krypton ion population peaks farther upstream; in detached conditions, reduced parallel transport can concentrate the ionized fraction closer to the target. This quantity complements [krypton_density](name:krypton_density), which gives the radially resolved density profile, and [carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target) for the analogous charge-state-summed carbon species.

The quantity is inferred from vacuum ultraviolet or extreme ultraviolet emission spectroscopy in the divertor volume, or from edge plasma transport simulations benchmarked against spectroscopic line-ratio diagnostics.

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Number density of lithium ions at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume in the plasma at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is summed over Li+, Li2+, and Li3+; neutral lithium is excluded.
NAMES.long:
Number density of lithium ions at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume in the plasma at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the lithium-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local lithium ion number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the number of lithium ions in a small plasma volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the divertor target.

For this ionic species-level quantity, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is summed over the positive ionization states $\mathrm{Li}^{+}$, $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$, and $\mathrm{Li}^{3+}$; neutral lithium atoms and lithium-bearing neutral molecules are excluded. This quantity is a non-negative particle number density, not a charge density or a charge-state-resolved lithium density.

NAMES.name: maximum_of_energy_flux_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Peak local total energy deposition rate per unit area on the divertor target, obtained by maximizing energy flux over the target surface.
NAMES.long:
The maximum energy flux at a divertor target is the greatest local rate of energy deposition per unit target-surface area over the specified divertor-target surface. It is the peak of the total [energy flux at the divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target), not an integrated deposited power.

The quantity is defined by

$$
q_{E,max} = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in S_{\mathrm{DT}}} q_E(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $q_E(\mathbf{x})$ is the local energy flux at position $\mathbf{x}$ and $S_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the divertor-target surface included in the maximization.

The energy flux includes conductive and convective charged-particle energy transport, neutral-particle energy deposition, and locally absorbed radiation. Unlike [parallel heat flux at the divertor target](name:parallel_heat_flux_at_divertor_target), this maximum represents the total incident energy flux rather than only its field-aligned component. Its surface-maximum role parallels [maximum of energy flux at first wall](name:maximum_of_energy_flux_at_first_wall).

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Number density of neon ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target, summed over all ionization states Ne1+ through Ne10+ and excluding neutral neon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Neon density at the divertor target is the local number density of neon ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to the divertor target surface, covering all ionization stages from Ne1+ through Ne10+ and excluding neutral neon atoms. It is a species-resolved member of the [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) family, evaluated just upstream of the electrostatic sheath entrance at the plasma–material interface.

The charge-state-summed density is defined as:

$$
n_{\text{Ne}} = \sum_{q=1}^{10} n_{\text{Ne}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\text{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the local number density of neon ions in charge state $q+$ at the near-target measurement position.

Neon is injected as a seeding impurity to drive radiative energy dissipation in the divertor volume, lowering the peak heat flux on plasma-facing surfaces. The near-target neon ion density reflects the balance between the seeding source rate, parallel and cross-field transport in the scrape-off layer, ionization, and recombination. In high-recycling or detached regimes the ionization balance shifts toward lower charge states and the sheath-entrance density can differ substantially from the upstream separatrix value. Analogous quantities for alternative seeding species are [nitrogen_density_at_divertor_target](name:nitrogen_density_at_divertor_target) and [xenon_density_at_divertor_target](name:xenon_density_at_divertor_target); the overall impurity content at the target is captured by [effective_charge_at_divertor_target](name:effective_charge_at_divertor_target), and the local [electron_temperature_at_divertor_target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target) governs which neon charge states dominate the ionization distribution.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Nitrogen density at the divertor target is the local number density of nitrogen ions immediately upstream of the sheath, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral nitrogen.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen density at the divertor target is the local number density of nitrogen ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the nitrogen-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local nitrogen number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_N = \frac{dN_N}{dV}
$$

where $N_N$ is the number of nitrogen ions in a small plasma volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the divertor target. The count includes nitrogen ions from N1+ through N7+, summed over all positive ionization states, and excludes neutral nitrogen atoms and nitrogen-bearing neutral molecules. Its target-local scope distinguishes it from [nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis), and it is a particle number density rather than a charge density.

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Number density of oxygen ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target, summed over all ionization charge states O1+ through O8+ and excluding neutral oxygen atoms.
NAMES.long:
Oxygen density at the divertor target is the local number density of ionized oxygen in the plasma next to a divertor target surface. It is the charge-state-summed oxygen ion population per unit volume at the plasma-material interface, spanning all ionization stages from singly ionized O$^{1+}$ through fully stripped O$^{8+}$, and excludes neutral oxygen atoms. As a species-resolved component of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target), it quantifies the oxygen impurity content at the sheath entrance of the divertor.

Oxygen is a low-Z impurity in fusion plasmas, entering through outgassing of vacuum vessel walls, residual water vapor, or erosion of oxide-forming plasma-facing components. Elevated oxygen density at the target enhances radiative power dissipation through line emission from partially stripped ions and raises [effective_charge_at_divertor_target](name:effective_charge_at_divertor_target) above unity, degrading fuel-ion purity. In strongly radiating or detached divertor regimes, distributed oxygen line radiation can partially detach the plasma and redistribute heat loads away from the target surface.

The oxygen ion density at the target is inferred from visible and vacuum-ultraviolet spectroscopy of oxygen emission lines near the divertor, combined with collisional-radiative modeling to relate observed line intensities to the total ion population across charge states. This interpretation requires concurrent knowledge of the local electron temperature and electron density to resolve the charge-state distribution. The oxygen contribution sums into [total_ion_density_at_divertor_target](name:total_ion_density_at_divertor_target) alongside fuel species such as [hydrogen_density_at_divertor_target](name:hydrogen_density_at_divertor_target); the volume-averaged confined-plasma counterpart is [volume_averaged_oxygen_density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density).
