sources.parent_definition: Oxygen (O)

NAMES.name: parallel_heat_flux_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Field-aligned power transported toward a divertor target, expressed per unit area normal to the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel heat-flux density incident on a divertor target is the target-directed component of the plasma energy-flux vector carried along the local magnetic field line. It represents field-aligned energy transport and excludes contributions that are not parallel to the field.

The target-directed component is defined by

$$
q_{\parallel}=\mathbf{q}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{t}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}$ is the plasma energy-flux vector and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{t}$ is the unit vector tangent to the local magnetic field line and directed toward the divertor target. This quantity is a directional component, whereas [energy flux at the divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target) includes all incident energy channels and [flux at the divertor target](name:flux_at_divertor_target) represents total deposited power flux density.
NAMES.sign: Positive when heat is transported along the local magnetic field line toward the divertor target.

sources.enhanced_context: Parallel heat flux (q∥) received by the plasma-facing element monitored by the infrared camera, as a function of distance mapped to the separatrix at the outboard midplane. Used to characterize power exhaust in the scrape-off layer.
sources.leaf_definition: Parallel heat flux received by the element monitored by the camera, along the distance_separatrix_midplane coordinate
sources.parent_definition: Quantities deduced from frame analysis for a set of time slices

NAMES.name: particle_flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling
NAMES.short: Rate at which recycling processes at divertor plasma-facing surfaces return particles to the plasma, encompassing neutral re-emission, molecular gas release, desorption, and ion reflection across the divertor assembly.
NAMES.long:
The particle flux of the divertor due to recycling is the global rate, in particles per second, at which recycling at divertor plasma-facing surfaces replenishes the edge plasma particle inventory. Recycling mechanisms include neutral re-emission, molecular gas release, desorption from the target material, and ion reflection, followed by dissociation or ionization that re-introduces particles into the plasma.

This quantity is the particle-channel specialization of the broader [flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling](name:flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling), which covers energy, momentum, and other transported channels in addition to particle content. It covers all divertor targets collectively; the fully aggregated instance summed over all divertor targets is [total_particle_flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling](name:total_particle_flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling). It excludes particle injection from wall or limiter surfaces, which is described by [source_rate_due_to_surface_emission](name:source_rate_due_to_surface_emission).

NAMES.name: power_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Power at a divertor target is the rate at which energy is deposited on one divertor target by a specified physical deposition channel, integrated over the target's wetted strike-zone surface.
NAMES.long:
Power at a divertor target is the rate at which energy is deposited on one divertor target by a specified physical deposition channel, integrated over the target's wetted strike-zone surface. The specified channel denotes a particular physical contribution to deposition and does not by itself imply an all-channel target total.

The deposited power for target $t$ and channel $c$ is defined from the channel-resolved energy-flux-density vector over that surface:

$$
P_{t,c} = -\int_{A_t} \mathbf{S}_{E,c}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_t(\mathbf{x}) \, dA
$$

where $P_{t,c}$ is the deposited power on target $t$ due to channel $c$, $A_t$ is the target's wetted strike-zone surface, $\mathbf{S}_{E,c}$ is the energy-flux-density vector for channel $c$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_t$ is the normalized surface normal directed from the target material toward the plasma-facing side, $\mathbf{x}$ labels a point on the target surface, and $dA$ is the surface element. The leading minus sign makes flux directed from the plasma toward the target material contribute to the deposited target power.

The channel label may distinguish conductive, convective, particle, radiative, or other deposition mechanisms, but this name does not prescribe a decomposition. For a complete mutually exclusive set of channel contributions on the same target, the channel sum equals the surface integral of the total [energy flux at a divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target); all-channel target powers at the inner and outer divertor targets are represented by [power at inner divertor target](name:power_at_inner_divertor_target) and [power at outer divertor target](name:power_at_outer_divertor_target). Conductive and convective channel contributions are represented by [power at divertor target due to conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction) and [power at divertor target due to convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), respectively.

sources.enhanced_context: Power deposited on a divertor target due to electric currents flowing onto the target surface. A positive value indicates net power deposition from current flow.
sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on this divertor target due to electric currents (positive means power is deposited on the target)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

sources.enhanced_context: Total power incident on a divertor target surface from all physical channels (conducted, convected, radiated, recombination, neutrals, currents). Parent structure partitioned into individual power components in sibling fields.
sources.leaf_definition: Total power incident on this target. This power is split in the various physical categories listed below
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: neutral_power_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Net rate of energy deposited on one divertor target by incident neutral particles, including charge-exchange neutrals and neutral products of volume recombination.
NAMES.long:
Neutral-particle target power is the rate at which neutral atoms or molecules transfer energy to one specified divertor target through bombardment from the plasma. It includes neutrals formed by charge exchange and volume recombination, and is distinct from the charged-particle target power [power at divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target).

$$
P_{\mathrm{n,t}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{t}}} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{n}}^{\mathrm{net}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p\to t}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{n,t}}$ is the deposited neutral-particle power, $A_{\mathrm{t}}$ is the surface area of the specified target, $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{n}}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net neutral energy-flux vector crossing that surface, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p\to t}}$ points from the plasma toward the target material.

The quantity excludes charged-particle sheath power, radiative absorption, and conductive power. Summing the corresponding contributions over all wetted divertor surfaces gives [neutral power of divertor](name:neutral_power_of_divertor); recombination-only contributions are covered by [power at divertor target due to recombination](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination).

sources.enhanced_context: Net power deposited on a divertor target by neutral particles, with positive values indicating power deposition on the target surface. Includes contributions from neutral particle fluxes impinging on the divertor.
sources.leaf_definition: Net power from neutrals on this divertor target (positive means power is deposited on the target)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: power_at_inner_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Total rate of energy deposition on the high-field-side inner divertor target, integrated over its wetted surface and including all incident energy channels.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total power deposited on the wetted surface of the high-field-side inner divertor target by all incident energy channels. It includes the electron and ion contributions represented by [electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target](name:electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target) and [ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target](name:ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target), together with other deposited channels.

The deposited power is defined by the surface integral

$$
P_{\rm in} = \\int_{A_{\rm wet}} \\mathbf{q}_{E} \\cdot \\hat{\\mathbf{n}}_{\rm t} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\rm in}$ is the total target power, $A_{\rm wet}$ is the wetted target surface, $\\mathbf{q}_{E}$ is the total incident energy-flux density described by [energy_flux_at_divertor_target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target), and $\\hat{\\mathbf{n}}_{\rm t}$ points from the plasma toward the target.

This is an instantaneous or interval-specific deposited power, not the maximum over a specified interval represented by [maximum_power_at_inner_divertor_target](name:maximum_power_at_inner_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Rate at which incident electron energy is deposited on the high-field-side inner divertor target, integrated over its wetted strike-zone surface.
NAMES.long:
Electron power at the inner divertor target is the rate at which energy carried by incident electrons is deposited on the high-field-side divertor target surface. It is the electron-channel contribution to the total target load, rather than the combined contribution of all incident energy channels.

The deposited electron power is defined by the surface integral

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{inner}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wet,inner}}} q_{e,\mathrm{dep}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{wet,inner}}$ is the wetted inner-target area, $q_{e,\mathrm{dep}}$ is the electron energy-deposition flux density in W m$^{-2}$, and $dA$ is an element of target surface area in m$^2$. The result is the electron contribution to [power at the inner divertor target](name:power_at_inner_divertor_target); ion energy is represented separately by [ion power at the inner divertor target](name:ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target), while neutral and radiative contributions are excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Electron power deposited on the inner divertor target, a time-resolved global quantity characterising the electron energy flux reaching the inner strike point region. Used in power exhaust and divertor heat load analysis.
sources.leaf_definition: Electron power on the inner target
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to electrons

NAMES.name: ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion power deposited on the inner, high-field-side divertor target is the rate at which incident ion energy is deposited over the wetted target surface.
NAMES.long:
Ion power at the inner divertor target is the rate at which energy carried by incident ions is deposited on the high-field-side target surface. It is the ion-channel contribution to [power at the inner divertor target](name:power_at_inner_divertor_target), distinct from electron, neutral, and radiative contributions.

A common definition is the surface integral of the ion-deposited heat-flux density over the wetted inner-target area:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{inner}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wet,inner}}} q_{i,\mathrm{dep}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{wet,inner}}$ is the wetted inner-target area, $q_{i,\mathrm{dep}}$ is the ion contribution to the deposited heat-flux density, and $dA$ is an element of target surface area. When species resolution is not retained, the ion contribution is summed over the contributing ion species and charge states. The related [total ion power at the inner divertor target](name:total_ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target) is a concrete specialization, while [electron power at the inner divertor target](name:electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target) represents the complementary electron channel.

NAMES.name: maximum_power_at_inner_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Maximum total power deposited on the inner, high-field-side divertor target over a specified interval, integrating all incident energy channels across the wetted strike-zone surface.
NAMES.long:
Maximum power at the inner divertor target is the greatest total rate at which energy is deposited on the high-field-side target surface during a specified time interval. It includes electron, ion, neutral, and radiative contributions integrated over the wetted strike-zone area, rather than a local heat-flux density.

The maximum is defined from the instantaneous quantity [power at the inner divertor target](name:power_at_inner_divertor_target) by

$$
P_{\mathrm{max,inner}} = \max_{t \in [t_1,t_2]} P_{\mathrm{inner}}(t)
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{max,inner}}$ is the maximum target power, $t$ is time, $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the interval endpoints, and $P_{\mathrm{inner}}(t)$ is the total instantaneous deposited power. The total includes the ion contribution represented by [ion power at the inner divertor target](name:ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target).

This quantity is a temporal maximum, not the energy deposited over the interval and not the power at a particular target location.

sources.enhanced_context: Maximum power density (peak heat flux) deposited on the inner divertor target as a global wall interaction metric, as a function of time. A key engineering and physics parameter for divertor thermal load assessment.
sources.leaf_definition: Maximum power density on the inner target
sources.parent_definition: Simple 0D description of plasma-wall interaction

NAMES.name: power_at_outer_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Power at the outer divertor target is the non-negative total rate of energy deposition on the low-field-side divertor target, the target at larger major radius R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height, integrated over its wetted strike-zone surface.
NAMES.long:
Power at the outer divertor target is the non-negative total rate of energy deposition on the low-field-side divertor target, the target at larger major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the all-channel deposited-power total over the wetted strike-zone surface of that single material target.

The deposited power is defined by integrating the local deposited energy-flux density over the wetted area of the outer target:

$$
P_{\mathrm{out}} = \int_{A_{w,\mathrm{out}}} q_{\perp,\mathrm{dep}} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the power at the outer divertor target, $A_{w,\mathrm{out}}$ is the wetted strike-zone area of the outer target, $dA$ is a target-surface area element, and $q_{\perp,\mathrm{dep}}$ is the local deposited energy-flux density through the material surface with the surface normal oriented into the target.

Only energy crossing into and deposited in the outer-target material is counted. This quantity is distinct from the inner-target counterpart [power at the inner divertor target](name:power_at_inner_divertor_target), from mechanism- or species-resolved target powers, and from spatial peak quantities such as [maximum power at the outer divertor target](name:maximum_power_at_outer_divertor_target). The surface-normal convention makes inward deposited energy contribute positively to $q_{\perp,\mathrm{dep}}$; the target-integrated deposited power is non-negative by definition.

NAMES.name: electron_power_at_outer_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target by incident electrons, integrated over the wetted strike-zone surface.
NAMES.long:
Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target by incident electrons integrated over the wetted strike-zone surface is the target-integrated electron energy-transfer rate to the material surface of that target. The outer divertor target is the target on the larger-major-radius side in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The deposited electron power is the surface integral of the local electron energy-flux density directed into the wetted outer-target area:

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{outer}} = \int_{A_{w,\mathrm{outer}}} q_{e,\perp}\,dA
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{outer}}$ is the electron power at the outer divertor target, $A_{w,\mathrm{outer}}$ is the wetted strike-zone area, $dA$ is a target-surface area element, and $q_{e,\perp}$ is the electron energy-flux density directed from the plasma into the target material.

This is the electron-channel component of [power at the outer divertor target](name:power_at_outer_divertor_target); ion, neutral, radiation, and other non-electron contributions are excluded. It is the outer-target counterpart of [electron power at the inner divertor target](name:electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target).

sources.enhanced_context: Electron power deposited on the outer divertor target (P_e,outer), a time-resolved global quantity. Key parameter for divertor heat load assessment and plasma-wall interaction studies.
sources.leaf_definition: Electron power on the inner target
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to electrons

NAMES.name: maximum_power_at_outer_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Maximum total power deposited on the outer divertor target by all incident energy channels over a specified interval, evaluated from the wetted strike-zone power.
NAMES.long:
Maximum total power deposited on the outer divertor target by all incident energy channels over a specified time interval is the largest target-integrated deposited energy-transfer rate attained during that interval. The outer divertor target is the target on the larger-major-radius side in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The maximum is defined from the instantaneous [power at the outer divertor target](name:power_at_outer_divertor_target) by

$$
P_{\mathrm{max,outer}} = \max_{t_1 \leq t \leq t_2} P_{\mathrm{outer}}(t)
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{max,outer}}$ is the maximum deposited power, $P_{\mathrm{outer}}(t)$ is the all-channel power integrated over the wetted outer-target strike zone at time $t$, and $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the bounds of the specified interval, measured in seconds.

This quantity is a temporal maximum, not an instantaneous value, time integral, or average. It is the outer-target counterpart of [maximum power at the inner divertor target](name:maximum_power_at_inner_divertor_target) and remains distinct from mechanism-resolved power or the instantaneous parent quantity.

sources.enhanced_context: Maximum power density (peak heat flux) deposited on the outer divertor target as a function of time. A critical engineering limit for divertor design and plasma-wall interaction studies.
sources.leaf_definition: Maximum power density on the outer target
sources.parent_definition: Simple 0D description of plasma-wall interaction

NAMES.name: power_due_to_conduction
NAMES.short: Thermal power deposited on one or more plasma-facing surfaces by electron and ion conduction along scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines, excluding convective, radiative, and neutral-particle power.
NAMES.long:
Conductive deposited power is thermal power transferred from scrape-off-layer plasma to one or more plasma-facing surfaces by electron and ion heat conduction along magnetic field lines. The selected surface may be an individual target, a divertor assembly, or a collection of wall and divertor surfaces.

The defining surface integral is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{cond}} = \int_S \left(\mathbf{q}_{e,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}} + \mathbf{q}_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the deposited power, $S$ is the selected plasma-facing surface, $\mathbf{q}_{e,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ and $\mathbf{q}_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ are the electron and ion conductive heat-flux vectors, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the plasma toward the material, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is a surface-area element.

The quantity excludes convective enthalpy, radiative absorption, and neutral-particle bombardment. A single-target instance is represented by [power at divertor target due to conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction), while the corresponding all-channel energy flux density is distinguished by [energy flux at divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction
NAMES.short: Thermal power deposited on a single divertor target by parallel electron and ion heat conduction along scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines, excluding convective, radiative, and neutral-particle channels.
NAMES.long:
The power at a divertor target due to conduction is the thermal energy deposited on one divertor target by electron and ion heat conduction along open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines. It excludes convective particle enthalpy, absorbed radiation, recombination, and neutral-particle power, and is the single-target specialization of [power_due_to_conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction).

The deposited conductive power is the normal component of the conductive heat flux integrated over the wetted target area:

$$
P_{\mathrm{cond,target}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{target}}} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the sum of the electron and ion conductive heat-flux vectors, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the plasma toward the target material, and $A_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the wetted target area. Unlike [power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction), this quantity applies to one divertor target rather than the complete divertor assembly.

sources.enhanced_context: Power conducted by the plasma onto a divertor target via thermal conduction. A time-resolved scalar representing the conductive heat flux channel contribution to the total power load on the target.
sources.leaf_definition: Power conducted by the plasma on this divertor target
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: power_due_to_convection
NAMES.short: Power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces by convective plasma particle flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Convective power quantifies the energy transported to a plasma-facing surface by the bulk flow of plasma particles — ions, electrons, and neutral species — streaming along open magnetic field lines from the scrape-off layer to bounding material surfaces. It represents the convective channel of the total surface power balance, distinct from the conductive contribution driven by parallel temperature gradients and from radiative deposition.

The local convective heat-flux density summed over particle species $s$ is

$$
q_{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_s n_s v_{\parallel,s} \left( \frac{\gamma_s}{\gamma_s - 1} k_B T_s + \frac{1}{2} m_s v_{\parallel,s}^2 \right)
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density, $v_{\parallel,s}$ the parallel flow speed, $\gamma_s$ the adiabatic index (5/3 for monatomic species), $T_s$ the temperature, and $m_s$ the particle mass. Integrating $q_{\mathrm{conv}}$ over the wetted surface area yields the total convective power in watts.

In experiments the convective power is inferred from Langmuir-probe measurements of particle flux and sheath-entrance temperature, or decomposed from total calorimetric measurements by subtracting the conductive fraction estimated via two-point model analysis. More specific realizations include [power at a single divertor target due to convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), [convective power summed over all divertor targets](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection), and [convective power at the first wall](name:power_at_wall_due_to_convection). The full surface load integrating all channels is characterized by heat_flux_of_plasma_facing_component.

NAMES.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection
NAMES.short: Power deposited on a single divertor target by convective plasma particle flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Convective power at a single divertor target quantifies the energy transported to that target by plasma particles streaming from the scrape-off layer. It includes thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried into the material surface and is the target-local contribution to [power due to convection](name:power_due_to_convection).

The target-integrated convective power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{conv,target}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{target}}} \sum_s n_s v_{n,s} \left[ \frac{\gamma_s}{\gamma_s-1} k_B T_s + \frac{1}{2}m_s v_{n,s}^{2} \right] \, dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the wetted target surface, $n_s$ is the number density of species $s$, $v_{n,s}$ is its flow speed normal to and into the target, $\gamma_s$ is its adiabatic index, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, $T_s$ is its temperature, and $m_s$ is its particle mass. The species sum includes the particle channels assigned to convective transport and excludes conductive and radiative deposition.

This quantity applies to one target; summing corresponding target contributions gives [convective power of the divertor](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection).

sources.enhanced_context: Power convected by the plasma onto a divertor target surface, representing the kinetic energy flux carried by plasma particle flow (convective heat transport) to the target. Complements the conducted power channel in the total target heat load.
sources.leaf_definition: Power convected by the plasma on this divertor target
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: power_due_to_fusion
NAMES.short: Nuclear fusion reaction energy deposition rate integrated over a specified plasma region or material component. It counts fusion-product energy where it is deposited, not merely where it is released.
NAMES.long:
Nuclear fusion reaction energy deposition rate integrated over a specified plasma region or material component is the rate at which energy whose ultimate source is fuel-ion fusion reactions is transferred to matter within that region or component. It is an extensive deposited-power quantity, so energy is assigned to the place where it is deposited, which may differ from the place where the fusion reaction occurred.

For a specified region or component $\Omega$, the quantity is defined by the local fusion-origin deposition rate density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\Omega) = \int_{\Omega} q_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{fusion,dep}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local rate density of energy deposited at position $\mathbf{x}$ by fusion products, fusion-neutron interactions, and secondary nuclear radiation, and $dV$ is the volume element of $\Omega$.

Each reaction channel contributes according to the partition of its released energy among products. For the deuterium-tritium channel, approximately one fifth of the fusion energy is born in the alpha particle and four fifths in the neutron; this birth partition does not imply local deposition. Charged-product energy is included in a plasma region only for the fraction actually deposited there during slowing down, while escaping charged products or neutrons contribute where they subsequently deposit energy through interactions and secondary radiation.

This name is distinct from [power density due to fusion](name:power_density_due_to_fusion), which denotes local fusion energy release rate before nonlocal transport, and from [neutron power](name:neutron_power), which tracks energy carried by neutrons rather than deposited energy in $\Omega$. [Power due to neutron interaction] is the neutron-interaction contribution when the interacting neutrons originate from fusion. The divertor specializations [deposited power of divertor due to fusion](name:deposited_power_of_divertor_due_to_fusion) and [power of divertor due to fusion](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_fusion) restrict $\Omega$ to the divertor; non-fusion heat loads such as conduction, plasma radiation, charge-exchange neutrals, and externally supplied heating are excluded.

NAMES.name: power_due_to_radiation
NAMES.short: Power due to radiation is the net rate at which photon energy is absorbed by a specified plasma-facing surface or assembly after reflected photon energy is excluded.
NAMES.long:
Power due to radiation is the net rate at which photon energy from plasma radiation is absorbed by a specified plasma-facing surface or assembly. It represents the radiative contribution to the surface heat load after excluding photon energy reflected by the material.

For a plasma-facing surface $S$, it is defined by integrating the absorbed part of the incident radiative power flux density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{rad}} = \int_S \left[1-\rho_\gamma(\mathbf{r})\right] q_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbf{r})\, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the power due to radiation, $q_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the non-negative incident photon energy flux density onto the surface at position $\mathbf{r}$, $\rho_\gamma(\mathbf{r})$ is the effective photon-energy reflectivity for the incident spectrum and angular distribution, and $dA$ is an element of the receiving surface. The local surface normal is directed from the material into the plasma-facing half-space, so incident photons propagate toward the material.

This quantity is an area-integrated absorbed power and is distinct from [flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation), which is an incident photon energy flux density at a wall, not a photon-number flux, before surface integration and before exclusion of reflected energy. It excludes conductive and convective plasma heat loads and power radiated by the material itself.

NAMES.name: power_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short: Power deposited on plasma-facing materials by recombination processes, encompassing both plasma-ion recombination and surface recombination of neutral atoms, without restriction to a particular surface location.
NAMES.long:
Recombination power is the heat load delivered to plasma-facing materials when ions recover electrons and transition to neutral states, releasing ionization potential energy and residual kinetic energy at or near material surfaces. Two principal channels contribute: sheath-accelerated plasma-ion recombination at target surfaces, and surface recombination of neutral atoms into molecules, which deposits the molecular binding energy directly into the wall or divertor plate material.

The integrated power from recombination events over a wetted area $A$ is:

$$P_\text{rec} = \sum_s \int_A \Gamma_s \, E_s \, dA$$

where $\Gamma_s$ [m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$] is the incident particle flux density for species $s$ and $E_s$ [J] is the energy released per recombination event for that species, including ionization potential and kinetic contributions.

This power channel is intrinsically non-negative and becomes particularly significant in detached and partially detached divertor regimes, where volumetric ion-electron recombination upstream of the strike point redistributes energy deposition away from the target. Location-specific realizations include [power deposited on a single divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), the [total over the full divertor assembly](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), and [power at first-wall surfaces](name:power_at_wall_due_to_recombination). The neutral recombination particle flux produced in these processes is characterized by [neutral_energy_flux_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

sources.enhanced_context: Power deposited on divertor targets due to recombination of plasma ions, summed over all targets of the divertor. Represents the energy released when ions recombine at the target surface, contributing to the total divertor heat load.
sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to recombination of plasma ions (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short: Total power deposited on a divertor target by recombination processes, summing the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination channels at the plasma-material interface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity captures the combined recombination power delivered to a single divertor target, encompassing two physically distinct contributions: energy released when plasma ions recombine at or near the target surface (the plasma channel, quantified by plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination) and energy deposited when neutral particles undergo recombination into lower-energy bound states at the material wall (the neutral channel, quantified by [neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination)).

The total recombination power at the target decomposes additively:

$$
P_{\rm rec,target} = P_{\rm rec,plasma} + P_{\rm rec,neutral}
$$

where $P_{\rm rec,plasma}$ is the ion-recombination contribution and $P_{\rm rec,neutral}$ is the neutral-particle recombination contribution, both in W.

This target-localized quantity is a spatial specialization of the volume-integrated [power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination), which integrates recombination power over the full plasma domain. In attached divertor operation, recombination power at the target is a minor fraction of the total heat load; in detached or high-recycling regimes, surface and volumetric recombination become significant energy sinks that reduce the conducted and convected flux reaching the target. It is inferred from edge plasma simulations or from particle flux measurements combined with surface energy-release models, and is non-negative by definition.

NAMES.name: neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral-particle power deposited on a divertor target by recombination processes at the plasma-material interface, excluding the plasma-ion recombination channel.
NAMES.long:
This quantity captures the neutral-particle recombination power delivered to a single divertor target, encompassing energy deposited when neutral particles recombine into lower-energy bound states at the plasma-material interface. Only the fraction of released binding, internal, and kinetic energy accommodated by the target material contributes to this quantity.

The target-localized neutral recombination power is the inward surface integral of the neutral-recombination energy-flux vector over the wetted target area:

$$
P_{\mathrm{rec,n,target}} = \int_{\mathcal{A}_t} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{rec,n}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{mat}} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{rec,n,target}}$ is the neutral-particle recombination power at the target, $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{rec,n}}$ is the energy-flux vector due only to neutral-particle recombination, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{mat}}$ is the unit normal to the target surface directed into the material, and $\mathcal{A}_t$ is the target area receiving that contribution.

This target-localized quantity is the neutral-particle channel of [power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), distinct from [plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), which describes recombination of plasma ions. It excludes conducted, convected, radiative, charge-exchange, ionization, and plasma-ion recombination heat loads. Summed over all divertor targets, it gives [neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination).

sources.enhanced_context: Thermal power deposited on a divertor target due to recombination of neutral particles into their ground state (e.g., molecule formation). One component of the total power load on the target plate.
sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on this divertor target due to recombination of neutrals into a ground state (e.g. molecules)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short: Plasma-ion power deposited on a divertor target by recombination processes at the plasma-material interface, excluding the neutral-particle recombination channel.
NAMES.long:
This quantity captures the plasma-ion recombination power delivered to a single divertor target, representing energy deposited when plasma ions recombine at or near the plasma-material interface. It excludes the neutral-particle recombination channel quantified by [neutral-particle recombination power](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination).

The plasma-ion contribution is obtained from the total target recombination power by subtracting the neutral-particle contribution:

$$
P_{\rm plasma,target} = P_{\rm rec,target} - P_{\rm neutral,target}
$$

where $P_{\rm plasma,target}$ is this plasma-ion recombination power, $P_{\rm rec,target}$ is the [total recombination power at the divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), and $P_{\rm neutral,target}$ is the neutral-particle contribution.

This is the single-target plasma-ion component of recombination power, distinct from [total divertor recombination power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), which aggregates over all divertor target surfaces and includes both plasma-ion and neutral-particle channels.

sources.enhanced_context: Power deposited on a divertor target due to plasma ion recombination. Quantifies the recombination power component of the divertor heat load, relevant for detachment and power exhaust studies.
sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on this divertor target due to recombination of plasma ions
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor
NAMES.short: Total rate of energy deposited on wetted plasma-facing surfaces throughout the divertor assembly, summed over all included components and deposition channels.
NAMES.long:
Divertor power is the total energy-deposition rate on the wetted plasma-facing surfaces of the complete divertor assembly. It includes deposition on all included divertor targets and other plasma-facing components, regardless of the deposition channel.

The total deposited power is defined by the surface integral

$$
P_{\mathrm{div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} q_{\mathrm{dep}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of wetted plasma-facing surfaces in the divertor assembly, $q_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the inward energy-deposition flux density at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is a surface element.

This quantity aggregates thermal plasma deposition, neutral-particle deposition represented by [neutral power of divertor](name:neutral_power_of_divertor), and other included channels without double counting. It is the parent quantity for the thermal contribution represented by [thermal power of divertor](name:thermal_power_of_divertor); power deposited outside the divertor assembly is excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Power deposited on divertor targets due to electric currents, summed over all targets. Positive values indicate net power deposition from current-driven processes at the divertor.
sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to electric currents (positive means power is deposited on the target) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

sources.enhanced_context: Total power incident on the divertor, summed over all target surfaces. Aggregates all plasma power load channels delivered to the divertor, decomposed into conducted, convected, radiated, and other physical contributions.
sources.leaf_definition: Total power incident on the divertor (sum over all targets). This power is split in the various physical categories listed below
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: neutral_power_of_divertor
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral power of divertor is the total rate of neutral-particle energy deposited on wetted plasma-facing surfaces throughout the divertor assembly.
NAMES.long:
Neutral power of divertor is the total rate of neutral-particle energy deposited on the wetted plasma-facing surfaces of the divertor assembly. It sums neutral-particle deposition over all included divertor targets and other divertor plasma-facing components.

The defining surface integral is

$$
P_{\mathrm{neu,div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} q_{\mathrm{neu}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of the included wetted divertor surfaces, $q_{\mathrm{neu}}$ is the neutral-particle deposited energy-flux density on those surfaces, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is the surface-area element. The neutral contribution includes charge-exchange neutrals and other neutral-particle impact channels.

This quantity is the neutral-channel component of [power_of_divertor](name:power_of_divertor). Unlike [neutral_power_at_divertor_target](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target), it aggregates deposition over the divertor assembly rather than one target. Energy carried by neutral particles that does not reach an included divertor surface, and deposition from charged-particle, radiative, or other non-neutral channels, is excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Net power deposited on the divertor targets by neutral particles (positive when power flows to the target), summed over all targets. Quantifies the neutral particle contribution to the divertor heat load.
sources.leaf_definition: Net power from neutrals on the divertor targets (positive means power is deposited on the target) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction
NAMES.short: Thermal power deposited on all divertor targets by parallel electron and ion heat conduction along open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines, excluding convective, radiative, and neutral-particle channels.
NAMES.long:
The power of the divertor due to conduction is the total thermal energy deposited on all divertor target surfaces by electron and ion heat conduction along open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines. It excludes convective particle enthalpy, absorbed radiation, recombination, and neutral-particle contributions, and is the divertor-wide counterpart of [power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction).

The total conductive power is defined by integrating the conductive heat-flux vector over every wetted divertor target surface:

$$
P_{\mathrm{div,cond}} = \sum_k \int_{A_k} \mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_k\,dA
$$

where $A_k$ is the wetted surface of target $k$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_k$ points from the plasma toward the target material, and $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the sum of the electron and ion conductive heat-flux vectors. This aggregate quantity covers the complete divertor assembly and is a locus-specific component of [power_due_to_conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), rather than the global wall quantity [power_at_wall_due_to_conduction](name:power_at_wall_due_to_conduction).

sources.enhanced_context: Power conducted by the plasma to the divertor targets (summed over all targets), representing the conductive heat flux channel in the plasma–divertor power exhaust balance. A key quantity for divertor heat load characterization.
sources.leaf_definition: Power conducted by the plasma on the divertor targets (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_convection
NAMES.short: Power deposited on all divertor targets by convective plasma particle flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Convective power at all divertor targets quantifies the energy transported to those targets by plasma particles streaming from the scrape-off layer. It comprises thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic-energy contributions carried by convective plasma particle flux into the material surfaces, summed over all divertor targets.

The all-target convective divertor power is the sum of the incident convective energy flux over the wetted surfaces of the divertor targets:

$$
P_{\mathrm{conv,div}} =
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{A_k}
\sum_s \Gamma_{s,k}^{\mathrm{in}}
\left(h_{s,k} + \frac{1}{2} m_s |\mathbf{u}_{s,k}|^2\right)
\, dA
$$

where $\mathcal{D}$ is the set of divertor target surfaces, $A_k$ is the wetted surface of target $k$, $dA$ is a surface-area element, and $s$ labels incident species in the convective channel, including streaming ion and electron species. $\Gamma_{s,k}^{\mathrm{in}}$ is the particle-flux density into the material, defined by the positive-into-target surface-normal projection $n_{s,k}\max(\mathbf{u}_{s,k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}_{\mathrm{in},k},0)$; $n_{s,k}$ is the particle density, $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\mathrm{in},k}$ is the surface normal directed from the plasma into the target, $h_{s,k}$ is the thermal enthalpy per particle, $m_s$ is the particle mass, and $\mathbf{u}_{s,k}$ is the directed flow velocity of the incident particles.

This quantity is the all-divertor-target realization of [convective power](name:power_due_to_convection); the corresponding single-target quantity is [convective power at a single divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), and the broader plasma-facing-surface counterpart is [convective power at plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces](name:power_at_wall_due_to_convection). It excludes [conductive divertor power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction), radiative deposition, and [recombination-related divertor plasma power](name:plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), which are separate channels of the divertor power balance.

sources.enhanced_context: Power convected by the plasma onto the divertor targets (summed over all targets), representing the kinetic energy flux of ions and electrons flowing along field lines. A key quantity for divertor power load assessment.
sources.leaf_definition: Power convected by the plasma on the divertor targets (sum over all targets)

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_fusion
NAMES.short: Nuclear power deposited in the divertor structure through neutron moderation and gamma absorption from fusion reactions, distinct from the plasma thermal load conducted or convected to divertor surfaces along magnetic field lines.
NAMES.long:
In a deuterium-tritium burning plasma, fusion reactions generate 14.1 MeV neutrons carrying approximately 80% of the 17.6 MeV reaction energy per event. These electrically neutral particles stream freely into surrounding structures, and the divertor assembly — comprising plasma-facing targets, support structures, and cooling circuits — absorbs a fraction via elastic and inelastic neutron scattering, radiative capture, and secondary gamma emission. This nuclear heating contribution is structurally and thermally distinct from [thermal_power_of_divertor](name:thermal_power_of_divertor), which quantifies the plasma heat exhaust deposited at divertor surfaces by conductive and convective transport along open field lines.

The nuclear power deposited in the divertor is the volume integral of the local nuclear heating power density $\dot{q}_{\rm nuc}$ over the divertor assembly:

$$
P_{\rm nuc,div} = \int_{V_{\rm div}} \dot{q}_{\rm nuc}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position within the divertor volume $V_{\rm div}$, which encompasses all structural and plasma-facing components.

Because neutrons cannot be directly calorimetrically resolved from plasma heat loads during operation, this quantity is computed via neutron transport calculations using divertor geometry and material nuclear cross-section data. It represents a volumetric heat source relevant to divertor coolant system design and structural integrity analysis. Analogous nuclear deposition integrals for breeding zone components are defined by [nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_layer](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_layer) and [nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_shield](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_shield); this divertor quantity is a sub-component of the total [power_due_to_fusion](name:power_due_to_fusion).

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_radiation
NAMES.short: Total net photon power absorbed by all divertor targets, summed over target surfaces after reflected radiative power is subtracted.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the divertor-wide net radiative power deposited on all divertor targets. It aggregates photon energy emitted by impurity and hydrogenic species, including line radiation, bremsstrahlung, and radiative recombination continuum.

The total is defined by summing the net radiative deposition over the set of divertor targets:

$$
P_{\mathrm{rad,div}} = \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{div}}} P_{\mathrm{rad},t}
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the set of divertor targets and $P_{\mathrm{rad},t}$ is the photon power incident on target $t$ minus the reflected photon power. This quantity is the all-target aggregation of [power due to radiation](name:power_due_to_radiation) and excludes particle, conductive, convective, ohmic, and halo-current power deposition.

sources.enhanced_context: Black-body radiated power emitted from all divertor target surfaces, accounting for surface emissivity. Represents the thermal radiative power loss from the divertor targets, summed over all target surfaces.
sources.leaf_definition: Black body radiated power emitted from the divertor targets (emissivity is included) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

sources.enhanced_context: Net radiated power from the divertor region, summed over all targets. Represents the total power emitted as radiation at the divertor surface during plasma-wall interaction.
sources.leaf_definition: Net radiated power on the divertor targets (incident - reflected) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short: Total power deposited on all divertor target surfaces by recombination processes, comprising both the plasma-ion and neutral-particle recombination channels summed over the full divertor assembly.
NAMES.long:
Total divertor recombination power is the combined rate at which recombination processes at or near the target surfaces of the divertor assembly release energy into the material, integrated over all targets. It is the divertor-surface counterpart of the volumetric [power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination) and unifies two physically distinct deposition channels:

$$
P_\mathrm{rec,div} = P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma} + P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma}$ is [plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), the energy deposited when plasma ions recombine or neutralize at the material surface, and $P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral}$ is [neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), the energy carried by neutral particles undergoing recombination reactions at the plasma-material interface.

This quantity is computed in edge-plasma codes that track ion and neutral fluxes to the targets and apply sheath-energy coefficients along with recombination cross-sections to determine surface deposition. It represents one component of the total divertor heat load alongside conducted, convected, and radiative contributions, and becomes a more prominent fraction of that load in detached or partially detached divertor regimes where volumetric recombination upstream suppresses the ion current reaching the targets.

NAMES.name: neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Thermal power deposited on divertor targets by recombination reactions of neutral particles at the plasma-material interface, summed over all targets. It represents the neutral-particle surface recombination contribution to the total divertor heat load.
NAMES.long:
Neutral recombination power of the divertor is the heat load delivered to divertor target surfaces when neutral particles undergo recombination reactions at the plasma-material interface. These reactions include surface association or recombination of neutral atoms, molecules, or molecular fragments into more tightly bound neutral species, such as molecule formation on a material surface. It is the neutral-particle surface-deposition channel of [total divertor recombination power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination).

The full-divertor value is the sum of the corresponding per-target neutral recombination powers:

$$
P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral} = \sum_t P_{\mathrm{rec},t}^\mathrm{neutral}
$$

where $t$ indexes divertor target surfaces and $P_{\mathrm{rec},t}^\mathrm{neutral}$ is [neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination) for target $t$.

This quantity excludes heat delivered by plasma ions, electrons, photons, conducted or convected plasma energy, and non-recombination neutral interactions, except for energy deposited through the neutral recombination process at the target. It is a surface-deposition quantity integrated over the full divertor assembly, distinct from volumetric [power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination).

sources.enhanced_context: Power deposited on divertor targets due to recombination of neutrals, summed over all divertor targets. Contributes to the total divertor heat load, particularly during detached plasma operation.
sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to recombination of neutrals into a ground state (e.g. molecules) (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short: Thermal power deposited on divertor targets by recombination or neutralization of plasma ions at the plasma-material interface, summed over all targets. It represents the plasma-ion surface recombination contribution to the total divertor heat load.
NAMES.long:
Plasma recombination power of the divertor is the heat load delivered to divertor target surfaces when plasma ions recombine or neutralize at the plasma-material interface. It is the plasma-ion surface-deposition channel of [total divertor recombination power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), integrated over all divertor targets.

It is defined as the surface integral of the local deposited-power density over the divertor target assembly:

$$
P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma} = \int_{A_\mathrm{div}} q_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{plasma} \, dA
$$

where $A_\mathrm{div}$ is the union of all divertor target surfaces, $dA$ is a target-surface element, and $q_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{plasma}$ is the local non-negative deposited-power density due only to recombination or neutralization of plasma ions incident from the plasma side.

This quantity is the plasma-component counterpart of [power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination). The complementary neutral-particle channel is [neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination); conducted, convected, radiated, and other non-recombination heat-load contributions are excluded. It may be equivalently represented as the sum of [plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination) over the target surfaces included in $A_\mathrm{div}$.

sources.enhanced_context: Power deposited on divertor targets due to recombination of plasma ions, summed over all targets of the divertor. Represents the energy released when ions recombine at the target surface, contributing to the total divertor heat load.
sources.leaf_definition: Power deposited on the divertor targets due to recombination of plasma ions (sum over all targets)
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertors

NAMES.name: radial_length_of_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Non-negative span of a divertor target’s plasma-facing surface along the major-radius direction, measured between its minimum and maximum R coordinates.
NAMES.long:
The radial span of a divertor target is the extent of its plasma-facing surface along the major-radius direction. It is a geometric extent, not the distance along the target surface or a power-deposition width. The direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$.

For the plasma-facing surface $S$, the span is defined by

$$
L_R = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in S} R(\mathbf{x}) - \min_{\mathbf{x}\in S} R(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is a point on $S$ and $R(\mathbf{x})$ is its major-radius coordinate. The quantity includes the full specified target surface and is non-negative. It complements the [vertical length of the divertor target](name:vertical_length_of_divertor_target), which uses the extrema of $Z$, while the [x coordinate of the divertor target](name:x_coordinate_of_divertor_target) identifies a Cartesian center rather than a surface span.

NAMES.name: surface_area_of_divertor_tile
NAMES.short: Geometric area of the plasma-facing surface of an individual divertor tile, defining the surface over which incident plasma loads are spatially integrated.
NAMES.long:
The tile surface area is the geometric area of the plasma-facing wetted surface of one individual divertor tile. It is a property of the tile geometry, independent of the incident heat, particle, or current load.

The area is defined by

$$
A_{\rm tile} = \int_{S_{\rm tile}} dA
$$

where $S_{\rm tile}$ is the plasma-facing tile surface and $dA$ is an elemental surface area. The result provides the geometric denominator for converting an integrated load into a tile-averaged surface density, such as the [energy flux at a divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target).

This quantity applies to one tile and must not be confused with the [wetted area of a divertor target](name:wetted_area_of_divertor_target), which characterizes a target-level deposited-flux region, or the total wetted area of the divertor summed over multiple targets.

sources.enhanced_context: Wetted surface area of an individual divertor tile facing the plasma. Geometric parameter used to compute incident heat and particle flux densities on divertor tiles.
sources.leaf_definition: Area of the tile surface facing the plasma

NAMES.name: temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of a specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a divertor-target sheath, distinct from the target material temperature.
NAMES.long:
Temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of a specified plasma population evaluated at the plasma side of a divertor-target sheath. It is a plasma boundary quantity for particles adjacent to, or incident on, the divertor target, not a thermodynamic property of the solid target material.

For a species or population $s$, the scalar target temperature is the one-third trace of the kinetic thermal-energy moment at the sheath edge:

$$
T_{s,t} = \frac{m_s}{3 n_{s,t}} \int |\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{s,t}|^2 f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $T_{s,t}$ is the temperature at the divertor target for population $s$, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $n_{s,t}$ is the particle number density at the sheath edge, $\mathbf{u}_{s,t}$ is the mean flow velocity there, and $f_{s,t}$ is the velocity distribution of that population at the plasma side of the sheath.

This generic quantity denotes the target temperature for the specified plasma population and is not an unqualified average over electrons and ions. For the electron population it corresponds to [electron temperature at divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target); for the ion population it corresponds to [ion temperature at divertor target](name:ion_temperature_at_divertor_target). It is the divertor-target counterpart of the more general [plasma temperature](name:plasma_temperature).

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of the electron population at the sheath entrance adjacent to a divertor target. It is a plasma kinetic temperature, not the material surface temperature of the target.
NAMES.long:
Electron temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of the electron population at the sheath entrance adjacent to a divertor target. It is a plasma kinetic temperature on the plasma side of the sheath, not the material surface temperature of the target.

For a scalar electron temperature, the defining pressure-density relation is:

$$
T_{e,t} = \frac{p_{e,t}}{e\,n_{e,t}}
$$

where $T_{e,t}$ is the electron temperature at the divertor target, $p_{e,t}$ is the scalar electron kinetic pressure at the sheath entrance, $n_{e,t}$ is the [electron density at the divertor target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), and $e$ is the elementary charge used as the energy conversion factor.

This quantity is population-resolved: it is the electron member of [temperature at the divertor target](name:temperature_at_divertor_target), and the corresponding ion quantity is [ion temperature at the divertor target](name:ion_temperature_at_divertor_target). It must not be interpreted as an electron-ion average, a target heat flux, or a full electron energy distribution; for a non-isotropic or non-Maxwellian electron population it denotes the scalar kinetic temperature associated with the electron pressure in the defining relation.

NAMES.name: ion_temperature_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Thermal energy per particle of the ion population in the region immediately adjacent to a divertor target, averaged over ion species at the sheath entrance where the Bohm criterion governs ion entry.
NAMES.long:
Ion temperature at the divertor target characterizes the mean kinetic energy scale of the ionic plasma population in the narrow layer adjacent to the target, evaluated at the sheath entrance where ions satisfy the Bohm condition. It is the ion-specific realization of [temperature at the divertor target](name:temperature_at_divertor_target).

The density-weighted ion temperature is defined by

$$
T_i = \frac{\sum_s n_s T_s}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $s$ indexes the included ion species, $n_s$ is the number density of species $s$, and $T_s$ is its kinetic temperature expressed in the same energy convention as $T_i$.

This aggregate excludes electrons and neutral particles. It is distinct from [electron temperature at the divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), which characterizes the electron population at the same sheath entrance.

sources.enhanced_context: Ion temperature (Ti) at the divertor target, averaged over ion species. Represents the thermal energy of ions at the target surface in the divertor region.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total positive-ion number density at the divertor target, summed over all ionic species and charge states at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local number density of all positive ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface. It is the all-ion aggregate of [ion density at the divertor target](name:ion_density_at_divertor_target), rather than a species-specific or charge-state-resolved density.

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_{i,total} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{Z \in \mathcal{Z}_s} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the total ion number density, $s$ indexes the included ionic species, $Z$ indexes their positive charge states, and $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of species $s$ in charge state $Z$. The sums include all positive-ion populations evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath.

Neutral atoms and molecules, as well as free electrons, are excluded. A density resolved for one charge state is represented separately by [ion charge state density](name:ion_charge_state_density).

sources.enhanced_context: Total ion density (ni,total) at a divertor target, summed over all ion species. Provides a local plasma density metric at the divertor strike point relevant to plasma-surface interaction and heat load assessment.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: total_ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Rate of energy deposition by all incident ion species and charge states on the inner, high-field-side divertor target, integrated over its wetted surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the ion-carried contribution to power deposited on the inner, high-field-side divertor target. It includes the thermal energy entering the electrostatic sheath and the directed kinetic energy acquired by ions across the sheath potential drop, while excluding electron, neutral-particle, photon, and halo-current contributions. It is the ion-resolved component of [ion power at the inner divertor target](name:ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target) and is distinct from the all-channel [power at the inner divertor target](name:power_at_inner_divertor_target).

The deposited ion power is defined by

$$
P_{i,in} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wetted,in}}} \mathbf{q}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{t}\, dA
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{in}}$ is the integrated ion power, $A_{\mathrm{wetted,in}}$ is the wetted inner-target surface, $\mathbf{q}_i$ is the total incident ion energy-flux density summed over ion species and charge states, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{t}$ points from the plasma toward the target material.

sources.enhanced_context: Total ion power (summed over all ion species) incident on the inner divertor target. A key quantity for divertor heat load assessment and plasma-wall interaction studies.
sources.leaf_definition: Total ion (summed over ion species) power on the inner target

NAMES.name: total_particle_flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling
NAMES.short: Rate at which particles are returned to the edge plasma by recycling on all divertor target surfaces, summed over every recycled carrier channel. For this total quantity, molecular and compound-particle multiplicity is applied so that each carrier contributes the number of individual particles it returns before summation.
NAMES.long:
Rate at which particles are returned to the edge plasma by recycling on all divertor target surfaces, expressed on a particle-number basis. For this total quantity, molecular and compound-particle carriers are resolved to their constituent-particle multiplicity before summation, so a released molecule contributes the number of atoms it delivers rather than a single carrier count, and the contributions of neutral, atomic, molecular, and ionic recycled products are then summed over the divertor target set.

The total recycled particle rate is the plasma-ward surface integral of the recycled particle flux density, summed over all divertor targets:

$$
\Phi_\mathrm{rec,tot}^\mathrm{div} = \sum_{t} \int_{S_t} m(\mathbf{r}) \, \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_\mathrm{rec}(\mathbf{r}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{p,t}(\mathbf{r}) \, dA
$$

where $S_t$ is the material surface of divertor target $t$, $dA$ is its surface area element, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_\mathrm{rec}$ is the local recycled carrier flux-density vector (in $\mathrm{m}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$), $m$ is the particle multiplicity of each carrier that converts carrier count to returned-particle count, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{p,t}$ is the unit normal directed from the target material surface toward the plasma.

This is the multiplicity-resolved, particle-number specialization of the recycling return rate [particle flux of divertor due to recycling](name:particle_flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling), and it is a component of the general recycling return rate [flux of divertor due to recycling](name:flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling). It excludes non-recycling sources such as external gas injection, sputtered impurity production, and pumping removal, and it is distinct from the energy, power, and momentum fluxes associated with the same surface processes.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the local recycled particle flux density is directed from the divertor target material surface toward the plasma.

sources.enhanced_context: Total recycled particle flux from the divertor, expressed in equivalent electrons per second, representing the rate at which neutrals and ions are re-emitted from divertor surfaces back into the plasma. Key quantity for particle balance and recycling studies.

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Tritium density at the divertor target is the local number density of T+ ions immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath, excluding neutral tritium atoms and molecules.
NAMES.long:
Tritium density at the divertor target is the local number density of tritium ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface, evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the tritium-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local number density is defined by the differential particle count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{T}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{T}^+}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{T}^+}$ is the number of atomic tritium ions in a small plasma volume $V$ whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

Because atomic tritium has one positive ionization state, this quantity represents the T+ population only. Neutral tritium atoms and molecules are excluded; [tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary) refers instead to the corresponding quantity at the last closed magnetic flux surface.

sources.enhanced_context: Tritium (T).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Number density of tungsten ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target, summed over all ionization stages W1+ through W74+ and excluding neutral tungsten atoms.
NAMES.long:
Tungsten density at the divertor target is the local number density of tungsten ions in the plasma adjacent to a divertor target surface, summed over all ionization stages W$^{1+}$ through W$^{74+}$ and excluding neutral tungsten atoms. As a fully charge-state-summed impurity ion density, it follows the convention of the parent [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) and is evaluated at the plasma-material interface immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath entrance.

Tungsten is a high-Z refractory metal with atomic number $Z = 74$. The total ion number density is defined as:

$$
n_W = \sum_{z=1}^{74} n_{W^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{W^{z+}}$ is the local number density of tungsten ions in charge state $z$. Tungsten ions at the divertor target arise primarily from physical sputtering of tungsten plasma-facing components by energetic incident hydrogenic and impurity ions.

Even trace tungsten concentrations that migrate from the divertor region into the core can produce severe radiative power losses at electron temperatures above a few keV, making this near-target density a critical diagnostic quantity for impurity transport and divertor detachment studies. It is distinct from the bulk plasma content captured by [tungsten_density](name:tungsten_density) and from the separatrix-averaged value given by [tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary). Near-target tungsten ion densities are inferred from vacuum-ultraviolet and optical emission spectroscopy of tungsten line radiation combined with impurity transport modeling.

sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: vertical_length_of_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Non-negative vertical span of a divertor target surface, defined by the difference between its maximum and minimum Z coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical extent of a divertor target is the range of vertical positions occupied by its surface, rather than the vertical position of its center.

$$
H_Z = Z_{\\max} - Z_{\\min}
$$

where $H_Z$ is the vertical span, and $Z_{\\max}$ and $Z_{\\min}$ are respectively the maximum and minimum vertical coordinates over the target surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame. Here, $R$ is major radius, $\\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This extent complements the [radial length of the divertor target](name:radial_length_of_divertor_target) and is distinct from the [Z coordinate of the divertor target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target), which locates its surface center.

sources.enhanced_context: Projected length of the divertor target along the vertical (Z) axis, characterizing the vertical extent of the target geometry. Used in divertor geometry description and power exhaust modelling.
sources.leaf_definition: Target length projected on the height axis
sources.parent_definition: Set of divertor targets

NAMES.name: vertical_outline_of_divertor_tile
NAMES.short: Vertical (Z) coordinate of the surface outline defining the geometric boundary of an individual divertor tile in the poloidal cross-section.
NAMES.long:
The vertical height component of each point defining the surface outline of a divertor tile within the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major radius from the toroidal symmetry axis and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate measured from the machine midplane. Paired with the corresponding radial outline coordinate, this quantity fully specifies the cross-sectional geometry of the tile surface in any toroidally axisymmetric representation, enabling computation of wetted surface area, heat-load distribution, and geometric shadowing between adjacent plasma-facing components.

Divertor tile outlines are obtained from engineering or CAD specifications of the first-wall assembly. The geometric boundary of the tile determines which surface elements intercept the scrape-off-layer heat flux in the vicinity of the magnetic strike-point. The outline is also used in optical and infrared camera line-of-sight calculations to monitor tile erosion and thermal response. For the analogous geometry of limiter tiles, see [vertical_outline_of_limiter_tile](name:vertical_outline_of_limiter_tile); for the vacuum vessel boundary, see [vertical_outline_of_vacuum_vessel](name:vertical_outline_of_vacuum_vessel). The center-point location of the divertor target surface is given by [vertical_coordinate_of_divertor_target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target), which captures a single reference point rather than a full outline contour.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the outline point is located above the machine midplane, in the direction of increasing $Z$.

sources.enhanced_context: Vertical (Z) coordinate of surface outline.
sources.leaf_definition: Height

NAMES.name: wetted_area_of_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Area of one divertor target receiving deposited heat flux at or above one e-folding below its peak, including flux expansion and spreading.
NAMES.long:
The wetted area is the portion of one divertor target surface that receives deposited heat flux at least equal to the peak target heat flux divided by $e$. It characterizes the heat-load footprint produced by mapping the scrape-off-layer heat-flux decay length to the target surface.

$$
A_w = \int_{A_t} H\!\left(q_t(\mathbf{s}) - \frac{q_{t,\max}}{e}\right)\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $A_t$ is the plasma-facing area of the target, $q_t(\mathbf{s})$ is the deposited heat-flux density at target position $\mathbf{s}$, $q_{t,\max}$ is its maximum value on that target, $H$ is the Heaviside step function, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is the surface-area element. The mapped footprint includes flux expansion and the spreading factor associated with the scrape-off-layer decay length.

This is a per-target footprint area, distinct from the geometric area of a [divertor tile](name:surface_area_of_divertor_tile). The total over all targets is [wetted area of the divertor](name:wetted_area_of_divertor).

sources.enhanced_context: Wetted area of the divertor target, defined by mapping the SOL heat flux decay length (λ_q) to the target plate using flux expansion and spreading factor. Represents the region receiving heat flux down to one e-folding decay from peak.
sources.leaf_definition: Wetted area of the target, defined by the SOL heat flux decay length (lambda_q) mapped to the target using flux expansion and spreading factor and the target toroidal circumference. In other words, this is the area getting heat flux from the maximum value down to one e-fold decay.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_divertor_target
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Number density of xenon ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to a divertor target, summed over all ionization charge states Xe1+ through Xe54+ and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Xenon density at the divertor target is the local number density of ionized xenon in the plasma immediately adjacent to the divertor target surface. It represents all occupied ionization stages in the thin plasma layer upstream of the electrostatic sheath entrance, excluding neutral xenon atoms, and is a species-resolved member of the [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) family.

The total xenon ion density is the sum over all occupied charge states:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \sum_{q=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the local number density of xenon ions in charge state $q$, summed from singly ionized Xe$^{1+}$ through fully stripped Xe$^{54+}$.

Xenon is introduced as a high-Z noble-gas seeding impurity to enhance radiative power dissipation in the divertor region, reducing peak target heat loads during high-power operation. At near-target plasma temperatures of a few to tens of eV, lower charge states dominate the local xenon ion population; higher charge states become significant only further upstream where the electron temperature is substantially greater. The near-target xenon density is inferred from spectroscopic line-emission measurements combined with impurity transport modeling.

For comparison, [neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target) gives the analogous quantity for the lighter noble-gas seeding species neon, and [xenon_density_at_limiter](name:xenon_density_at_limiter) provides the corresponding xenon ion density at a limiter surface rather than a divertor target.
