NAMES.name: boron_density
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Elemental boron number density, summed over neutral atoms and all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+.
NAMES.long:
Boron density is the elemental boron particle density, with neutral boron and every ionic charge state included in one additive quantity.

$$
n_B = \sum_{Z=0}^{5} n_{B,Z}
$$

where $n_B$ is the elemental boron density, $Z$ is the boron ionic charge state with $Z=0$ denoting neutral boron, and $n_{B,Z}$ is the density of boron in state $Z$.

The quantity is the underlying boron density field; [line-averaged boron density](name:line_averaged_boron_density) and [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density) are distinct averages of it. It excludes no boron charge state but is not a charge-state-specific or charge-weighted density.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the local elemental-boron population contributes additively to the particle density.

NAMES.name: carbon_density
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Carbon density is the local number density of elemental carbon in the plasma, summed over neutral carbon atoms and all ionic charge states through fully stripped C6+.
NAMES.long:
Carbon density is the local number density of elemental carbon in the plasma, summed over neutral carbon atoms and all ionic charge states through fully stripped $C^{6+}$. It represents the elemental carbon population per physical volume, independent of ionization balance.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by the number-density sum:

$$
n_C = \sum_{z=0}^{6} n_{C^{z+}}
$$

where $n_C$ is the carbon density, $z=0$ denotes neutral carbon, $z=1,\ldots,6$ denote ionic charge states, and $n_{C^{z+}}$ is the number density of carbon in charge state $z$.

This quantity is unweighted by charge, mass, or radiation emissivity and is distinct from electron density, charge density, and individual charge-state densities. Spatially averaged or locus-specific carbon-density quantities include [volume_averaged_carbon_density](name:volume_averaged_carbon_density), [flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary), and the ion-only divertor-target quantity [carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: charge_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Charge at the pedestal top is a generic ionic charge-state metric for the plasma at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge pedestal. The specific child quantity defines which species, charge states, and weighting are included.
NAMES.long:
Charge at the pedestal top is an ionic charge-state metric evaluated at the pedestal top, the core-side shoulder of the steep-gradient H-mode edge transport barrier. It characterizes the local ion mixture or selected ion population according to the aggregation convention specified by the more specific quantity.

This parent quantity defines the pedestal-top locus and the general ionic-charge concept only. It does not prescribe charge-squared weighting, species inclusion, charge-state aggregation, or normalization; those distinctions belong to child quantities such as [effective charge at the pedestal top](name:effective_charge_at_pedestal_top). It is distinct from electric charge density, net charge balance, and analogous charge metrics at other plasma loci.

NAMES.name: charge_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Charge at the plasma boundary is a generic charge measure for the ion mixture evaluated at the plasma boundary. Specific child quantities define the charge moment, normalization, and species aggregation used.
NAMES.long:
Charge at the plasma boundary is a generic charge measure for the plasma composition evaluated at the plasma boundary. It identifies the boundary locus of the charge-related quantity without prescribing a particular charge moment or normalization.

Concrete specializations define the mathematical charge weighting and population scope. For example, [effective charge at the plasma boundary](name:effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary) uses a charge-squared ionic density moment normalized to electron density; other charge measures need not share that weighting or its bounds.

This parent quantity must not be interpreted as a specific effective-charge definition, a signed electric charge density, or a net boundary charge. It is an abstraction over charge-type scalar quantities at the plasma boundary; the defining equation belongs to each child quantity.

NAMES.name: collisionality_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Dimensionless comparison of a plasma population’s collision frequency with its characteristic bounce, transit, or streaming frequency.
NAMES.long:
Collisionality measures whether a plasma population undergoes many or few collisions during a characteristic orbital or streaming timescale. It provides a dimensionless indicator of the collisional transport regime.

The generalized collisionality is defined by

$$
\nu_* = \frac{\nu_{\mathrm{coll}}}{\omega_{\mathrm{char}}}
$$

where $\nu_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the relevant collision frequency and $\omega_{\mathrm{char}}$ is the characteristic bounce, transit, or streaming frequency, both expressed as inverse times. A value larger than unity indicates frequent collisions during the characteristic motion, while a value smaller than unity indicates weak collisionality. Specific realizations may select a particle species and location, such as [electron collisionality](name:electron_collisionality) or [electron collisionality at the pedestal top](name:electron_collisionality_at_pedestal_top); normalized variants may use a trapped-particle bounce frequency, as in [normalized electron collisionality at the pedestal top](name:normalized_electron_collisionality_at_pedestal_top).

NAMES.name: decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short: Characteristic outward distance over which a decaying plasma quantity decreases by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for a plasma quantity that decreases outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The operand may be a particle density, temperature, or heat-flux magnitude.

$$
L_f = \left|\frac{d\ln f}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_f$ is the e-folding length, $f$ is the positive scalar quantity or magnitude being characterized, and $x$ is outward distance from the confined plasma in the direction normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The scale is defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is nonzero.

The general quantity includes the electron number-density specialization [electron decay length](name:electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), the ion number-density specialization [ion decay length](name:ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), and the heat-flux specialization [heat decay length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). It does not select a species, transport channel, or particular decaying quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the reference direction is outward from the confined plasma into the scrape-off layer and the associated quantity decreases along it.

NAMES.name: density_at_launching_position
NAMES.short: Number density of a designated plasma species evaluated at the wave launcher aperture or waveguide mouth, where externally injected electromagnetic waves first encounter the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Number density at the launching position is the particle count per unit volume of a designated plasma species at the geometric location of a wave launcher aperture or waveguide mouth.

The launching position identifies the spatial point where an injected wave first contacts the plasma boundary or the adjacent edge region; the local density at this locus sets the plasma frequency and governs accessibility of the injected wave to the plasma interior. The launching-position locus is distinct from the broader [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) concept, which is defined over the entire last closed flux surface rather than a specific aperture geometry.

The species-specific realization [electron_density_at_launching_position](name:electron_density_at_launching_position) gives the electron number density at this locus.

NAMES.name: density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Number density of a specified plasma particle population evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local number density of a specified plasma particle population at the H-mode pedestal top, the core-side shoulder of the edge transport barrier. It provides the shared density concept for [electron density at the pedestal top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top), [ion density at the pedestal top](name:ion_density_at_pedestal_top), and species-specific impurity densities such as [carbon density at the pedestal top](name:carbon_density_at_pedestal_top).

The number density is defined by

$$
n_s(r_p) = \frac{dN_s}{dV}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of population $s$, $N_s$ is the number of particles belonging to that population, $V$ is physical volume, and $r_p$ identifies the pedestal-top location.

The population and aggregation scope are supplied by the specific subject. Elemental and fuel-ion densities include the ionic charge states belonging to the named population unless a charge-state-resolved quantity is specified; electron density counts electrons directly. Neutral-particle inclusion is likewise population-dependent and is not implied by this unspecific parent name.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the specified population contributes particles to the local number count.

NAMES.name: argon_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Number density of argon impurity ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, summed over all ionization states from singly ionized Ar+ through fully stripped Ar18+.
NAMES.long:
Argon density at the pedestal top is the local number density of argon impurity ions at the shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over all ionization states from singly ionized Ar+ through fully stripped Ar18+. The pedestal top is the common evaluation locus for the [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family.

The pedestal-top value is the local charge-state-summed argon ion density evaluated at the pedestal-top flux surface:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar,ped}} = \left.\sum_{q=1}^{18}\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}{dV}\right|_{\rho=\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar,ped}}$ is the argon ion number density, $q$ is the argon ionic charge state, $dN_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number of ions in charge state $q$, $dV$ is a physical volume element, $\rho$ is the radial flux-surface label in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, $\theta$ and $\phi$ are the poloidal and toroidal angular coordinates, and $\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}$ identifies the pedestal-top surface.

This quantity excludes neutral argon and is an impurity-specific contribution to [ion density at the pedestal top](name:ion_density_at_pedestal_top); it is distinct from the corresponding [krypton density at the pedestal top](name:krypton_density_at_pedestal_top).

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Number density of beryllium impurity ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, summed over all ionization states unless a specific charge state is specified.
NAMES.long:
Beryllium density at the pedestal top is the local number density of beryllium impurity ions at the shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over all charge states from singly ionized Be$^+$ through fully stripped Be$^{4+}$ unless a specific ionization stage is identified separately. This quantity is the beryllium-specific member of the [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family, which spans all plasma species evaluated at this locus.

The species-summed number density is defined as:

$$
n_\mathrm{Be} = \sum_{j=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{j+}}
$$

where $j$ indexes the ionization stage from singly ionized ($j=1$) to fully stripped ($j=4$, atomic number $Z=4$).

The pedestal top marks the core-side end of the steep H-mode edge-transport barrier, where the edge density and temperature gradients transition toward the flatter confined-region profiles. Beryllium is a light impurity that enters the plasma via sputtering and recycling from beryllium plasma-facing components; its concentration at the pedestal top influences hydrogenic fuel dilution and edge radiated power.

Beryllium density at the pedestal can be inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or from passive UV/VUV spectroscopy of beryllium emission lines. The complementary locus-resolved quantities [beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis) bracket this pedestal-top value radially, while [beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density) describes the full spatial profile.

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Number density of boron impurity ions at the pedestal top is the particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over charge states from singly ionized B+ through fully stripped B5+ unless a specific charge state is named.
NAMES.long:
Number density of boron impurity ions at the pedestal top is the local particle count per volume of boron ions at the core-side shoulder of an H-mode pedestal. The pedestal top is the transition where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter confined-core density variation, distinct from a separatrix or plasma-boundary value. For bare boron, the density is summed over all ionization charge states from singly ionized $\mathrm{B}^{+}$ through fully stripped $\mathrm{B}^{5+}$ unless a specific charge state is explicitly named; neutral boron atoms are excluded.

For the boron ion population on the pedestal-top flux surface, the defining local density is

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}}(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}) = \sum_{q=1}^{5} n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}) = \left.\sum_{q=1}^{5}\frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}}{dV}\right|_{\xi=\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the charge-state-summed boron ion number density, $q$ is the positive integer ion charge state, $n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the number density of boron ions in charge state $q+$, $N_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the particle count of that charge state, $V$ is physical volume, and $\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}$ is the explicitly chosen radial label of the pedestal-top flux surface, for example normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$ or normalized poloidal flux $\psi_N$.

This quantity is species-resolved and charge-state aggregated for ionized boron only. It is distinct from total ion density, electron density, a charge-state-resolved boron density, and any neutral-boron population density at the same pedestal-top locus.

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Number density of carbon impurity ions at the H-mode pedestal top is the particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over C+ through fully stripped C6+.
NAMES.long:
Number density of carbon impurity ions at the H-mode pedestal top is the local particle count per volume of carbon ions evaluated on the flux surface marking the core-side shoulder of the edge transport barrier. It is the carbon-specific member of [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) and is distinct from the electron population represented by [electron_density_at_pedestal_top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top).

For the carbon-ion population, the defining local density is

$$
n_{\mathrm{C}} = \left.\sum_{q=1}^{6} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{C}^{q+}}}{dV}\right|_{\xi=\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{C}}$ is carbon-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{C}^{q+}}$ is the dimensionless count of carbon ions in charge state $q$, $V$ is physical volume in m$^{3}$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}$ is the dimensionless radial label of the pedestal-top flux surface, expressed using an explicitly named coordinate such as normalized poloidal flux.

The sum includes carbon ions from singly ionized C+ through fully stripped C6+ and excludes neutral carbon. The locus is the confined-plasma pedestal top, not the separatrix, plasma boundary, or scrape-off layer; [carbon_density](name:carbon_density) denotes the corresponding elemental density without this pedestal-top localization.

NAMES.name: density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Number density of a specified plasma particle population at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local, intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Number density of a specified plasma particle population at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive particle count per physical volume for that population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed magnetic flux surface separating the confined plasma from the scrape-off-layer region. The specified population may be electrons, ions, neutral particles, or an impurity species.

The local number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the distribution function at a boundary point:

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \int f_s(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of population $s$, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the phase-space distribution function for population $s$, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

When the specified population is a chemical or isotope species without an explicit charge state, the boundary density is summed over all charge states of that species; a charge-state-resolved population denotes only particles in the stated ionization state. Species-qualified boundary-density names such as [electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), [ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), and krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary are population-specific instances of this quantity.

This quantity denotes a local value at the boundary, not an average over the boundary surface or over a volume. Averaged counterparts include [flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary) for a flux-surface average at the same boundary and [volume_averaged_neutral_species_density](name:volume_averaged_neutral_species_density) for a volume average; densities evaluated at other loci, such as density_at_pedestal and [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis), are distinct.

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Number density of boron, summed over neutral atoms and all ionization states from B+ through fully stripped B5+, at the plasma boundary — the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Boron density at the plasma boundary is the number of boron particles per unit volume — encompassing neutral boron atoms and all ionization states from singly charged B$^+$ through fully stripped B$^{5+}$ (atomic number $Z = 5$) — evaluated locally at the separatrix, the last closed flux surface that forms the outer boundary of the magnetically confined plasma.

The total boron density aggregates contributions across all charge states:

$$
n_B = \sum_{q=0}^{5} n_{B^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{B^{q+}}$ is the local number density of boron in ionization state $q$, with $q = 0$ denoting neutral boron. This boundary value enters impurity particle continuity and transport equations and provides the outer boundary condition for core–edge impurity coupling; see [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) for the general multi-species framework. The local separatrix value is distinct from the poloidally averaged form [flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which is frequently used in radial transport analysis.

Separatrix boron density is inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or passive spectroscopy of boron emission lines in the edge region, and is compared with [electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary) to derive the fractional boron impurity concentration. In boronized tokamaks, separatrix boron densities span roughly $10^{16}$–$10^{18}$ m$^{-3}$, corresponding to fractional concentrations of order $10^{-4}$–$10^{-2}$ relative to the separatrix electron density, and are sensitive to recent wall conditioning and boronization frequency.
NAMES.sign: Positive when boron particles are present at the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: density_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short: Number density of a specified particle population serving as the low-density baseline on the open-field-line side of an edge-pedestal fit.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the number density assigned to a specified particle population as the low-density baseline of an analytic edge-pedestal representation on the open-field-line side of the confined plasma. It represents the offset from which the pedestal rise is described.

For a fitted density representation, the baseline is the offset term:

$$
n_{\mathrm{fit}}(\xi)=n_{\mathrm{base}}+\Delta n(\xi)
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{fit}}$ is the fitted number density, $n_{\mathrm{base}}$ is the baseline number density, $\Delta n(\xi)$ is the pedestal-dependent contribution, and $\xi$ is an edge coordinate.

The particle population is specified by each specialization; [electron density over scrape-off layer](name:electron_density_over_scrape_off_layer) is one concrete instance. The baseline is distinct from the density at the plasma boundary, represented by [density at plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), and from the density at the pedestal top, represented by [density at pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top).

NAMES.name: derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed derivative of fitted electron density with respect to normalized poloidal flux coordinate, evaluated at the H-mode pedestal location where the absolute derivative is largest.
NAMES.long:
Signed derivative of fitted electron density with respect to normalized poloidal flux coordinate, evaluated at the H-mode pedestal location where the absolute derivative is largest, is the algebraically signed slope of the fitted electron-density function of $\psi_N$. The normalized poloidal flux coordinate $\psi_N$ labels poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces and increases from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

The pedestal-maximum derivative is defined by

$$
G_{n_e,\mathrm{ped,max}} =
\left.\frac{d n_e}{d\psi_N}\right|_{\psi_N=\xi_{\max}},
\qquad
\xi_{\max}=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\xi\in P_{\mathrm{ped}}}
\left|\left.\frac{d n_e}{d\psi_N}\right|_{\psi_N=\xi}\right|
$$

where $G_{n_e,\mathrm{ped,max}}$ denotes this derivative, $n_e$ is the fitted [electron density](name:electron_density), $\psi_N=(\psi-\psi_0)/(\psi_b-\psi_0)$ is the normalized poloidal flux coordinate, $\psi$ is [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux), $\psi_0$ is its value at the magnetic axis, $\psi_b$ is its value at the plasma boundary, $P_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the H-mode pedestal interval in $\psi_N$, and $\xi_{\max}$ is the coordinate value selected by the maximum absolute derivative.

The maximum qualifier is a locus-selection rule based on absolute derivative, not a statement that the reported derivative is non-negative and not the location of maximum density. This quantity is distinct from [gradient_of_radial_electron_density](name:gradient_of_radial_electron_density), which is the density-gradient quantity associated with the pedestal-top core-side shoulder locus. It is the electron-density counterpart of [gradient_of_electron_pressure](name:gradient_of_electron_pressure), and it differs from [electron-pressure pedestal-top derivative](name:derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top) and [electron-temperature pedestal-top derivative](name:derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_temperature_at_pedestal_top), which fix the evaluation point at the pedestal top rather than at the steepest H-mode pedestal slope.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $n_e$ increases with increasing normalized poloidal flux coordinate $\psi_N$.

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Number density of deuterium ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter core plasma.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium density at the pedestal top is the local number density of deuterium ions (D$^+$, $Z=1$, $A=2$) at the shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, where the steep edge density gradient transitions to the flatter confined-plasma core profile. As the primary fuel ion species in standard deuterium operations, this quantity is a species-resolved member of the [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family and represents the dominant single ion contribution to the total pedestal charge balance.

The deuterium ion density at the pedestal top participates in the local quasi-neutrality constraint alongside all other ion populations:

$$
n_e = n_D + \sum_s Z_s \, n_s
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $n_D$ is the deuterium number density (D$^+$ carries a single ionization state), $Z_s$ is the charge number of impurity or minority species $s$, and $n_s$ is the number density of that species at the pedestal top.

Deuterium pedestal density is inferred from Thomson scattering electron density profiles combined with quasi-neutrality, from Balmer-series Stark broadening, or from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy. In H-mode tokamaks, pedestal-top densities range from roughly $1$–$10 \times 10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on plasma current, toroidal field, and fueling rate. Species-resolved siblings include [hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top](name:hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top) for protium, [helium_4_density_at_pedestal_top](name:helium_4_density_at_pedestal_top) for helium-4 ash, and [electron_density_at_pedestal_top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top) for the complementary electron population at this radial location.

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Number density of the effective deuterium–tritium fuel-ion population evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, where the steep-gradient barrier meets the flatter core plasma.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium–tritium density at the pedestal top is the local number density of the effective deuterium–tritium fuel-ion population at the shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, where the steep edge density gradient transitions to the flatter confined-plasma core variation. The pedestal top is the common evaluation locus for the [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family.

The pedestal-top value is the combined local density of deuterium and tritium fuel ions evaluated on the pedestal-top flux surface:

$$
n_{\mathrm{DT,ped}} = \left.\left(n_{\mathrm{D}^+} + n_{\mathrm{T}^+}\right)\right|_{\rho=\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{D}^+}$ and $n_{\mathrm{T}^+}$ are the local densities of deuterium and tritium ions, respectively, $\rho$ is the radial flux-surface label in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, and $\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}$ identifies the pedestal-top surface.

This quantity represents an effective single fuel species, not the deuterium–tritium fusion reaction channel. It includes the ionized deuterium and tritium fuel populations, excludes neutral atoms and molecules, and combines the separate [deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top](name:deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top) and [tritium_density_at_pedestal_top](name:tritium_density_at_pedestal_top) contributions at the same locus.

NAMES.name: edge_localized_mode_frequency
NAMES.subject: edge_localized_mode
NAMES.short: Rate of recurrent edge-localized mode events during an ELMing H-mode phase, expressing the cadence of pedestal-relaxation bursts rather than their amplitude or exhaust.
NAMES.long:
The edge-localized mode frequency is the event rate of recurrent pedestal-relaxation bursts during an ELMing H-mode phase. It characterizes the cadence of ELM events, not their amplitude, duration, expelled particle content, or transient energy.

$$
f_{\mathrm{ELM}} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{ELM}}}{\Delta t}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{ELM}}$ is the ELM event frequency, $N_{\mathrm{ELM}}$ is the number of identified ELM events, and $\Delta t$ is the elapsed interval over which those events are counted. The interval must represent the ELMing phase being characterized; isolated events outside that phase are excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Edge Localized Mode (ELM) frequency, the repetition rate of ELM events during an H-mode discharge. A key parameter characterizing the ELM regime and its impact on divertor heat loads.

NAMES.name: effective_charge_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Effective charge at the pedestal top is the local plasma effective charge evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the steep-gradient H-mode edge transport barrier. It measures the charge-squared weighted contribution of all ion species and charge states relative to the local electron density.
NAMES.long:
Effective charge at the pedestal top is the local plasma effective charge evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the steep-gradient H-mode edge transport barrier. It characterizes the all-ion charge-squared weighting relative to the local electron density at that locus.

The local effective charge is defined by the charge-squared weighted ion-density sum normalized by electron density:

$$
Z_\mathrm{eff} = \frac{\sum_{s,c} n_{s,c} Z_{s,c}^{2}}{n_e}
$$

where $s$ labels ion species, $c$ labels charge state, $n_{s,c}$ is the number density of ions of species $s$ in charge state $c$, $Z_{s,c}$ is the corresponding positive charge number, and $n_e$ is the electron number density.

The sum includes hydrogenic fuel ions, helium ash, and impurity ions in all populated charge states at the pedestal top. For a quasineutral plasma, $n_e = \sum_{s,c} n_{s,c} Z_{s,c}$, so a plasma containing only singly ionized hydrogenic ions has $Z_\mathrm{eff}=1$; higher charge states increase $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ in proportion to $n_{s,c} Z_{s,c}^{2}$. This is the pedestal-top specialization of [effective_charge](name:effective_charge) and is the same physical mixture quantity denoted by [charge_at_pedestal_top](name:charge_at_pedestal_top), not a separate component or subterm.

NAMES.name: effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Effective charge number of the ion mixture at the plasma boundary is the charge-squared-weighted sum of ionic number densities divided by the electron number density at that boundary. It equals one for a purely singly charged hydrogenic ion mixture and increases with impurity charge content.
NAMES.long:
Effective charge number of the ion mixture at the plasma boundary is the charge-squared-weighted sum of ionic number densities divided by the electron number density, evaluated at the plasma boundary where the confined plasma meets the last closed flux surface. Because each ion population is weighted by the square of its charge number, higher charge states contribute disproportionately to this quantity relative to their particle density.

The boundary value is defined from the charge-state-resolved ion densities by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff},b} = \frac{\sum_i n_{i,b} Z_i^2}{n_{e,b}}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},b}$ is the effective charge at the plasma boundary, $i$ indexes every ion species and charge state present at the boundary, $n_{i,b}$ is the number density of ion population $i$ at the boundary in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, $Z_i$ is its charge number, and $n_{e,b}$ is the electron number density at the boundary in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$. Under quasineutrality, $n_{e,b} = \sum_i n_{i,b} Z_i$, so the denominator equals the charge-weighted (first-moment) sum of the same ion densities.

The sum includes all ion species and all charge states at the boundary; for a quasineutral, purely singly charged hydrogenic ion mixture, $Z_{\mathrm{eff},b} = 1$, and any admixture of multiply charged impurities raises the value above unity. This local boundary value is distinct from [flux-surface-averaged effective charge at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary), which applies an explicit average over the boundary flux surface, and from [effective charge at the limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter), which is evaluated at the limiter contact location rather than at the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: electron_average_temperature_at_midplane
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron average temperature at midplane is the path-length-weighted mean electron kinetic temperature along an open scrape-off-layer magnetic field line between its upstream midplane crossing and its connected downstream divertor target.
NAMES.long:
Electron average temperature at midplane is the path-length-weighted mean electron kinetic temperature along an open scrape-off-layer magnetic field line, assigned to the field line's upstream midplane crossing. The upstream endpoint is the same midplane locus used for [electron temperature at midplane](name:electron_temperature_at_midplane), and the downstream endpoint is the connected divertor-target locus used for [electron temperature at divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target). The midplane is a surface of constant vertical coordinate $Z=Z_\mathrm{mid}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Let $s$ be distance along the magnetic field line, increasing from the upstream midplane endpoint $s_u$ to the downstream divertor-target endpoint $s_d$. The field-line average is

$$
\langle T_e \rangle_\parallel = \frac{1}{s_d - s_u}\int_{s_u}^{s_d} T_e(s)\,ds
$$

where $T_e(s)$ is the local electron kinetic temperature on the same field line, $s_u$ is the upstream midplane endpoint, $s_d$ is the downstream divertor-target endpoint, and $s_d-s_u$ is the parallel connection length between them.

This quantity is an arclength average over a single connected open field-line segment, not a volume average, a flux-surface average, or a local endpoint temperature. It is defined for open field lines that intersect the midplane and terminate on a divertor target.

NAMES.name: electron_collisionality_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of the electron collision frequency to the characteristic electron bounce frequency at the H-mode pedestal top, governing the neoclassical transport regime of the pedestal electron population.
NAMES.long:
Electron collisionality at the pedestal top quantifies the ratio of the electron collision rate to the trapped-electron bounce frequency at the inner shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is the electron-specific member of [collisionality_at_pedestal_top](name:collisionality_at_pedestal_top) and determines whether pedestal electrons occupy the banana, plateau, or Pfirsch–Schlüter transport regime.

The standard dimensionless electron collisionality is

$$
\nu_e^* = \frac{\nu_{ei} \, q R}{\epsilon^{3/2} \, v_{\mathrm{the}}}
$$

where $\nu_{ei}$ is the electron–ion collision frequency, $q$ is the local safety factor, $R$ is the major radius, $\epsilon = r/R$ is the inverse aspect ratio at the pedestal with minor radius $r$, and $v_{\mathrm{the}} = \sqrt{2T_e/m_e}$ is the electron thermal speed with electron temperature $T_e$ and electron mass $m_e$.

This parameter is central to pedestal physics: $\nu_e^* \ll 1$ places electrons in the banana regime where trapped particles complete bounce orbits and bootstrap current is substantial, while $\nu_e^* \gg 1$ suppresses trapping effects and enhances Pfirsch–Schlüter transport. At the pedestal top, electron collisionality enters peeling-ballooning and kinetic-ballooning-mode stability criteria. It is computed from pedestal electron density and temperature profiles, commonly from Thomson scattering, combined with the [coulomb_logarithm_at_pedestal_top](name:coulomb_logarithm_at_pedestal_top) to evaluate $\nu_{ei}$.

In H-mode operation, pedestal electron collisionality spans approximately 0.01–1 depending on device size, toroidal field, and heating power; projected burning-plasma devices are expected to operate in the low-collisionality banana regime ($\nu_e^* \lesssim 0.1$). The child quantity [normalized_electron_collisionality_at_pedestal_top](name:normalized_electron_collisionality_at_pedestal_top) expresses this ratio relative to a reference value for cross-machine comparisons.

NAMES.name: electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Characteristic outward distance over which electron number density decreases by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for electron number density that decreases outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It is the electron-density member of the [decay-length family](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), distinct from the [ion decay length](name:ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

$$
L_e = \left|\frac{d\ln n_e}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_e$ is the electron-density e-folding length, $n_e$ is electron number density, and $x$ is outward distance normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The quantity is defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is nonzero; the magnitude gives the positive distance associated with the outward decrease. It does not denote the decay length of temperature or heat flux, which are separate members of the family.

sources.enhanced_context: Radial e-folding decay length of the electron density (λne) in the scrape-off layer (SOL), defined as the inverse of the logarithmic gradient of ne. Characterizes the width of the particle transport channel in the SOL.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron density radial decay length inv(grad ne/ne)

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_launching_position
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron number density at the wave-launching position is the local free-electron count per unit volume where an injected electromagnetic wave first contacts the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local free-electron number density at the geometric launching position, such as a wave launcher aperture or waveguide mouth where an injected electromagnetic wave first contacts the edge plasma. It is the electron-specific component of [number density at the launching position](name:density_at_launching_position).

The density is defined from the electron velocity-distribution function by

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}})=\int f_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_e$ is electron number density, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}}$ is the launching position, $f_e$ is the electron velocity-distribution function, and $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity.

This is a local value for free electrons at the launching position, not a density summed over plasma species, a flux-surface average, or a wave-power quantity. It is distinct from [electron number density at the plasma boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which is evaluated at the last closed flux surface.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of electrons at the pedestal top is the particle count per volume for the electron population at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
Number density of electrons at the pedestal top is the particle count per volume for the electron population evaluated at the core-side shoulder of an H-mode pedestal. The pedestal top is the transition where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter confined-core electron-density variation, distinct from a separatrix or plasma-boundary value.

For the electron population on the pedestal-top flux surface, the defining local density is

$$
n_e(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}) = \left.\frac{dN_e}{dV}\right|_{\xi=\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}}
$$

where $n_e$ is electron number density, $N_e$ is the dimensionless electron count, $V$ is physical volume, and $\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}$ is the selected radial label of the pedestal-top flux surface.

This electron-specific quantity is a member of the general [density at pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family and counts electrons rather than ions; the corresponding [ion density at pedestal top](name:ion_density_at_pedestal_top) counts the ion population.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Electron density at the plasma boundary is the local number density of electrons evaluated on the last closed flux surface (LCFS), which separates nested closed-field-line plasma from open-field-line scrape-off-layer plasma. It is the electron-specific instance of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

The defining local relation is

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{b}} = \left.\frac{dN_e}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{LCFS}}
$$

where $N_e$ is the number of electrons, $V$ is volume, and the subscript $\mathrm{b}$ denotes evaluation at the LCFS.

This quantity includes electrons only and excludes ion and impurity number densities. It is a local boundary value, distinct from [flux-surface-averaged electron density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which applies an additional average over the LCFS.

NAMES.name: electron_density_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged electron number density in the scrape-off layer, the open-field-line plasma region outside the last closed flux surface. In analytic H-mode pedestal representations it is the scrape-off-layer-side density offset, not a density at the boundary or pedestal top.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged electron number density over the scrape-off layer is the electron count per volume assigned to the open-field-line plasma region outside the last closed flux surface. The conventional symbol is $n_{e,\mathrm{SOL}}$.

For a resolved electron-density field, the scrape-off-layer value is the volume average over the scrape-off-layer volume:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{SOL}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron number density, $V_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the scrape-off-layer volume, and $dV$ is the volume element.

When used as a parameter of an analytic H-mode pedestal representation, the same quantity denotes the scrape-off-layer-side density offset or floor that represents this regional low-density baseline. It is distinct from [electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which is evaluated at the last closed flux surface, and from electron_density_at_pedestal, which is evaluated at the pedestal reference location.

NAMES.name: energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.short: Fick's-law coefficient relating the diffusive thermal energy flux of a plasma constituent to its local temperature gradient, serving as the species-agnostic parent abstraction over electron, ion, and neutral population specializations.
NAMES.long:
The energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven thermal energy transport for any plasma constituent — electrons, ions, or neutrals — by specifying the proportionality between the diffusive heat flux and the local temperature gradient in the Fick's-law sense. It is the thermal-energy channel of the general diffusion_coefficient, which governs particle, momentum, and energy transport alike, and it is distinct from convective or $E \times B$ contributions to the total heat flux.

The defining relation for the diffusive energy flux $\mathbf{Q}_\mathrm{diff}$ of a given constituent is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_\mathrm{diff} = -D_E \, \nabla T
$$

where $D_E$ is the energy diffusion coefficient and $\nabla T$ is the temperature gradient of that constituent. In a magnetized plasma $D_E$ is strongly anisotropic; radial cross-field values govern energy confinement while values along field lines are orders of magnitude larger.

Species-resolved children include [electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient) for the electron population and [ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) for the total ion population aggregated over all charge states; neutral-particle transport is handled by analogous neutral specializations. The effective diffusivity that combines diffusive and convective contributions is tracked separately by energy_effective_diffusivity.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of argon ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix), summed over all ionization stages from Ar+ through fully stripped Ar18+.
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged argon density at the plasma boundary is the argon ion number density, summed over all ionization states from Ar+ through fully stripped Ar18+, averaged over the last closed flux surface (separatrix) that divides magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The flux-surface average is defined as:

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}} \rangle = \frac{\oint n_{\mathrm{Ar}} \, dl / B_p}{\oint dl / B_p}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the local argon number density summed over all charge states, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, and the integrals are taken along the separatrix contour at constant poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$.

This boundary-averaged quantity is inferred from visible and vacuum ultraviolet spectroscopy of argon emission lines combined with collisional-radiative ionization balance modeling to reconstruct the full charge-state distribution. It serves as a boundary condition for impurity transport calculations in the confined plasma and is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of [argon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary), which retains the full poloidal variation along the separatrix.

Related boundary-averaged impurity densities following the same averaging convention include [flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when argon ions are present at the separatrix, which holds for all plasma states with non-zero argon seeding.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Flux-surface average of the beryllium-ion number density over the plasma boundary, summed across beryllium ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged number density of beryllium ions on the plasma boundary, with contributions from Be+ through Be4+. It differs from the local [beryllium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary) by averaging over the entire boundary surface.

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}} \rangle = \frac{\oint n_{\mathrm{Be}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi|}{\oint dS/|\nabla\psi|}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}} = \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the total beryllium-ion number density, $dS$ is the surface element, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label. The average is evaluated on the separatrix, the outermost closed magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the beryllium-ion number density is positive.

sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of boron, including neutral atoms and all ionization states, evaluated on the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the boron particle number density averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary. It includes neutral boron and all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+, rather than selecting a single charge state. It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of [boron density at the plasma boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary).

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm B}\rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm B}\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} \frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

Here $n_{\mathrm B}$ is the local total boron particle number density, $\psi$ is the poloidal-flux surface label, $\psi_b$ identifies the plasma-boundary surface, and $dS$ is its surface element. The result is an average over the complete surface, not the density at a selected point or for a selected ionization state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the underlying boron number density is positive.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of carbon ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix), summed over all ionization stages from singly ionized C+ through fully stripped C6+.
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged carbon ion number density at the plasma boundary is the mean of the local carbon ion count per unit volume over the last closed flux surface that separates the magnetically confined plasma from the open scrape-off layer. The averaging eliminates poloidal asymmetries along the separatrix contour and yields a single representative scalar for total carbon impurity content, summed over all charge states from C+ through fully stripped C6+ (atomic number $Z_C = 6$).

The flux-surface average is defined as:

$$
\langle n_C \rangle = \frac{\oint n_C \, dl/B}{\oint dl/B}
$$

where $n_C$ is the local carbon number density summed over all ionization states, $B$ is the magnetic field magnitude, and the line integral runs along the poloidal contour of the plasma boundary flux surface.

Carbon enters the plasma primarily through physical sputtering and chemical erosion of carbon-based plasma-facing components; its concentration at the separatrix reflects edge wall source rates, cross-field diffusion, and parallel transport in the scrape-off layer. The boundary value is inferred from passive spectroscopy of carbon emission lines or active charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, or computed by impurity transport simulations tracking wall sources.

This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged transformation of its parent [carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary), which gives the local (non-averaged) separatrix density. The volume-integrated carbon content is captured by [carbon_density](name:carbon_density). Analogous flux-surface-averaged boundary densities exist for other impurity species: flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary, [flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary), and [flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when carbon ions are present at the plasma boundary; zero in the carbon-free limit.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged deuterium ion number density at the plasma boundary is the boundary flux-surface average of local deuterium ion density, summed over all ionic charge states and excluding neutral deuterium atoms and molecules.
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface-averaged deuterium ion number density at the plasma boundary is the scalar flux-surface average of local deuterium ion number density on the separatrix, the last closed magnetic flux surface separating closed confined field lines from open scrape-off-layer field lines. At species level, the deuterium ion population is summed over all ionic charge states and excludes neutral deuterium atoms and molecules.

The boundary flux-surface average is defined in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ labels nested flux surfaces and $\rho_b$ labels the plasma boundary:

$$
\langle n_D \rangle_{\rho_b} = \frac{\int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{2\pi} n_D(\rho_b,\theta,\phi)\,J(\rho_b,\theta,\phi)\,d\theta\,d\phi}{\int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{2\pi} J(\rho_b,\theta,\phi)\,d\theta\,d\phi}
$$

where $n_D$ is the local charge-state-summed deuterium ion number density, $J$ is the flux-coordinate Jacobian, $\theta$ is a poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with $R$ major radius and $Z$ vertical height.

This is a flux-surface average over the boundary surface, not a local point value such as [deuterium ion number density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary). It is the deuterium species contribution distinct from the species-summed [flux-surface-averaged ion density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) and is directly analogous to [flux-surface-averaged hydrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [flux-surface-averaged tritium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of deuterium-tritium pseudo-species ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix).
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of deuterium-tritium pseudo-species ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix) is the particle density of the effective deuterium-tritium fuel species averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface. The pseudo-species represents the deuterium-tritium fuel mixture as a single ion constituent with effective mass number 2.5; as a species-level density, it is summed over all charge states.

Using the poloidal-contour representation of a flux-surface average in an axisymmetric equilibrium, the boundary value is defined by:

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_b =
\frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm{DT}}(l)\, dl / B_p(l)}
{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} dl / B_p(l)}
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_b$ is this boundary average, $\psi_b$ labels the plasma-boundary flux surface, $l$ is poloidal arc length along that surface, and $B_p$ is the [poloidal magnetic-field magnitude]. The local pseudo-species density is $n_{\mathrm{DT}} = n_{\mathrm{D}} + n_{\mathrm{T}}$, where $n_{\mathrm{D}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ are the corresponding charge-state-summed deuterium and tritium ion densities.

This quantity is the plasma-boundary member of [flux-surface-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary) and the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of [deuterium-tritium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which retains variation around the same boundary surface. The single-isotope boundary analog [flux-surface-averaged deuterium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary) separates one isotope contribution, while [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density) averages the same effective fuel population over the confined-plasma volume. It excludes scrape-off-layer and material-limiter densities, including [deuterium-tritium density at a limiter](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter).

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Flux-surface average of electron number density on the last closed flux surface, representing the separatrix density approached from the confined-plasma side.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the electron number density averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface (LCFS), which bounds the magnetically confined plasma. It represents the separatrix value approached from closed-field-line surfaces.

The confined-side flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_{\mathrm{LCFS}} = \lim_{\psi\to\psi_b^-} \frac{\oint_{\psi} n_e\,dl/B_p}{\oint_{\psi} dl/B_p}
$$

where $n_e$ is the local electron number density, $\psi$ is a poloidal-flux surface label, $\psi_b$ labels the LCFS, $l$ is distance along the surface, and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude.

Unlike the local [electron density at the plasma boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), this quantity averages the density around each closed flux surface before taking the boundary limit. It is the electron-specific counterpart of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.enhanced_context: Electron density (ne) at the separatrix, flux-surface averaged over the entire core-SOL boundary. Represents the local electron particle density at the plasma-edge interface.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron density

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix), summed over all helium-4 charge states (He+ and He2+).
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged helium-4 ion number density at the plasma boundary is the poloidal average of $n_{\rm He4}$ over the last closed flux surface, the separatrix dividing the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. Helium-4, produced primarily by deuterium–tritium fusion reactions, constitutes the principal fusion ash species; its concentration at the boundary characterizes helium exhaust efficiency and the risk of core fuel dilution. The density is summed over all helium-4 charge states present as ions, $\mathrm{He}^+$ and fully stripped $\mathrm{He}^{2+}$, consistent with the parent quantity [helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The flux-surface average reduces the poloidal variation to a single scalar via:

$$
\langle n_{\rm He4} \rangle = \frac{\oint n_{\rm He4} \, dS \, / |\nabla \psi|}{\oint dS \, / |\nabla \psi|}
$$

where $dS$ is the surface element on the flux surface and $\nabla \psi$ is the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$.

This scalar boundary value provides an outer boundary condition for helium-4 transport modeling in the confined plasma. It is inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or passive spectroscopic emission measurements in the edge region, or from integrated edge transport simulations. Elevated values relative to the main ion density indicate insufficient helium pumping. The analogous quantity for the helium-3 isotope is [flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary), and [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary) provides the corresponding main fuel species reference.
NAMES.sign: Positive when helium-4 ions are present at the plasma boundary; as a particle number density, this quantity is non-negative by definition.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged hydrogen ion number density at the plasma boundary, summed over all hydrogen ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface-averaged hydrogen ion number density at the plasma boundary is the charge-state-summed density of hydrogen ions, averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface (separatrix).

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm H}\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\oint_{\mathrm{sep}} n_{\mathrm H}\,dl/B_{\mathrm p}}{\oint_{\mathrm{sep}} dl/B_{\mathrm p}}
$$

Here $n_{\mathrm H}$ is the local hydrogen ion number density, $dl$ is poloidal arc length, and $B_{\mathrm p}$ is the magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field; both integrals follow the separatrix. The hydrogen charge-state sum is formed before the flux-surface average. This quantity is the averaged counterpart of [hydrogen ion number density at the plasma boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which denotes the corresponding local boundary value.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged total number density of lithium ions, summed over all charge states from Li+ through Li3+, evaluated at the plasma boundary (separatrix).
NAMES.long:
This is the flux-surface average of lithium ion number density, summed over all ionization stages from Li$^+$ through fully stripped Li$^{3+}$, evaluated on the last closed flux surface (separatrix) that bounds the confined plasma. The averaging collapses poloidal variation along the boundary into a single representative scalar, yielding the mean lithium impurity content at the confined-plasma edge — the flux-surface-averaged counterpart to [lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The flux-surface average of lithium number density $n_{Li}$ on the separatrix is defined as

$$
\langle n_{Li} \rangle = \frac{\oint n_{Li}\, dl / B_p}{\oint dl / B_p}
$$

where $l$ is the poloidal arc length along the separatrix contour and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field strength.

This quantity is inferred from impurity transport modeling constrained by edge spectroscopy — passive emission of lithium lines or charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy — and serves as a standard boundary condition in edge and core transport codes. Analogous flux-surface-averaged boundary densities for other species include [flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary), [flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary), and [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary). In lithium-coated wall devices, separatrix lithium densities can reach $10^{16}$–$10^{18}$ m$^{-3}$; under trace impurity conditions the boundary value falls in the range $10^{14}$–$10^{16}$ m$^{-3}$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the separatrix plasma contains lithium impurity ions.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix), summed over all ionization stages from Ne+ through fully stripped Ne10+.
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged neon density at the plasma boundary is the poloidal-flux-surface average of the neon ion number density, encompassing all charge states from Ne+ through fully stripped Ne10+, evaluated on the last closed flux surface that separates the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It provides a single representative scalar characterizing the neon impurity content at the plasma edge, suppressing poloidal asymmetries that arise from localized recycling, divertor pumping, or asymmetric gas puffing.

The flux-surface average is defined as

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{Ne} \rangle_\mathrm{FS} = \frac{\oint n_\mathrm{Ne}(\ell)\, d\ell / B_p}{\oint d\ell / B_p}
$$

where $n_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the local neon number density summed over all charge states, $\ell$ is the arc length along the separatrix contour, and $B_p$ is the local poloidal magnetic field magnitude.

This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged variant of [neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary); the two differ in that the parent retains the full poloidal dependence while this quantity condenses it to a single scalar. Structurally parallel quantities at the same locus exist for other impurity and fuel species, including [flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary), and [flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary). Neon is widely deployed as a radiative seed impurity for boundary power exhaust management, and the separatrix-averaged density is a key input to edge transport models and empirical scaling studies. It is inferred from VUV or charge-exchange spectroscopy combined with boundary plasma modeling.
NAMES.sign: Positive for non-zero neon impurity concentration at the plasma boundary.

NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Number density of oxygen impurity ions evaluated at the plasma boundary is the flux-surface average of the charge-state-summed oxygen ion concentration on the last closed flux surface. It is summed over all ionization states of oxygen and excludes neutral oxygen.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of positively charged tungsten ions on the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the number density of tungsten ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface, with all positive ionization states included and neutral tungsten excluded. It is the surface-averaged counterpart of the local [tungsten density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The flux-surface average at the plasma-boundary flux label is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}} \rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm{W}}\,d\ell_p/B_p}{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} d\ell_p/B_p}
$$

where $\psi_b$ is the flux label of the plasma boundary, $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the local summed tungsten-ion density, $d\ell_p$ is poloidal contour length, and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. The quantity is distinct from [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), which averages over the enclosed plasma volume.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the flux-surface average represents a positive count of tungsten ions on the boundary, rather than a signed perturbation.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of xenon ions at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface), summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged xenon density at the plasma boundary is the poloidal flux-surface average of the local xenon ion number density evaluated on the last closed flux surface (separatrix), summed over all ionization stages from Xe$^{1+}$ through fully stripped Xe$^{54+}$ — the same charge-state aggregation used by [xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary). The flux-surface average removes the poloidal dependence and yields a single scalar characterizing xenon impurity content at the separatrix.

The flux-surface average on the separatrix is defined as:

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{Xe} \rangle_\mathrm{sep} = \frac{\oint n_\mathrm{Xe} \, dl / |\nabla \psi|}{\oint dl / |\nabla \psi|}
$$

where $n_\mathrm{Xe}$ is the local xenon number density summed over all ionization states, $dl$ is the poloidal arc length element, and $\nabla \psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux gradient evaluated at the separatrix.

Xenon is a heavy noble-gas impurity injected in tokamak experiments to promote edge radiative power loss and to facilitate divertor detachment. This separatrix-averaged density reflects the balance of impurity injection, cross-field transport, and recycling near the plasma boundary, and is inferred from edge spectroscopic measurements of xenon emission lines combined with impurity transport modeling. In seeded or detached regimes the separatrix value lies in the range $10^{14}$–$10^{16}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on seeding rate and plasma configuration. Analogous quantities for lighter impurities include [flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when xenon ions are present at the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short: Characteristic outward distance over which a decaying heat-flux magnitude decreases by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer, without selecting an electron or ion channel.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for a heat-flux magnitude that decreases outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It represents the common decay-length concept for both electron and ion heat fluxes without selecting either channel.

$$
L_q = \left|\frac{d\ln q}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_q$ is the e-folding length, $q$ is the positive heat-flux magnitude, and $x$ is outward distance normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The scale is defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is nonzero. The quantity is the heat-flux specialization of [decay length over scrape-off layer](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer); its species-resolved instances include [electron heat decay length](name:electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer) and [ion heat decay length](name:ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the reference direction is outward from the confined plasma into the scrape-off layer and the heat-flux magnitude decreases along it.

NAMES.name: electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Radial e-folding decay length of the electron heat flux in the scrape-off layer, defined by the inverse magnitude of its outward logarithmic gradient.
NAMES.long:
The electron heat decay length in the scrape-off layer (SOL) is the radial distance over which the electron heat-flux profile falls to $1/e$ of its separatrix value. It characterizes the spatial scale of electron heat exhaust across the open-field-line region and specializes the channel-unspecified [heat decay length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

The decay length is defined as the inverse magnitude of the outward logarithmic gradient of the electron heat flux:

$$
\lambda_{q,e} = \left| \frac{\partial \ln q_e}{\partial r} \right|^{-1}
$$

where $q_e$ is the electron heat flux and $r$ is radial distance measured outward from the separatrix into the SOL.

This quantity includes only the electron heat channel and is distinct from the corresponding [ion heat decay length](name:ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). As the magnitude of a logarithmic gradient, the decay length is non-negative.

sources.enhanced_context: Electron heat flux radial decay length in the scrape-off layer (SOL), defined as the inverse of the logarithmic gradient of the electron heat flux (qe): λqe = |qe / (dqe/dr)|. Characterizes how rapidly the electron heat flux falls off radially in the SOL.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron heat flux radial decay length inv(grad qe/qe)

NAMES.name: heat_flux
NAMES.short: Vector of plasma energy transport per unit area, whose projection through an oriented surface gives the power crossing it through convective, conductive, and turbulent channels.
NAMES.long:
The heat-flux vector represents the net transport of plasma energy through space, including convective, conductive, cross-field, field-aligned, and fluctuation-driven contributions when included in the energy balance.

For an oriented surface $S$, the transported power is defined by

$$
P_S = \int_S \mathbf{q} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\,dA
$$

where $\mathbf{q}$ is the heat-flux vector, $P_S$ is the crossing power in W, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen unit normal, and $dA$ is a surface element in m$^2$. The [parallel heat flux](name:parallel_heat_flux) is its projection along the local magnetic-field direction. Convective transport may be parameterized by the [ratio of heat flux to product of particle flux and particle temperature due to convection](name:ratio_of_heat_flux_to_product_of_particle_flux_and_particle_temperature_due_to_convection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the local component of $\mathbf{q}$ points along the chosen oriented surface normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Number density of helium-3 ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter core profile, summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Helium-3 density at the pedestal is the local number density of helium-3 ions ($Z=2$, $A=3$) at the top of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over all ionization states from singly ionized $\mathrm{He}^+$ through fully stripped $\mathrm{He}^{2+}$. The pedestal top is the radial position where the steep edge density gradient transitions to the more weakly varying confined-core density; it is distinct from the separatrix or [density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) locus.

$$
n_{\mathrm{He3}}(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}) = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{He3}}}{dV}\right|_{\xi = \xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{He3}}$ is the helium-3 ion count summed over charge states $q = 1$ and $q = 2$, $V$ is physical volume in m$^3$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}$ is the radial label of the pedestal-top flux surface (for example $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ or $\psi_N$). This name is the helium-3 isotopic member of the [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family; the helium-4 isotopic counterpart is [helium_4_density_at_pedestal_top](name:helium_4_density_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when helium-3 ions are present in the pedestal plasma.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Helium-3 density at the plasma boundary is the particle number density of helium-3 ions evaluated at the last closed flux surface, which separates magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It is the helium-3 specialization of [density at plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{^3\mathrm{He}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density, $q$ is the ionic charge state, and $n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}$ is the density of helium-3 ions in charge state $q$. Neutral helium-3 is excluded. The local value differs from the flux-surface average defined by [flux-surface-averaged helium-3 density at plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when helium-3 ions are present at the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix), summed over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged helium-3 ion number density at the plasma boundary is the mean particle concentration of ³He ions across the last closed flux surface (separatrix), summed over all ionization states — singly ionized He³⁺ through fully stripped He³²⁺. This quantity forms the explicit flux-surface-averaged counterpart of [helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary), anchoring the helium-3 inventory to the outermost magnetically confined flux surface that separates the confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The flux-surface average is defined as:

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{He3}} \rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\oint_{\psi_b} n_{\mathrm{He3}} \, dA}{\oint_{\psi_b} dA}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He3}}$ is the local helium-3 number density at the boundary flux surface identified by poloidal magnetic flux value $\psi_b$, and the surface integrals are evaluated over the full last closed flux surface.

Helium-3 (nuclear charge $Z = 2$, mass number $A = 3$) arises as a D–D fusion product and is used as a minority ion-cyclotron resonance heating species. The boundary density characterizes the helium-3 content available for recycling into the scrape-off layer and informs edge particle balance assessments. It is inferred from edge charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or line-emission spectroscopy, combined with equilibrium reconstruction to locate and integrate over the separatrix geometry. The sibling quantity [flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary) provides the corresponding value for the ⁴He isotope, while [flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary) gives the main-fuel boundary density at the same locus.
NAMES.sign: Positive when helium-3 ions are present at the plasma boundary.
