NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Number density of helium-4 ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter core profile, summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 density at the pedestal is the local number density of helium-4 ions ($Z=2$, $A=4$) at the top of the H-mode edge transport barrier, the radial position where the steep edge density gradient transitions to the more weakly varying confined-plasma core. Helium-4 is the primary fusion-product ash in deuterium–tritium burning plasmas and may also serve as a minority working gas; it is summed over all ionization stages (He$^+$ and He$^{2+}$) unless a specific charge state is specified.

The total helium-4 number density at the pedestal top is:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He\text{-}4}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He\text{-}4},\, q+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He\text{-}4},\, q+}$ is the local number density of helium-4 ions in charge state $q+$.

Pedestal-top values are inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, wherein fully stripped helium-4 captures an electron from a diagnostic neutral beam and emits measurable line radiation; the pedestal-top radial position is identified from electron pressure profiles as for all members of the [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family.

Helium-4 concentrations at the pedestal top span a few percent up to 10–20% of the local electron density, depending on divertor pumping efficiency and helium recycling. The companion [helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top](name:helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top) captures the minority mass-3 helium isotope at the same location, enabling comparative helium-isotope transport studies.

NAMES.name: ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Characteristic outward distance over which ion number density decreases by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer, equal to the positive inverse magnitude of its outward logarithmic gradient normal to magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for ion number density that decreases outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It represents the ion-density member of the scrape-off-layer decay-length family; the operand is an ion number density, not an electron number density or heat-flux magnitude.

The local ion decay length is the positive inverse magnitude of the outward logarithmic gradient of the ion density:

$$
L_\mathrm{ion} = \left|\frac{d\ln n_\mathrm{ion}}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_\mathrm{ion}$ is the ion e-folding length, $n_\mathrm{ion}$ is the positive ion number density being characterized, and $x$ is outward distance from the confined plasma in the direction normal to magnetic flux surfaces toward the scrape-off layer. The scale is defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is nonzero; for an ion species aggregated over charge states, $n_\mathrm{ion}$ is summed over all charge states before the gradient is taken.

The attested total-ion specialization [total ion decay length](name:total_ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer) applies this definition to total ion number density. This quantity remains a specialization of the fully generic [scrape-off-layer decay length](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer) and is not the parent of electron-density or heat-flux decay lengths.

NAMES.name: ion_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Number density of ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, the radial location where the steep edge transport barrier transitions toward the flatter core plasma.
NAMES.long:
Ion number density at the pedestal top is the local number of ions per unit volume at the top of the H-mode edge transport barrier. The pedestal top marks the inner shoulder of the steep-gradient region where the edge density gradient relaxes toward the more weakly varying confined-plasma core profile, and is a primary characterization point for H-mode confinement quality.

As the parent entry in the [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family, this quantity generalizes over any ion population evaluated at that locus. The primary concrete specialization is [total_ion_density_at_pedestal_top](name:total_ion_density_at_pedestal_top), which sums contributions over all ion species and charge states. Species-resolved siblings such as [deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top](name:deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top) and [hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top](name:hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top) provide single-species values at the same radial location.

The ion densities at the pedestal top are related to the local electron density through the quasi-neutrality condition:

$$
n_e = \sum_s Z_s \, n_s
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $Z_s$ is the charge number of ion species $s$, and $n_s$ is its number density at the pedestal top.

Ion pedestal densities are inferred from Thomson scattering electron density profiles combined with quasi-neutrality, from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy for individual species, or from neutral beam diagnostics. In H-mode tokamaks, pedestal-top number densities span roughly $1$–$10 \times 10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on plasma current, magnetic field, and fueling.

NAMES.name: ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Number density of ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It may be species-resolved or aggregated over charged ion species, and excludes electrons and neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Ion density at the plasma boundary is the number density of charged ions evaluated on the last closed flux surface (LCFS), which separates nested closed-field-line plasma from open-field-line scrape-off-layer plasma. It is the ion-specific instance of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), not the broader all-particle boundary density.

The defining local relation for an ion population or aggregate $i$ is

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{b}} = \left.\frac{dN_i}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{LCFS}}
$$

where $N_i$ is the number of charged ions in the selected species, charge-state set, or ion aggregate, $V$ is volume, and the subscript $\mathrm{b}$ denotes evaluation at the LCFS.

This parent spans species-resolved and aggregate ion boundary densities. A species-level ion density that is not explicitly charge-state-resolved is a charge-state-summed per-volume amount over ionized charge states; examples include [hydrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) and charge-state-summed impurity densities such as [iron density at the plasma boundary](name:iron_density_at_plasma_boundary). An aggregate such as [total ion density at the plasma boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) sums charged ion species and charge states, while [flux-surface-averaged ion density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) applies an additional average over the LCFS. Electrons and neutral particles are excluded; as a number density, $n_{i,\mathrm{b}} \ge 0$.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Number density of ions at the plasma boundary, averaged over the last closed flux surface to represent the separatrix population rather than a single local value.
NAMES.long:
Ion density at the plasma boundary is the flux-surface-averaged number density of charged ions on the last closed flux surface (LCFS), which separates confined closed-field-line plasma from open-field-line scrape-off-layer plasma. It is the averaged component of [ion density at the plasma boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), rather than the broader all-particle [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

For the selected ion population $i$, the boundary flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_i\rangle_{\mathrm{b}} = \frac{\displaystyle\int_{\psi=\psi_b} n_i\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}{\displaystyle\int_{\psi=\psi_b}\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

where $n_i$ is the local number density of the selected charged-ion population, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label, $\psi_b$ labels the LCFS, and $dS$ is the surface-area element. Species-level values are summed over ionized charge states unless a charge state is explicitly selected; electrons and neutrals are excluded. Unlike the local parent quantity, this value averages variation around the LCFS, as in [flux-surface-averaged hydrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the selected charged-ion population contributes positively to the number density on the LCFS.

NAMES.name: ion_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion diffusivity is the vector of directional effective Fickian coefficients for particle transport of the ion population summed over all charge states. A positive component corresponds to diffusive ion flux opposite to the total-ion density gradient in the same direction.
NAMES.long:
Ion diffusivity is the vector of directional effective Fickian coefficients for particle transport of the ion population summed over all charge states. Each component relates the diffusive total-ion particle flux projected along one resolved physical direction to the physical gradient of the total ion number density along that direction.

The component definition is

$$
\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,a}\left(\hat{e}_a \cdot \nabla n_i\right)
$$

where $a$ labels one resolved physical direction, $\hat{e}_a$ is the normalized direction vector, $D_{i,a}$ is the corresponding ion diffusivity component, $\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive total-ion particle flux component, and $n_i$ is the total ion number density. The projection $\hat{e}_a \cdot \nabla n_i$ is the metric-scaled physical gradient along $a$, not a bare derivative with respect to a coordinate label.

The charge-state aggregation is defined through the flux-gradient relation: $n_i$ and $\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ are sums over all ion charge states before the effective coefficient is formed. Therefore $D_{i,a}$ is not generally a density-weighted mean of [charge-state-resolved ion diffusivities](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity). The quantity includes only the diffusive, gradient-driven coefficient; it excludes advective or convective particle transport, source terms, and off-diagonal cross-gradient elements of a rank-two tensor. It differs from the scalar [ion diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient) by preserving resolved directional components; examples of such components are [poloidal ion diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_diffusion_coefficient) and [radial ion diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the diffusive ion particle flux component is opposite to the total-ion density gradient along the same resolved direction.

NAMES.name: ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Radial e-folding decay length of the ion heat flux in the scrape-off layer, defined by its outward logarithmic decrease.
NAMES.long:
The ion heat decay length in the scrape-off layer (SOL) is the radial distance over which the ion heat-flux profile falls to $1/e$ of its separatrix value, characterizing the spatial scale of ion heat exhaust across the open-field-line region.

The decay length is defined by the inverse magnitude of the outward logarithmic radial gradient of the ion heat flux $q_i$:

$$
\lambda_{q,i} = \left| \frac{\partial \ln q_i}{\partial r} \right|^{-1}
$$

where $r$ is radial distance measured outward from the separatrix and $q_i$ is the ion contribution to the heat flux. This species-resolved quantity is the ion-channel specialization of [heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer); the corresponding electron channel is [electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer](name:electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). It excludes the electron heat contribution and any unspecified total heat-flux combination.

NAMES.name: iron_density
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Total number density of iron impurity ions in the plasma, summed over all ionization states from singly to fully ionized iron (atomic number Z = 26).
NAMES.long:
Iron density is the total number density of iron ions present in the plasma, aggregated over all charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$). It characterizes the iron impurity content without resolving the per-charge-state distribution, and may refer to a local point value or a spatially averaged quantity depending on the sampling convention.

The total iron ion number density $n_\mathrm{Fe}$ is defined as:

$$
n_\mathrm{Fe} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of iron in charge state $z$.

Iron enters confined plasmas primarily through physical sputtering of high-$Z$ plasma-facing components. Spectroscopic measurements in the vacuum-ultraviolet and soft X-ray ranges resolve individual charge-state emission lines; the total iron density is reconstructed by summing ionization-state-resolved densities derived from ionization balance calculations.

This general quantity is concretized by spatial-sampling variants: [flux_surface_averaged_iron_density](name:flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary) averages the local density over a magnetic flux surface, [line_averaged_iron_density](name:line_averaged_iron_density) represents a chord-integrated value divided by path length, and [volume_averaged_iron_density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density) integrates over the full plasma volume. Position-specific forms are available at key radial locations such as [iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis), iron_density_at_pedestal, and [iron_density_at_limiter](name:iron_density_at_limiter).
NAMES.sign: Positive when iron ions are present in the sampled plasma volume; the quantity is intrinsically non-negative as a particle number density.

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Number density of iron impurity ions at the H-mode pedestal top is the particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of iron impurity ions at the H-mode pedestal top is the local particle count per volume of iron ions evaluated on the flux surface marking the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is the iron-specific child of [density at pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), where the steep pedestal gradient joins the flatter confined-core density variation.

For iron ions, the defining local density is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{dV}\right|_{\xi=\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the dimensionless count of iron ions, $V$ is physical volume in m$^{3}$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}$ is the radial label of the pedestal-top flux surface.

The quantity is summed over ionic charge states from Fe$^{+}$ through fully stripped Fe$^{26+}$ and excludes other elements and the total ion mixture represented by [total ion density at pedestal top](name:total_ion_density_at_pedestal_top).

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Number density of iron impurity ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer, summed over all ion charge states from Fe+ through fully stripped Fe26+.
NAMES.long:
Iron density at the plasma boundary is the number of iron impurity ions per unit volume — summed over all ion charge states from singly ionized Fe$^+$ through fully stripped Fe$^{26+}$ (atomic number $Z = 26$) — evaluated at the separatrix, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It represents the charge-state-summed iron impurity concentration on that boundary.

The charge-state aggregation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron ion number density at the plasma boundary, $z$ is the positive ion charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of iron ions in charge state $z+$ at the same boundary; these number-density variables have the unit specified for this standard name.

The sum is over ion charge states only, so neutral iron Fe$^0$ is excluded. As a scalar number density, the quantity is non-negative, with zero denoting absence of iron ions at the plasma boundary. It is distinct from [flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which denotes a flux-surface-averaged boundary value rather than the local boundary density.

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Number density of krypton impurity ions at the pedestal top is the particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over all ionization charge states.
NAMES.long:
Number density of krypton impurity ions at the pedestal top is the particle count per volume for krypton ions evaluated at the core-side shoulder of an H-mode pedestal. The pedestal top is the transition where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter confined-core density variation, distinct from a separatrix or plasma-boundary value. This quantity is the krypton-specific specialization of [density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), while [ion density at the pedestal top](name:ion_density_at_pedestal_top) denotes the corresponding broader ion population.

The defining local density is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr}}(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}) = \sum_{Z=1}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{Z+}}(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}) = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Kr}}}{dV}\right|_{\xi=\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{Z+}}$ is the density for charge state $Z$, $N_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the dimensionless krypton-ion count, $V$ is physical volume in m$^3$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}$ is the radial label of the pedestal-top location. The sum includes singly ionized through fully stripped krypton and excludes neutral krypton.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Number density of nitrogen impurity ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, summed over all ionization states unless a specific charge state is named.
NAMES.long:
Number density of nitrogen impurity ions at the H-mode pedestal top is the local particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is the nitrogen-specific member of the shared [density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) concept and is distinct from the corresponding [ion density at the pedestal top](name:ion_density_at_pedestal_top).

The number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{N}}(r_p) = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{N}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the nitrogen-ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the number of nitrogen ions, $V$ is physical volume, and $r_p$ identifies the pedestal-top location.

This quantity is summed over nitrogen ionization states from singly ionized $\mathrm{N}^{+}$ through fully stripped $\mathrm{N}^{7+}$. Neutral nitrogen and any individual charge-state-resolved density are excluded.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Number density of nitrogen impurity ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating magnetically confined plasma from open-field-line scrape-off-layer plasma, summed over all ion charge states from singly ionized N+ through fully stripped N7+.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen density at the plasma boundary is the number of nitrogen impurity ions per unit volume — summed over all ion charge states from singly ionized N$^+$ through fully stripped N$^{7+}$ (atomic number $Z = 7$) — evaluated at the last closed flux surface (LCFS), which separates magnetically confined plasma from open-field-line scrape-off-layer plasma.

The charge-state-summed local number density is the zeroth velocity moment of the nitrogen-ion distribution functions at a boundary point:

$$
n_\mathrm{N}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{7} n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{7} \int f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_\mathrm{N}$ is the nitrogen impurity-ion density, $n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}$ is the density of nitrogen ions in charge state $q+$, $q$ is the charge-state index, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed flux surface, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that charge state, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This species-level boundary density excludes neutral nitrogen atoms and is charge-state-summed, not a density-weighted mean over charge states. It is a local value at the boundary, not an average over the boundary surface or over a volume; the corresponding boundary-surface average is [flux-surface-averaged nitrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary). It is the nitrogen-specific impurity-ion instance of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) and a species-resolved contribution to [ion density at the plasma boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary).

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged number density of nitrogen impurity ions at the last closed flux surface, summed over all ionization stages from N+ through fully stripped N7+.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the nitrogen impurity-ion number density on the plasma boundary, or last closed magnetic flux surface. The local density is summed over nitrogen ions from singly ionized N+ through fully stripped N7+ and excludes neutral nitrogen.

$$
\langle n_N \rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_N\,d\ell/B}{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} d\ell/B}
$$

Here $\langle n_N \rangle_{\psi_b}$ is the averaged density, $n_N$ is the local charge-state-summed nitrogen-ion density, $\psi_b$ is the poloidal-flux label of the plasma boundary, $d\ell$ is differential length along the closed poloidal contour, and $B$ is the magnetic-field magnitude. This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of [nitrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the nitrogen ion number density is counted as a particle density, independent of orientation of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: normalized_electron_collisionality_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Normalized electron collisionality at the pedestal top is the local electron-ion collision frequency divided by the trapped-electron bounce frequency, evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
Normalized electron collisionality at the pedestal top is the local electron-ion collision frequency divided by the characteristic trapped-electron bounce frequency, evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It quantifies the relative importance of collisional detrapping and trapped-electron bounce motion on the pedestal-top flux surface.

The pedestal-top value is defined by the trapped-electron neoclassical normalization:

$$
\nu^*_{e,\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{q_{\mathrm{ped}} R_{\mathrm{ped}} \, \nu_{ei,\mathrm{ped}}}{v_{\mathrm{th},e,\mathrm{ped}} \, \epsilon_{\mathrm{ped}}^{3/2}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the dimensionless safety factor of the pedestal-top flux surface, $R_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is its major radius in m measured from the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $\nu_{ei,\mathrm{ped}}$ is the local electron-ion collision frequency in s$^{-1}$, $v_{\mathrm{th},e,\mathrm{ped}} = \sqrt{2 T_e / m_e}$ is the electron thermal speed in m/s with $T_e$ the local electron temperature expressed as an energy in J and $m_e$ the electron mass in kg, and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{ped}} = r_{\mathrm{ped}} / R_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the local inverse aspect ratio, with $r_{\mathrm{ped}}$ the minor radius of the pedestal-top flux surface in m. The denominator $v_{\mathrm{th},e}\,\epsilon^{3/2}/(qR)$ is the effective trapped-electron bounce frequency, so values well below unity indicate that trapped electrons complete many banana orbits between collisions.

This name denotes the same dimensionless collision-to-bounce-frequency ratio as [electron_collisionality_at_pedestal_top](name:electron_collisionality_at_pedestal_top); the two are equivalent quantities, this entry merely carrying the normalization explicitly in its name rather than designating a physically distinct measure. It is the pedestal-top evaluation of the local quantity [electron_collisionality](name:electron_collisionality). It is not the unnormalized electron-ion collision frequency $\nu_{ei}$.

NAMES.name: normalized_poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Normalized poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top is the value of the normalized poloidal magnetic flux on the flux surface identified as the top of the H-mode edge pedestal. It is the poloidal flux difference from the magnetic axis divided by the axis-to-boundary flux difference, equal to zero at the magnetic axis and one at the plasma boundary, and equals the square of the normalized poloidal flux coordinate at that surface.
NAMES.long:
Normalized poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top is the value of the normalized poloidal magnetic flux $\psi_N$ on the flux surface identified as the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier joins the core profile. The normalized poloidal magnetic flux is a dimensionless label of equilibrium flux surfaces that is zero at the magnetic axis and one at the plasma boundary.

The value is defined by the linear flux ratio

$$
\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{\psi_{\mathrm{ped}} - \psi_0}{\psi_b - \psi_0}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top), $\psi_0$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis), and $\psi_b$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary).

This quantity is the normalized poloidal magnetic flux itself, without a square root; it is distinct from the minor-radius-like [normalized poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate) $\rho_{\mathrm{pol}}$, whose square it equals, so that $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}} = \rho_{\mathrm{pol,ped}}^2$ on the same pedestal-top surface. The corresponding coordinate value is [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). This quantity locates only the pedestal-top flux surface; it does not specify the pedestal width, the pedestal center, or an absolute poloidal magnetic flux value.

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Number density of oxygen impurity ions at the pedestal top is the local particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over O+ through fully stripped O8+.
NAMES.long:
Number density of oxygen impurity ions at the pedestal top is the local particle count per volume of oxygen ions at the core-side shoulder of an H-mode pedestal. The pedestal top is the transition where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter confined-core density variation, distinct from a separatrix or plasma-boundary value. This oxygen-specific quantity is a species-resolved specialization of [density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) and parallels [nitrogen density at the pedestal top](name:nitrogen_density_at_pedestal_top).

For the oxygen ion population on the pedestal-top surface, the defining local density is

$$
n_{\mathrm{O}}(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}) = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{O}}}{dV}\right|_{\xi=\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the dimensionless count of oxygen ions, $V$ is physical volume in m$^{3}$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}$ is the selected radial label of the pedestal-top surface.

The density is summed over oxygen ionization states from O$^{+}$ through fully stripped O$^{8+}$ and excludes neutral oxygen. It is not a charge-state-resolved density.

NAMES.name: parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Signed projection of the local electric field along the local magnetic-field direction, evaluated at the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The parallel electric field at the plasma boundary is the signed projection of the local [electric field](name:electric_field) vector onto the local magnetic-field direction at the last closed flux surface. It is a point-local boundary value, distinct from the [parallel flux-surface-averaged electric field](name:parallel_flux_surface_averaged_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary).

The defining projection is

$$
E_\parallel = \mathbf{E} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{E} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $E_\parallel$ and $\mathbf{E}$ are the parallel component and electric-field vector in V m$^{-1}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit vector. All quantities are evaluated at the same boundary location.

The plasma boundary is the separatrix or last closed flux surface; no flux-surface or regional averaging is implied.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electric field has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_particle_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed field-aligned component of the effective electron particle convection velocity representing advective electron transport along local magnetic-field lines.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the effective electron particle convection velocity projected onto the local magnetic-field direction. It represents the advective part of parallel electron particle transport and is distinct from the electron-fluid velocity and from energy convection.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{\parallel,e}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathbf{v}_{e}^{\mathrm{conv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $v_{\parallel,e}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the parallel electron particle convection velocity, $\mathbf{v}_{e}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the effective electron particle convection-velocity vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit direction.

In a particle-flux decomposition, the convective contribution is $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_e\mathbf{v}_{e}^{\mathrm{conv}}$, where $n_e$ is electron number density. It is distinct from [parallel electron velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity), which denotes the electron-fluid bulk velocity, and from [parallel electron energy convection velocity](name:parallel_electron_energy_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective electron particle convection velocity points along the local magnetic-field direction $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_flux_surface_averaged_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged field-aligned electric field at the separatrix, using the electric-field–magnetic-field contraction normalized by a signed reference toroidal field rather than a local unit-vector projection.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged field-aligned electric-field measure on the plasma boundary, or separatrix. It is distinct from the local projection of the electric field onto the magnetic-field unit vector.

It is defined by

$$
\mathcal{E}_{\parallel,\mathrm{FS}} = \left\langle \frac{\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}}{B_\phi^{\mathrm{ref}}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{sep}}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B_\phi^{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the signed reference toroidal magnetic-field component, and the brackets denote the prescribed flux-surface average over the separatrix. In the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis, the reference component is $B_\phi^{\mathrm{ref}} = \mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{ref}}\cdot\hat{\phi}$. The quantity therefore differs from the local [parallel electric field at the plasma boundary](name:parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary), which uses the local magnetic-field magnitude for projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the separatrix average of $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}/B_\phi^{\mathrm{ref}}$ is positive, with positive $B_\phi^{\mathrm{ref}}$ directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: parallel_heat_flux
NAMES.short: Signed component of the plasma heat-flux vector along the local magnetic-field direction, separating field-aligned energy transport from cross-field heat transfer.
NAMES.long:
Parallel heat flux is the signed scalar projection of the plasma heat-flux vector onto the local magnetic-field direction. It is the field-aligned component of the total [heat flux](name:heat_flux), not the magnitude of the full heat-flux vector.

The defining relation is

$$
q_\parallel = \mathbf{q} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{q} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $q_\parallel$ and $\mathbf{q}$ are heat-flux quantities measured in W.m$^{-2}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector measured in tesla, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the corresponding dimensionless unit vector. The quantity is undefined where the magnetic-field magnitude vanishes.
NAMES.sign: Positive when energy is transported in the direction of the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_heat_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Signed field-aligned convection velocity for transporting aggregate bulk-ion thermal energy in the parallel ion energy balance. It is a species-level intensive velocity, interpreted as the density-weighted mean over all ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Signed field-aligned convection velocity for transporting aggregate bulk-ion thermal energy in the parallel ion energy balance is the scalar coefficient multiplying bulk-ion thermal enthalpy density in the convective part of the parallel ion energy flux. It is defined along the local magnetic-field unit vector and describes the charge-state-aggregated bulk-ion population, not a single ion charge state.

The defining relation to the convective contribution to the parallel ion energy flux is

$$
q_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \frac{5}{2}\, n_i T_i\, v_{\parallel,\mathrm{heat}}^{i}
$$

where $q_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective contribution to the [parallel ion energy flux](name:parallel_ion_energy_flux), $n_i$ is the bulk-ion number density, $T_i$ is the bulk-ion temperature expressed as particle energy, and $v_{\parallel,\mathrm{heat}}^{i}$ is this velocity. The factor $5/2$ is the monatomic ideal-gas enthalpy convention.

This quantity is an effective heat-convection coefficient, not the total ion flow velocity, conductive heat flux, or total ion energy flux. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted mean of the corresponding charge-state-resolved ion heat-convection velocities over all ion charge states, with weights given by the charge-state number densities; the charge-state-resolved counterpart is [effective thermal ion charge-state energy velocity due to convection](name:effective_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection). It is the parallel component of [ion heat convection velocity] and is distinct from [parallel total ion energy convection velocity](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the convective contribution to the parallel ion energy flux is directed along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_species_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Effective coefficient relating neutral-species particle flux along magnetic field lines to the neutral number-density gradient in edge-plasma transport.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral-species particle diffusivity is the effective Fickian transport coefficient for particle-number diffusion along the local magnetic-field direction. It characterizes neutral particle transport, not neutral thermal-energy transport.

The parallel diffusive particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,n} = -D_{\parallel,n}\nabla_{\parallel} n_n
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,n}$ is the signed neutral particle flux density, $D_{\parallel,n}$ is the parallel diffusivity, $n_n$ is the neutral-species number density, and $\nabla_{\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\nabla$ is the derivative along the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}$. The minus sign specifies flux down the density gradient. This coefficient is the directional counterpart of the [neutral diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from the [poloidal neutral energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), which governs thermal-energy transport.

NAMES.name: parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective field-aligned convection velocity multiplying convective transport of total ion energy, with the energy summed over all ion species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective velocity associated with the convective part of the total ion-energy transport along magnetic field lines. It is a transport coefficient, not necessarily the bulk-flow velocity of any individual ion species.

The convective parallel energy flux is defined by

$$
F_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = v_{i,\parallel}^{E} E_{i,\mathrm{tot}}
$$

where $F_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the parallel convective ion-energy flux (W m$^{-2}$), $E_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion-energy density (J m$^{-3}$) summed over ion species, and $v_{i,\parallel}^{E}$ is this effective convection velocity. The quantity excludes nonconvective conductive, diffusive, and source terms. It is the field-aligned counterpart of [radial ion energy convection velocity](name:radial_ion_energy_convection_velocity) and is distinct from [parallel ion heat convection velocity](name:parallel_ion_heat_convection_velocity), which refers specifically to bulk ion thermal-energy advection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective velocity points along the magnetic-field vector, with the magnetic field represented in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: parallel_total_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.short: Effective field-aligned convection velocity multiplying convective transport of total plasma momentum in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Effective field-aligned convection velocity multiplying convective transport of total plasma momentum in the edge plasma is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the field-line-parallel convective flux of total parallel momentum density to that total parallel momentum density. It is defined for the total plasma momentum variable summed over the plasma species and charge states included in the total-momentum balance, and it is not necessarily the parallel bulk velocity of any single species.

The constitutive definition of the coefficient is:

$$
v_{\parallel,\mathrm{conv}} = \frac{\Gamma_{P_\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}}{P_\parallel}
$$

where $\Gamma_{P_\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-line-parallel convective flux of total parallel momentum density, $P_\parallel$ is the total parallel momentum density, and $v_{\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ is this convection velocity. The density $P_\parallel$ may be written inline as $P_\parallel = \sum_a m_a n_a u_{a,\parallel}$, where $a$ indexes the included plasma species or charge states, $m_a$ is particle mass, $n_a$ is number density, and $u_{a,\parallel}$ is field-line-parallel velocity.

This quantity is an effective coefficient for the transported total momentum variable: it equals a center-of-mass parallel flow only when the closure uses that same flow to advect the summed momentum. Related effective-velocity coefficients for different transported variables include [parallel total ion energy convection velocity](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity), [parallel ion charge state convection velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity), and [parallel neutral internal state momentum convection velocity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity); the cross-field counterpart for total momentum transport is [radial effective momentum convection velocity].
NAMES.sign: Positive when the velocity is directed along the local magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: particle_diffusivity
NAMES.short: Effective particle diffusivity of a generic particle population, whose directional components relate the diffusive particle flux to the local number-density gradient along flux-coordinate directions.
NAMES.long:
Particle diffusivity is the transport coefficient quantifying how readily particles spread in response to number-density gradients in a magnetized plasma. In the anisotropic geometry of a toroidal device, the diffusivity is resolved into components along the flux-coordinate directions $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ is a radial flux-surface label, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

The component diffusivity $D_i$ along coordinate direction $x^i$ enters the diffusive particle flux via:

$$
\Gamma_i = -D_i \, g^{ii} \frac{\partial n}{\partial x^i}
$$

where $\Gamma_i$ is the local particle flux along $x^i$, $g^{ii}$ is the contravariant metric element for that direction, and $n$ is the number density.

These coefficients are inferred in edge transport modeling by fitting experimental profiles — measured by Thomson scattering, reflectometry, or interferometry — against solutions of the particle continuity equation with the diffusive flux parametrized as above. Effective particle diffusivities in the tokamak edge span roughly 0.1–10 m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, with anomalous turbulence-driven values dominating over neoclassical estimates in most regimes. The [poloidal_particle_diffusivity](name:poloidal_particle_diffusivity) is the primary attested directional component, resolved along $\hat{\theta}$; related transport coefficients include [neutral_diffusivity](name:neutral_diffusivity) for neutral particle transport and [ion_charge_state_diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity) for charge-state-resolved ion populations.

NAMES.name: poloidal_flux_surface_averaged_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Poloidal flux-surface-averaged electron beta at the pedestal top is the dimensionless ratio of flux-surface-averaged electron kinetic pressure to the magnetic pressure associated with the flux-surface-averaged poloidal magnetic field, evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal flux-surface-averaged electron beta at the pedestal top is the electron contribution to poloidal beta on the flux surface at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It compares the flux-surface-averaged electron kinetic pressure with the magnetic pressure formed from the flux-surface-averaged magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field on the same surface.

The defining relation is:

$$
\beta_{p,e}^{\mathrm{fs}}(\psi_{\mathrm{top}}) = \frac{2\mu_0\,\langle p_e\rangle_{\psi_{\mathrm{top}}}}{\left(\langle |B_p|\rangle_{\psi_{\mathrm{top}}}\right)^2}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{top}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux coordinate labeling the pedestal-top flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi_{\mathrm{top}}}$ denotes a flux-surface average on that surface using the normalized measure $dS/|\nabla\psi|$, $p_e$ is the electron kinetic pressure in pascals, $|B_p|$ is the magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field in tesla, and $\mu_0$ is the magnetic permeability of free space in henries per meter. The denominator uses the square of the averaged field magnitude, not the flux-surface average of $B_p^2$.

The pressure term is the pedestal-top electron kinetic pressure represented by [electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top](name:electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top), with averaging over the same pedestal-top flux surface. Ion pressure and total thermal pressure contributions are excluded. The flux-surface-averaged denominator distinguishes this quantity from [poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side) and [poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side), which use local poloidal-field values at specified poloidal locations, and from [poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side), which does not specify flux-surface averaging of the poloidal field.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Diffusion coefficient for total-ion particle transport along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates, relating poloidal particle flux to the metric-scaled gradient of total ion density.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion diffusivity quantifies gradient-driven (Fickian) transport of the total ion population along the poloidal direction. It is the poloidal component of [ion diffusivity](name:ion_diffusivity), expressed as an effective scalar in flux coordinates rather than the field-aligned transport described by [parallel ion diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_diffusivity).

The down-gradient poloidal ion particle flux obeys:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\theta i}\frac{1}{h_\theta}\frac{\partial n_i}{\partial\theta}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal particle flux in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, $D_{\theta i}$ is the poloidal ion diffusivity in m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, $n_i$ is total ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and $h_\theta$ is the poloidal metric scale factor in m.

The flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ use $\rho$ as a radial flux label, $\theta$ as poloidal angle, and $\phi$ as toroidal angle. This coefficient applies to total ion particle transport, not species- or charge-state-resolved transport or thermal-energy transport such as [poloidal ion energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top is the signed value of the poloidal magnetic flux function on the H-mode pedestal-top flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top is the signed value of the poloidal magnetic flux function on the H-mode pedestal-top flux surface. The pedestal top is the core-side top of the steep edge pedestal and may be identified by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the value can be represented as the flux through a horizontal disk bounded by a point on that flux surface:

$$
\psi_\mathrm{ped} = \int_0^{R_\mathrm{ped}} B_Z(R', Z_\mathrm{ped})\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $\psi_\mathrm{ped}$ denotes this quantity, $(R_\mathrm{ped}, Z_\mathrm{ped})$ is any point on the pedestal-top flux surface with $R_\mathrm{ped}$ and $Z_\mathrm{ped}$ in meters, $R'$ is the disk-integration radius in meters, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component in tesla. The integral fixes the additive reference to the zero-radius disk on the toroidal symmetry axis; only differences in $\psi$ are invariant under an added constant.

This dimensional flux value is related to [normalized poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top](name:normalized_poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top) through the normalization $(\psi_\mathrm{ped}-\psi_0)/(\psi_b-\psi_0)$, where $\psi_0$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis) and $\psi_b$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary). It is not a radius-like coordinate such as [toroidal flux radius at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_flux_radius_at_pedestal_top), and it is distinct from values at the pedestal center or maximum-gradient surface unless those loci are defined to coincide with the pedestal top.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $B_Z$ on the horizontal integration disk points in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: poloidal_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.short: Effective coefficient relating particle transport to number-density gradients along the poloidal direction of flux coordinates.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for particle spreading driven by a number-density gradient along the poloidal direction of the flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is the poloidal component of the generic [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity) quantity.

For physical poloidal arclength, the diffusive particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{pol}} = -D_{\mathrm{pol}}\frac{1}{h_\theta}\frac{\partial n}{\partial \theta}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the particle flux, $D_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal diffusivity, $n$ is particle number density, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $h_\theta = \left|\partial\mathbf{r}/\partial\theta\right|$ is the metric scale factor converting poloidal-angle displacement to physical arclength. The derivative is taken at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$.

This generic quantity is distinct from species-specific [poloidal ion diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_diffusivity) and [poloidal electron diffusivity](name:poloidal_electron_diffusivity); it does not by itself select a particle species or charge state.

NAMES.name: power_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short: Total power of a specified physical process integrated over the scrape-off layer, the open-field-line plasma region between the separatrix and the material boundaries.
NAMES.long: Power over the scrape-off layer quantifies the total power contributed by a specified physical process or channel, integrated over the plasma volume occupying open magnetic field lines between the last closed flux surface (separatrix) and the plasma-facing components. This parent concept generalizes over process-specific realizations: the accepted child [radiated_power_over_scrape_off_layer](name:radiated_power_over_scrape_off_layer) gives the total electromagnetic radiation emitted by all plasma species and emission channels within that region. The upstream power boundary condition — total power crossing the separatrix from the confined plasma into the SOL — is given by [total_lost_power_over_scrape_off_layer](name:total_lost_power_over_scrape_off_layer), which is distinct from the process-attributed power described here.

NAMES.name: pressure_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Kinetic plasma pressure evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier for a specified population or defined aggregate.
NAMES.long:
Pedestal-top pressure is the kinetic pressure of a specified plasma population or defined aggregate, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. Its location is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), and its value represents the fitted pedestal-height amplitude.

For an isotropic kinetic population, pressure is related to its density and temperature by:

$$
p_{\mathrm{ped}} = n_{\mathrm{ped}} k_B T_{\mathrm{ped}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the pedestal-top kinetic pressure, $n_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the corresponding [number density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), $T_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the corresponding [average temperature at the pedestal top](name:average_temperature_at_pedestal_top), and $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant.

A population-specific value is a partial pressure; an aggregate value is the sum of the included partial pressures. The [electron pressure at the pedestal top](name:electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top) is a concrete population-specific instance. This quantity is distinct from a pressure gradient, a maximum-steepness derivative, or a volume-averaged scrape-off-layer pressure.

NAMES.name: electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron pressure at the pedestal top is the electron kinetic pressure pedestal-height amplitude at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is the electron partial-pressure contribution, distinct from total plasma pressure at the pedestal top.
NAMES.long:
Electron pressure at the pedestal top is the electron kinetic pressure pedestal-height amplitude at the fitted core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. The quantity represents the electron partial-pressure component assigned to that fitted top.

For scalar electron kinetic pressure, the defining relation to the corresponding pedestal-top electron density and electron temperature is:

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{ped}} = n_{e,\mathrm{ped}}\, e\, T_{e,\mathrm{ped}}
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{ped}}$ is this quantity, the subscript $\mathrm{ped}$ denotes the pedestal top, $n_{e,\mathrm{ped}}$ is [electron_density_at_pedestal_top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top), $T_{e,\mathrm{ped}}$ is [electron_temperature_at_pedestal_top](name:electron_temperature_at_pedestal_top) expressed in electronvolts, and $e$ is the elementary-charge conversion factor satisfying $1\,\mathrm{eV}=e\,\mathrm{J}$.

This quantity is distinct from [pressure_at_pedestal_top](name:pressure_at_pedestal_top), which includes electron and ion pressure components at the same fitted pedestal top. It also excludes separate pedestal-location, width, baseline, and gradient quantities, which characterize the position or shape of the edge transport barrier rather than the electron pressure height.

NAMES.name: derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed local derivative of fitted electron pressure with respect to the normalized poloidal flux coordinate at the H-mode pedestal top. It describes the core-side pedestal-top variation of the fitted electron-pressure function, not the pressure value or a maximum over a pedestal interval.
NAMES.long:
Signed local derivative of fitted electron pressure with respect to the normalized poloidal flux coordinate at the H-mode pedestal top is the local rate of change of the fitted electron-pressure function with the flux coordinate $\psi_N$ at the pedestal-top locus. It is not the derivative of the scalar [electron pressure at the H-mode pedestal top](name:electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top); that scalar is the pressure value at the same locus.

The derivative is defined by differentiating the fitted electron-pressure function with respect to $\psi_N$ and evaluating the result at the pedestal top:

$$
D_{p_e,\mathrm{ped\ top}} = \left.\frac{\partial p_e}{\partial \psi_N}\right|_{\mathrm{ped\ top}}
$$

where $D_{p_e,\mathrm{ped\ top}}$ is this quantity, $p_e$ is [electron pressure](name:electron_pressure), and $\psi_N$ is the normalized poloidal flux coordinate, with $\psi_N=0$ at the magnetic axis and $\psi_N=1$ at the plasma boundary.

This quantity is a local pedestal-top derivative. It excludes the steepest pressure-gradient value over a pedestal interval, represented by [gradient of electron pressure](name:gradient_of_electron_pressure), and it is distinct from electron-density derivatives such as [derivative with respect to normalized poloidal flux coordinate of electron density at pedestal maximum](name:derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum).
NAMES.sign: Positive when electron pressure increases with increasing normalized poloidal flux coordinate $\psi_N$ from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: pressure_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Pressure at the plasma boundary is the isotropic kinetic pressure of a specified plasma constituent or population evaluated on the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer. It represents scalar momentum flux from random particle motion at that boundary.
NAMES.long:
Pressure at the plasma boundary is the isotropic kinetic pressure of a specified plasma constituent or population evaluated on the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating closed magnetic flux surfaces from the scrape-off layer. It is the scalar part of the kinetic pressure tensor at that locus and represents momentum flux from random particle motion, not magnetic pressure or directed-flow dynamic pressure.

The scalar boundary pressure for population $a$ is defined from its kinetic pressure tensor evaluated at the boundary as:

$$
p_{a,\mathrm{b}} = \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\!\left(\mathbf{P}_a\right)_{\mathrm{b}}
$$

where $p_{a,\mathrm{b}}$ is the boundary pressure of population $a$, $\mathbf{P}_a$ is its kinetic pressure tensor, and subscript $\mathrm{b}$ denotes evaluation on the plasma boundary. For an isotropic Maxwellian population, this is equivalent to $p_{a,\mathrm{b}} = n_{a,\mathrm{b}} k_\mathrm{B} T_{a,\mathrm{b}}$, where $n_{a,\mathrm{b}}$ is the boundary number density of that population, $T_{a,\mathrm{b}}$ is its boundary thermodynamic temperature, and $k_\mathrm{B}$ is the Boltzmann constant.

The constituent or population may be electrons, ions, neutrals, or an explicitly defined subset; [electron pressure at the plasma boundary](name:electron_pressure_at_plasma_boundary) is the electron-specific instance. For a species-level constituent that contains multiple charge states, this pressure is summed over charge states because pressure tensors from distinct particle populations add.

NAMES.name: electron_pressure_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Isotropic momentum-flux density of random electron motion evaluated on the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Electron thermal pressure at the plasma boundary is the isotropic momentum-flux density produced by random electron motion on the last closed magnetic flux surface. It is the electron-specific contribution to [thermal pressure at the plasma boundary](name:pressure_at_plasma_boundary), not the total plasma pressure.

For an isotropic electron population, the pressure is defined by

$$
p_e = \frac{2}{3} n_e \langle E_e \rangle
$$

where $p_e$ is electron thermal pressure, $n_e$ is electron number density, and $\langle E_e \rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron. The quantity is related to [electron temperature at the plasma boundary](name:electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary) through $p_e = n_e T_e$ when $T_e$ is expressed as thermal energy per particle.

The definition excludes directed electron bulk-flow momentum and nonthermal stress contributions; the plasma boundary denotes the separatrix between closed and open magnetic field lines.

NAMES.name: pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short: Thermal pressure of a plasma constituent or neutral-gas population in the open-field-line scrape-off layer, the region between the last closed flux surface and the material plasma-facing components.
NAMES.long:
The scrape-off layer (SOL) is the open-field-line region extending from the last closed flux surface to the material plasma-facing components, where local pressure governs energy and particle exhaust, neutral recycling, ionization balance, and the onset of divertor detachment. This parent name generalizes over species-resolved SOL pressure quantities: [electron pressure over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) represents the electron partial pressure and additionally anchors the pressure baseline offset in H-mode pedestal profile fits, while [neutral pressure over the scrape-off layer](name:neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) characterizes the neutral gas inventory affecting recycling, pumping balance, and detachment control.

For any thermally equilibrated species $s$, the scalar thermal pressure satisfies:

$$
p_s = n_s k_B T_s
$$

where $n_s$ is the species number density and $T_s$ is its temperature in energy units.

SOL pressure is inferred from a combination of diagnostics: Langmuir probes provide local electron pressure at plasma-facing surfaces from saturation current and electron temperature; neutral gas pressure gages directly measure gas pressure in the divertor pumping region; Thomson scattering resolves electron density and temperature profiles from which electron pressure is derived. The characteristic radial scale over which pressure falls from the separatrix outward is described by the [decay length over the scrape-off layer](name:decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

NAMES.name: electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged thermal pressure of electrons in the scrape-off layer, the open-field-line region between the last closed flux surface and material plasma-facing components.
NAMES.long:
Electron pressure over the scrape-off layer is the volume-averaged thermal pressure of electrons in the open-field-line region between the last closed flux surface and the material plasma-facing components. It represents the electron partial-pressure contribution to [pressure over the scrape-off layer](name:pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) over that volume.

The volume average is defined from the local electron thermal pressure over the scrape-off-layer volume:

$$
\langle p_e \rangle_{\mathrm{SOL}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} n_e(\mathbf{x}) T_e(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $\langle p_e \rangle_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the volume-averaged electron pressure over the scrape-off layer, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron number density, $T_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron temperature expressed as thermal energy per electron, $V_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the scrape-off-layer volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\mathbf{x}$ is position.

This quantity excludes ion partial pressures and the neutral-gas pressure described by [neutral pressure over the scrape-off layer](name:neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer). It is a SOL volume average, not the [electron pressure at the plasma boundary](name:electron_pressure_at_plasma_boundary), and it is related to [electron density over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_density_over_scrape_off_layer) through the same averaging domain but is a density-temperature moment rather than a number-density average.

NAMES.name: neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged thermal pressure of neutral atoms and molecules in the scrape-off layer, the open-field-line region between the last closed flux surface and material plasma-facing components.
NAMES.long:
Neutral pressure over the scrape-off layer is the volume-averaged thermal pressure of neutral atoms and molecules in the open-field-line region between the last closed flux surface and the material plasma-facing components. It represents the neutral-gas contribution to the SOL pressure, distinct from the electron partial pressure described by [electron pressure over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer), and is a component of [pressure over the scrape-off layer](name:pressure_over_scrape_off_layer).

The defining volume average is

$$
\overline{p}_{\mathrm{n,SOL}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} \int_{\mathrm{SOL}} p_{\mathrm{n}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V, \qquad p_{\mathrm{n}}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_s n_s(\mathbf{r}) k_B T_s(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the scrape-off-layer volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $p_{\mathrm{n}}$ is local neutral pressure, $s$ indexes neutral atomic and molecular species, $n_s$ is their number density, $T_s$ is their thermodynamic temperature, and $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant.

The quantity excludes charged-particle pressure and represents an average over the entire scrape-off-layer domain rather than a pressure evaluated at a particular location.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_particle_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective Fickian coefficient for cross-field radial transport of the total charged-ion population, relating its diffusive particle flux to the negative radial gradient of ion density.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion particle diffusivity is the effective Fickian coefficient for cross-field transport of the total charged-ion population across neighboring magnetic flux surfaces. It describes diffusive particle transport, excluding convective, energy, and momentum transport.

The defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,r}^{\mathrm{part}}\frac{\partial n_i}{\partial r}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive ion particle flux, $D_{i,r}^{\mathrm{part}}$ is this diffusivity, $n_i$ is the total charged-ion number density, and $r$ is a radial coordinate increasing away from the magnetic axis.

The density $n_i$ is summed over charged ion species and all charge states without charge, mass, or atomic-number weighting. This total-population quantity is related to [radial ion diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from [radial ion charge-state diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity), which applies to one specified charge state.

NAMES.name: radiated_power_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.short: Total electromagnetic power radiated from the open field-line scrape-off layer plasma by all species and emission channels combined.
NAMES.long:
The radiated power over the scrape-off layer is the total electromagnetic power emitted by plasma occupying the open field-line region between the magnetic separatrix and the first wall or divertor structures. Contributions arise from line radiation of impurity ions (both intrinsic and deliberately seeded species such as argon or neon), hydrogen isotope resonance emission, bremsstrahlung, and radiative recombination, integrated over the full SOL volume.

The total SOL radiated power is the volume integral of the local emissivity:

$$
P_\mathrm{rad,SOL} = \int_\mathrm{SOL} \varepsilon_\mathrm{rad}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $\varepsilon_\mathrm{rad} = n_e \sum_z n_z L_z(T_e, n_e)$, with $n_e$ the electron number density, $n_z$ the density of radiating species $z$, and $L_z$ the temperature- and density-dependent cooling function for species $z$.

It is measured via resistive or photodiode bolometer arrays, with the spatial distribution recovered by tomographic inversion. Alternatively, it is inferred from global power balance by subtracting the conducted and convected power reaching the divertor targets from the total power crossing the separatrix given by total_lost_power_at_plasma_boundary.

A high SOL radiated power fraction $f_\mathrm{rad} = P_\mathrm{rad,SOL} / P_\mathrm{SOL}$ is the primary control target in reactor-relevant divertor detachment scenarios, as it disperses the power load before it reaches solid surfaces. The residual non-radiated heat governs the radial heat-flux profiles characterized by the [electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer](name:electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer) and [ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer](name:ion_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). This quantity is the radiated sub-component of power_over_scrape_off_layer.

NAMES.name: temperature_at_midplane
NAMES.short: Local kinetic temperature of a plasma population at the outboard, low-field-side midplane in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Local kinetic temperature of a plasma population at the outboard, low-field-side midplane is the scalar kinetic temperature of the specified population evaluated locally at the upstream low-field-side equatorial crossing of the scrape-off-layer plasma. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, this locus is on the larger-$R$ side of the magnetic midplane.

For a plasma population $a$ described by a scalar pressure relation, the temperature $T_a$ is defined through the local pressure-density relation:

$$
p_a = e\, n_a\, T_a
$$

where $p_a$ is the scalar pressure of population $a$, $n_a$ is its number density, $T_a$ is its temperature measured in electronvolts, and $e$ is the elementary charge that converts electronvolts to energy.

This population-generic quantity does not by itself specify electrons, ions, impurities, charge state, or a species-combined temperature. More specific quantities select the population, such as [electron_temperature_at_midplane](name:electron_temperature_at_midplane) and [ion_temperature_at_midplane](name:ion_temperature_at_midplane). It is a pointwise local temperature, not a flux-surface average, poloidal average, or field-line average; the related local temperature at a limiter contact locus is [temperature_at_limiter](name:temperature_at_limiter). When the specified population is a species spanning multiple charge states, the species temperature is the density-weighted mean over all charge states.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_midplane
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Local kinetic temperature of the electron population at the outboard, low-field-side midplane in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Local kinetic temperature of the electron population at the outboard, low-field-side midplane is the thermal spread of the electron velocity distribution evaluated at the outboard, low-field-side crossing of the scrape-off-layer plasma. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height, this locus is the larger-$R$ intersection of the scrape-off layer with the magnetic midplane on the low-field side of the magnetic axis.

For electrons described by a scalar pressure relation, the electron temperature $T_e$ at this locus is defined through the local pressure-density relation:

$$
p_e = e\, n_e\, T_e
$$

where $p_e$ is the scalar electron pressure, $n_e$ is the electron number density, $T_e$ is the electron temperature measured in electronvolts, and $e$ is the elementary charge that converts electronvolts to energy.

This quantity specializes [temperature_at_midplane](name:temperature_at_midplane) for the electron population. It is a pointwise local electron temperature, not a flux-surface average, poloidal average, midplane average, or field-line average such as [electron_average_temperature_at_midplane](name:electron_average_temperature_at_midplane). The corresponding ion quantity is [ion_temperature_at_midplane](name:ion_temperature_at_midplane).

NAMES.name: ion_temperature_at_midplane
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local kinetic temperature of the ion population at the outboard, low-field-side midplane in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
Local kinetic temperature of the ion population at the outboard, low-field-side midplane is the scalar kinetic temperature of the specified ion population evaluated locally at the upstream low-field-side equatorial crossing of the scrape-off-layer plasma. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, this locus is on the larger-$R$ side of the magnetic midplane.

For an ion population $i$ described by a scalar pressure relation, its temperature $T_i$ is defined through the local pressure-density relation:

$$
p_i = e\, n_i\, T_i
$$

where $p_i$ is the scalar ion pressure, $n_i$ is the ion number density, $T_i$ is the temperature measured in electronvolts, and $e$ is the elementary charge that converts electronvolts to energy.

This ion-specific quantity is a member of the population-generic [temperature_at_midplane](name:temperature_at_midplane) family and is distinct from [electron_temperature_at_midplane](name:electron_temperature_at_midplane). It is a pointwise local temperature, not a flux-surface, poloidal, or field-line average; [temperature_at_limiter](name:temperature_at_limiter) applies at a different locus. For an ion species spanning multiple charge states, the temperature is the density-weighted mean over all charge states.

NAMES.name: temperature_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Temperature-valued quantity associated with the core-side shoulder of an H-mode edge transport barrier, covering population kinetic temperatures, density-weighted averages, and stability thresholds.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is a temperature associated with the pedestal top, defined as the core-side shoulder of an H-mode edge transport barrier. Its instance-specific interpretation may be a plasma population's kinetic temperature, a density-weighted population average, or a critical threshold for pedestal stability.

For population-temperature instances, an isotropic kinetic temperature satisfies

$$
\frac{3}{2} k_B T = \langle E_{\mathrm{kin}} \rangle
$$

where $T$ is the population temperature, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, and $\langle E_{\mathrm{kin}} \rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per particle. The [electron temperature at the pedestal top](name:electron_temperature_at_pedestal_top) and [average temperature at the pedestal top](name:average_temperature_at_pedestal_top) are population-temperature instances. The [critical temperature at the pedestal top](name:critical_temperature_at_pedestal_top) instead denotes the threshold for marginal ideal magnetohydrodynamic peeling-ballooning stability and is distinct from a measured or fitted population temperature.

NAMES.name: average_temperature_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Average temperature at the pedestal top is the density-weighted kinetic temperature of a specified plasma population at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pedestal.
NAMES.long:
Average temperature at the pedestal top is the density-weighted kinetic temperature of a specified plasma population evaluated at the top, or height, of the H-mode pedestal transport barrier. It is a population-averaged specialization of [temperature at the pedestal top](name:temperature_at_pedestal_top).

The pedestal top is the fitted transition location where the steep edge temperature gradient relaxes toward the flatter confined-core region, rather than the physical plasma boundary or a particular outboard point.

Using the normalized poloidal flux coordinate $\psi_N$, the average temperature is defined by

$$
T_{\mathrm{avg,ped}} = \frac{\sum_{a \in \mathcal{P}} n_a(\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}) T_a(\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}})}{\sum_{a \in \mathcal{P}} n_a(\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}})}
$$

where $\mathcal{P}$ is the specified set of species and charge-state components, $n_a$ is the number density of component $a$, $T_a$ is its kinetic temperature, and $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}$ is the fitted pedestal-top coordinate. For example, [ion average temperature at the pedestal top](name:ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top) includes all ion species and charge states in $\mathcal{P}$.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron temperature at the pedestal top is the kinetic temperature of the electron population at the core-side shoulder of an H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
Electron temperature at the pedestal top is the kinetic temperature of the electron population evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is the electron-specific instance of [temperature at the pedestal top](name:temperature_at_pedestal_top).

For an isotropic electron population, the kinetic temperature is defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_{\mathrm{kin},e}\rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature and $\langle E_{\mathrm{kin},e}\rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron.

This population-specific thermal quantity is distinct from the density-weighted [average temperature at the pedestal top](name:average_temperature_at_pedestal_top) and from the stability threshold represented by the [electron critical temperature at the pedestal top](name:electron_critical_temperature_at_pedestal_top). Its thermodynamic relationship to [electron pressure at the pedestal top](name:electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top) follows the electron equation of state.

NAMES.name: derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_temperature_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed core-side slope of the electron temperature versus normalized poloidal flux at the H-mode pedestal top.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed local slope of the electron temperature at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It represents the derivative extracted from the modified hyperbolic-tangent characterization of the pedestal and complements the value [electron temperature at the pedestal top](name:electron_temperature_at_pedestal_top).

The derivative is defined as

$$
\left.\frac{\mathrm{d}T_e}{\mathrm{d}\psi_N}\right|_{\mathrm{pedestal\ top}}
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature, $\psi_N$ is the normalized poloidal flux coordinate, and the subscript denotes evaluation at the pedestal top.

This is the signed local slope at the pedestal top, not the maximum absolute gradient over the pedestal. Its sign is retained rather than replaced by a magnitude.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron temperature increases toward increasing normalized poloidal flux, from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Density-weighted kinetic temperature of all ion species and charge states evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pedestal.
NAMES.long:
Ion average temperature at the pedestal top is the density-weighted kinetic temperature of the combined ion population at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pedestal. It is the ion-specific component of [average temperature at the pedestal top](name:average_temperature_at_pedestal_top).

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_s n_s T_s}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $T_{i,\mathrm{avg}}$ is the ion average temperature, $n_s$ is the number density of ion species or charge state $s$, and $T_s$ is its kinetic temperature. The sum includes all ion species and charge states in the defined ion population; it is not an electron temperature or a temperature for a single ion species. The weighting denominator is the total ion density represented by [total ion density at the pedestal top](name:total_ion_density_at_pedestal_top).
