NAMES.name: temperature_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Temperature at the plasma boundary is the kinetic temperature of a specified plasma particle population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface or separatrix. It generalizes species-specific boundary temperatures, such as the electron boundary temperature, without changing the boundary locus.
NAMES.long:
Temperature at the plasma boundary is the kinetic temperature of a specified plasma particle population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface or separatrix. It characterizes the random, thermal part of particle motion at that boundary and does not change the boundary locus when the particle population changes.

For a nonrelativistic population with mean flow removed, the scalar boundary temperature is defined by the trace of the random kinetic energy per particle:

$$
T_{a,\mathrm{bdry}} = \frac{1}{3} m_a \left\langle \left|\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_a\right|^2 \right\rangle_{\mathrm{bdry}}
$$

where $a$ denotes the specified particle population, $m_a$ is the particle mass of that population, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_a$ is the mean flow velocity of that population, and $\langle \cdot \rangle_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ is the particle average over population $a$ at the plasma boundary.

This parent generalizes over particle population while retaining the plasma-boundary locus. The electron specialization is [electron temperature at the plasma boundary](name:electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary); quantities at other named locations are distinct from this boundary value. If the specified population is a species aggregated over charge states, this intensive quantity is the density-weighted mean over the included charge states.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Thermal energy of the bulk electron population at the plasma boundary expressed as a kinetic temperature, equal to two-thirds of the mean random electron kinetic energy per particle. The boundary value is evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface or separatrix.
NAMES.long:
Thermal energy of the bulk electron population at the plasma boundary expressed as a kinetic temperature, equal to two-thirds of the mean random electron kinetic energy per particle, is the scalar electron temperature evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. In a diverted plasma the boundary is the separatrix; in a limiter plasma it is the limiting last closed flux surface. The boundary surface is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For an isotropic scalar-temperature electron distribution at that boundary, the defining thermal-energy relation is:

$$
\left\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}}\right\rangle_b = \frac{3}{2}\,k_B T_{K,b} = \frac{3}{2}\,e\,T_{e,b}
$$

where $\left\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}}\right\rangle_b$ is the mean random kinetic energy per bulk electron at the boundary, subscript $b$ denotes boundary evaluation, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, $T_{K,b}$ is the thermodynamic electron temperature in kelvin, $T_{e,b}$ is this boundary electron temperature in electronvolts, and $e$ is the elementary-charge magnitude converting electronvolts to joules.

This quantity is the electron-species member of [temperature_at_plasma_boundary](name:temperature_at_plasma_boundary) and refines [electron_temperature](name:electron_temperature) by locus. It denotes the local confined-plasma-side boundary value and is not a flux-surface average; the corresponding averaged quantity is [flux_surface_averaged_electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary). With [electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), it gives the scalar isotropic boundary electron-pressure relation $p_{e,b}=n_{e,b} e T_{e,b}$ when such a pressure is defined. As a scalar kinetic temperature of the thermal bulk population, it is non-negative and excludes separately represented nonthermal electron components.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-weighted mean of the bulk electron kinetic temperature on the last closed magnetic flux surface, with poloidal and toroidal variation averaged out.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the bulk electron temperature on the plasma boundary, represented by the last closed magnetic flux surface. It retains the boundary-surface locus while removing variation along that surface.

$$
\langle T_e\rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} T_e\,\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} \frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

Here, $T_e$ is the local electron temperature, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux surface label, $\psi_b$ is its value at the plasma boundary, $dS$ is the surface-area element, and $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of the flux-label gradient. This averaged quantity is distinct from the pointwise boundary value [electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_temperature_at_plasma_boundary) and from the volume average [volume_averaged_electron_temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature).

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Positive outward e-folding distance of the thermal electron temperature in the scrape-off layer, distinct from electron-density and heat-flux decay lengths.
NAMES.long:
The thermal electron temperature decay length is the positive e-folding distance associated with the outward decrease of electron temperature in the scrape-off layer. It characterizes temperature falloff rather than electron-density or heat-flux falloff.

It is defined from the outward logarithmic temperature gradient as

$$
\lambda_{T_e} = \left|\frac{d\ln T_e}{d r_\perp}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $\lambda_{T_e}$ is the temperature decay length, $T_e$ is the thermal electron temperature, and $r_\perp$ is outward distance across the scrape-off layer.

This quantity is distinct from the [electron decay length over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), which applies the same scale-length definition to electron number density, and from the [electron heat decay length over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), which applies it to electron heat flux.

NAMES.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Toroidal argon velocity at the pedestal top is the φ component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the density-weighted mean bulk flow of argon impurity ions where the H-mode pedestal transitions to the confined core.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal argon velocity at the pedestal top is the $\phi$ component, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of the density-weighted mean bulk flow of argon impurity ions where the H-mode pedestal transitions to the confined core. As an intensive species-level quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all argon charge states, not a charge-state-summed velocity.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by the density-weighted mean at the pedestal top:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}^{\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes argon ionization state, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the local number density of that charge state, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is its toroidal velocity component at the pedestal top.

It is inferred primarily from Doppler spectroscopy of argon emission, often charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy when suitable neutral-beam excitation is available. The observed line shift and viewing geometry determine the velocity projected onto the $\hat{\phi}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; estimating the all-charge-state mean may require emissivity modeling, ionization-balance information, or collisional equilibration assumptions.

Because pedestal argon rotation is sensitive to external torque, radial electric-field shear, neoclassical friction, turbulence-driven momentum transport, and charge-state distribution, no device-independent numerical range is implied. This value is commonly interpreted with same-species values at other loci, including [toroidal argon velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), [toroidal argon velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), [toroidal argon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and [toroidal flux-surface-averaged argon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted mean argon flow points in the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Toroidal component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame of the argon-ion bulk-flow velocity at the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of the argon-ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed flux surface. It is a pointwise boundary value rather than an average over that flux surface.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal velocity is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{Ar},\phi} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z} v_{\mathrm{Ar},z,\phi}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{Ar},\phi}$ and $v_{\mathrm{Ar},z,\phi}$ are toroidal velocity components in m s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$ is the argon-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, and $z$ indexes argon ion charge states. The toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The local value is distinct from the [toroidal flux-surface-averaged argon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which averages the same component over the boundary flux surface. Neutral argon is excluded from the ion bulk-flow aggregation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the argon-ion bulk velocity projects onto the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of beryllium ions at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, density-weighted over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the beryllium impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, conventionally called the pedestal top.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{Be},\phi} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be},z} v_{\mathrm{Be},z,\phi}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be},z}}
$$

where $z$ indexes the included beryllium ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Be},z}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\mathrm{Be},z,\phi}$ is the charge-state-resolved toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The result is a density-weighted intensive mean, not a sum of charge-state velocities; the corresponding elemental concentration is represented by [beryllium density at the pedestal top](name:beryllium_density_at_pedestal_top). It is evaluated at the pedestal top rather than at the magnetic axis, as in [toroidal beryllium velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the beryllium bulk flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The carbon impurity-ion fluid velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the density-weighted bulk-flow velocity of all contributing carbon ion charge states, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is the toroidal component rather than the total three-dimensional speed, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

$$
v_{\phi,C}=\frac{\sum_q n_{C^{q+}}v_{\phi,C^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{C^{q+}}}
$$

Here, $q$ indexes the contributing carbon ion charge states, $n_{C^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,C^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. Neutral carbon is excluded because this quantity is defined for impurity ions. The pedestal-top value is distinct from the [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the carbon-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the last closed magnetic flux surface, resolved along increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The carbon impurity-ion toroidal velocity at the plasma boundary is the local density-weighted mean of the bulk-flow velocities of all included carbon ion charge states on the last closed magnetic flux surface. It is not a flux-surface average; that distinct quantity is the [toroidal flux-surface-averaged carbon velocity](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), while the magnetic-axis counterpart is [toroidal carbon velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

The defining local component is

$$
V_{\phi,C}(R,Z)=\frac{\sum_{q\in Q} n_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)\,\mathbf{V}_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_{q\in Q} n_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)}
$$

where $Q$ is the set of included carbon ion charge states, $n_{C^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf{V}_{C^{q+}}$ is its bulk velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The component is resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the carbon-ion bulk flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the bulk flow velocity assigned to the effective deuterium–tritium fuel species at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge pedestal.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the bulk-flow velocity of deuterium and tritium treated as one effective fuel species, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is distinct from the velocity of deuterium alone, such as [toroidal deuterium velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

The effective toroidal velocity is the mass-density-weighted mean of the isotope flow components:

$$
v_{\mathrm{DT},\phi} = \frac{m_D n_D v_{D,\phi} + m_T n_T v_{T,\phi}}{m_D n_D + m_T n_T}
$$

where $m_D$ and $m_T$ are the deuterium and tritium masses in kg, $n_D$ and $n_T$ are their number densities in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{D,\phi}$ and $v_{T,\phi}$ are their toroidal velocity components in m.s$^{-1}$. The effective species uses the deuterium–tritium fuel convention with mean atomic mass 2.5; this local quantity is not a flux-surface average or a value at the plasma boundary, such as [toroidal deuterium–tritium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the bulk flow velocity of the fictitious deuterium-tritium single-species (atomic mass 2.5 amu), evaluated at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The toroidal deuterium-tritium velocity at the plasma boundary is the $\hat{\phi}$-component of the bulk-flow velocity of a fictitious single-species representing a deuterium-tritium fuel mixture with atomic mass 2.5 amu, evaluated at the plasma boundary — the last closed flux surface separating magnetically confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.

The toroidal projection is defined as:

$$
v_\phi^{DT} = \mathbf{v}_{DT} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{DT}$ is the bulk-flow velocity of the fictitious deuterium-tritium species and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a local point evaluation at the plasma boundary, distinct from [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which gives the flux-surface mean at the same location, and from [toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which resolves the deuterium species independently rather than treating the D-T mixture as a single effective species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the bulk flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Toroidal deuterium-ion fluid velocity at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, averaged over deuterium ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-ion toroidal fluid velocity at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier represents the bulk rotational flow of deuterium ions. It is the density-weighted mean over all deuterium ion charge states, rather than a thermal speed or velocity magnitude.

$$
v_{phi,D} = \frac{\sum_q n_{D,q} v_{phi,D,q}}{\sum_q n_{D,q}}
$$

where $q$ labels deuterium ion charge state, $n_{D,q}$ is its number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,D,q}$ is its toroidal fluid-velocity component in m.s$^{-1}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The locus is the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, and the quantity is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal hydrogen-ion velocity](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the deuterium-ion fluid velocity has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of deuterium ions at the last closed flux surface, resolved along increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The deuterium toroidal velocity is the local toroidal projection of the density-weighted bulk-flow velocity of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed flux surface. It excludes neutral deuterium and is not a flux-surface average.

$$
v_{D,\phi}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\frac{\sum_{q\in Q_D}n_{D,q}\mathbf{v}_{D,q}}{\sum_{q\in Q_D}n_{D,q}}
$$

Here $Q_D$ is the set of included deuterium ion charge states, $n_{D,q}$ is the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{D,q}$ is its bulk-flow velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The local quantity is distinct from the [toroidal flux-surface-averaged deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and from the corresponding value at the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the deuterium bulk velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk-flow velocity of elemental argon ions at the plasma boundary, combining charge states through a density-weighted mean.
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk-flow velocity of elemental argon ions describes the toroidal component of their collective motion over the plasma-boundary flux surface. It includes the argon ion population rather than a single charge state.

The boundary flux-surface average is defined by:

$$
\left\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}\right\rangle_{\psi_b}
= \frac{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\psi_b}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi|}{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\psi_b}} dS/|\nabla\psi|}
$$

where $\psi$ is a scalar magnetic-flux label, $\psi_b$ is its value on the plasma boundary, $S_{\psi_b}$ is the complete boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux label. The component $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}$ is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For charge-state index $z$, with density $n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$ and bulk velocity $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$, the local elemental-argon velocity is the density-weighted mean $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ar}}=\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ar},z}/\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$. Thus, this quantity differs from the local, unaveraged [toroidal argon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and parallels the charge-state aggregation used for [toroidal flux-surface-averaged deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the argon bulk-flow component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of beryllium ions, flux-surface averaged at the plasma boundary over all populated charge states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the beryllium-ion bulk-flow velocity, averaged over the plasma-boundary flux surface. The toroidal projection is taken in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame onto $\hat{\phi}$.

Let $\mathcal{S}_b$ denote the plasma-boundary, or separatrix, flux surface. The density-weighted combination of beryllium ion charge states is defined by:

$$
\left\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}} \right\rangle_{\mathcal{S}_b} = \frac{\sum_q \left\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}^{q+}} \right\rangle_{\mathcal{S}_b}}{\sum_q \left\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}} \right\rangle_{\mathcal{S}_b}}
$$

where angle brackets denote flux-surface averaging over $\mathcal{S}_b$, $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}$ is the number density in m$^{-3}$, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}$ is the toroidal bulk-flow velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $q$ indexes all populated beryllium ion charge states. This intensive mean is distinct from the local quantity [toroidal beryllium velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the beryllium bulk-flow component $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of carbon impurity ions, averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal carbon velocity is the density-weighted mean toroidal bulk-flow velocity of carbon impurity ions over the last closed magnetic flux surface. All carbon ion charge states are included in the mean.

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle V_\phi \rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\oint V_\phi\,dl/B_p}{\oint dl/B_p}
$$

where $V_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component, $dl$ is poloidal arc length along the flux surface, and $B_p$ is the magnitude of the poloidal magnetic field. The quantity is distinct from the local [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and from velocities of other impurity species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the carbon-ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of an effective deuterium–tritium fuel species, averaged over the last closed flux surface at the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of deuterium and tritium treated as one effective fuel species, averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary.

$$
\left\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\left\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{\left\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

Here, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}}$ is the local toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the effective deuterium–tritium species, $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is its number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a flux-surface average over the plasma-boundary surface. This averaged quantity is distinct from the local value represented by [toroidal deuterium–tritium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged deuterium-ion bulk-flow velocity along increasing toroidal angle on the last closed magnetic surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, with ionization states density-weighted.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the toroidal component of the deuterium-ion bulk velocity on the plasma boundary, defined as the last closed magnetic flux surface. The deuterium velocity is the density-weighted mean over all deuterium ionization states.

$$
\left\langle V_{\phi,D} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\displaystyle \oint_{\mathcal{S}_b} V_{\phi,D}\,\frac{dS}{|\mathbf{B}|}}{\displaystyle \oint_{\mathcal{S}_b} \frac{dS}{|\mathbf{B}|}}
$$

Here, $V_{\phi,D}=\mathbf{V}_D\cdot\hat{\phi}$ is the deuterium bulk-velocity projection onto the toroidal unit vector, $\mathcal{S}_b$ is the boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [toroidal deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), this quantity is averaged over the entire boundary surface rather than evaluated at a local point.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the deuterium bulk velocity has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocity of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary (separatrix).
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged toroidal velocity of helium-3 ($^3$He) ions quantifies the bulk toroidal flow of this light helium isotope (2 protons, 1 neutron) evaluated on the last closed flux surface that separates the confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This boundary value characterizes net toroidal rotation of $^3$He ions at the separatrix, relevant to impurity transport, momentum balance, and plasma–wall interaction studies.

The flux-surface average of the toroidal velocity component is defined as:

$$
\langle v_\phi \rangle = \frac{\oint v_\phi \, dl / B_p}{\oint dl / B_p}
$$

where $v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He_3}} \cdot \hat{\phi}$ is the ion fluid velocity projected onto $\hat{\phi}$ — the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame — $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude, and $dl$ is the arc-length element along the separatrix contour.

Toroidal rotation at the boundary is driven by external momentum sources such as neutral beam injection, intrinsic rotation arising from turbulent and neoclassical stresses, and the edge radial electric field. The quantity is inferred from charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) using injected neutral beams that stimulate helium-3 charge-exchange emission lines whose Doppler shift encodes the local toroidal velocity.

Boundary toroidal flow speeds for light ions in tokamak edge plasmas are of order $10^3$–$10^4$ m s$^{-1}$, depending on heating power, plasma current, and confinement regime. The analogous quantities for tritium and hydrogen are [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary); the generic multi-species form is toroidal_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary.
NAMES.sign: Positive when helium-3 ions flow in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$).

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk-flow velocity of helium-4 ions at the separatrix, density-weighted over all helium-4 charge states.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the flux-surface average over the separatrix of the toroidal component of the helium-4 ion bulk-flow velocity. The helium-4 value includes all helium-4 charge states through a density-weighted mean, rather than a sum of their velocities.

For charge-state-resolved density $n_{4,q}$ and toroidal velocity $v_{\phi,4,q}$, the species velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{FS}} = \left\langle \frac{\sum_q n_{4,q}v_{\phi,4,q}}{\sum_q n_{4,q}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{sep}}
$$

where $q$ indexes helium-4 charge state, $n_{4,q}$ is its number density in m$^{-3}$, $v_{\phi,4,q}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{sep}}$ denotes the flux-surface average over the separatrix. The toroidal component is taken along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This averaged quantity is distinct from the local [toroidal helium-4 velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary); the corresponding isotope-specific construction for helium-3 is [toroidal flux-surface-averaged helium-3 velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-4 bulk-flow component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of hydrogen ions, averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface and combining all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the density-weighted mean toroidal bulk-flow velocity of hydrogen ions at the plasma boundary, combining all hydrogen ionization states. The average is taken over the last closed magnetic flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

$$
\bar v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\sum_q \left\langle n_{\mathrm{H},q}v_{\phi,\mathrm{H},q}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{\sum_q \left\langle n_{\mathrm{H},q}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

Here $q$ indexes the hydrogen ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{H},q}$ is the number density of state $q$, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{H},q}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes the flux-surface average over the plasma boundary.

The charge-state aggregation is a density-weighted mean, not a sum of velocities. It differs from the local quantity [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) because that quantity is not flux-surface averaged, and from [toroidal flux-surface-averaged ion velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which represents the total ion fluid.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted hydrogen-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the total ion fluid at the plasma boundary, representing the density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the ion bulk-flow velocity, flux-surface averaged over the plasma boundary — the last closed flux surface forming the core–scrape-off-layer interface. For a plasma containing multiple ion species and charge states, the ion velocity is the density-weighted mean

$$
v_\phi = \frac{\sum_s n_s \, v_{\phi,s}}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density and $v_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal velocity of species $s$, with the sum running over all ion species and charge states present.

The flux-surface average is evaluated as $\langle A \rangle = \oint A \, dl/B_p \,/\, \oint dl/B_p$, where $dl$ is the poloidal arc-length element and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude, integrated along the plasma boundary flux surface. Species-resolved counterparts such as [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) give contributions from individual ion species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal component of the iron impurity ion bulk flow velocity at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the iron impurity bulk flow velocity, averaged over the magnetic flux surface coinciding with the plasma boundary, characterizes the net toroidal rotation of iron ions at the last closed flux surface. The flux-surface average eliminates poloidal asymmetries in the local velocity distribution, providing a single scalar representative of the toroidal impurity flow at the edge.

The flux-surface average of a quantity $f$ on a given flux surface is defined as:

$$
\langle f \rangle = \frac{\oint f \, dl_p / B_p}{\oint dl_p / B_p}
$$

where $l_p$ is the poloidal arc length along the flux-surface contour and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude. Iron ($Z = 26$) is a high-$Z$ metallic impurity that enters the confined plasma through sputtering of plasma-facing components; its toroidal rotation at the boundary reflects edge momentum transport and neoclassical impurity flow physics.

This quantity is measured via charge exchange recombination spectroscopy, exploiting Doppler shifts of iron charge-state emission lines recorded along multiple poloidal viewing chords; the flux-surface-averaged value is then reconstructed from multi-chord data. This name is directly analogous to boundary velocity names for lighter impurities such as [carbon](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), [argon](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), and [neon](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). Where poloidally resolved measurements are available, the local counterpart [toroidal iron velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) provides additional information on poloidal asymmetries not captured by the flux-surface average.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the iron ion velocity is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_krypton_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk velocity of krypton ions, averaged over all ionization states and the last closed magnetic flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal krypton velocity is the density-weighted mean over all krypton ionization states on the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed magnetic flux surface. The toroidal direction is the direction of increasing angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\left\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS},b} = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} \left(\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\right)\frac{dl}{B_p}}{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} \left(\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\right)\frac{dl}{B_p}}
$$

Here $q$ indexes krypton ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the number density of state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal bulk velocity, $dl$ is poloidal arc length, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, and $\psi_b$ labels the boundary surface. This species-resolved quantity differs from the total-ion quantity [toroidal flux-surface-averaged ion velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary); its locus differs from [toroidal krypton velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the krypton-ion bulk velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_lithium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Charge-state-aggregated toroidal bulk-flow velocity of lithium ions, averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the lithium-ion bulk-flow velocity, flux-surface averaged over the separatrix, which is the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary. Lithium ions comprise Li+ through Li3+, combined using their particle densities.

$$
\left\langle v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{3}\left\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{\sum_{q=1}^{3}\left\langle n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

Here, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is the toroidal bulk-flow velocity of lithium charge state $q$, $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is its number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes averaging over the separatrix. The toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The related [flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary) supplies the corresponding charge-state-summed density, not a velocity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the lithium-ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface average of the toroidal neon-ion bulk velocity on the last closed magnetic flux surface, with all ionization states combined by density weighting.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the density-weighted mean toroidal bulk velocity of neon ions, averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface at the plasma boundary. It includes ionized neon charge states and excludes neutral neon. The corresponding unaveraged local quantity is [toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

For the flux surface labeled by $psi_b$, the defining average is

$$
\overline{u}_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}}(\psi_b)=
\frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b}\left(\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{q=1}^{10} n_q\mathbf{u}_q}{\displaystyle\sum_{q=1}^{10} n_q}\cdot\hat{\phi}\right)\frac{dl}{B_p}}
{\displaystyle\oint_{\psi=\psi_b}\frac{dl}{B_p}}
$$

where $q$ is the neon charge state, $n_q$ is its number density, $\mathbf{u}_q$ is its bulk velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $dl$ is poloidal arc length, $B_p$ is poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, and $\psi_b$ is the boundary flux label. Components use the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$.

The density weighting gives the neon-ion fluid velocity rather than an unweighted average of charge-state velocities. The deuterium counterpart is [toroidal flux-surface-averaged deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted neon-ion velocity has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, along $+\hat{\phi}$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Density-weighted, flux-surface-averaged toroidal bulk-flow velocity of oxygen impurity ions, combined over all ionization states on the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the toroidal component of the oxygen impurity-ion bulk velocity on the last closed magnetic flux surface, with oxygen ionization states combined by density weighting. It is a surface average rather than the velocity at a particular poloidal location.

The toroidal direction is $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The defining density-weighted average is:

$$
\overline{V}_{\phi,\mathrm{O}}^{\mathrm{LCFS}} = \frac{\left\langle \sum_q n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}} V_{\phi,\mathrm{O}^{q+}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}{\left\langle \sum_q n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included oxygen ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is the local number density of state $q$, $V_{\phi,\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow velocity, and angle brackets denote flux-surface averaging on the last closed flux surface. The quantity excludes other ion species; the corresponding all-ion quantity is [toroidal flux-surface-averaged ion velocity at plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). The local, non-averaged counterpart is [toroidal oxygen velocity at plasma boundary](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the oxygen-ion bulk flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_total_plasma_momentum_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged total plasma momentum in the toroidal direction at the plasma boundary is the signed flux-surface average, on the last closed magnetic flux surface, of the cumulative toroidal linear momentum enclosed by that surface, summed over electrons and all ion species. Positive values point along increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface-averaged total plasma momentum in the toroidal direction at the plasma boundary is the flux-surface average, on the last closed magnetic flux surface, of the cumulative toroidal component of plasma linear momentum enclosed by that surface. The cumulative momentum includes electrons and all ion species and is treated as a flux-surface scalar before averaging.

The cumulative boundary value is defined by the enclosed-volume integral; writing the flux-surface average explicitly gives:

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{FSA}}^{\mathrm{b}}
=
\frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_\mathrm{b}} P_\phi(\psi_\mathrm{b})\, dA/|\nabla\psi|}
     {\oint_{\psi=\psi_\mathrm{b}} dA/|\nabla\psi|}
=
\int_{V_\mathrm{b}} \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{x})\, v_{\phi,s}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_{\phi,\mathrm{FSA}}^\mathrm{b}$ is this quantity, $P_\phi(\psi_\mathrm{b})$ is the [toroidal total plasma momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum) associated with the boundary flux label, $\psi_\mathrm{b}$ is the boundary value of the [poloidal magnetic-flux label](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface), $dA/|\nabla\psi|$ is the flux-surface averaging measure normalized by the denominator, $V_\mathrm{b}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, $dV$ is the volume element, $s$ runs over electrons and all ion species, $m_s$ is species mass, $n_s$ is species number density, and $v_{\phi,s}=\mathbf{v}_s\cdot\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal velocity component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The product $m_s n_s v_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal momentum density contribution of species $s$, so the flux-surface average is applied to the enclosed total $P_\phi(\psi_\mathrm{b})$, not directly to this local density.

This quantity is not a boundary-surface integral of local toroidal momentum density, not the flux-surface average of the local density $g_\phi=\sum_s m_s n_s v_{\phi,s}$ alone, and not a major-radius-weighted angular-momentum measure. It is the flux-surface-averaged representation of [toroidal total plasma momentum at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum_at_plasma_boundary); the analogous cumulative value at the pedestal top is [toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the enclosed total toroidal momentum is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Density-weighted flux-surface average of the toroidal bulk-flow velocity of tritium ions on the last closed flux surface at the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the toroidal component of the tritium-ion bulk-flow velocity, averaged over the separatrix, or last closed magnetic flux surface. The tritium value is the density-weighted mean over all tritium ion charge states and describes directed ion motion rather than thermal speed.

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\left\langle v_\phi \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\oint_{\mathrm{sep}} v_\phi\, dl/B_p}{\oint_{\mathrm{sep}} dl/B_p}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity, $dl$ is differential distance along the separatrix, and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. The toroidal projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Its charge-state aggregation complements [flux-surface-averaged tritium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary); the corresponding total-ion quantity is [toroidal flux-surface-averaged ion velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tritium bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: The right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)-frame toroidal component of the flux-surface-averaged tungsten ion bulk velocity at the plasma boundary is a density-weighted average, with the species velocity taken as the density-weighted mean over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$-frame toroidal component of the flux-surface-averaged tungsten ion bulk velocity at the plasma boundary is the density-weighted average of the tungsten impurity-ion bulk-flow component along $\hat{\phi}$ on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The species-level tungsten velocity is the density-weighted mean over all tungsten ionization states.

The density-weighted flux-surface average is defined by:

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{tungsten},b}^{\mathrm{FS}} =
\frac{\displaystyle \int_{S_b} \left(\sum_q n_{\mathrm{tungsten},q} v_{\phi,\mathrm{tungsten},q}\right) \frac{dS}{|\nabla \rho|}}
{\displaystyle \int_{S_b} \left(\sum_q n_{\mathrm{tungsten},q}\right) \frac{dS}{|\nabla \rho|}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{tungsten},b}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is this quantity, $S_b$ is the last closed magnetic flux surface, $q$ indexes tungsten ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{tungsten},q}$ is the local number density of ionization state $q$, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{tungsten},q}$ is its local toroidal bulk-flow component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $dS$ is the surface area element on $S_b$, and $\rho$ is the radial flux coordinate in a flux coordinate set $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ labeling the nested magnetic flux surfaces. The factor $dS/|\nabla\rho|$ gives the volume-derivative flux-surface-average measure, and any monotonic relabeling of $\rho$ gives the same ratio on a given surface.

This quantity represents the boundary value only; for a diverted boundary it is understood as the limit approaching the last closed magnetic flux surface from inside the confined plasma. It is distinct from the local [toroidal tungsten velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which is not flux-surface averaged, and from [toroidal tungsten velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), which is evaluated at a different locus. Because velocity is intensive, aggregation over ionization states is by density-weighted mean rather than by summation of velocities.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted mean tungsten ion bulk-flow component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal component of xenon ion bulk flow velocity at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The flux-surface-averaged toroidal xenon velocity at the plasma boundary quantifies the mean azimuthal flow of xenon impurity ions around the torus, averaged along the last closed flux surface (separatrix). Xenon ($Z=54$) is a heavy noble-gas impurity used in radiative-mantle experiments to spread divertor heat loads, and its toroidal rotation reflects momentum balance between collisional coupling to the bulk plasma, neoclassical forces, and external toroidal momentum input.

The flux-surface average of the toroidal velocity component $v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe}$ is defined as:

$$
\langle v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe} \rangle = \frac{\oint v_\phi^\mathrm{Xe} \, B_p^{-1} \, dl}{\oint B_p^{-1} \, dl}
$$

where $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic field magnitude and the line integrals are taken along the plasma boundary contour.

Toroidal impurity velocities at the separatrix are measured primarily by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), resolving Doppler shifts from charge exchange between injected neutral beam atoms and Xe ions; a poloidally distributed array of sightlines is necessary to reconstruct the flux-surface average. The non-averaged counterpart is given by [toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), while analogous averaged quantities for lighter seeding species include [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the xenon ion flow is directed in the sense of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top, resolved along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the density-weighted mean over all helium-3 ion charge states and is signed positive for flow toward increasing φ.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top is the helium-3 ion bulk-flow component resolved along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. For species-level helium-3, this intensive quantity is the density-weighted mean over all helium-3 ion charge states at the pedestal top.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\,^3\mathrm{He}}^{\mathrm{ped}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes helium-3 ion charge state, $n_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the number density of that charge state at the pedestal top, $\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ped}}$ is its ion fluid velocity there, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity excludes radial and vertical components in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, vector speed, arithmetic averages over charge states, and values at other loci such as the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis). It is defined where the total helium-3 ion density in the averaging denominator is nonzero.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-3 ion fluid velocity is directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He)

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the helium-4 ion fluid velocity evaluated at the H-mode pressure pedestal top, resolved along the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the helium-4 ion fluid velocity evaluated at the H-mode pressure pedestal top, resolved along the direction of increasing toroidal angle, is the signed bulk-flow component of helium-4 ions along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The pedestal top is the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pressure pedestal. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all helium-4 ionization charge states in the ion population.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal component at the pedestal top is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{ped}}^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} =
\frac{\sum_q n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} \left(\mathbf{v}_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}
{\sum_q n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}}
$$

where $q$ labels helium-4 ionization charge states, $n_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}$ is the local number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_q^{{}^4\mathrm{He}}$ is its fluid velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$; all quantities are evaluated at the pedestal-top location.

This quantity is local to the pedestal top and is not an average over the full pedestal or scrape-off layer. It is a species-level helium-4 velocity, so it differs from charge-state-resolved helium-4 velocities by the density-weighted charge-state aggregation and from other isotope velocities only by the selected ion species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-4 ion flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Toroidal fluid velocity of hydrogen ions at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion fluid velocity component tangent to the toroidal direction at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It describes the directed bulk motion of the hydrogen-ion population, rather than its speed or a thermal velocity spread.

$$
v_{\phi,H} = \mathbf{v}_H \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_H$ is the hydrogen-ion fluid-velocity vector and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The pedestal-top locus denotes the inner shoulder of the edge transport barrier and is distinct from the hydrogen-ion velocity evaluated at an internal transport barrier, as in [toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier). The quantity is a directed component, not the magnitude of the hydrogen-ion velocity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the hydrogen-ion fluid velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Local toroidal component of the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity at the plasma boundary, density-weighted over all hydrogen charge states.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity component tangent to the toroidal direction at the plasma boundary, rather than a flux-surface average. Hydrogen denotes the combined hydrogen-ion population.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{phi,H}(R,Z)=\mathbf{v}_H(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\phi},\qquad \mathbf{v}_H=\frac{\sum_q n_{H,q}\mathbf{v}_{H,q}}{\sum_q n_{H,q}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_H$ is the hydrogen bulk-flow velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $n_{H,q}$ is the density of hydrogen charge state $q$, and $\mathbf{v}_{H,q}$ is its bulk-flow velocity. The coordinates $R$ and $Z$ are major radius and vertical height, respectively. The local quantity is distinct from the [toroidal flux-surface-averaged hydrogen velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the hydrogen bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal iron velocity at the pedestal top is the density-weighted mean bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron ions at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It includes all populated iron charge states from Fe+ through fully stripped iron and excludes neutral iron.

For charge states $q=1,\ldots,26$, the velocity is defined by

$$
v_\phi^{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{26} n_q u_{\phi,q}}{\sum_{q=1}^{26} n_q}
$$

where $n_q$ is the number density of iron charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, $u_{\phi,q}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow component in m s$^{-1}$, and $v_\phi^{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the resulting density-weighted velocity. This charge-state aggregation is distinct from a charge-state-resolved velocity and is analogous to [toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top); its locus differs from [toroidal iron velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted iron-ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the bulk-flow velocity of iron impurity ions evaluated at the last closed flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal projection of the bulk-flow velocity of iron impurity ions at the last closed flux surface. The iron bulk-flow velocity is the density-weighted mean over all included iron ionization states.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the projection is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Fe}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the toroidal velocity component, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$; $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The value is local to the plasma boundary and is distinct from the [flux-surface-averaged toroidal iron velocity](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which averages the same projection over that surface. It is the iron-species counterpart of [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the iron bulk-flow velocity has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top is the toroidal component of the density-weighted mean krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the H-mode pedestal top, taken over all krypton charge states. It is resolved along increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top is the toroidal component of the krypton ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated at the H-mode pedestal-top reference location. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all krypton ion charge states, not a sum of charge-state velocities. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The charge-state aggregation and toroidal projection are defined by

$$
v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow velocity, and $v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the resulting signed species-level toroidal velocity.

This quantity is inferred from krypton line spectroscopy or other impurity-flow diagnostics localized near the pedestal top, with viewing-geometry corrections used to isolate the toroidal component. Because line emission is often charge-state selective, interpretation must map measured charge-state velocities onto the density-weighted species mean. Momentum-balance or radial-force-balance analysis may combine this quantity with [poloidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top], pressure-gradient, electric-field, and magnetic-field information.

No universal krypton-specific pedestal range applies across devices. Representative signed impurity toroidal velocities at pedestal-top conditions are commonly in the range $-5 \times 10^4$ to $5 \times 10^4$ m.s$^{-1}$, with higher-rotation cases approaching $\pm 10^5$ m.s$^{-1}$ in either toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted krypton ion bulk flow at the pedestal top is along $+\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the lithium impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top. It represents the local azimuthal rotation of lithium impurity ions at the steep-gradient edge transport barrier, not a pedestal-region average.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal lithium ion fluid velocity at the pedestal top is the $\hat{\phi}$-projection of the lithium impurity ion mean velocity vector at the radial reference location where the H-mode edge transport barrier steep-gradient region joins the flatter core profile. This is a point-evaluated quantity, not a spatial average over the pedestal region.

The toroidal component is defined as:

$$
v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Li}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium ion fluid velocity vector and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Lithium toroidal rotation at the pedestal is inferred from charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) using Doppler shifts of lithium spectral lines following charge exchange with an injected neutral beam. The pedestal-top reference location is identified from the steep-gradient region of the relevant kinetic profile. Comparable pedestal-top rotation measurements for other impurity species are provided by [toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top); the lithium ion rotation at other radial reference points is covered by [toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Li}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the density-weighted neon-ion fluid velocity at the core-side top of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neon-ion velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid velocities of all represented neon ion charge states at the core-side shoulder of the edge transport barrier. It is a signed projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
V_{\mathrm{Ne},\phi} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne},q} v_{\mathrm{Ne},q,\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne},q}}
$$

Here, $q$ labels neon ion charge state, $n_{\mathrm{Ne},q}$ is its number density, and $v_{\mathrm{Ne},q,\phi}$ is its toroidal fluid-velocity component. The quantity is distinguished from [toroidal neon velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) by its pedestal-top location and is a species-specific counterpart of [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neon-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon impurity ions at the last closed flux surface, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the density-weighted mean over all neon ion charge states and is local, not a flux-surface average.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon impurity ions at the last closed flux surface. The toroidal component is taken in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Because no neon ionization state is specified, the elemental neon velocity is the density-weighted mean over all neon ion charge states present at that locus.

The component and charge-state aggregation are defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \left(\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}\right) \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $q$ indexes neon ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is its bulk velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity is a local boundary value and does not imply a flux-surface average, poloidal average, toroidal average, or charge-state sum. The flux-surface-averaged boundary counterpart is [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary); the same toroidal component at other radial loci includes [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted neon ion flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of ionized nitrogen across its charge states, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal nitrogen velocity at the pedestal top is the density-weighted mean flow of ionized nitrogen ions over all nitrogen charge states at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It describes flow rather than abundance, which is represented by [nitrogen density at the pedestal top](name:nitrogen_density_at_pedestal_top).

For nitrogen charge states $q=1,\ldots,7$, the species velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,N} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{7} n_q v_{\phi,q}}{\sum_{q=1}^{7} n_q}
$$

where $n_q$ is the number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$ and $v_{\phi,q}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$, measured in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Neutral nitrogen is excluded. The pedestal-top value is distinguished from the corresponding [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) by its edge-barrier location.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at the H-mode pedestal reference location, projected along the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal oxygen velocity at the pedestal top characterizes the impurity ion fluid flow projected onto the $\hat{\phi}$ direction at the H-mode edge transport barrier's outer shoulder, where the steep-gradient pedestal region transitions to the flatter core profile. Oxygen (atomic number $Z = 8$) is a common intrinsic or deliberately seeded impurity in tokamaks, present in charge states spanning O$^{5+}$ through O$^{8+}$ in the pedestal; this quantity represents the oxygen fluid velocity aggregated over the predominant charge states unless a specific ionization state is separately resolved.

The toroidal component is defined by the projection:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen ion fluid velocity vector evaluated at the pedestal-top locus.

This quantity is measured via charge exchange recombination spectroscopy, which resolves the Doppler shift of oxygen emission lines following charge exchange with an injected neutral beam. Toroidal rotation velocities at the pedestal top in H-mode span roughly $10^3$–$10^5$ m s$^{-1}$, reflecting neutral beam torque input, intrinsic rotation, and impurity-specific flow corrections. Comparison with [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_pedestal_top) enables cross-species benchmarking of pedestal rotation profiles.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the oxygen ion flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the oxygen impurity ion bulk flow velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
NAMES.long:
The toroidal velocity of oxygen impurity ions at the plasma boundary quantifies the toroidal momentum carried by the oxygen ion population at the last closed flux surface, which separates the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This local point value is distinct from the flux-surface-averaged quantity [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), which integrates the velocity weighted by the boundary flux-surface geometry.

The toroidal component $v_\phi$ is the projection of the oxygen bulk flow velocity onto the toroidal direction:

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{O} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{O}$ is the oxygen ion bulk flow velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Oxygen toroidal velocity at the boundary is primarily measured by charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS), exploiting the Doppler shift of oxygen emission lines to extract the ion flow velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$. Analogous boundary velocities for other impurity species include [toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the oxygen ion flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise when viewed from above in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction).

NAMES.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top is the volume-integrated toroidal linear momentum of the confined plasma inside the pedestal-top flux surface, summed over electrons and all ion species. It is the pedestal-top endpoint of total toroidal plasma momentum, not a local momentum density or toroidal angular momentum.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top is the cumulative toroidal component of plasma linear momentum contained inside the flux surface located at the top of the H-mode pedestal, summed over electrons and all ion species. The toroidal component is taken in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Let $\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}$ denote the radial flux-surface label of the pedestal-top flux surface and let $V(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}})$ be the plasma volume enclosed by that surface. The quantity is the radial cumulative [toroidal_total_plasma_momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum) evaluated at the pedestal-top endpoint:

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{ped}} = P_\phi(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}) = \int_{V(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}})} \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{x}) v_{\phi,s}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_\phi(\rho)$ is the cumulative toroidal plasma momentum inside the flux surface labeled by $\rho$, $s$ indexes electrons and all ion species, $m_s$ is the species particle mass, $n_s$ is the species number density, $v_{\phi,s}$ is the signed toroidal velocity component, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

This quantity is an endpoint value of a volume-integrated radial function: it is not the local toroidal momentum density $\sum_s m_s n_s v_{\phi,s}$ on the pedestal-top surface, and it is not a flux-surface average. It is also not toroidal angular momentum; the angular-momentum integral would include the moment arm $R$ multiplying the toroidal linear-momentum density. The same cumulative quantity has related endpoint values at the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_magnetic_axis) and at the [plasma boundary].
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net toroidal plasma momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Total plasma toroidal momentum (Lφ), summed over all ion species and electrons, evaluated at the pedestal top. Captures the net toroidal angular momentum at this key boundary transport layer.
