NAMES.name: toroidal_total_plasma_momentum_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Signed total plasma linear momentum along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed (R, φ, Z) frame, integrated within the separatrix and summed over electrons and all ion species.
NAMES.long:
Total toroidal plasma momentum at the separatrix is the net linear momentum carried in the geometric toroidal direction by electrons and all ion species within the volume bounded by the separatrix. The separatrix defines the outer boundary of the confined-plasma volume; this quantity is not toroidal angular momentum.

The defining volume integral is

$$
P_\phi(\mathcal{S}) = \int_{V(\mathcal{S})} \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{r}) v_{\phi,s}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\mathcal{S}$ is the separatrix, $V(\mathcal{S})$ is the enclosed plasma volume, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$ in kg, $n_s$ is its number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,s}$ is its signed toroidal velocity in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The summation includes electrons and all ion species.

This boundary-specific quantity complements [toroidal total plasma momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum) and differs from [toroidal plasma momentum at magnetic axis](name:toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_magnetic_axis) by its evaluation locus.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Total plasma toroidal momentum (Lφ), summed over all ion species and electrons, evaluated at the separatrix. Captures the net toroidal angular momentum of the plasma at this boundary location.

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Density-weighted mean toroidal velocity of tungsten impurity ions at the H-mode pedestal top, averaged over all tungsten ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal tungsten velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid velocities of tungsten impurity ions over their ionization states. It is evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the edge transport barrier in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining charge-state average is

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{W}} = \frac{\sum_q n_q v_{\phi,q}}{\sum_q n_q}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{W}}$ is the tungsten toroidal velocity, $n_q$ is the number density of tungsten ions in charge state $q$, and $v_{\phi,q}$ is their toroidal velocity component.

The average is density-weighted over tungsten ion charge states, not a sum of velocities and not a flux-surface average. It therefore differs from the [toroidal flux-surface-averaged tungsten velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary); [toroidal carbon velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_pedestal_top) is the analogous species-specific quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tungsten velocity component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of tungsten impurity ions at the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal projection of the tungsten impurity-ion bulk velocity at the plasma boundary, defined on the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer. It is a density-weighted mean over the included tungsten ion charge states.

$$
v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{W}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)=\\frac{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)\\left[\\mathbf{v}_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)\\cdot\\hat{\\boldsymbol{\\phi}}\\right]}{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)}
$$

Here, $q$ is the tungsten ion charge state, $n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its number density, $\\mathbf{v}_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its bulk velocity, $\\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the boundary, and $\\hat{\\boldsymbol{\\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame. Unlike [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), this quantity is local rather than flux-surface averaged.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tungsten-ion velocity component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Tungsten (W).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of xenon ions, averaged over all ionization states at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity at the H-mode pedestal top. It is the density-weighted mean over all xenon ionization states, rather than a sum of their velocities.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe},q} V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe},q}}
$$

Here $q$ labels xenon ionization state, $n_{\mathrm{Xe},q}$ is the number density of that state, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe},q}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow component. The denominator is the total xenon ion density corresponding to [xenon density at the pedestal top](name:xenon_density_at_pedestal_top). The value is evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier and is distinct from [toroidal xenon velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and [toroidal xenon velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$ is positive in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Xenon (Xe).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated on the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the geometric toroidal direction at the plasma boundary. The xenon-ion bulk velocity is the density-weighted mean over all xenon ion charge states and excludes thermal random motion.

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Xe}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity in m s$^{-1}$ and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ frame. The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface. This local value is distinct from the flux-surface average [toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: total_ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Positive e-folding distance for the outward decrease of total ion number density across magnetic flux surfaces in the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the positive cross-field decay length of the total ion number density in the scrape-off layer. It is the species- and charge-state-summed specialization of [ion decay length over the scrape-off layer](name:ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer).

$$
\lambda_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \left|\frac{1}{n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}\frac{\partial n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}{\partial \ell_\perp}\right|^{-1}
$$

Here $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion number density, summed over the included ion species and charge states, and $\ell_\perp$ is outward distance normal to magnetic flux surfaces, measured in m. The quantity excludes electron and neutral-particle densities and is non-negative by definition.

sources.enhanced_context: Total ion density radial decay length (λ_ni) in the scrape-off layer, defined as the inverse logarithmic gradient of the ion density: [grad(ni)/ni]^-1. Characterizes the spatial scale of ion density fall-off across the SOL.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion density radial decay length inv(grad ni/ni)

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Number density of all ions at the H-mode pedestal top is the ion particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is summed over all ion species and positive charge states in the confined plasma.
NAMES.long:
Number density of all ions at the H-mode pedestal top is the ion particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It includes every positive ion species present at that locus; for each species, the contribution is summed over all positive charge states.

The species and charge-state aggregation is defined by:

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_{Z>0} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ denotes this quantity, $s$ indexes ion species, $Z$ is the ion charge number, and $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ions of species $s$ in charge state $Z$.

The pedestal top is in the confined plasma at the core-side shoulder of the edge transport barrier, not at the separatrix, plasma boundary, or scrape-off layer. This quantity is the aggregate over ion populations at that locus, not any one population's [ion density at pedestal top](name:ion_density_at_pedestal_top).

Species-specific pedestal-top densities such as [hydrogen density at pedestal top](name:hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top), [deuterium density at pedestal top](name:deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top), [carbon density at pedestal top](name:carbon_density_at_pedestal_top), and [nitrogen density at pedestal top](name:nitrogen_density_at_pedestal_top) are charge-state-summed contributions to this total. Electrons and neutral particles are excluded.

This is an unweighted ion particle density, not an ion charge density and not the [electron density at pedestal top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top). For a quasineutral plasma, $n_e = \sum_s \sum_{Z>0} Z n_{s,Z}$, where $n_e$ is the electron density at the pedestal top; this quantity equals $n_e$ only when every contributing ion is singly charged.

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total ion number density at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per volume, summing all charged ion species and charge states while excluding neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Total ion density at the plasma boundary is the local number density of all positively charged ion populations at the separatrix, the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. It is the charge-state-summed specialization of [ion density at the plasma boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state $Z$, and the sums include every charged ion species and charge state present at the boundary.

Neutral particles are excluded, and each ion contributes one particle regardless of its charge. The corresponding surface average is [flux-surface-averaged total ion density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), which averages this local quantity over the separatrix.

sources.enhanced_context: Total ion density (ni_total) summed over all ion species at the separatrix. A key boundary parameter for edge plasma modelling and SOL transport.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged total ion number density at the plasma boundary, summing all charged ion species and charge states equally while excluding neutral particles.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the total charged-ion particle density on the plasma boundary. Each charged ion contributes one particle regardless of species or charge state, while neutral atoms and molecules are excluded.

The defining average is

$$
\langle n_i \rangle_b = \frac{\displaystyle\int_{S_b} \left(\sum_s \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{s,Z}\right)\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}{\displaystyle\int_{S_b}\frac{dS}{|\nabla\psi|}}
$$

where $S_b$ is the plasma-boundary flux surface, $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state $Z$, $dS$ is the surface-area element, and $\psi$ is a flux-surface label. This is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [total ion density at the plasma boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), not a charge-weighted density or a neutral-particle density.

sources.enhanced_context: Total ion density (ni_total), the sum of densities over all ion species, flux-surface averaged at the separatrix. Represents the total ion particle content at the core-SOL boundary.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Number density of tritium ions evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter core plasma.
NAMES.long:
Tritium density at the pedestal top is the local number density of tritium ions (T$^+$, $Z=1$, $A=3$) at the shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, where the steep edge density gradient transitions to the flatter confined-plasma core profile. The pedestal top is the common evaluation locus for the [density_at_pedestal_top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) family.

The pedestal-top value is the local tritium ion density evaluated at the pedestal-top flux surface:

$$
n_{\mathrm{T,ped}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{T}^+}}{dV}\right|_{\rho=\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $dN_{\mathrm{T}^+}$ is the number of singly ionized tritium ions in the volume element $dV$, $\rho$ is the radial flux-surface label in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, $\theta$ and $\phi$ are the poloidal and toroidal angular coordinates in that coordinate set, and $\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the value of $\rho$ at the pedestal-top surface.

As a species-level number density, this quantity is summed over all ionized charge states; for tritium, whose nuclear charge is one, the ionized contribution is T$^+$, so the charge-state sum reduces to the singly ionized tritium density. It excludes neutral tritium atoms and molecules, is one species-resolved contribution to [ion_density_at_pedestal_top](name:ion_density_at_pedestal_top), and is distinct from [deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top](name:deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top) and the effective combined-fuel quantity [deuterium_tritium_density_at_pedestal_top](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_pedestal_top).

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Number density of tritium ions at the plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface separating the magnetically confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
The tritium density at the plasma boundary is the local number density of ionized tritium evaluated on the last closed flux surface (LCFS), which separates confined plasma from open-field-line scrape-off-layer plasma.

The tritium-ion number density $n_T$ satisfies the continuity relation

$$
\frac{\partial n_T}{\partial t} = -\nabla \cdot \Gamma_T + S_T
$$

where $\Gamma_T$ is the tritium-ion particle flux and $S_T$ is the net tritium-ion source rate. The quantity includes ionized tritium and excludes neutral tritium; it is a local boundary value rather than the flux-surface average defined by [flux-surface-averaged tritium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary). It is the tritium-specific instance of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.parent_definition: Tritium

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Flux-surface average of tritium ion number density evaluated at the plasma boundary, with the species-level ion density summed over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface average of tritium ion number density evaluated at the plasma boundary is the value obtained by applying the flux-surface-average operator to the local tritium ion number density on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix bounding the confined plasma.

The average at the boundary flux value $\psi_b$ is defined in flux coordinates $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$ by the Jacobian-weighted surface integral:

$$
\langle n_T \rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{2\pi} n_T(\psi_b,\theta,\phi)\,\mathcal{J}(\psi_b,\theta,\phi)\,d\theta\,d\phi}{\int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{2\pi} \mathcal{J}(\psi_b,\theta,\phi)\,d\theta\,d\phi}
$$

where $n_T$ is the local [tritium ion number density at the plasma boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), $\psi_b$ is the boundary value of the poloidal magnetic flux, $\theta$ and $\phi$ are the poloidal and toroidal coordinates in the flux-coordinate tuple $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$, and $\mathcal{J}$ is the positive coordinate Jacobian of the flux-coordinate mapping. Equivalently, $\mathcal{J}\,d\theta\,d\phi$ is the flux-surface measure $dS/|\nabla\psi|$ at fixed $\psi$.

The species-level tritium density is summed over all charge states of tritium ions. It excludes neutral tritium atoms and tritium-bearing molecules, and is distinct from [flux-surface-averaged total ion density], which aggregates over all ion species.

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Number density of tungsten impurity ions at the pedestal top is the particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, summed over W1+ through W74+ and excluding neutral tungsten atoms.
NAMES.long:
Number density of tungsten impurity ions at the pedestal top is the local particle count per volume for tungsten ions evaluated at the core-side shoulder of an H-mode pedestal. The pedestal top is the transition where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter confined-core density variation, distinct from a separatrix or plasma-boundary value. This quantity is the tungsten-specific specialization of [density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top).

The tungsten density at the pedestal-top location is defined by

$$
n_{\rm W}(\xi_{\rm ped,top}) = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(\xi_{\rm ped,top})
$$

where $n_{\rm W}$ and $n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, $Z$ is the dimensionless tungsten charge-state index, and $\xi_{\rm ped,top}$ is the radial label of the pedestal-top location.

The sum includes tungsten ions from W1+ through fully stripped W74+ and excludes neutral tungsten atoms. Unlike [tungsten density](name:tungsten_density), this quantity is restricted to the pedestal-top locus; [iron density at the pedestal top](name:iron_density_at_pedestal_top) is an analogous species-resolved family member.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_neutral_species_density
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Mean number density of a specified neutral species over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface during plasma initiation.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the spatial mean of the local number density of one specified neutral species within the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface during plasma initiation. The local quantity is distinguished from [neutral_density](name:neutral_density), which is evaluated at a point.

$$
\overline{n}_0 = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} n_0(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_0(\mathbf{r})$ is the local number density of the specified neutral species at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The average is species-specific and excludes neutral particles outside the enclosed volume. It is not the charge-state or population aggregate represented by [total_neutral_density](name:total_neutral_density), nor the volume average of ion density represented by [volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density).

NAMES.name: vorticity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: Signed field-parallel component of the curl of diamagnetic drift velocity for a plasma species or effective fluid, measuring rotational structure from pressure-gradient-driven cross-field motion.
NAMES.long:
Field-parallel diamagnetic vorticity is the signed projection of the curl of a species or effective-fluid diamagnetic drift velocity onto the local magnetic-field direction. It describes rotational structure generated by pressure-gradient-driven cross-field drift, not a parallel flow velocity.

$$
\omega_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}} = \hat{\mathbf b} \cdot \left(\nabla \times \mathbf v_{\mathrm{dia}}\right), \qquad \hat{\mathbf b} = \frac{\mathbf B}{|\mathbf B|}
$$

Here, $\omega_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the field-parallel diamagnetic vorticity, $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic drift velocity, $\nabla \times$ denotes the curl, $\mathbf B$ is the local magnetic field, $|\mathbf B|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field.

The effective-fluid interpretation is related to [plasma velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), while a species-resolved interpretation uses [ion charge state diamagnetic velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). Only the diamagnetic-drift contribution is included; electric-field-driven and other flow contributions are excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the curl of the diamagnetic drift velocity points along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Number density of xenon impurity ions at the pedestal top is the particle count per volume at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge barrier, summed over Xe+ through fully stripped Xe54+ unless a charge state is specified.
NAMES.long:
Number density of xenon impurity ions at the pedestal top is the local particle count per volume of xenon ions at the core-side shoulder of an H-mode pedestal. The pedestal top is the transition where the steep-gradient edge transport barrier meets the flatter confined-core density variation, distinct from a separatrix or plasma-boundary value. This quantity is summed over xenon ionization states; an explicitly named charge state denotes only that state.

For xenon evaluated at the pedestal-top radial label, the defining density is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}})=\sum_{Z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{Z+}}(\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{Z+}}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, $Z$ is the xenon ionization charge state, and $\xi_{\mathrm{ped,top}}$ identifies the pedestal-top location. This xenon-specific member of [density at pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top) is distinct from [xenon density at internal transport barrier](name:xenon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), which refers to a different transport-barrier locus.

NAMES.name: bulk_plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift_magnitude
NAMES.short: Magnitude of the thermal bulk-plasma velocity contribution associated with pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift, independent of its direction.
NAMES.long:
Diamagnetic-drift speed is the magnitude of the thermal bulk-plasma velocity contribution associated with the pressure-gradient term in the perpendicular fluid momentum balance. It describes a collective center-of-mass flow contribution, not an individual-particle drift.

The speed is defined from the corresponding velocity vector:

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia}} = \left|\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia}}\right|
$$

where $v_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic-drift speed and $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the bulk plasma velocity due to diamagnetic drift, defined in [bulk plasma velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:bulk_plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

The magnitude is non-negative and contains no directional sign; signed projections of the same velocity are distinct quantities.

NAMES.name: coulomb_logarithm_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Dimensionless Coulomb logarithm at the H-mode pressure pedestal top, expressing the range of impact parameters contributing to cumulative small-angle Coulomb scattering.
NAMES.long:
The Coulomb logarithm at the H-mode pressure pedestal top is the local dimensionless factor that represents the effective range of impact parameters contributing to cumulative small-angle Coulomb scattering. It is the pedestal-top specialization of the [coulomb logarithm](name:coulomb_logarithm).

$$
\ln\Lambda = \ln\left(\frac{b_{\max}}{b_{\min}}\right), \qquad b_{\max} \sim \lambda_D
$$

where $\Lambda$ is the impact-parameter ratio, $b_{\max}$ and $b_{\min}$ are the maximum and minimum effective impact parameters, respectively, and $\lambda_D$ is the Debye screening length; these three quantities are lengths. Debye shielding limits the long-range contribution, while the short-range limit is set by the applicable classical or quantum scattering scale.

This quantity is evaluated locally at the pressure pedestal top and is not a collision frequency, collisionality, or spatially averaged Coulomb logarithm.

NAMES.name: diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short: Diamagnetic component of the electric current density generated by heat-viscosity terms in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure, projected perpendicular to both the magnetic field and poloidal-flux gradient.
NAMES.long:
The diamagnetic heat-viscosity current density is the signed component of the electric current density generated when heat-viscosity terms in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure drive net charge transport.

$$
j_{\mathrm{hv,d}}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{d}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{d}}=\hat{\mathbf{b}}\times\frac{\nabla\psi}{|\nabla\psi|},\qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

Here $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its unit direction, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label. The projection is defined where $\nabla\psi$ is nonzero and excludes the field-aligned component represented by [parallel heat-viscosity current density](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity). It is distinct from diamagnetic current contributions due to parallel or perpendicular viscosity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the heat-viscosity current-density vector points in the direction $\hat{\mathbf{d}}$, with vector products interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short: Diamagnetic component of the electric current density driven by frictional momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles in a partially ionized plasma, projected along the local unit vector parallel to the magnetic field crossed with the ion-pressure gradient. Positive values correspond to current in that direction.
NAMES.long:
Diamagnetic current density due to ion-neutral friction is the component of the ion-neutral-friction current density in the local ion-diamagnetic direction. The local ion-diamagnetic unit vector is directed parallel to $\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_i$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field and $p_i$ is the ion pressure.

The scalar projection is defined by

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia,in}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{dia}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{dia}} = \frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_i}{|\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_i|}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia,in}}$ is this scalar component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the [ion-neutral-friction current density](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), and $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is defined where $\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_i$ is nonzero.

This quantity is a directional projection of the current driven by ion-neutral friction, not the full pressure-gradient diamagnetic current density. It complements the [parallel](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), [radial](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, [poloidal](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, [toroidal](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and [vertical](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame projections of the same parent vector.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion-neutral-friction current density has a positive projection along $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{dia}}$, directed parallel to $\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_i$.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_wall
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Kinetic temperature of the electron population evaluated immediately on the plasma side of a plasma-facing wall surface, distinct from the solid wall’s material temperature.
NAMES.long:
Electron temperature at the wall is the scalar kinetic temperature of electrons in the plasma-side limit adjacent to a plasma-facing wall. It is a population-specific component of [temperature at wall](name:temperature_at_wall), not the temperature of the wall material.

For an isotropic electron velocity distribution, the temperature in energy units is defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_e\rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature and $\langle E_e\rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron, both expressed in energy units. The value applies to the electron population at the plasma-side wall interface and excludes sheath potential energy and solid-material thermal energy. A divertor-specific instance is represented by [electron temperature at divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: electrostatic_potential_at_midplane
NAMES.short: Electrostatic potential at midplane is the voltage-valued scalar potential of the quasineutral plasma evaluated on the equatorial midplane relative to a chosen electrical reference. Its negative spatial gradient defines the local electrostatic field, and it is distinct from near-wall plasma potential and floating potential.
NAMES.long:
Electrostatic potential at midplane is the voltage-valued scalar potential of the quasineutral plasma evaluated on the equatorial midplane of the device. It is the midplane restriction of the plasma [electrostatic_potential](name:electrostatic_potential) relative to a chosen electrical reference.

The midplane value is defined by restricting the electrostatic potential to $Z=0$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
\varphi_{\mathrm{mid}}(R,\phi) = \varphi(R,\phi,Z=0)
$$

where $\varphi$ is the plasma electrostatic potential, $\varphi_{\mathrm{mid}}$ is its midplane value, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The associated electrostatic field is $\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{es}}=-\nabla\varphi$ evaluated on the same locus.

The midplane qualifier specifies a spatial locus, not a material boundary or sheath location. This quantity is distinct from [electrostatic_potential_at_wall](name:electrostatic_potential_at_wall), which is the plasma-side potential adjacent to a plasma-facing surface, and from [floating_electrostatic_potential](name:floating_electrostatic_potential), which is the potential acquired by an electrically isolated surface when the net collected current is zero. Adding a common constant to the potential and to the electrical reference leaves electric fields and potential differences unchanged.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the midplane plasma potential exceeds the chosen electrical reference potential.

sources.enhanced_context: Plasma potential (Vp) measured by a reciprocating Langmuir probe during a plunge. Represents the local electrostatic potential of the plasma in the scrape-off layer or boundary region.
sources.leaf_definition: Plasma potential
sources.parent_definition: Set of plunges of this probe during the pulse, each plunge being recorded as a time slice from the Access Layer point of view. The time child node corresponds to the time of maximum penetration of the probe during a given plunge. The dynamics of physicas quantities within the plunge are described via the time_within_plunge vector.

NAMES.name: electrostatic_potential_at_wall
NAMES.short: Electrostatic potential at wall is the voltage-valued scalar potential of the plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing wall, relative to a chosen electrical reference.
NAMES.long:
Electrostatic potential at wall is the voltage-valued scalar potential of the plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing wall, relative to a chosen electrical reference. It is the wall-local restriction of [electrostatic potential](name:electrostatic_potential).

The electrostatic contribution to the electric field is defined by

$$
\mathbf{E}_{\rm es} = -\nabla \Phi
$$

where $\Phi$ is the electrostatic potential, $\mathbf{E}_{\rm es}$ is the electrostatic electric field, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient.

This quantity refers to the plasma-side potential adjacent to the wall, not the electrical potential of the wall material, an applied wall bias, or the [floating electrostatic potential](name:floating_electrostatic_potential), which is established by a zero-net-current condition. The full electric field may additionally contain an inductive contribution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a positive test charge has greater electrostatic potential energy at the specified location than at the chosen electrical reference.

NAMES.name: gradient_of_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Algebraically signed slope of electron pressure with respect to normalized poloidal magnetic flux, evaluated where its absolute steepness is greatest in the H-mode pedestal.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local electron-pressure slope at the H-mode pedestal location where the magnitude of the slope is greatest. It is distinct from the [electron pressure](name:electron_pressure) itself and from the pressure slope evaluated specifically at the pedestal top.

$$
G_{e,*} = \left.\frac{\partial p_e}{\partial \psi_N}\right|_{\psi_N=\psi_*},\qquad \psi_* = \underset{\psi_N\,\mathrm{in\ the\ pedestal}}{\operatorname{arg\,max}}\left|\frac{\partial p_e}{\partial \psi_N}\right|
$$

Here $p_e$ is electron pressure, $\psi_N$ is the normalized poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate increasing from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary, and $\psi_*$ is the selected pedestal location. The selection is based on absolute steepness, while $G_{e,*}$ retains the algebraic sign; it therefore differs from [derivative with respect to normalized poloidal flux coordinate of electron pressure at pedestal top](name:derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_pressure_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when electron pressure increases toward increasing normalized poloidal magnetic flux.

NAMES.name: ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion current density is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux carried by ions, obtained by charge-weighting their directed particle motion across unit area.
NAMES.long:
Ion current density $\mathbf{J}_i$ is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux carried by ions. It represents signed charge transport from all included ion species and charge states.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the ion distribution functions:

$$
\mathbf{J}_i(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}} q_s \int \mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}} q_s n_s \mathbf{u}_s
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes ion species and charge states, $q_s$ is the charge of population $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is its velocity-space distribution function, $n_s$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{u}_s$ is its mean velocity.

This quantity includes ion-carried charge flux and excludes electron-carried and displacement-current density. Its qualified instances may select a magnetic-field-aligned projection such as [parallel ion current density](name:parallel_ion_current_density), a temporal fluctuation measure such as [fluctuating ion current density](name:fluctuating_ion_current_density), or an ion-saturation collection condition.
NAMES.sign: Positive when an ion-carried charge-flux component is aligned with the positive direction of its defining basis vector or oriented surface normal.

NAMES.name: fluctuating_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Fluctuating ion current density is the temporal standard deviation of ion-carried vector charge transport per unit area about its mean, with charge weighting across included ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Fluctuating ion current density is the temporal spread of the ion-carried contribution to vector charge transport per unit area, evaluated about its temporal mean. It preserves the charge weighting and species and charge-state aggregation of the [ion current density](name:ion_current_density), while describing variation rather than the mean current.

The componentwise temporal standard deviation is defined by

$$
\sigma_{i,k} = \left\langle \left[J_{i,k}(t) - \left\langle J_{i,k}(t) \right\rangle_t\right]^2 \right\rangle_t^{1/2}
$$

where $J_{i,k}(t)$ is component $k$ of the [ion current density](name:ion_current_density) at time $t$, $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes temporal averaging, and $\sigma_{i,k}$ is the corresponding fluctuation amplitude.

The vector is formed from the relevant component or projection standard deviations and is not the signed temporal mean current. For example, [parallel fluctuating ion current density](name:parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density) applies the same fluctuation definition after projection along the local magnetic-field direction, whereas [fluctuating saturated ion current density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density) is restricted to ion-saturation current.

NAMES.name: parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Temporal standard deviation of the total ion charge-current density after projection onto the local magnetic-field direction at a plasma-facing probe.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the temporal standard deviation of the total ion-carried charge-current density after projection onto the local magnetic-field direction at the specified plasma-facing probe. Ion contributions from all included species and charge states are summed with their signed charge weighting before the fluctuation statistic is evaluated. It is the parallel specialization of [fluctuating ion current density](name:fluctuating_ion_current_density).

With $t$ denoting time in seconds, the defining relation is:

$$
\sigma_{j_i,\parallel}=\left\langle\left[j_{i,\parallel}(t)-\left\langle j_{i,\parallel}\right\rangle_t\right]^2\right\rangle_t^{1/2},\qquad j_{i,\parallel}(t)=\mathbf{j}_i(t)\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}(t),\qquad \hat{\mathbf b}(t)=\frac{\mathbf{B}(t)}{|\mathbf{B}(t)|}
$$

Here $\mathbf{j}_i$ is the aggregated ion current-density vector in A m$^{-2}$, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field in tesla, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes the temporal average.

The aggregation and projection precede the standard-deviation operation; this is not a sum of separately calculated species fluctuations. Unlike [fluctuating saturated ion current density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density), it represents the total ion current rather than only the ion-saturation current component. The result is nonnegative even when the underlying parallel current changes sign.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Parallel ion current density is the projection of charge-weighted ion electric-current density onto the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion current density is the magnetic-field-aligned component of the ion contribution to charge transport per unit area. It retains the species and charge-state aggregation of the [ion current density](name:ion_current_density) while selecting only the component along the local magnetic field.

$$
J_{i\parallel} = \mathbf{J}_i \cdot \mathbf{b}, \qquad \mathbf{b} = \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $J_{i\parallel}$ is the parallel ion current density, $\mathbf{J}_i$ is [ion current density](name:ion_current_density), $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector.

This quantity is distinct from [parallel ion particle flux](name:parallel_ion_particle_flux), which counts ion transport without electric-charge weighting. It represents the aggregate ion contribution rather than only a mechanism-specific component such as [parallel current density due to ion inertia](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion current-density vector has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: saturated_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Saturated ion current density is the ion charge flux per collecting area at the ion-saturation limit, when a sufficiently negative bias suppresses electron collection.
NAMES.long:
Saturated ion current density is the ion-carried conventional charge transport per collecting area at the ion-saturation limit of a negatively biased collecting surface. It represents directed ion collection rather than net charge transport at an arbitrary bias.

In a sheath representation, the defining relation is

$$
J_{i,\mathrm{sat}} = \sum_s q_s\,\Gamma_{s,\mathrm{sat}} = \sum_s q_s\,n_{s,\mathrm{se}}\,u_{s,\mathrm{B}}
$$

where $J_{i,\mathrm{sat}}$ is the saturated ion current density, $q_s$ is the charge of ion population $s$, $\Gamma_{s,\mathrm{sat}}$ is its particle flux toward the collecting surface, $n_{s,\mathrm{se}}$ is its sheath-edge number density, and $u_{s,\mathrm{B}}$ is its directed Bohm-entry speed.

The quantity preserves charge weighting over the included ion species and charge states and excludes electron current. It is the saturation-limit specialization of [ion current density](name:ion_current_density), distinct from the area-integrated [saturated ion current](name:saturated_ion_current) and from temporal fluctuations represented by [fluctuating saturated ion current density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when positive ion charge flows toward the collecting surface.

NAMES.name: fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Standard deviation of temporal fluctuations in the ion saturation current density collected by a Langmuir probe biased sufficiently negative to repel all electrons, characterizing the amplitude of turbulent transport at the plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
The fluctuating saturated ion current density is the standard deviation of the time-resolved [saturated_ion_current_density](name:saturated_ion_current_density) — the ion current per unit probe area collected when the probe is biased sufficiently negative to fully repel the electron population. Following the convention of the `fluctuating_` qualifier family established by sibling quantities such as [parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density](name:parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density) and [fluctuating_floating_electrostatic_potential](name:fluctuating_floating_electrostatic_potential), the `fluctuating_` prefix denotes the standard deviation over the measurement interval.

The defining relation is:

$$
\sigma_{j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}} = \left\langle \left( j_{i,\mathrm{sat}} - \langle j_{i,\mathrm{sat}} \rangle \right)^{2} \right\rangle^{1/2}
$$

where $j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}$ is the instantaneous ion saturation current density and $\langle \cdot \rangle$ denotes time averaging over the measurement interval.

This quantity is intrinsically non-negative. It is distinct from the time-mean [saturated_ion_current_density](name:saturated_ion_current_density), which captures the mean ion flux at the probe surface, and from the total collected current [saturated_ion_current](name:saturated_ion_current), which is the area-integrated counterpart.

NAMES.name: magnetic_shear_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Magnetic shear evaluated at the H-mode pedestal top, defined as the normalized logarithmic derivative of the safety factor with respect to normalized toroidal flux radius.
NAMES.long:
Magnetic shear at the pedestal top is the value of [magnetic shear](name:magnetic_shear) at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.

Using the normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ as the radial label, the defining relation is

$$
s_{\mathrm{ped}} = \left.\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}}{q}\frac{dq}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}}\right|_{\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}=\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}}
$$

where $q$ is the safety factor, $\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux radius of the pedestal top, and $s_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the corresponding magnetic shear. This is a point evaluation at the pedestal-top location, distinct from the flux-surface-averaged [magnetic shear at the plasma boundary](name:magnetic_shear_at_plasma_boundary) and from magnetic shear at the magnetic axis.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $q^{-1}dq/d\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is positive as the normalized toroidal flux radius increases outward from the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: magnetic_shear_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Magnetic shear evaluated at the plasma boundary, equal to the normalized logarithmic derivative of the safety factor with respect to normalized toroidal flux radius, flux-surface averaged over the separatrix.
NAMES.long:
Magnetic shear at the plasma boundary is the flux-surface average of [magnetic shear] over the outermost closed flux surface — the separatrix bounding the confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.

Using the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate) $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ as the radial label ($\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = 1$ at the separatrix), the defining relation is

$$
s_{\mathrm{bdy}} = \left\langle \frac{\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}}{q} \frac{dq}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{sep}}
$$

where $q$ is the safety factor and $\langle \cdot \rangle_{\mathrm{sep}}$ denotes the flux-surface average over the separatrix.

This boundary evaluation is distinct from interior counterparts such as [magnetic_shear_at_pedestal_top](name:magnetic_shear_at_pedestal_top) and [magnetic_shear_at_magnetic_axis](name:magnetic_shear_at_magnetic_axis), which are evaluated on flux surfaces interior to the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $q^{-1}dq/d\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is positive as $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ increases outward at the separatrix.

NAMES.name: momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short: Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction unchanged.
NAMES.long:
In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive closures can produce momentum-flux densities that exceed the physically realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient regions such as the scrape-off layer and divertor. A flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_m$ is introduced to bound the effective flux: the limited momentum-flux density magnitude cannot exceed $\alpha_m$ times a free-streaming reference scale, while the sign follows the underlying diffusive flux direction.

The limited momentum-flux density $\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is formed by the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux estimate, $\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} = m n v_{\mathrm{th}}^2$ is the free-streaming scale with $m$ the particle mass, $n$ the number density, and $v_{\mathrm{th}}$ the thermal speed. When $|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$; when $|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| \ll \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

Specializations target individual projection directions, such as parallel_momentum_coefficient for field-aligned transport, and individual particle populations, such as ion_state_momentum_coefficient for specific ion charge states or parallel_neutral_state_momentum_coefficient for neutral-particle parallel transport. The coefficient is intrinsically non-negative; values in the range 0.1–1 are common in edge-plasma simulations, selected by calibration against experimental separatrix and divertor data.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming bound component-by-component, capping flux magnitude while preserving its sign.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for gradient-driven momentum transport, providing one limiter factor for each selected spatial transport component. It is the ion specialization of [momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), scaling the collisionless free-streaming bound while preserving the direction supplied by the underlying diffusive closure.

For each selected component, the limited momentum-flux density is defined by the harmonic-mean closure:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\alpha_m$ is the momentum-flux limiter coefficient, $\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming reference momentum-flux density, $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux estimate, and $\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the resulting limited flux density.

The shared quantity spans parallel, poloidal, and radial ion components; [parallel ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and [poloidal ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) are concrete instances. It applies to momentum flux rather than particle, heat, or energy flux, and the coefficient is non-negative.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated limited momentum-flux density points along the selected positive transport direction: along the magnetic field for parallel transport, along increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ for poloidal transport, or toward increasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame for radial transport; the coefficient does not reverse that direction.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Dimensionless vector flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density component-by-component in edge-plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The neutral momentum coefficient is the neutral-particle specialization of the general momentum_coefficient vector, providing one dimensionless limiter factor per spatial direction for neutral momentum transport in multi-fluid edge plasma models. Each directional component independently bounds the corresponding neutral momentum flux density, preventing unphysical exceedance of the free-streaming limit when the neutral mean free path is large relative to macroscopic gradient scales.

The component $\alpha_\alpha$ in direction $\hat{e}_\alpha$ is defined as the ratio of the modeled flux to its free-streaming upper bound:

$$
\alpha_\alpha = \frac{\Pi_\alpha}{\Pi_\alpha^{\rm free}}
$$

where $\Pi_\alpha$ is the modeled neutral momentum flux density in direction $\hat{e}_\alpha$ and $\Pi_\alpha^{\rm free} = m_n n_n u_\alpha^{\rm free}$ is the free-streaming estimate, with $m_n$ the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ the neutral number density, and $u_\alpha^{\rm free}$ the direction-$\alpha$ free-streaming reference speed. The constraint $\alpha_\alpha \in [0, 1]$ ensures the closure preserves the sign of the momentum flux while bounding its magnitude. The field-aligned component is analogous to parallel_neutral_state_momentum_coefficient, which resolves the same quantity by internal neutral state.

Components are computed within edge-plasma transport closures as a function of local collisionality; values near 1 characterize the collision-dominated limit, while values near 0 indicate strongly free-streaming conditions where the limiter actively constrains the flux.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral momentum flux in the corresponding direction is in the same sense as the free-streaming estimate along the respective axis of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame or along the magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the dimensionless ion momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming bound on parallel ion momentum-flux density.
NAMES.long:
The parallel component of the dimensionless ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient scales the free-streaming upper bound imposed on ion momentum-flux density along the local magnetic-field direction. It is the parallel member of the vector quantity [ion momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

The limiting relation is

$$
\left|\Pi_{\parallel,i}\right| \leq C_{\parallel,i}\,\Pi_{\parallel,\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $C_{\parallel,i}$ is this dimensionless coefficient, $\Pi_{\parallel,i}$ is the signed parallel ion momentum-flux density, and $\Pi_{\parallel,\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming bound; the two flux densities have pressure-equivalent units. The coefficient applies to the parallel direction and is distinct from the [radial ion momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:radial_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and from charge-state-resolved parallel coefficients.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated parallel ion momentum flux is co-directed with the local magnetic-field vector.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Dimensionless parallel momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density in edge-plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient is the parallel component of the neutral-particle specialization of the general momentum flux-limiter coefficient vector, providing the dimensionless limiter factor for neutral momentum transport along the magnetic-field direction. It bounds the field-aligned neutral momentum-flux density so that the modeled flux does not exceed the free-streaming momentum-flux-density scale when the neutral mean free path is large relative to macroscopic gradient scales.

The coefficient $\alpha_\parallel$ along the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$ is defined as the ratio of the magnitude of the modeled field-aligned neutral momentum-flux density to its free-streaming upper bound:

$$
\alpha_\parallel = \frac{|\Pi_\parallel|}{\Pi_\parallel^{\rm free}},\qquad \Pi_\parallel^{\rm free} = m_n n_n \left(u_\parallel^{\rm free}\right)^2
$$

where $\Pi_\parallel$ is the modeled neutral momentum-flux density component along $\hat{b}$, $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the [neutral number density], and $u_\parallel^{\rm free}$ is the characteristic collisionless neutral speed projected along $\hat{b}$ for the same neutral population. The constraint $\alpha_\parallel \in [0,1]$ makes $\Pi_\parallel^{\rm free}$ an upper bound on $|\Pi_\parallel|$; the sign of the momentum flux is carried by $\Pi_\parallel$, not by the limiter coefficient.

This coefficient is field-aligned and is distinct from the [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and [vertical](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) components, which apply to fixed directions in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is also distinct from the [parallel neutral internal-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which assigns separate parallel limiter factors to individual neutral internal states.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the dimensionless ion momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming bound on poloidal ion momentum-flux density.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the dimensionless ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient scales the free-streaming upper bound imposed on ion momentum-flux density in the local poloidal direction. It is the poloidal member of the vector quantity [ion momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), with the poloidal direction tangent to a magnetic flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The limiting relation is

$$
\left|\Pi_{\theta,i}\right| \leq C_{\theta,i}\,\Pi_{\theta,\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $C_{\theta,i}$ is this coefficient, $\Pi_{\theta,i}$ is the signed poloidal ion momentum-flux density, and $\Pi_{\theta,\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative poloidal free-streaming bound.

The coefficient is nonnegative and applies to ion momentum-flux density summed over charge states. It is distinct from the charge-state-resolved [poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated signed poloidal momentum-flux density points in the positive local poloidal direction.

NAMES.name: poloidal_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short: Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on poloidal momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction unchanged. It is the momentum-specific poloidal flux limiter, not a particle-, heat-, or energy-flux limiter.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for gradient-driven momentum transport in the poloidal tangent direction associated with increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$ in a specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, embedded in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$. Here $\rho$ is a flux-surface label, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. It scales the collisionless free-streaming bound used to limit modeled poloidal momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures; the associated signed flux component is positive for transport toward increasing $\theta$.

The coefficient defines the upper bound enforced on the limited poloidal momentum-flux density:

$$
|\Pi_\theta^{\mathrm{lim}}| \le \alpha_\theta \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\Pi_\theta^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the signed limited poloidal momentum-flux density, $\alpha_\theta$ is the poloidal momentum coefficient, and $\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the positive collisionless free-streaming momentum-flux reference scale for the transported particle population. For an underlying collisional diffusive estimate $\Pi_\theta^{\mathrm{diff}}$, the limiter changes magnitude only as needed to satisfy the bound and leaves the sign direction of the flux set by $\Pi_\theta^{\mathrm{diff}}$.

This quantity is the poloidal specialization of [momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). The shorter [poloidal flux limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient) is conceptually identical only when its limited quantity is the poloidal momentum-flux density; the momentum qualifier here excludes limiters for particle, heat, energy, or current flux. The coefficient is non-negative; reversal of poloidal transport is represented by the sign of the limited momentum-flux density, not by a negative coefficient.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Radial component of the dimensionless ion momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming bound on radial ion momentum-flux density.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the dimensionless ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient scales the free-streaming upper bound imposed on ion momentum-flux density in the cylindrical radial direction. It is the radial member of the vector quantity [ion momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), with radial referring to the $\hat{R}$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The limiting relation is

$$
\left|\Pi_{R,i}\right| \leq C_{R,i}\,\Pi_{R,\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $C_{R,i}$ is this coefficient, $\Pi_{R,i}$ is the signed radial ion momentum-flux density, and $\Pi_{R,\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative radial free-streaming bound; the two flux densities have the same pressure-equivalent units.

As a magnitude-limiter coefficient, $C_{R,i}$ is nonnegative and has no independent sign; the sign of any limited radial ion momentum flux is inherited from the associated signed momentum-flux density. The ion-level coefficient applies to charge-state-summed radial ion momentum-flux density and is distinct from the [parallel ion momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), the [poloidal ion momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), and the charge-state-resolved [ion charge-state momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

NAMES.name: radial_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short: Dimensionless momentum-flux-density limiter that scales the collisionless free-streaming bound for gradient-driven radial momentum transport in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It caps the modeled radial momentum-flux density while leaving its direction set by the underlying transport closure.
NAMES.long:
The radial momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for gradient-driven momentum transport in the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It scales the collisionless free-streaming bound used to limit the modeled radial momentum-flux density without determining whether the flux is inward or outward.

The bound imposed by the coefficient is:

$$
|\Pi_R^{\mathrm{lim}}| \le C_R \, \Pi_R^{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $C_R$ is the radial momentum coefficient, $\Pi_R^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited radial momentum-flux density, and $\Pi_R^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the non-negative collisionless free-streaming reference scale; both $\Pi_R^{\mathrm{lim}}$ and $\Pi_R^{\mathrm{FS}}$ are expressed in pascals.

This coefficient specifies only the multiplier on the free-streaming bound; the algebraic limiter used to approach the bound is a separate transport-closure choice. It is the radial-direction specialization of [momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and the component-family counterpart of [poloidal_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:poloidal_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). Here radial means projection onto $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, not projection along the normal to a magnetic flux surface; any inward or outward sign belongs to the limited momentum-flux density, not to the coefficient.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Dimensionless toroidal momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density in edge-plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient is the toroidal component of the neutral-particle specialization of the general momentum flux-limiter coefficient vector, providing the dimensionless limiter factor for neutral momentum transport along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It bounds the toroidal neutral momentum-flux density, preventing unphysical exceedance of the free-streaming upper limit when the neutral mean free path is large relative to macroscopic gradient scales.

The toroidal component $\alpha_\phi$ is defined as the nonnegative limiter multiplying the positive free-streaming upper bound on the magnitude of the toroidal neutral momentum-flux density:

$$
|\Pi_\phi| \le \alpha_\phi \, \Pi_{\phi,\max}^{\rm free}, \qquad 0 \le \alpha_\phi \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_\phi$ is the modeled toroidal neutral momentum-flux density and $\Pi_{\phi,\max}^{\rm free}$ is the free-streaming upper bound for the magnitude of the same component.

This coefficient applies to neutral-particle momentum aggregated over internal neutral states. It is the toroidal projection of the [neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), distinct from the [parallel neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), the [vertical neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), and the [toroidal neutral internal-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). The coefficient limits only the magnitude of the $\hat{\phi}$ component and does not define the direction of the momentum flux itself.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Dimensionless vertical momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density in edge-plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The vertical neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient is the vertical component of the neutral-particle specialization of the general momentum flux-limiter coefficient vector, providing the dimensionless limiter factor for neutral momentum transport along the vertical $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame in multi-fluid edge-plasma models. It bounds the vertical neutral momentum-flux density by the free-streaming limit when the neutral mean free path is large relative to macroscopic gradient scales.

The vertical component $\alpha_Z$ is defined as the ratio of the magnitude of the modeled vertical neutral momentum-flux density to its positive free-streaming upper bound:

$$
\alpha_Z = \frac{|\Pi_Z|}{\Pi_Z^{\rm free}}, \qquad \Pi_Z^{\rm free} = m_n n_n \left(u_Z^{\rm free}\right)^2
$$

where $\Pi_Z$ is the modeled vertical neutral momentum-flux density component along $\hat{Z}$, $\Pi_Z^{\rm free}$ is the corresponding free-streaming upper bound, $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number density, and $u_Z^{\rm free}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming reference speed for neutral motion along $\hat{Z}$. The constraint $\alpha_Z \in [0, 1]$ makes the coefficient a magnitude limiter; any sign of the vertical momentum flux is carried by $\Pi_Z$, not by $\alpha_Z$.

This quantity is the vertical member of the [neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) vector and is distinct from the [parallel neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which is taken along the magnetic-field direction, and the [toroidal neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which is taken along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is a limiter coefficient, not the neutral momentum-flux density itself.

NAMES.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal
NAMES.short: Radial flux-surface location of the H-mode pedestal or edge transport barrier, expressed by the normalized poloidal flux coordinate.
NAMES.long:
The normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal is the value of the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate) $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}$ on the closed flux surface that contains the characteristic radial location of the H-mode pedestal, also called the edge transport barrier. It locates the pedestal between the magnetic axis and the last closed flux surface using the same flux-surface label as the parent coordinate.

The pedestal value of the coordinate is defined by evaluating the normalized poloidal flux coordinate at the pedestal flux surface:

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm,ped}} = \sqrt{\frac{\psi_{\mathrm{ped}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux on the pedestal flux surface, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the value at the magnetic axis, and $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the value at the last closed flux surface. For a pedestal flux surface inside the last closed flux surface, the coordinate lies between zero at the magnetic axis and one at the last closed flux surface.

This quantity denotes the flux-coordinate location of the pedestal as a whole; it is not specifically the pedestal top, pedestal foot, or maximum-gradient locus unless that locus is part of the pedestal definition being used. It is distinct from [normalized poloidal magnetic flux at pedestal top](name:normalized_poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top), which refers specifically to the pedestal-top locus and uses the unsquare-rooted normalized poloidal magnetic flux rather than $\rho_{\mathrm{pol,norm}}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the electric current density generated by heat-viscosity terms in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure, projected along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
The parallel heat-viscosity current density is the field-aligned component of the electric current density generated when heat-viscosity terms in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure drive net charge transport. It is the parallel projection of the parent [heat-viscosity current density](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity).

The defining projection is

$$
j_{\mathrm{hv},\parallel}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}\cdot\mathbf{b}, \qquad \mathbf{b}=\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the heat-viscosity current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\mathbf{b}$ is the corresponding unit vector.

This quantity includes only the heat-viscosity mechanism and field-aligned projection; [parallel current density due to parallel viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) represents a distinct viscosity contribution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the heat-viscosity current density points along the local magnetic-field direction $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_diamagnetic_current_density
NAMES.short: Field-aligned component of the diamagnetic current density, projected onto the local magnetic field direction in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The parallel diamagnetic current density is the projection of the total [diamagnetic_current_density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) onto the local magnetic field direction at each point in the edge plasma. The diamagnetic current arises from the gyration of magnetized particles in a pressure-gradient field; in an isotropic ideal plasma, $\mathbf{j}_\mathrm{dia} = (\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p)/B^2$ is purely perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$, so its parallel component vanishes in that limit. In more complete descriptions including pressure anisotropy, finite Larmor radius corrections, or the inhomogeneous magnetic geometry of the tokamak edge, a field-aligned component emerges and must be tracked separately.

The parallel projection is defined as:

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}} = \mathbf{j}_\mathrm{dia} \cdot \hat{b}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_\mathrm{dia}$ is the diamagnetic current density vector and $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field of magnitude $B$.

In edge plasma current decompositions, this component is closely related to [parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which encodes the same physical mechanism through the explicit drift formalism. The toroidal_diamagnetic_current_density provides the complementary geometric projection of the same vector field onto the toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current flows in the direction of the local magnetic field unit vector $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/B$.

NAMES.name: parallel_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.short: Fickian diffusivity for neutral thermal-energy transport along magnetic field lines, relating the parallel diffusive energy flux to the parallel gradient of neutral thermal-energy density.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral energy diffusivity is the effective scalar transport coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of neutral thermal-energy density along magnetic field lines. It represents the Fickian part of neutral energy transport, distinct from particle diffusion, bulk-flow convection, and explicitly nonlocal kinetic transport.

The defining closure for the parallel diffusive energy flux is:

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,\parallel} = -\chi_{E,\parallel}\,\hat{\mathbf{b}}\left(\hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\nabla w_n\right)
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,\parallel}$ is the parallel diffusive thermal-energy flux, $\chi_{E,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral energy diffusivity, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector tangent to magnetic field lines, and $w_n$ is neutral thermal-energy density. The negative sign specifies down-gradient transport. This coefficient acts on energy density rather than the particle density governed by [neutral_diffusivity](name:neutral_diffusivity); when neutral internal states are resolved, it is distinct from [parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity) and is a directional component of [energy_diffusivity](name:energy_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Parallel ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for a specified ionization state along magnetic-field lines.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state along the magnetic-field direction. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the field-aligned diffusive particle flux of that charge state to the negative field-aligned gradient of its number density.

For the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}$, the defining Fickian relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,\parallel} = -D_{s,\parallel}\,\nabla_\parallel n_s
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,\parallel}$ is the diffusive particle-flux density projected along $\hat{\mathbf b}$, $D_{s,\parallel}$ is this parallel diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of ionization state $s$, and $\nabla_\parallel n_s = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\nabla n_s$ is its field-aligned gradient.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and excludes cross-field diffusion, convective or pinch transport, particle sources and sinks, and energy or momentum transport. It is the parallel directional counterpart of [ion charge-state diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity), distinct from [radial ion charge-state diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity); [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) denotes the same Fickian coefficient when that convention is used.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Parallel ion charge-state momentum source is the parallel projection of the area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It represents momentum transfer along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum source is the parallel projection of the area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It represents directional momentum transfer to or from that charge state resolved along the local magnetic-field direction, rather than summed over charge states.

The parallel projection is defined by projecting the momentum-source vector for that charge state onto the local magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
S_{\parallel,i,Z} = \mathbf{S}_{i,Z} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i,Z}$ is the area-normalized momentum-source vector acting on ion species $i$ in charge state $Z$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.

This quantity is distinct from the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source) and the [toroidal ion charge-state momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), which use poloidal and toroidal projections of the same charge-state-resolved momentum source.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the momentum-source vector acting on the charge state has a component in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, the local magnetic-field unit vector.
