NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel flux-limiter coefficient that sets a nonnegative cap on the field-aligned neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a specified internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming bound, without reversing the signed component.
NAMES.long:
Parallel flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles occupying a specified internal state is the directional coefficient used to bound the component of the corresponding neutral internal-state momentum-flux density parallel to the magnetic field. The internal state may be an electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation state, and this scalar coefficient applies to the field-aligned projection rather than to the poloidal or toroidal projection.

For the parallel component, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\parallel}| \le \lambda_{\parallel}\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\parallel}|,\qquad 0 \le \lambda_{\parallel} \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\parallel}$ is the limited component of the neutral internal-state momentum-flux density parallel to the magnetic field, $\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\parallel}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming component whose magnitude defines the bound, and $\lambda_{\parallel}$ is this coefficient.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the realized momentum-flux density. Because $\lambda_{\parallel}$ is nonnegative, applying the limiter may reduce or bound a signed parallel momentum-flux component but does not reverse its direction; a nonzero limited component retains the sign of the underlying field-aligned component to which the cap is applied. This scalar coefficient is the field-aligned member of the [neutral internal-state momentum-flux limiter coefficient over the edge region](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region) and is distinct from the [poloidal](name:poloidal_momentum_neutral_internal_state_flux_limiter_coefficient) and [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) directional members.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states. Its sign distinguishes momentum transfer along and opposite to the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
The parallel component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states, is the net neutral momentum transfer per unit area resolved along the local magnetic-field direction. It is one component of the aggregate [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source) acting in the neutral momentum balance.

The parallel component is defined by projecting the parent source vector onto the magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
S_{n,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{S}_n \cdot \hat{b}
$$

where $S_{n,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral momentum source, $\boldsymbol{S}_n$ is the area-normalized neutral momentum source vector, and $\hat{b}$ is the unit vector in the local magnetic-field direction.

The quantity is summed over all neutral states and excludes ion momentum sources. Unlike the [radial neutral momentum source](name:radial_neutral_momentum_source), [poloidal neutral momentum source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source), and [toroidal neutral momentum source](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_source), it resolves momentum transfer along the magnetic-field direction rather than along a geometric direction such as $\hat{R}$, a poloidal direction, or $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral momentum source points in the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.short: Vector of directional diffusion coefficients governing diffusive transport of plasma momentum aggregated over all ion species and charge states, forming the diagonal of the bulk ion-fluid momentum diffusivity tensor.
NAMES.long:
The plasma momentum diffusion coefficient vector collects the anisotropic directional components of the bulk plasma momentum diffusivity, each relating the diffusive flux of ion-fluid momentum along a given geometric direction to the local flow-velocity gradient. By summing over all ion species and charge states, it characterizes the ion fluid as a composite transport medium; the radial cross-field projection is the most directly accessible component, as attested by [radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).

The defining Fickian relation for the diffusive momentum flux density along direction $i$ is

$$
\Pi_i^{\rm diff} = -\rho \, D_i^{\rm plasma} \, \frac{\partial u_i}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\rho$ is the local ion-fluid mass density in kg m$^{-3}$, $u_i$ is the fluid velocity component along direction $i$, and $D_i^{\rm plasma}$ is the plasma momentum diffusion coefficient in that direction.

Magnetized plasmas are strongly anisotropic: cross-field components are suppressed by Lorentz-force confinement, while the field-aligned component — exemplified by [parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity) — can exceed cross-field values by several orders of magnitude. In edge and divertor regions, turbulent and neoclassical processes set the effective cross-field diffusivities, which are inferred from momentum-balance analysis of measured toroidal or poloidal flow profiles. This quantity is the plasma-species member of the [momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) family; species-resolved variants resolve transport per ion population, while neutral-particle analogs account for the charge-exchange coupling that transfers momentum between ions and neutrals in the edge.

NAMES.name: radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.short: Effective kinematic coefficient governing down-gradient transport of bulk plasma momentum along R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height. Bulk plasma momentum is ion-fluid momentum summed over all ion species and charge states; electron inertial momentum is excluded.
NAMES.long:
The radial plasma momentum diffusion coefficient is the effective kinematic coefficient governing down-gradient transport of bulk plasma momentum along $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. The radial direction specifies the transport direction, not the component of momentum being transported.

In a Fickian closure, the coefficient is defined component-wise by the relation between radial diffusive momentum flux and the major-radius gradient of the corresponding momentum density:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\mathcal{P}_j,R} = -D_{\mathcal{P},R}\,\frac{\partial \mathcal{P}_j}{\partial R}
$$

where $D_{\mathcal{P},R}$ is the radial plasma momentum diffusion coefficient, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\mathcal{P}_j,R}$ is the diffusive flux of the $j$-th component of bulk plasma momentum through a surface of constant $R$ and is positive in the $+\hat{R}$ direction, $\mathcal{P}_j$ is the bulk plasma momentum density component, and $j$ denotes any chosen momentum-vector component. The derivative is taken with respect to $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The leading minus sign fixes the down-gradient diffusion convention: a positive $D_{\mathcal{P},R}$ transports each component from larger toward smaller $\mathcal{P}_j$ along $R$.

Bulk plasma momentum density means the charge-state-summed ion-fluid momentum density, $\mathcal{P}_j = \sum_{a,z} m_a n_{a,z} u_{a,z,j}$, where $a$ indexes ion species, $z$ indexes charge state, $m_a$ is ion mass, $n_{a,z}$ is ion number density, and $u_{a,z,j}$ is the corresponding ion fluid-velocity component. Electron inertial momentum and neutral momentum are excluded.

This quantity is the $R$-directed member of the bulk plasma-momentum diffusion-coefficient family anchored by [plasma momentum diffusion coefficient](name:plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), with the $Z$-directed counterpart [vertical plasma-momentum transport coefficient](name:vertical_plasma_momentum_diffusivity). It is distinct from a flux-surface-normal momentum-transport coefficient such as [radial momentum transport coefficient](name:radial_momentum_diffusivity), from the charge-state-resolved [radial ion charge-state momentum transport coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), and from the neutral-fluid analog [radial neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). In an anisotropic tensor representation, it corresponds to a radial diagonal transport coefficient; related ion-momentum tensor-family quantities include [ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and the toroidal diagonal component [toroidal ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: plasma_momentum_flux
NAMES.short: Rate of transport of linear momentum per unit area across an oriented surface, summed over charged plasma populations and excluding neutral transport.
NAMES.long:
The plasma momentum flux describes the rate at which charged plasma populations transport linear momentum through a unit area of an oriented surface. It includes convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or turbulent-stress contributions.

$$
\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pl}} = \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}, \qquad \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}} = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{charged}}\left(\rho_s\mathbf{v}_s\mathbf{v}_s + p_s\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_s\right)
$$

Here, $\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the momentum-flux vector, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the charged-plasma momentum-flux tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the oriented unit surface normal. The sum covers charged species $s$; $\rho_s$ is mass density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ bulk velocity, $p_s$ scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ the viscous or turbulent stress tensor.

This charged-plasma specialization belongs to the broader [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) family and excludes the neutral contribution represented by [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux). Its field-aligned projection is [parallel plasma momentum flux](name:parallel_plasma_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when momentum transport across the surface is directed along the chosen surface normal.

NAMES.name: parallel_plasma_momentum_flux
NAMES.short: Scalar obtained by projecting the charged-plasma momentum-flux tensor onto the local magnetic-field direction for both transported momentum and flux direction. It includes advective, isotropic-pressure, and parallel stress contributions.
NAMES.long:
Parallel plasma momentum flux is the flux density of plasma momentum carried in the local magnetic-field direction, with the transported momentum and flux direction both projected parallel to the field. It is the parallel scalar component of the parent [plasma momentum flux](name:plasma_momentum_flux).

$$
\Pi_{\parallel}=\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{\Pi}\cdot\mathbf{b},\qquad \mathbf{b}=\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

Here $\Pi_{\parallel}$ is the parallel momentum flux, $\mathbf{\Pi}$ is the charged-plasma momentum-flux tensor, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $\mathbf{b}$ is its unit direction. The tensor includes bulk-flow transport, isotropic pressure, and viscous or other anisotropic stress. This quantity includes the charged plasma as a whole and excludes neutral momentum; [parallel ion momentum flux](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux) is its ion-only counterpart.

NAMES.name: plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: The plasma velocity due to diamagnetic drift is a signed scalar component of the bulk-plasma diamagnetic drift velocity, obtained by projecting the mass-weighted pressure-gradient-driven species drifts onto a specified positive component direction.
NAMES.long:
The plasma velocity due to diamagnetic drift is a signed scalar component of the pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular drift of the bulk plasma. It is the projection of the mass-weighted charged-species center-of-mass diamagnetic-drift velocity, not a direction-free speed and not a charge-weighted diamagnetic-current quantity.

The defining scalar projection of the [bulk-plasma diamagnetic-drift velocity](name:bulk_plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) onto the specified unit direction $\hat{e}$ is:

$$
v_{\ast,\mathrm{plasma},\hat{e}} = \hat{e}\cdot\mathbf{v}_{\ast,\mathrm{plasma}} = \hat{e}\cdot\frac{\sum_s m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_{\ast s}}{\sum_s m_s n_s}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\ast,\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the bulk-plasma diamagnetic-drift velocity, $s$ indexes charged plasma species, $m_s$ is species mass, $n_s$ is number density, and $\mathbf{v}_{\ast s}$ is the species diamagnetic-drift velocity. For a charged species, $\mathbf{v}_{\ast s} = -\nabla p_s \times \mathbf{B}/(q_s n_s B^2)$, where $p_s$ is species partial pressure, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, and $q_s$ is signed species charge.

The mass weighting makes this a bulk-plasma flow component; it is distinct from the signed bulk component along the local diamagnetic direction, [diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and from the corresponding direction-free magnitude, [bulk_plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift_magnitude](name:bulk_plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift_magnitude).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the bulk-plasma diamagnetic-drift velocity has a component in the positive sense of the specified unit direction $\hat{e}$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the current density arising from heat-viscosity terms in a collisional edge-plasma closure.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density due to heat viscosity is the component of the heat-viscosity current density tangent to a flux surface in the poloidal direction of the flux coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. It isolates the part of the electric current density attributed to heat-flux-related viscous stress terms in a collisional edge-fluid closure.

The component is defined by projecting the heat-viscosity current density onto the poloidal unit direction:

$$
j_{\theta}^{\mathrm{hv}} = \mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}
$$

where $j_{\theta}^{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the poloidal component in A m$^{-2}$, $\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the heat-viscosity current-density vector in A m$^{-2}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is the dimensionless unit vector in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

In edge-fluid models, $\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{hv}}$ is usually a closure-derived contribution rather than a directly measured diagnostic quantity. It is associated with the divergence of a heat-flux-dependent viscous stress tensor, commonly represented at the species level by $\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{hv}}_s$ in momentum balance, where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{hv}}_s$ is a stress tensor and its divergence is a force density. The exact constitutive coefficients, species weighting, and metric factors depend on the collisional closure and on the chosen flux coordinates.

No universal numerical range is intrinsic to this term. Reported magnitudes should be interpreted relative to the total current density and to related viscosity-driven components; the value can be zero when the heat-viscosity closure is not included and can vary strongly with edge gradients, collisionality, magnetic geometry, and plasma regime.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the heat-viscosity current density points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the electric current density driven by frictional momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles in a partially ionized plasma, resolved along increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density due to ion-neutral friction is the poloidal projection of [current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), produced by collisional momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral atoms or molecules. It is resolved along increasing poloidal angle on a surface of constant rho in flux coordinates (rho, theta, phi), and is distinct from [poloidal_current_density_due_to_collisions](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_collisions), which has a broader collision attribution.

The defining projection is

$$
j_{\mathrm{in},\theta} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{in},\theta}$ is the poloidal component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the full ion-neutral-friction current-density vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is the unit vector tangent to the flux surface in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

Only the contribution attributable to ion-neutral friction is included; contributions from other collisional processes are excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion-neutral-friction current points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the current density generated by perpendicular viscous stress, directed along increasing poloidal angle on a labeled magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the poloidal projection of the current-density contribution generated by the divergence of the perpendicular viscous stress tensor in a magnetized plasma. It represents the component tangent to a magnetic flux surface in the poloidal plane.

$$
J_{\pi_\perp,\theta}=\mathbf{J}_{\pi_\perp}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta=\frac{\left[\mathbf{B}\times(\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\pi}_\perp)\right]\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta}{B^2}
$$

Here $\mathbf{J}_{\pi_\perp}$ is the perpendicular-viscosity current-density contribution, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $\boldsymbol{\pi}_\perp$ is the perpendicular viscous stress tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ is the unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. The component is resolved in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This component is one projection of [current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity) and is distinct from the toroidal projection [toroidal current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity). It is also the perpendicular-viscosity contribution to [poloidal current density due to viscosity](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_viscosity), which includes other viscous mechanisms.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current-density projection points toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Directional electron particle diffusion coefficient linking the poloidal diffusive electron flux to the electron density gradient in a magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron diffusivity is an effective scalar transport coefficient for diffusive electron-particle transport along the poloidal direction of flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The constitutive relation is

$$
\Gamma_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,\theta}\,\nabla_\theta n_e
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal component of the diffusive electron particle-flux vector, $D_{e,\theta}$ is the poloidal electron diffusivity, $\nabla_\theta n_e$ is the metric-scaled electron-density gradient along increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, and $n_e$ is electron number density. The associated flux component is positive toward increasing $\theta$.

This is the poloidal projection of the anisotropic transport represented by [electron diffusivity](name:electron_diffusivity). It describes diffusive transport only and excludes convective fluxes, particle sources, and sinks; [poloidal particle diffusivity](name:poloidal_particle_diffusivity) is the corresponding species-independent quantity.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Effective Fickian diffusivity for electron thermal energy transport in the poloidal direction on magnetic flux surfaces, multiplying the electron-temperature gradient to give the conductive electron heat flux.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron energy diffusivity, usually denoted $\chi_{e,\theta}$, is the effective Fickian transport coefficient for conductive transport of electron thermal energy in the poloidal direction on a magnetic flux surface. It represents the part of the electron heat-flux closure driven by the poloidal electron-temperature gradient, distinct from convective transport of electron energy by a pinch or flow velocity.

For flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, with $\rho$ increasing from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary, $\theta$ a chosen poloidal angle, and $\phi$ the toroidal angle of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, the conductive poloidal heat-flux projection is commonly written as:

$$
q_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{cond}} = -\chi_{e,\theta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta \cdot \nabla T_e
$$

where $q_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive electron heat-flux projection along $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the unit vector tangent to increasing $\theta$ on a surface of constant $\rho$, $\chi_{e,\theta}$ is the poloidal electron energy diffusivity, and $T_e$ is the electron temperature expressed as the energy variable used in the electron energy equation. The minus sign sets the diffusive direction: a positive electron-temperature gradient along increasing $\theta$ gives a negative heat-flux projection, so conductive transport is toward lower electron temperature.

This quantity is the poloidal member of [electron_energy_diffusivity](name:electron_energy_diffusivity) and is distinct from [parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity](name:parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity). It is a scalar diagonal Fickian coefficient; density factors, heat-capacity factors, metric factors, nonlocal terms, off-diagonal transport, and advective transport are separate elements of a transport closure rather than part of this coefficient.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the poloidal Fickian diffusivity for thermal-energy transport of a specified ion charge state in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ), defined so the diffusive energy flux along increasing poloidal angle θ at fixed radial flux label ρ and toroidal angle φ is proportional to and opposite the corresponding gradient of that state's thermal-energy density.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of the thermal-energy density of one specified ion charge state along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It represents the Fickian part of that charge state's thermal-energy transport along the poloidal coordinate direction, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources, and is the poloidal component of [ion charge-state energy diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity).

The defining closure for the poloidal component is

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,z}\cdot\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}} = -\chi_{E,z}^{\mathrm{pol}}\,\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}\cdot\nabla w_z
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,z}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux density of ion charge state $z$, $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local unit tangent generated by increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed radial flux label $\rho$ and fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, $\chi_{E,z}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity, $w_z$ is the thermal-energy density of that charge state, and $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}\cdot\nabla w_z$ is the corresponding poloidal gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over ion species or charge states, unlike [poloidal ion energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusivity). The field-aligned directional counterpart is [parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity). A temperature-gradient form is equivalent only when the relevant density and heat-capacity factors are explicitly included in the coefficient.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Fickian diffusivity for poloidal thermal-energy transport of the ion population, defining the down-gradient part of ion energy flux tangent to increasing θ at fixed ρ and φ in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion energy diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of ion thermal-energy density in the poloidal direction. The poloidal direction is the tangent to increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed radial flux label $\rho$ and toroidal angle $\phi$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. It represents the Fickian part of ion energy transport, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources or sinks.

The defining closure relates the physical diffusive ion thermal-energy flux component along the poloidal tangent to the metric poloidal gradient of ion thermal-energy density:

$$
q_{\theta,E,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{\theta,E,i}\,\nabla_\theta w_i = -\chi_{\theta,E,i}\,\frac{1}{h_\theta}\left(\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial\theta}\right)_{\rho,\phi}
$$

where $q_{\theta,E,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux component in the direction of increasing $\theta$, $\chi_{\theta,E,i}$ is poloidal ion energy diffusivity, $w_i$ is ion thermal-energy density, $\nabla_\theta w_i$ is the metric poloidal gradient, and $h_\theta=|\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial\theta|_{\rho,\phi}$ is the poloidal metric scale factor for the position vector $\mathbf{x}(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. The minus sign specifies that positive $\chi_{\theta,E,i}$ gives down-gradient transport along poloidal arclength.

For an unresolved ion population, $w_i$ and $q_{\theta,E,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ denote quantities summed over the included ion species and charge states before the effective coefficient is applied; the coefficient is not the arithmetic sum of charge-state diffusivities. Charge-state-resolved quantities such as [poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity) retain that resolution. This quantity is the poloidal directional form of [ion energy diffusivity](name:ion_energy_diffusivity) and is distinct from field-aligned [parallel ion energy diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusivity), from [poloidal ion diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_diffusivity) for particle transport, and from [poloidal ion momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity) for momentum transport.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Diffusion coefficient relating the diffusive poloidal ion momentum flux to the local poloidal ion momentum density gradient, expressing the rate at which diffusive processes redistribute poloidal momentum within the total ion population summed over charge states.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion momentum diffusivity $D_{\rm pol}^i$ is the effective diffusion coefficient characterizing down-gradient redistribution of the poloidal component of momentum within the total ion population summed over all charge states. It specializes [ion_momentum_diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity) to poloidal transport and complements [poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which resolves the same transport by ion charge state.

The diffusive poloidal ion momentum flux density satisfies:

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{\mathrm{pol}} = -D_{\mathrm{pol}}^i\frac{\partial \Pi_i^{\mathrm{pol}}}{\partial \ell_{\mathrm{pol}}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the diffusive flux density of poloidal ion momentum, $\Pi_i^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local poloidal ion momentum density, and $\ell_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is poloidal arc length.

This coefficient describes only the diffusive, down-gradient contribution for the charge-state-summed ion population; convective, source, and charge-state-resolved contributions are excluded. It is distinct from the cross-flux-surface coefficient [radial_momentum_diffusivity](name:radial_momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective poloidal diffusivity for neutral thermal-energy transport, relating the diffusive energy flux tangent to constant-ρ surfaces to the local poloidal gradient of neutral energy density.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral energy diffusivity is the effective diagonal transport coefficient for diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by neutral atoms and molecules along the poloidal direction.

In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, its defining constitutive relation is

$$
q_{n,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}=-D_{n,\theta}\frac{\partial u_n}{\partial s_\theta}
$$

where $q_{n,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive neutral-energy flux density, $D_{n,\theta}$ is the poloidal diffusivity, $u_n$ is neutral thermal-energy density, and $s_\theta$ is physical arclength along the poloidal tangent at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$. The diffusivity has units of m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, while $s_\theta$ is measured in m.

This quantity is the poloidal specialization of [neutral energy diffusivity](name:neutral_energy_diffusivity). It aggregates the relevant neutral populations and is distinct from the state-resolved [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective diagonal diffusivity for down-gradient transport of energy carried by neutral particles in a specified internal state along poloidal flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the [effective neutral internal-state energy diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity) tensor expresses effective Fickian transport of energy carried by neutral particles occupying a specified internal state. It acts along the poloidal tangent to a flux surface, rather than along the magnetic-field direction.

$$
\Gamma_{E,\theta}=-D^{\mathrm{eff}}_{E,\theta}\left.\frac{\partial e_{n,s}}{\partial \ell_\theta}\right|_{\rho,\phi}
$$

Here $\Gamma_{E,\theta}$ is the poloidal energy flux, $D^{\mathrm{eff}}_{E,\theta}$ is this diffusivity, $e_{n,s}$ is the energy density of neutral particles in internal state $s$, and $\ell_\theta$ is distance along the poloidal tangent. The coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ are the flux-surface, poloidal-angle, and toroidal-angle coordinates; the derivative is taken at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$.

This effective coefficient represents the net phenomenological response, not a single microscopic mechanism. Its directional and state scope is shared by the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), while the parallel counterpart resolves transport along magnetic field lines.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal poloidal component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor, governing down-gradient redistribution of aggregate neutral momentum along increasing poloidal angle θ on flux surfaces in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ). The poloidal qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal poloidal component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor. It parameterizes down-gradient diffusive transport of aggregate neutral momentum density along the poloidal coordinate direction, tangent to increasing $\theta$ at fixed flux label and toroidal angle in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

The component $D_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{mom}}$ enters a local diffusive closure for the poloidal flux of neutral momentum density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{mom}}\,\frac{\partial \mathbf{g}_n}{\partial l_\theta}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the vector flux of neutral momentum density in the poloidal transport direction, $\mathbf{g}_n$ is the aggregate neutral momentum density, and $l_\theta$ is arclength along increasing $\theta$ at fixed $(\rho,\phi)$. The minus sign denotes down-gradient diffusion.

This quantity is the poloidal member of [neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:neutral_momentum_diffusivity), distinct from [parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), [toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), and [vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity). It applies to the aggregate neutral population represented by $\mathbf{g}_n$; a state-resolved or species-resolved diffusivity would require an explicit state or species qualifier. The coefficient may represent neutral-neutral viscous transport, charge-exchange momentum coupling with ions, and unresolved kinetic effects only insofar as they are represented by an effective diffusive closure.

NAMES.name: poloidal_total_current_density
NAMES.short: Poloidal total current density is the component of the aggregated current-density vector resolved along the poloidal unit vector tangent to increasing θ at fixed ρ and φ in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ), combining ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions over all plasma species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal total current density is the component of the aggregated current-density vector [total_current_density](name:total_current_density) resolved along the poloidal unit vector of the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ is the selected radial flux label, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle. It combines ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven current contributions over all plasma species and charge states. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the normalized tangent to the curve of increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$; embedded in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, this tangent lies in the poloidal cross-section spanned by $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\theta,\mathrm{total}} = \mathbf{J}_\mathrm{total}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta = \left(\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{ohmic} + \mathbf{J}_\mathrm{bootstrap} + \mathbf{J}_\mathrm{drive}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta
$$

where $j_{\theta,\mathrm{total}}$ is the scalar poloidal total current density, $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{total}$ is the aggregated total current-density vector, $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{ohmic}$ is the inductive ohmic contribution, $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{bootstrap}$ is the pressure-gradient-driven bootstrap contribution, and $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{drive}$ collects externally driven current sources.

This quantity is the total-current counterpart of [poloidal_current_density](name:poloidal_current_density), which does not by itself specify the ohmic-bootstrap-drive aggregation. It is distinct from [poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), a particular neoclassical contribution, and from directional siblings such as [radial_total_current_density](name:radial_total_current_density), [vertical_total_current_density](name:vertical_total_current_density), and [parallel_total_current_density](name:parallel_total_current_density), which project the same aggregate vector along different directions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional current flows in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Radial component of the effective electron particle convection velocity, the advective coefficient multiplying electron density in a radial particle-transport flux law.
NAMES.long:
Radial electron convection velocity is the effective advective velocity component for electron particle transport in the radial direction of a flux coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is a transport coefficient rather than necessarily the microscopic electron fluid velocity, representing directed electron particle transport after diffusive density-gradient transport is separated.

The radial electron particle flux is decomposed into diffusive and convective contributions:

$$
\Gamma_{e,\rho} = -D_{e,\rho}\frac{1}{h_\rho}\frac{\partial n_e}{\partial \rho} + n_e v_{e,\rho}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\rho}$ is the radial electron particle flux, $D_{e,\rho}$ is the radial electron particle diffusivity, $n_e$ is electron number density, $v_{e,\rho}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial electron convection velocity, $\rho$ is the radial flux coordinate, and $h_\rho$ converts variation in $\rho$ into physical distance. This component specializes the effective [electron convection velocity] and complements the [poloidal electron convection velocity](name:poloidal_electron_convection_velocity); its species contrast is the [radial ion convection velocity](name:radial_ion_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when electron particle convection is directed toward increasing radial flux coordinate $\rho$.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of free electrons per physical volume resolved with respect to radial position, retaining the local density rather than a line- or volume-averaged value.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume resolved with respect to radial position is the local continuum count density of electrons not bound to atoms, molecules, or ions. It describes the unqualified free-electron population rather than a selected thermal or fast component.

For a representative physical volume associated with radial position label $\xi$, the defining ratio is:

$$
n_e(\xi) = \frac{N_e(\xi)}{V(\xi)}
$$

where $n_e(\xi)$ is the local electron density, $N_e(\xi)$ is the number of free electrons in the representative volume, $V(\xi)$ is that physical volume, and $\xi$ labels radial position. The volume is small on macroscopic plasma scales but contains enough particles for a continuum quantity.

This is the radial specialization of [electron_density](name:electron_density), not a line- or volume-averaged density. A derivative such as [gradient of radial electron density](name:gradient_of_radial_electron_density) describes the signed radial variation of this density and is distinct from the density itself.

NAMES.name: gradient_of_radial_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Gradient of radial electron density is the signed local derivative of electron number density with respect to normalized poloidal magnetic flux, evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of an H-mode pedestal. It describes the density slope at that pedestal-top locus, not the maximum pedestal density gradient.
NAMES.long:
Gradient of radial electron density is the signed local derivative of electron number density with respect to the normalized poloidal magnetic flux coordinate $\psi_N$, evaluated at the fitted core-side shoulder of an H-mode pedestal. The fitted core-side shoulder is the pedestal-top locus associated with the density value [electron_density_at_pedestal_top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top).

The derivative is defined by

$$
G_{n_e,\mathrm{core}} = \left.\frac{d n_e}{d\psi_N}\right|_{\psi_N = \psi_{N,\mathrm{core}}}
$$

where $G_{n_e,\mathrm{core}}$ is this quantity, $n_e(\psi_N)$ is electron number density as a function of $\psi_N$, $\psi_N$ is the dimensionless normalized poloidal magnetic flux coordinate, and $\psi_{N,\mathrm{core}}$ is the fitted core-side shoulder location.

This is a local first derivative at the fitted core-side shoulder, not the electron density value at that location, an average change across the pedestal, or the maximum-gradient pedestal slope [derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum](name:derivative_with_respect_to_normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum).
NAMES.sign: Positive when electron number density increases with increasing normalized poloidal magnetic flux coordinate $\psi_N$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state along the radial direction.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state along the radial direction. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the radial diffusive particle flux density of that charge state to the negative radial gradient of its number density.

For the radial projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the defining Fickian relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,R} = -D_{s,R}\,\nabla_R n_s
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,R}$ is the radial diffusive particle flux density of charge state $s$, $D_{s,R}$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of charge state $s$, and $\nabla_R n_s = \hat{\mathbf{R}}\cdot\nabla n_s$ is its derivative along increasing $R$.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and applies to one ionization state, unlike the charge-state-averaged [ion diffusivity](name:ion_diffusivity). It is the radial counterpart of [ion charge-state diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity) and is equivalent to [radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) when the same Fickian closure is used. Radial denotes the cylindrical $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ projection and is not synonymous with a flux-surface-normal projection; convective transport and particle sources or sinks are excluded.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective radial coefficient for convective transport of ion particle density across the edge plasma; it multiplies ion density in the convective particle-flux relation and need not equal the ion fluid velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the radial component of the effective ion convection velocity used to represent convective cross-field particle transport in the edge plasma. It is the radial specialization of [ion convection velocity], not necessarily the local ion fluid velocity.

$$
\Gamma_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_i\,v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective ion particle flux, $n_i$ is the ion number density, and $v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective coefficient. The component is defined along the cylindrical $R$ direction, distinct from the diffusive coefficient represented by [radial ion particle diffusivity](name:radial_ion_particle_diffusivity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the convective ion particle flux points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective radial transport velocity for convective ion-energy transport in the edge plasma; it need not equal the radial ion particle-flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective velocity assigned to the convective component of ion-energy transport in the edge plasma. It parameterizes energy advection and is not, by definition, the ion particle-flow velocity.

Its defining relation to the convective ion-energy flux is

$$
u_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \frac{Q_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}}}{W_{i,E}}$$

where $Q_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective ion-energy flux and $W_{i,E}$ is the corresponding ion-energy density. The quantity is defined where $W_{i,E}$ is nonzero and excludes diffusive, conductive, and source contributions. It is the radial component of ion_energy_convection_velocity, and differs from [radial_ion_convection_velocity](name:radial_ion_convection_velocity), which parameterizes particle transport.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated convective ion-energy flux points in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states. Its sign distinguishes outward from inward neutral momentum transfer.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states, is the net neutral momentum transfer per unit area resolved along the radial direction. It is one component of the aggregate [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source) acting in the neutral momentum balance.

The radial component is defined by projecting the parent source vector onto the radial unit vector:

$$
S_{n,R} = \boldsymbol{S}_n \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $S_{n,R}$ is the radial neutral momentum source, $\boldsymbol{S}_n$ is the area-normalized neutral momentum source vector, and $\hat{R}$ is the radial unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is summed over all neutral states and excludes ion momentum sources. Unlike the [toroidal neutral momentum source](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_source), it resolves momentum transfer along increasing major radius rather than the toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral momentum source points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$, away from the cylindrical symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_total_current_density
NAMES.short: Radial total current density is the component of the total electric current density resolved normal to magnetic flux surfaces, summing ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions over all plasma species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
The radial total current density is the component of the aggregated current density vector [total_current_density](name:total_current_density) resolved in the direction normal to magnetic flux surfaces. It sums all current-carrying mechanisms — ohmic induction, bootstrap, and externally driven currents — over all resolved species and charge states. This cross-flux-surface radial direction is distinct from the cylindrical major-radius $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The aggregate radial current density satisfies:

$$
J_r = J_{\mathrm{ohmic},r} + J_{\mathrm{bootstrap},r} + J_{\mathrm{drive},r}
$$

where $J_{\mathrm{ohmic},r}$, $J_{\mathrm{bootstrap},r}$, and $J_{\mathrm{drive},r}$ are the ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions projected onto the flux-surface-normal direction, each in A m$^{-2}$.

In edge plasma models, the radial current density is resolved on generalized geometry grids spanning the pedestal, scrape-off layer, and divertor region. It appears in current continuity equations and the perpendicular Ohm's law governing cross-field charge transport, complementing the field-aligned [parallel_total_current_density](name:parallel_total_current_density) and azimuthal toroidal_total_current_density projections of the same total current.
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional current flows outward along the flux-surface normal, away from the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_vertical_vorticity_to_major_radius
NAMES.short: Vertical plasma vorticity divided by the local major radius, retaining the signed rotation rate about the vertical axis with inverse-length scaling.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the major-radius-scaled form of [vertical vorticity](name:vertical_vorticity), measuring local bulk-plasma rotation about the vertical direction per unit major radius. It is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\omega_Z^*(R,\phi,Z)=\frac{\omega_Z(R,\phi,Z)}{R},\qquad \omega_Z=(\nabla\times\mathbf{v})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma bulk-velocity vector, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The scaling applies to the vertical-vorticity component itself and does not represent the full [vorticity](name:vorticity) vector.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the bulk-flow rotation is in the $+Z$ sense, namely counterclockwise in the $(R,\phi)$ plane when viewed from $+Z$.

NAMES.name: safety_factor_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Safety factor at the pedestal top; it is the toroidal-to-poloidal magnetic-flux increment ratio on that flux surface and gives the number of toroidal turns in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame per poloidal turn.
NAMES.long:
The safety factor at the pedestal top is the value of the [safety factor](name:safety_factor) on the flux surface associated with the pedestal top of the edge transport barrier. It characterizes magnetic-field-line winding: the number of toroidal turns a field line makes per poloidal turn in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is defined by evaluating the toroidal-to-poloidal flux-increment ratio on the pedestal-top flux surface:

$$
q_\mathrm{ped} = \left.\frac{d\Phi}{d\Psi}\right|_{\mathcal{S}_\mathrm{ped}}
$$

where $\Phi$ is toroidal magnetic flux in webers, $\Psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux in webers, and $\mathcal{S}_\mathrm{ped}$ is the flux surface associated with the pedestal top. Because the numerator and denominator are magnetic-flux increments, $q_\mathrm{ped}$ is dimensionless.

The pedestal top is the inner edge of the steep-gradient pedestal region, so this quantity is tied to the pedestal-top flux surface rather than to a fixed normalized poloidal flux value. It is distinct from [safety_factor_at_normalized_poloidal_magnetic_flux_equal_to_0_95](name:safety_factor_at_normalized_poloidal_magnetic_flux_equal_to_0_95), which is evaluated where $\psi_N=0.95$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when an infinitesimal change to neighboring closed flux surfaces at the pedestal top gives toroidal and poloidal magnetic-flux increments $d\Phi$ and $d\Psi$ with the same sign.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Directional, charge-state-resolved coefficient for Fickian diffusion of thermal energy carried by a specified ion state, with each component selecting a spatial transport direction.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the directional, charge-state-resolved energy-diffusion coefficient for thermal energy carried by a specified ion charge state. It generalizes directional components such as the [radial thermal ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) without selecting one spatial projection.

For each selected direction $a$, the Fickian relation is

$$
Q_{E,s}^{(a)}=-n_s\,\chi_{E,s}^{(a)}\,\nabla_a T_s
$$

where $Q_{E,s}^{(a)}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux of charge state $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, $\chi_{E,s}^{(a)}$ is the corresponding directional diffusion coefficient, $\nabla_a$ is the temperature gradient along direction $a$, and $T_s$ is its thermal temperature.

Only the specified ion charge state is included; the coefficient is not summed over charge states or over the total ion population. The minus sign describes flux down the temperature gradient and does not define a signed coefficient. This distinguishes it from the population-aggregated [radial ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: radial_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial Fickian diffusion coefficient governing cross-field transport of thermal energy carried by a specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the [thermal ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) governs the diffusive transport of thermal energy associated with one specified ion charge state. It excludes convective and other non-diffusive transport contributions.

For the thermal-energy density $u_{E,i,z}$ of ion species $i$ in charge state $z$, the radial diffusive energy flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{E,i,z,R} = -D_{E,i,z,R}\frac{\partial u_{E,i,z}}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{E,i,z,R}$ is the radial energy flux, $D_{E,i,z,R}$ is this diffusion coefficient, and $R$ is the radial coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Unlike [radial ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient), this quantity is resolved to a specified ion charge state rather than aggregated over the total ion population.

NAMES.name: thermal_plasma_pressure
NAMES.short: Isotropic scalar pressure of the bulk thermal plasma in a continuum description, serving as the bulk-thermal member of plasma_pressure and formed from thermal electron and ion kinetic motion while excluding fast, suprathermal, and runaway populations.
NAMES.long:
The thermal plasma pressure $p_\mathrm{th}$ is the isotropic scalar pressure of the bulk thermal plasma in a fluid continuum description. It is the bulk-thermal member of [plasma pressure](name:plasma_pressure), formed from thermal electron and bulk thermal ion kinetic pressure rather than from the first-order pressure deviation represented by [perturbed plasma pressure](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure).

For isotropic thermal species, the equation of state is:

$$
p_\mathrm{th} = n_e k_B T_e + \sum_i n_i k_B T_i
$$

where $n_e$ is the bulk thermal electron number density, $T_e$ is the bulk thermal electron temperature, $n_i$ and $T_i$ are the number density and temperature of bulk thermal ion species $i$, $k_B$ is the Boltzmann constant, and the sum is over bulk thermal ion species.

It excludes pressure contributions from fast ions, nonthermal fusion-born particles, suprathermal tails, and runaway electrons. [Total thermal pressure](name:total_thermal_pressure) denotes the local species-summed thermal pressure; when the same electron and ion populations are included, it has the same scalar value, while $p_\mathrm{th}$ emphasizes the bulk-thermal member of the [plasma pressure](name:plasma_pressure) family. For an isotropic ideal-gas closure, the volume integral of $p_\mathrm{th}$ scaled by $3/2$ gives [thermal plasma energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy).

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
NAMES.short: Toroidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the component along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame of the current-density contribution generated by parallel viscous stress.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the component along the toroidal basis direction of the electric current-density contribution generated by parallel viscous stress in a magnetized plasma. The projection is taken along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The toroidal component of the full [parallel-viscous current-density contribution](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) is defined by

$$
J_{\Pi_\parallel,\phi}=\mathbf{J}_{\Pi_\parallel}\cdot\hat{\phi}=\frac{\left(\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel\right)\times\mathbf{B}}{B^2}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\Pi_\parallel}$ is the full current-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel$ is the parallel viscous stress tensor, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector. Parallel refers to the stress-tensor contribution aligned with the magnetic field, not necessarily to the direction of the resulting current.

This quantity excludes the [toroidal current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity) and the [toroidal current density due to heat viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $J_{\Pi_\parallel,\phi}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_radius_at_pedestal_top
NAMES.short: Toroidal flux radius at the pedestal top is a non-negative effective minor-radius label for the H-mode pedestal’s core-side shoulder.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux radius at the pedestal top is the non-negative, radius-like label of the magnetic flux surface identified as the H-mode pedestal’s core-side shoulder. It is the pedestal-top value of the [toroidal flux radius](name:toroidal_flux_radius) coordinate and provides an effective minor-radius scale rather than a cylindrical major-radius coordinate.

The pedestal-top coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,ped}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,ped}}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,ped}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the pedestal-top flux surface, $B_0$ is the reference toroidal magnetic field, and “ped” denotes evaluation at the pedestal top. The principal square root is used.

This quantity is the value of the dimensional toroidal-flux radial coordinate at the surface located by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It differs from [toroidal flux radius at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_flux_radius_of_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal flux radius at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_radius_at_plasma_boundary) by its evaluation surface.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for a specified ion charge state represents directional momentum transfer in an edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for a specified ion charge state represents directional momentum transfer in an edge plasma. It is resolved for one ion species and charge state rather than summed over charge states.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
S_{\phi,i,q} = \mathbf{S}_{i,q} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i,q}$ is the area-normalized momentum source for ion species $i$ in charge state $q$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is the toroidal specialization of the charge-state-resolved vector [ion charge state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source). It represents net momentum transfer associated with ionization, recombination, charge exchange, and related collisional processes; unlike [toroidal ion momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_source), it is not summed over ion charge states. Its corresponding poloidal projection is [poloidal ion charge state momentum source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the sourced momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal directional diffusion coefficient governing diffusive transport of bulk-ion momentum as the toroidal diagonal component of the ion momentum diffusivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion momentum diffusion coefficient is the toroidal directional component of the [ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) vector and the $\hat{\phi}\hat{\phi}$ diagonal component of the bulk-ion momentum diffusivity tensor. It relates the diffusive flux of charge-state-summed bulk-ion toroidal momentum density along $\hat{\phi}$ to the local gradient of that momentum density along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a gradient-diffusion closure, this diagonal component satisfies:

$$
\Pi_{\phi\phi,i}^{\rm diff} = -\chi_{\phi,i}\,\frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial}{\partial \phi}\left(m_i n_i v_{\phi,i}\right)
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi\phi,i}^{\rm diff}$ is the $\hat{\phi}$ projection of the diffusive flux of bulk-ion toroidal momentum density, positive for transport in the direction of increasing $\phi$; $\chi_{\phi,i}$ is this coefficient; $m_i$ is ion mass; $n_i$ is bulk-ion number density summed over all charge states; and $v_{\phi,i}$ is the density-weighted mean bulk-ion flow velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$ over all charge states, positive in the direction of increasing $\phi$. The derivative is taken at fixed $R$ and $Z$, so $R^{-1}\partial/\partial\phi$ is the directional derivative along $\hat{\phi}$.

The toroidal qualifier denotes the tensor direction of both the transported momentum component and the spatial flux-gradient projection; it is not a cross-flux-surface coefficient for transport of toroidal momentum. This distinguishes it from [toroidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which is charge-state resolved and flux-surface-normal, positive toward increasing flux label. Convective momentum transport, explicit momentum sources or sinks, and residual-stress contributions are excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a positive derivative of the bulk-ion toroidal momentum density along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ produces a diffusive flux of that momentum in the direction of decreasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Effective diffusivity, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the momentum diffusion coefficient for neutral particles in a resolved neutral-state channel. It governs Fickian redistribution of that state's momentum along the toroidal direction.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the momentum diffusion coefficient for neutral particles in a resolved neutral-state channel. It is the effective kinematic coefficient governing Fickian redistribution of momentum carried by neutrals along the toroidal direction.

Let $\mathbf{D}^{(s)}$ denote the neutral internal-state momentum-diffusion vector for resolved state $s$, and let $\hat{\phi}$ be the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The toroidal component is defined by:

$$
D_\phi^{(s)} = \mathbf{D}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

Here $D_\phi^{(s)}$ is the toroidal diffusivity and $s$ identifies the specified electronic, vibrational, or rotational neutral state.

This is the toroidal directional member of the [neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). It is distinct from the [poloidal neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), while the associated [toroidal neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) represents transported momentum rather than the coefficient governing its diffusive redistribution.

sources.enhanced_context: Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of d.
sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Effective diffusivity, on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal toroidal component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, governing down-gradient redistribution of aggregate neutral momentum along increasing toroidal angle φ. The toroidal qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal toroidal component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor. It parameterizes how aggregate neutral momentum density, summed over the neutral states represented in the neutral population, is smoothed by diffusive transport along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local diagonal diffusive closure, the toroidal component of the diffusive flux of a neutral momentum-density component is related to its toroidal gradient by:

$$
\Gamma_{\Pi_j,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\mathrm{mom},\phi}^{n}\,\frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial \Pi_j^{n}}{\partial \phi}
$$

where $D_{\mathrm{mom},\phi}^{n}$ is this quantity, $\Pi_j^{n}=\sum_s m_s n_s u_{j,s}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum-density component for momentum component $j$, $s$ labels neutral states, and $\Gamma_{\Pi_j,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the scalar flux component positive along $+\hat{\phi}$. The factor $R^{-1}\partial/\partial\phi$ is the derivative with respect to arclength in the toroidal direction, and the minus sign gives down-gradient diffusion.

The toroidal qualifier identifies the transport direction, namely the flux component and gradient direction, not the component $j$ of momentum being transported. This coefficient is one directional component of [neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:neutral_momentum_diffusivity), complementary to [parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), [poloidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), and [vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity); it is distinct from the resulting toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux and from convective or source terms in the neutral momentum balance.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states. Its sign distinguishes neutral momentum transfer along increasing versus decreasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states, is the net neutral momentum transfer per unit area resolved along the toroidal direction. It is one component of the aggregate [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source) acting in the neutral momentum balance.

The toroidal component is defined by projecting the parent source vector onto the toroidal unit vector:

$$
S_{\phi,n} = \boldsymbol{S}_n \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $S_{\phi,n}$ is the toroidal neutral momentum source, $\boldsymbol{S}_n$ is the area-normalized [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source) vector, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is summed over all neutral states and excludes ion momentum sources. Unlike the [radial neutral momentum source](name:radial_neutral_momentum_source), [poloidal neutral momentum source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source), and [parallel neutral momentum source](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_source), it resolves momentum transfer along the toroidal direction rather than along major radius, the local poloidal direction, or the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral momentum source points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of momentum.
sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
sources.parent_definition: Source term for momentum equations (sum over states when multiple states are considered), on various grid subsets

NAMES.name: total_momentum_flux
NAMES.short: Rate at which linear momentum crosses an oriented surface per unit area in the plasma, combining convective, pressure, viscous, and turbulent stress contributions.
NAMES.long:
The momentum flux describes the rate at which linear momentum crosses a unit area of an oriented surface in the plasma. It encompasses convective ram pressure, isotropic pressure, and viscous or turbulent stress contributions.

The momentum-flux tensor for a plasma fluid is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi} = \rho\,\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v} + p\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}
$$

where $\rho$ is mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ is bulk flow velocity, $p$ is scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}$ is viscous stress. The momentum current through an oriented surface is $\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}$, where $\hat{n}$ is its outward unit normal.

This general quantity includes species- and direction-resolved forms of [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux); [toroidal total momentum flux](name:toroidal_total_momentum_flux) is one such projection. Its divergence supplies the momentum-transport term in fluid momentum balance.

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_momentum_flux
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of total edge-plasma momentum-flux density, combining advective, pressure, viscous, and turbulent stress contributions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the total edge-plasma momentum-flux density, representing transport of toroidal linear momentum rather than stored momentum or a torque source. It is the toroidal projection of [total momentum flux](name:total_momentum_flux).

The total contribution is defined by

$$
\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{adv}} + \Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{pres}} + \Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{visc}} + \Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{turb}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total toroidal momentum-flux density and the terms represent advective, pressure, viscous, and turbulent-stress contributions, respectively. The toroidal direction is $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal momentum-flux component points along $\hat{\phi}$, toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the electric current density produced by frictional momentum exchange between plasma ions and background neutral particles in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical current density due to ion-neutral friction is the vertical component of the electric current density contribution from collisional momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral atoms or molecules. It is a projection of the full [ion-neutral-friction current density](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The defining projection is:

$$
j_{\mathrm{in},Z}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{in},Z}$ is the vertical component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the ion-neutral-friction current-density vector, both expressed in A.m$^{-2}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the unit vector along increasing $Z$.

Only the current contribution attributed to ion-neutral momentum exchange is included; contributions from other collision or transport processes and the total plasma current are excluded. Unlike the [parallel current density due to ion-neutral friction](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), this quantity is a geometric vertical projection rather than a field-aligned projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the friction-associated current points along $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$, toward increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective vertical convection velocity that advects a chosen component of ion momentum density for a specified ion species, represented as the density-weighted mean over all charge states. The vertical label names the velocity direction, not the transported momentum component.
NAMES.long:
The vertical ion momentum convection velocity is the vertical effective velocity that advects a chosen component of ion momentum density for a specified ion species. The vertical direction is the $Z$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the vertical label names the velocity direction, not the transported momentum component. Because this is an intensive species-level quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all charge states of that species.

The vertical convective flux density of an ion-momentum component is represented by:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,a},Z} = p_{i,a}\,V_{i,\mathrm{mom,conv},Z}
$$

where $p_{i,a}=n_i m_i u_{i,a}$ is the ion momentum density associated with ion flow component $u_{i,a}$, $n_i$ is the ion density, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $a$ labels the momentum component being transported, $V_{i,\mathrm{mom,conv},Z}$ is the vertical ion momentum convection velocity, and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,a},Z}$ is the corresponding vertical convective flux density of that momentum component.

This quantity is the convective coefficient multiplying local ion momentum density; it excludes diffusive viscosity, residual stress, and explicit momentum sources. It is not generally identical to the bulk [vertical ion velocity](name:vertical_ion_velocity), because it characterizes transport of momentum density rather than the mean particle flow. The unprojected coefficient is [ion momentum convection velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity); other projections specify their own directions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective convection carries the selected ion momentum density toward increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_total_current_density
NAMES.short: Vertical total current density is the Z component of net conventional current density in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, combining ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions over all plasma species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Vertical total current density is the component of the aggregated current-density vector [total current density](name:total_current_density) resolved along the vertical direction. It combines ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions over all included plasma species and charge states, distinguishing it from the generic [vertical current density](name:vertical_current_density).

The defining projection is:

$$
J_{\mathrm{v,total}} = \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{total}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $J_{\mathrm{v,total}}$ is the vertical total current density, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{total}}$ is the aggregated conventional current-density vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional current has a component in the $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction, corresponding to increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_neutral_temperature
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged translational kinetic temperature, expressed as energy per particle, of the selected neutral population inside the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the volume average of the translational kinetic temperature of the selected neutral species or state, with mean flow removed. It applies to the volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface and follows the state-aggregation convention of [neutral temperature](name:neutral_temperature).

The defining volume average is

$$
\langle T_n\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_{\rm LCFS}}\int_{V_{\rm LCFS}} T_n(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_n\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged neutral temperature, $T_n(\mathbf{r})$ is the local neutral temperature at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\rm LCFS}$ is the volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume element.

When multiple neutral internal states are included, the local temperature is density-weighted across those states before the volume average; a state-specific selection uses only that state. This quantity is distinct from [thermal neutral pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure), which is an isotropic kinetic pressure rather than an energy-per-particle temperature.
