NAMES.name: product_of_poloidal_current_function_and_derivative_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate_of_poloidal_current_function
NAMES.short: Product of the poloidal current function and its derivative with respect to the poloidal magnetic flux coordinate; a flux-surface scalar in axisymmetric equilibrium.
NAMES.long:
Product of the poloidal current function and its derivative with respect to the poloidal magnetic flux coordinate is a flux-surface scalar in axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium. It represents the coordinate derivative of the toroidal-field contribution associated with the [poloidal current function](name:poloidal_current_function) along surfaces labeled by poloidal magnetic flux.

The defining relation is

$$
Q_F(\psi) = F(\psi)\frac{dF}{d\psi}
$$

where $Q_F$ denotes this quantity, $F=R B_\phi$ is the [poloidal current function](name:poloidal_current_function), $R$ is major radius, $B_\phi$ is the toroidal magnetic-field component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\psi$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at flux surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface) used as the flux coordinate.

Equivalently, $Q_F=(1/2)d(F^2)/d\psi$, linking this quantity to the flux derivative of the product $F^2$. In the Grad-Shafranov force balance, $F\,dF/d\psi$ is the magnetic free-function term appearing with the pressure-gradient term; it contributes to the $R$-weighted toroidal current-density balance but is not the same quantity as [product of current density and major radius](name:product_of_current_density_and_major_radius). The derivative is with respect to the flux coordinate $\psi$, not a spatial derivative such as the [gradient of poloidal magnetic flux](name:radial_derivative_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $F^2$ increases with increasing poloidal magnetic flux coordinate $\psi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Product F·dF/dψ, where F = R·Bφ is the poloidal current function and ψ is the poloidal flux. Appears in the Grad-Shafranov equation and relates toroidal current density to pressure balance on flux surfaces.
sources.leaf_definition: Derivative of F w.r.t. Psi, multiplied with F

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_current_center
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of the plasma-current centroid, obtained as the current-density-weighted first moment over the poloidal cross-section.
NAMES.long:
The plasma-current centroid is the effective radial location of the toroidally distributed plasma current, distinct from the geometric axis of the plasma boundary. Its vertical counterpart is the [vertical coordinate of the current center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_current_center).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, its major-radius coordinate is defined by

$$
R_c = \frac{\int_A R\,j_\phi(R,Z)\,dA}{\int_A j_\phi(R,Z)\,dA}
$$

where $R_c$ and $R$ are major-radius coordinates in meters, $j_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the conventional plasma [current density](name:current_density), $dA$ is the differential area in the poloidal cross-section, and $A$ is the cross-sectional domain containing the plasma current. The weighting uses the signed toroidal current distribution and excludes currents outside the defined plasma-current domain.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_dr_dz_zero_point
NAMES.short: Major radius coordinate of the point on a plasma boundary or flux surface where dR/dZ = 0, locating the inboard or outboard midplane extremity of the contour in the poloidal plane.
NAMES.long:
The dR/dZ = 0 point marks the poloidal location on a plasma boundary or flux-surface contour in the poloidal cross-section where the boundary tangent is vertical — equivalently, where the major radius $R$ reaches a local extremum as the height $Z$ varies along the contour. For a convex, simply connected tokamak boundary, two such points exist per flux surface: the outboard (maximum $R$) and inboard (minimum $R$) extremes, both situated near the magnetic midplane.

The defining geometric condition is

$$\left.\frac{dR}{dZ}\right|_{\text{contour}} = 0$$

where $R$ is the major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\phi$ the toroidal angle.

This coordinate is obtained from equilibrium reconstruction by numerically locating the $R$ extremum on the reconstructed last-closed flux surface or separatrix contour. It provides a compact boundary-shape descriptor complementary to the X-point geometry described by [radial_coordinate_of_x_point](name:radial_coordinate_of_x_point), and is geometrically paired with its vertical counterpart vertical_coordinate_of_dr_dz_zero_point.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the dR/dZ = 0 point lies at a positive major radius measured outward from the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, which is satisfied everywhere in the plasma-accessible region where $R > 0$.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_geometric_axis
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of the geometric axis of the last closed plasma boundary, equal to the midpoint between the maximum and minimum boundary values of R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Major-radius coordinate of the geometric axis is the $R$ coordinate of the horizontal geometric center of the last closed plasma boundary in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is measured from the toroidal symmetry axis. It characterizes the boundary geometry, not the magnetic-flux extremum.

The coordinate is defined by the radial extrema of the same boundary:

$$
R_\mathrm{geom} = \frac{R_\mathrm{max} + R_\mathrm{min}}{2}
$$

where $R_\mathrm{max}$ and $R_\mathrm{min}$ are respectively the largest and smallest $R$ values attained by the last closed plasma boundary in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the magnetic axis](name:radial_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis), which is defined by the extremum of poloidal magnetic flux rather than by boundary extrema. Together with the [minor radius of the plasma boundary](name:minor_radius_of_plasma_boundary), it gives the radial midpoint and radial half-width of the boundary cross-section.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of the magnetic axis, the O-point where the poloidal magnetic field vanishes and nested closed flux surfaces are centered.
NAMES.long:
The major-radius coordinate of the magnetic axis is the value of $R$ locating the O-point of a nested-flux-surface equilibrium. It identifies the center of the magnetic flux surfaces and is distinct from the geometric axis of the plasma boundary.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the magnetic axis satisfies

$$
\nabla\psi(R_{\rm axis},Z_{\rm axis})=0
$$

where $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux, and $R_{\rm axis}$ and $Z_{\rm axis}$ are the radial and vertical coordinates of the O-point. The corresponding flux value is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis), which provides the inner reference for the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate). The [radial coordinate of the geometric axis](name:radial_coordinate_of_geometric_axis) instead describes the boundary geometry.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_measurement_position
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of a measurement position, equal to its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate is the major-radius location $R$ of the measurement position, measured perpendicularly from the toroidal symmetry axis. It identifies the position's distance in the radial direction and is independent of its toroidal and vertical coordinates.

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ basis, with $z$ aligned with the vertical $Z$ direction. The associated toroidal location is given by the [toroidal coordinate of measurement position](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_measurement_position). As a distance from the symmetry axis, $R$ is non-negative.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_strike_point
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of a magnetic strike point where the plasma separatrix meets a divertor target or first-wall surface in the poloidal cross-section.
NAMES.long:
The strike-point major radius is the distance from the toroidal symmetry axis to the intersection of the plasma separatrix with a divertor target or first-wall surface. It is evaluated in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Let $\mathbf{x}_{\rm sp}$ denote the strike-point position and $R(\mathbf{x}_{\rm sp})$ its major-radius coordinate:

$$
R_{\rm sp}=R(\mathbf{x}_{\rm sp})
$$

The quantity refers to the radial coordinate of the separatrix–surface intersection, not to the nearby magnetic null represented by the [radial coordinate of the X-point](name:radial_coordinate_of_x_point). It complements the general [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) used to specify positions in the poloidal plane.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_x_point
NAMES.short: Major radius R coordinate of the magnetic X-point, the null of the poloidal magnetic field at which the separatrix forms and the confined plasma meets the scrape-off layer.
NAMES.long:
The X-point is the location in the poloidal $(R, Z)$ plane where the poloidal magnetic field vanishes, creating the degenerate separatrix topology that separates the closed-field-line confined plasma region from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. Its radial coordinate $R_X$ is the major-radius distance from the toroidal symmetry axis to this null, measured in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is the horizontal distance from the machine symmetry axis.

The null condition defining the X-point is:

$$
\left.\nabla\psi\right|_{(R_X,\, Z_X)} = 0
$$

where $\psi(R, Z)$ is the poloidal magnetic flux function and $Z_X$ is the companion vertical X-point coordinate.

The X-point location is inferred from equilibrium reconstruction constrained by external magnetic diagnostics including flux loops, Rogowski coils, and magnetic pickup probes. The X-point radial position is displaced from the [radial coordinate of the magnetic axis](name:radial_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis) by an amount that reflects the poloidal asymmetry of the diverted plasma configuration; in single-null geometries, $R_X$ shifts inboard or outboard depending on the divertor target orientation and plasma shaping. The [current center radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate_of_current_center) provides a complementary moment-based measure of the current distribution centroid, distinct from the X-point null.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the X-point lies outward from the toroidal symmetry axis in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_derivative_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux
NAMES.short: The radial derivative of poloidal magnetic flux is its scalar derivative with respect to the dimensionful toroidal flux radius coordinate.
NAMES.long:
The radial derivative of poloidal magnetic flux is the scalar coordinate derivative of the poloidal magnetic-flux function $\psi$ with respect to the dimensionful toroidal flux radius coordinate $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$. It is defined on nested equilibrium magnetic flux surfaces and gives the local mapping between the poloidal-flux label and the toroidal-flux-radius label.

The defining relation is the derivative of the flux-function relation $\psi(\rho_{\mathrm{tor}})$:

$$
D_{\psi\rho}(\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}) = \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}
$$

where $D_{\psi\rho}$ denotes this quantity, $\psi$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) function, and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the [toroidal flux radius](name:toroidal_flux_radius), a dimensionful flux coordinate increasing outward from the magnetic axis. No additional normalization or factor of $2\pi$ is introduced by this derivative.

This is a scalar derivative between flux-surface labels, not the spatial gradient of the poloidal magnetic-flux field; [gradient_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux](name:radial_derivative_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux) denotes that spatial-gradient quantity. It is also distinct from a partial derivative with respect to the major-radius coordinate $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The second_radial_derivative_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux is the derivative of this quantity with respect to the same $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ coordinate, while flux_surface_averaged_metric is a separate radial metric using the same flux label.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\psi$ increases as $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ increases from the magnetic axis toward outer flux surfaces.

NAMES.name: radial_magnetization_of_iron_core_segment
NAMES.short: Magnetization of an iron-core segment expressed as magnetic flux density, projected onto the outward major-radius direction and uniform within the segment.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the radial component of an iron-core segment’s material magnetization expressed as magnetic flux density, with the magnetization taken to be uniform throughout the segment. It is distinct from the total magnetic field produced by the plasma, coils, and magnetized material.

The magnetic-flux-density-equivalent magnetization is defined by

$$
B_{\mathrm{mag},R} = \mu_0 M_R
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{mag},R}$ is the named quantity, $M_R$ is the material-magnetization component along the cylindrical major-radius direction, and $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space. Its vertical counterpart is [vertical magnetization of an iron-core segment](name:vertical_magnetization_of_iron_core_segment).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the segment’s magnetization points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Radial non-axisymmetric magnetic field is the signed R component of the toroidally varying vacuum field after its toroidally averaged component is removed.
NAMES.long:
Radial non-axisymmetric magnetic field is the radial component of the toroidally varying part of a vacuum magnetic field in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It is the radial projection of the [non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field) produced by external coil currents, excluding the axisymmetric vacuum contribution and plasma-response field.

At fixed major radius and vertical height, the component is defined by

$$
B_{\mathrm{na},R}(R,\phi,Z)=B_{\mathrm{vac},R}(R,\phi,Z)-\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi}B_{\mathrm{vac},R}(R,\phi',Z)\,d\phi'
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{na},R}$ and $B_{\mathrm{vac},R}$ are radial magnetic-field components in tesla, $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height in meters, and $\phi$ and $\phi'$ are toroidal angles in radians, with $\phi'$ the integration variable. The radial projection is along the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ direction, distinct from the toroidal component [toroidal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field) and the vertical component.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $B_{\mathrm{na},R}$ points in the increasing-$R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis.

NAMES.name: radius_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Radius of plasma boundary is a scalar radius measure characterizing the size of the plasma-boundary contour in a poloidal cross-section. Specializations define the particular radius descriptor, such as the minor-radius half-width in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radius of plasma boundary is a scalar radius measure assigned to the closed contour that represents the plasma boundary in a poloidal cross-section. It defines the common boundary-radius concept; concrete specializations determine which radius descriptor is used, while the locus remains the plasma-boundary contour.

For the representative [minor radius of plasma boundary](name:minor_radius_of_plasma_boundary) specialization, the descriptor is the half difference between the maximum and minimum major radius of the same boundary contour in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height: $a = (R_{\max} - R_{\min})/2$. Other specializations preserve the same boundary locus and differ only in the radius descriptor.

This quantity excludes coordinates of individual boundary points, boundary perimeter, enclosed area, and flux-surface labels; those describe boundary geometry or labeling rather than a scalar radius descriptor.

NAMES.name: minor_radius_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Minor radius of the last closed plasma-boundary contour, obtained from its maximum and minimum major-radius coordinates.
NAMES.long:
The minor radius of the plasma boundary is the radial half-width of the last closed plasma-boundary contour in a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the component-specific radial measure represented by [radius of plasma boundary](name:radius_of_plasma_boundary).

The minor radius is defined by

$$
a = \frac{R_{\max} - R_{\min}}{2}
$$

where $a$ is the minor radius, and $R_{\max}$ and $R_{\min}$ are the maximum and minimum values of the major-radius coordinate along the complete boundary contour, measured in m. The definition excludes vertical extent, contour perimeter, and shaping parameters.

NAMES.name: radius_of_plasma_filament
NAMES.short: Radius of a plasma filament is the geometric radius of a circular boundary of the annular cross-section representing a current-carrying plasma filament. In the hollow-disk geometry it denotes either the inner or outer boundary radius.
NAMES.long:
Radius of a plasma filament is the geometric radius of a circular boundary of the annular cross-section representing a current-carrying plasma filament. The cross-section is a hollow disk bounded by concentric inner and outer circular boundaries, so this generic quantity denotes either boundary radius when the boundary is not otherwise specified.

For a circular boundary in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the radius $a$ is the distance from the filament cross-section center $(R_c, Z_c)$ to any point $(R, Z)$ on that boundary:

$$
a = \sqrt{(R - R_c)^2 + (Z - Z_c)^2}
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, and $(R_c, Z_c)$ is the center of the annular cross-section.

An annular plasma filament has an [inner radius](name:inner_radius_of_plasma_filament) and an [outer radius](name:outer_radius_of_plasma_filament), with $0 \le a_\mathrm{inner} \le a_\mathrm{outer}$; the current-carrying cross-section occupies the region between those two circular boundaries. This quantity excludes the curvature radius of a noncircular contour segment and the major radius of a filament centerline about the toroidal symmetry axis.

sources.enhanced_context: Curvature radius of each arc of circle segment describing the cross-sectional contour of a plasma current filament element. Part of the piecewise arc-of-circle geometry representation used in electromagnetic circuit calculations.
sources.leaf_definition: Curvature radius of each arc of circle
sources.parent_definition: Description of the element contour by a set of arcs of circle. For each of these, the position of the start point is given together with the curvature radius. The end point is given by the start point of the next arc of circle.

NAMES.name: inner_radius_of_plasma_filament
NAMES.short: Inner radius of the annular cross-section of a plasma current-carrying filament element, marking the boundary between the hollow central region and the conducting annular zone.
NAMES.long:
The inner radius $r_\mathrm{inner}$ specifies the radial position of the inner wall of an annular plasma filament cross-section, defining the boundary between the hollow (non-current-carrying) core and the conducting annular region. In filamentary models of distributed plasma current, individual elements may be assigned annular geometries bounded at the outer wall by [outer_radius_of_plasma_filament](name:outer_radius_of_plasma_filament) $r_\mathrm{outer}$, with current flowing only in the region $r_\mathrm{inner} \leq r \leq r_\mathrm{outer}$.

The conducting cross-sectional area of the annular element is:

$$
A = \pi \left( r_\mathrm{outer}^2 - r_\mathrm{inner}^2 \right)
$$

where $A$ is the geometric cross-sectional area corresponding to area_of_plasma_filament. A valid annular geometry requires $0 \leq r_\mathrm{inner} < r_\mathrm{outer}$; setting $r_\mathrm{inner} = 0$ recovers a solid circular cross-section with no hollow core.

This parameter is a geometric input to the filamentary discretization of the plasma current distribution and is always specified alongside [outer_radius_of_plasma_filament](name:outer_radius_of_plasma_filament). For rectangular filament cross-sections the analogous spatial parameters are [height_of_plasma_filament](name:height_of_plasma_filament) and width_of_plasma_filament.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the inner boundary of the annular cross-section is measured outward from the local geometric center of the filament element.

sources.enhanced_context: Inner radius of an annular cross-section element representing a discrete plasma current-carrying filament in the pf_plasma IDS. Defines the inner boundary of the annulus in axisymmetric plasma current distribution modelling.
sources.leaf_definition: Inner radius
sources.parent_definition: The element is an annulus of centre R, Z, with inner radius radius_inner and outer radius radius_outer

NAMES.name: outer_radius_of_plasma_filament
NAMES.short: Outer radius of the annular cross-section of a discrete plasma current-carrying filament element, marking the external radial boundary of the hollow-disk geometry.
NAMES.long:
The outer radius defines the external boundary of an annular cross-section when a plasma current filament element is represented as a hollow cylinder. Together with [inner_radius_of_plasma_filament](name:inner_radius_of_plasma_filament), it fully characterizes the annular geometry, which contrasts with the rectangular cross-section model parametrized by [height_of_plasma_filament](name:height_of_plasma_filament) and width_of_plasma_filament.

For an annular cross-section, the cross-sectional area relates to both radii by:

$$
A = \pi \left( r_\mathrm{outer}^2 - r_\mathrm{inner}^2 \right)
$$

where $r_\mathrm{outer}$ is this outer radius, $r_\mathrm{inner}$ is the inner radius, and $A$ is the area_of_plasma_filament.

The outer radius is specified as input geometry when constructing discrete filamentary representations of plasma current distributions used in equilibrium reconstruction and mutual-inductance computations. The constraint $r_\mathrm{outer} > r_\mathrm{inner} \geq 0$ must be satisfied to define a valid non-degenerate annular region.
NAMES.sign: Positive when measured as a radial distance from the cross-section center to the outer boundary, satisfying $r_\mathrm{outer} > r_\mathrm{inner} \geq 0$.

sources.leaf_definition: Outer radius

NAMES.name: reference_major_radius
NAMES.short: Perpendicular distance from the machine's toroidal symmetry axis to the fixed reference point at which the toroidal vacuum magnetic field is specified, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It serves as the geometric normalization radius paired with the reference toroidal field value.
NAMES.long:
The reference major radius $R_0$ is the perpendicular distance from the machine's toroidal symmetry axis to the fixed reference point at which the toroidal vacuum magnetic field is specified, measured in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$ and $Z$ is the vertical height. It specializes [major_radius](name:major_radius) to a single fixed reference locus and acts as the geometric normalization radius of the axisymmetric vacuum toroidal field.

Together with the signed [toroidal reference magnetic field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field) $B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}$, it fixes the amplitude of the current-free toroidal field, which varies inversely with the independent major-radius coordinate:

$$
B_{\phi,\mathrm{vac}}(R) = B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}\,\frac{R_0}{R}
$$

where $R$ is the independent major-radius coordinate in meters, $R_0$ is the reference major radius in meters, $B_{\phi,\mathrm{vac}}(R)$ is the signed toroidal vacuum field component at $R$, and $B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}$ is the signed reference value at $R_0$. The ordered pair $(R_0, B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}})$ must be used consistently, since only their product-scaled ratio has physical meaning.

The reference point is a fixed geometric convention of the device (commonly the geometric center of the vacuum vessel), independent of the plasma state. It is therefore distinct from the magnetic axis, the plasma geometric axis, and the plasma boundary, and it is not a flux-surface quantity such as the [flux-surface-averaged major radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_major_radius). It is likewise not a position-specific $R$ value such as the [radial coordinate of a measurement position](name:radial_coordinate_of_measurement_position), and it carries no magnetic-field sign, which resides entirely in $B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}$.

NAMES.name: rotational_transform
NAMES.short: Dimensionless field-line winding number on a magnetic flux surface, equal to the number of poloidal turns per toroidal circuit and the inverse of the safety factor.
NAMES.long:
Rotational transform is the field-line winding number on a magnetic flux surface, measuring poloidal winding relative to toroidal winding. It can vary from one nested magnetic flux surface to another.

The rotational transform is defined by

$$
\iota(\psi) = \frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}}{d\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}} = \frac{1}{q(\psi)}
$$

where $\iota$ is the rotational transform, $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is poloidal magnetic flux, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is toroidal magnetic flux, and $q(\psi)$ is the [safety factor](name:safety_factor). The relation is differential, so the flux increments are evaluated on neighboring surfaces rather than as a ratio of total fluxes.

sources.enhanced_context: Rotational transform (1/q).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Rotational transform (1/q)

NAMES.name: squareness_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Squareness of the plasma boundary is a dimensionless Luce shape coefficient quantifying the whole-boundary corner deviation of the last closed flux surface from the reference ellipse set by the boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity. Positive values make the corner regions boxier, approaching the circumscribing rectangle; negative values make them more diamond-like.
NAMES.long:
Squareness of the plasma boundary is a dimensionless Luce shape coefficient quantifying the deviation of the corner regions of the last closed flux surface from the reference ellipse whose semi-axes are set by the boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity. It is the whole-boundary summary of the quadrant-level squareness values, characterizing whether the poloidal cross-section corners bulge outward toward the circumscribing rectangle or are pinched inward relative to the elliptical reference contour.

In a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, each quadrant of the boundary is bounded by its radial extremum (innermost or outermost major-radius point) and its vertical extremum (topmost or bottommost point), and a reference ellipse is constructed through these two extrema; the semi-axes of this ellipse are fixed by the boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity. Along the diagonal from the ellipse center $O$ toward the corner $F$ of the rectangle circumscribing the quadrant, the quadrant squareness is

$$
\zeta = \frac{\overline{OD} - \overline{OE}}{\overline{OF} - \overline{OE}}
$$

where $D$ is the intersection of the diagonal with the plasma boundary, $E$ its intersection with the reference ellipse, and $\overline{OD}$, $\overline{OE}$, $\overline{OF}$ are distances from the ellipse center. With this construction $\zeta = 0$ when the boundary follows the elliptical arc, $\zeta = 1$ when it passes through the rectangle corner, and $\zeta < 0$ when the corner is indented inside the ellipse (diamond- or bean-like).

This whole-boundary quantity summarizes the four quadrant-resolved members [upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), [upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), [lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), and [lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), and decomposes into [inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) on the high-field side (smaller major radius $R$) and [outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) on the low-field side (larger $R$). Use the quadrant- or side-resolved members when the boundary corners are shaped asymmetrically; this quantity carries no information about up-down or in-out asymmetry of the corner shaping.

NAMES.name: inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the Luce shape coefficient for the high-field-side corner pair, referenced to an ellipse defined by boundary size and shaping.
NAMES.long:
Inner squareness of the plasma boundary is a dimensionless Luce shape coefficient characterizing how the high-field-side corners of the last closed flux surface depart from a reference ellipse. It covers the inner corner behavior represented separately by the [upper-inner squareness](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) and [lower-inner squareness](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) quantities, rather than selecting one vertical quadrant.

In a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the coefficient for an inner quadrant is

$$
\zeta = \frac{\overline{OD} - \overline{OE}}{\overline{OF} - \overline{OE}}
$$

where $O$ is the reference-ellipse center, $D$ is the boundary intersection along the corner diagonal, $E$ is the corresponding ellipse intersection, and $F$ is the corner of the circumscribing rectangle; the overbars denote distances. The reference ellipse is set by the boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity. This component refines the whole-boundary [squareness of the plasma boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary) to its high-field-side corners.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the inner boundary corner lies outward from the reference ellipse toward the circumscribing rectangle.

NAMES.name: lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Dimensionless Luce squareness parameter for the lower-inner (below-midplane, high-field-side) plasma boundary in a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measuring its departure from the reference ellipse set by boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity.
NAMES.long:
The lower-inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the dimensionless Luce shape coefficient quantifying how much the lower-inboard quadrant of the last-closed flux surface deviates from the reference ellipse determined by the boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity. The lower-inboard quadrant is the part of the boundary at smaller major radius and below the reference-ellipse center in a poloidal cross-section.

In the Luce higher-order boundary parameterization, the lower-inner boundary contour at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is represented over the lower-inboard interval of the poloidal angle $\theta$ by the coefficient $\zeta_{\mathrm{LI}}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
R(\theta) &= R_{\mathrm{geo}} + a\cos\!\left[\theta + \arcsin(\delta_{\mathrm{ref}})\sin\theta - \zeta_{\mathrm{LI}}\sin(2\theta)\right],\\
Z(\theta) &= Z_{\mathrm{geo}} + a\kappa_{\mathrm{ref}}\sin\!\left[\theta + \zeta_{\mathrm{LI}}\sin(2\theta)\right]
\end{aligned}
$$

where $R(\theta)$ and $Z(\theta)$ are the major-radius and vertical coordinates of the boundary point, $R_{\mathrm{geo}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{geo}}$ are the coordinates of the geometric center of the reference ellipse, $a$ is the boundary minor radius, $\kappa_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\delta_{\mathrm{ref}}$ are the elongation and triangularity entering the same reference boundary description, and $\theta=0$ labels the outboard midplane with increasing $\theta$ first moving toward $+Z$. The geometric center of the reference ellipse is not the magnetic-axis position unless those points coincide for the chosen boundary geometry.

This quantity is restricted to the lower-inboard quadrant and excludes the upper-inboard quadrant represented by [upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary). It is a quadrant-resolved component of [inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), distinct from the outer-side squareness components, and complements [elongation_of_plasma_boundary](name:elongation_of_plasma_boundary) and [triangularity_of_plasma_boundary](name:triangularity_of_plasma_boundary) in describing boundary shape beyond the reference ellipse. With the sign shown in the Luce representation, positive $\zeta_{\mathrm{LI}}$ moves the lower-inboard corner toward smaller $R$ and lower $Z$ relative to the reference ellipse, making that corner more rectangular; negative values make it rounder.

sources.enhanced_context: Lower inner squareness (ζ_LI) of the plasma boundary shape parameter, defined following the T. Luce convention. Quantifies the deviation of the lower inner quadrant of the plasma cross-section from an elliptical shape.
sources.leaf_definition: Lower inner squareness of the plasma boundary (definition from T. Luce, Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 55 (2013) 095009)
sources.parent_definition: Description of the plasma boundary used by fixed-boundary codes and typically chosen at psi_norm = 99.x% of the separatrix

NAMES.name: outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient measuring how both outboard (low-field-side) corners of the plasma boundary depart from the reference ellipse defined by minor radius, elongation, and triangularity.
NAMES.long:
The outer squareness of the plasma boundary is the Luce (2013) dimensionless shape coefficient characterizing how the low-field-side (large-$R$) corners of the last-closed flux surface poloidal cross-section depart from the reference ellipse defined by the boundary minor radius $a$, elongation $\kappa$, and triangularity $\delta$. It is the parent quantity for [upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) and [lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), which resolve the upper-outboard and lower-outboard corner contributions separately.

A positive outer squareness indicates the outboard corners of the plasma cross-section lie outside the reference ellipse (a more rectangular boundary), while a negative value indicates inward concavity at the outboard corners. The outer squareness is particularly sensitive to X-point geometry and the configuration of low-field-side shaping coils, making it relevant to heat-load distribution and edge stability.

Outer squareness is inferred from equilibrium reconstruction by fitting the poloidal boundary contour $\{R(\xi), Z(\xi)\}$, where $\xi$ is a poloidal parameter, to external magnetic measurements and internal constraints. The global single-coefficient summary is provided by [squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary), while the high-field-side corner contributions are captured by [lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) and upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the outer boundary corner lies outside the reference ellipse at the corner poloidal angle, i.e., the outboard boundary is displaced toward larger minor radius relative to the inscribed ellipse in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient measuring how the lower outboard (low-field-side) corner of the plasma boundary departs from the reference ellipse defined by boundary minor radius, lower elongation, and lower triangularity.
NAMES.long:
The lower outer squareness $\zeta_{lo}$ is one of four corner-specific shape parameters in the Luce (2013) plasma boundary parameterization, describing how much the lower outer quadrant of the plasma cross-section boundary deviates from the reference ellipse defined by the boundary minor radius $a$, lower elongation $\kappa_l$, and lower triangularity $\delta_l$. The lower outer quadrant is the low-field-side, large-$R$ corner below the magnetic-axis height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

Within the Luce corner parameterization, the coefficient is related to the lower-outer superellipse exponent $n_{lo}$ by

$$
\zeta_{lo} = 1 - \frac{2}{n_{lo}}
$$

where $n_{lo}$ controls the local corner curvature of the lower-outboard boundary segment. The reference ellipse corresponds to $n_{lo}=2$.

Positive values indicate that the lower-outboard boundary corner lies outside the reference ellipse at the corresponding corner location, giving a more rectangular boundary; $\zeta_{lo}=0$ indicates the reference ellipse; negative values indicate that the corner lies inside the reference ellipse, giving inward concavity relative to that ellipse. This coefficient excludes the upper-outboard and high-field-side corner contributions represented by [upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), [lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), and [upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary); [outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) combines the outboard corner behavior, and [squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary) is the global single-coefficient summary.

NAMES.name: surface_area_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Total geometric area of a closed toroidal magnetic flux surface, obtained by revolving its poloidal contour through one complete toroidal revolution about the symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the total geometric area of a closed toroidal magnetic flux surface in an axisymmetric equilibrium. It measures the magnetic surface itself, rather than the area enclosed by its poloidal cross-section.

For an axisymmetric surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the area is defined by

$$
A_{\mathrm{s}} = \oint_{\mathcal{C}} 2\pi R\,\mathrm{d}l_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the surface area, $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in meters, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in radians, $Z$ is the vertical coordinate in meters, $\mathcal{C}$ is the closed poloidal contour, and $\mathrm{d}l_{\mathrm{p}}$ is its differential arc length in meters. The related [area of a flux surface] is the enclosed poloidal cross-sectional area and must not be confused with this toroidal surface area.

NAMES.name: thickness_of_plasma_filament
NAMES.short: Full thickness of a rectangular plasma filament cross-section, measured along the in-plane direction normal to the filament's central segment. It is the transverse side length of the rectangle, complementing the tangential length measured along the segment.
NAMES.long:
Thickness of a plasma filament is the full transverse extent of a rectangular (thick-line) filament cross-section, measured in the local plane of the element along the direction normal to the filament's central segment. The central segment lies in a poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and the local tangential-normal basis is defined within that plane: the tangential direction follows the central segment while the normal direction is the in-plane perpendicular. It is a full side length, not a half-width.

For a rectangular filament cross-section, the cross-sectional area is the product of the two full local side lengths:

$$
A_\mathrm{fil} = L_\mathrm{tan}\, t
$$

where $A_\mathrm{fil}$ is the filament cross-sectional area in $\mathrm{m}^2$, $L_\mathrm{tan}$ is the [tangential length](name:thickness_of_plasma_filament) in $\mathrm{m}$, and $t$ is the thickness in $\mathrm{m}$. When the local tangential and normal directions align with the cylindrical axes, the thickness coincides with either the width (radial $R$-direction extent) or the [height](name:height_of_plasma_filament) (vertical $Z$-direction extent) of the same rectangular cross-section.

In equilibrium filament descriptions, the thickness is set by the chosen local geometric representation of a discrete current-carrying plasma element. For a thick-line element it is specified directly as the rectangle side perpendicular to the central segment.

The value is a non-negative geometric length governed by the spatial resolution and local size of the filament representation. No universal device-independent numerical range applies; it should be interpreted relative to the associated tangential length and to neighboring filament spacing.

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_control_surface
NAMES.short: Toroidal angle locating each point of a control surface about the machine symmetry axis, measured in the right-handed cylindrical frame from the facility-defined zero direction.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal angle identifies the azimuthal location of a point on the control surface about the machine symmetry axis. It is the geometrical coordinate defined for [toroidal angle](name:toroidal_angle), with the control-surface locus providing the points to which it applies.

For a point with Cartesian coordinates $x$ and $y$ in the right-handed $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, the angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame is defined by:

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(y,x) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $R$ is the major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, and the zero of $\phi$ follows the facility-defined reference direction. The angle is periodic, so values differing by an integer multiple of $2\pi$ represent the same toroidal direction; it is distinct from the [vertical coordinate of the control surface](name:vertical_coordinate_of_control_surface).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above the $+\hat{Z}$ direction.

NAMES.name: toroidal_angle_of_measurement_position
NAMES.short: Toroidal angle of a measurement position is the azimuthal coordinate of the specified point around the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal angle of a measurement position is the azimuthal coordinate $\phi$ of the specified point associated with a measurement in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. In this frame, $R$ is major radius from the toroidal symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height.

Together with the radial and vertical coordinates of the same locus, it specifies the measurement-position point. It is the measurement-position-specific form of [toroidal_angle](name:toroidal_angle); [toroidal_coordinate_of_measurement_position](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_measurement_position) and [toroidal_angle_of_line_of_sight](name:toroidal_angle_of_line_of_sight) are related angular-coordinate quantities for nearby geometric contexts. The coordinate is periodic modulo $2\pi$, with $0 \le \phi < 2\pi$ denoting one complete non-overlapping branch.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density
NAMES.short: Toroidal current density is the conventional charge flux per unit area projected onto the geometric toroidal direction, including all charged-particle contributions.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the [current density](name:current_density) vector quantifies conventional charge transport per unit area along the geometric toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It includes all charged-particle species and current mechanisms.

The defining projection is:

$$
J_\phi = \mathbf{J} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}$ is the total current-density vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, and $J_\phi$ is its toroidal component.

This quantity excludes displacement-current density and is distinct from a scalar electric current, which is the flux of $\mathbf{J}$ through a specified surface. A restricted contribution, such as [toroidal current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), represents only one mechanism.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\mathbf{J}$ has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_diamagnetic_magnetic_flux_at_inside_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Toroidal diamagnetic magnetic flux at an inside flux surface is the diamagnetic contribution to the toroidal magnetic flux through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by a selected closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal diamagnetic magnetic flux at an inside flux surface is the diamagnetic contribution to the [toroidal magnetic flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux) through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by a selected closed flux surface. It is a surface-dependent cumulative flux inside the plasma boundary, not only a boundary value.

For an axisymmetric equilibrium in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height, let $S_\chi$ be the constant-$\phi$ poloidal cross-section enclosed by the flux surface labeled by $\chi$. With $d\mathbf{A}_\phi = \hat{\phi}\,dA$ oriented toward increasing $\phi$, the enclosed diamagnetic toroidal flux is defined by:

$$
\Phi_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}}(\chi) = \int_{S_\chi} \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}(R,Z) \cdot d\mathbf{A}_\phi = \int_{S_\chi} B_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $\chi$ identifies the selected flux surface, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to the equilibrium magnetic field, $B_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}\cdot\hat{\phi}$ is its toroidal component, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle, and $dA$ is the positive scalar area element on $S_\chi$.

This quantity includes only the diamagnetic magnetic-field contribution. It is distinct from the total [toroidal_magnetic_flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux), which includes all magnetic-field contributions, from [toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), which is evaluated at the plasma boundary, and from [toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current), which isolates the poloidal-current contribution at that boundary.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net diamagnetic magnetic-field contribution through the enclosed poloidal cross-section points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, counter-clockwise viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

The names of the child nodes correspond to the following definition: the solver aims at minimizing a cost function defined as : J=1/2*sum_i [ weight_i^2 (reconstructed_i - measured_i)^2 / sigma_i^2 ]. in which sigma_i is the standard deviation of the measurement error (to be found in the IDS of the measurement)

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_radius
NAMES.short: Toroidal flux radius is the non-negative effective minor-radius label of a nested magnetic flux surface, defined from the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux and a positive reference vacuum toroidal-field magnitude. It is a magnetic flux-surface label rather than a geometric distance.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux radius is the non-negative effective minor-radius label assigned to a nested magnetic flux surface from the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed between the magnetic axis and that surface. It is determined by magnetic flux topology, not by geometric distance from the magnetic axis.

For an enclosed toroidal flux $\Phi_\mathrm{tor}$ and a positive reference toroidal-field magnitude $B_\mathrm{ref}$, the toroidal flux radius $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is defined by:

$$
\rho_\mathrm{tor} = \sqrt{\frac{|\Phi_\mathrm{tor}|}{\pi B_\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\Phi_\mathrm{tor}$ is the [toroidal magnetic flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux) enclosed between the magnetic axis and the flux surface, and $B_\mathrm{ref}$ is the positive magnitude of the reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field used for the equilibrium normalization.

It is zero at the magnetic axis and increases monotonically over nested flux surfaces as the enclosed flux magnitude increases. The [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate) is obtained by dividing $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ by its value at the last closed flux surface; toroidal flux radius itself remains an effective radius and equals a geometric minor radius only in the circular, uniform-reference-field limit.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_radius_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Non-negative radius-like coordinate assigned to the plasma boundary from its enclosed toroidal magnetic flux and a reference toroidal field.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux radius at the plasma boundary is the non-negative, radius-like label of the outermost closed magnetic flux surface. It is the boundary value of the [toroidal flux radius](name:toroidal_flux_radius) coordinate and provides an effective minor-radius scale rather than a cylindrical major-radius coordinate.

The boundary coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor},b} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the plasma boundary, $B_0$ is the reference toroidal magnetic field, and $b$ denotes evaluation at the boundary. The principal square root is used.

This quantity is the outer endpoint of the dimensional toroidal-flux radial coordinate and is distinct from [toroidal flux radius at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_flux_radius_of_magnetic_axis), which evaluates the same coordinate at the central flux surface.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_radius_of_magnetic_axis
NAMES.short: Non-negative radius-like coordinate assigned at the magnetic axis from enclosed toroidal magnetic flux and a reference toroidal field.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux radius at the magnetic axis is the non-negative, radius-like label of the central magnetic flux surface. It is the axis value of the [toroidal flux radius](name:toroidal_flux_radius) coordinate and provides an effective minor-radius scale rather than a cylindrical major-radius coordinate.

The axis coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor},a} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},a}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},a}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed at the magnetic axis, $B_0$ is the reference toroidal magnetic field, and $a$ denotes evaluation at the magnetic axis. The principal square root is used.

This quantity is the central endpoint of the dimensional toroidal-flux radial coordinate and is distinct from [toroidal flux radius at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_radius_at_plasma_boundary), which evaluates the same enclosed-flux coordinate at the outermost closed magnetic flux surface.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_current_density_at_constraint_position
NAMES.short: Toroidal flux-surface-averaged current density at a constraint position is the flux-surface average of the toroidal component of plasma current density in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, evaluated on the magnetic surface at the constraint point's normalized toroidal flux radius.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux-surface-averaged current density at a constraint position is the flux-surface average of the toroidal component of plasma current density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, evaluated on the magnetic surface at the constraint point's normalized toroidal flux radius, specified by [normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_constraint_position](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_constraint_position). In this frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The flux-surface average on the selected surface $\rho_c$ is defined by:

$$
\left\langle j_\phi \right\rangle(\rho_c) = \frac{\displaystyle\oint_{\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}=\rho_c} j_\phi \, dl_p / B_p}{\displaystyle\oint_{\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}=\rho_c} dl_p / B_p}
$$

where $\rho_c$ is the normalized toroidal flux radius of the constraint point, $j_\phi$ is the toroidal component of plasma current density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude in tesla, and $dl_p$ is an element of poloidal arc length in meters. The closed integrals run over one full poloidal circuit on the surface at fixed $\rho_c$; any common toroidal-symmetry factor cancels between numerator and denominator.

This quantity is the constrained-surface evaluation of toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_current_density, not the radial dependence over all magnetic surfaces. It averages the toroidal component and is distinct from [parallel_flux_surface_averaged_current_density_at_constraint_position](name:parallel_flux_surface_averaged_current_density_at_constraint_position), which averages the component of current density parallel to the magnetic field on the same selected surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal current density points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal component of the total equilibrium magnetic field evaluated at the magnetic axis, including vacuum and plasma-current contributions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the total equilibrium magnetic field at the magnetic-axis position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
B_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}) \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $B_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-field component at the axis, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{total}}$ is the equilibrium field including vacuum and plasma-current contributions, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. It is the axis-local counterpart of the general [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field) and is distinct from the [toroidal reference magnetic field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field) when that reference uses a separate prescribed location or convention.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the total magnetic field at the magnetic axis points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.short: Toroidal magnetic flux is the net magnetic flux through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface, complementing poloidal flux as a radial surface label.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal magnetic flux is the surface integral of the magnetic field through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface. It is the toroidal member of the [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux) family and quantifies the net field threading that cross-section.

The defining surface integral is:

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{pol}}} \mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}\, dA
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $S_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the enclosed poloidal cross-section, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, and $dA$ is the scalar area element in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

In an axisymmetric equilibrium, the toroidal flux is constant on each nested flux surface and provides a radial flux label complementary to the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux). Its boundary value is the [toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the magnetic field threading the poloidal cross-section points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the net flux of toroidal magnetic field through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by the plasma boundary, including externally imposed and plasma-poloidal-current contributions.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the net flux of the toroidal magnetic-field component through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by the plasma boundary. It is the boundary value of toroidal magnetic flux used to define toroidal-flux radial labels.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height, the boundary toroidal flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b} = \int_{\Omega_b} \mathbf{B}\cdot\hat{\phi}\, dA_{RZ} = \int_{\Omega_b} B_\phi(R,Z)\, dA_{RZ} = \int_{\Omega_b} \frac{F(\psi(R,Z))}{R}\, dA_{RZ}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b}$ is this boundary toroidal flux, $\Omega_b$ is the boundary-enclosed region in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B_\phi$ is its toroidal component in tesla, $dA_{RZ}$ is the poloidal cross-sectional area element in square meters, $F(\psi)=R B_\phi$ is the poloidal-current function in tesla meters, and $\psi$ is the equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux label.

The geometric measure of $\Omega_b$ is the [poloidal cross-sectional area of the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_cross_sectional_area_of_plasma_boundary). $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b}$ includes both externally imposed toroidal-field flux and the contribution associated with plasma poloidal current, and is distinct from [toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary due to poloidal current](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current), which contains only that plasma-current contribution. It also differs from [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), which is magnetic flux through a horizontal disk rather than through the boundary-enclosed poloidal cross-section.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net toroidal magnetic field threading the plasma-boundary poloidal cross-section points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Toroidal non-axisymmetric magnetic field is the signed component of the toroidally varying vacuum magnetic field along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal non-axisymmetric magnetic field is the toroidal component of the toroidally varying part of a vacuum magnetic field in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius in meters, $\phi$ is toroidal angle in radians, and $Z$ is vertical height in meters. It is the signed component along increasing $\phi$ and excludes the axisymmetric equilibrium contribution.

The component projection is defined by

$$
B_\phi^{\mathrm{NA}}(R,\phi,Z) = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{NA}}(R,\phi,Z) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $B_\phi^{\mathrm{NA}}$ is the toroidal component in tesla, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{NA}}$ is the non-axisymmetric vacuum magnetic-field vector in tesla, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector.

Together with the [radial non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field) and [vertical non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:vertical_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), this component decomposes the [non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field) is the corresponding projection of the total magnetic field and is not restricted to its non-axisymmetric part.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the non-axisymmetric magnetic field points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: triangularity_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Dimensionless triangularity shape parameter for a nested magnetic flux surface, given by the normalized inward radial displacement of its upper or lower vertical extremum.
NAMES.long:
Flux-surface triangularity is the signed shaping parameter that measures the horizontal displacement of a flux surface’s vertical extremum from its geometric center, normalized by the surface’s minor radius. It characterizes triangular shaping in a poloidal cross-section.

For the relevant upper or lower vertical extremum, the defining relation is:

$$
\delta = \frac{R_c - R_{\mathrm{ext}}}{a}
$$

where $\delta$ is triangularity, $R_c$ is the major-radius coordinate of the geometric center, $R_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the major-radius coordinate of the vertical extremum, and $a$ is the flux-surface minor radius; $R_c$, $R_{\mathrm{ext}}$, and $a$ are lengths in meters. These quantities are defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The parent quantity is not restricted to one vertical extremum. When the lower extremum is resolved separately, it is represented by [lower triangularity of a flux surface](name:lower_triangularity_of_flux_surface). Triangularity is distinct from [elongation of a flux surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface), which measures aspect ratio, and [squareness of a flux surface](name:squareness_of_flux_surface), which measures non-elliptical corner shaping.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the relevant vertical extremum lies at smaller major radius $R$ than the geometric center, corresponding to an inward displacement.

NAMES.name: lower_triangularity_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Lower triangularity of a flux surface is the dimensionless triangularity shape parameter defined at the lower vertical extremum of a nested magnetic flux surface, using the flux-surface geometric center as the radial reference.
NAMES.long:
Lower triangularity of a flux surface is the dimensionless triangularity shape parameter defined at the lower vertical extremum of a nested magnetic flux surface. It is the normalized inward radial displacement of that lower extremum relative to the flux-surface geometric center in a poloidal cross-section.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ major radius, $\phi$ toroidal angle, and $Z$ vertical height, the lower triangularity is defined as:

$$
\delta_\mathrm{lower} = \frac{R_\mathrm{c} - R_\mathrm{lower}}{a}
$$

where $R_\mathrm{c} = (R_\mathrm{out}+R_\mathrm{in})/2$ is the major radius of the flux-surface geometric center, $R_\mathrm{lower}$ is the major radius of the point on the same flux surface with minimum $Z$, and $a = (R_\mathrm{out}-R_\mathrm{in})/2$ is the minor radius of that flux surface. Here $R_\mathrm{out}$ and $R_\mathrm{in}$ are the largest and smallest major radii of the poloidal contour.

This definition is a flux-surface shape parameter, not a displacement from the magnetic axis; a radially shifted but geometrically elliptical flux surface has zero lower triangularity by this definition. It distinguishes lower shaping from [upper triangularity of a flux surface]; for an up-down symmetric flux surface the upper and lower triangularities are equal.

NAMES.name: triangularity_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Dimensionless shaping parameter equal to the mean normalized inward radial displacement of the upper and lower plasma-boundary extrema from the geometric center.
NAMES.long:
Triangularity of the plasma boundary is a signed dimensionless measure of the horizontal displacement of its upper and lower poloidal extrema relative to the geometric center. The parent quantity averages the upper and lower contributions rather than selecting either extremum alone.

$$
\delta = \frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{R_0-R_u}{a}+\frac{R_0-R_l}{a}\right]
$$

Here, $\delta$ is the average triangularity; $R_0$ is the major-radius coordinate of the geometric center; $R_u$ and $R_l$ are the major-radius coordinates of the upper and lower vertical extrema; and $a$ is the plasma-boundary minor radius, with all lengths measured in m in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The component quantities [upper triangularity](name:upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary) and [lower triangularity](name:lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary) provide the two terms, while the normalization uses the boundary radius defined by [radius of plasma boundary](name:radius_of_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the upper and lower extrema are displaced inward, toward decreasing major radius $R$, relative to the geometric center.

NAMES.name: lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Lower triangularity is a dimensionless shape parameter measuring the inward radial displacement of the lower plasma-boundary extremum from the geometric center, normalized by the plasma minor radius.
NAMES.long:
Lower triangularity $\delta_L$ quantifies triangular shaping of the lower half of the plasma boundary in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

It is defined from the lower vertical extremum of the last closed magnetic-flux-surface contour:

$$
\delta_L = \frac{R_\mathrm{geo} - R_L}{a}
$$

where $R_\mathrm{geo} = (R_\mathrm{max} + R_\mathrm{min})/2$ is the major radius of the geometric center, $R_L$ is the major radius at the boundary point of minimum $Z$, and $a = (R_\mathrm{max} - R_\mathrm{min})/2$ is the plasma minor radius.

This lower component combines with [upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary) to form the average [triangularity_of_plasma_boundary](name:triangularity_of_plasma_boundary). It applies to the plasma boundary, whereas [lower_triangularity_of_flux_surface](name:lower_triangularity_of_flux_surface) describes a nested interior flux surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the lower boundary extremum is displaced inward, toward smaller major radius $R$, relative to the geometric center.

NAMES.name: upper_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: The upper-inner squareness of a flux surface is the dimensionless Luce (2013) shape coefficient that characterizes how the upper, high-field-side quadrant of a nested toroidal magnetic flux surface departs from a reference ellipse; positive values are boxier and negative values are more diamond-like or indented.
NAMES.long:
The upper-inner squareness of a flux surface is the dimensionless Luce (2013) shape coefficient that characterizes how the upper, high-field-side quadrant of a nested toroidal magnetic flux surface departs from a reference ellipse sharing the same center, horizontal half-width, and [elongation](name:elongation_of_flux_surface). It is the upper quadrant-resolved component of [inner_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:inner_squareness_of_flux_surface), complementing [lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface). The upper-inner quadrant is the segment from the top of the surface to the inner midplane, on the high-field side at smaller major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coefficient $\zeta_\mathrm{ui}$ enters the Luce parametric flux-surface shape model as an additional harmonic beyond elongation $\kappa$ and [triangularity](name:triangularity_of_flux_surface):

$$
Z(\theta)-Z_c = a\kappa\sin\!\left[\theta + \zeta_\mathrm{ui}\sin(2\theta)\right], \qquad \pi/2 \le \theta \le \pi
$$

where $Z(\theta)$ is the vertical coordinate of the contour, $Z_c$ is the vertical coordinate of the surface center, $a$ is the horizontal half-width, $\theta$ is the geometric poloidal angle measured about the surface center in the $(R,Z)$ cross-section with $\theta=0$ at the outboard midplane and increasing toward $+Z$, and $\zeta_\mathrm{ui}$ is the upper-inner squareness coefficient. Setting $\zeta_\mathrm{ui}=0$ recovers the corresponding reference ellipse for this quadrant.

This quantity is a quadrant-local squareness coefficient, not an average over the two inner quadrants and not an outboard squareness coefficient in the broader [squareness_of_flux_surface](name:squareness_of_flux_surface) family. It describes corner shaping not represented by elongation or triangularity alone.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the upper high-field-side corner of the flux-surface cross-section is boxier than the reference ellipse; negative values indicate a more diamond-like or indented corner.

NAMES.name: upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Upper-inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the dimensionless Luce shape coefficient measuring the upper high-field-side corner’s signed departure from a reference ellipse.
NAMES.long:
The upper-inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the dimensionless Luce shape coefficient quantifying the departure of the upper inboard corner of the last closed flux surface from a reference ellipse. It is the upper-quadrant component of the [inner squareness of the plasma boundary](name:inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), paired with the [lower-inner squareness of the plasma boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary).

In a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the coefficient is

$$
\zeta_{\mathrm{UI}} = \frac{\overline{OD} - \overline{OE}}{\overline{OF} - \overline{OE}}
$$

where $O$ is the reference-ellipse center, $D$ is the upper-inner boundary intersection along the corner diagonal, $E$ is the corresponding ellipse intersection, and $F$ is the corner of the circumscribing rectangle. The reference ellipse is determined by the boundary size and shaping parameters.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the upper-inner boundary corner lies outward from the reference ellipse toward the corresponding corner of the circumscribing rectangle.

sources.parent_definition: Description of the plasma boundary used by fixed-boundary codes and typically chosen at psi_norm = 99.x% of the separatrix

NAMES.name: upper_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient for the upper outboard quadrant of each nested flux surface, measuring the departure of that corner from a reference ellipse with the same center, horizontal half-width, and elongation.
NAMES.long:
The upper outer squareness $\zeta_{uo}$ is the dimensionless Luce (2013) shape coefficient for the upper outboard ($+Z$, large-$R$) corner of each nested magnetic flux surface, measuring how much that quadrant departs from a reference ellipse sharing the same geometric center, horizontal half-width, and elongation. It is one of four quadrant-resolved squareness parameters — alongside the [lower outer squareness](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface), [upper inner squareness](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface), and [lower inner squareness](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface) — extending the standard elongation-triangularity shape description to higher order.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the flux-surface boundary in the upper outer quadrant is described by the Luce parameterization as:

$$
R = R_\mathrm{geo} + a\cos\!\bigl(\theta + \delta_{uo}\sin\theta + \zeta_{uo}\sin 2\theta\bigr)
$$

with $Z = Z_\mathrm{geo} + \kappa\, a\sin\theta$, where $R_\mathrm{geo}$ and $Z_\mathrm{geo}$ are the coordinates of the flux-surface geometric center, $a$ is the minor radius, $\kappa$ is the elongation, $\delta_{uo}$ is the upper outer triangularity, and $\theta \in [0, \pi/2]$ is the geometric poloidal angle spanning the upper outboard quadrant.

Values near zero indicate an approximately elliptic corner; positive values are characteristic of D-shaped cross-sections with a squared-off outboard corner, while negative values correspond to a more concave or helmet-shaped upper outer region. The coefficient is extracted from equilibrium reconstruction by fitting computed flux-surface contours to the Luce parameterization in the upper outboard region. The symmetric combination of upper and lower outer quadrant values constitutes the aggregate [outer_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:outer_squareness_of_flux_surface), and the value at the outermost flux surface corresponds to [upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the upper outer corner of the flux surface protrudes beyond the reference ellipse, giving the cross-section a more rectangular (D-shaped) outboard corner.

NAMES.name: upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient measuring how the upper outboard (low-field-side) corner of the plasma boundary departs from the reference ellipse defined by boundary minor radius, upper elongation, and upper triangularity.
NAMES.long:
The upper outer squareness $\zeta_{uo}$ is one of four corner-specific shape parameters in the Luce (2013) plasma boundary parameterization, describing how much the upper outer quadrant of the plasma cross-section boundary deviates from the reference ellipse defined by the boundary minor radius $a$, upper elongation $\kappa_u$, and upper triangularity $\delta_u$. In the poloidal cross-section expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height, this quadrant is the large-$R$, larger-$Z$ corner relative to the boundary shape center.

With poloidal parameter $\theta$ increasing from the outboard midplane point to the top point, the upper-outboard Luce boundary segment is parameterized by

$$
\begin{aligned}
R(\theta) &= R_0 + a\cos\left[\theta + \arcsin(\delta_u)\sin\theta - \zeta_{uo}\sin(2\theta)\right],\\
Z(\theta) &= Z_0 + \kappa_u a\sin\left[\theta + \zeta_{uo}\sin(2\theta)\right],\quad 0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

where $(R(\theta), Z(\theta))$ is the boundary point in the poloidal cross-section, $R_0$ and $Z_0$ are the shape-center coordinates, $a$ is the boundary minor radius, $\kappa_u$ is the upper elongation, and $\delta_u$ is the upper triangularity.

The value $\zeta_{uo}=0$ is the reference-ellipse case for the upper-outboard quadrant after $a$, $\kappa_u$, and $\delta_u$ have been fixed; nonzero values describe residual corner shaping rather than minor radius, elongation, or triangularity. Together with [lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), [upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), and [lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), it forms the four-corner boundary squareness decomposition; [outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) combines the two outboard corner contributions, while [squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary) is the single-coefficient boundary summary.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the upper outer boundary corner lies outside the reference ellipse at the same poloidal parameter, i.e., toward larger $R$ and larger $Z$ relative to the shape center in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Upper triangularity is a dimensionless shape parameter measuring the inward radial displacement of the upper plasma-boundary extremum from the geometric center, normalized by the plasma minor radius.
NAMES.long:
Upper triangularity $\delta_U$ quantifies triangular shaping of the upper half of the plasma boundary in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. It measures the inward displacement of the boundary point at maximum $Z$ relative to the geometric center, normalized by the plasma minor radius.

The upper triangularity is defined as:

$$
\delta_U = \frac{R_{\rm geo} - R_U}{a}
$$

where $R_U$ is the major radius at the uppermost boundary point, $R_{\rm geo} = (R_{\rm max} + R_{\rm min})/2$ is the major radius of the geometric center, and $a = (R_{\rm max} - R_{\rm min})/2$ is the plasma minor radius.

This directional component contributes to [triangularity of plasma boundary](name:triangularity_of_plasma_boundary), whose average combines the upper and [lower triangularity of plasma boundary](name:lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary).
