sources.leaf_definition: Generated signal amplitude
sources.parent_definition: Temperature sensor

NAMES.name: wave_beam_energy
NAMES.short: Wave-beam energy is the pulse integral of the cycle-averaged electromagnetic energy-flow rate transported by a coherent wave beam through a specified oriented transverse surface at a specified position along its propagation path. It excludes energy absorbed or deposited before reaching that surface.
NAMES.long:
Wave-beam energy is the pulse-integrated cycle-averaged electromagnetic energy transported by a coherent wave beam through a specified oriented transverse surface at a specified position along its propagation path. Cycle averaging is over the carrier oscillation; the pulse envelope time dependence is retained until integration over the pulse interval.

The defining relation to wave-beam power is:

$$
E_\mathrm{beam}(s) = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} P_\mathrm{beam}(s,t)\,dt
$$

where $E_\mathrm{beam}(s)$ has unit $\mathrm{J}$, $P_\mathrm{beam}(s,t)$ is [wave-beam power](name:power_of_wave_beam) through the same oriented surface and has unit $\mathrm{W}$, $t$, $t_1$, and $t_2$ have unit $\mathrm{s}$ and bound the pulse interval, and $s$ labels position along the beam centerline and has unit $\mathrm{m}$.

This quantity is distinct from [wave-beam power](name:power_of_wave_beam), which is an energy-flow rate rather than its pulse integral. It also differs from [power of beam-tracing beam](name:power_of_beam_tracing_beam), which denotes residual power at the endpoint of a traced beam trajectory rather than the general pulse-integrated energy through an arbitrary beam cross-section.

sources.enhanced_context: Energy of the Thomson scattering laser pulse measured after crossing the plasma. Used to quantify laser attenuation through the plasma for absolute calibration of the scattered signal intensity.
sources.leaf_definition: Energy of the laser pulse measured after crossing the plasma
sources.parent_definition: Set of probing lasers

NAMES.name: wave_beam_energy_at_launching_position
NAMES.short: Total electromagnetic energy carried by a coherent wave-beam pulse at its launching position, before interaction with plasma or another target medium.
NAMES.long:
Total electromagnetic energy carried by a coherent wave-beam pulse at its launching position is the pulse-integrated electromagnetic energy crossing the launch reference surface before absorption, scattering, or other interaction with plasma or another target medium. It is a nonnegative energy for a single launched pulse.

The launch-position wave-beam energy is defined as the time integral of the incident beam power at that surface over the pulse interval:

$$
E_\mathrm{inc} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} P_\mathrm{inc}(t)\,dt
$$

where $E_\mathrm{inc}$ is the launch-position wave-beam energy in J, $P_\mathrm{inc}(t)$ is the instantaneous wave-beam power crossing the launch reference surface in W, and $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the pulse start and end times in s.

This quantity is the launch-position specialization of [wave_beam_energy](name:wave_beam_energy). For a coherent wave-beam pulse at the launch reference surface, it has the same physical identity as [energy_at_launching_position](name:energy_at_launching_position); it excludes energy lost or gained after the launch reference surface and is not an additional component of that quantity.

sources.enhanced_context: Energy of the Thomson scattering laser pulse measured just before entering the vacuum vessel. Used to monitor the incident laser energy for absolute calibration of scattered signal intensities.
sources.leaf_definition: Energy of the laser pulse measured just before entering the vacuum vessel
sources.parent_definition: Set of probing lasers

NAMES.name: wavelength
NAMES.short: Vacuum electromagnetic wavelength specifying a wave period, a spectral transition, or a characteristic point on an optical response.
NAMES.long:
Vacuum electromagnetic wavelength is the spatial period of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum and the spectral coordinate associated with a transition or optical response. It may characterize a propagating beam, an unshifted spectral line, or a selected point in an instrument response.

$$
\lambda_0 = \frac{c}{\nu_0} = \frac{2\pi}{\lvert \mathbf{k}_0 \rvert}
$$

where $\lambda_0$ is vacuum wavelength, $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum in m s$^{-1}$, $\nu_0$ is temporal frequency in s$^{-1}$, and $\mathbf{k}_0$ is the vacuum wave vector in m$^{-1}$. The shared quantity includes characteristic response wavelengths such as those of a [spectrometer channel](name:wavelength_of_spectrometer_channel), a [detector pixel](name:wavelength_of_detector_pixel), or an [optical element](name:spectral_wavelength_of_optical_element), as well as the rest-frame wavelength of a [spectral line](name:wavelength_of_spectral_line). It excludes in-medium wavelength unless that quantity is explicitly defined through a separate medium-dependent convention.

NAMES.name: wetted_area_of_langmuir_probe
NAMES.short: Geometric surface area of a Langmuir probe collector directly exposed to plasma and available to receive particle current, excluding shielded surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The wetted area of a Langmuir probe is the portion of the collector's geometric surface directly exposed to plasma and available to receive particle current. It represents the plasma-contacting area rather than the full hardware extent described by [area of a Langmuir probe](name:area_of_langmuir_probe).

The wetted area is defined by integrating the surface element over the plasma-exposed collector surface:

$$
A_w = \int_{S_\mathrm{exp}} dS
$$

where $S_\mathrm{exp}$ is the plasma-exposed portion of the collector and $dS$ is its differential surface-area element. Surfaces shielded from direct plasma contact are excluded. This geometric contact area is distinct from the [effective area of a Langmuir probe](name:effective_area_of_langmuir_probe), which accounts for projection relative to the local magnetic field.

sources.enhanced_context: Area of the probe surface exposed to the plasma for an embedded Langmuir probe. Used to convert ion saturation current to current density, directly affecting derived quantities such as electron density (ne) and parallel heat flux.
sources.leaf_definition: Area of the probe surface exposed to the plasma
sources.parent_definition: Set of embedded (in a plasma facing component) probes or probe pins

sources.enhanced_context: Area of the collector surface exposed to the plasma for each reciprocating Langmuir probe pin. Used for computing current density and ion saturation current density from raw probe current measurements.
sources.leaf_definition: Area of the surface exposed to the plasma of each collector (constant assuming negligible dependence on e.g. the magnetic field line angle)
sources.parent_definition: Set of reciprocating probes or probe pins

NAMES.name: width_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short: Full width of a rectangular neutron-detector aperture along its detector-local X1 direction, defining the transverse collimation boundary.
NAMES.long:
The width is the non-negative distance between the two opposing boundaries of a rectangular neutron-detector aperture along the detector-local X1 direction. It specifies one transverse opening dimension and is distinct from the aperture's second-direction [height](name:height_of_neutron_detector).

$$
w_1 = x_{1,\max} - x_{1,\min}
$$

where $w_1$ is the aperture width, and $x_{1,\max}$ and $x_{1,\min}$ are the maximum and minimum boundary coordinates along X1 in the detector-local Cartesian $(X_1, X_2)$ frame with basis $(\hat{X}_1, \hat{X}_2)$. The quantity describes the geometric opening only; it excludes detector efficiency, active-area weighting, and any projection onto the magnetic-field direction.

sources.enhanced_context: Full width of the neutron detector aperture in the X1 direction. This geometric parameter applies only when the aperture geometry type is rectangular (geometry_type = 3).
sources.leaf_definition: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3
sources.parent_definition: Detector geometry

NAMES.name: width_of_wave_beam
NAMES.short: Transverse semi-axis of the elliptical cross-section of a propagating electromagnetic wave beam, measured from the central ray to the beam-spot boundary.
NAMES.long:
The width of a wave beam is a transverse semi-axis of its elliptical cross-section, measured from the central ray to the corresponding peripheral boundary ray.

For an elliptical beam cross-section, the boundary is defined by

$$
\frac{x^2}{w_1^2}+\frac{y^2}{w_2^2}=1
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal transverse distances from the central ray, and $w_1$ and $w_2$ are the corresponding non-negative semi-axis widths. This quantity denotes one of these semi-axis widths, not the full diameter, a full-width-at-half-maximum measure, or the total cross-sectional area. The orientation of the elliptical axes is described separately by the [tilt angle of the beam-tracing beam](name:tilt_angle_of_beam_tracing_beam).

sources.parent_definition: Spot ellipse characteristics

NAMES.name: x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short: X component of the neutron-detector direction unit vector is the direction cosine along the x axis of the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame, from a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center. It is a component of a normalized pointing direction, not a position coordinate.
NAMES.long:
X component of the neutron-detector direction unit vector is the projection of the normalized direction from a field-of-view voxel center to the neutron-detector center onto the positive $\hat{x}$ axis. The component is resolved in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis and is a direction cosine, not a Cartesian position coordinate.

The normalized pointing component is defined by

$$
d_x = \left(\frac{\mathbf r_{\rm det}-\mathbf r_{\rm vox}}{\left\lVert \mathbf r_{\rm det}-\mathbf r_{\rm vox}\right\rVert}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf x}
$$

where $d_x$ is the x component of the neutron-detector direction unit vector, $\mathbf r_{\rm det}$ is the detector-center position, $\mathbf r_{\rm vox}$ is the voxel-center position, and $\hat{\mathbf x}$ is the positive x basis vector.

Together with the [y component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector) and [z component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector), $d_x$ specifies the full normalized direction from the voxel center toward the detector center; for nonzero separation the components satisfy $d_x^2+d_y^2+d_z^2=1$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the normalized direction from the voxel center to the detector center has a component in the $+\hat{x}$ direction.

sources.enhanced_context: X coordinate of direction to detector.
sources.leaf_definition: Components along X axis for each voxel
sources.parent_definition: Vector that points from the centre of the voxel to the centre of the detector, described in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system, where X is the major radius axis for phi = 0, Y is the major radius axis for phi = pi/2, and Z is the height axis.

NAMES.name: xenon_density
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Number density of xenon ions at a given point in the plasma, summed over all ionization states from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon, excluding neutral xenon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Xenon is a high-$Z$ noble-gas impurity (atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Xe} = 54$) introduced into fusion plasmas for radiative-mantle experiments, impurity-transport studies, and disruption mitigation. The xenon ion number density $n_\mathrm{Xe}$ quantifies the local concentration of all charged xenon species and enters the plasma effective charge through $Z_\mathrm{eff} = \sum_i Z_i^2 n_i / n_e$, where $n_i$ is the partial density of ion species $i$ and $n_e$ is the electron density.

The total xenon ion density is the sum over all ionic charge states:

$$
n_\mathrm{Xe} = \sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of xenon ions carrying charge $ze$. The charge-state distribution is determined by coronal equilibrium or collisional-radiative modeling at the local electron temperature and density.

The xenon density profile is inferred from vacuum-ultraviolet or soft-X-ray line emission via spectroscopy and tomographic inversion, or from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy using neutral-beam injection. Spatially resolved forms include [xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis) at the innermost flux surface and xenon_density_at_pedestal in the edge transport barrier, while [volume_averaged_xenon_density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density) provides the global impurity content figure of merit. The dimensionless impurity fraction relative to electron density is given by xenon_fraction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ionized xenon is present in the plasma.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_xenon_density
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Line-averaged number density of xenon ions along a chord through the plasma, obtained by dividing the path integral of the local xenon ion density by the chord length.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged xenon ion number density is the chord-path mean of the local [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which sums all charged xenon ionization states from Xe$^{1+}$ through Xe$^{54+}$, normalized by the measurement chord length through the plasma.

The defining relation is:

$$
\bar{n}_\mathrm{Xe} = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell) \, d\ell
$$

where $n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)$ is the local xenon ion number density at arc-length position $\ell$ along the chord and $L$ is the total chord length.

This quantity is inferred from line-integrated emission diagnostics sensitive to xenon spectral lines — including soft X-ray arrays and visible-range spectrometers — combined with knowledge of the chord geometry. The [volume_averaged_xenon_density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density) provides the spatial mean over the full plasma volume, and [xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis) captures the on-axis value. The analogous chord-averaged quantity for argon is documented as [line_averaged_argon_density](name:line_averaged_argon_density).

In trace impurity transport experiments, xenon concentrations yield $\bar{n}_\mathrm{Xe} \sim 10^{14}$–$10^{16}$ m$^{-3}$; during disruption-mitigation massive gas injection or shattered-pellet scenarios, values can reach $10^{17}$–$10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when xenon ions are present along the measurement chord.

NAMES.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short: Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the y direction cosine, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) basis, of the unit vector from a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center.
NAMES.long:
Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the signed projection, in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, of the unit vector directed from a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center. It is the y direction cosine of that line-of-sight direction.

The component is defined by projecting the detector-directed unit vector onto the $\hat{y}$ basis vector:

$$
u_y = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}} \cdot \hat{y} = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}) \cdot \hat{y}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}} \rVert}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the unit vector from the field-of-view voxel center to the detector center, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the detector-center position, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}$ is the field-of-view voxel-center position, and $\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

This quantity is a signed direction-cosine component, not a position coordinate, distance, or unnormalized displacement component. Together with the corresponding x and z components it satisfies $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$ when the field-of-view voxel center and detector center are distinct.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the direction from the field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center has a component in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

NAMES.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
NAMES.short: Z component in the right-handed Cartesian (x̂, ŷ, ẑ) basis of the unit direction vector from each field-of-view voxel to the neutron detector center, with ẑ vertical. It is the vertical direction cosine, not a position coordinate.
NAMES.long:
Z component in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis of the unit direction vector from each field-of-view voxel to the neutron detector center is the projection of that voxel-to-detector direction onto the vertical basis vector $\hat{z}$. It represents the vertical direction cosine of the ray from the voxel toward the detector center.

The component is defined by the normalized displacement from the voxel position to the detector-center position:

$$
u_z = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_d - \mathbf{r}_v) \cdot \hat{z}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_d - \mathbf{r}_v \rVert}
$$

where $u_z$ is the z component of the direction unit vector, $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the field-of-view voxel position, $\mathbf{r}_d$ is the neutron detector-center position, and $\hat{z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis.

Together with [x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector) and [y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector), it forms the direction-cosine triplet of the same voxel-to-detector ray, so $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$ and $-1 \le u_z \le 1$. This quantity is a direction cosine, not a vertical position coordinate or displacement magnitude; it is the neutron-detector analog of [z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the direction from the field-of-view voxel toward the neutron detector center has a component in the $+\hat{z}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_atomic_number
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Nuclear proton count of the fast ion species detected in charge exchange spectroscopy, uniquely identifying the element independently of its ionization state.
NAMES.long:
The fast ion atomic number $Z_n$ is the number of protons in the nucleus of the energetic (non-thermal) ion species observed via Fast Ion Charge eXchange (FICX) spectroscopy. As an intrinsic nuclear property, $Z_n$ is invariant with respect to ionization state and unambiguously identifies the element: $Z_n = 1$ for hydrogen isotopes (deuterium, tritium), $Z_n = 2$ for helium (alpha particles), $Z_n = 6$ for carbon, and $Z_n = 74$ for tungsten.

This quantity is the fast-ion-population counterpart of [ion_atomic_number](name:ion_atomic_number), which gives the same nuclear property for a general ion species. It is physically distinct from [fast_ion_charge](name:fast_ion_atomic_number), which specifies the ionic charge state $Z_\text{ion}$ — the net charge arising from electron removal — and which can vary for the same element at different ionization conditions. Together with [fast_ion_mass](name:ion_atomic_mass), the atomic number fully characterizes the fast ion species entering the spectral interpretation of FICX emission.

In charge exchange diagnostics, the fast ion species is identified prior to line inversion; $Z_n$ is an integer-valued input parameter rather than a derived measurement, taking values from 1 (hydrogenic fast ions in D-T plasmas) to the atomic number of the heaviest injected impurity species.

NAMES.name: floating_electrostatic_potential
NAMES.short: Floating electrostatic potential is the voltage-valued potential of an electrically isolated probe or surface when net current from the plasma is zero.
NAMES.long:
Floating electrostatic potential is the voltage-valued scalar potential established at an electrically isolated probe or surface when the net current from the plasma to that object is zero. It is a floating realization of [electrostatic_potential](name:electrostatic_potential), distinct from a prescribed wall voltage, material wall voltage, or applied bias.

Its defining current-balance condition is

$$
I_{\rm net}(\Phi_f) = 0
$$

where $\Phi_f$ is the floating potential expressed in volts and $I_{\rm net}$ is the total conventional electric current collected by the isolated object, expressed in amperes.

The value is determined by the balance of all included charged-particle current contributions. It is distinct from the adjacent plasma potential represented by [electrostatic_potential_at_wall](name:electrostatic_potential_at_wall). The corresponding [fluctuating floating electrostatic potential](name:fluctuating_floating_electrostatic_potential) describes variation about this floating value rather than the mean potential itself.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a positive test charge has greater electrostatic potential energy at the isolated object than at the chosen electrical reference.

sources.enhanced_context: Floating potential (Vf) measured by an embedded Langmuir probe, the electrostatic potential at which the net current to the probe is zero. Used to estimate plasma potential and electron temperature at the plasma-facing surface.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_argon_density
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Chord-averaged number density of argon ions along a specified plasma path, with contributions from all ionization stages summed together.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged argon ion number density is the argon ion concentration averaged along a specified chord through the plasma, including all ionization stages.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{Ar} = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}(\mathbf{r}(l))\,dl
$$

where $L$ is the chord length, $l$ is distance along the chord, $\mathbf{r}(l)$ is the position on the chord, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}$ is the local number density of argon ions in charge state $q$.

This path average is distinct from the local [argon ion density](name:argon_density) and from the plasma-volume average [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density).

NAMES.name: line_averaged_boron_density
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Line-averaged boron density is the total elemental boron number density averaged along a chord through the plasma. It includes neutral boron and all boron ionization states, giving a chord-averaged measure of elemental boron impurity content.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged boron density is the total elemental boron number density averaged along a chord through the plasma. It includes neutral boron and all ionization states of boron, so it represents the chord-averaged elemental boron impurity content rather than a local point value.

The line average over a chord of path length $L$ is defined by the path integral of the local charge-state-summed boron density along arc length $l$:

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{B},\ell} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \sum_{z=0}^{5} n_\mathrm{B}^{(z)}(l)\, dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{B},\ell}$ is the line-averaged boron density, $n_\mathrm{B}^{(z)}(l)$ is the local boron number density in ionization state $z$ at position $l$ along the chord, $z=0$ denotes neutral boron, $z=5$ denotes fully stripped B$^{5+}$, and $L$ is the total path length used for the average.

This quantity is a chord average of the charge-state-summed elemental [boron density](name:boron_density); it is not a charge-state-resolved boron density and does not exclude neutral boron. It differs from [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density), which averages the same elemental density over the confined plasma volume.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_carbon_density
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Line-averaged total number density of elemental carbon along a specified plasma chord, summed over neutral carbon and all ionic charge states through C6+.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged carbon density is the chord average of the total number density of elemental carbon, encompassing neutral carbon atoms and all ionic charge states from singly ionized C+ through fully stripped C6+.

It is defined from the local [carbon density](name:carbon_density) along the chord:

$$
\bar n_C = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_C(\ell)\,d\ell = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \sum_{z=0}^{6} n_{C^{z+}}(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\bar n_C$ is the line-averaged carbon density, $n_C(\ell)$ is the local carbon density in m$^{-3}$, $n_{C^{z+}}(\ell)$ is the local density of carbon charge state $z+$ in m$^{-3}$, $\ell$ is distance along the chord in m, and $L$ is the chord length in m. This chord average is distinct from [volume-averaged carbon density](name:volume_averaged_carbon_density), which averages over the confined plasma volume.

sources.parent_definition: Carbon

NAMES.name: line_averaged_deuterium_density
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Deuterium ion density averaged along a plasma chord is the mean local number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is charge-state-summed over ionized deuterium and excludes neutral or molecular deuterium and non-deuterium species.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium ion density averaged along a plasma chord is the mean local number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It represents the path-length mean of the local deuterium density along the specified chord, with deuterium treated as a species-level ion density.

The line average is defined by the path-length average of the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density):

$$
\langle n_D \rangle_\ell = \frac{1}{L} \int_{\ell_0}^{\ell_1} n_D(\ell) \, d\ell
$$

where $\langle n_D \rangle_\ell$ is the line-averaged deuterium density, $\ell$ is arclength along the chord, $\ell_0$ and $\ell_1$ are the endpoints of the averaging interval, $L = \ell_1 - \ell_0$ is the chord path length, and $n_D(\ell)$ is the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) at position $\ell$.

The local deuterium density entering the integral is charge-state-summed over ionized atomic charge states; for deuterium this reduces to the singly ionized deuteron population. Neutral deuterium atoms, molecular deuterium, and non-deuterium species are excluded. This quantity is a path average; local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) and [deuterium ion density averaged over the total plasma volume](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) are distinct quantities.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium

NAMES.name: line_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Chord-averaged ion number density of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species along a specified line of sight.
NAMES.long:
The deuterium-tritium density is the chord-averaged ion count per unit volume of the fictitious combined fuel pseudo-species formed by merging deuterium and tritium ions. It is derived from the local [deuterium-tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density) along a specified chord.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\bar{n}_{DT} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{DT}(l)\,dl
$$

where $\bar{n}_{DT}$ is the chord-averaged density, $L$ is the chord length, $l$ is distance along the chord, and $n_{DT}(l)$ is the local deuterium-tritium pseudo-species density. The quantity is a line average and must not be interpreted as the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density); both retain the deuterium-plus-tritium aggregation convention.

sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: line_averaged_effective_charge
NAMES.short: Line-averaged effective charge of the plasma, equal to the chord-length average of local effective ionic charge along a specified viewing path.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged effective charge is the chord-length mean of the local effective ionic charge encountered along a specified plasma-crossing path. It characterizes the impurity content weighted along that path rather than at a single location.

The defining relation is:

$$
\langle Z_\text{eff} \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L} \int_\mathcal{L} Z_\text{eff}(l)\,dl
$$

where $Z_\text{eff}(l)$ is the local effective charge at path coordinate $l$, $\mathcal{L}$ is the chord, and $L$ is its total length. The parent [effective charge](name:effective_charge) defines the local quantity being averaged. This path average is distinct from the [volume-averaged effective charge](name:volume_averaged_effective_charge), which weights the plasma volume rather than a chord.

sources.enhanced_context: Effective charge.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Effective charge

NAMES.name: line_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Energy-equivalent measure of the mean random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population, averaged uniformly along a specified plasma chord.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged electron temperature is the energy-equivalent measure of the mean random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population, averaged uniformly along a specified plasma chord. It is a spatially averaged form of the local [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature).

For a chord of length $L$, the defining relation is

$$
T_{e,\mathrm{line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L T_e(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $T_e(\ell)$ is the local electron temperature at path coordinate $\ell$, $L$ is the chord length, and $T_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the resulting line average.

The average is uniform with respect to distance along the specified chord and characterizes the bulk electron population. It differs from the [volume-averaged electron temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature), which averages over a confined plasma volume. Fast or suprathermal electrons are excluded unless explicitly included in the population being characterized.

sources.enhanced_context: Electron temperature (Te), line-averaged along a chord through the plasma. Represents the thermal energy of the bulk electron population averaged along the line of sight.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron temperature

NAMES.name: line_averaged_hydrogen_density
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Number density of hydrogen (protium) ions averaged along a specified chord through the plasma, representing path-normalized ion content.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged hydrogen density quantifies the chord-averaged concentration of protium ions along a specified path through the plasma. It is derived from the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density) and excludes neutral atomic hydrogen and heavier hydrogen isotopes.

The line-averaged density $\overline{n}_H$ is defined as

$$
\overline{n}_H = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_H(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_H(l)$ is the local hydrogen-ion number density at path coordinate $l$, and $L$ is the chord length. The average is over path length rather than plasma volume; the corresponding volume average is [volume_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen

NAMES.name: line_averaged_iron_density
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Line-averaged iron density is the path-length mean of total iron impurity-ion number density, summed over Fe1+ through Fe26+.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged iron density is the chord-length mean of the total iron ion number density along a specified line of sight. It includes all ionization states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ and does not resolve their individual contributions.

The line average is defined as

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe,line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{Fe}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe,line}}$ is the line-averaged density, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}(l)$ is the local iron ion number density at path coordinate $l$, and $L$ is the total chord length.

The local quantity being averaged is the charge-state-summed [iron density](name:iron_density). This chord average is distinct from [line_averaged_argon_density](name:line_averaged_argon_density), which applies the same path averaging to argon ions, and from a volume-averaged iron density, which averages over a plasma volume rather than a line of sight.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_lithium_density
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Path-length-averaged total number density of lithium ions along a specified plasma chord, summed over Li+ through fully stripped Li3+ and excluding neutral lithium.
NAMES.long:
This is the path-length average of lithium ion number density, summed over all ionization stages from Li$^+$ through fully stripped Li$^{3+}$, along a specified chord through the plasma.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{Li} \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{Li}(s)\,ds
$$

where $n_{Li}(s)$ is the local lithium ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $s$ is path length in meters along the chord, and $L$ is the total chord length in meters.

This quantity weights each path-length element equally and excludes neutral lithium. It differs from the [flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which averages over a separatrix, and from [volume-averaged lithium density](name:volume_averaged_lithium_density), which averages over confined plasma volume.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_total_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total ion number density averaged along a specified plasma chord, summing all ion species and charge states, including thermal and non-thermal ions.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged total ion density is the chord average of the local [total ion density](name:total_ion_density), including all ion species, resolved charge states, and thermal and non-thermal ion populations. It excludes electron density.

$$
n_{\mathrm{i,line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{i,total}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $l$ is distance along the chord, $L$ is chord length, $n_{\mathrm{i,total}}(l)$ is local total ion density, and $n_{\mathrm{i,line}}$ is the resulting line average. Unlike the [volume-averaged total ion density](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_density), it averages along a chord rather than throughout a volume.

sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: line_averaged_tritium_density
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Chord-averaged number density of tritium ions, obtained by averaging local tritium ion density along a specified chord.
NAMES.long:
Chord-averaged tritium ion density is the path-length mean of the local tritium ion number density along a specified chord. It is derived from the local [tritium_density](name:tritium_density) and represents the chord-integrated fuel content normalized by chord length.

$$
\overline{n}_T = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_T(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\overline{n}_T$ is the chord-averaged density, $n_T(\ell)$ is the local tritium ion density at path coordinate $\ell$, and $L$ is the chord length. The average includes the specified chord segment and is distinct from the confined-volume mean [volume_averaged_tritium_density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density) and from the corresponding helium-4 quantity [line_averaged_helium_4_density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density).

NAMES.name: motional_stark_radiance_at_spectral_line
NAMES.short: Photon-count radiance from an identified motional-Stark-split component of a spectral emission line, integrated along the viewing path and resolved by projected area and solid angle.
NAMES.long:
Motional-Stark radiance at a spectral line is the photon-count radiance emitted by moving neutral-beam atoms in one identified Stark-split component. It is integrated along the viewing path and defined per projected area normal to the viewing direction and per solid angle.

The line-integrated photon radiance is defined by

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MS,ph}} = \int_{\Delta\lambda_{\mathrm{MS}}} \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MS,ph},\lambda}(\lambda)\,d\lambda
$$

where $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MS,ph},\lambda}$ is the photon spectral radiance of the selected motional-Stark component, $\lambda$ is wavelength, and $\Delta\lambda_{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the wavelength interval assigned to that component. Unlike the energy-basis [radiance at a spectral line](name:radiance_at_spectral_line), this quantity counts photons rather than weighting them by photon energy. The selected component is distinguished by its motional-Stark wavelength displacement, related to the [fast-neutral-beam motional-Stark wavelength displacement](name:difference_of_fast_neutral_beam_motional_stark_wavelength_and_fast_neutral_beam_reference_wavelength_of_spectral_line).

NAMES.name: neutral_beam_atomic_number
NAMES.subject: neutral_beam
NAMES.short: Nuclear charge number of the neutral-beam species, equal to the integer count of protons in its nucleus and invariant across ionization states and isotopes.
NAMES.long:
The atomic number $Z$ of a neutral-beam species is the integer count of protons in its nucleus. It is an invariant elemental identifier that remains unchanged when the element is ionized or when a different isotope is considered.

The nuclear charge associated with the element is defined by

$$
Q = Z e
$$

where $Q$ is the nuclear charge and $e$ is the elementary charge. The neutral-beam qualifier identifies the species context, not a different nuclear property. This quantity is the neutral-beam specialization of [atomic_number](name:atomic_number) and has the same elemental meaning as [ion_atomic_number](name:ion_atomic_number) for the corresponding ion species; it does not specify isotope mass or instantaneous charge state.

sources.enhanced_context: Ion charge (Z) of the diagnostic neutral beam particle used in Beam Emission Spectroscopy (BES) measurements within the charge exchange diagnostic. Specifies the beam ion charge state for spectral line identification and cross-section calculations.

NAMES.name: total_ion_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, with all species and charge states contributing according to their number densities.
NAMES.long:
The total ion temperature is the density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The local effective temperature is defined by

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} n_s T_s}{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} n_s}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density and $T_s$ is the ion temperature of species or charge state $s$, and $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of included thermal ion populations. Thus, “total” denotes a density-weighted combination, not an arithmetic sum of temperatures. Spatially transformed instances apply line or volume averaging to this combined quantity, as in [line_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature) and [volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature); the underlying species-resolved quantity is [ion_temperature](name:ion_temperature).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted random kinetic energy of the included thermal ions is positive.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_total_ion_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, with all species and charge states contributing by number density and averaged along a specified plasma chord.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged total ion temperature is the line average of the local density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The chord average is defined by

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{line}} = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{C}} T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\ell)\,d\ell}{\int_{\mathcal{C}}d\ell}
$$

where $T_{i,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-averaged quantity, $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\ell)$ is the local [total ion temperature](name:total_ion_temperature), $\ell$ is path length along the chord, and $\mathcal{C}$ is the specified chord. Species and charge states are combined by number density before the line average is taken. Unlike the [volume-averaged total ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity weights positions by chord length rather than plasma volume.

sources.enhanced_context: Line-averaged ion temperature (Ti) averaged over all ion species. A key global thermal parameter representing the mean ion thermal energy along a chord through the plasma.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: accumulated_deuterated_methane_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: deuterated_methane
NAMES.short: Cumulative deuterated methane (CD4) delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count units per neutral molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral deuterated methane molecules introduced by gas injection after plasma breakdown, represented using an equivalent-electron counting convention.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = 10N_{\mathrm{CD4}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{CD4}}$ is the cumulative number of injected CD4 molecules. The factor 10 is the sum of carbon's six atomic-number contributions and one contribution from each of the four deuterium atoms.

The inventory is specific to deuterated methane and excludes gas introduced before plasma breakdown or from other species. It differs from [deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection), which counts only the deuterium-atom contribution.

sources.enhanced_context: Beryllium.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium

NAMES.name: accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, assigning two count units to each atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It represents delivered atomic inventory, not the number of free plasma electrons or the ionization state of the helium-3.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}(t')\,dt'
$$

Here, $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}=2$ is the helium-3 atomic number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the helium-3 atom delivery rate in atoms per second, $t$ and $t'$ are times in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

The quantity includes only helium-3 delivered after breakdown and is cumulative rather than instantaneous. The corresponding instantaneous delivery rate is [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), while [accumulated helium-3 prefill count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection) covers delivery before breakdown.

NAMES.name: accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of helium-3 atoms introduced by gas injection during plasma prefill before plasma breakdown, with two count units assigned per atom.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the cumulative inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It covers injection before plasma breakdown and excludes helium-3 introduced after breakdown.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}} N_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}} = 2\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}=2$ is the helium-3 atomic number, $N_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the injected helium-3 atom count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the injection rate in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times in s.

This is the pre-breakdown counterpart of [accumulated helium-3 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection); [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) represents the instantaneous rate rather than the accumulated inventory.

NAMES.name: accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of lithium introduced by gas injection during plasma prefill, with three count units assigned to each lithium atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the accumulated lithium inventory delivered by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as equivalent electrons rather than as a count of free plasma electrons.

The defining relation is:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}} N_{\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{prefill}}
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron inventory, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{prefill}}$ is the accumulated number of injected lithium atoms, and $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is lithium's atomic number.

The quantity includes only lithium introduced during prefill by gas injection. It is distinct from the post-breakdown [accumulated lithium count](name:accumulated_lithium_count), while [lithium count](name:lithium_count) defines the corresponding equivalent-electron convention without the prefill and accumulation-locus restriction.

NAMES.name: accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: methane_carbon_13
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of carbon-13-labeled methane delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, with ten count units assigned to each neutral 13CH4 molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of neutral carbon-13-labeled methane introduced by gas injection after plasma breakdown. It counts injected molecules rather than free electrons retained in the plasma.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=10\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}(t')\,dt'
$$

Here $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the injection rate of neutral methane molecules in s$^{-1}$, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$, $t$, and $t'$ are times in seconds. The factor 10 is the sum of six equivalent electrons from carbon and four from hydrogen in each neutral molecule; carbon-13 labeling does not change the atomic number. The quantity excludes methane introduced during prefill, which is represented by [methane carbon-13 prefill count](name:methane_carbon_13_prefill_count), and is the time integral of the corresponding [methane carbon-13 source rate](name:methane_carbon_13_source_rate).

NAMES.name: accumulated_oxygen_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown oxygen inventory delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with eight count units per neutral oxygen atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of oxygen atoms admitted after plasma breakdown through gas injection, converted to an equivalent-electron count. Each oxygen atom contributes eight equivalent electrons, corresponding to oxygen's atomic number.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 8N_{\mathrm{O}}(t) = 8\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the cumulative oxygen-atom count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen-atom injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation time. The count quantities are dimensionless and the injection rate has units of inverse seconds.

Only oxygen delivered after plasma breakdown by gas injection is included; prefill oxygen is excluded and is represented by [accumulated_oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection). The instantaneous counterpart is [oxygen_source_rate](name:oxygen_source_rate), while [accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection) uses the corresponding atomic-number weighting for carbon.

NAMES.name: accumulated_oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Cumulative oxygen gas introduced during the prefill phase by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each oxygen atom contributes 8 count units equal to its atomic number.
NAMES.long:
The prefill phase precedes plasma breakdown, during which controlled gas injection establishes an initial neutral gas background in the vessel. This quantity accumulates the total oxygen inventory delivered during that phase, representing each oxygen atom as 8 equivalent electrons equal to the atomic number $Z_\mathrm{O} = 8$.

The equivalent-electron inventory is defined as:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{O} \cdot N_\mathrm{O}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{O}$ is the total number of oxygen atoms injected during the prefill interval and $Z_\mathrm{O} = 8$ is the atomic number of oxygen.

The count is inferred from calibrated gas injection valve records integrated over the prefill interval, from the start of the prefill phase through plasma breakdown. It is the accumulated component of oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection and follows the same equivalent-electron convention applied to helium-3 in [accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection) and to lithium in [accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection). Post-breakdown oxygen injection is tracked separately by [oxygen_count](name:accumulated_oxygen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

NAMES.name: accumulated_particle_count_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of particles released by ablation from an injected pellet up to a specified position along its trajectory.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative particle release from pellet ablation as the pellet travels through the plasma. It counts particles removed from the pellet up to the specified trajectory position, rather than particles remaining in the pellet.

The accumulated release at path distance $\ell$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{abl}}(\ell)=\int_{\ell_0}^{\ell}\frac{dN_{\mathrm{abl}}}{d\ell'}\,d\ell'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{abl}}$ is the dimensionless released-particle count, $\ell$ and $\ell'$ are distances along the pellet trajectory in m, $\ell_0$ is the trajectory entry position, and $dN_{\mathrm{abl}}/d\ell'$ is the local ablation release per unit path distance.

The count is nondecreasing along the trajectory when the ablation release rate is nonnegative. It represents deposited pellet material and is distinct from the initial pellet inventory given by [count of pellet](name:count_of_pellet).

NAMES.name: accumulated_total_gas_count_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short: Accumulated total gas count at midplane due to gas injection is the cumulative unweighted count of neutral gas particles introduced by all injection valves near the equatorial midplane over the specified accumulation interval. It sums all injected species and is not weighted by neutral electron count, atomic number, mass, or valve identity.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated total gas count at midplane due to gas injection is the cumulative unweighted count of neutral gas particles introduced by all gas-injection valves assigned to the equatorial-midplane valve group. It aggregates all injected species and all valves in that group; each gas particle contributes one count to the total inventory.

The accumulation over a specified time interval is the time integral of the unweighted total midplane gas-particle source rate:

$$
N_{\mathrm{gas,mid}}(t_1;t_0) = \int_{t_0}^{t_1} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{gas,mid}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{gas,mid}}$ is the accumulated dimensionless count, $t_0$ and $t_1$ are the interval endpoints in seconds, $t'$ is the integration time in seconds, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{gas,mid}}$ is the [total gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection](name:total_gas_source_rate_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection) in particles per second, summed over all midplane gas-injection valves and all injected species.

For a post-breakdown accumulated inventory, $t_0$ is the plasma-breakdown time; for a prefill inventory, the interval is the pre-breakdown gas-fill interval. This quantity is the midplane contribution to the all-position [accumulated total particle count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection), not a per-valve count and not an equivalent-electron inventory. Species-specific inventories such as [accumulated neon count due to gas injection], [accumulated nitrogen count due to gas injection], and [accumulated carbon count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection) are separate components of the injected species inventory.

NAMES.name: accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short: Accumulated total particle count due to gas injection is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of neutral gas introduced by gas injection over the prefill interval or since plasma breakdown, summed over all species as a vessel-wide total.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated total particle count due to gas injection is the vessel-wide cumulative inventory of neutral gas introduced by gas injection over a defined accumulation window, summed over all injected species using the equivalent-electron convention. Post-breakdown accumulation starts at plasma breakdown, while prefill accumulation covers gas introduced before plasma breakdown. It counts the electrons that the injected neutral particles would contribute if fully ionized, rather than the unweighted number of neutral atoms or molecules.

The accumulated count over an interval beginning at $t_0$ is defined by the species-weighted time integral of the injection rates:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq}(t;t_0)=\sum_s z_s^\mathrm{eq} N_s(t;t_0)=\sum_s z_s^\mathrm{eq}\int_{t_0}^{t}\Gamma_s(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_\mathrm{eq}$ is the dimensionless total equivalent-electron count, $s$ indexes all injected neutral species, $z_s^\mathrm{eq}$ is the dimensionless number of bound electrons in one neutral injected particle of species $s$ when fully ionized, $N_s$ is the dimensionless accumulated injected-particle count for species $s$, $\Gamma_s$ is the injection rate of species $s$ with dimensions of count per time, $t'$ is integration time, and $t$ is the evaluation time. For post-breakdown accumulation, $t_0$ is the plasma-breakdown time; for prefill accumulation, $t_0$ is the start of the prefill interval and $t$ is no later than plasma breakdown.

This quantity is a vessel-wide total over injection locations and species. It excludes gas not introduced by gas injection and excludes location-resolved partial sums unless those partial sums are explicitly combined over a complete injector partition. Species-resolved accumulated counts, such as [accumulated neon count](name:accumulated_neon_count) and [accumulated carbon count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection), are contributions to the sum over $s$ before forming the total.

NAMES.name: accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of tritium atoms delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each tritium atom corresponds to one equivalent electron.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated tritium count due to gas injection is the running total of tritium ($^3\mathrm{H}$) atoms introduced to the plasma vessel through gas injection valves, accumulated continuously from plasma breakdown onward. The quantity is dimensionless, representing each injected atom as an equivalent-electron contribution scaled by its atomic number.

For tritium, whose atomic number is $Z = 1$, the equivalent-electron inventory equals the raw atom count directly:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z \cdot N_\mathrm{atoms} = N_\mathrm{atoms}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{atoms}$ is the total number of tritium atoms injected after breakdown. The equivalent-electron convention provides a species-independent basis for comparing injected particle inventories — for higher-$Z$ species such as argon ($Z = 18$), the multiplier is correspondingly larger.

This is the time-integrated form of tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection, accumulating monotonically as gas is puffed after breakdown. Tritium introduced before breakdown is tracked separately as [tritium_prefill_count](name:tritium_prefill_count). The deuterium analog in the same equivalent-electron framework is [deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection).

NAMES.name: ammonia_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia
NAMES.short: Inventory of ammonia (NH3) in the plasma vessel expressed as an equivalent-electron count, where each NH3 molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons equal to the total electron count of neutral ammonia.
NAMES.long:
The ammonia equivalent-electron count represents the NH3 inventory in the plasma vessel using a species-neutral currency: each ammonia molecule is assigned 10 equivalent electrons, the sum of the atomic numbers of its constituent atoms — nitrogen ($Z_\mathrm{N} = 7$) plus three hydrogen atoms each with $Z_\mathrm{H} = 1$.

The defining conversion is:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = 10 \times N_\mathrm{NH_3}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{NH_3}$ is the number of ammonia molecules and $N_\mathrm{eq}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count.

Ammonia is used in fusion devices as a controlled impurity for radiative seeding, plasma termination, or disruption mitigation. The equivalent-electron representation provides a unified basis for comparing the total electron contribution across different injected species. This general count is partitioned by injection phase: [accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count) tracks NH3 delivered since plasma breakdown, while [ammonia_prefill_count](name:ammonia_prefill_count) captures the pre-breakdown prefill contribution. The closely related deuterated variant is characterized by [ammonia_deuterated_count](name:ammonia_deuterated_count), which applies the same 10-electron-per-molecule convention to ND3. Values are inferred from calibrated valve-actuation and gas-flow records.

NAMES.name: accumulated_ammonia_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of ammonia molecules introduced into the plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count units assigned to each neutral NH3 molecule.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated ammonia count is the cumulative post-breakdown amount of NH3 introduced into the plasma vessel, represented using an equivalent-electron accounting convention. It is the post-breakdown component of the total [ammonia count](name:ammonia_count), not a direct count of free plasma electrons.

$$
C_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} = (Z_\mathrm{N}+3Z_\mathrm{H})N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} = 10N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}
$$

Here, $C_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the cumulative number of ammonia molecules introduced after plasma breakdown, and $Z_\mathrm{N}=7$ and $Z_\mathrm{H}=1$ are the atomic numbers of nitrogen and hydrogen. The quantity excludes ammonia introduced during prefill, which is represented by [ammonia prefill count](name:ammonia_prefill_count), and does not represent instantaneous injection rate, retained neutral inventory, ionization state, or actual free-electron content.

NAMES.name: ammonia_deuterated_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia_deuterated
NAMES.short: Deuterated ammonia (ND3) count is the cumulative molecular inventory of ND3 expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons, from nitrogen plus three deuterium atoms.
NAMES.long:
Deuterated ammonia (ND3) count is the cumulative molecular inventory of ND3 expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It is a bookkeeping count formed by weighting each ND3 molecule by the total atomic-number content of its constituent atoms.

The defining relation is:

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3 Z_{\mathrm{D}}) N_{\mathrm{ND_3}} = 10 N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}$ is the deuterated-ammonia equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}$ is the number of ND3 molecules, $Z_{\mathrm{N}} = 7$ is the atomic number of nitrogen, and $Z_{\mathrm{D}} = 1$ is the atomic number of deuterium.

The scope is restricted to the fixed molecular species ND3; it is not a sum over arbitrary injected gasses, ammonia isotopologues, fragments, ions, or reaction products. Time-window or phase qualifiers define specializations, such as [accumulated deuterated-ammonia count](name:accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count), without changing the per-molecule weighting.

NAMES.name: accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia_deuterated
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3), expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count units per molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative number of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3) molecules introduced after plasma breakdown, converted to an equivalent-electron count. It is the post-breakdown contribution to [ammonia_deuterated_count](name:ammonia_deuterated_count), distinct from the prefill contribution [ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count](name:ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count).

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3Z_{\mathrm{D}})N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} = 10N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}$ is the cumulative neutral-molecule count after breakdown, and $Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ are the atomic numbers of nitrogen and deuterium. This is a bookkeeping quantity, not the number of free electrons in the plasma and not an instantaneous injection rate.

NAMES.name: ammonia_deuterated_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ammonia_deuterated
NAMES.short: Instantaneous molecular injection rate of deuterated ammonia (ND3) supplied to the plasma vessel by gas injection.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the rate at which deuterated ammonia (ND3) molecules are admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection. It counts ND3 molecules directly rather than converting them to an equivalent-electron inventory.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of injected ND3 molecules and $t$ is time. The rate is distinct from the [ammonia source rate](name:ammonia_source_rate), which refers to NH3 molecules, and its time integral gives the injected molecular inventory represented by the [accumulated deuterated ammonia count](name:accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count).

NAMES.name: argon_count
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Count of argon atoms expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory, where each argon atom contributes 18 equivalent electrons equal to its atomic number.
NAMES.long:
The argon count quantifies the number of argon atoms in terms of a dimensionless equivalent-electron inventory. Each argon atom is assigned a contribution equal to its atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Ar} = 18$, giving:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{Ar} \cdot N_\mathrm{Ar}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{Ar}$ is the number of argon atoms and $N_\mathrm{eq}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count. This normalization places argon on a common electron-equivalent basis with other injected species, enabling direct comparison across impurity inventories.

The [accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count) is a specific instance representing the cumulative argon delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown. For the local particle density of argon ions in the plasma, see [argon_density](name:argon_density).

NAMES.name: accumulated_argon_count
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Accumulated argon count is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of argon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. Each argon atom contributes 18 equivalent electrons, equal to its atomic number; this is delivered inventory, not plasma electron content or ionization state.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated argon count is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of argon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. Each delivered argon atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}=18$ equivalent electrons, equal to the atomic number of argon.

The accumulated count is defined by integrating the delivered argon atom injection rate from the plasma-breakdown time:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t')\,dt', \qquad Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron argon count, $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the dimensionless atomic number of argon, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate in atoms per second, $t$ is time in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time in seconds.

This quantity includes only argon delivered after breakdown. Argon introduced before breakdown belongs to the pre-breakdown inventory represented by [argon_count](name:argon_count); the accumulated value is not a measure of free electrons, plasma argon content, retained argon, or argon ionization state, and is not reduced by subsequent pumping, exhaust, wall retention, ionization, radiation, or redistribution.

NAMES.name: beryllium_source_rate
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Electron-equivalent beryllium particle-source rate, obtained by weighting the net beryllium-nucleus rate by beryllium’s atomic number of four.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the electron-equivalent particle-source rate associated with beryllium. It counts each beryllium nucleus as four electron-equivalent particles rather than as one nucleus.

The defining conversion is:

$$
S_{\mathrm{Be}}^{(e)} = Z_{\mathrm{Be}} S_{\mathrm{Be}} = 4S_{\mathrm{Be}}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{Be}}^{(e)}$ is the electron-equivalent beryllium source rate, $S_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the net beryllium-nucleus source rate, and $Z_{\mathrm{Be}}=4$ is beryllium’s atomic number.

The weighting is a nuclear-charge bookkeeping convention, not a statement that four free electrons are created or removed. The quantity is distinct from the actual [electron source rate](name:electron_source_rate) and from the [beryllium density](name:beryllium_density); a positive rate denotes net beryllium supply, while a negative rate denotes net removal.

NAMES.name: carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory introduced as carbon gas during plasma prefill, with six count units assigned to each injected carbon atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of carbon introduced by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, before plasma breakdown. It represents injected carbon atoms rather than an instantaneous injection rate.

The defining relation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{C,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{C}}N_{\mathrm{C}} = 6N_{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the cumulative number of injected carbon atoms, and $Z_{\mathrm{C}}=6$ is the carbon atomic number. Both counts are dimensionless.

The prefill interval ends at plasma breakdown, so post-breakdown carbon delivery is represented separately by [accumulated carbon count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection). The aggregation convention parallels [accumulated hydrogen prefill count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count), with the atomic number providing the equivalent-electron weighting.

NAMES.name: coolant_pressure
NAMES.short: Absolute static pressure of the coolant or working fluid at a plant-system component port, referenced to perfect vacuum rather than atmospheric or another gage reference.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the local thermodynamic pressure of the coolant or working fluid at a component-port interface, with perfect vacuum as the zero-pressure reference. Static pressure is the isotropic mechanical stress of the fluid and excludes kinetic-energy contributions associated with bulk flow.

$$
\boldsymbol{\sigma}=-p_{\mathrm{abs}}\mathbf{I}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the isotropic fluid Cauchy stress, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the absolute static pressure, and $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor.

The value represents local pressure at the port, not stagnation pressure, pressure drop, or pressure difference. At a cooling-circuit inlet, it is related to [cooling-circuit inlet pressure](name:pressure_at_cooling_circuit_inlet), while [coolant flow through a plant component port](name:coolant_flow_of_plant_component_port) describes mass transport rather than mechanical pressure.

sources.enhanced_context: Fluid pressure (p) at a component port in the balance-of-plant power conversion system. Characterizes the thermodynamic state of the working fluid at the interface between connected system components.

NAMES.name: coolant_temperature
NAMES.short: Coolant temperature is the absolute thermodynamic temperature of a coolant or working fluid at a plant-system component port. It characterizes the local thermal state of the fluid stream.
NAMES.long:
Coolant temperature is the absolute thermodynamic temperature of a coolant or working fluid at a plant-system component port. It is a local equilibrium state variable of the fluid and may denote an unspecified port unless the locus is restricted by a more specific name.

The absolute temperature is the thermodynamic variable conjugate to entropy in the fundamental relation for internal energy, equivalently defined by the entropy derivative:

$$
\frac{1}{T} = \left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial U}\right)_{V,\{N_i\}}
$$

where $T$ is coolant temperature, $S$ is entropy in joules per kelvin, $U$ is internal energy in joules, $V$ is volume in cubic meters, and $N_i$ is the amount of species $i$ in moles held fixed in the derivative.

This name is not specific to inlet or outlet; use [coolant_temperature_at_inlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_inlet) or [coolant_temperature_at_outlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_outlet) when the port location is part of the quantity identity. It denotes the fluid temperature, not the solid component temperature, wall temperature, or a temperature difference across the component.

sources.enhanced_context: Fluid temperature at a port (inlet or outlet) of a balance-of-plant power conversion system component. Characterises the thermal state of the working fluid at that connection point for thermodynamic cycle analysis.
sources.leaf_definition: Fluid temperature
sources.parent_definition: Set of ports (input or output) of the component

NAMES.name: core_density_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Number density of atoms of a specified constituent species within the condensed core of a pellet before it is shattered for disruption mitigation.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the number of atoms of a specified constituent species per unit volume of the condensed pellet core before fragmentation. For molecular materials, the count is assigned to individual atoms rather than molecules.

$$
n_s = \frac{N_s}{V_{\mathrm{core}}}
$$

where $n_s$ is the species atom number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_s$ is the dimensionless number of atoms of species $s$, and $V_{\mathrm{core}}$ is the core volume in m$^3$. It is the core-specific derivative of [density of pellet](name:density_of_pellet), restricted to the constituent species and core region.

The quantity describes the unshattered pellet core and is distinct from [shattered pellet fragment density](name:shattered_pellet_fragment_density), which applies to an individual fragment after shattering.

sources.enhanced_context: Number density of an atomic species composing the core of a shattered pellet injector (SPI) pellet. Characterizes the material composition of the pellet core used for disruption mitigation.
sources.leaf_definition: Density of the species
sources.parent_definition: Atomic species in the shell composition

NAMES.name: count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of atoms delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count weighted by each species’ atomic number.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of a specified atomic gas species delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed using equivalent-electron count units. Material introduced during the prefill phase is excluded.

For species $s$, the equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq},s}(t) = Z_s N_s(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq},s}$ and $N_s$ are dimensionless cumulative counts, and $Z_s$ is the dimensionless atomic number of species $s$. The count increases by $Z_s$ for every delivered atom and represents an atomic inventory, not an instantaneous injection rate or an ionization-state population. The [carbon count due to gas injection](name:carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection) and [helium-4 count due to gas injection](name:helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection) are species-specific instances of this definition.

NAMES.name: carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of carbon atoms delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count weighted by the carbon atomic number. Each injected neutral carbon atom contributes six counts, and prefill material is excluded.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of carbon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Material introduced during the prefill phase is excluded.

For carbon, the equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq},C}(t) = Z_C N_C(t) = 6 N_C(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq},C}$ is the carbon equivalent-electron count, $N_C$ is the cumulative count of delivered carbon atoms after breakdown, and $Z_C=6$ is the atomic number of carbon.

The count increases by six for every delivered neutral carbon atom and represents an atomic inventory, not an instantaneous injection rate or an ionization-state population. This is the carbon-specific instance of [count due to gas injection](name:count_due_to_gas_injection); temporal specializations such as [accumulated carbon count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection) specify how the running total is reported in time.

NAMES.name: accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown carbon inventory from gas injection, expressed as six equivalent-electron counts for every injected neutral carbon atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of carbon atoms delivered by gas injection, represented as an equivalent-electron count. It excludes carbon introduced during the plasma prefill phase and does not represent an instantaneous source rate or a charge-state-resolved ion inventory.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}(t)=6N_{\mathrm{C}}(t)=6\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{gas}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the cumulative number of injected carbon atoms, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{gas}}$ is the carbon injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation time. The factor 6 is carbon's atomic number. This is the post-breakdown component of [carbon count due to gas injection](name:carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection) and is distinct from [carbon prefill count due to gas injection](name:carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).
