NAMES.name: count_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Total discrete particle inventory of a pellet, encompassing both the individual atom count of the pellet material and the propellant gas-molecule count carried with the pellet.
NAMES.long: The count of a pellet captures the total discrete particle inventory attributable to one injected pellet, abstracting over both its solid material constituents and its gas-phase payload. The [atomic count](name:atomic_count_of_pellet) tallies every individual atom present in the pellet, counting each atom once regardless of whether the propellant material is monatomic, diatomic, or molecular in form. The [gas count] enumerates the propellant gas molecules carried with the pellet, representing the gas-phase component of the overall particle inventory. Together these two child quantities partition the total pellet particle inventory and are applied in pellet fueling efficiency analysis, particle balance accounting, and ablation modeling for pellet injection systems.

NAMES.name: atomic_count_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Number of individual atoms associated with a pellet, counted independently of molecular bonding, constituent species, or physical layer.
NAMES.long:
Atomic count is the inventory of individual atoms associated with one pellet, including atoms bound in molecules and atoms in distinct material layers. It is the atomic component of [count of pellet](name:count_of_pellet), which also includes separately counted gas molecules.

For constituent entity types indexed by $i$, the atomic inventory is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{atom}} = \sum_i a_i N_i
$$

where $N_i$ is the number of entities of type $i$ and $a_i$ is the number of atoms in each entity; molecular multiplicity is represented by [molecular atomic multiplicity](name:molecular_atomic_multiplicity). The whole-pellet value is unnormalized. Layer-restricted values, such as [core atomic count of pellet](name:core_atomic_count_of_pellet) and [outer atomic count of pellet](name:outer_atomic_count_of_pellet), partition the same atomic inventory, while [normalized atomic count of pellet](name:normalized_atomic_count_of_pellet) applies a scaling convention.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the pellet contains atoms and each counted atom contributes +1 to the inventory.

NAMES.name: core_atomic_count_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Core atomic count of a pellet is the total inventory of atomic nuclei in its innermost material layer, independent of molecular bonding, phase, or species.
NAMES.long:
Core atomic count of a pellet is the total inventory of atomic nuclei contained in the pellet's innermost material layer. Molecules, compounds, and mixtures are converted to their constituent atoms before summation, regardless of molecular bonding or phase.

For constituent entity types indexed by $i$, the core inventory is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{core}} = \sum_i a_i N_{i,\mathrm{core}}
$$

where $N_{i,\mathrm{core}}$ is the number of entities of type $i$ in the core layer and $a_i$ is the number of atoms in each entity. The value is an unnormalized component of [atomic count of pellet](name:atomic_count_of_pellet); together with [outer atomic count of pellet](name:outer_atomic_count_of_pellet), it partitions the whole-pellet atomic inventory when those layers form the complete pellet.

NAMES.name: deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of deuterium atoms delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count; each deuterium atom contributes one count, and prefill material is excluded.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of deuterium atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed using equivalent-electron count units. Material introduced during the prefill phase is excluded.

For deuterium, the equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq},D}(t) = Z_D N_D(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq},D}$ and $N_D$ are dimensionless cumulative counts, and $Z_D$ is the dimensionless atomic number of deuterium, equal to one. Thus, the count increases by one for every delivered deuterium atom and represents an atomic inventory, not an instantaneous injection rate or an ionization-state population. This is the deuterium-specific instance of [count due to gas injection](name:count_due_to_gas_injection), distinct from the helium-4 inventory [helium-4 count due to gas injection](name:helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection) and from the prefill inventory [deuterium prefill count](name:deuterium_prefill_count).

NAMES.name: diameter_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Transverse extent of the intact cylindrical pellet before injection and shattering, defined as the full width of its circular cross-section perpendicular to the pellet axis.
NAMES.long:
Transverse extent of the intact cylindrical pellet before injection and shattering is the full width of its circular cross-section measured perpendicular to the pellet axis. It defines the pellet cross-sectional geometry before fragmentation, ablation, or interaction with the plasma.

For an ideal right circular cylindrical pellet, the diameter and axial length determine the pellet volume by

$$
V_\mathrm{pellet} = \frac{\pi}{4} d_\mathrm{pellet}^2 L_\mathrm{pellet}
$$

where $V_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the pellet volume, $d_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the pellet diameter, and $L_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the [length of pellet](name:length_of_pellet).

This quantity excludes the axial extent of the pellet, which is the [length of pellet](name:length_of_pellet), and excludes characteristic sizes of shattered fragments, ablated material, or the post-shattering material cloud.

sources.enhanced_context: Physical diameter of a shattered pellet injector (SPI) pellet prior to injection and shattering. A key geometric parameter determining the pellet mass and material inventory delivered to the plasma for disruption mitigation.

sources.parent_definition: Information related to the pellet

NAMES.name: efficiency_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system converts input power or energy into a specified useful output, abstracting over thermal and net efficiency definitions.
NAMES.long:
The efficiency of a plant system is a dimensionless performance metric expressing the fraction of input power or energy that the plant converts into a specified useful output. The exact physical scope depends on the efficiency type applied: [thermal efficiency](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system) characterizes heat-to-work conversion across all thermodynamic conversion stages, while [net efficiency](name:net_efficiency_of_plant_system) accounts for the signed ratio of exported electrical power to total plant electrical consumption including recirculating power.

The general defining relation takes the form:

$$
\eta = \frac{W_\text{out}}{W_\text{in}}
$$

where $W_\text{out}$ is the useful output (work, exported electrical power, or heat converted to work) and $W_\text{in}$ is the total input power or energy over the same operating interval.

Efficiency is evaluated from calorimetric heat-flow surveys, electrical generation meters, and auxiliary power consumption measurements across all plant subsystems. For fusion facilities, thermal conversion efficiencies in steam-cycle plants lie in the range 30–45%, and net electrical efficiencies are further reduced by recirculating power fractions for heating, current drive, and cooling systems.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the plant system delivers net useful output, so that $W_\text{out} > 0$.

NAMES.name: electron_source_rate_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection is the charge-weighted electron-equivalent production rate from ablation and ionization of pellet material at a specified position along the injected pellet trajectory.
NAMES.long:
Electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection is the charge-weighted electron-equivalent production rate from ablation and ionization of pellet material at a specified position along the injected pellet trajectory. It counts the free-electron source associated with material reaching that path position, not the electron concentration of the surrounding plasma.

For trajectory coordinate $\ell$ and time $t$, the local rate is defined by the charge-weighted sum over ablated pellet constituents contributing at that same path position:

$$
S_e(\ell,t) = \sum_a Z_a^\mathrm{eff}(\ell,t)\,\dot{N}_a(\ell,t)
$$

where $S_e$ is the electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection, $a$ indexes the pellet constituents or represented charge-state groups, $\dot{N}_a$ is the local production rate of constituent $a$ by ablation and ionization, and $Z_a^\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective number of free electrons contributed by one produced constituent. For a fully ionized atomic constituent, $Z_a^\mathrm{eff}$ reduces to its nuclear charge.

This is a path-position rate, not a source density per distance along the pellet trajectory or a volume-integrated source. The [electron source rate due to injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection) is obtained only after aggregating the appropriate local electron-equivalent contributions, while [electron density of pellet path] describes electron concentration along the same trajectory. The [accumulated particle count at pellet path due to pellet injection](name:accumulated_particle_count_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection) is an unweighted cumulative particle count; it is not an electron-equivalent accumulated source unless the same charge weighting and time integration are applied.

The value is non-negative and is zero where injected pellet material at the considered path position does not produce free electrons.

sources.enhanced_context: Ablation rate of particles along the pellet path, giving the number of electrons released per unit time at each position along the pellet trajectory as it ablates inside the plasma.

NAMES.name: energy_of_plant_component_port
NAMES.short: Energy of a plant component port is the cumulative amount of energy transferred across a plant-component port for a specified energy-transfer channel. It is the time integral of the corresponding port power and is the parent concept for forms such as thermal energy extracted through a cooling loop.
NAMES.long:
Energy of a plant component port is the cumulative amount of energy transferred across a port of a plant component during a specified time interval. It represents the time-integrated counterpart of the relevant port power for the same component, port, and energy-transfer channel.

The cumulative port energy for a chosen energy-transfer channel is defined by integrating the corresponding port power over time:

$$
E_{\mathrm{port}}(t) = \int_{t_0}^{t} P_{\mathrm{port}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{port}}$ is the energy of the plant component port, $P_{\mathrm{port}}$ is the corresponding port power for the same component, port, and energy-transfer channel, and $t_0$ is the beginning of the accumulation interval.

This parent quantity does not specify the physical form, carrier, or mechanism of the energy transfer. Those restrictions belong to more specific child quantities, such as the [thermal energy of a plant component port](name:thermal_energy_of_plant_component_port), and it is distinct from instantaneous port power, such as [thermal power of a plant component port](name:thermal_power_of_plant_component_port).

NAMES.name: ethane_count
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short: Ethane equivalent-electron count is the inventory of ethane molecules expressed as the number of electrons in the corresponding neutral C2H6 molecules, assigning 18 counts per molecule.
NAMES.long:
Ethane equivalent-electron count is the ethane-only molecular inventory expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. Each neutral ethane molecule contributes the total atomic number of its constituent atoms.

The defining relation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq},\mathrm{C_2H_6}} = 18\,N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq},\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the ethane equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the number of neutral ethane molecules represented by the inventory. The factor $18$ is the sum of the atomic numbers of two carbon atoms and six hydrogen atoms in one neutral ethane molecule.

This quantity is scoped to ethane alone and is not a generic sum over multiple injected gas species. The [accumulated ethane count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) is the cumulative form of this same ethane-only equivalent-electron count.

NAMES.name: accumulated_ethane_count
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of ethane molecules injected after plasma breakdown, assigning 18 equivalent-electron counts to each neutral C2H6 molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the post-breakdown cumulative ethane-gas inventory expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral C2H6 molecule contributes 18 counts: 12 from its two carbon atoms and 6 from its six hydrogen atoms.

The accumulated count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 18\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the ethane molecule injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation time.

This quantity is the accumulated post-breakdown form of the [ethane count](name:ethane_count) convention. It excludes ethane introduced during prefill, represented by [ethane prefill count](name:ethane_prefill_count), and differs from the instantaneous [ethane source rate](name:ethane_source_rate).

sources.enhanced_context: Ethane (C2H6).

sources.parent_definition: Ethane (C2H6)

NAMES.name: ethane_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short: Instantaneous ethane-gas injection rate into the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent electrons per second, with 18 equivalent electrons assigned to each neutral C2H6 molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which neutral ethane molecules are delivered to the plasma vessel, converted to an equivalent-electron rate. It counts the electrons associated with neutral molecular composition, not free electrons produced by ionization.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron injection rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the neutral ethane molecular injection rate in molecules per second, and $t$ is time in seconds. The factor $18=2\times6+6\times1$ is the total atomic-number electron count of one C2H6 molecule.

This is an instantaneous rate rather than a cumulative inventory; its time integral gives the accumulated equivalent-electron count represented by [accumulated ethane count](name:accumulated_ethane_count). It excludes other molecular species, including the distinct [ethylene source rate](name:ethylene_source_rate).

NAMES.name: ethylene_count
NAMES.subject: ethylene
NAMES.short: Cumulative ethylene (C2H4) gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each ethylene molecule contributes 16 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
Cumulative ethylene (C2H4) delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as a dimensionless equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethylene molecule contributes 16 equivalent electrons, reflecting two carbon atoms at atomic number $Z = 6$ and four hydrogen atoms at $Z = 1$.

The equivalent-electron count $N_\mathrm{eq}$ for an injected number of ethylene molecules $N_\mathrm{mol}$ is:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = 16 \, N_\mathrm{mol}
$$

where the factor $16 = 2 \times 6 + 4 \times 1$ is the total bound-electron inventory of a neutral C$_2$H$_4$ molecule. The count accumulates from the moment of plasma breakdown and resets between discharges, providing a measure of the total electron inventory introduced via ethylene injection. It complements hydrocarbon siblings such as [accumulated_ethane_count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) and contributes to the cross-species total captured by [accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection)
NAMES.sign: Positive when ethylene gas has been injected into the vessel since plasma breakdown.

sources.enhanced_context: Ethylene (C2H4).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ethylene (C2H4)

NAMES.name: accumulated_ethylene_count
NAMES.subject: ethylene
NAMES.short: Cumulative ethylene (C2H4) gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each ethylene molecule contributes 16 equivalent electrons (2 carbon atoms at Z = 6 each, 4 hydrogen atoms at Z = 1 each).
NAMES.long:
Ethylene (C2H4) is a two-carbon hydrocarbon molecule in which each molecule contributes 2 carbon atoms (atomic number $Z_C = 6$) and 4 hydrogen atoms ($Z_H = 1$), yielding 16 equivalent electrons per molecule.

The accumulated equivalent-electron count is defined by:

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 16 \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}}{dt'} \, dt'
$$

where $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the time of plasma breakdown and $dN_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}/dt$ is the instantaneous ethylene injection rate in molecules per second.

The integral runs from plasma breakdown onward, excluding any prefill contribution. The quantity is inferred from calibrated gas-valve flow measurements and tracks the hydrocarbon-based electron inventory added to the plasma, relevant to impurity seeding and disruption mitigation experiments. Closely related hydrocarbon counts include [accumulated_ethane_count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) (C2H6, 18 equivalent electrons per molecule) and [accumulated_propane_count](name:accumulated_propane_count) (C3H8, 26 equivalent electrons per molecule). For the species-summed inventory across all injected gasses, see [accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.enhanced_context: Ethylene (C2H4).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ethylene (C2H4)

NAMES.name: ethylene_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ethylene
NAMES.short: Instantaneous injection rate of ethylene (C2H4) gas into the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent electrons per second with each molecule counted as 16 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
Ethylene (C2H4) is a two-carbon, four-hydrogen molecule used as a gaseous source of both carbon and hydrogen in plasma fueling and wall-conditioning experiments. The source rate is the instantaneous equivalent-electron delivery rate to the plasma vessel, where each molecule is assigned 16 equivalent electrons based on the total atomic electron inventory of the molecular formula.

The equivalent-electron rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq}$ relates to the molecular injection rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ by

$$
\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq} = 16\,\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}
$$

where the factor $16 = 2Z_\mathrm{C} + 4Z_\mathrm{H}$, with $Z_\mathrm{C} = 6$ the carbon atomic number and $Z_\mathrm{H} = 1$ the hydrogen atomic number.

The injection rate is inferred from valve conductance calibrations and upstream pressure measurements. Its time-integral gives the [accumulated ethylene count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count), which tracks the total equivalent-electron inventory delivered since plasma breakdown. Related molecular and atomic injection rates include [silane_source_rate](name:silane_source_rate) for SiH4 and [hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) for atomic hydrogen delivery.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ethylene gas flows from the injection system into the plasma vessel.

NAMES.name: first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short: Unit vector specifying the first measurement direction of the shatter cone, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Unit vector specifying the first measurement direction of the shatter cone, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. It gives the directed orientation associated with the first shatter-cone measurement direction, not a position, displacement, cone opening angle, or axis length.

The vector is represented by its Cartesian basis expansion and constrained to have unit Euclidean norm:

$$
\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{sc},1} = d_x\hat{x} + d_y\hat{y} + d_z\hat{z}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{sc},1}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{sc},1}=1
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{sc},1}$ is the first measurement direction unit vector of the shatter cone, $d_x$, $d_y$, and $d_z$ are its Cartesian scalar components, and $\hat{x}$, $\hat{y}$, and $\hat{z}$ are the basis vectors of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, with $\hat{z}$ vertical.

The first measurement direction is distinct from the second measurement direction and from the major-axis and minor-axis directions of an elliptic shatter-cone description, except in geometries where those directions are explicitly aligned.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along X axis
sources.parent_definition: Unit vector of the cone direction

NAMES.name: helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of helium-4 atoms delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count weighted by the helium-4 atomic number. This name fixes the species and its equivalent-electron weighting; temporal specializations select how the running total is reported in time.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of helium-4 atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed using equivalent-electron count units. Material introduced during the prefill phase is excluded.

For helium-4, the equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq},{}^4\mathrm{He}}(t) = 2\,N_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq},{}^4\mathrm{He}}$ and $N_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}$ are dimensionless cumulative counts and the factor 2 is the atomic number of helium. The count increases by two for every delivered atom and represents an atomic inventory, not an instantaneous injection rate and not an ionization-state population. Both helium isotopes share the same atomic-number weighting; this name is distinguished from a helium-3 counterpart by the delivered isotope, not by the weighting factor.

Within the broader [count due to gas injection](name:count_due_to_gas_injection) convention, this name fixes only the species and its equivalent-electron weighting; it does not prescribe how the running total is reported in time. Temporal specializations such as [accumulated helium-4 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection) select a specific reporting of that total — the time-integrated inventory from breakdown to the evaluation time — while inheriting the weighting and post-breakdown gas-injection scope defined here.

NAMES.name: accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Time-integrated equivalent-electron inventory of helium-4 atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, using atomic number Z = 2 so each atom contributes two equivalent electrons. It is an accumulated inventory, not an instantaneous injection rate.
NAMES.long:
Time-integrated equivalent-electron inventory of helium-4 atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown is the cumulative amount of helium-4 added through gas-injection fueling, counted with atomic number $Z=2$ so each atom contributes two equivalent electrons. The accumulation starts at plasma breakdown and includes only helium-4 gas injected after that time.

The accumulated equivalent-electron count is defined from the equivalent-electron injection rate, or equivalently from the neutral helium-4 atom injection rate:

$$
N_{\mathrm{He4,eq}}(t) = \int_{t_0}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4,eq}}(t')\,dt' = 2\int_{t_0}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4,atom}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{He4,eq}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count (dimensionless), $t$ and $t_0$ are times in seconds, $t_0$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron gas-injection rate in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4,atom}}$ is the corresponding neutral helium-4 atom injection rate in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The factor of 2 is the helium atomic number and must not be applied again when the integrated rate is already expressed as an equivalent-electron rate.

This quantity is distinct from an instantaneous [helium-4 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). It has the same post-breakdown equivalent-electron counting convention as [helium-4 count due to gas injection](name:helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection); the explicit accumulated name denotes the time integral over the gas-injection history rather than a rate or an atomic-particle count.

NAMES.name: hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of hydrogen atoms delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count; each hydrogen atom contributes one count, and prefill material is excluded.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of hydrogen atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Material introduced during the prefill phase is excluded.

For hydrogen, the equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq},\mathrm{H}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{H}} N_{\mathrm{H}}(t) = N_{\mathrm{H}}(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq},\mathrm{H}}$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron count due to gas injection, $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the cumulative count of delivered hydrogen atoms at time $t$, and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ is the atomic number of hydrogen.

The count increases by one for each delivered hydrogen atom and represents the delivered neutral atomic inventory, not an instantaneous injection rate, a prefill inventory, or a plasma ionization-state population. The [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection) is a concrete accumulated specialization of this hydrogen-specific definition.

NAMES.name: accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown equivalent-electron inventory of neutral hydrogen delivered by gas injection, with one count unit assigned to each hydrogen atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral hydrogen atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Hydrogen contributes one equivalent electron per atom because its atomic number is one.

$$
N_{H,mathrm{gas}}(t)=Z_H\,\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_H(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{H,\mathrm{gas}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $Z_H=1$ is hydrogen's atomic number, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $\dot{N}_H$ is the neutral-hydrogen injection rate. The corresponding instantaneous rate is [hydrogen source rate due to gas injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

The accumulation begins at breakdown and excludes hydrogen introduced during prefill; it represents delivered hydrogen inventory rather than the number of free plasma electrons or the ionization-state distribution. It is the post-breakdown component of [hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection), distinct from [accumulated hydrogen prefill count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count).

NAMES.name: krypton_count
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Count of krypton atoms expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory, where each krypton atom contributes 36 equivalent electrons equal to its atomic number.
NAMES.long:
The krypton count quantifies the inventory of krypton atoms in the plasma system as a dimensionless equivalent-electron count. The conversion uses the atomic number of krypton, $Z_\mathrm{Kr} = 36$, so that each krypton atom contributes 36 equivalent electrons:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{Kr} \cdot N_\mathrm{Kr}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{Kr}$ is the number of krypton atoms and $N_\mathrm{eq}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count.

The time-integrated form accumulated since plasma breakdown is given by [accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count). The same equivalent-electron convention applies to other impurity species, such as [argon_count](name:argon_count) and [neon_count](name:neon_count), each scaled by their respective atomic numbers.

NAMES.name: accumulated_krypton_count
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of krypton atoms injected into the machine since plasma breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated krypton count is the running total of krypton atoms introduced since plasma breakdown, converted to an electron-equivalent basis where each krypton atom contributes $Z_{\rm Kr} = 36$ electron equivalents when fully stripped of its bound electrons.

The quantity is obtained by integrating the instantaneous injection rate $\dot{N}_{\rm Kr}$ over time from the moment of plasma breakdown $t_0$:

$$
N_{\rm Kr,eq} = Z_{\rm Kr} \int_{t_0}^{t} \dot{N}_{\rm Kr}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $Z_{\rm Kr} = 36$ is the atomic number of krypton and $\dot{N}_{\rm Kr}$ is in atoms per second. This is distinct from the prefill-phase contribution captured by [krypton_prefill_count](name:krypton_prefill_count), which records only the gas load introduced before breakdown. Krypton serves as a heavy radiative seed impurity for power exhaust management and as a disruption mitigation agent; the cumulative injection inventory is therefore essential for interpreting bolometric radiated-power fractions and spectroscopic charge-state distributions throughout the discharge. Analogous running totals are defined for other injected species, including [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) and [accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when krypton has been cumulatively injected into the plasma since breakdown.

NAMES.name: length_of_pellet
NAMES.short: End-to-end extent of an intact cylindrical pellet measured along its symmetry axis before injection or shattering.
NAMES.long:
The pellet axial length is the distance between the two end faces measured parallel to the symmetry axis of the intact cylindrical pellet.

$$
L_p = z_2 - z_1
$$

where $L_p$ is the axial length and $z_1$ and $z_2$ are the axial coordinates of the two end faces, ordered so that $z_2 > z_1$ along the chosen axial direction.

This quantity describes the unshattered pellet before injection or fragmentation and excludes its transverse size, which is described by the [diameter of the pellet](name:diameter_of_pellet).

NAMES.name: lithium_count
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Lithium count is the amount of lithium represented as an equivalent-electron count, with each lithium atom contributing three counts because lithium has atomic number 3. It is the lithium-scoped parent for accumulated or phase-specific lithium inventories.
NAMES.long:
Lithium count is an extensive lithium-only inventory expressed using an equivalent-electron counting convention. It represents the amount of lithium before specifying an accumulation interval, injection phase, delivery mechanism, removal mechanism, or retention locus.

The equivalent-electron count for lithium is defined by:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Li,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}} N_{\mathrm{Li}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Li,eq}}$ is the lithium equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the number of lithium atoms represented, and $Z_{\mathrm{Li}} = 3$ is the atomic number of lithium.

This quantity is not a multi-species material count; only lithium atoms contribute to $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$. More specific phase or interval forms specialize this parent, for example [accumulated lithium count](name:accumulated_lithium_count) and [accumulated lithium prefill count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection). A rate form such as [lithium source rate due to gas injection](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) is a time derivative of a lithium count rather than a count itself.

NAMES.name: accumulated_lithium_count
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Cumulative lithium delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with three counts per lithium atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the post-breakdown gas-injection contribution to [lithium count](name:lithium_count), expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It includes lithium atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown and excludes prefill delivery and lithium introduced by other mechanisms.

The defining relation is

$$
C_{\mathrm{Li,gas}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Li}} N_{\mathrm{Li,gas}}(t) = 3N_{\mathrm{Li,gas}}(t)
$$

where $C_{\mathrm{Li,gas}}(t)$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Li,gas}}(t)$ is the number of lithium atoms delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown, and $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is lithium's atomic number. The quantity is the time integral of the corresponding [lithium gas-injection source rate](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), and is distinct from the [accumulated lithium prefill count](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).

NAMES.name: maximum_gas_flow
NAMES.short: Maximum gas flow is the largest pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the upper bound of its controllable range.
NAMES.long:
Maximum gas flow is the upper reliable operating limit of the pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve. It is a static hardware capability that bounds the same physical quantity represented by [gas flow], while [minimum gas flow](name:minimum_gas_flow) gives the corresponding lower limit.

The underlying pressure-volume gas throughput is defined by

$$
Q = p\,\dot{V}
$$

where $Q$ is the gas throughput, $p$ is the gas pressure, and $\dot{V}$ is the volumetric flow rate. The maximum gas flow is the upper reliable value of $Q$ for the valve, not a particle source rate; for an ideal gas, the corresponding molecular source rate is $\dot{N}=Q/(k_B T_g)$, where $T_g$ is the gas temperature and $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant.

This quantity defines the upper endpoint of the valve's controllable gas-flow range and excludes gas throughput from other injection or pumping components.

sources.enhanced_context: Maximum volumetric flow rate of a gas injection valve. An engineering limit parameter defining the peak throughput capacity of the valve for fuelling, impurity seeding, or disruption mitigation.

NAMES.name: methane_carbon_13_source_rate
NAMES.subject: methane_carbon_13
NAMES.short: Instantaneous injection rate of carbon-13-labeled methane (13CH4) into the plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron rate where each molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
Carbon-13-labeled methane (13CH4) is deployed as a controlled tracer gas for erosion and carbon transport studies in fusion devices, because the stable 13C isotope can be discriminated spectroscopically from the naturally occurring 12C background. The equivalent-electron weighting assigns a factor of 10 to each injected 13CH4 molecule, reflecting the total electron count of the neutral species: atomic number $Z = 6$ for carbon plus $Z = 1$ for each of the four hydrogen atoms.

The instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate $\dot{S}$ accumulates over time to give the total equivalent-electron inventory:

$$
N(t) = \int_0^t \dot{S}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $N(t)$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron count tracked by [accumulated 13CH4 injection](name:accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection).

The rate is inferred from upstream reservoir pressure and valve conductance measurements. For comprehensive carbon gas accounting, this quantity complements [carbon_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:carbon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), which sums contributions from all carbon-bearing gas species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when 13CH4 gas flows from the injection system into the plasma vessel.

NAMES.name: methane_source_rate
NAMES.subject: methane
NAMES.short: Instantaneous rate of neutral methane-molecule delivery into the plasma vessel by gas injection, counted per molecule rather than as an equivalent-electron or elemental source.
NAMES.long:
Methane source rate is the instantaneous rate at which neutral methane molecules are delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection. It counts methane molecules directly, rather than converting them to equivalent electrons or to elemental carbon or hydrogen.

The source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t) = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of methane molecules delivered by gas injection and $t$ is time. The quantity is distinct from the [methane carbon-13 source rate](name:methane_carbon_13_source_rate), which applies specifically to carbon-13-labeled methane.

NAMES.name: minimum_gas_flow
NAMES.short: Minimum gas flow is the smallest pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the lower bound of its controllable range.
NAMES.long:
Minimum gas flow is the lower reliable operating limit of the pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve. It is a static hardware capability that bounds the same physical quantity represented by [gas flow], while [maximum gas flow](name:maximum_gas_flow) gives the corresponding upper limit.

The pressure-volume gas throughput is defined by

$$
Q = p\,\dot{V}
$$

where $Q$ is the gas throughput, $p$ is the gas pressure, and $\dot{V}$ is the volumetric flow rate. The minimum gas flow is the lower reliable value of $Q$ for the valve, not a particle source rate; for an ideal gas, the corresponding molecular source rate is $\dot{N}=Q/(k_B T_g)$, where $T_g$ is the gas temperature and $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant.

This quantity defines the lower endpoint of the valve's controllable gas-flow range and excludes gas throughput from other injection or pumping components.

NAMES.name: molecular_neutral_species_flow_at_outlet
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Molecular neutral species flow at an outlet is the pressure-volume throughput of one molecular neutral species removed across a pumping outlet. It is defined by the outlet partial pressure of that species and the corresponding effective pumping speed, not by total neutral pressure.
NAMES.long:
Molecular neutral species flow at an outlet is the pressure-volume throughput of one molecular neutral species removed across a pumping outlet. It is species-specific and uses the outlet partial pressure of that molecular neutral species rather than the [total neutral pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure).

The outlet throughput is defined by the product of the outlet species partial pressure and the effective pumping speed for that species:

$$
Q_{s,\mathrm{out}} = p_{s,\mathrm{out}} S_{s,\mathrm{out}}
$$

where $Q_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is this molecular neutral species flow at the outlet, $p_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is the outlet partial pressure of molecular neutral species $s$, and $S_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is the effective pumping speed for species $s$ at the outlet.

This quantity is an outlet removal throughput, distinct from a gas source into the vessel such as [gas injection](name:total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection). It is the molecular, species-resolved outlet form of [neutral species flow](name:molecular_neutral_species_flow_at_outlet) and a species-specific specialization of [gas flow].
NAMES.sign: Positive when the molecular neutral species is removed through the outlet in the pumping direction away from the vessel.

sources.enhanced_context: Pumping flow rate of a specific molecular species through a gas pumping duct, representing the volumetric throughput removed from the vessel per unit time. Key quantity for particle inventory and exhaust control.
sources.leaf_definition: Pumping flow rate of that species
sources.parent_definition: Molecular species pumped via this duct

NAMES.name: neon_count
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Count of neon atoms expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory, where each neon atom contributes 10 equivalent electrons equal to its atomic number Z = 10.
NAMES.long:
The neon count quantifies the neon atom inventory as a dimensionless equivalent-electron count. Each neon atom contributes $Z_{\rm Ne}$ equivalent electrons equal to the atomic number of neon, so the total inventory is:

$$
N_{\rm eq} = Z_{\rm Ne} \cdot N_{\rm Ne}
$$

where $N_{\rm Ne}$ is the number of neon atoms and $Z_{\rm Ne} = 10$ is the neon atomic number. This convention is shared across noble-gas and impurity species inventories; for comparison, [argon_count](name:argon_count) uses $Z_{\rm Ar} = 18$ and [krypton_count](name:krypton_count) uses $Z_{\rm Kr} = 36$. The [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) is the time-integrated form of this quantity, accumulating since plasma breakdown; the present quantity is the instantaneous or snapshot total at a given time.

NAMES.name: accumulated_neon_count
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of neon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated neon count is the running temporal integral of the neon gas injection rate from plasma breakdown onward, giving the total neon inventory delivered to the plasma vessel over the discharge. Each injected neon atom contributes to the tally in equivalent-electron units — the raw particle count scaled by the neon atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Ne} = 10$ — enabling direct comparison with other injected fuel and impurity species.

The defining integral is:

$$
N_\mathrm{acc}(t) = Z_\mathrm{Ne} \int_{t_0}^{t} \dot{n}_\mathrm{Ne}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $\dot{n}_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the instantaneous neon injection rate in atoms per second, $t_0$ is the time of plasma breakdown, and $Z_\mathrm{Ne} = 10$ is the neon atomic number.

This quantity is determined from calibrated gas valve flow measurements integrated temporally throughout the discharge. It is particularly relevant in impurity seeding and disruption mitigation experiments where the cumulative neon dose governs radiated power fractions and pedestal stability.

The parent neon_count provides phase-specific or instantaneous counts; [neon_prefill_count](name:neon_prefill_count) covers the pre-breakdown injection phase exclusively. Analogous accumulated quantities for other injected species include [accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection) and [accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when neon gas is injected, so the accumulated count increases monotonically from zero at plasma breakdown.

sources.enhanced_context: Neon.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Neon

NAMES.name: neon_source_rate
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Instantaneous injection rate of neon gas into the plasma vessel, expressed in equivalent electrons per second.
NAMES.long: The neon source rate quantifies the instantaneous rate at which neon gas is introduced into the plasma vessel through gas injection systems. Each neon atom (atomic number $Z = 10$) contributes 10 equivalent electrons to the count, so the source rate equals 10 times the atomic injection rate expressed in atoms per second. Neon seeding is widely applied in fusion devices to control edge radiation and protect plasma-facing components from excessive heat loads, and is also employed in disruption mitigation scenarios requiring rapid radiative cooling. The source rate is inferred from calibrated flow controllers or gas injection valve diagnostics, with values ranging from $10^{20}$ to $10^{23}$ s$^{-1}$ depending on the seeding scenario. Integrating this rate over time yields the [accumulated neon count](name:accumulated_neon_count). Analogous injection rates for other species include [nitrogen_source_rate](name:nitrogen_source_rate) and [oxygen_source_rate](name:oxygen_source_rate), which follow the same equivalent-electron convention.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neon gas is being injected into the plasma vessel.

NAMES.name: net_efficiency_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system delivers signed net electrical power to an external load relative to the total internal electrical consumption needed to operate it.
NAMES.long:
The net efficiency of a plant system is the dimensionless ratio of signed net electrical power exported outside the plant boundary to total internal electrical power consumed by plant systems over the same accounting interval. It is the net-electrical-gain specialization of [efficiency of a plant system](name:efficiency_of_plant_system), with recirculating electrical loads included in the net exported power balance.

The defining relation, including the corresponding net-power balance, is:

$$
\eta_{\mathrm{net,plant}} = \frac{P_{\mathrm{net}}}{P_{\mathrm{cons}}}, \qquad
P_{\mathrm{net}} = P_{\mathrm{gen}} - P_{\mathrm{int}}, \qquad
P_{\mathrm{cons}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{plant}}} P_{\mathrm{load},i}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the [net electrical power of the plant system](name:net_power_of_plant_system) in W, $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is the positive total electrical consumption represented by [power of the plant system](name:power_of_plant_system) in W, $P_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is gross generated electrical power in W, $P_{\mathrm{int}}$ is the internal operational electrical consumption subtracted in the net-power balance in W, $P_{\mathrm{load},i}$ is the electrical consumption of included load $i$ in W, and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{plant}}$ is the set of electrically powered plant loads included in the accounting boundary.

The denominator $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is a gross positive consumption quantity, not the signed net exchange $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ and not the gross generated power $P_{\mathrm{gen}}$. It equals the internal-consumption term $P_{\mathrm{int}}$ only when the same loads, plant boundary, and interval define both the net-power balance and the denominator. Unlike [thermal efficiency of the plant system](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system), this quantity relates net electrical export to internal electrical consumption rather than gross electrical output to thermal input.
NAMES.sign: Positive when signed net electrical power is exported from the plant system to an external electrical network or load.

sources.enhanced_context: Plant electricity gain (Q_plant), defined as the ratio of net electric power output to the total plant electrical consumption during operation. A key reactor-level performance metric for fusion power plant feasibility assessments.
sources.leaf_definition: Electricity gain of the plant (ratio of net electric / plant electricity during operation)

NAMES.name: nitrogen_count
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Count of nitrogen particles expressed as a dimensionless equivalent-electron inventory, where each nitrogen atom contributes 7 equivalent electrons equal to its atomic number Z = 7.
NAMES.long:
The nitrogen count quantifies the nitrogen particle inventory by converting the atom count to an equivalent-electron basis using the atomic number $Z_\mathrm{N} = 7$ of nitrogen.

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{N} \cdot N_\mathrm{N}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{N}$ is the number of nitrogen atoms and $Z_\mathrm{N} = 7$. This equivalent-electron convention, shared across gas-injection inventory quantities such as [argon_count](name:argon_count), enables consistent comparison of particle inventories across species with different atomic numbers. The [accumulated_nitrogen_count](name:accumulated_nitrogen_count) is the time-integrated form of this quantity, tracking cumulative nitrogen introduced since plasma breakdown.

NAMES.name: accumulated_nitrogen_count
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Cumulative nitrogen delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory with seven counts per nitrogen atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of nitrogen atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. It is the gas-injection contribution to the [nitrogen count](name:nitrogen_count), not the actual free-electron inventory or a charge-state-resolved particle count.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by:

$$
N_{\mathrm{N,eq}}^{\mathrm{gas}}(t)=7\,N_{\mathrm{N}}^{\mathrm{gas}}(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{N}}^{\mathrm{gas}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of nitrogen atoms delivered by gas injection from plasma breakdown to time $t$, and the dimensionless factor 7 is nitrogen's atomic number. The quantity includes only nitrogen attributed to post-breakdown gas injection; it excludes nitrogen introduced by other delivery channels and does not represent the instantaneous ionization-state population.

sources.parent_definition: Nitrogen

NAMES.name: nitrogen_source_rate
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Instantaneous rate of neutral molecular nitrogen admitted to the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent-electron particles with fourteen counts assigned to each molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the equivalent-electron source rate carried by neutral molecular nitrogen admitted to the plasma vessel. It represents delivered molecular inventory, not free-electron production, ionization rate, or nitrogen ions retained in the plasma.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = 14\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}$ is the injection rate of nitrogen molecules. The factor 14 assigns seven equivalent-electron counts to each of the two nitrogen atoms in a molecule.

This species-resolved rate is consistent with the aggregate [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). Integrating it over a time interval gives the corresponding accumulated nitrogen inventory represented by [accumulated nitrogen count](name:accumulated_nitrogen_count).

NAMES.name: normalized_atomic_count_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Normalized atomic count of a pellet is the total inventory of atomic nuclei associated with one pellet after division by a fixed reference inventory of 10^20 atomic nuclei, independent of molecular bonding, phase, or species.
NAMES.long:
Normalized atomic count of a pellet is the total inventory of atomic nuclei associated with one pellet after division by a fixed reference atomic inventory. Molecules, compounds, and mixtures are converted to their constituent atoms before summation, regardless of molecular bonding, phase, or species.

For constituent entity types indexed by $i$, the normalized atomic inventory is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{atom,n}} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{atom}}}{N_{\mathrm{ref}}} = \frac{1}{N_{\mathrm{ref}}}\sum_i a_i N_i
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{atom,n}}$ is the normalized atomic count, $N_{\mathrm{atom}}$ is the physical atomic inventory, $N_{\mathrm{ref}}=10^{20}$ is the fixed reference atomic inventory, $N_i$ is the number of entities of type $i$, and $a_i$ is the number of atomic nuclei in each entity; molecular multiplicity is represented by [molecular atomic multiplicity](name:molecular_atomic_multiplicity).

This quantity is the scaled counterpart of [atomic count of pellet](name:atomic_count_of_pellet), which is unnormalized, and remains an atomic inventory rather than a separately counted molecule inventory in [count of pellet](name:count_of_pellet). Layer-restricted values, such as [core atomic count of pellet](name:core_atomic_count_of_pellet) and [outer atomic count of pellet](name:outer_atomic_count_of_pellet), partition the same atomic inventory, while normalized atomic count applies only the reference scaling; it is not a fraction or probability.

NAMES.name: outer_atomic_count_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Outer atomic count of a pellet is the total inventory of atomic nuclei in its outer material layer, independent of molecular bonding, phase, or species.
NAMES.long:
Outer atomic count of a pellet is the total inventory of atomic nuclei contained in the pellet's outer material layer. Molecules, compounds, and mixtures are converted to their constituent atoms before summation, regardless of molecular bonding or phase.

For constituent entity types indexed by $i$, the outer-layer atomic inventory is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{outer}} = \sum_i a_i N_i
$$

where $N_i$ is the number of entities of type $i$ in the outer layer and $a_i$ is the number of atoms in each entity. This layer-restricted quantity contributes to [atomic count of pellet](name:atomic_count_of_pellet); together with [core atomic count of pellet](name:core_atomic_count_of_pellet), it partitions the pellet's atomic inventory when those are the defined material layers. The count is unnormalized and excludes separately counted propellant-gas molecules.

NAMES.name: oxygen_source_rate
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of oxygen gas admitted to the plasma vessel, counting eight bound-electron equivalents per oxygen atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous oxygen inventory rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed using equivalent bound-electron counts. The weighting is based on oxygen atomic content rather than the molecular representation of the injected gas.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq,O}}(t)=8\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}(t)=16\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O_2}}(t)
$$

where $t$ is time, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq,O}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the injected oxygen-atom rate, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O_2}}$ is the injected molecular-oxygen rate. The factors 8 and 16 are the numbers of bound-electron equivalents per oxygen atom and oxygen molecule, respectively.

This instantaneous rate is the time derivative of the cumulative inventory represented by [accumulated oxygen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_oxygen_count_due_to_gas_injection) and is a species-specific form of [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pellet_path
NAMES.short: Poloidal magnetic flux at a pellet-path point is the value of the equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function evaluated at the position of a pellet along its injection trajectory. For an axisymmetric equilibrium it depends only on the major-radius and vertical coordinates of that trajectory point.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal magnetic flux at a pellet-path point is the value of the equilibrium [poloidal_magnetic_flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) function sampled at the location of a pellet along its injection trajectory. It labels the magnetic flux surface threading that trajectory point and shares the sign and normalization of the underlying equilibrium flux function.

The quantity is the equilibrium poloidal flux function evaluated at the pellet position:

$$
\psi_p = \psi\!\left(R_p, Z_p\right)
$$

where $\psi(R, Z)$ is the axisymmetric equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height, and $(R_p, Z_p)$ are the major-radius and vertical coordinates of the pellet-path point. Because the equilibrium is axisymmetric, $\psi$ is independent of the toroidal angle $\phi$, so the toroidal location of the trajectory point does not enter this value.

This is one scalar flux value associated with a single point on the pellet trajectory; sampled at successive points or instants along the path it traces the sequence of flux-surface labels crossed by the pellet. It differs from [poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface), which is the flux value attached to a specified magnetic flux surface independent of any trajectory. It is not the toroidal magnetic flux, the pellet trajectory geometry, or a derivative of the flux label with respect to a flux coordinate.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the vertical magnetic field on the horizontal disk that defines the equilibrium poloidal flux points in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: power_at_inlet
NAMES.short: Rate of energy transfer entering a system at its inlet boundary, encompassing all physical mechanisms by which power is delivered to that subsystem.
NAMES.long:
Power at inlet is the total rate at which energy crosses the inlet boundary of a system or subsystem, summed over all transport mechanisms present at that boundary.

It enters system-level energy-balance equations for a control volume as:

$$
\dot{E} = P_{\rm in} - P_{\rm out}
$$

where $P_{\rm in}$ is the inlet power, $P_{\rm out}$ is the [power at the outlet](name:power_at_outlet), and $\dot{E}$ is the net rate of energy accumulation within the control volume.

In fusion-plant and industrial power-system contexts, inlet power sets the upper bound on what any downstream conversion stage can recover. The thermal specialization [thermal_power_at_inlet](name:thermal_power_at_inlet) resolves the heat-carrying component entering a thermodynamic conversion cycle prior to electricity generation. Comparing inlet power with the net absorbed contribution, available via [net_absorbed_power_of_plant_system](name:net_absorbed_power_of_plant_system), characterizes overall subsystem energy efficiency.

NAMES.name: power_of_breeder_blanket
NAMES.short: Power of breeder blanket is the rate of energy transfer assigned to the tritium-breeding blanket. It is a parent concept for blanket power specializations distinguished by mechanism, boundary, or accounting convention, not specifically thermal, non-nuclear, surface, volumetric, input, or extracted power.
NAMES.long:
Power of breeder blanket is the rate of energy transfer assigned to the tritium-breeding blanket as a plant component. It is the common parent concept for blanket power quantities that may be specialized by physical mechanism, spatial accounting boundary, or energy-accounting convention.

For a specified blanket energy account, the associated power is the time derivative of that account:

$$
P_\mathrm{blanket} = \frac{dE_\mathrm{blanket}}{dt}
$$

where $E_\mathrm{blanket}$ is the energy deposited in, generated within, removed from, or otherwise assigned to the blanket by the particular specialization, and $t$ is time.

This parent name does not by itself select a contribution type such as surface thermal loading, volumetric nuclear heating, radiative deposition, total deposited power, or extracted thermal power. Child quantities define those restrictions explicitly; for example, [thermal power of breeder blanket](name:thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket) denotes a thermal-load specialization, while [heating power of breeder blanket](name:heating_power_of_breeder_blanket) denotes a heating-power specialization.

NAMES.name: power_of_plant_component_port
NAMES.short: Power of a plant component port is the signed rate of energy transfer across a boundary connection of a plant component, independent of the physical carrier or mechanism. It generalizes mechanism-specific port powers such as thermal power carried by a coolant circuit.
NAMES.long:
Power of a plant component port is the signed rate at which energy crosses a boundary connection of a plant component. The quantity is defined for the port as an energy-transfer interface and is independent of whether the transferred energy is thermal, mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, or another mechanism-specific form.

For an oriented port whose positive direction is from the component to the connected carrier or circuit, the port power is

$$
P_{\mathrm{port}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{out}}}{dt}
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the energy transferred through the port from the plant component to the connected carrier or circuit, and $t$ is time.

This parent quantity is mechanism-agnostic. The [thermal power of a plant component port](name:thermal_power_of_plant_component_port) is a specific contribution in which the transferred energy is heat carried by a thermal working fluid; coolant enthalpy differences define that child, not the generic parent.
NAMES.sign: Positive when net energy transfer through the port is from the plant component to the connected carrier or circuit.

NAMES.name: power_of_plant_subsystem
NAMES.short: Real electrical power consumed by an individual plant subsystem at its electrical boundary, contributing to auxiliary-load accounting without including plant-wide aggregation.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the real electrical power consumed by one plant subsystem at its electrical boundary. It represents the subsystem's contribution to auxiliary electrical load, distinct from plant-wide aggregation and net electrical balance quantities.

$$
P_{\rm sub} = \left\langle v(t)i(t) \right\rangle_t
$$

where $P_{\rm sub}$ is the boundary real power, $v(t)$ is the instantaneous terminal voltage, $i(t)$ is the instantaneous current directed into the subsystem, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes averaging over the relevant operating interval. For multiple terminals, the boundary power is the algebraic sum of the terminal power contributions. Positive power denotes consumption by the subsystem; exported or generated power is not included as consumed load. The quantity is distinct from [absorbed power of a plant system](name:absorbed_power_of_plant_system), [total power of a plant system](name:total_power_of_plant_system), and [net power of a plant system](name:net_power_of_plant_system).

NAMES.name: power_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Real electrical power assigned at a plant-system boundary, representing absorbed load, net generation balance, or an aggregate of included system loads.
NAMES.long:
Real electrical power is the rate of electrical-energy transfer or accounting associated with a plant system at its electrical boundary. It excludes reactive power and other non-electrical energy flows.

The instantaneous power is defined by

$$
P = \frac{\mathrm{d}E}{\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $E$ is the electrical energy associated with the accounting boundary and $t$ is time.

The accounting convention is fixed by the specialized quantity. [Absorbed power of a plant system](name:absorbed_power_of_plant_system) represents one-way incoming electrical load, [net power of a plant system](name:net_power_of_plant_system) represents generation minus internal consumption and is positive for net export, and [total power of a plant system](name:total_power_of_plant_system) is the sum of the loads of all included systems. These forms are distinct applications of the same plant-boundary electrical-power concept.

sources.enhanced_context: Electrical power consumed by a specific system in the balance-of-plant electric plant operation. Represents the instantaneous power draw of the named system as part of the overall plant power balance accounting.

NAMES.name: absorbed_power_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Real electrical power absorbed by an individual plant system during operation, evaluated at the system electrical boundary. It is the one-way incoming load component, excluding locally generated or returned real power and distinct from generated-minus-consumed net balance.
NAMES.long:
Absorbed power of a plant system is the real electrical power crossing the electrical boundary of one plant system into that system, with inward transfer represented as a one-way absorbed component. It describes electrical boundary input at system level, not thermal power, apparent power, reactive power, accumulated energy, internal dissipation, or storage inside the boundary.

For $M$ electrical terminals referenced so that positive terminal real power enters the plant-system boundary, absorbed power is defined as the sum of positive incoming terminal real-power components:

$$
P_\mathrm{abs} = \sum_{k=1}^{M} [P_k]_+,\qquad P_k = \left\langle v_k(t)\,i_k(t)\right\rangle
$$

where $M$ is the number of included electrical terminals, $P_\mathrm{abs}$ is this absorbed plant-system power in W, $P_k$ is the signed real power at terminal $k$ in W, $v_k$ is terminal voltage in V, $i_k$ is terminal current in A, $\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes the averaging needed to form real power, and $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. For sinusoidal steady state, the same terminal real power may be written $P_k=\Re\{V_k I_k^*\}$, where $V_k$ and $I_k$ are RMS voltage and current phasors in V and A with the current phasor referenced inward.

Generated or returned real electrical power crossing outward is not counted as negative absorbed power; it is excluded from $P_\mathrm{abs}$. The corresponding [net_absorbed_power_of_plant_system](name:net_absorbed_power_of_plant_system) combines incoming consumption with local generation or returned real power using consumed-minus-generated accounting, whereas [net_power_of_plant_system](name:net_power_of_plant_system) uses generated-minus-consumed accounting. Consistently bounded subsystem contributions are related to [power_of_plant_subsystem](name:power_of_plant_subsystem), and the unqualified load-positive system boundary quantity is [power_of_plant_system](name:power_of_plant_system).

NAMES.name: net_absorbed_power_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Signed net electrical load of a plant system: internally consumed power minus locally generated power, positive for net electrical uptake.
NAMES.long:
Net absorbed power is the real electrical load balance of a plant system, representing internal consumption after local generation is accounted for.

$$
P_{\mathrm{net,abs}} = P_{\mathrm{cons}} - P_{\mathrm{gen}} = -P_{\mathrm{net}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is the real electrical power consumed within the system, $P_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is real electrical power generated locally within the same boundary, and $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the generated-minus-consumed balance defined by [net power of plant system](name:net_power_of_plant_system). Positive values indicate net electrical uptake; negative values indicate that local generation exceeds consumption. This signed balance is distinct from [absorbed power of plant system](name:absorbed_power_of_plant_system), which denotes one-way inward electrical boundary transfer, and from [power of plant system](name:power_of_plant_system), which denotes gross electrical draw without the local-generation subtraction.

NAMES.name: net_power_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Net real electrical power of a plant system, defined as generation minus internal electrical consumption at the same system boundary; positive values denote net export.
NAMES.long:
Net power of a plant system is the real electrical power balance of one plant system, with generation counted positively and internal consumption counted negatively. It is the generated-minus-consumed counterpart to the load-oriented [power of a plant system](name:power_of_plant_system), rather than thermal, apparent, reactive, or accumulated energy.

For a consistently defined system boundary, the net power is defined as

$$
P_\mathrm{net} = P_\mathrm{generated} - P_\mathrm{consumed} = -P_\mathrm{system}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{net}$ is this plant-system quantity, $P_\mathrm{generated}$ is real electrical power generated within the boundary, $P_\mathrm{consumed}$ is real electrical power consumed within the boundary, and $P_\mathrm{system}$ is [power of a plant system](name:power_of_plant_system) using the load-positive convention. Internal transfers between included subsystems cancel. The quantity is the negative of [net absorbed power of a plant system](name:net_absorbed_power_of_plant_system) when both use the same boundary and scope; positive values denote net electrical export from the system boundary.

NAMES.name: prefill_count
NAMES.short: Dimensionless equivalent-electron count of gas introduced by injection during the plasma prefill phase before breakdown, where each injected atom or molecule contributes a count equal to the total number of its bound electrons.
NAMES.long:
The prefill count is a species-resolved, dimensionless measure of the neutral gas inventory accumulated in the vessel during the prefill phase — the interval from the start of gas injection up to plasma breakdown. Rather than reporting raw atom or molecule numbers, the quantity normalizes each species to equivalent electrons so that inventories of different gasses are directly comparable on a common electron-inventory scale.

For a single injected species, the equivalent-electron count is:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{eff} \, N
$$

where $N$ is the total number of injected atoms or molecules accumulated during the prefill phase and $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ is the number of bound electrons per atom or molecule (equal to the atomic number $Z$ for monatomic species, or the sum of constituent atomic numbers for molecular species). For example, [argon_prefill_count](name:argon_prefill_count) uses $Z_\mathrm{eff} = 18$ per atom, while [nitrogen_prefill_count](name:nitrogen_prefill_count) uses $Z_\mathrm{eff} = 7$ per atom (14 per N$_2$ molecule). For [hydrogen_prefill_count](name:hydrogen_prefill_count) and [deuterium_prefill_count](name:deuterium_prefill_count), $Z_\mathrm{eff} = 1$, so the equivalent-electron count equals the atom count directly.

This quantity covers only gas introduced by active injection during the prefill phase; contributions from wall recycling, neutral beams, pellets, or post-breakdown fueling are excluded. The post-breakdown counterpart is represented by the accumulated count family, such as [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count).

NAMES.name: ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia_deuterated
NAMES.short: Deuterated ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral ND3 introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 10 count units per molecule.
NAMES.long:
Deuterated ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ND3 molecule contributes ten equivalent electrons: seven from nitrogen and one from each of its three deuterium atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3Z_{\mathrm{D}})N_{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}} = 10\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ are atomic numbers, $N_{\mathrm{ND_3,prefill}}$ is the accumulated molecule count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}$ is the molecule injection rate, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times.

This quantity includes only ND3 introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the deuterated-ammonia component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), distinct from [ammonia_prefill_count](name:ammonia_prefill_count) and post-breakdown [accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count).

NAMES.name: ammonia_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia
NAMES.short: Ammonia prefill count is the total amount of NH3 introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count of 10 per neutral molecule.
NAMES.long:
Ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral ammonia, NH3, introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral NH3 molecule contributes ten count units: seven from nitrogen and one from each of its three hydrogen atoms.

The count is defined by the accumulated molecular amount over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}} = 10N_{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} 10\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}}$ is the accumulated number of ammonia molecules, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the ammonia injection rate in molecules per second, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the start of prefill and plasma-breakdown times in seconds.

This species-specific contribution is included in the common prebreakdown bookkeeping of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count). Ammonia introduced after breakdown is excluded and is represented by [accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count).

NAMES.name: argon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Argon prefill count is the total amount of neutral argon (Ar) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18 per atom.
NAMES.long:
Argon prefill count is the total amount of neutral argon (Ar) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral argon atom contributes 18 equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating injected argon atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the argon atomic number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} N_{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t)\,dt = 18\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-argon atom count, $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}=18$ is the argon atomic number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only argon introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the argon-specific component of [prefill count](name:prefill_count) and follows the isotope-resolved convention used for [tritium prefill count](name:tritium_prefill_count).

NAMES.name: deuterium_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Deuterium prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterium introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with one count unit per atom.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium prefill count is the total amount of neutral deuterium (D) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral deuterium atom contributes one equivalent electron.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating injected deuterium atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the deuterium atomic number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{D,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{D}} N_{\mathrm{D,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{D}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)\,dt = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{D,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{D,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-deuterium atom count, $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ is the deuterium atomic number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the deuterium atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only deuterium introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the deuterium-specific component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count) and uses the same isotope-resolved convention as [tritium_prefill_count](name:tritium_prefill_count).

NAMES.name: ethane_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short: Ethane prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethane (C2H6) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18 equivalent electrons per molecule.
NAMES.long:
Ethane prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethane (C2H6) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethane molecule contributes 18 equivalent electrons: 12 from its two carbon atoms and 6 from its six hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}} = 18N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}18\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{C_2H_6,prefill}}$ are pure counts, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the neutral-ethane introduction rate in molecules s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$, and $t$ are the prefill start, plasma-breakdown, and time variables in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral ethane introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the ethane component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_ethane_count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) represents distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while [ethylene_prefill_count](name:ethylene_prefill_count) applies the same convention to a different hydrocarbon.

NAMES.name: ethylene_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ethylene
NAMES.short: Ethylene prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethylene (C2H4) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 16 equivalent electrons per molecule.
NAMES.long:
Ethylene prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethylene (C2H4) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethylene molecule contributes sixteen equivalent electrons: twelve from two carbon atoms and four from four hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = (2Z_{\mathrm{C}}+4Z_{\mathrm{H}})N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = 16N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}16\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{C}}=6$ and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ are the atomic numbers of carbon and hydrogen, $N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}}$ is the accumulated ethylene-molecule count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}$ is the ethylene introduction rate, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and plasma-breakdown times.

This quantity includes only neutral ethylene introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the ethylene component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_ethylene_count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count) represents the distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while [ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count) applies the same convention to a different molecule.
