NAMES.name: hydrogen_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Hydrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral hydrogen introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with one equivalent electron per atom.
NAMES.long:
Hydrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral hydrogen (H) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral hydrogen atom contributes one equivalent electron because the atomic number of hydrogen is $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{H,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}N_{\mathrm{H,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$, $N_{\mathrm{H,prefill}}$ is the accumulated hydrogen-atom count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen-atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only hydrogen introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the hydrogen component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count) is the accumulated gas-injection specialization of this quantity, distinct from isotope-specific prefill counts such as [deuterium_prefill_count](name:deuterium_prefill_count).

NAMES.name: accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of hydrogen atoms introduced by gas injection during prefill before plasma breakdown; hydrogen contributes one count per atom.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the cumulative hydrogen atom inventory delivered by gas injection during the prefill interval ending at plasma breakdown, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention. It is the hydrogen-specific contribution to the [hydrogen prefill count](name:hydrogen_prefill_count).

$$
N_{\mathrm{H,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}N_{\mathrm{H}} = N_{\mathrm{H}}, \qquad N_{\mathrm{H}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}(t)\,dt
$$

Here $N_{\mathrm{H,eq}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ are dimensionless equivalent-electron and atom counts, $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ is hydrogen's atomic number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen injection rate in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times in s. Only pre-breakdown gas injection is included; post-breakdown delivery is represented by [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen

NAMES.name: krypton_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Krypton prefill count is the total amount of neutral krypton introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 36 count units per atom.
NAMES.long:
Krypton prefill count is the total amount of neutral krypton (Kr) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral krypton atom contributes 36 equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating the injected krypton atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the krypton atomic number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt = 36 \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the dimensionless accumulated neutral-krypton atom count, $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}=36$ is the dimensionless atomic number of krypton, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the neutral-krypton atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the start of prefill, and $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only krypton introduced before breakdown and excludes later fueling, other gas species, and the retained or ionized inventory. It uses the common equivalent-electron bookkeeping of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), with [xenon_prefill_count](name:xenon_prefill_count) providing the analogous noble-gas convention for xenon.

NAMES.name: methane_carbon_13_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: methane_carbon_13
NAMES.short: Methane carbon-13 prefill count is the total amount of neutral 13CH4 introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 10 count units per molecule.
NAMES.long:
Methane carbon-13 prefill count is the total amount of neutral carbon-13-labeled methane (13CH4) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral 13CH4 molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons: six from carbon and one from each of four hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{13\mathrm{CH_4,prefill}} = 10N_{13\mathrm{CH_4,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} 10\dot{N}_{13\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{13\mathrm{CH_4,prefill}}$ and $N_{13\mathrm{CH_4,prefill}}$ are pure counts, $\dot{N}_{13\mathrm{CH_4}}$ is the molecule introduction rate in molecules s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$, and $t$ are times in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral 13CH4 introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the methane carbon-13 component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection) represents the distinct post-breakdown accumulation.

NAMES.name: neon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Neon prefill count is the total amount of neutral neon (Ne) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 10 equivalent electrons per atom.
NAMES.long:
Neon prefill count is the total amount of neutral neon (Ne) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral neon atom contributes 10 equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = 10N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}10\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the neon equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-neon atom count, both pure counts; $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ is the atomic number of neon; $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neutral-neon atom introduction rate in atoms s$^{-1}$; and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and plasma-breakdown times, with $t$ in s.

This quantity includes only neutral neon introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. The equivalent-electron convention is an accounting normalization based on neutral atomic composition, not a statement that the gas is fully ionized during prefill. It is the neon component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) represents distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while [argon_prefill_count](name:argon_prefill_count) applies the same convention to a different noble gas.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Nitrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral nitrogen (N or N₂) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 7 per atom or 14 per N₂ molecule.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral nitrogen (N or N₂) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral nitrogen atom contributes 7 equivalent electrons, so each N₂ molecule contributes 14.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{N,prefill}} = 7N_{\mathrm{N,prefill}} + 14N_{\mathrm{N_2,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \left[7\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N}}(t) + 14\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}(t)\right]dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{N,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{N,prefill}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{N_2,prefill}}$ are accumulated neutral atom and molecule counts, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N}}$ and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}$ are their introduction rates. The counts are pure counts, the rates are in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and plasma-breakdown times in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral nitrogen introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the nitrogen component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), whereas [accumulated_nitrogen_count](name:accumulated_nitrogen_count) represents post-breakdown nitrogen accumulation.

NAMES.name: prefill_gas_pressure
NAMES.short: Pressure of the neutral gas introduced before plasma breakdown, governing the pressure-dependent ionization conditions for early electron-avalanche breakdown.
NAMES.long:
Prefill gas pressure is the thermodynamic pressure of the neutral gas present before plasma breakdown. It establishes the gas conditions used in the Townsend electron-avalanche criterion during plasma initiation.

For an ideal neutral gas, pressure is related to particle density and temperature by:

$$
p_g = n_g k_B T_g
$$

where $p_g$ is the prefill gas pressure, $n_g$ is the neutral particle number density, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, and $T_g$ is the neutral-gas temperature. This ideal-gas relation applies when the ideal-gas approximation is valid.

This quantity describes the prebreakdown gas state; it is not the accumulated injected inventory represented by [prefill_count](name:prefill_count) or the pressure of the plasma formed after breakdown.

sources.enhanced_context: Prefill gas pressure used as input to the Townsend electric field calculation during plasma initiation. Determines the ionization conditions for electron avalanche breakdown in the early startup phase.

NAMES.name: propane_count
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short: Amount of propane (C3H8) in or injected into the plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron count assigning 26 count units per neutral propane molecule.
NAMES.long:
The propane count quantifies a propane inventory associated with plasma operations as a dimensionless equivalent-electron count. Each neutral propane molecule carries 26 bound electrons, derived from its molecular composition: 3 carbon atoms (atomic number $Z_C = 6$) and 8 hydrogen atoms (atomic number $Z_H = 1$), giving $3 \times 6 + 8 \times 1 = 26$ electrons per molecule.

The equivalent-electron count $N_\mathrm{eq}$ is defined as:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = 26 \times N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}$ is the number of propane molecules. This convention normalizes gas inventories across molecular species to a common electron-equivalent basis, facilitating comparisons of impurity and fuel contributions to the plasma electron budget.

Propane injection amounts are inferred from calibrated gas valve records or pressure measurements in the injection line. Specializations include [accumulated_propane_count](name:accumulated_propane_count), the time-integrated post-breakdown inventory, and [propane_prefill_count](name:propane_prefill_count), restricted to the prefill phase. Analogous counts for other hydrocarbons follow the same convention: [ethane_count](name:ethane_count) assigns 18 electrons per C2H6 molecule and [accumulated_ethylene_count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count) assigns 16 electrons per C2H4 molecule.

NAMES.name: accumulated_propane_count
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown propane injection expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory, assigning 26 count units to each neutral C3H8 molecule.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated propane count is the equivalent-electron inventory added by neutral propane gas injection after plasma breakdown. It is the post-breakdown component of the broader [propane count](name:propane_count).

The defining accumulation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{acc}}(t)=26\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $t$ is the evaluation time, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}$ is the neutral propane molecular injection rate in molecules per second. The factor 26 is the total bound-electron count per molecule, $3\times 6+8\times 1$, using the atomic numbers of carbon and hydrogen.

The accumulation starts at plasma breakdown and excludes prefill injection represented by [propane prefill count](name:propane_prefill_count). It is cumulative and distinct from the instantaneous [propane source rate](name:propane_source_rate).

NAMES.name: propane_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short: Propane prefill count is the total amount of C3H8 introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 26 count units per neutral propane molecule.
NAMES.long:
Propane prefill count is the total amount of neutral propane (C3H8) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each propane molecule contributes 26 equivalent electrons: 18 from three carbon atoms and 8 from eight hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating the injected propane molecules over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = (3Z_C + 8Z_H)N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = 26N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}}$ is the accumulated propane molecule count, $Z_C=6$ and $Z_H=1$ are the atomic numbers of carbon and hydrogen, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}$ is the propane molecule injection rate, $t_0$ is the start of prefill, and $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only propane introduced before breakdown and excludes later fueling, other gas species, and the retained or ionized inventory. It uses the common equivalent-electron bookkeeping of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), with [ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count) providing the analogous molecular-species convention.

NAMES.name: propane_source_rate
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short: Instantaneous propane (C3H8) injection rate into the plasma vessel, converted from molecules to equivalent electrons using 26 electrons per neutral molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous source rate of propane gas entering the plasma vessel, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention. Each neutral C3H8 molecule contributes the total electron count of its constituent atoms.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
S_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)=26\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the propane molecular injection rate in molecules per second, $t$ is time, and 26 is the dimensionless electron count per neutral molecule: three carbon atoms contribute 18 electrons and eight hydrogen atoms contribute 8 electrons. This is an instantaneous rate, distinct from the accumulated [propane count](name:propane_count), which is the time-integrated equivalent-electron inventory.

NAMES.name: radial_coordinate_of_shattering_position
NAMES.short: Major-radius coordinate of the shatter-cone origin, defined as its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial coordinate of the shatter-cone origin is the major-radius location of the pellet shattering position, measured perpendicular to the toroidal symmetry axis. It locates the origin independently of its toroidal angle and vertical height, using the same radial-coordinate meaning as [radial coordinate of a measurement position](name:radial_coordinate_of_measurement_position).

$$
R_{\mathrm{sc}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{sc}}^2 + y_{\mathrm{sc}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{sc}}$ is the shatter-cone origin's radial coordinate, and $x_{\mathrm{sc}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{sc}}$ are its horizontal Cartesian coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ frame, with $z=Z$. The resulting coordinate is the nonnegative perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_velocity_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Major-radius component of the shattered-pellet center-of-mass velocity in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the velocity of a shattered pellet’s center of mass projected onto the major-radius direction. It describes the collective radial motion of the fragments, not the velocity of an individual fragment or the plasma.

The radial component is defined by

$$
v_R = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the center-of-mass velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the outward radial unit vector, and $v_R$ is the resulting component. The frame is the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{\mathbf{R}}, \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}, \hat{\mathbf{Z}})$. The center-of-mass velocity is mass-weighted over the shattered fragments. Together with the [toroidal velocity of the pellet](name:toroidal_velocity_of_pellet) and [vertical velocity of the pellet](name:vertical_velocity_of_pellet), this component specifies the pellet center-of-mass velocity in the cylindrical frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the shattered-pellet center of mass moves toward increasing major radius $R$, along $+\hat{\mathbf{R}}$.

NAMES.name: shattered_pellet_fragment_density
NAMES.subject: shattered_pellet_fragment
NAMES.short: Number density of atoms of a specified constituent species within one material fragment produced by a shattered pellet injector, summed over all charge states of that species.
NAMES.long:
Number density of atoms of a specified constituent species within one material fragment produced by a shattered pellet injector is the count of atoms of that species in the fragment divided by the fragment physical volume. The species-level value is summed over all charge states of that atomic species.

For species $s$ in a fragment of volume $V_f$, the density is defined by

$$
n_s = \frac{N_s}{V_f}
$$

where $n_s$ is the species number density, $N_s$ is the dimensionless count of atoms of species $s$ in the fragment, and $V_f$ is the physical volume of that fragment.

This quantity applies to a single condensed shattered-pellet fragment and is resolved by constituent species. It differs from [density_of_pellet](name:density_of_pellet), which describes the atom number density of an intact pellet as a whole, and from [core_density_of_pellet](name:core_density_of_pellet), which describes the atom number density in the pellet core rather than in an individual shattered fragment. It also excludes the density of ablated gas or plasma produced after material leaves the condensed fragment.

sources.enhanced_context: Number density of a given atomic species within a shattered pellet (SPI) fragment. Characterizes the material composition of the individual SPI fragment.
sources.leaf_definition: Density of the species
sources.parent_definition: Atomic species in the fragment composition

NAMES.name: shattered_pellet_fragment_volume
NAMES.subject: shattered_pellet_fragment
NAMES.short: Volume occupied by one solid fragment produced when a pellet is shattered for plasma fueling, excluding surrounding space and unincorporated gas.
NAMES.long:
The fragment volume is the three-dimensional geometric volume occupied by the solid material of one shattered-pellet fragment.

The defining relation is

$$
V_f = \int_{\Omega_f} dV
$$

where $V_f$ is the fragment volume, $\Omega_f$ is the region occupied by the fragment, and $dV$ is an infinitesimal volume element.

This quantity excludes surrounding voids, carrier gas, and plasma volume. It is distinct from [shattered-pellet fragment density](name:shattered_pellet_fragment_density), which describes the number density of an atomic species within the fragment.

sources.enhanced_context: Volume of an individual shattered pellet fragment as a function of time or fragment index. Used to characterise the fragment size distribution in shattered pellet injector (SPI) disruption mitigation studies.

sources.parent_definition: Set of shattered pellet fragments

NAMES.name: silane_count
NAMES.subject: silane
NAMES.short: Cumulative gas-injection inventory after plasma breakdown, represented as an equivalent-electron count based on the injected species’ atomic content.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of gas introduced by injection after plasma breakdown, expressed using an equivalent-electron counting convention rather than as a direct particle count.

For injected molecular species, the equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = \sum_m Z_m N_m
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $N_m$ is the cumulative number of injected molecules of species $m$, and $Z_m$ is the sum of the atomic numbers of the atoms in one neutral molecule of species $m$.

The quantity accumulates post-breakdown injection and excludes gas introduced during the prefill phase. It is distinct from the instantaneous [silane source rate](name:silane_source_rate) and is instantiated for silane by [accumulated silane count](name:accumulated_silane_count); [silane prefill count](name:silane_prefill_count) represents the separate pre-breakdown interval.

NAMES.name: accumulated_silane_count
NAMES.subject: silane
NAMES.short: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of silane (SiH4) molecules delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18 counts per molecule.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of silane (SiH4) delivered by gas injection, expressed using an equivalent-electron counting convention rather than as a direct molecular count.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{SiH_4}}(t) = 18\,N_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}(t)
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{SiH_4}}(t)$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of silane molecules injected after plasma breakdown. The factor 18 is the sum of the silicon atomic number 14 and the four hydrogen atomic numbers, each equal to 1.

This quantity is the post-breakdown component of [silane_count](name:silane_count). It excludes silane introduced during prefill, represented by [silane_prefill_count](name:silane_prefill_count), and counts delivered molecules rather than electrons currently present in the plasma or a particular molecular ionization state.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Silane (SiH4)

NAMES.name: silane_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: silane
NAMES.short: Accumulated equivalent-electron count of silane (SiH4) gas injected during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, where each SiH4 molecule contributes 18 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The silane prefill count is the dimensionless total of silane (SiH4) gas introduced into the plasma vessel during the prefill phase — before plasma breakdown — expressed using the equivalent-electron convention in which each atom contributes a weight equal to its atomic number.

Each SiH4 molecule contributes 18 equivalent electrons: 14 from the silicon nucleus ($Z_\mathrm{Si} = 14$) and 1 from each of the four hydrogen atoms ($Z_\mathrm{H} = 1$):

$$
C_{\mathrm{SiH_4}} = Z_\mathrm{Si} + 4\,Z_\mathrm{H} = 14 + 4 = 18
$$

where $N_\mathrm{mol}$ is the number of SiH4 molecules injected before breakdown, giving a total prefill count of $18\,N_\mathrm{mol}$.

The prefill phase precedes plasma ignition and is used to condition the vessel or establish a neutral-gas background. The accumulated count records all injection events within that window, giving a species-resolved inventory of silicon and hydrogen introduced before breakdown. The corresponding post-breakdown tally is provided by [accumulated_silane_count](name:accumulated_silane_count), and the instantaneous injection rate is tracked by [silane_source_rate](name:silane_source_rate). Analogous prefill counts for other species include [accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count) and [nitrogen_prefill_count](name:nitrogen_prefill_count).
NAMES.sign: Positive when silane gas is injected into the vessel during the prefill phase.

sources.enhanced_context: Silane (SiH4).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Silane (SiH4)

NAMES.name: silane_source_rate
NAMES.subject: silane
NAMES.short: Instantaneous injection rate of silane (SiH4) gas into the plasma vessel, expressed in equivalent electrons per second.
NAMES.long:
Silane ($\mathrm{SiH_4}$, silicon tetrahydride) is a silicon-bearing compound injected as a controlled impurity source in plasma experiments. The source rate quantifies the instantaneous rate of silane introduction expressed as an equivalent-electron flux, where each $\mathrm{SiH_4}$ molecule contributes the combined atomic numbers of its constituent atoms.

Each silane molecule carries $Z_\mathrm{Si} + 4\,Z_\mathrm{H} = 14 + 4 = 18$ equivalent electrons. The equivalent-electron rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq}$ relates to the molecular injection flux $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}$ by:

$$
\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq} = 18 \, \dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{Si} = 14$ is the atomic number of silicon, $Z_\mathrm{H} = 1$ is the atomic number of hydrogen, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}$ is the molecular injection rate in molecules per second.

The instantaneous rate is inferred from calibrated gas-valve systems monitoring flow at the injection manifold. Integrating this rate over the plasma discharge from breakdown gives the [accumulated silane count](name:accumulated_silane_count), which tracks the total equivalent-electron inventory of silane introduced during a discharge. Analogous rate quantities for other injected species include [xenon_source_rate](name:xenon_source_rate) and [nitrogen_source_rate](name:nitrogen_source_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when silane gas is being injected into the plasma vessel.

sources.enhanced_context: Silane (SiH4).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Silane (SiH4)

NAMES.name: source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected atom contributes Z equivalent electrons per second according to its atomic number.
NAMES.long:
The source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral gas is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Every injected atom of atomic number $Z$ contributes $Z$ equivalent electrons per second to the total inventory rate, providing a unified accounting framework across species of differing nuclear charge.

The defining relation for a single injected species is:

$$
\dot{S} = Z \cdot \dot{N}_{\mathrm{atoms}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{atoms}}$ is the raw atomic delivery rate in atoms per second and $Z$ is the atomic number of the injected species. For simultaneous multi-species injection, contributions are summed over all active species.

This rate is inferred from calibrated mass-flow controllers or upstream pressure-rise measurements on the gas supply plumbing. It is the instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated equivalent-electron inventories, such as [accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count) or [accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection). The nearest-peer quantity gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection provides the vessel-integrated analog expressed in raw gas-phase particles rather than equivalent electrons.
NAMES.sign: Positive when gas is being delivered into the vessel at a nonzero rate, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

NAMES.name: argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron argon source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected argon atom with Z = 18 contributes 18 equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The argon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral argon with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. The equivalent-electron convention counts each injected neutral argon atom as 18 equivalent electrons because neutral argon has 18 electrons; this is an inventory-accounting convention, not a statement about subsequent ionization or confinement.

The defining relation for injected argon is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the raw argon-atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is the dimensionless atomic number of argon.

This quantity is the argon-species member of [source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). It is the instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated equivalent-electron inventory [accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count), and differs from raw gas-particle source rates by the factor $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when argon is delivered into the plasma vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

sources.enhanced_context: Argon.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon

NAMES.name: carbon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron carbon source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, with each injected carbon atom contributing six equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The carbon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral carbon with atomic number six is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. It is the carbon-specific component of [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

For carbon injection, the defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{C}} = 6\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the raw carbon-atom delivery rate; both rates have units of inverse seconds.

This quantity counts injected carbon atoms, not electrons currently present in the plasma, carbon ionization states, or the net carbon balance after transport and removal. Its time integral gives [accumulated carbon count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection). The same equivalent-electron convention applies to [tritium source rate due to gas injection](name:tritium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), with a different atomic-number factor.
NAMES.sign: Positive when carbon gas is delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon

NAMES.name: helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Instantaneous rate of helium-3 atom delivery into the plasma vessel by gas injection, where each He-3 atom counts as two equivalent electrons due to its atomic number Z = 2.
NAMES.long:
The helium-3 source rate due to gas injection is the instantaneous equivalent-electron count rate for helium-3 ($^3$He, $Z = 2$) delivered by external gas injection systems into the plasma vessel. In the equivalent-electron counting convention, each injected helium-3 atom contributes 2 count units to the rate, so the reported value equals twice the physical atom delivery rate.

The equivalent-electron rate $\dot{N}_{\text{He-3}}$ is the time derivative of the cumulative helium-3 inventory:

$$
\dot{N}_{\text{He-3}} = \frac{d N_{\text{He-3}}}{dt}
$$

where $N_{\text{He-3}}$ is the [accumulated helium-3 count since plasma breakdown](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection).

The injection rate is inferred from calibrated gas feed diagnostics such as piezoelectric or solenoid valves with integrated flow metering. Helium-3 is employed for minority-species ion cyclotron heating, specialized fueling experiments, and impurity studies requiring a light noble gas. The analogous hydrogen rate is [hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), and the species-summed total across all injected gasses is given by [source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when helium-3 gas is being delivered into the plasma vessel.

NAMES.name: helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of helium-4 delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection, with each helium-4 atom contributing two equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The helium-4 source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral helium-4 is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas-injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Each helium-4 atom contributes two counts because helium has atomic number 2.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{He4}} = Z_{\mathrm{He}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}} = 2\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{He}}=2$ is helium's atomic number. This is the helium-4 component of the [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection); integrating it over time gives the [accumulated helium-4 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection). The [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) uses the same atomic-number weighting but represents a separate isotope inventory.
NAMES.sign: Positive when helium-4 gas is delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

sources.enhanced_context: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons.

sources.parent_definition: Helium isotope with 4 nucleons

NAMES.name: hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron hydrogen source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems; each hydrogen atom contributes one equivalent-electron count.
NAMES.long:
The hydrogen source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral hydrogen atoms are admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Because hydrogen has atomic number one, each atom contributes one equivalent-electron count.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{H}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}} = \dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}, \qquad Z_{\mathrm{H}} = 1
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the neutral hydrogen-atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen atomic number. This is the hydrogen component of the total [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). Its time integral gives the accumulated hydrogen inventory [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when hydrogen gas is being delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

NAMES.name: krypton_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron krypton source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected krypton atom with Z = 36 contributes 36 equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The krypton source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral krypton with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Each neutral krypton atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ equivalent electrons to the equivalent particle inventory; this accounting uses nuclear charge and does not imply ionization at the injection location.

The defining relation for krypton injection is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton equivalent-electron source rate in equivalent-electron counts per second, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the neutral krypton atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36$ is the atomic number of krypton.

This is the krypton-species contribution to [source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) and is the instantaneous time derivative of [accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) when the same equivalent-electron accounting is used. It excludes krypton supplied by mechanisms other than gas injection and differs from gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection, which is counted as raw gas-phase particles rather than equivalent electrons. It is directly parallel to same-family species quantities such as [argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), differing by the injected species and its atomic number.

NAMES.name: lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron lithium source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, with each injected lithium atom contributing three equivalent-electron counts.
NAMES.long:
The lithium source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral lithium with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. It is the lithium-specific component of the [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), rather than the raw lithium-atom delivery rate.

For lithium, the defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Li}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}} = 3\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the raw lithium atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is lithium's dimensionless atomic number.

The equivalent-electron convention assigns three source counts to each injected lithium atom and excludes other gas species. This rate is the time derivative of the corresponding [accumulated lithium count](name:accumulated_lithium_count); its atomic-number weighting distinguishes it from the [helium-3 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when lithium is delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

NAMES.name: source_rate_due_to_injection
NAMES.short: Source rate due to injection is the instantaneous rate of electron-equivalent particles supplied by active injection, formed by nuclear-charge weighting of the injected species. It represents the injection-only material source and excludes particle production or loss after injection.
NAMES.long:
Source rate due to injection is the instantaneous rate of electron-equivalent particles supplied by active injection. It is an additive material source for the plasma particle inventory, formed by weighting each injected particle by the total nuclear charge associated with that injected particle.

The electron-equivalent aggregate is defined by

$$
S_\mathrm{inj}(t) = \sum_j Z_j \frac{dN_{j,\mathrm{inj}}}{dt}
$$

where $S_\mathrm{inj}$ is this source rate, $N_{j,\mathrm{inj}}$ is the cumulative count of injected particles of species $j$, $Z_j$ is the total nuclear charge number carried by one injected particle of species $j$, and $t$ is time.

The sum is over active injection only and excludes changes to free-particle populations caused after injection by ionization, recombination, charge exchange, recycling, pumping, or plasma reactions. For an elemental species not resolved by charge state, the contribution is charge-state-summed before the nuclear-charge weighting is applied; species-resolved injected source rates such as [deuterium source rate due to injection](name:deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection) are unweighted summands until this weighting relation is applied. The electron-equivalent convention makes [electron source rate due to injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection) the nearest electron-population counterpart, while [electron source rate](name:electron_source_rate) is broader because it is not restricted to active injection. A [gas source rate at wall](name:total_particle_source_rate_at_wall_due_to_gas_injection) is wall-referenced rather than a species-weighted aggregate; a [total particle source rate] includes additional source mechanisms when defined with a compatible counting convention.
NAMES.sign: Positive when active injection adds electron-equivalent particles to the plasma particle inventory.

NAMES.name: deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Instantaneous rate of deuterium particles supplied by active injection, expressed on a common equivalent-electron basis.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous particle supply from active injection systems for deuterium, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. Because each deuterium atom has nuclear charge number one, the equivalent-electron rate equals the deuterium particle rate.

The defining relation is

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D,eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{D}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)=\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the injected deuterium particle rate, and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ is the dimensionless deuterium nuclear charge number. This is a component of the multi-species [source rate due to injection](name:source_rate_due_to_injection) and is distinct from the charge-weighted [electron source rate due to injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection). It represents injected inventory supply, not a local volumetric particle source or a net plasma production-minus-loss rate.

NAMES.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_injection
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Instantaneous rate of electron-equivalent particles supplied by active injection, obtained by nuclear-charge weighting each injected atomic species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the instantaneous particle supply from active injection systems, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis when multiple injected species are combined. It represents the electron inventory that the supplied material can contribute after ionization.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=\sum_s Z_s\dot{N}_s(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $\dot{N}_s$ are source rates, $s$ indexes the injected atomic species, and $Z_s$ is the dimensionless nuclear charge number. For molecular feeds, each constituent atom is included with its nuclear-charge weighting. This is the charge-weighted instance of the [source rate due to injection](name:source_rate_due_to_injection); for unit-charge deuterium, it equals the [deuterium source rate due to injection](name:deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection).

This is an injected inventory rate, not a local volumetric particle source or a net plasma production-minus-loss rate such as the [total electron source rate](name:total_electron_source_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when active injection increases the supplied equivalent-electron inventory.

NAMES.name: temperature_at_inlet
NAMES.short: Absolute thermodynamic temperature characterizing the thermal state of a coolant or working fluid at a defined plant-system location.
NAMES.long:
Absolute thermodynamic temperature is the intensive thermal state variable of a coolant or working fluid at a defined plant-system location. It describes the fluid temperature itself, not a temperature difference or temperature rise.

The quantity applies to fluid states at component or system ports. For the inlet-specific instance, [coolant temperature at inlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_inlet) describes the coolant as it enters a cooling loop or plant component; corresponding outlet quantities describe the downstream state, such as [coolant temperature at outlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_outlet).

NAMES.name: coolant_temperature_at_inlet
NAMES.short: Coolant temperature at the inlet is the absolute thermodynamic temperature of the coolant or working fluid as it enters a cooling loop, plant component, or calorimetry component. It is the coolant-specific inlet temperature and not a temperature rise.
NAMES.long:
Coolant temperature at the inlet is the absolute thermodynamic [coolant temperature](name:coolant_temperature) of the coolant or working fluid at the upstream boundary of a cooling loop, plant component, or calorimetry component. It is the coolant-specific form of [temperature at inlet](name:temperature_at_inlet) and denotes the state of the entering fluid, not the temperature of a solid wall or downstream fluid.

The inlet value is the coolant-temperature value on the inlet boundary:

$$
T_\mathrm{in} = T_\mathrm{coolant}\rvert_{\Gamma_\mathrm{in}}
$$

where $T_\mathrm{coolant}$ is the coolant thermodynamic temperature and $\Gamma_\mathrm{in}$ is the boundary across which the coolant enters the loop or component.

This name is generic for an inlet; a more specific name that identifies a cooling circuit, port, or component denotes the same physical quantity evaluated at that narrower inlet. It is distinct from [coolant_temperature_at_outlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_outlet); the difference $T_\mathrm{out}-T_\mathrm{in}$ may enter enthalpy or thermal-power balances, but this quantity is not itself a temperature difference or transferred thermal power.

NAMES.name: temperature_at_outlet
NAMES.short: Absolute thermodynamic temperature of a fluid stream at a component outlet, defining its downstream thermal state.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the absolute thermodynamic temperature of a fluid as it exits a component or cooling loop. It defines the outlet thermal state and may serve as a downstream boundary condition; [coolant temperature at outlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_outlet) is a coolant-specific instance.

For a fluid in thermodynamic equilibrium, absolute temperature is defined by

$$
T = \left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial S}\right)_{V,N}
$$

where $T$ is absolute temperature, $U$ is internal energy, $S$ is entropy, $V$ is volume, and $N$ is the amount of substance held fixed in the derivative.

The quantity refers to the state at the exit location and is distinct from the upstream [temperature at inlet](name:temperature_at_inlet); it does not by itself represent a temperature difference, heat flow, or transferred power.

NAMES.name: coolant_temperature_at_outlet
NAMES.short: Absolute thermodynamic temperature of coolant as it leaves a cooling component or loop, defining the downstream thermal state of the coolant stream.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the absolute thermodynamic temperature of the coolant stream at a cooling component or loop outlet. It defines the coolant’s downstream thermal state and is the coolant-specific form of [temperature at outlet](name:temperature_at_outlet).

The outlet value refers to the coolant at the outlet boundary and excludes the inlet state, which is represented by [coolant temperature at inlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_inlet). It applies to the coolant or working fluid identified as the cooling medium and does not represent the temperature of the cooled component or the temperature rise across the circuit.

NAMES.name: thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system converts total thermal input into gross useful electrical output across its heat-conversion system.
NAMES.long:
The thermal efficiency of a plant system is the dimensionless ratio of gross useful electrical power produced to total thermal power supplied to the heat-conversion system over the same accounting interval. It is a specific conversion metric within the broader [efficiency of a plant system](name:efficiency_of_plant_system) concept.

The defining relation is:

$$
\eta_{\mathrm{th}} = \frac{P_{\mathrm{gross}}}{P_{\mathrm{th,in}}} = 1 - \frac{P_{\mathrm{th,out}}}{P_{\mathrm{th,in}}}
$$

where $\eta_{\mathrm{th}}$ is thermal efficiency, $P_{\mathrm{gross}}$ is gross useful electrical power, $P_{\mathrm{th,in}}$ is total thermal power entering the conversion cycle as represented by [total thermal power at inlet](name:total_thermal_power_at_inlet), and $P_{\mathrm{th,out}}$ is rejected thermal power represented by [total thermal power at outlet](name:total_thermal_power_at_outlet).

Thermal efficiency accounts for thermal-to-electric conversion and excludes subtraction of internal electrical consumption from gross output. That recirculating-power accounting distinguishes it from [net efficiency of a plant system](name:net_efficiency_of_plant_system).

NAMES.name: thermal_energy_of_plant_component_port
NAMES.short: Cumulative thermal energy extracted through a cooling-loop port on a plant component since the start of the plasma pulse, obtained by time-integrating the measured coolant enthalpy balance.
NAMES.long:
The thermal energy of a plant component port is the total heat removed by the cooling loop of that component, accumulated from pulse start to the current measurement time. It is the time-integral of the instantaneous [thermal power extracted at the port](name:thermal_power_of_plant_component_port), making it a running calorimetric total rather than a rate quantity.

The defining relation is:

$$
E_\text{th}(t) = \int_0^t P_\text{th}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $P_\text{th}$ is the instantaneous extracted thermal power (in W) and the lower integration limit is the start of the pulse.

The integrand $P_\text{th}$ is itself derived from the coolant enthalpy balance $P_\text{th} = \dot{m} c_p (T_\text{out} - T_\text{in})$, where $\dot{m}$ is the coolant mass flow rate, $c_p$ is the specific heat capacity of the coolant, and $T_\text{out}$ and $T_\text{in}$ are the [outlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_outlet) and [inlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_inlet) coolant temperatures. This cumulative measure is used in pulse-integrated heat load accounting for plasma-facing components and cooling circuits, complementing the instantaneous power signal for assessing total energy deposition over a discharge.

sources.enhanced_context: Cumulative thermal energy extracted from a calorimetry component since the start of the pulse. Derived from the time-integral of the measured coolant enthalpy balance over the measurement interval.
sources.leaf_definition: Energy extracted from the component since the start of the pulse

NAMES.name: thermal_power_at_inlet
NAMES.short: Thermal power delivered to the heat-input side of a power conversion system, representing the rate of recoverable heat entering the cycle prior to thermal-to-electric conversion.
NAMES.long:
The thermal power at inlet quantifies the rate of thermal energy crossing the inlet boundary of a power conversion system. It represents the total recoverable heat flowing into the cycle from primary heat-transfer circuits — such as blanket coolant loops and divertor circuits in a fusion plant — before any conversion into electrical work. This quantity is the thermal specialization of the more general [power_at_inlet](name:power_at_inlet), which encompasses all power forms at the system inlet.

The thermodynamic conversion efficiency $\eta_{th}$ links this quantity to the gross electrical output $P_{elec}$ via:

$$
\eta_{th} = \frac{P_{elec}}{P_{th,in}}
$$

where $P_{th,in}$ is the thermal power at inlet and $P_{elec}$ is the gross electrical power delivered by the conversion cycle.

The child quantity [total_thermal_power_at_inlet](name:total_thermal_power_at_inlet) gives the gross aggregate thermal input summed over all heat sources entering the cycle. The rejected heat leaving the cycle is captured by [thermal_power_at_outlet](name:thermal_power_at_outlet), and together these quantities constrain the [thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system). In fusion power plant studies, the thermal power at inlet from blanket and divertor circuits is expected to reach the multi-gigawatt range for reactor-scale devices.

NAMES.name: thermal_power_at_outlet
NAMES.short: Thermal power rejected through a system outlet as waste heat rather than converted into useful electrical output.
NAMES.long:
Thermal outlet power is the rate at which energy leaves a power-conversion system through its outlet as rejected heat. It is the thermal-waste component of [power at outlet](name:power_at_outlet), distinct from energy converted into useful electrical output.

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,out}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{waste}}}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th,out}}$ is the thermal outlet power, $E_{\mathrm{waste}}$ is cumulative rejected thermal energy, and $t$ is time.

The quantity is a rate, not cumulative thermal energy, and includes the common physical meaning represented by [total thermal power at outlet](name:total_thermal_power_at_outlet).

NAMES.name: thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket
NAMES.short: Thermal power of the breeder blanket is the integrated non-nuclear heat load entering the blanket through its plasma-facing surface, excluding volumetric neutron and photon heating. It is a blanket-level surface-deposition power, distinct from module-level coolant heat removal.
NAMES.long:
Thermal power of the breeder blanket is the total rate at which non-nuclear thermal energy enters the breeder blanket through its plasma-facing surface. It represents an integrated surface heat load on the blanket, not a local heat-flux density.

For a surface heat-load representation, the integrated power is defined by the area integral of the local non-nuclear heat flux entering the blanket:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,bb}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf,bb}}} q_{\mathrm{th}} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th,bb}}$ is the thermal power of the breeder blanket, $A_{\mathrm{pf,bb}}$ is the plasma-facing surface area of the breeder blanket included in the blanket-level total, $q_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local non-nuclear heat-flux density directed into the blanket, and $dA$ is the surface element.

This quantity excludes volumetric neutron and photon energy deposition in blanket material, which is represented by [nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket). It also differs from [thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), which denotes module-level thermal power associated with an individual breeder-blanket module rather than the blanket-level plasma-facing surface load.

NAMES.name: thermal_power_of_plant_component_port
NAMES.short: Rate of heat removed from a plant component by coolant, determined by the coolant enthalpy increase between the associated inlet and outlet.
NAMES.long:
Thermal power at a plant-component port is the rate of heat energy transferred from the component into the coolant circuit. It is the thermal component of [power of a plant component port](name:power_of_plant_component_port).

The defining relation is

$$
P_\mathrm{th} = \dot{m}\left(h_\mathrm{out}-h_\mathrm{in}\right)
$$

where $P_\mathrm{th}$ is thermal power, $\dot{m}$ is coolant mass flow rate in kg s$^{-1}$, and $h_\mathrm{in}$ and $h_\mathrm{out}$ are the coolant specific enthalpies at the inlet and outlet in J kg$^{-1}$, respectively.

Positive values mean that the coolant gains enthalpy along the flow path and therefore removes heat from the plant component. This quantity excludes electrical, radiative, and other non-coolant-mediated power transfers.

NAMES.name: toroidal_velocity_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the shattered-pellet center-of-mass velocity along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal center-of-mass velocity is the signed translational velocity of the shattered pellet's mass distribution projected onto the geometric toroidal direction. The center-of-mass velocity represents the mass-weighted motion of the pellet fragments, excluding their internal relative motions.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{cm}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the shattered-pellet center-of-mass velocity in m s$^{-1}$ and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is distinct from the [radial shattered-pellet velocity](name:radial_velocity_of_pellet) and [vertical shattered-pellet velocity](name:vertical_velocity_of_pellet), which are the corresponding $R$ and $Z$ projections.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the shattered-pellet center of mass moves in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: total_gas_source_rate_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short: Gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection is the non-negative total unweighted rate at which neutral gas particles are injected by gas valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane. It is not an electron-equivalent or charge-weighted rate.
NAMES.long:
Gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection is the instantaneous total unweighted source rate of neutral gas particles injected by gas-injection valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane. It counts injected neutral gas particles themselves, not electron-equivalent particles, charge-weighted particles, or particles produced by later plasma or wall interactions.

For the set of midplane injection valves, the total rate is the sum of the individual unweighted valve particle throughputs:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\mathrm{gas\,inj}} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{mid}}} \dot{N}_k
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\mathrm{gas\,inj}}$ is the gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection, $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{mid}}$ is the set of gas-injection valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane, and $\dot{N}_k$ is the unweighted neutral-particle throughput of valve $k$.

The total includes all gas-injection valves in the midplane group and excludes upper, lower, wall, recycling, pumping, ionization, and transport contributions. It is not additive with regional gas-source quantities that use an electron-equivalent or charge-weighted convention. Its time integral is the corresponding [accumulated total gas count at midplane due to gas injection](name:accumulated_total_gas_count_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection).

sources.enhanced_context: Gas injection rate from all valves located near the equatorial midplane.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Gas injection rate from all valves located near the equatorial midplane

NAMES.name: total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short: Instantaneous total rate at which neutral gas is introduced into the lower vacuum-vessel region by gas injection valves, summed over lower-region valves and expressed using the equivalent-electron convention across injected species.
NAMES.long:
Instantaneous total rate at which neutral gas is introduced into the lower vacuum-vessel region by gas injection valves is the lower-region aggregate equivalent-electron source rate due to gas injection. It counts each injected neutral atom or molecule by the number of electrons associated with its neutral composition and sums over all injected species and all lower-region gas-injection valves.

The multi-species aggregate is defined by:

$$
\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{lower}} = \sum_{v \in \mathrm{lower}} \sum_m E_m\,\dot{N}_{v,m}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{lower}}$ is this total lower gas source rate, $\dot{N}_{v,m}$ is the neutral gas injection rate of atomic or molecular species $m$ from lower-region valve $v$, and $E_m = \sum_a \nu_{a,m} Z_a$ is the equivalent-electron count for one neutral injected particle of species $m$, with $\nu_{a,m}$ the stoichiometric count of atom $a$ in species $m$ and $Z_a$ its atomic number.

This quantity is an injected source into the vacuum vessel and excludes pumping, wall recycling, ionization losses after entry, and gas introduced outside the lower region. Species-level quantities such as [neon source rate](name:neon_source_rate) and [propane source rate](name:propane_source_rate) are individual species contributions under the same equivalent-electron convention; [gas source rate of the vacuum vessel due to gas injection] is the vessel-level source quantity without the lower-region restriction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral gas is introduced into the vacuum vessel through lower-region injection valves.

sources.enhanced_context: Gas injection rate from all valves located near near the bottom of the vaccuum chamber.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Gas injection rate from all valves located near near the bottom of the vaccuum chamber

NAMES.name: total_particle_source_rate_at_wall_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.short: Total rate at which neutral particles are supplied through wall gas-injection sources, summed over the included injection channels and particle species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the incoming neutral-particle source rate produced by gas injection at the wall. It represents injected particles, not particles recycled from or incident on the wall.

The total rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{wall,gas}}(t)=\sum_i \dot{N}_i(t)
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{wall,gas}}$ is the total wall gas-injection particle source rate, and $\dot{N}_i$ is the injection rate for included particle species and gas-injection sources indexed by $i$. The aggregation uses particle counts on the selected species basis and does not apply charge-state or electron-equivalent weighting.

This incoming source is distinct from the [neutral particle flux at the wall](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall), which describes particles arriving at the wall per unit area, and from the [total gas source rate at the midplane due to gas injection](name:total_gas_source_rate_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection), which has a different injection locus.

sources.leaf_definition: Gas puff rate (in equivalent electrons)
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to electrons

sources.enhanced_context: Gas puff rate for a neutral species at the wall, representing the flux of neutral gas injected into the plasma volume from wall sources. Used in plasma-wall interaction and particle balance analyses.

NAMES.name: total_power_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Total real electrical power consumed by all included plant systems, obtained by summing their individual electrical loads at the corresponding system boundaries.
NAMES.long:
Total power of plant systems is the real electrical power consumed by the included plant systems, summed over their individual electrical loads. It is the aggregate auxiliary load counterpart to [power of a plant system](name:power_of_plant_system), rather than thermal, apparent, reactive, or accumulated energy.

For the selected set of plant systems, the total power is defined as

$$
P_\mathrm{total} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} P_i
$$

where $P_\mathrm{total}$ is the aggregate plant-system power, $P_i$ is the real electrical power consumed by plant system $i$, and $N$ is the number of included plant systems.

The sum represents one-way consumption at each system electrical boundary and excludes locally generated or returned real power. It differs from [net power of a plant system](name:net_power_of_plant_system), which accounts for generation minus consumption at one system boundary, and from [absorbed power of a plant system](name:absorbed_power_of_plant_system), which describes an individual system.

sources.enhanced_context: Total electrical power consumed to operate the plant (P_plant_op), encompassing all auxiliary systems. Subtracted from generated electrical power to obtain the net electricity output of the fusion power plant.
sources.leaf_definition: Total electrical power used to operate the plant
sources.parent_definition: Electric plant operation

NAMES.name: total_thermal_coolant_absorbed_power_at_wall
NAMES.short: Thermal power extracted by active coolant circuits from cooled plasma-facing wall surfaces, representing energy removal from the wall rather than incident plasma power.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total heat-transfer rate from cooled plasma-facing wall structures into their active coolant circuits. It represents energy removed from the wall and is distinct from [total incident power at the wall](name:total_incident_power_at_wall), which measures plasma power arriving at wall surfaces.

$$
P_{\mathrm{cool}} = \sum_i \dot{Q}_{i}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cool}}$ is the total coolant-absorbed thermal power and $\dot{Q}_{i}$ is the heat-transfer rate from the wall into coolant circuit $i$. The sum includes all active cooling circuits serving the cooled plasma-facing surfaces and excludes heat deposited on uncooled structures or power merely incident on the wall.

sources.enhanced_context: Power transferred from the plasma-facing wall to the active cooling systems. Represents the total thermal power extracted by cooling, balancing incident plasma heat loads and accounting for energy removal from the tokamak wall.
sources.leaf_definition: Power to cooling systems
sources.parent_definition: Simple 0D description of plasma-wall interaction

NAMES.name: total_thermal_power_at_inlet
NAMES.short: Thermal power at inlet is the recoverable heat-input rate entering a power-conversion cycle at its heat-input boundary before thermal-to-electric conversion, aggregated over all inlet streams feeding the cycle.
NAMES.long:
Thermal power at inlet is the recoverable heat-input rate entering a power-conversion cycle at its heat-input boundary before thermal-to-electric conversion. This member is the cycle-level total, summed over all inlet streams and heat-input contributions feeding the cycle, rather than the rate of a single stream or port.

The total inlet heat-input rate is the sum over the heat-input boundary contributions:

$$
P_\mathrm{th,in} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}_\mathrm{in}} \dot{Q}_{\mathrm{th,in},i}
$$

where $\mathcal{I}_\mathrm{in}$ is the set of heat-input boundary contributions, $\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{th,in},i}$ is the recoverable thermal power delivered by contribution $i$ into the cycle in watts, and $P_\mathrm{th,in}$ is the aggregate inlet thermal power in watts. Each per-port contribution corresponds to a [thermal power of plant component port](name:thermal_power_of_plant_component_port) evaluated at an inlet port, and the single-stream counterpart is [thermal power at inlet](name:thermal_power_at_inlet).

This quantity excludes [total thermal power at outlet](name:total_thermal_power_at_outlet), which is the heat rejected from the cycle, and excludes net electrical output. Over the same balance boundary, [thermal efficiency of plant system](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system) relates these quantities through $\eta_\mathrm{th} = (P_\mathrm{th,in} - P_\mathrm{th,out})/P_\mathrm{th,in}$, where $P_\mathrm{th,out}$ is the rejected thermal power.
NAMES.sign: Positive when net heat flows into the power-conversion cycle across the heat-input boundary.

sources.enhanced_context: Total thermal power supplied to the power conversion cycle of a fusion power plant, representing gross heat input driving thermal-to-electric conversion. Includes contributions from fusion reactions and blanket energy multiplication.
sources.leaf_definition: Total heat flow being supplied to the thermal plant (fusion thermal power)
sources.parent_definition: Energy conversion

NAMES.name: total_thermal_power_at_outlet
NAMES.short: Total thermal power at the outlet is the aggregate rate at which thermal energy leaves a power-conversion cycle through all heat-rejection outlet streams. It includes all rejected heat contributions and excludes useful electrical output.
NAMES.long:
Total thermal power at the outlet is the aggregate rate at which thermal energy leaves a power-conversion cycle through all heat-rejection outlet streams. It represents the total rejected heat load delivered from the conversion cycle to its heat sink, excluding useful electrical output.

The total outlet thermal power is the sum of the thermal-power contributions from the individual heat-rejection outlet streams:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,out}}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{O}} P_{\mathrm{th,out},i} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{waste,out}}}{dt}
$$

where $\mathcal{O}$ is the set of heat-rejection outlet streams, $P_{\mathrm{th,out},i}$ is the thermal power carried by outlet stream $i$, $E_{\mathrm{waste,out}}$ is the cumulative rejected thermal energy in J, and $t$ is time in s.

This quantity is the aggregate over outlet streams; an individual outlet-stream contribution is [thermal_power_at_outlet](name:thermal_power_at_outlet). For a steady conversion cycle with no net energy accumulation inside the conversion boundary, it is related to [total_thermal_power_at_inlet](name:total_thermal_power_at_inlet) by the first-law balance $P_{\mathrm{th,out}}^{\mathrm{tot}} = P_{\mathrm{th,in}}^{\mathrm{tot}} - P_{\mathrm{net}}$, where $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net useful electrical power delivered by the conversion system.

sources.enhanced_context: Total thermal power rejected from the power plant thermodynamic cycle to the environment (waste heat not converted to electricity). Represents the heat sink load governed by the second law of thermodynamics in the fusion power plant balance.
sources.leaf_definition: Total heat flow being rejected from the thermal plant
sources.parent_definition: Energy conversion

NAMES.name: tritium_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Accumulated number of tritium atoms injected as gas during the plasma prefill phase, expressed in equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The tritium prefill count records the total number of tritium atoms ($^3_1\text{H}$, charge number $Z = 1$) delivered to the vessel as neutral gas during the prefill phase — the period from the start of gas injection up to plasma breakdown. Because tritium is a hydrogen isotope with $Z = 1$, the equivalent-electron count equals the raw atom count directly.

The prefill phase establishes the initial neutral gas background required for reproducible plasma initiation; the tritium component is particularly relevant in deuterium-tritium operations, where it contributes to the initial fuel mix and breakdown conditions. The count is accumulated from calibrated gas injection valve signals integrated over the duration of the prefill phase. For multi-species prefill scenarios, the total electron-equivalent inventory is $\sum_s Z_s N_s$, where $Z_s$ is the charge number and $N_s$ the atom count for species $s$.

This quantity complements [deuterium_prefill_count](name:deuterium_prefill_count), [neon_prefill_count](name:neon_prefill_count), and [krypton_prefill_count](name:krypton_prefill_count), which together with this name characterize the full multi-species neutral gas inventory available at breakdown; the aggregate is captured by [prefill_count](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when tritium atoms have been injected into the vessel during the prefill phase.

NAMES.name: tritium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Instantaneous equivalent-electron tritium source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection, with each injected tritium atom contributing one equivalent-electron count.
NAMES.long:
The tritium source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral tritium with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{T}} = 1$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. It is the tritium-specific component of the [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{T}} = Z_{\mathrm{T}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}} = \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the raw tritium atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{T}}$ is tritium's atomic number. The rate is the instantaneous derivative of the accumulated inventory [accumulated tritium count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection), and it counts delivered atoms rather than plasma electron content or ionization state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when tritium gas is being delivered into the vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_pellet_path_point
NAMES.short: Vertical Z coordinate of a point on a pellet injection trajectory in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured relative to the tokamak equatorial plane.
NAMES.long:
The vertical coordinate of a pellet path point is the $Z$ position of a specified point on a pellet injection trajectory. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius in meters, $\phi$ is toroidal angle in radians increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height in meters measured relative to the tokamak equatorial plane. Together with the [major radius] and [toroidal angle], it specifies the spatial location of the path point.

Values are usually obtained from injector and guide-tube geometry, alignment surveys, trajectory modeling, or reconstruction of the pellet path when direct position observations are available. The coordinate describes the geometry of the path point and does not by itself specify pellet speed, mass, fragmentation, ablation rate, or time of flight.

For paths crossing the confined plasma, $Z$ is commonly within -1 to 1 m in medium-sized tokamaks and can span about -3 to 3 m in large tokamaks. Points near injectors or external launch structures can lie farther from the equatorial plane, depending on the device geometry.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the path point lies above the tokamak equatorial plane in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_shattering_position
NAMES.short: Vertical coordinate of the shattering position is the Z coordinate of the shatter-cone origin relative to the equatorial plane Z = 0 in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, locating the pellet-fragmentation point.
NAMES.long:
Vertical coordinate of the shattering position is the $Z$ coordinate of the shatter-cone origin in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It locates the pellet-fragmentation point relative to the equatorial plane $Z=0$.

The coordinate is the vertical projection of the shattering-position displacement vector:

$$
Z_\mathrm{shat} = \mathbf{r}_\mathrm{shat} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{shat}$ is the displacement vector from the coordinate origin $R=0$, $Z=0$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame to the shattering position, expressed in meters; $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit basis vector; and $Z_\mathrm{shat}$ is the resulting vertical coordinate, expressed in meters.

Together with [radial_coordinate_of_shattering_position](name:radial_coordinate_of_shattering_position), this quantity specifies the poloidal location of pellet fragmentation. It is distinct from [vertical_coordinate_of_pellet_path_point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_pellet_path_point), which denotes the vertical coordinate of a point on the pellet path rather than the fixed shattering position.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the shattering position lies above the equatorial plane $Z=0$, in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_velocity_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the shattered-pellet center-of-mass velocity, resolved along the Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the translational velocity component of the shattered-pellet center of mass along the vertical direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
v_Z = \frac{dZ_{\rm cm}}{dt} = \mathbf{v}_{\rm cm} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $Z_{\rm cm}$ is the vertical coordinate of the pellet center of mass, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}_{\rm cm}$ is its velocity vector, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector. This component is distinct from the [radial velocity of the pellet](name:radial_velocity_of_pellet) and [toroidal velocity of the pellet](name:toroidal_velocity_of_pellet); it is not the total center-of-mass speed.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the shattered-pellet center of mass moves toward increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short: X component of the shatter-cone major-axis unit vector, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The major-axis unit vector $\hat{e}_\mathrm{maj}$ describes the orientation of the major axis of the elliptic shatter cone in a shattered pellet injector. This quantity is the $x$-component of $\hat{e}_\mathrm{maj}$, projected onto the $x$-axis of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame:

$$
(\hat{e}_\mathrm{maj})_x = \hat{e}_\mathrm{maj} \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $\hat{x}$ is the unit vector along the $x$-axis. Because $\hat{e}_\mathrm{maj}$ is a unit vector, the sum of squares of its three Cartesian components equals unity. Together with [y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone](name:z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), this component fully specifies the major-axis orientation of the shatter cone. The complementary minor-axis x-component is [x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).
