NAMES.name: xenon_count
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Number of xenon atoms expressed as a dimensionless equivalent-electron count, where each xenon atom contributes 54 equivalent electrons equal to its atomic number Z = 54.
NAMES.long:
The xenon count quantifies the xenon inventory in the plasma vessel as a dimensionless equivalent-electron count. The conversion uses xenon's atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Xe} = 54$:

$$
N_\mathrm{eq} = Z_\mathrm{Xe}\, N_\mathrm{Xe} = 54\, N_\mathrm{Xe}
$$

where $N_\mathrm{Xe}$ is the number of xenon atoms and $N_\mathrm{eq}$ is the equivalent-electron count. This convention places xenon on the same dimensionless electron-inventory basis as other injected species, enabling direct comparison of their contributions to the total electron budget. The [accumulated_xenon_count](name:accumulated_xenon_count) is the specific instance that time-integrates this inventory over the post-breakdown phase.

NAMES.name: accumulated_xenon_count
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of xenon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons, where each xenon atom contributes 54 equivalent electrons corresponding to its atomic number Z = 54.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated xenon count tracks the total xenon atoms introduced by gas injection from plasma breakdown onward, expressed as a dimensionless equivalent-electron tally in which each neutral xenon atom contributes 54 counts equal to its atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} = 54$.

The defining integral is:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}(t) = 54 \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dt'} \, dt'
$$

where $dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}/dt'$ is the instantaneous xenon injection rate in atoms s$^{-1}$, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the time of plasma breakdown in s, and $N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}$ is dimensionless. The prefill xenon inventory prior to breakdown is excluded from this integral and is tracked separately by [accumulated_xenon_prefill_count](name:accumulated_xenon_prefill_count).

The instantaneous injection rate contributing to this integral is characterized by [xenon_source_rate](name:xenon_source_rate). Xenon is employed as a high-$Z$ impurity in disruption mitigation and radiative cooling experiments; in massive gas injection scenarios the equivalent-electron count can reach $10^{23}$–$10^{24}$. For lighter noble gas comparisons, see [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) ($Z = 10$) and [accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) ($Z = 36$).
NAMES.sign: Positive when xenon gas is injected into the vessel after plasma breakdown, incrementing the cumulative count.

sources.enhanced_context: Xenon.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon

NAMES.name: xenon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Equivalent-electron count of xenon gas introduced during the plasma prefill phase before breakdown, with each xenon atom contributing 54 equivalent electrons equal to its atomic number.
NAMES.long:
Xenon prefill count is the total amount of xenon introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral xenon atom contributes 54 equivalent electrons equal to the atomic number of xenon, $Z_{Xe} = 54$.

The equivalent-electron count is accumulated over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{Xe,\mathrm{prefill}} = Z_{Xe} \, N_{Xe,\mathrm{prefill}} = Z_{Xe} \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{Xe}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{Xe,\mathrm{prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{Xe,\mathrm{prefill}}$ is the accumulated xenon atom count, $\dot{N}_{Xe}$ is the xenon atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the start of the prefill interval, and $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

The gas-injection contribution is tracked by [accumulated_xenon_prefill_count](name:accumulated_xenon_prefill_count). Xenon's atomic number of 54 places it at the upper end of the prefill-species family — compare [krypton_prefill_count](name:krypton_prefill_count) ($Z = 36$) and [neon_prefill_count](name:neon_prefill_count) ($Z = 10$) — and all are reported on the same dimensionless equivalent-electron basis under [prefill_count](name:prefill_count).

NAMES.name: accumulated_xenon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of neutral xenon introduced during plasma prefill, ending at plasma breakdown, with 54 count units per atom.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the equivalent-electron inventory of neutral xenon gas introduced between the start of prefill and plasma breakdown. It represents the accumulated prefill contribution, not an instantaneous injection rate.

The defining accumulation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}^{\mathrm{prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)$ is the neutral xenon atom injection rate, $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and breakdown times, and $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}=54$ is xenon's atomic number. The resulting count assigns 54 equivalent-electron units to each xenon atom.

This quantity is the prefill component of [xenon_prefill_count](name:xenon_prefill_count) and excludes xenon introduced after breakdown, which is represented by [accumulated_xenon_count](name:accumulated_xenon_count).

sources.enhanced_context: Xenon.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon

NAMES.name: xenon_source_rate
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Instantaneous injection rate of xenon gas into the plasma vessel, where each xenon atom is counted as Z = 54 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The xenon source rate quantifies the instantaneous flux of xenon gas delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems. Xenon (atomic number Z = 54) is a heavy noble gas used as a high-radiating impurity for plasma control, impurity seeding, and disruption mitigation in fusion devices.

The equivalent-electron rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{Xe}$ is obtained by weighting the instantaneous atom injection rate by xenon's atomic number:

$$
\dot{N}_\mathrm{Xe} = 54 \cdot \dot{n}_\mathrm{Xe}
$$

where $\dot{n}_\mathrm{Xe}$ is the xenon atom flux in atoms s$^{-1}$ and 54 is the atomic number of xenon.

The injection rate is inferred from valve conductance and upstream gas pressure measurements. Integrating over time yields the cumulative xenon inventory. The [krypton_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:krypton_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) follows the same equivalent-electron convention for the neighboring noble gas krypton, while [electron_source_rate_due_to_injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection) aggregates equivalent-electron contributions across all injected species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when xenon gas flows from the injection system into the plasma vessel.

sources.enhanced_context: Xenon.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon

NAMES.name: y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short: Y component of the shatter-cone major-axis unit vector, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The major-axis unit vector $\hat{e}_\mathrm{maj}$ defines the orientation of the principal semiaxis of the elliptic shatter cone in a shattered pellet injector. This component is the projection $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj},y} = \hat{e}_\mathrm{maj} \cdot \hat{y}$ onto the Cartesian $y$-axis of the right-handed $(x, y, z)$ frame, where $\hat{y}$ is the unit vector in the $y$-direction.

Together with the [X component](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and the [Z component](name:z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), this component fully specifies the direction of the shatter-cone major axis in three-dimensional space. The three Cartesian components satisfy the normalization identity $(\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj},x})^2 + (\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj},y})^2 + (\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj},z})^2 = 1$. The major axis is geometrically distinct from, and orthogonal to, the minor axis described by [y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone](name:y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).

NAMES.name: y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short: Y-directed projection of the unit vector defining the minor axis of an elliptic shatter cone, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the Cartesian y component of the unit vector that defines the minor axis of the elliptic shatter cone. It specifies one directional component of the shatter-cone orientation.

In the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$, it is defined by:

$$
u_{\mathrm{min},y} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{min}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{min}}$ is the normalized minor-axis unit vector, $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the Cartesian y unit vector, and $u_{\mathrm{min},y}$ is their scalar projection. The vector satisfies $\lVert\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{min}}\rVert=1$.

This component is distinct from the corresponding [x component](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [z component](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), and from the [y component of the major-axis unit vector](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the minor-axis unit vector projects in the direction of increasing Cartesian y.

NAMES.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the unit vector along the unshattered pellet velocity immediately before shattering, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the z-direction projection of the pellet injector's direction unit vector, representing the direction of the unshattered pellet velocity immediately before shattering. It is resolved in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, where $\hat{z}$ is the vertical unit vector.

The component is defined by

$$
u_z = \hat{\mathbf{u}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$ is the unit vector along the unshattered pellet velocity and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the Cartesian z-axis unit vector. The complete injection direction is specified jointly with the [x component](name:x_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector) and [y component](name:y_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector), subject to $\lVert\hat{\mathbf{u}}\rVert=1$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the injection direction points toward increasing $z$ in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis.

NAMES.name: z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
NAMES.short: Z component of the shatter-cone major-axis unit vector, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The shatter cone is an elliptic cone forming the impact surface of a shattered pellet injector. When a pellet strikes this cone it fragments into a spray of shards directed toward the plasma vessel. The orientation of the cone's elliptic cross-section is described by two orthogonal unit vectors; the major-axis unit vector $\hat{e}_\mathrm{major}$ defines the long axis of that ellipse.

The z-component of the major-axis unit vector is the projection

$$
(\hat{e}_\mathrm{major})_z = \hat{e}_\mathrm{major} \cdot \hat{z}
$$

where $\hat{z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, aligned with the vertical axis $\hat{Z}$ of the cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. As a unit-vector component this quantity is dimensionless and lies in $[-1, 1]$.

Together with [x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), this component fully specifies the direction of the cone's major axis in three-dimensional space. The corresponding minor-axis complement is [z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone). The cone direction is determined from injector geometry surveys or hardware design records.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the major axis of the shatter cone has a component pointing in the $+z$ (vertically upward) direction.

NAMES.name: thermal_power_of_divertor
NAMES.short: Thermal power of divertor is the rate of thermal energy deposited on wetted divertor surfaces, integrated over included targets and divertor components.
NAMES.long:
Thermal power of divertor is the total rate of thermal energy deposited on the wetted plasma-facing surfaces of the divertor assembly. It sums thermal deposition over all included divertor targets and other divertor plasma-facing components.

The defining surface integral is

$$
P_{\mathrm{div,th}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} q_{\mathrm{th}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of the included wetted divertor surfaces, $q_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal deposited-energy flux density, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is the surface-area element. The thermal contribution is a component of [power_of_divertor](name:power_of_divertor) and is distinct from neutral deposition represented by [neutral_power_of_divertor](name:neutral_power_of_divertor), as well as from electrical-current and other nonthermal contributions. Deposition on main-wall or other non-divertor plasma-facing components is excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Thermal power directed toward the divertor as a component of the plant-level power balance. Represents the heat load deposited on the divertor system, a critical parameter for divertor design and exhaust studies.

NAMES.name: area_of_optical_element
NAMES.short: Total geometric surface area of the optically active surface of a device component, equal to the actual material area capable of interacting with radiation rather than the projected aperture area.
NAMES.long:
Geometric surface area is the integral of the differential area element $dA$ over the full extent of the optically active material surface:

$$
A = \int_{\mathcal{S}} dA
$$

where $\mathcal{S}$ denotes the physical surface of the component. This quantity measures the actual curved or planar material area, not the projected cross-sectional aperture seen from a particular viewing direction.

The scope of integration is the optically active region — the surface or surfaces that participate in radiation interaction (reflection, transmission, absorption, or scattering). For a component with multiple optically active faces, all contributing faces are included in the total. The [surface area of an optical element](name:surface_area_of_optical_element) is a concrete instance of this quantity, where the surface is the optically active face of a diagnostic or beam-line optical component. This quantity is intrinsically non-negative and is independent of the orientation of any illuminating beam.

NAMES.name: charge_at_limiter
NAMES.short: Charge at a limiter is a charge-number-related scalar characterizing the ion charge-state composition of plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. This parent quantity covers specifically defined limiter charge measures without fixing a particular charge-state weighting or averaging convention.
NAMES.long:
Charge at a limiter is a charge-number-related scalar for the local ion charge-state composition of plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. It is the parent concept for specifically defined charge measures evaluated at that limiter-adjacent plasma locus.

This parent does not prescribe a charge-state weighting, species aggregation, or normalization; those are defined by its concrete children. For example, [effective charge at limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter) is the charge-squared-weighted mean charge number at the same locus, whereas this parent denotes only the shared charge-at-limiter abstraction.

It is not the electrical charge deposited on, stored by, or flowing into the limiter material, and it is not a particle, heat, or current flux to the surface.

NAMES.name: density_at_limiter
NAMES.short: Local number density of a selected charged plasma population evaluated immediately on the plasma-facing side of a limiter surface.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local number density of a selected charged plasma population at the plasma-facing side of a limiter. The selection may be electrons, an ion species summed over its ionization states, or a defined fuel pseudo-species formed by combining constituent ion populations.

$$
n_s(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_s}{dV}
$$

where $n_s$ is the selected population number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_s$ is the number of counted particles, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The position is immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing limiter, on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

Population aggregation is part of the specialization: ion species quantities may be summed over positive ionization states while excluding neutrals, electrons count the electron population, and the deuterium–tritium pseudo-species combines the corresponding ion densities. Concrete members include [electron density at a limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter), [ion density at a limiter](name:ion_density_at_limiter), and [deuterium-tritium density at a limiter](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter). The bare quantity does not imply a sum over all charged populations.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the selected charged population is present at the limiter-side evaluation location.

NAMES.name: argon_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Argon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral argon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Argon density at a limiter is the local number density of argon ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, and neutral argon atoms are excluded.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\sum_{q>0} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}(\mathbf{r}_L)
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, $q$ is the positive argon ionization state, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This is the argon-specific member of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It counts argon ions rather than the electrons represented by [electron density at a limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter), and is local rather than the flux-surface average represented by [flux-surface-averaged argon density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

NAMES.name: beryllium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Beryllium ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all beryllium ionization states from Be1+ through Be4+.
NAMES.long:
Beryllium density at a limiter is the local number density of beryllium ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on the material surface. Unless a specific ionization stage is resolved, this quantity is summed over all charged beryllium states; neutral beryllium atoms are excluded.

The charge-state-summed density is defined as:

$$
n_\mathrm{Be} = \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in ionization state $z$, spanning all four stages accessible under edge-plasma conditions.

Beryllium is used as a plasma-facing material in several tokamak devices; sputtering of beryllium limiter surfaces introduces impurity ions into the scrape-off layer, where they contribute to fuel dilution and raise the effective charge $Z_\mathrm{eff}$. This limiter-edge density sets the impurity source boundary condition in edge transport models and is inferred from spectroscopic line-emission measurements of beryllium charge states combined with sheath or presheath models, or computed self-consistently in coupled plasma-fluid and impurity-continuity solvers.

This quantity is the limiter-surface analog of [beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary) at the last-closed flux surface and of [beryllium_density_at_divertor_target](name:beryllium_density_at_divertor_target) at the divertor target. The parent [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) defines the evaluation locus shared by all species-resolved limiter density quantities, including the fuel-ion member [deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter). The volumetric profile away from the limiter is given by [beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density).

NAMES.name: boron_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Boron ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral boron atoms.
NAMES.long:
Boron density at a limiter is the local number density of boron ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}}}{dV}=\sum_{q=1}^{5}n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}(\mathbf{r}_L)
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the boron-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the number of counted boron ions, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, $n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the density of boron charge state $q$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The sum includes boron ions from B$^{+}$ through fully stripped B$^{5+}$ and excludes neutral boron atoms. This is the boron-specific specialization of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter); unlike [boron density at the plasma boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary), it is evaluated specifically at the limiter-side location.

NAMES.name: carbon_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Carbon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all carbon ionization states and excluding neutral carbon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Carbon density at a limiter is the local number density of carbon ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, consistent with the parent [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) framework. Carbon supports six ionization states ($\text{C}^{1+}$ through $\text{C}^{6+}$), and this quantity sums over all of them; neutral carbon atoms are excluded from this count.

The total charge-state-summed carbon density at the limiter is:

$$
n_\text{C} = \sum_{z=1}^{6} n_{\text{C}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\text{C}^{z+}}$ is the number density of carbon ions in charge state $z$ at the limiter evaluation point.

Carbon enters the edge plasma primarily through physical sputtering, chemical erosion, and recycling from carbon-based plasma-facing components. The density is inferred from spectroscopic line emission (C II through C VI) analyzed with collisional-radiative models that convert observed photon emissivities to charge-state-resolved densities.

In carbon-wall configurations, $n_\text{C}$ at the limiter spans approximately $10^{15}$–$10^{18}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on the carbon source rate, local electron temperature, and scrape-off-layer plasma density. Carbon impurities contribute to [effective_charge_at_limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter) and radiate strongly at edge electron temperatures of 10–100 eV. Analogous carbon densities at other boundary locations are tracked by [carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: deuterium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Deuterium ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium density at a limiter is the local number density of deuterium ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on the limiter material. Because deuterium carries only a single ionization state ($\mathrm{D}^+$, charge number $Z = 1$), no charge-state summation is required, in contrast to impurity-species counterparts such as [carbon_density_at_limiter](name:carbon_density_at_limiter) or [argon_density_at_limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter).

This density, together with [electron_temperature_at_limiter](name:electron_temperature_at_limiter), determines the ion saturation current flux to the limiter and governs local deuterium recycling and redeposition. In two-point model analyzes of the scrape-off layer, the limiter-side density is linked to the upstream separatrix density through parallel momentum and energy balance along magnetic field lines, with the Bohm sheath criterion $v_s = c_s = \sqrt{(T_e + T_i)/m_i}$ setting the flow speed at the sheath entrance, where $T_e$ and $T_i$ are the electron and ion temperatures and $m_i$ is the deuterium ion mass.

Measurement methods include flush-mounted Langmuir probes that yield the ion saturation current density from which the density is extracted, spectroscopic observation of deuterium Balmer emission combined with collisional-radiative modeling, and edge transport simulations constrained by upstream density profiles. Representative scrape-off-layer values at the limiter span $10^{17}$–$10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on global plasma density, fueling, and limiter geometry.

As a member of the [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) parent family, this quantity complements the tritium fuel-ion counterpart [tritium_density_at_limiter](name:tritium_density_at_limiter) and [hydrogen_density_at_limiter](name:hydrogen_density_at_limiter). The corresponding quantity at the magnetic separatrix is [deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, equal to the sum of the local deuterium and tritium ion densities.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-tritium density at the limiter is the local number density of the combined DT fuel ion pseudo-species in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. The DT pseudo-species represents deuterium and tritium ions as a single fictitious fuel constituent with an effective per-ion mass of $\bar{m} \approx 2.5\,m_u$ (where $m_u$ is the unified atomic mass unit) for an equimolar D-T mixture.

The quantity equals the sum of the separate deuterium and tritium ion densities at the limiter contact point:

$$
n_{DT} = n_D + n_T
$$

where $n_D$ is the local deuterium ion number density and $n_T$ is the local tritium ion number density at the same evaluation point.

This quantity is the limiter-contact analog of [deuterium_tritium_density](name:deuterium_tritium_density) and the DT-fuel counterpart of [deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter) at the same locus. It differs from [deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary) in evaluation geometry: the limiter contact lies in the scrape-off layer on open field lines, not at the last-closed flux surface. As a member of the [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) parent family, the presheath evaluation convention and locus definition follow those of [electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter) and other sibling fuel-species densities.

NAMES.name: effective_charge_at_limiter
NAMES.short: Effective charge number of the local ion mixture in boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
NAMES.long:
The effective charge at a limiter quantifies the charge-squared-weighted composition of the local positive-ion mixture immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing limiter surface. It is the limiter-local specialization of [charge_at_limiter](name:charge_at_limiter).

$$
Z_\mathrm{eff} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{\sum_i n_i Z_i}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective charge number, $n_i$ is the number density of ion population $i$ in m$^{-3}$, and $Z_i$ is its positive integer charge number. The sum includes positive ion species and charge states, while neutral atoms are excluded. A pure hydrogenic ion mixture gives $Z_\mathrm{eff}=1$; admixture of multiply charged impurity ions raises the value. The limiter location distinguishes this quantity from [effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary](name:effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary), which is evaluated at the plasma boundary.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Effective charge

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Electron density at a limiter is the local number density of electrons in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

$$
n_e(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_e}{dV}
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_e$ is the number of electrons, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Unlike [ion density at a limiter](name:ion_density_at_limiter), this quantity counts electrons only and includes neither ions nor neutral atoms. It is the electron-specific member of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and is distinct from [electron density at the plasma boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which uses a different evaluation locus.

sources.parent_definition: Electron density

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_wall
NAMES.short: Total power per unit area incident on a plasma-facing wall surface from the plasma side, serving as the parent concept for process-resolved wall energy fluxes covering kinetic, radiative, and electromagnetic contributions.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at the wall is the total power per unit area incident on a plasma-facing boundary surface from the plasma and surrounding radiation fields, encompassing kinetic energy transported by ions, electrons, and neutral particles, radiative power from photons, and electromagnetic contributions from induced currents. It is the most general wall energy-flux concept, with the net wall heat load defined as the difference between this incident quantity and the outgoing [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) returning toward the plasma.

For a kinetically described species $s$ with velocity distribution function $f_s(\mathbf{v})$, the incident kinetic energy flux contribution is

$$
Q_s = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n} < 0} \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2\, f_s(\mathbf{v})\,|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}|\,d^3v
$$

where $\hat{n}$ is the inward-pointing wall-normal unit vector and $m_s$ is the particle mass. The total incident energy flux sums $Q_s$ over all contributing particle species and adds radiative and electromagnetic terms.

Process-resolved decompositions include [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation) for the photon channel and [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current) for the electromagnetic Joule-heating contribution. Species-resolved kinetic counterparts are captured by [electron_energy_flux_at_wall](name:electron_energy_flux_at_wall) and [neutral_energy_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_energy_flux_at_wall), while the analogous particle-count flux is described by [particle_flux_at_wall](name:particle_flux_at_wall).

The total incident energy flux is evaluated from plasma simulation codes resolving parallel transport and plasma-material interactions, with experimental constraints from infrared thermography and surface calorimetry. Under steady-state scrape-off-layer conditions incident fluxes span roughly 0.1–10 MW m$^{-2}$; transient ELMs or disruptions can drive local fluxes to tens of MW m$^{-2}$, and the spatial peak across all surfaces is tracked by peak_power_density_at_wall.

NAMES.name: electron_energy_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Energy flux carried by emitted electrons leaving a plasma-facing wall surface, per unit area — the electron contribution to the outgoing surface-emission energy flux returned from the material toward the adjacent plasma or vacuum.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux carried by emitted electrons leaving a plasma-facing wall surface, per unit area — the electron contribution to the outgoing surface-emission energy flux returned from the material toward the adjacent plasma or vacuum. It is the kinetic energy transported by electrons emitted or reflected from the material surface, including secondary electron emission, backscattering, thermionic emission, and photoemission.

For an emitted electron velocity distribution at the surface, the energy flux density is the first kinetic-energy moment over electrons crossing outward through the surface:

$$
q_{e,\mathrm{emit}} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}_w>0} \tfrac{1}{2} m_e v^2 f_{e,\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{v})\,(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}_w)\,d^3v = \Gamma_{e,\mathrm{emit}}\,\langle E_k \rangle_\Gamma
$$

where $m_e$ is the electron mass, $v$ is the electron speed, $\hat{n}_w$ is the unit surface normal pointing from the material into the plasma-facing region, and $f_{e,\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted-electron velocity distribution function. $\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{emit}}$ is the corresponding [electron_particle_flux_at_wall](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall), and $\langle E_k \rangle_\Gamma$ is the flux-weighted mean kinetic energy per emitted electron.

This quantity includes only outgoing emitted or reflected electrons and excludes incident plasma electrons, ion and neutral kinetic energy fluxes, photon power, and electromagnetic wall-heating terms. It is the electron component of [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), which offsets the incident [energy_flux_at_wall](name:energy_flux_at_wall) in the net wall heat load.
NAMES.sign: Positive when emitted electron kinetic energy flows across the wall surface along $\hat{n}_w$, from the material into the plasma-facing region.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short: Outgoing energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident plasma ions recombine at the surface, summed over incident-ion species, incident-ion charge states, recombination channels, and emitted product species and states.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which recombination-associated energy is emitted from a plasma-facing surface per unit area as a result of incident plasma ions recombining or neutralizing at the material boundary. It is the total outgoing energy flux carried by emitted recombination products or quanta, not the incident plasma energy flux or heat deposited in the wall material.

The total recombination energy flux at wall location $\mathbf{x}_w$ is defined as the product-energy moment of the outgoing recombination source:

$$
Q_\mathrm{rec}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{i,\,\zeta,\,c,\,a,\,k}\int E_\mathrm{out}\,\frac{d\Gamma_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}}{dE_\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{x}_w,E_\mathrm{out})\,dE_\mathrm{out}
$$

where $i$ identifies the incident-ion species, $\zeta$ the incident-ion charge state, $c$ the surface recombination or neutralization channel, $a$ the emitted product species, $k$ the product internal state or emission class, $E_\mathrm{out}$ the energy carried into the plasma-facing half-space by an emitted product or quantum, and $d\Gamma_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}/dE_\mathrm{out}$ the corresponding outgoing recombination-product flux distribution with respect to product energy. For discrete product energies, the integral is replaced by the corresponding sum.

This quantity is the energy-weighted counterpart of [particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), which counts the same surface recombination source without energy weighting, and is the energy-flux realization of [flux at the wall due to recombination](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). The incident-ion decomposition is charge-state-summed in this total: [ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) resolves a specified incident-ion species and charge state, while [ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) is the corresponding ion contribution after summing over charge states. Neutral-product particle specializations such as [neutral particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) partition emitted-product counts and do not by themselves include energy weighting.
NAMES.sign: Positive when recombination-associated energy is emitted away from the plasma-facing wall surface into the plasma-facing half-space.

NAMES.name: flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current
NAMES.short: Flux at wall due to eddy current is the plasma-facing wall surface density of power whose causal origin is eddy-current induction in conducting material. It identifies the eddy-current-attributed wall boundary flux without fixing the internal conversion, transport, or surface-emission pathway.
NAMES.long:
Flux at wall due to eddy current is the plasma-facing wall surface density of power whose causal origin is eddy-current induction in conducting material. It denotes the boundary flux associated with eddy-current effects as a class, independent of the particular internal conversion, transport, or surface-emission pathway by which that power appears at the wall.

The local value is defined as the surface density of eddy-current-attributed power associated with a wall surface element:

$$
q_{\mathrm{ec,w}} = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{ec,w}}}{dA}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{ec,w}}$ is the local wall flux due to eddy current, $P_{\mathrm{ec,w}}$ is the eddy-current-attributed power associated with the wall surface, and $A$ is wall surface area.

The common semantics are the wall locus and the eddy-current causal attribution. More specific members such as [energy flux at wall due to eddy current](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current) may constrain the transported quantity or realization pathway; fluxes caused by plasma particles, radiation, neutrals, externally applied heating, or other non-eddy-current sources are excluded.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current
NAMES.short: Energy flux at the wall due to eddy current is the thermal energy flux density emitted from a plasma-facing wall surface toward the plasma by heat generated from eddy-current Joule dissipation in conducting structures.
NAMES.long:
Energy flux at the wall due to eddy current is the thermal energy flux density emitted from a plasma-facing wall surface toward the plasma by heat generated from eddy-current Joule dissipation in conducting structures. It is the wall-normal component of the heat-flux field attributable to eddy-current heating, evaluated at the plasma-facing boundary.

The signed surface flux is the projection of the eddy-current heat-flux vector onto the local surface normal from wall material toward plasma:

$$
q_\mathrm{wall}^{\mathrm{eddy}} = \mathbf{q}_\mathrm{th}^{\mathrm{eddy}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{wall}\to\mathrm{plasma}}
$$

where $q_\mathrm{wall}^{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is the signed surface energy flux density in W m$^{-2}$, $\mathbf{q}_\mathrm{th}^{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is the heat-flux vector due only to eddy-current Joule heating with components in W m$^{-2}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{wall}\to\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the unit normal directed from the wall material toward the plasma.

The underlying volumetric Joule source is $p_\mathrm{eddy} = \mathbf{J}_\mathrm{eddy}\cdot\mathbf{E}_\mathrm{eddy}$, equal to $|\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{eddy}|^2/\sigma_w$ for scalar Ohmic conductivity $\sigma_w$. This surface quantity includes only the portion of that internally generated thermal power crossing the plasma-facing surface; it excludes eddy-current power retained elsewhere in the structure, heat leaving other surfaces, and energy fluxes at the wall due to radiation, particle impact, or plasma-side electromagnetic fields. Its area integral over a specified wall surface gives the corresponding emitted power, distinct from total [power at the wall due to Ohmic dissipation](name:power_at_wall_due_to_ohmic_dissipation).
NAMES.sign: Positive when thermal energy crosses the plasma-facing wall surface from the wall material toward the plasma.

NAMES.name: flux_due_to_radiation
NAMES.short: Radiative energy-transfer rate delivered per unit surface area to a receiving surface by photon transport.
NAMES.long:
Radiative energy flux density is the rate at which photon-carried energy arrives at a receiving surface, normalized by the surface area. It represents the radiation-specific contribution to energy transfer and is independent of conductive, particle, or mechanical transport.

The quantity is defined by

$$
q_{\mathrm{rad}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}E_{\mathrm{rad}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the radiative energy flux density, $E_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the arriving radiative energy, $A$ is the receiving surface area, and $t$ is time. The wall-localized instance [flux at wall due to radiation](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation) applies this general quantity to a plasma-facing wall. It is the radiation-specific component of [energy flux](name:energy_flux).

NAMES.name: flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation
NAMES.short: Flux at wall due to radiation is the radiation-caused areal flux incident on a material wall or plasma-facing surface. It is the wall-scoped member of radiation-flux quantities; concrete descendants specify the transported quantity, such as photon-carried energy.
NAMES.long:
Flux at wall due to radiation is the radiation-caused areal flux incident on a material wall or plasma-facing surface. It is the wall-scoped radiation-flux abstraction; concrete descendants specify the transported quantity carried by photons.

For a radiation-carried quantity $Q$, the incident wall flux is defined as the areal rate at which that quantity crosses onto a wall surface element:

$$
F_{Q,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{rad}} = \frac{dQ_{\mathrm{rad}\to\mathrm{wall}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{rad}\to\mathrm{wall}}$ is the amount of $Q$ transported by photons onto the wall surface element, $dA$ is that wall surface element, and $dt$ is the time interval.

This parent standard name does not by itself choose the transported quantity; concrete descendants specify it, such as the [energy flux at wall due to radiation](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation). It describes incident radiative transfer to the wall and excludes non-radiative particle, conductive, convective, and electromagnetic-work contributions, as well as changes after incidence such as absorption, reflection, or re-emission.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation
NAMES.short: Incident photon energy crossing onto a plasma-facing material surface per unit area, before absorption, reflection, or re-emission modifies the radiation.
NAMES.long:
Incident radiative energy flux density is the incoming photon power crossing a plasma-facing material surface, resolved per unit surface area. It is the incident component of [flux at wall due to radiation](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation), not the net energy deposited in the material.

For an incident radiation field, the flux is defined by

$$
q_{\mathrm{rad}}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{in}}} I_{\mathrm{rad}}(\hat{\mathbf{s}})\,[-\hat{\mathbf{s}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}] \, d\Omega
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the frequency-integrated radiance, $\hat{\mathbf{s}}$ is the photon propagation direction, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the outward surface normal, $\Omega_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the set of directions propagating toward the surface, and $d\Omega$ is solid angle. The quantity excludes energy removed by absorption, redirected by reflection, or returned by surface re-emission; those effects are not part of the incident flux itself.

NAMES.name: flux_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short: Particle flux due to recombination is the surface-normal particle-number flux density across an oriented surface attributable to recombination processes. It covers recombined products such as neutral atoms or molecules without fixing the wall locus, species, incidence class, or internal state.
NAMES.long:
Particle flux due to recombination is the surface-normal particle-number flux density across an oriented surface attributable to recombination processes. Recombination denotes the conversion of charged plasma particles into a lower-charge or neutral product, including electron-ion recombination in a volume and surface-assisted formation of neutral atoms or molecules when the counted population crosses the chosen surface.

The local flux density is defined by the net signed recombination-attributable particle count crossing a differential surface element:

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{rec}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}$ is the recombination particle flux density, $dN_{\mathrm{rec}}$ is the signed number of particles in the stated population whose crossing is attributed to recombination, $dA$ is the surface area in square meters, and $dt$ is the elapsed time in seconds.

This quantity is process-resolved: it excludes particle transport not attributable to recombination, such as direct plasma impact, sputtering, evaporation, externally injected neutrals, and charge-exchange transport unless the counted particles are recombination products. The wall-specific realization is [particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination); internal-state-resolved and incident-neutral wall realizations are [internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), [incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), and [incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). The corresponding transported energy is [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).
NAMES.sign: Positive when recombination-attributable particles cross the oriented surface in the direction of the chosen unit normal.

NAMES.name: flux_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short: Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a material surface through emission processes such as particle recycling, sputtering, or secondary electron and photon emission.
NAMES.long:
Surface emission encompasses the range of physical processes by which plasma-facing material surfaces re-emit particles, energy, or radiation into the plasma or surrounding environment. These include neutral recycling (incident ions reflected or thermally desorbed as neutrals), physical and chemical sputtering (wall atoms ejected by energetic ion bombardment), secondary electron emission (electrons liberated by ion or electron impact), and thermal or fluorescence photon emission from heated or excited surface atoms.

The emitted flux $\Gamma_\mathrm{emit}$ at a surface element is related to the incident driving flux $\Gamma_\mathrm{incident}$ through a process-specific emission yield $Y$:

$$
\Gamma_\mathrm{emit} = Y \cdot \Gamma_\mathrm{incident}
$$

where $Y$ is the emission yield (dimensionless for particle emission, or carrying the appropriate units ratio for energy or photon emission), and $\Gamma_\mathrm{incident}$ is the incident flux of the driving species.

The specific instantiation of this flux at the first wall is described by [flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). For the total radiated thermal power emitted by wall material, see [thermal_power_of_wall_material_due_to_radiation_emission](name:thermal_power_of_wall_material_due_to_radiation_emission). General energy transport through a surface is captured by [energy_flux](name:energy_flux).

NAMES.name: flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short: Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface through emission processes such as sputtering, desorption, photon emission, and secondary-electron emission. The transported quantity may be particle number, energy, momentum, or radiative power in a more specific member.
NAMES.long:
Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface through emission processes such as sputtering, desorption, thermal evaporation, photon emission, secondary-electron emission, or surface de-excitation. It is the surface-normal flux density generated by the material response at the wall and carried from the material side toward the plasma side.

The emission flux is related to incident driving fluxes through surface-emission yield or response coefficients:

$$
F_Q^{\mathrm{emit}} = \sum_k Y_{Qk}^{\mathrm{emit}} F_k^{\mathrm{inc}}
$$

where $F_Q^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted flux density of physical quantity $Q$, $F_k^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is incident channel $k$ that drives surface emission, and $Y_{Qk}^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the surface-emission coefficient for producing the emitted $Q$ flux.

This quantity is the wall-specific member of [flux_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_due_to_surface_emission) and is an abstraction over component channels. The energy channel is [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), while [energy_flux_at_wall](name:energy_flux_at_wall) denotes energy flux at the wall without specifying surface emission as the cause. It excludes flux incident on the wall from the plasma or radiation field except as a driver of emission; [flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_radiation) denotes radiative flux at the wall rather than material emission generated by the wall.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net emitted flux is directed from the wall material into the plasma.

NAMES.name: energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short: Total energy flux density at a plasma-facing wall surface due to surface emission processes, encompassing kinetic and potential energy carried by emitted particles and photons.
NAMES.long:
Surface emission at the plasma-facing wall encompasses secondary electron emission, neutral and ion sputtering, particle reflection, and photon emission stimulated by plasma–wall interactions. Each emission channel carries energy away from the wall surface, and this quantity represents their aggregate energy flux per unit area. It is the energy-channel specialization of [flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), which spans multiple transported quantities at the wall interface.

The total emitted energy flux $Q_\mathrm{em}$ is expressed by summing over all surface-emitted species $s$ the energy-weighted flux of particles leaving the surface:

$$
Q_\mathrm{em} = \sum_s \int E_s \, f_s(E_s) \, v_{\perp,s} \, dE_s
$$

where $E_s$ is the energy of emitted species $s$, $f_s$ is its energy distribution function, and $v_{\perp,s}$ is the wall-normal velocity component. The kinetic contribution alone is resolved separately as [kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).

Contextualizing this emission flux against the incident plasma heat flux quantifies the effective energy reflection coefficient of the plasma-facing surface, a key parameter for thermal design of wall components. The net deposited power density derives from the difference between the incident and emitted energy fluxes and connects to aggregate quantities such as [energy_flux_at_wall](name:energy_flux_at_wall) and plasma_deposited_power_at_wall.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Helium-3 ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.
NAMES.long:
Helium-3 density at a limiter is the local number density of helium-3 ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

$$
n_{^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{^3\mathrm{He}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density, $N_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the counted number of helium-3 ions, $V$ is volume, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The density is summed over all positive helium-3 ionization states and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms. It is the helium-3-specific member of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and differs from [ion density at a limiter](name:ion_density_at_limiter), which is not restricted to helium-3; [helium-4 density at a limiter](name:helium_4_density_at_limiter) describes the corresponding isotope.

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Local particle number density of helium-4 ions evaluated in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing limiter surface, on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. The value is summed over He+ and He2+ ionization states and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 density at a limiter is the local number density of helium-4 ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, not inside the limiter material or in neutral gas retained at the surface. It is summed over the helium-4 ion charge states He$^+$ and He$^{2+}$, and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms.

The charge-state-summed helium-4 ion density is related to the charge-state-resolved velocity distribution functions by:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} \int f_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $q$ is the positive ion charge state, $f_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}$ is the velocity distribution function of helium-4 ions with charge state $q+$, and the integral is taken over all particle velocities at the limiter-side evaluation point.

This quantity is the helium-4 isotope contribution to [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and to the unweighted ion population represented by [total_ion_density_at_limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter). In a quasineutral boundary plasma, [electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter) is coupled to the charge-weighted ion sum, so helium-4 contributes $\sum_{q=1}^{2} q\,n_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}$ to that balance. The corresponding helium-3 isotope quantity is [helium_3_density_at_limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter).

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Local particle number density of hydrogen ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Hydrogen density at a limiter is the local number density of hydrogen ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance; neutral hydrogen is excluded. For hydrogen, the charge-state sum reduces to the density of positively charged hydrogen ions, H+.

The local hydrogen-ion density is defined from the velocity distribution function:

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}^+} = \int f_{\mathrm{H}^+}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}^+}$ is the hydrogen-ion number density, $f_{\mathrm{H}^+}$ is the hydrogen-ion velocity distribution function, and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity at the evaluation point.

This quantity is the hydrogen-specific component of [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It counts hydrogen ions separately from [deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter), and does not include neutral hydrogen or other ion species.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Outgoing energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident plasma ions of a specified species and charge state recombine at the surface, restricted to the ion-associated channel and summed over surface recombination channels and emitted product species and states.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which recombination-associated energy from incident plasma ions of a specified species and charge state leaves a plasma-facing surface per unit area. It is the ion-associated component for that incident-ion population, not the incident plasma energy flux or heat deposited in the wall material.

The ion charge-state recombination energy flux at wall location $\mathbf{x}_w$ for incident species $i$ and charge state $\zeta$ is defined as the product-energy moment of the outgoing ion-associated recombination source:

$$
Q^{\mathrm{ion}}_{\mathrm{rec},i,\zeta}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{c,\,a,\,k}\int E_\mathrm{out}\,\frac{d\Gamma^{\mathrm{ion}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}}{dE_\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{x}_w,E_\mathrm{out})\,dE_\mathrm{out}
$$

where $i$ identifies the incident-ion species, $\zeta$ the incident-ion charge state, $c$ an ion-associated surface recombination or neutralization channel, $a$ the emitted product species, $k$ the product internal state or emission class, $E_\mathrm{out}$ the energy carried into the plasma-facing half-space by an emitted product or quantum, and $d\Gamma^{\mathrm{ion}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}/dE_\mathrm{out}$ the corresponding outgoing recombination-product flux distribution with respect to product energy. For discrete product energies, the integral is replaced by the corresponding sum.

This quantity resolves the incident-ion species and charge state within the ion-associated recombination energy channel. Summing over incident-ion charge states and incident-ion species gives [ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination); the broader [energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) also includes recombination energy channels outside this ion-associated component. It is the energy-weighted counterpart of [particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) for the same surface recombination source.

NAMES.name: ion_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local particle number density of an ion population evaluated in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Ion density at a limiter is the local number density of an ion population in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on the limiter material. The ion population may be a specified set of ionic species or an aggregate over species and charge states; electrons and neutral atoms are excluded.

For an aggregated ion population, the extensive number density is summed over the included ion species and over all their ionized charge states:

$$
n_i = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{q \in \mathcal{Q}_s} n_{s,q}
$$

where $\mathcal{I}$ is the included set of ion species, $\mathcal{Q}_s$ is the set of positive charge states of species $s$, and $n_{s,q}$ is the local number density of ions of species $s$ in charge state $q$ at the limiter evaluation point.

This quantity is an ion-only specialization of [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). The species-and-charge-state-summed realization is [total_ion_density_at_limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter). It remains distinct from [electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter): quasineutrality at the sheath entrance relates $n_e$ to the charge-weighted ion sum, $n_e \approx \sum_{s,q} q\,n_{s,q}$, whereas $n_i$ is the unweighted ion particle count density.

NAMES.name: ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Outgoing energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident plasma ions recombine at the surface, restricted to the ion-associated channel and summed over incident-ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which recombination-associated energy from incident plasma ions leaves a plasma-facing surface per unit area. It is the ion-associated component summed over incident-ion species and charge states, not the incident plasma energy flux or energy deposited in the wall material.

The aggregate is defined from charge-state-resolved components by:

$$
Q_{\mathrm{rec,ion}}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{s,q} Q_{\mathrm{rec},s,q}(\mathbf{x}_w)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_w$ is the wall location, $s$ identifies an incident-ion species, $q$ identifies its charge state, and $Q_{\mathrm{rec},s,q}$ is the corresponding [ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). The sum includes all represented incident-ion species and charge states.

As a component of [energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), this quantity retains only the ion-associated energy channel. Unlike [particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), it weights the outgoing recombination contribution by carried energy; it is distinct from incident [ion kinetic energy flux at the wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall).

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Iron ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all ionization stages and excluding neutral iron atoms.
NAMES.long:
Iron density at a limiter is the local number density of iron ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, consistent with the parent [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). Unless a single ionization stage is specified in context, this quantity is summed over all iron charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ to Fe$^{26+}$, excluding neutral iron atoms.

The total iron ion number density at the limiter is defined as:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}$ is the local number density of iron in charge state $z$.

Iron enters the edge plasma primarily through physical sputtering of metallic plasma-facing components by energetic ions and charge-exchange neutrals impacting the limiter surface. At the limiter, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on the material boundary, sputtered iron atoms are ionized within a thin ionization front and become subject to parallel and cross-field impurity transport. The local iron ion density at the limiter characterizes the impurity source strength at this plasma-wall interface and serves as a boundary condition for edge impurity transport modeling. It connects to [iron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:iron_density_at_plasma_boundary) and [iron_density_at_divertor_target](name:iron_density_at_divertor_target), which describe the same impurity density evaluated at different plasma-facing surfaces.

NAMES.name: kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall
NAMES.short: Total kinetic power per unit area incident on a plasma-facing wall surface from plasma particles, excluding radiative and electromagnetic contributions.
NAMES.long:
Kinetic energy flux at the wall is the power per unit area incident on a plasma-facing boundary surface from plasma particles, carried by their translational kinetic energy. It is the particle-kinetic contribution to [energy_flux_at_wall](name:energy_flux_at_wall), independent of whether the particles are ions, electrons, or neutrals.

For contributing particle populations $s$, the incident kinetic-energy flux is

$$
Q_{\mathrm{kin}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}<0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}|\,d^3v
$$

where $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of population $s$, $m_s$ is its particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity relative to the wall, and $\hat{n}$ is the inward-pointing wall-normal unit vector. The sum and any internal-state aggregation follow the defined particle population; [ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall) is one species-aggregated instance, while [neutral_energy_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_energy_flux_at_wall) represents a neutral-particle instance. Radiative, electromagnetic, and outgoing surface-emission contributions are excluded.

NAMES.name: ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Incident kinetic-energy power flux delivered by all plasma ions striking a plasma-facing wall, summed over ion species and charge states and excluding electrons and neutrals.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the ion-resolved component of the incident kinetic-energy flux at a plasma-facing wall. It contributes to the parent [kinetic energy flux at wall](name:kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall) and includes all incident ion species and charge states, but excludes electron, neutral-particle, radiative, and electromagnetic contributions.

For an outward wall normal $\hat{n}$ directed from the material into the plasma, the flux is defined by

$$
q_{i}^{\mathrm{kin}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}<0} \frac{1}{2}m_s |\mathbf{v}|^2 (-\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species and charge states, $m_s$ is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_s$ is the incident velocity distribution. The minus sign converts the inward particle velocity into a positive arrival flux; the resulting quantity is non-negative.

NAMES.name: kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short: Kinetic-energy power flux density carried away from a plasma-facing surface by emitted particles, including ions and electrons and aggregated over species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by particles emitted from a plasma-facing surface through sputtering, reflection, secondary emission, or related surface-emission processes. It includes all emitted particle species and charge states, rather than selecting a particular ion or charge state.

The kinetic-energy flux density is defined by

$$
q_{\mathrm{kin}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\,(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ indexes emitted particle species and charge states, $m_s$ is particle mass in kg, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity in m/s, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$, $\mathbf{n}$ is the outward surface-normal unit vector, and $f_s$ is the emitted-particle velocity distribution. The outward condition excludes particles incident on the surface. This is the kinetic component of [energy flux at wall due to surface emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), excluding particle potential-energy contributions and photon or other radiative energy; [ion charge-state kinetic energy flux at wall due to surface emission](name:ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) is a charge-state-resolved instance.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Kinetic-energy power flux density carried by ions in a specified charge state leaving a plasma-facing surface through sputtering, reflection, or related surface-emission processes.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by ions in a specified species and charge state emitted from a plasma-facing surface through sputtering, reflection, or related surface-emission processes.

The charge-state-resolved kinetic-energy flux density is defined by

$$
q_{\mathrm{kin},s} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\,(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the selected ion species and charge state, $m_s$ is its particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$, $\mathbf{n}$ is the outward surface-normal unit vector, and $f_s$ is its emitted-particle velocity distribution. The outward condition excludes particles incident on the surface.

This is one charge-state contribution to [kinetic-energy flux at wall due to surface emission](name:kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), excluding other ion charge states, electrons, particle potential energy, photons, and other radiative energy. The ion-aggregated quantity [ion kinetic-energy flux at wall due to surface emission](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) sums this contribution over ion species and charge states.

NAMES.name: ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Kinetic energy flux density carried by ions leaving the plasma-facing wall through surface emission processes such as physical sputtering and ion backscattering.
NAMES.long:
The kinetic energy flux density at the plasma-facing wall surface carried by ions emitted outward via surface emission — the family of plasma–wall interaction processes, including physical sputtering, chemical sputtering, and ion backscattering, that return ionic species from the wall to the plasma. The `kinetic` qualifier restricts this to translational kinetic energy of the emitted ion velocity distribution, excluding potential energy stored in electronic excitation or residual ionization charge, which is captured separately by [energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

The emitted kinetic energy flux $\Phi_{\mathrm{kin,emit}}$ sums over all emitted ion species $s$:

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{kin,emit}} = \sum_s \int_{v_n > 0} \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2 \, v_n \, f_{s,\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion mass of species $s$, $v = |\mathbf{v}|$ is the ion speed, $v_n > 0$ is the outward surface-normal velocity component at the wall, and $f_{s,\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution function of emitted ions.

In plasma–surface interaction modeling, this flux is evaluated by convolving incident plasma conditions with energy-resolved surface emission yields and backscattering coefficients from binary-collision approximation databases. It is the mechanism-attributed form of [ion_energy_flux_at_wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) and the emitted counterpart to [ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall), which captures the incident kinetic flux. Charge-state-resolved contributions are tracked by ion_state_energy_flux_at_wall, and the electron analog is [electron_energy_flux_at_wall](name:electron_energy_flux_at_wall).

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Krypton ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all krypton ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Krypton density at a limiter is the local number density of krypton ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance at the plasma–limiter contact, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on the material boundary.

Unless a single charge state is explicitly specified, the quantity represents the charge-state-summed total:

$$
n_\mathrm{Kr} = \sum_{q=1}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the number density of krypton ions in ionization state $q$, ranging from $q = 1$ (singly ionized) to $q = 36$ (fully stripped). Neutral krypton atoms are excluded from this quantity.

Krypton is a high-$Z$ noble gas ($Z = 36$) injected as a seeding impurity to enhance radiative dissipation in the scrape-off layer, redistributing heat load away from plasma-facing components. Its local density at the limiter characterizes krypton availability for charge exchange, ionization, and plasma–material interactions at the wall. Even modest krypton concentrations significantly elevate [effective_charge_at_limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter) due to its high nuclear charge.

Within the [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) family, krypton density serves as a heavier-impurity counterpart to lighter noble-gas seeds such as [argon_density_at_limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter), and contrasts with fuel-ion species such as [deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter). Under quasi-neutrality, the charge-weighted sum of all ion densities at the limiter equals [electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter).

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Local number density of lithium ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states and excluding neutral lithium atoms.
NAMES.long:
Lithium density at a limiter is the local number density of lithium ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the counted number of lithium ions, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius in m, $\phi$ is toroidal angle in radians, and $Z$ is vertical height in m.

The quantity is summed over all positive lithium ionization states and excludes neutral lithium atoms. It is the lithium-specific specialization of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and differs from the broader [ion density at a limiter](name:ion_density_at_limiter), which does not select lithium.
