NAMES.name: mass_of_wall_material
NAMES.short: Mass of a single atom, specified isotope, or isotopic composition that constitutes a plasma-facing wall material, referenced to the carbon-12 atomic-mass scale.
NAMES.long:
Mass of wall material is the rest mass of a single constituent atom, specified isotope, or isotopic composition of a plasma-facing material. It is a constituent property of the wall material and is independent of the amount of material present or the plasma state.

The carbon-12 atomic-mass scale relates the physical mass to the value of this quantity by:

$$
m_\mathrm{wall} = M_\mathrm{wall} m_\mathrm{u}, \qquad m_\mathrm{u} = \frac{1}{12} m({}^{12}\mathrm{C})
$$

where $m_\mathrm{wall}$ is the physical rest mass of the wall-material constituent, $M_\mathrm{wall}$ is its numerical value on the carbon-12 scale, $m_\mathrm{u}$ is the atomic mass constant, and $m({}^{12}\mathrm{C})$ is the mass of a neutral carbon-12 atom in its ground state.

For an element with unspecified isotope composition, the quantity denotes the composition-weighted atomic mass for that wall-material constituent; for a specified isotope, it denotes that isotope's atomic mass. It excludes macroscopic wall-component mass, molar mass, bulk mass density, areal mass loading, and mass of incident plasma species.

NAMES.name: atomic_mass_of_wall_material
NAMES.short: Atomic mass of a selected element, isotope, or isotopic composition constituting a plasma-facing wall material, referenced to the carbon-12 mass scale.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the atomic mass of the selected element, isotope, or isotopic composition that constitutes a plasma-facing wall material. It describes a constituent or specified composition, not the total mass of a wall or macroscopic wall component.

The atomic-mass scale is defined by

$$
m_{\rm atom} = A u, \qquad u = \frac{1}{12}m(^{12}\mathrm{C})
$$

where $m_{\rm atom}$ is the atomic mass, $A$ is its numerical value on the scale, $u$ is the unified atomic mass unit, and $m(^{12}\mathrm{C})$ is the mass of a carbon-12 atom. For an isotopic composition, the value is the abundance-weighted mean of the constituent isotope masses.

This is the atomic-mass specialization of [mass_of_wall_material](name:mass_of_wall_material). It is distinct from [ion_mass_number](name:ion_mass_number), which is the integer nucleon count and does not include the isotope-specific mass defect.

NAMES.name: maximum_of_energy_flux_at_first_wall
NAMES.short: Spatial maximum of the total energy flux density over the entire first-wall plasma-facing surface, identifying the peak thermal load point at a given instant.
NAMES.long:
The maximum of energy flux at the first wall is the highest value of [energy_flux_at_wall](name:energy_flux_at_wall) sampled over the entire first-wall plasma-facing surface at a given instant.

$$
q_\mathrm{max} = \max_{\mathbf{x}\,\in\,\mathcal{S}_\mathrm{FW}} q(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $q(\mathbf{x})$ is the local total energy flux and $\mathcal{S}_\mathrm{FW}$ denotes the first-wall surface.

The base quantity $q(\mathbf{x})$ encompasses all energy-transport channels — kinetic energy carried by ions, electrons, and neutrals together with radiative and electromagnetic contributions — consistent with [energy_flux_at_wall](name:energy_flux_at_wall). The maximum is taken across the full first-wall geometry at each time point, not area-averaged. It is distinct from [maximum_of_energy_flux_at_divertor_target](name:maximum_of_energy_flux_at_divertor_target), which applies the same spatial-maximum operator to the divertor target surface rather than the first wall.

sources.enhanced_context: Peak power flux density incident on the first wall of the fusion device. Provides a device-level metric for assessing peak thermal loading of plasma-facing components during plasma operation.

sources.enhanced_context: Peak power flux on the first wall excluding divertor surfaces, a device-level metric for plasma-wall interaction and thermal loading. Groups time-resolved data and associated uncertainties for the maximum heat load per unit area on the main chamber wall.

NAMES.name: maximum_of_energy_flux_at_limiter
NAMES.short: Peak plasma energy deposition per unit area on the plasma-facing surface of a limiter.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the largest local plasma energy flux deposited on the plasma-facing material surface of a limiter. It represents the peak heat load over the limiter surface rather than an area-integrated power.

$$
q_{E,\mathrm{max}}^{L} = \max_{\mathbf{x} \in S_L} q_E(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $q_E$ is the local plasma energy flux deposited on the surface and $S_L$ is the set of points comprising the limiter surface.

This is the limiter-surface counterpart of [energy flux at wall](name:energy_flux_at_wall). It denotes the total surface energy deposition and is not restricted to the field-aligned component represented by [parallel heat flux](name:parallel_heat_flux).

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Neon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all neon ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
Neon density at a limiter is the local number density of neon ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance at the limiter contact, not the magnetic separatrix, consistent with the parent [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter).

Unless a charge-state-resolved quantity specifies a particular ionization stage, this density is summed over all positive neon charge states ($\mathrm{Ne}^{1+}$ through $\mathrm{Ne}^{10+}$):

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{z=1}^{10} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of neon ions in charge state $z$.

Neon is introduced as a controlled radiative impurity for power exhaust and divertor detachment. At the limiter, the local neon density governs recycling fluxes, charge-exchange with neutral neon, and impurity-driven edge plasma cooling near the wall. Edge Langmuir probes and vacuum ultraviolet or extreme ultraviolet spectroscopy provide experimental access to this quantity.

The neon density in the scrape-off layer at neon-seeded discharges spans roughly $10^{16}$–$10^{18}$ m$^{-3}$, falling toward the lower end at low seeding rates and rising with neon puff level. The corresponding quantity evaluated at the separatrix is [neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary); [xenon_density_at_limiter](name:xenon_density_at_limiter) is the analogous quantity for xenon impurity injection.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Incident neutral-particle flux at a plasma-facing wall, resolved to a specified internal quantum state and kinetic-energy channel. It counts neutral atoms or molecules occupying that state, with kinetic energy within the channel, crossing from the plasma side into the material surface. It is an arrival-particle flux, not a kinetic-energy-weighted power flux.
NAMES.long:
Incident neutral-particle flux at a plasma-facing wall, resolved to a specified internal quantum state and kinetic-energy channel, counts the neutral atoms or molecules occupying that state whose kinetic energy lies within the channel as they cross from the plasma-facing region into the material surface, per unit wall area per unit time. Because a bound internal quantum state belongs to a specific neutral species, the state identifier fixes the species; no species sum is implied at the state-resolved level.

Let $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w$ be the local unit normal directed from the wall into the plasma-facing domain, so incident velocities satisfy $\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w < 0$. For internal state $s$ and kinetic-energy channel $k$ with energy interval $\Delta_k$, the flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{s,k}^{w} = \int_{\substack{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w < 0 \\ \tfrac{1}{2} m_s |\mathbf{v}|^2 \in \Delta_k}} \left(-\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w\right) f_{s}(\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $f_{s}$ is the velocity distribution of neutral particles in internal state $s$ at the plasma side of the wall and $m_s$ is the mass of the neutral species carrying state $s$.

The kinetic-energy channel resolves the arrival flux by energy without weighting the integrand by kinetic energy, so the quantity remains a particle flux and is distinct from a power flux onto the wall. Summing over all kinetic-energy channels yields the [neutral internal-state particle flux at the wall](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall). Summing over all internal quantum states, and thereby over neutral species since each state belongs to one species, yields the species-summed [neutral energy flux at the wall](name:neutral_energy_flux_at_wall) in the corresponding kinetic-energy channel. The counterpart not restricted to neutrals is the [internal-state energy flux at the wall](name:internal_state_energy_flux_at_wall). Only the incident half-space contributes: neutrals leaving the surface, such as reflected, recycled, or desorbed particles, are excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral particles move from the plasma-facing region toward the wall surface, that is, when their velocity satisfies $\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w < 0$ with $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w$ directed from the wall into the plasma-facing domain.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Incident number flux density of neutral particles arriving at a plasma-facing wall, resolved by a specified electronic, vibrational, or rotational internal state.
NAMES.long:
Incident number flux density of neutral particles arriving at a plasma-facing wall is the rate at which neutral particles in a specified electronic, vibrational, or rotational internal state cross a local wall surface from the plasma-facing side, per surface area. It is an incident scalar at the wall and is not a signed transport-flux component.

The incident flux density is the normal velocity moment of the neutral velocity distribution over the wall-incident half-space:

$$
\Gamma_{\alpha,w}^{\mathrm{inc}} = -\int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w < 0} \left(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w\right) f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{x}_w,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\alpha,w}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is this incident number flux density for internal state $\alpha$ at wall point $\mathbf{x}_w$, $f_{\alpha}$ is the neutral-particle velocity distribution function for that internal state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w$ is the local inward unit normal of the plasma-facing region, directed from the wall into that region. The condition $\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w < 0$ selects particles moving toward the wall, so the leading minus sign makes the incident scalar nonnegative.

This quantity includes wall-incident neutral particles in the specified internal state without separating the physical process that produced them before impact. Process-resolved contributions, such as [incident neutral internal-state particle flux at wall due to recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), are distinct components; [neutral internal-state particle flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) is the corresponding flux quantity not restricted to wall incidence.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral internal-state particle flux at a wall due to recombination is the outgoing particle flux density of neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state produced by ion recombination at a plasma-facing wall surface.
NAMES.long:
Neutral internal-state particle flux at a wall due to recombination is the particle flux density of neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state that are produced by ion recombination at a plasma-facing wall surface and cross that surface away from the wall. It is resolved by the neutral product species and by the internal quantum state of that product.

For neutral product species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, with $\hat{\mathbf n}_w$ the unit normal directed from wall material into the adjacent plasma, the outgoing recombination contribution is defined by

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{rec,out}}_{n,\alpha} = \int_{\mathbf v \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_w > 0} (\mathbf v \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_w)\, f^{\mathrm{rec}}_{n,\alpha}(\mathbf v)\, d^3\mathbf v
$$

where $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity and $f^{\mathrm{rec}}_{n,\alpha}$ is the velocity-space distribution at the wall of neutral products generated by recombination.

This quantity includes only neutral recombination products in the specified internal state. Summing over internal states for the same neutral product species gives the [neutral particle flux at wall due to recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination); the incident-direction counterpart is [incident neutral internal-state particle flux at wall due to recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral recombination products cross the wall surface along the wall normal directed from the wall material into the plasma.

NAMES.name: incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Incident number flux density of neutral recombination products arriving at a plasma-facing wall, resolved by neutral species and internal quantum state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the incident number flux density of neutral particles produced by recombination and arriving at a plasma-facing wall, resolved by neutral species and by the internal quantum state of each particle. It is the incident component of the [neutral internal-state particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

The defining relation is

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{rec,inc}}_{a,s} = \frac{\mathrm{d}N^{\mathrm{rec,inc}}_{a,s}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{rec,inc}}_{a,s}$ is the incident flux density for neutral species $a$ in internal state $s$, $N^{\mathrm{rec,inc}}_{a,s}$ is the number of such particles arriving, $A$ is wall area, and $t$ is time.

The quantity counts arrivals rather than signed net transport. It excludes neutral particles produced by recycling, sputtering, radiation, or other mechanisms unrelated to recombination.

NAMES.name: nitrogen_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Nitrogen ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral nitrogen.
NAMES.long:
Nitrogen density at a limiter is the local number density of nitrogen ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, where the limiter terminates open field lines in the scrape-off layer.

The charge-state-summed density is defined from the velocity distribution functions by:

$$
n_{\mathrm{N}} = \sum_{q=1}^{q_{\max}} \int f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $q$ is the positive nitrogen ion charge state, $q_{\max}$ is the highest included ionization state, and $f_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution function of that ion state at the evaluation point.

This is the nitrogen-specific component of [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It excludes neutral nitrogen and is distinct from [neon_density_at_limiter](name:neon_density_at_limiter), which applies the same boundary definition to neon ions.

NAMES.name: oxygen_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Oxygen density at a limiter is the local number density of oxygen ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all oxygen ionization states from O+ through O8+ and excluding neutral oxygen atoms.
NAMES.long:
Oxygen density at a limiter is the local number density of oxygen ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance at the limiter. It is summed over all oxygen ionization states from O$^+$ through O$^{8+}$, and excludes neutral oxygen atoms.

For oxygen ion charge states from singly ionized to fully stripped, the charge-state-summed limiter density is defined as:

$$
n_{\mathrm{O},\mathrm{lim}} = \sum_{q=1}^{8} n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+},\mathrm{lim}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O},\mathrm{lim}}$ is the oxygen ion density at the limiter, $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+},\mathrm{lim}}$ is the local density of oxygen ions with charge state $q$, and the upper limit is the nuclear charge of oxygen.

This quantity is species-specific and charge-state-summed; it is not the neutral oxygen density, [electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter), or [total_ion_density_at_limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter). At the sheath entrance, oxygen charge-state densities contribute to quasineutrality through their charge-weighted sum and to the local effective charge. The analogous oxygen density at divertor target surfaces is [oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: particle_flux_at_wall
NAMES.short: Number of particles arriving at a plasma-facing wall surface per unit area per unit time from the plasma side, serving as the parent concept for species-resolved wall particle fluxes covering electrons, ions of any charge state, and neutral atoms or molecules.
NAMES.long:
Particle flux at the wall is the number rate per unit area at which plasma-side particles — electrons, ions of any charge state, or neutral atoms and molecules — impinge on a plasma-facing boundary surface. It is the most general form of the wall particle-flux concept, abstracting over the species identity of the arriving particles.

For a particle species $s$ with velocity distribution function $f_s(\mathbf{v})$, the incident flux is

$$
\Gamma_s = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n} < 0} f_s(\mathbf{v})\,|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}|\,d^3v
$$

where $\hat{n}$ is the inward-pointing wall-normal unit vector and the integral extends over particle velocities directed toward the surface. The total wall particle flux is obtained by summing $\Gamma_s$ over all contributing species.

Species-resolved refinements include [electron_particle_flux_at_wall](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall) for the electron channel, [ion_particle_flux_at_wall](name:ion_particle_flux_at_wall) for ions aggregated over all charge states, and [neutral_particle_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall) for neutral atoms and molecules summed over quantum states. The particle flux at the wall drives key plasma-material interaction processes including physical sputtering, chemical erosion, fuel retention, and recycling, and is closely coupled to the kinetic energy delivered to the surface, described by incident_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall.

In scrape-off-layer plasmas the ion component to a divertor target spans roughly $10^{21}$–$10^{24}$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ depending on plasma density, confinement mode, and divertor geometry; electron fluxes are comparable in magnitude at the sheath edge where quasi-neutrality is maintained.

NAMES.name: electron_particle_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number of electrons arriving at a plasma-facing wall surface per unit area per unit time from the plasma side, forming the electron-resolved component of wall particle flux.
NAMES.long:
The electron particle flux at the wall is the number rate per unit area at which plasma-side electrons impinge on a plasma-facing boundary surface. It is the electron-resolved component of [particle flux at the wall](name:particle_flux_at_wall).

For the electron population, the incident flux is

$$
\Gamma_e = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n} < 0} f_e(\mathbf{v})\,|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}|\,d^3v
$$

where $f_e(\mathbf{v})$ is the electron velocity distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $\hat{n}$ is the inward-pointing wall-normal unit vector. The integral includes only electrons directed toward the surface.

This quantity includes no ion or neutral contribution; the corresponding aggregate ion channel is [ion particle flux at the wall](name:ion_particle_flux_at_wall).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_particle_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Incident particle flux of ions in a specified charge state arriving at the plasma-facing wall per unit area per unit time.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state particle flux at the wall is the rate per unit area at which ions of a specified charge state impinge on a plasma-facing material surface from the plasma side. It is the charge-state-resolved refinement of [ion_particle_flux_at_wall](name:ion_particle_flux_at_wall), which aggregates this quantity over all ion charge states.

For ions in charge state $q$ with velocity distribution function $f_q(\mathbf{v})$, the incident flux is

$$
\Gamma_q = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n} < 0} f_q(\mathbf{v})\,|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}|\,d^3v
$$

where $\hat{n}$ is the inward-pointing wall-normal unit vector and the integration extends over velocities directed toward the surface. Summing $\Gamma_q$ over all charge states recovers [ion_particle_flux_at_wall](name:ion_particle_flux_at_wall); summing further over all species — including electrons and neutrals — recovers the parent [particle_flux_at_wall](name:particle_flux_at_wall).

This quantity is non-negative and is distinct from [neutral_particle_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall), which counts uncharged species arriving at the wall.

NAMES.name: ion_particle_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Number of ions arriving at a plasma-facing wall surface per unit area per unit time from the plasma side, summed over all ion charge states and forming the ion component of wall particle flux.
NAMES.long:
The ion particle flux at the wall is the number rate per unit area at which plasma-side ions impinge on a plasma-facing boundary surface. It is the ion-resolved component of [particle flux at the wall](name:particle_flux_at_wall), aggregated over all ion species and charge states.

For ion species $s$ and charge state $q$, the incident flux is

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{ion}} = \sum_{s,q} \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}<0} f_{s,q}(\mathbf{v})\,|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}|\,d^3v
$$

where $f_{s,q}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution function for ions of species $s$ and charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\hat{n}$ is the inward-pointing wall-normal unit vector. The integral includes only velocities directed toward the surface.

This quantity excludes electron and neutral-particle contributions. The charge-state-resolved refinement is [ion charge-state particle flux at the wall](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_at_wall), while the neutral contribution is represented separately by [neutral particle flux at the wall](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall).

NAMES.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Incident flux of neutral particles (atoms and molecules) arriving at the plasma-facing wall per unit area per unit time, summed over all quantum states of the neutral species.
NAMES.long:
The neutral particle flux at the wall is the local rate per unit area at which neutral atoms and molecules impinge on plasma-facing material from the plasma-boundary region. It is the total neutral contribution to [particle_flux_at_wall](name:particle_flux_at_wall), summed over all quantum states of the neutral species. Neutrals reaching the wall arrive primarily through charge-exchange reactions and recombination in the scrape-off layer, gas injection, and desorption from the surface.

The incident neutral flux density is defined by integrating the wall-directed component of the neutral velocity distribution:

$$
\Gamma_n = \int_{v_\perp > 0} v_\perp \, f_n(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $v_\perp$ is the velocity component directed toward the wall surface and $f_n(\mathbf{v})$ is the neutral particle velocity distribution function.

This flux is a primary driver of fuel recycling, hydrogenic implantation, and physical sputtering of plasma-facing components. The quantum-state-resolved analog [neutral_state_particle_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall) decomposes this total by individual electronic excitation state, while [neutral_energy_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_energy_flux_at_wall) gives the associated kinetic energy carried by the same neutral population. The species counterparts [ion_particle_flux_at_wall](name:ion_particle_flux_at_wall) and [electron_particle_flux_at_wall](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall) complete the particle-species decomposition of the total wall loading.

NAMES.name: particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.short: Outgoing particle-number flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident plasma ions recombine at the surface, summed over emitted product species and states.
NAMES.long:
Particle flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which recombination-associated particles are emitted from a plasma-facing surface per unit area as a result of incident plasma ions recombining or neutralizing at the material boundary. It is the total count flux of emitted product particles, not the incident plasma flux or the energy deposited in the wall.

The total recombination particle flux at wall location $\mathbf{x}_w$ is defined by

$$
\Gamma_\mathrm{rec}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{a,\,q,\,c,\,k} \Gamma_{a,q,c,k}(\mathbf{x}_w)
$$

where $a$ identifies the emitted product species, $q$ the incident-ion charge state, $c$ the recombination channel, $k$ the product internal state or energy class, and $\Gamma_{a,q,c,k}$ the corresponding emitted-particle flux. For continuous product variables, the corresponding sums become integrals.

This quantity is the particle-count counterpart of [energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) and is the component-specific realization of [flux at the wall due to recombination](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). The neutral-product specialization is [neutral particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

NAMES.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Outgoing neutral-particle number flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident plasma ions recombine at the surface, summed over neutral product species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral particle flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which neutral particles are emitted from a plasma-facing surface per unit area as a result of incident plasma ions recombining or neutralizing at the material boundary. It is the outgoing neutral-particle count flux, not the incident neutral flux or the energy deposited in the wall.

The total neutral recombination particle flux at wall location $\mathbf{x}_w$ is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{neutral,rec}}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{a,\,q,\,c,\,k} \Gamma_{a,q,c,k}(\mathbf{x}_w)
$$

where $a$ identifies the emitted neutral product species, $q$ the incident-ion charge state, $c$ the recombination channel, $k$ the product internal state or energy class, and $\Gamma_{a,q,c,k}$ the corresponding emitted-neutral particle flux. For continuous product variables, the corresponding sums become integrals.

This quantity is the neutral-product specialization of [particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). Its state-resolved counterpart is [neutral internal state particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), while [incident neutral particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) describes the opposite direction of transport.

NAMES.name: incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Incident number flux density of neutral recombination products arriving at a plasma-facing wall, summed over neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the incoming neutral-particle count flux at a wall attributable to recombination, with neutral product species and internal states aggregated. It selects particles arriving at the surface, rather than neutral particles emitted from it.

The incident flux density is defined from the recombination-attributed neutral distribution by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{rec}}(\mathbf{x}_w)=\int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}<0} \left|\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right| f_{\mathrm{n,rec}}(\mathbf{x}_w,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_w$ is the wall position, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the outward wall normal, $\mathbf{v}$ is neutral-particle velocity, and $f_{\mathrm{n,rec}}$ is the recombination-attributed neutral distribution summed over species and internal states.

This incident quantity is distinct from the outgoing emission described by [neutral particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). A state-resolved counterpart, [incident neutral internal-state particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), retains the internal-state distinction.

NAMES.name: radial_total_current_density_at_wall
NAMES.short: Radial (R-direction) component of the total electric current-density vector at a plasma-facing wall in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height. It is signed positive toward increasing R.
NAMES.long:
Radial (R-direction) component of the total electric current-density vector at a plasma-facing wall is the projection of the local total electric current-density vector onto the $\hat{R}$ basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining projection at a wall point $\mathbf{x}_w$ is:

$$
j_{R,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{wall}}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{x}_w) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}(\mathbf{x}_w)
$$

where $j_{R,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{wall}}$ denotes this scalar quantity, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total [current_density](name:current_density), $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the local unit vector toward increasing $R$, and $\mathbf{x}_w$ lies on the plasma-facing material wall.

Total means all current-carrying contributions included in the physical current-density vector, such as inductive, neoclassical, wave-driven, kinetic, conductive, charged-particle, and sheath-mediated currents. This quantity is the wall-evaluated radial projection of the total vector, not a process-resolved contribution such as [radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). A tile current such as [current_of_divertor_tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile) is a surface integral of the current-density component normal to that tile; it equals an area integral of this radial component only where the tile normal is parallel to $\hat{R}$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ at the wall points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: source_rate_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.short: Global rate at which surface emission (recycling, outgassing, and sputtering) at plasma-facing surfaces supplies ionized particles to the plasma, summed over all surfaces and weighted by each species' particle multiplicity.
NAMES.long:
The surface emission source rate is the total number of particles per second added to the plasma from all material boundaries through recycling of incident plasma species, thermal outgassing, and physical or chemical sputtering. Each emitted neutral atom or molecule is weighted by the number of plasma particles it yields upon ionization, so a molecule that releases multiple ions on ionization contributes proportionally more than a monatomic species.

The defining relation for the aggregate rate is:

$$
S_{\rm surf} = \sum_{\rm surfaces} \int_A \sum_{k} \Gamma_k(\mathbf{r})\, w_k\, dA
$$

where $\Gamma_k(\mathbf{r})$ is the emitted particle flux density of neutral species $k$ at wall position $\mathbf{r}$, $w_k$ is the ionization-weighted particle multiplicity (number of plasma particles produced per emitted neutral of species $k$), and the area integral runs over all plasma-facing surfaces.

This parent name abstracts over species-resolved surface source rates; the concrete electron-equivalent contribution is given by [electron_source_rate_due_to_surface_emission](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_surface_emission). For comparison, [total_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:total_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) gives the corresponding neutral flux leaving surfaces before ionization, while [particle_flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling](name:particle_flux_of_divertor_due_to_recycling) isolates the recycling-specific input at divertor targets. In edge plasma and scrape-off-layer modeling, this source rate enters the global particle balance alongside volumetric ionization from the bulk, and is non-negative by construction.

NAMES.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_surface_emission
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission of material from plasma-facing surfaces, weighted by the electron contribution of each emitted species after ionization.
NAMES.long:
Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by surface emission is the rate at which ionization of material released from plasma-facing surfaces adds electrons to the plasma particle balance. It aggregates all emitted fuel, molecular, and impurity species over all plasma-facing surfaces, with each emitted particle weighted by the number of bound electrons it can contribute after full ionization.

The global rate is defined by integrating the emitted particle flux density over the plasma-facing surface area:

$$
S_e^{\mathrm{surf}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf}}} \sum_s \nu_{e,s}\,\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA
$$

where $S_e^{\mathrm{surf}}$ is the electron-equivalent surface-emission source rate, $A_{\mathrm{pf}}$ is the total plasma-facing surface area, $s$ indexes emitted species, $\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{emit}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the emitted particle flux density of species $s$ at surface position $\mathbf{x}$ directed toward the plasma, $dA$ is a surface element, and $\nu_{e,s}$ is the electron yield of one emitted particle on full ionization. For an emitted atom, $\nu_{e,s}=Z_s$ with $Z_s$ the nuclear charge number; for an emitted molecule or compound particle, $\nu_{e,s}$ is the sum of the nuclear charge numbers of its constituent atoms.

Surface emission includes recycling, delayed outgassing, and physical or chemical sputtering only insofar as the released material returns toward the plasma and is ionized. This quantity is the electron-specific counterpart of [source_rate_due_to_surface_emission](name:source_rate_due_to_surface_emission), is distinct from externally supplied material represented by [electron_source_rate_due_to_injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection), excludes electron loss by incidence on surfaces, and contributes to [total_electron_source_rate](name:total_electron_source_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when ionization of material emitted from plasma-facing surfaces supplies electron-equivalent particles to the plasma.

NAMES.name: surface_area_of_optical_element
NAMES.short: Geometric area of the specified optically active material surface of an optical element, measured on the physical surface rather than as its projected aperture.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the geometric area contributed by one specified optically active surface of an optical element. It is a component of the total [area of the optical element](name:area_of_optical_element), not the projected clear-aperture area.

The component area is defined by

$$
A_c = \int_{\mathcal{S}_c} dA
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_c$ is the specified physical material surface and $dA$ is its differential surface-area element. The surface may be curved or planar. Inactive material regions and projected-area representations are excluded; when the active surfaces form a disjoint partition, their component areas sum to the total optical-element area.

NAMES.name: surface_emissivity
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of thermal radiation emitted by a surface to blackbody radiation at the same surface temperature, with the stated spectral and angular averaging.
NAMES.long:
Surface emissivity is the effectiveness of a material surface in emitting thermal electromagnetic radiation relative to an ideal blackbody at the same temperature. It is a material property of the emitting surface and is distinct from the emitted energy flux described by [energy flux due to surface emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).

The effective emissivity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon = \frac{M_{\mathrm{emit}}(T_s)}{M_{\mathrm{bb}}(T_s)}
$$

where $M_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the surface thermal radiative exitance, $M_{\mathrm{bb}}$ is the blackbody exitance, and $T_s$ is the surface temperature. The ratio applies to the specified spectral band and angular averaging; it is not a wavelength- and direction-resolved emissivity. Incident radiation and geometric surface area, such as [optical-element area](name:area_of_optical_element), are excluded.

NAMES.name: surface_temperature
NAMES.short: Surface temperature is the thermodynamic temperature of the exposed material boundary of a plasma-facing component at a specified surface point. It refers to the surface material state, not to an area aggregate or regional extremum.
NAMES.long:
Surface temperature is the thermodynamic temperature of the material at the exposed boundary of a plasma-facing component. It is a local scalar assigned to a specified material surface point and time, representing the state of the surface material rather than the temperature of the adjacent plasma, sheath, neutral gas, or radiation field.

For an extended exposed surface, the unqualified quantity denotes the local point value at each surface point, not an area average, integral, percentile, or extremum. Region-level aggregates require distinct standard names; the maximum over a specified exposed surface region is [maximum_surface_temperature](name:maximum_surface_temperature). [temperature_at_wall](name:temperature_at_wall) is the corresponding boundary-locus temperature when the wall is the defining locus.

NAMES.name: maximum_surface_temperature
NAMES.short: Peak apparent temperature of the exposed plasma-facing surface over all valid points within a defined infrared-camera region of interest.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the largest apparent temperature assigned to the exposed material surface of a plasma-facing component within a specified infrared-camera region of interest. It is an extremum of the local [surface temperature](name:surface_temperature), not a local value, area average, or heat-flux measure.

$$
T_{\mathrm{max,ROI}} = \max_{\mathbf{x} \in V_{\mathrm{ROI}}} T_s(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $T_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the surface temperature at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and $V_{\mathrm{ROI}}$ is the set of valid surface positions in the defined region of interest. Points excluded from the valid set do not contribute to the maximum.

NAMES.name: temperature_at_limiter
NAMES.short: Kinetic temperature of a specified plasma population or density-weighted local mixture evaluated on the plasma-facing side of a limiter.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the kinetic temperature of a plasma population or local population mixture at the plasma-facing side of a limiter, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate. It includes species-specific quantities such as [electron temperature at the limiter](name:electron_temperature_at_limiter) and density-weighted mixture quantities such as [average temperature at the limiter](name:average_temperature_at_limiter).

For an isotropic population, the kinetic temperature is defined by

$$
\frac{3}{2} k_B T = \langle E_{\mathrm{rand}} \rangle
$$

where $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, $T$ is the kinetic temperature, and $\langle E_{\mathrm{rand}} \rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per particle. For a mixture, the average temperature is density-weighted over the included populations.

The quantity refers to the plasma side of the limiter and excludes the temperature of the solid limiter material. It is a local boundary-plasma quantity, distinct from [temperature at the plasma boundary](name:temperature_at_plasma_boundary) when that boundary is not the limiter.

NAMES.name: average_temperature_at_limiter
NAMES.short: Local density-weighted average temperature at the plasma-wall interface on the plasma-facing side of a limiter, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on material surfaces.
NAMES.long:
Average temperature at the limiter is the local density-weighted mean temperature of the plasma population on the plasma-facing side of a limiter surface, at the plasma-wall interface where open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines intersect material structures. It characterizes the effective thermal energy of the mixed plasma at the sheath edge, accounting for contributions weighted by the local species densities, and is not the temperature of the solid limiter material.

The density-weighted average temperature $T_\text{avg}$ is defined as:

$$
T_\text{avg} = \frac{\sum_s n_s T_s}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where the sum runs over all plasma species $s$ in scope (ion species across charge states, and potentially electrons), $n_s$ is the local number density of species $s$ at the limiter-side plasma, and $T_s$ is the corresponding local temperature of species $s$. The summation scope defines the sub-variant: [ion average temperature at the limiter](name:ion_average_temperature_at_limiter) restricts the average to ion species and charge states only.

In experiments this quantity is inferred from combinations of Langmuir-probe current–voltage characteristics, edge spectroscopy, and scrape-off-layer transport modeling constrained by edge and wall measurements, with corrections for sheath physics, magnetic-field incidence angle, secondary electron emission, and collisionality.

Together with [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter), the average temperature supports local pressure estimates at the limiter. It is one component of the broader [temperature_at_limiter](name:temperature_at_limiter) family, which also encompasses species-resolved temperatures such as [electron_temperature_at_limiter](name:electron_temperature_at_limiter).

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Kinetic temperature of the electron population evaluated at the plasma-facing side of a limiter, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local kinetic temperature of the electron population at the plasma-wall interface on the plasma-facing side of a limiter, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate. It is the electron-specific member of [temperature at limiter](name:temperature_at_limiter).

For an isotropic electron population, its temperature expressed in energy units is defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_{\mathrm{kin},e} \rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron kinetic temperature and $\langle E_{\mathrm{kin},e} \rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron.

The quantity refers to electrons on the plasma-facing side of the limiter interface and does not denote the temperature of the limiter material. It is distinct from the density-weighted population average [average temperature at limiter](name:average_temperature_at_limiter), which combines the relevant plasma populations.

sources.enhanced_context: Electron temperature (Te) at the limiter location. Provides a local measure of the electron thermal energy at the plasma–limiter interface as part of the discharge summary.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Electron temperature

NAMES.name: ion_average_temperature_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Density-weighted mean kinetic temperature of all ion species and charge states on the plasma-facing side of a limiter, providing the ion component of the local average plasma temperature.
NAMES.long:
The ion component of the local plasma temperature at a limiter is the density-weighted mean kinetic temperature of all positive ion species and charge states on the plasma-facing side of the limiter. It is the ion-specific component of [average temperature at the limiter](name:average_temperature_at_limiter).

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_s \sum_q n_{s,q} T_{s,q}}{\sum_s \sum_q n_{s,q}}
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes their positive charge states, $n_{s,q}$ is the corresponding ion number density, and $T_{s,q}$ is its kinetic temperature. The denominator is the [total ion density at the limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter).

This quantity includes all ion species and charge states in the local plasma population and excludes electrons, neutral particles, and the solid limiter material. It is distinct from [temperature at the limiter](name:temperature_at_limiter), which may denote a specified population or a different population aggregation.

sources.enhanced_context: Ion temperature (Ti) averaged over ion species at the limiter location. Groups the value, source, and uncertainty for this local plasma parameter summary quantity.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Ion temperature (average over ion species)

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_of_vacuum_vessel
NAMES.short: Net conduction current circulating around the vacuum vessel, induced by time-varying magnetic flux linked with the vessel.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net conduction current carried by the vacuum-vessel material in the toroidal direction. It represents an induced eddy current driven by changing magnetic flux linked with the conducting vessel, excluding currents in the plasma, external coils, and other conductors.

The net current is the signed cross-sectional integral of the toroidal conduction-current density:

$$
I_{\mathrm{vessel}} = \int_S j_\phi\,\mathrm{d}S
$$

where $j_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the conduction-current density, $S$ is a cross section of the vessel material normal to the toroidal direction, and $\mathrm{d}S$ is its area element. The toroidal direction is the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. Faraday induction drives the current through the changing linked magnetic flux; its response is determined by the vessel's electromagnetic impedance. This is a vessel-specific instance of [current of passive structure](name:current_of_passive_structure) and is distinct from [toroidal current of cryostat](name:toroidal_current_of_cryostat).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net conduction current points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Toroidal current (j_phi) induced in a block element of the vacuum vessel structure, representing eddy or inductively driven currents in the toroidal direction. Relevant for electromagnetic load analysis and disruption studies.
sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal current induced in this block element
sources.parent_definition: Set of block elements

sources.enhanced_context: Toroidal current (Iφ) flowing in the vacuum vessel wall, induced by changing magnetic flux during plasma operation. Contributes to passive stabilization of vertical displacement events and affects equilibrium reconstruction.
sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal current flowing in the vacuum vessel
sources.parent_definition: Simple 0D description of plasma-wall interaction

NAMES.name: total_incident_power_at_wall
NAMES.short: Total plasma power arriving at all plasma-facing wall surfaces, summed over conducted, convected, radiative, and other incident energy channels.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total energy delivered from the plasma to plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces by all incident channels. It represents the area-integrated power arriving at those surfaces before reflection or re-emission.

The total incident power is defined by integrating the incident energy-flux density over the complete plasma-facing area:

$$
P_{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wall}}} q_{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf r)\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the total incident power, $A_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the union of the relevant plasma-facing surfaces, $q_{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf r)$ is the incident power per unit area at surface position $\mathbf r$, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is a differential surface area. The integrand is the area-density counterpart [energy flux at wall](name:energy_flux_at_wall). The total includes all incident energy channels and excludes power emitted from the wall toward the plasma or vacuum.

sources.enhanced_context: Total power incident on the first wall and divertor surfaces from the plasma, representing the sum of all power channels delivered to wall-facing components. Acts as the overall normalization for conducted, convected, radiated, and other power components.
sources.leaf_definition: Total power incident on the wall. This power is split in the various physical categories listed below
sources.parent_definition: Simple 0D description of plasma-wall interaction

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Charge-state-summed number density of all ion species in the boundary plasma immediately on the plasma-facing side of a limiter surface.
NAMES.long:
Total ion density at a limiter is the local number density of all charged ion species and ionization states at the plasma-side evaluation point adjacent to the limiter. It is the charge-state-summed component of [ion_density_at_limiter](name:ion_density_at_limiter).

The defining aggregation is

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state $Z$, and the sums include every ion species and positive charge state present at the evaluation point.

Neutral atoms and molecules are excluded, as is electron density. The limiter-local aggregation is distinct from the corresponding total quantity at the plasma boundary, [total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), because the evaluation locus is specifically the plasma-facing side of a limiter surface.

sources.enhanced_context: Total ion density (ni_total) at the limiter, summed over all ion species. Represents the net ion particle density at the limiter plasma-facing surface.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Local particle number density of tritium ions evaluated in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
NAMES.long:
Tritium density at a limiter is the local number density of tritium ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance, not inside limiter material or in neutral gas at the surface. The quantity excludes neutral tritium atoms.

Because tritium is hydrogenic, its charge-state-summed ion density is the density of singly charged tritium ions:

$$
n_{\mathrm{T}} = n_{\mathrm{T}^{+}} = \int f_{\mathrm{T}^{+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^{3}v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the tritium ion number density, $f_{\mathrm{T}^{+}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution function of singly charged tritium ions, and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity.

This isotope contribution is included in [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It is evaluated at a limiter rather than at the separatrix, unlike [tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), and is the tritium counterpart of [deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter).

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium

NAMES.name: tungsten_density
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Number density of tungsten ions summed over all positive ionization states, excluding neutral tungsten, at a specified location or spatial average.
NAMES.long:
Tungsten-ion number density is the particle count per unit volume for all positively charged tungsten ions, with neutral tungsten excluded. It may denote a local value or a spatially averaged value over a defined domain.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}} = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{W}}^{Z+}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, and $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge state. Specific instances include [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), [tungsten density at magnetic axis](name:tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis), and [tungsten density at divertor target](name:tungsten_density_at_divertor_target); these differ by evaluation locus or averaging domain. Neutral tungsten is not included.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the counted tungsten-ion population has positive particle number.

sources.enhanced_context: Tungsten.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Local particle number density of tungsten ions evaluated in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over ionization states and excluding neutral tungsten.
NAMES.long:
Number density of tungsten ions evaluated at the plasma-limiter interface on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. The limiter terminates open magnetic field lines in the scrape-off layer, so this quantity describes the tungsten impurity population participating in limiter-adjacent plasma–surface interactions.

The charge-state sum is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm W} = \sum_{Z\ge 1} n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}} = \sum_{Z\ge 1}\int f_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm W}$ is the total tungsten-ion number density, $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge number, $n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}$ is the density of charge state $Z$, and $f_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity distribution function. The sum includes all tungsten ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten.

This quantity specializes [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) to tungsten and contributes to [ion_density_at_limiter](name:ion_density_at_limiter). It is evaluated at the limiter rather than the divertor-target location used by [tungsten_density_at_divertor_target](name:tungsten_density_at_divertor_target).

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture
NAMES.short: Signed vertical coordinate of the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured from the machine midplane.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the vertical coordinate of the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The aperture is treated as a geometric opening rather than a plasma or wall surface.

For an aperture region with geometric area $A$, the center coordinate is defined by the area centroid:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{c}} = \frac{1}{A}\int_A Z\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{c}}$ is the aperture-center coordinate, $Z$ is the vertical coordinate of each area element, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is the differential aperture area. This cylindrical-frame coordinate is distinct from the camera-frame [y coordinate of the diagnostic aperture](name:y_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture) and is the diagnostic-aperture-specific counterpart of [vertical coordinate of aperture](name:vertical_coordinate_of_aperture).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aperture center lies toward increasing $Z$, upward from the machine midplane.

NAMES.name: vertical_coordinate_of_optical_element
NAMES.short: Signed vertical coordinate of the geometric center of an optical element, measured from the machine midplane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the vertical position of an optical element's geometric center relative to the machine midplane. It refers to the element as a whole, not to an aperture, active optical surface, or another internal feature.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{opt}} = Z_{\mathrm{center}} - Z_{\mathrm{midplane}}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{center}}$ is the center's vertical coordinate and $Z_{\mathrm{midplane}}$ is the vertical coordinate of the machine midplane. Both are defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity is analogous to the [vertical coordinate of an aperture](name:vertical_coordinate_of_aperture) and [vertical coordinate of a Bragg crystal](name:vertical_coordinate_of_bragg_crystal), but applies to the geometric center of the optical element.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the geometric center lies above the machine midplane, in the direction of increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: x_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture
NAMES.short: Signed x coordinate of the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture, measured from the origin of its right-handed camera Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity locates the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture along the x axis of its right-handed camera Cartesian basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$. It is a signed geometric position, not an aperture dimension or orientation.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
x_A = (\mathbf{r}_A - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_A$ is the position of the aperture center, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the frame origin, $\hat{x}$ is the unit vector along the x axis, and $x_A$ is measured in m. The corresponding [y coordinate of the diagnostic aperture](name:y_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture) uses the same origin and camera basis; this quantity is distinct from cylindrical radial and vertical aperture coordinates.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aperture center lies in the direction of increasing x from the frame origin.

sources.parent_definition: Pinhole position in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system

NAMES.name: x_coordinate_of_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Signed Cartesian x-coordinate locating the geometric center of a divertor target surface in the right-handed (x, y, z) frame, with +x at toroidal angle φ = 0.
NAMES.long:
The x coordinate of a divertor target is the signed Cartesian position of the geometric center of its target surface. It locates that center in the right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$, where $\hat{z}$ is vertical and the positive x direction is horizontal at toroidal angle $\phi=0$.

The coordinate is defined by projection of the center position onto the Cartesian x unit vector:

$$
x_c = \mathbf{r}_c \cdot \hat{\mathbf{x}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_c$ is the position vector of the target-surface geometric center, $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$ is the Cartesian x unit vector, and $x_c$ is the resulting signed coordinate. The corresponding center location is completed by the [y coordinate of the divertor target](name:y_coordinate_of_divertor_target) and [z coordinate of the divertor target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target); this quantity does not specify the target surface extent.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the target center lies in the direction of increasing Cartesian x from the coordinate origin.

sources.parent_definition: Position of the center of the targeted surface

NAMES.name: x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera
NAMES.short: X-axis component of the unit vector defining the line-of-sight direction of a camera, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The x-component $d_x$ of the unit vector $\hat{d}$ that specifies the line-of-sight (viewing) direction of the camera in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame. Together with the [y-component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_camera) and [z-component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera), it fully determines the camera pointing direction as $\hat{d} = (d_x, d_y, d_z)$ with $d_x^2 + d_y^2 + d_z^2 = 1$.

This quantity is geometrically distinct from the [x_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera](name:x_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera), which encodes the image-plane vertical orientation rather than the viewing axis.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the camera's line-of-sight direction has a component in the $+x$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_limiter
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Xenon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive charge states and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Xenon density at the limiter is the local number density of xenon ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance at the plasma-limiter contact, consistent with the parent quantity [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter).

When charge states are not individually resolved, this quantity represents the sum over all positive xenon charge states $\text{Xe}^{q+}$, $q = 1, \ldots, 54$:

$$
n_{\text{Xe}} = \sum_{q=1}^{54} n_{\text{Xe}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\text{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the number density of xenon in charge state $q$. Neutral xenon atoms are excluded from this sum.

Xenon is used as a high-$Z$ impurity seed for radiative power exhaust management in the scrape-off layer. Its concentration at the limiter is set by the balance of ionization, recombination, and cross-field impurity transport, and it determines the local particle flux, radiative power load, and potential sputtering damage to the plasma-facing surface. This quantity can be inferred from edge emission spectroscopy combined with collisional-radiative modeling. For xenon impurity density inside the confined plasma, see [xenon_density](name:xenon_density); for the analogous quantity at a divertor surface, see [xenon_density_at_divertor_target](name:xenon_density_at_divertor_target); and for xenon at the last closed flux surface, see [xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

NAMES.name: y_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture
NAMES.short: Signed y coordinate of the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture in the right-handed camera Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the signed Cartesian y coordinate of a diagnostic aperture's geometric center, measured from the origin of the right-handed camera basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$. It locates the aperture along the camera-frame y axis.

The coordinate is defined by projection of the center position vector:

$$
y_{\rm ap} = \mathbf{r}_{\rm ap} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $y_{\rm ap}$ is the coordinate value, $\mathbf{r}_{\rm ap}$ is the aperture-center position relative to the camera-frame origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the positive y-axis unit vector; the length quantities are expressed in m.

This camera-frame coordinate is distinct from the radial and vertical coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Together with the [x coordinate of the diagnostic aperture](name:x_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture), it locates the aperture center in the camera frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aperture center lies in the positive y direction from the camera-frame origin.

sources.leaf_definition: Component along Y axis
sources.parent_definition: Pinhole position in the (X,Y,Z) coordinate system

NAMES.name: y_coordinate_of_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Cartesian Y coordinate of the divertor target surface center in the right-handed (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The Y coordinate locates the center of the divertor target surface along the $\hat{y}$ axis of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, where $\hat{z} = \hat{Z}$ is vertical and $\hat{x}$ is aligned with $\phi = 0$, with the toroidal angle $\phi$ increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$. This coordinate relates to the cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ description of the same point by the standard transformation $y = R\sin\phi$, where $R$ is the major radius from the toroidal symmetry axis and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

This coordinate is used alongside [x_coordinate_of_divertor_target](name:x_coordinate_of_divertor_target) and [vertical_coordinate_of_divertor_target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target) to fully specify the three-dimensional Cartesian position of the divertor target center in plasma-wall interaction modeling. It is obtained from engineering drawings of the divertor geometry or from geometric calibration of diagnostics such as infrared cameras that image the target surface.

The magnitude of $y$ is bounded by the major radius of the machine; for a target segment at toroidal angle $\phi$ and radial distance $R$ from the symmetry axis, $|y|$ spans zero to approximately $R$ depending on the toroidal location of the target.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the divertor target center is displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Y coordinate of target surface center.

NAMES.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_camera
NAMES.short: Y-axis component of the direction unit vector defining the line-of-sight orientation of a camera, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The direction unit vector $\hat{d}$ of a camera specifies the orientation of its line of sight in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame. This scalar quantity is the projection of $\hat{d}$ onto the $\hat{y}$ axis:

$$
\hat{d}_y = \hat{d} \cdot \hat{y}
$$

where $|\hat{d}| = 1$ by construction, bounding $\hat{d}_y \in [-1, 1]$. Together with the [x-axis component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera) and [z-axis component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera), it fully determines the three-dimensional camera pointing direction. This quantity is distinct from [y_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera](name:y_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera), which gives the image-plane vertical orientation perpendicular to the viewing direction rather than the viewing direction itself.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the camera line-of-sight direction has a component in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: y_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera
NAMES.short: Y-axis projection of the unit vector defining the image-up orientation direction of a camera, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The image-up unit vector of a camera specifies the spatial direction in three-dimensional space that corresponds to the upward direction within the camera's image plane, defining the camera's rotational orientation about its optical axis. The Y component gives the projection of this orientation vector onto the $\hat{y}$ axis of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, where $\hat{x}$, $\hat{y}$, and $\hat{z}$ are mutually orthogonal basis vectors satisfying $\hat{x} \times \hat{y} = \hat{z}$.

The three Cartesian components of the image-up unit vector satisfy the normalization constraint:

$$
u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1
$$

where $u_x$, $u_y$, and $u_z$ are the X, Y, and Z projections respectively, each dimensionless and bounded in $[-1, 1]$.

The image-up direction is perpendicular to the camera's line-of-sight (optical axis) and lies in the image plane; it is determined by the physical mounting orientation of the camera on the diagnostic structure. Together with [x_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera](name:x_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera), the full image-up orientation can be reconstructed. The value is set at installation or calibration time from a survey of the camera geometry in the device coordinate frame.

NAMES.name: z_coordinate_of_divertor_target
NAMES.short: Vertical Cartesian coordinate of the geometric center of a divertor target surface, identifying its location along the facility's vertical axis.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the vertical coordinate of the geometric center of a divertor target surface. It identifies the center point rather than the target's vertical extent or surface outline.

In the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, the coordinate is defined by

$$
z_{\mathrm{target}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the position vector of the target surface center relative to the frame origin and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The $z$ direction corresponds to $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Together with the [x coordinate of the divertor target](name:x_coordinate_of_divertor_target) and [y coordinate of the divertor target](name:y_coordinate_of_divertor_target), this quantity locates the target surface center. It is distinct from the [vertical length of the divertor target](name:vertical_length_of_divertor_target) and the [vertical outline of the divertor tile](name:vertical_outline_of_divertor_tile), which describe extent and boundary geometry rather than the center position.
