NAMES.name: fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volumetric torque density deposited in the fast-electron population through Coulomb collisions, the local rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume.
NAMES.long:
The fast-electron collisional torque density is the net rate at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum per unit volume to the suprathermal electron population. It is the fast-electron contribution to [electron torque density due to collisions](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

It is defined from the collisional force density by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is displacement from the torque axis in m, and $\mathbf{f}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density on fast electrons in N m$^{-3}$. For the toroidal specialization, the transfer rate is $R f_\phi$, where $R$ is major radius in m and $f_\phi$ is the force-density projection onto $\hat{\phi}$; this is represented by [toroidal fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Orbit-resolved forms distinguish co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped fast electrons. The fast-electron contribution excludes the bulk thermal-electron component represented by [thermal-electron torque density due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and is distinct from the volume-integrated [fast-electron torque due to collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the relevant angular-momentum transfer points along the positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis; for toroidal transfer, positive means $f_\phi$ points toward increasing $\phi$.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volumetric torque density deposited in co-passing fast electrons through Coulomb collisions, the local rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume.
NAMES.long:
The co-passing fast-electron collisional torque density is the net rate at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum per unit volume to suprathermal electrons on co-passing guiding-center orbits. It is the co-passing-orbit contribution to [fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

It is defined from the collisional force density on the co-passing fast-electron population by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{e,f,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the co-passing fast-electron collisional torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is displacement from the torque axis, and $\mathbf{f}_{e,f,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density on co-passing fast electrons. For the toroidal specialization, the transfer rate is $R f_\phi$, where $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and $f_\phi$ is the force-density projection onto $\hat{\phi}$; this is represented by [toroidal co-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The co-passing restriction excludes counter-passing and trapped fast-electron orbits, represented by [counter-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [trapped fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). It is distinct from the orbit-summed fast-electron torque density and from any volume-integrated torque.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the selected component of angular-momentum transfer points along the corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; for the toroidal component, this means $f_\phi$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volumetric torque density deposited in counter-passing fast electrons through Coulomb collisions, the local rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume.
NAMES.long:
The counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque density is the net rate at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum per unit volume to suprathermal electrons whose guiding-center parallel velocity is opposite the toroidal plasma-current direction. It is the counter-passing component of the [fast-electron collisional torque density](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), with all directional components retained.

The angular-momentum moment of the Coulomb collision operator is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{cp}} = \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{cp}}} \mathbf{r} \times m_e\mathbf{v}\, C[f_e^{\mathrm{fast}}] \, d^3v
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the toroidal symmetry axis, $m_e$ is electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $C$ is the Coulomb collision operator, and $f_e^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-electron distribution. The domain $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ selects counter-passing guiding-center orbits.

The quantity excludes co-passing and trapped fast electrons. The [toroidal counter-passing fast-electron torque density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is its toroidal projection, while the [co-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) provides the corresponding opposite orbit-class contribution.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated torque transferred to the fast, non-thermal electron population through Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma.
NAMES.long:
The fast-electron collisional torque quantifies the net rate of angular momentum transferred to the non-thermal electron population through Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma.

The vector torque is the volume integral of the moment of the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{fe,\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{fe,\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position relative to the torque origin, $\mathbf{f}_{fe,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density acting on fast electrons, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

This quantity is the fast-electron contribution to the total [electron collisional torque](name:electron_torque_due_to_collisions). Its toroidal projection is represented by [toroidal fast-electron collisional torque](name:toroidal_fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions), while [thermal electron collisional torque](name:thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions) describes the corresponding transfer to the bulk thermal population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal component of angular momentum is transferred to fast electrons in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to a specified fast ion charge state through Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum source associated with Coulomb momentum transfer to a specified fast ion charge state. Orbit classes and directional components select particular contributions without changing this common physical meaning.

For a selected angular-momentum direction, the torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a} = (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_a
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}$ is the torque density about direction $a$, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the rotation axis, $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to the specified fast ion charge state, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the corresponding unit vector. For toroidal angular momentum in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this relation reduces to $R f_\phi$.

This quantity is the fast-ion, charge-state-resolved realization of [ion charge-state torque density due to collisions]; [co-passing fast ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [toroidal fast ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) are orbit-resolved or component-resolved instances.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the selected angular-momentum transfer is in the positive orientation of its stated axis; for toroidal angular momentum, positive is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Torque density vector giving the angular-momentum source per unit volume deposited by Coulomb collisions on co-passing fast ions in a specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
The collisional torque density vector for co-passing fast ions in charge state $q$ quantifies the angular-momentum source per unit volume arising from Coulomb collisions of those ions with background plasma particles. Co-passing fast ions are suprathermal ions whose guiding-center orbits circulate continuously around the torus in the same direction as the plasma current.

The quantity is the first angular-momentum moment of the Coulomb collision operator restricted to the co-passing phase-space domain $\Omega_\mathrm{co}$:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{q,\mathrm{co}} = m_i \int_{\Omega_\mathrm{co}} (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{v})\, C[f_q]\, d^3v
$$

where $m_i$ is the fast-ion mass, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity, $C[f_q]$ is the Coulomb collision operator acting on the fast-ion distribution function $f_q$ for ions in charge state $q$, and $\Omega_\mathrm{co}$ is the co-passing region of phase space.

This quantity is the co-passing orbit-class contribution to the charge-state-resolved fast-ion collisional torque density [fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions), excluding trapped and counter-passing populations. Its toroidal projection is [toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions). The orbit-integrated counterpart without charge-state resolution is [co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal angular-momentum source acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Collisional torque-density vector transferred to counter-passing fast ions in a specified charge state by Coulomb collisions with background plasma particles.
NAMES.long:
The collisional torque-density vector for counter-passing fast ions in charge state $q$ quantifies the angular-momentum source per unit volume arising from Coulomb collisions with background plasma particles.

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{q,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{q}^{\mathrm{cp}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

Here $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{q,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}_{q}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the angular-momentum density of the counter-passing fast-ion population in charge state $q$, and the subscript indicates the collisional contribution.

The quantity includes only transfer to the specified counter-passing fast-ion charge-state population; it excludes co-passing and thermal-ion populations and noncollisional transfer. It is the counter-passing component of the broader [fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions), while [co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) represents the corresponding co-passing branch.

The vector components are expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive components point along the corresponding positive $R$, $\phi$, or $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_critical_energy
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Threshold energy at which Coulomb drag on a fast ion from thermal electrons equals that from thermal ions, determining the partition of fast-ion power between electron and ion heating channels.
NAMES.long:
The fast-ion critical energy $E_c$ separates two collisional energy-loss regimes for suprathermal ions decelerating in a thermal plasma. Above $E_c$, fast ions lose energy predominantly to thermal electrons via Coulomb drag; below $E_c$, energy is deposited preferentially in the bulk thermal ion population, directly controlling the electron-to-ion power balance in transport modeling.

The critical energy follows from equating the electron and ion frictional forces on the decelerating fast ion:

$$
E_c = T_e \left(\frac{3\sqrt{\pi}}{4}\right)^{2/3} \left(\frac{m_f}{m_e}\right)^{1/3} \left(\sum_i \frac{n_i Z_i^2}{n_e} \frac{m_f}{m_i}\right)^{2/3}
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature, $m_f$ and $m_e$ are the fast-ion and electron masses, $n_i$, $Z_i$, and $m_i$ are the density, charge number, and mass of background ion species $i$, and $n_e$ is the electron density.

The critical energy varies radially through its dependence on local $T_e$ and plasma composition and is computed from kinetic plasma data rather than measured directly. For NBI-injected deuterons at $T_e \approx 3$–$8$ keV, $E_c$ falls in the range 30–150 keV; for fusion alpha particles, it reaches several hundred keV at reactor-relevant temperatures.

This quantity is the ion-specific form of [fast_particle_critical_energy](name:fast_ion_critical_energy), which spans both electron and ion fast-particle populations. The equivalent name with the thermalization mechanism made explicit is [critical_fast_particle_energy_due_to_thermalization](name:fast_ion_critical_energy). The thermal-plasma heating power that accumulates as fast ions slow through $E_c$ is quantified by [thermal_particle_heating_power_due_to_thermalization_of_fast_particles](name:thermal_particle_power_due_to_thermalization).

NAMES.name: fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Torque per unit volume transferred to fast ions by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species, summed over all fast-ion orbit classes and all background species included in the collision model.
NAMES.long:
Torque per unit volume transferred to the fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species, representing the volumetric angular momentum source for suprathermal ions. This quantity aggregates contributions from all fast-ion orbit classes — co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped — and from every background species in the collision model. It is the fast-ion component of the broader [ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The collisional torque density is obtained by weighting the Coulomb collision operator with specific angular momentum and integrating over velocity space:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{fi} = \int m_{fi} (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{v}) \, C_{fi}[f_{fi}, f_{bg}] \, d^3 v
$$

where $m_{fi}$ is the fast-ion mass, $\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{v}$ is the specific angular momentum lever arm, $f_{fi}$ is the fast-ion distribution function, and $C_{fi}$ is the Coulomb collision operator coupling fast ions to background species $f_{bg}$.

This quantity is computed in fast-ion slowing-down and orbit-following models where collisional pitch-angle scattering and velocity-space drag govern thermalization of suprathermal ions. The toroidal projection [toroidal_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) enters directly into toroidal angular momentum balance. Orbit-class resolution is available via [co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions). The companion volumetric energy exchange rate for the same population is [fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net torque acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Collisional torque density for co-passing fast ions is the local rate of angular-momentum transfer per plasma volume caused by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density for co-passing fast ions is the local source density of angular momentum transferred to or from the co-passing fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions. It retains the full torque-density vector rather than selecting a toroidal projection.

The collisional torque-density vector is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{co}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{co}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the angular-momentum density of co-passing fast ions, and $t$ is time.

The quantity aggregates the included background collision partners and defines the co-passing branch of [fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Its toroidal projection is [toroidal co-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), while [trapped fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) represents a distinct orbit class.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a torque-density component increases co-passing fast-ion angular momentum along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Torque per unit volume transferred to counter-passing fast ions by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species, summed over all background species included in the collision model and excluding co-passing and trapped fast-ion orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
Torque per unit volume transferred to the counter-passing fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species, representing the volumetric angular momentum source for that fast-ion orbit class. This quantity retains the full torque-density vector for counter-passing fast ions and sums over every background species included in the collision model. It is the counter-passing orbit-class contribution to the broader [fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), not an aggregate over co-passing or trapped fast ions.

The collisional torque density for counter-passing fast ions is defined by weighting the Coulomb collision operator with particle angular momentum and integrating over the counter-passing part of local fast-ion velocity space:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{fi,cp}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{s \in bg} \int_{\Omega_{cp}(\mathbf{r})} m_{fi} (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{v}) \, C_{fi,s}[f_{fi}, f_s](\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3 v
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{fi,cp}$ is the counter-passing fast-ion collisional torque-density vector, $s$ indexes background species, $\Omega_{cp}(\mathbf{r})$ is the counter-passing part of local fast-ion velocity space at position $\mathbf{r}$, $m_{fi}$ is the fast-ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{fi}$ is the fast-ion distribution function, $f_s$ is the distribution function of background species $s$, and $C_{fi,s}$ is the Coulomb collision operator coupling fast ions to species $s$.

The toroidal component, the projection along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, is [toroidal counter-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions). The sibling orbit-class quantities [co-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [trapped fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) describe disjoint fast-ion populations and are not subcomponents of the counter-passing quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component of the torque-density vector points along the positive direction of the stated projection axis; for the toroidal projection this is the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: fast_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated angular-momentum transfer rate to the fast (non-thermal) particle population through Coulomb collisions with all thermal plasma species, including electrons and all ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
The fast collisional torque is the net angular-momentum transfer rate to the fast (suprathermal) particle population arising from Coulomb collisions with all background thermal plasma species, encompassing both thermal electrons and every thermal ion species and charge state. It is a vector quantity that generalizes over its geometrically resolved projections; the toroidal component is captured by [toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions) and enters the plasma toroidal momentum balance directly. This quantity belongs to the [torque_due_to_collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions) family alongside species-differentiated members such as [fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions) and fast_ion_state_torque_due_to_collisions.

The volume-integrated collisional torque on the fast-particle population is defined as:

$$
\mathbf{T}_\mathrm{fast,coll} = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll,fast}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll,fast}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local angular-momentum source density on the fast-particle distribution due to Coulomb collisions and $V$ is the plasma volume.

The fast-particle distribution function is driven away from thermal equilibrium by suprathermal sources such as neutral beam injection, ion cyclotron resonance heating, and fusion-born alpha particles. Coulomb friction (slowing-down) and pitch-angle scattering terms in the Fokker–Planck collision operator govern the angular-momentum exchange between the fast-particle population and the thermal background, making this torque an essential input to global plasma momentum transport modeling.

NAMES.name: flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion
NAMES.short: Flux due to beam-beam fusion is the volume-integrated rate at which selected fusion products are generated, or selected fusion reaction events occur, in fast-fast reactions between two nonthermal fuel-ion populations.
NAMES.long:
Flux due to beam-beam fusion is the volume-integrated production count rate for a specified counted fusion product or reaction-branch event in reactions where both fuel-ion reactants belong to nonthermal fast-ion distributions. It is a count-rate quantity, not an energy flux and not a vector flux through a surface.

For a specified included branch set $S$, the counted beam-beam contribution is defined by the fast-ion phase-space integral:

$$
\Gamma_{bb}^{(S)} = \int_V \sum_{c \in S} \frac{m_c}{1 + \delta_{a_c b_c}} \iint f_{a_c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v}_1) f_{b_c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v}_2) \sigma_c(v_{\mathrm{rel}}) v_{\mathrm{rel}}\, d^3v_1\, d^3v_2\, dV
$$

where $\Gamma_{bb}^{(S)}$ is the flux due to beam-beam fusion for branch set $S$, $c$ indexes included fusion reaction branches, $a_c$ and $b_c$ are the reacting fuel-ion species in branch $c$, $\delta_{a_c b_c}$ is one for identical reactant species and zero otherwise, $m_c$ is the count multiplier for the selected product or event, $f_{a_c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ and $f_{b_c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ are nonthermal fast-ion distribution functions, $\sigma_c$ is the fusion cross section, $v_{\mathrm{rel}} = |\mathbf{v}_1 - \mathbf{v}_2|$ is the relative speed, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

The branch set $S$ and multiplier $m_c$ define the counting scope: product-specific quantities count the selected emitted products with their branch multiplicity, while reaction-pair quantities count the selected branch events. The [deuterium-deuterium beam-beam fusion flux] and [deuterium-tritium beam-beam fusion flux] restrict the reacting isotope pair, whereas the [neutron flux due to beam-beam fusion](name:neutron_flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion) counts neutron products from beam-beam branches. Reactions with one fast reactant and one bulk reactant, or with only bulk reactants, are outside this fast-fast population scope; the [neutron source rate due to fusion] may aggregate neutron production from multiple fusion population classes.

NAMES.name: flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion
NAMES.short: Global emission rate of fusion reaction products produced by beam-thermal fusion reactions between neutral-beam-injected fast ions and thermal plasma ions. It covers channel-specific and channel-summed beam-thermal product rates.
NAMES.long:
Global emission rate of fusion reaction products produced by beam-thermal fusion reactions between neutral-beam-injected fast ions and thermal plasma ions is the scalar rate at which the counted products are created over the emitting plasma volume. The counted products and included reaction channels are those selected by the specific member of this quantity family.

For a selected set of reaction channels $C$ and counted product set $P$, the rate is defined by the velocity-distribution average of the beam-thermal fusion source:

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{bt}} = \int_V \sum_{c \in C} \nu_{P,c} \int f_{b,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v}_b) f_{t,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v}_t) \sigma_c(v_{\mathrm{rel}}) v_{\mathrm{rel}} \, d^3v_b \, d^3v_t \, dV
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{bt}}$ is the global emission rate in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $V$ is the emitting plasma volume, $C$ is the selected set of fusion reaction channels, $\nu_{P,c}$ is the dimensionless number of counted products in $P$ produced per reaction in channel $c$, $f_{b,c}$ and $f_{t,c}$ are the fast beam-ion and thermal ion velocity distribution functions for the two reactants in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}(\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1})^{-3}$, $\sigma_c$ is the reaction cross-section in $\mathrm{m}^2$, and $v_{\mathrm{rel}} = |\mathbf{v}_b - \mathbf{v}_t|$ is the relative speed in $\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. This expression may equivalently be represented by a beam-thermal reactivity average over the two reactant distributions; it is not limited to a cold-target approximation.

For a channel-specific quantity, $C$ contains only the named reaction channel; for a channel-summed quantity, $C$ contains the included beam-thermal channels. This quantity excludes thermal-thermal fusion, represented by [source rate due to thermal fusion](name:source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion), and beam-beam fusion; when the counted products are neutrons it contributes to [total neutron flux due to fusion](name:total_neutron_flux_due_to_fusion). The word flux denotes an integral source or emission rate, not a signed surface-normal transport flux.

NAMES.name: flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: Pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic contribution to momentum-flux density across an oriented surface, with species, charge state, momentum component, and projection unspecified.
NAMES.long:
Flux due to diamagnetic drift is the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic contribution to momentum-flux density across an oriented reference surface. It is a scalar contraction of the diamagnetic part of the momentum-flux tensor, leaving the species, charge state, transported momentum component, and surface projection unspecified.

For a selected momentum-component direction and positive surface normal, the scalar flux is defined by the tensor contraction:

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{dia}}^{(m)} = \hat{\mathbf{e}}_m \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{dia}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to the momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_m$ selects the transported momentum component, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen positive normal to the reference surface.

The diamagnetic contribution is associated with the species pressure-gradient drift; for isotropic species pressure its drift velocity is $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia}} = \mathbf{B}\times\nabla p/(q n B^2)$, where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic drift velocity, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $p$ is species pressure, $q$ is species charge, $n$ is species number density, and $B=|\mathbf{B}|$. This parent is restricted to flux density of momentum: it is not a [momentum source due to diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and [diamagnetic momentum diffusivity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity) denotes a related transport coefficient rather than a flux. [Momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the direct momentum-flux specialization; [radial ion momentum flux at flux surface due to diamagnetic drift](name:radial_ion_momentum_flux_at_flux_surface_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) fixes the species to ions summed over charge states, evaluates the quantity at a magnetic flux surface, and fixes the transported momentum component to $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the diamagnetic-drift contribution transports the selected momentum component through the reference surface in its chosen positive normal direction.

NAMES.name: flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short: Flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor, or vector of factors, that scales a collisionless free-streaming bound on a flux density while preserving the direction or sign of each resolved flux component.
NAMES.long:
Flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor, or vector of factors, that scales a collisionless free-streaming upper bound on a flux density in a transport closure. It limits the magnitude permitted by that bound while preserving the direction or sign assigned to each resolved flux component by the underlying closure.

For a resolved flux-density component indexed by $i$, a direction-preserving limited flux can be expressed as:

$$
F_i = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_i F_i^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $F_i$ is the limited flux-density component, $F_i^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the unconstrained closure value, $F_i^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming bound, and $L_i$ is the flux limiter coefficient for that component. The limiting range is typically $0 \le L_i \le 1$, with smaller values imposing a stricter cap.

This parent quantity does not specify the transported quantity, resolved component, or spatial region. It covers both generic region-scoped flux limiting, such as the [edge-region flux limiter coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region), and quantity-specific limiting, such as the [momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient); child names identify any additional component or region semantics.

NAMES.name: gyrocenter_frequency
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Angular velocity vector of a charged-particle gyrocenter orbit in a magnetized plasma, with toroidal and poloidal components giving the rates of gyrocenter advance in their respective angular coordinates.
NAMES.long:
The gyrocenter frequency vector characterizes how rapidly a charged particle's guiding center advances angularly in the confining magnetic geometry, after averaging over the fast cyclotron gyration to isolate the slower drift and bounce or transit dynamics relevant to transport and stability.

The vector decomposes into two principal angular components. The [toroidal gyrocenter frequency](name:toroidal_gyrocenter_frequency) $\dot{\phi}_{gc} = d\phi_{gc}/dt$ is the rate of change of the gyrocenter toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major radius and $Z$ is the vertical height. The [poloidal gyrocenter frequency](name:poloidal_gyrocenter_frequency) $\dot{\theta}_{gc} = d\theta_{gc}/dt$ is the rate of advance in poloidal angle $\theta$ as measured in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ is a radial flux-surface label. The two components have qualitatively different characters: passing particles circulate continuously in the poloidal direction, while trapped particles bounce and primarily precess toroidally.

These frequencies are computed in gyrokinetic codes from the guiding-center orbit equations derived from the gyrocenter Hamiltonian, and may be averaged over the particle distribution function to yield population-representative angular velocities. They enter directly into the calculation of resonance conditions for wave-particle interactions and neoclassical transport coefficients.
NAMES.sign: Positive toroidal component when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$; positive poloidal component when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Particle number density of helium-3 ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over all helium-3 ion charge states and excluding neutral helium-3.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of helium-3 ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the helium-3-ion population at that flux-surface location. Helium-3 (${}^3\mathrm{He}$, mass number $A = 3$, atomic number $Z = 2$) has a nucleus with two protons and one neutron; at species level this quantity includes singly ionized ${}^3\mathrm{He}^{+}$ and fully ionized ${}^3\mathrm{He}^{2+}$ and excludes neutral ${}^3\mathrm{He}$ atoms.

The charge-state-summed particle number density is defined by

$$
n_{{}^3\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ITB}} = \left.\lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N_{{}^3\mathrm{He}^{+}} + \Delta N_{{}^3\mathrm{He}^{2+}}}{\Delta V}\right|_{\mathrm{ITB}}
$$

where $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density at the internal-transport-barrier reference flux surface, $\Delta N_{{}^3\mathrm{He}^{+}}$ and $\Delta N_{{}^3\mathrm{He}^{2+}}$ are the counted singly ionized and fully ionized helium-3 ions in the volume element $\Delta V$, and the vertical bar denotes evaluation at that assigned flux surface.

This is a particle number density, not a charge-weighted density; both ionization stages contribute one counted ion per particle. It is the internal-transport-barrier evaluation of [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density) and the helium-3-specific member of [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier), distinct from broader ion aggregates such as [ion density at the internal transport barrier](name:ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and from isotope counterparts such as [helium-4 density at the internal transport barrier](name:helium_4_density_at_internal_transport_barrier). The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density gradients.

NAMES.name: helium_3_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Particle number density of the helium-3 ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis, summed over all helium-3 ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the helium-3 ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local helium-3 ion count per physical volume at the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces, summed over all helium-3 ionic charge states. The magnetic axis is the locus where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes.

The on-axis density is defined by the limiting value of the local helium-3 ion density field:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He3}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}} \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He3},q}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He3},q}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density of helium-3 ions in charge state $q$, $q=1,2$ denotes the ionic charge state, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position.

This isotope-specific quantity is a specialization of [density at magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis), excludes neutral helium-3, and is distinct from the charge-state-summed local [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density).

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Particle number density of helium-4 ions at the internal transport barrier, the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep radial helium-4 density gradients to form.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of helium-4 ions at the internal transport barrier is the local, isotope-resolved helium-ion density on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. Helium-4 ($^4\mathrm{He}$, mass number $A = 4$) is the stable alpha-particle product of deuterium-tritium fusion and may also be present from helium fueling or wall recycling. The internal transport barrier is a confined-plasma flux-surface region where locally reduced cross-field transport permits steep radial gradients to form.

The local density is the charge-state-summed zeroth velocity moment evaluated at the ITB reference radius:

$$
n_{{}^4\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ITB}} = \sum_{q>0} \int f_{{}^4\mathrm{He}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v}, \rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm,ITB}})\, d^3v
$$

where $q$ indexes positive ion charge states, $f_{{}^4\mathrm{He}^{q+}}$ is the phase-space distribution function of helium-4 ions with charge state $q+$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, the integral is over velocity space, and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm,ITB}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux radius of the ITB reference flux surface.

Unless a charge state is specified separately, this species-level density is summed over all helium-4 ion charge states and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms; in hot core plasma the ionic population is commonly dominated by fully stripped $\mathrm{He}^{2+}$. This is the helium-4 member of [density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and a species-specific instance of [ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier); it is distinct from [helium_3_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:helium_3_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) by isotope mass and from [electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) by particle species.

NAMES.name: helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Particle number density of the helium-4 ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis, summed over all helium-4 ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of the helium-4 ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local helium-4 ion count per physical volume at the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces, summed over all helium-4 ionic charge states. The magnetic axis is the locus where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes.

The on-axis density is defined by the limiting value of the local helium-4 ion density field:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}} \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He4},q}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4},q}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density of helium-4 ions in charge state $q$, $q=1,2$ denotes the ionic charge state, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position.

This isotope-specific quantity is a specialization of [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis) and excludes neutral helium. It is distinct from the corresponding [helium_3_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:helium_3_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies to the helium-3 isotope.

NAMES.name: helium_confinement_time
NAMES.subject: helium
NAMES.short: Characteristic e-folding time for the loss of confined thermalized helium-4 ash ions when their outward loss rate is proportional to the confined inventory.
NAMES.long:
The global particle confinement time of thermalized helium-4 ash is the characteristic retention timescale for fully ionized helium-4 ions in the confined plasma. It describes particle loss from the total confined inventory, rather than the confinement of thermal energy or the survival of the plasma as a whole.

For source-free decay, the confinement time is defined by

$$
\frac{dN_{\mathrm{He}}}{dt}=-\frac{N_{\mathrm{He}}}{\tau_{\mathrm{p,He}}}, \qquad \tau_{\mathrm{p,He}}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{He}}}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{He,loss}}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{He}}$ is the total confined helium-4 ion inventory, $t$ is time, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{He,loss}}$ is the corresponding outward particle-loss rate. The definition assumes loss proportional to inventory and excludes helium sources during the decay interval. It is distinct from [energy confinement time](name:energy_confinement_time) and [plasma confinement time](name:plasma_confinement_time).

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Local number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma, giving the count of H+ particles per unit volume at a specified spatial position.
NAMES.long:
The hydrogen density quantifies the local concentration of protium ions ($^1$H$^+$, the lightest hydrogen isotope with mass number $A = 1$) at a point in the plasma. It is distinct from the neutral atomic hydrogen density and from the number densities of heavier hydrogenic isotopes such as deuterium ($^2$H) and tritium ($^3$H).

The number density $n_H$ at position $\mathbf{r}$ is defined as

$$
n_H(\mathbf{r}) = \frac{dN_H}{dV}
$$

where $N_H$ is the number of hydrogen ions within the infinitesimal volume element $dV$ centered at $\mathbf{r}$.

Spatially averaged forms provide experimentally accessible measures of the same quantity: [line_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density) gives the path-length-normalized ion count along a spectroscopic or interferometric chord, while [volume_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density) integrates the ion content over the full plasma volume. The isotopic composition of the hydrogenic fuel is tracked by [ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_total_hydrogenic_density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density), which expresses $n_H$ relative to the combined protium, deuterium, and tritium ion density. The aggregate over all three hydrogen isotopes is given by hydrogenic_density, and the full multi-species ion sum by [total_ion_density](name:total_ion_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when hydrogen ions are present at the specified location.

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Particle number density of hydrogen ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over all protium ion charge states and excluding neutral hydrogen. Hydrogen denotes protium, mass number 1; the barrier is where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport can sustain steep fuel-density gradients.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of hydrogen ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the hydrogen-ion population at that flux-surface location. Here hydrogen denotes protium, $^1\mathrm{H}$, with mass number $A = 1$, distinct from deuterium and tritium fuel isotopes.

The species-level hydrogen density is the charge-state sum

$$
n_\mathrm{H} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_\mathrm{H}} n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_\mathrm{H}$ is the hydrogen-ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}}$ is the density of protium ions with charge state $q$, and $Z_\mathrm{H}=1$ is the hydrogen atomic number. The neutral population $q=0$ is excluded.

This quantity is the hydrogen isotope instance of [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and an ion-species contribution to [ion density at the internal transport barrier](name:ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), without charge weighting. It is distinct from [deuterium density at the internal transport barrier](name:deuterium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and from the combined [deuterium-tritium density at the internal transport barrier](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier). The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep fuel-density gradients.

NAMES.name: hydrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Particle number density of hydrogen ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, summed over all hydrogen ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of hydrogen ions evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local particle count per physical volume at the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces. The magnetic axis is the locus where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes, so this quantity is the central value of the hydrogen-ion density field.

The on-axis density is defined by the limiting value of the local hydrogen-ion density field:

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}} n_{\mathrm{H}}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the hydrogen-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position.

The hydrogen population denotes protium ions, with density summed over all hydrogen ionic charge states and excluding neutral hydrogen. This is the hydrogen-specific realization of [density at magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis) and follows the same aggregation convention as [ion density at magnetic axis](name:ion_density_at_magnetic_axis); it is a local density, not an integrated particle inventory.

NAMES.name: ion_atomic_mass
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Atomic mass of an ion species, identifying its isotope and setting the inertial mass scale for collisional and transport calculations.
NAMES.long:
Ion atomic mass is the rest-mass scale assigned to a specified ion species, determined by its isotope and elemental or molecular composition. It characterizes the inertia of the ionic constituent used in collisional, momentum, gyroradius, and transport relations.

The numerical atomic mass is represented by

$$
m_s = A_s\,u
$$

where $m_s$ is the mass of ion species $s$, $A_s$ is its dimensionless numerical atomic mass, and $u$ is the unified atomic mass unit, defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a neutral carbon-12 atom.

This ion-specific quantity is the ionic member of the broader [atomic mass](name:atomic_mass) concept and is distinct from the [neutral species atomic mass](name:neutral_species_atomic_mass). It is also distinct from [ion mass number](name:ion_mass_number), which is the integer count of nucleons rather than the measured atomic-mass value.

NAMES.name: ion_atomic_number
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Nuclear charge number of the ion species, equal to the number of protons in the nucleus, serving as its invariant elemental identifier independent of ionization state.
NAMES.long:
The ion atomic number $Z_n$ is the number of protons in the nucleus of the ion species, an intrinsic nuclear property that is independent of ionization state and uniquely identifies the element. In fusion-relevant plasmas, common values include $Z_n = 1$ for hydrogen isotopes (deuterium, tritium), $Z_n = 2$ for helium, $Z_n = 6$ for carbon, $Z_n = 18$ for argon, and $Z_n = 74$ for tungsten.

The maximum realizable ionization charge for a fully stripped ion equals $Z_n$, making it the natural upper bound for ion_charge. The effective plasma charge $Z_\mathrm{eff} = \sum_i n_i Z_i^2 / n_e$, where $n_i$ is the number density of ion species $i$, $Z_i$ is its ionization charge state, and $n_e$ is the electron density, depends directly on $Z_n$ for fully ionized impurities.

As a fixed nuclear property, $Z_n$ is an invariant input to plasma transport modeling rather than a plasma-measurable quantity. Unlike ion_charge, which reflects the realized ionization state and varies with local temperature and density, $Z_n$ is immutable for a given element. The companion quantity [ion_atomic_mass](name:ion_atomic_mass) provides the nuclear mass, while [atomic_number](name:ion_atomic_number) covers the same concept without restricting to the ion population.
NAMES.sign: Positive for all physical ion species, as $Z_n$ counts nuclear proton number and is never negative.

NAMES.name: ion_charge
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ionic charge number, equal to an ion’s net charge in elementary-charge units, with averaging specified by the quantity’s scope.
NAMES.long:
An ionic charge number identifies the net electric charge of an ion relative to its neutral atomic state. It describes a resolved ionization state directly and provides the underlying quantity for population- or volume-averaged charge measures.

The defining relation is

$$
Z = \frac{q}{e}
$$

where $Z$ is the charge number, $q$ is the net ionic charge, and $e$ is the elementary charge. A resolved ionization state has an integer $Z$; an averaged value may be noninteger.

The species scope, averaging measure, and contributing charge states are specified by each specialization. The population-level form [average charge number](name:average_charge_number) and the volume-averaged form [volume-averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge) use this same charge-number definition. This quantity is distinct from ion number density and total electric charge.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_average_charge_number
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Density-weighted mean ionic charge number for a grouped population of charge states, expressing its effective ionization level.
NAMES.long:
The mean charge number represents the effective ionization level of a grouped population of ion charge states. It is distinct from the upper-bound charge number, which identifies only the highest included state.

For charge states indexed by $z$, the mean charge number is defined by

$$
\overline{Z} = \frac{\sum_z n_z Z_z}{\sum_z n_z}
$$

where $n_z$ is the number density of charge state $z$, and $Z_z$ is its ionic charge number as defined by [ion charge](name:ion_charge). This is the charge-state average represented by [average charge number](name:average_charge_number). The charge-state sum is restricted to the defined ion bundle. Spatially aggregated instances, such as [volume-averaged ion charge-state average charge number](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number), apply the specified spatial averaging to this local charge-state mean.

sources.enhanced_context: Concentration-weighted mean charge number (⟨Z⟩) of an ion charge-state bundle, volume-averaged over the plasma radius. Computed as Σ(Z·x_z) over all charge states within the bundle; scalar complement to the radial profile z_average_1d.
sources.leaf_definition: Average Z of the charge state bundle, volume averaged over the plasma radius (equal to z_min if no bundle), = sum (Z*x_z) where x_z is the relative concentration of a given charge state in the bundle, i.e. sum(x_z) = 1 over the bundle.
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Local number density of ions in a specified charge state, aggregating contributions from all ion populations — both thermal and fast (non-thermal) — without restriction on the velocity distribution.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state number density is the count of ions per unit volume carrying a specified charge state $Z$, regardless of whether those ions belong to the thermal (Maxwellian) or fast (non-thermal) population. It is defined by integrating the full ion velocity distribution function over all velocities:

$$
n_{i,Z} = \int f_{i,Z}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $f_{i,Z}(\mathbf{v})$ is the ion velocity distribution function for charge state $Z$.

Unlike [fast_ion_charge_state_density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density), which restricts the count to suprathermal ions in a given charge state, this quantity sums over the entire ion population — thermal and suprathermal — in that charge state. Summing over all charge states of a species recovers the total species number density; the related quantity [ion_density](name:ion_density) performs that sum. The charge-state-summed fast-ion analog is [fast_ion_density](name:fast_ion_density).

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Number density of fast, non-thermal ions carrying a specified ionic charge state, excluding thermal ions and other charge states.
NAMES.long:
The fast-ion charge-state density counts fast, non-thermal ions of a selected species and ionic charge state at a plasma location. It resolves the fast population by charge state rather than aggregating all fast ions.

$$
n_{\mathrm{fast},Z}(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{3}} f_{\mathrm{fast},Z}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^{3}\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{fast},Z}$ is the number density, $f_{\mathrm{fast},Z}$ is the fast-ion velocity distribution for charge state $Z$, $\mathbf{r}$ is the spatial position, and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity.

This quantity excludes thermal ions and does not sum over other charge states. The charge-state-summed counterpart is [fast-ion density](name:fast_ion_density), while the all-population quantity is [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Effective Fickian coefficient for particle transport by ions in a specified charge state, relating diffusive flux to that charge state’s density gradient without selecting a spatial direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective Fickian particle diffusion coefficient for ions in a specified charge state. It describes transport of that charge-state population without summing over ion charge states or selecting a spatial projection.

The diffusive particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,q}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,q}\nabla n_{i,q}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,q}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle flux of ion charge state $q$, $D_{i,q}$ is this diffusion coefficient, and $n_{i,q}$ is the number density of that charge state.

The [radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) and [poloidal ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) are directional forms of this quantity. The charge-state-specific scope distinguishes it from the [electron diffusion coefficient](name:electron_diffusion_coefficient), which describes electron particle transport.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state, without specifying a spatial projection.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state, without specifying a spatial projection. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the diffusive particle flux component of that charge state to the negative directional gradient of its number density.

For a chosen projection direction $\hat{\mathbf{e}}$, the defining Fickian relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,e} = -D_s\,\nabla_e n_s
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,e}$ is the projected diffusive particle flux density of charge state $s$, $D_s$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of charge state $s$, and $\nabla_e n_s = \hat{\mathbf{e}}\cdot\nabla n_s$ is the directional derivative of that number density. A positive flux component is directed along $+\hat{\mathbf{e}}$; the minus sign makes a positive diffusivity drive diffusive flux opposite to the projected density gradient.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved: it applies to a single ionization state rather than to the density-weighted mean over all charge states represented by [ion diffusivity](name:ion_diffusivity). It is the same physical coefficient as [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) when that name is used for the same Fickian closure. Directionally specified counterparts include [radial ion charge-state diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity) and [parallel ion charge-state diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_diffusivity); convective or pinch transport, particle sources and sinks, and energy or momentum transport coefficients are separate quantities.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Fickian diffusivity for thermal-energy transport of a specified ion charge state, defined so its diffusive energy flux is proportional to and opposite the gradient of that state’s thermal-energy density.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of the thermal-energy density of one specified ionization stage. It represents the Fickian part of that stage’s thermal-energy transport, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources, and is the charge-state-specific form of [energy diffusivity](name:energy_diffusivity).

The defining closure is

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,z} = -\chi_{E,z}\nabla w_z
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,z}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux density of ionization stage $z$, $\chi_{E,z}$ is its energy diffusivity, $w_z$ is its thermal-energy density, and $\nabla w_z$ is the spatial gradient of that density. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over ion species or charge states, unlike [ion energy diffusivity](name:ion_energy_diffusivity). Directional instances apply the same closure to selected components, including [parallel ion charge-state energy diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity) and [poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity). A temperature-gradient form is equivalent only when the relevant density and heat-capacity factors are explicitly included in the coefficient.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Ion charge-state energy flux is the signed power-per-area contribution carried across an oriented surface by ions in one specified ionization charge state.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state energy flux is the signed component of ion charge-state energy-flux density normal to an oriented surface. It gives the rate at which energy carried by ions in one specified ionization charge state crosses the surface per unit area, including convective and conductive contributions when those channels are in scope.

For an oriented surface with unit normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, the energy flux $F_{E,k}$ is defined by

$$
F_{E,k} = \mathbf{q}_{E,k} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,k}$ is the energy-flux-density vector carried by ions in charge state $k$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ defines the positive crossing direction.

This quantity is resolved for one ionization charge state and is not summed over charge states. It is the charge-state-specific form of [energy flux](name:energy_flux), distinct from [ion charge-state particle flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux), which describes number transport, and from [parallel ion charge-state energy flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux), which restricts the projection to the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion charge-state energy-flux density has a component in the direction of the chosen unit normal to the oriented surface.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_number_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Number density of ions of a specified species and ionic charge state, with the included ion population defined by each specialization.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the number density of ions selected by both species and ionic charge state. It is resolved by charge state rather than summed over the charge states of a species.

$$
n_{s,q} = \frac{N_{s,q}}{V}
$$

where $n_{s,q}$ is the number density for species $s$ and charge state $q$, $N_{s,q}$ is the corresponding number of ions, and $V$ is the volume defining the population sample.

The population qualifier determines which ions are included. For example, [thermal ion charge-state number density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density) restricts the population to Maxwellian thermal ions and excludes fast and suprathermal ions, whereas [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) aggregates contributions from all ion populations.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Ion charge-state pressure at a plasma location is the isotropic scalar kinetic pressure of ions in a specified charge state, including contributions from the full velocity distribution with both thermal and non-thermal populations.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state pressure at a plasma location is the isotropic scalar kinetic pressure of ions of a specified parent ion species in a specified charge state. It is the trace part of the kinetic pressure tensor for that charge-state distribution and includes all particles in that charge state, including thermal and non-thermal populations.

For parent ion species $i$ and charge state $q$, the scalar pressure is the second central velocity moment of the charge-state distribution:

$$
p_{i,q} = \frac{m_i}{3}\int \left|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{i,q}\right|^2 f_{i,q}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_i$ is the mass of the parent ion species, common to its charge states; $f_{i,q}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity-space distribution function of species $i$ in charge state $q$; and $\mathbf{u}_{i,q}$ is the mean flow velocity of that charge-state population.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved. The corresponding species-level [ion pressure](name:ion_pressure) is summed over all charge states of the parent ion species, while [thermal ion pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure) restricts the population scope to thermal ions.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Fast-ion charge-state pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic pressure of suprathermal ions in a specified ionization state, formed from velocity fluctuations about that population's mean flow. It is represented by the parallel and perpendicular pressure components relative to the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion charge-state pressure is the gyrotropic kinetic pressure of suprathermal ions for a specified ion species and ionization state, formed from velocity fluctuations about that population's mean flow. It is represented by the pair of pressure components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction; this pair parameterizes a gyrotropic pressure tensor and is not a spatial vector.

The component pair is defined from the fast-ion distribution function by the velocity-fluctuation moments:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
p_{\parallel,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}} \\
p_{\perp,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}
\end{pmatrix}
=
m_s \int f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})
\begin{pmatrix}
[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\mathbf{b}]^2 \\
\frac{1}{2}\left|(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})-[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}})\cdot\mathbf{b}]\mathbf{b}\right|^2
\end{pmatrix}
\, d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ and $p_{\perp,s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ are the pressure components for species $s$ in ionization state $q$, $m_s$ is the ion mass for species $s$, $f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal part of the distribution function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the mean flow velocity of the same population, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and the integral is over velocity space.

The scope is gyrotropic pressure: the two transverse directions perpendicular to $\mathbf{b}$ are averaged, so the perpendicular component is one half of the transverse fluctuation moment. A fully non-gyrotropic pressure tensor with unequal transverse components or off-diagonal terms is outside this standard name. Because pressure is an extensive per-volume velocity moment, aggregate [parallel fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure) and [perpendicular fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure) are obtained by summing the corresponding components over all fast-ion species and ionization states.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Angular velocity vector of a specified ion charge state, characterizing its bulk rotational motion; each resolved component is determined from the corresponding bulk-flow component and its geometric rotation lever arm.
NAMES.long:
Angular velocity vector of a specified ion charge state is the vector of angular rates associated with the bulk flow of that charge-state population. It is charge-state-resolved and excludes density-weighted averaging over other charge states.

For any resolved angular coordinate $q$, the component is the corresponding bulk-flow velocity component divided by the geometric rotation lever arm for that coordinate:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,\zeta} = \sum_{q\in\mathcal{A}} \Omega^{q}_{i,\zeta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}, \qquad \Omega^{q}_{i,\zeta} = \frac{\mathbf{v}_{i,\zeta}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}}{h_q}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,\zeta}$ is the ion-charge-state rotation-frequency vector, $i$ labels the ion species, $\zeta$ labels the charge state, $\mathcal{A}$ is the set of resolved angular coordinate directions, $\mathbf{v}_{i,\zeta}$ is the bulk velocity vector of the same charge-state population, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}$ is the positive tangent direction of angular coordinate $q$, and $h_q=|\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial q|$ is its geometric rotation lever arm. For the toroidal component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, $q=\phi$ and $h_\phi=R$, so the component is the [toroidal ion-charge-state rotation frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency).

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved counterpart of [ion rotation frequency](name:ion_rotation_frequency). The charge-state-aggregated ion quantity is the density-weighted mean over charge states, not a sum, because rotation frequency is an intensive bulk-flow quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component corresponds to motion in the positive tangent direction of its associated angular coordinate; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the toroidal component is positive for motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Energy-equivalent kinetic temperature of ions occupying one specified charge state, calculated from their random motion after subtracting the charge-state bulk flow.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the scalar kinetic temperature of ions in a specified charge state, representing their random thermal energy rather than ordered flow energy.

For an isotropic or trace-equivalent temperature, the defining relation is:

$$
T_{i,s} = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle \frac{1}{2}m_i\left|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{i,s}\right|^2 \right\rangle_{i,s}
$$

where $T_{i,s}$ is the energy-equivalent temperature, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is an individual ion velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{i,s}$ is the mean bulk velocity of species $i$ in charge state $s$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{i,s}$ denotes an average over that charge-state population.

The charge-state resolution distinguishes this quantity from the population-level [ion temperature](name:ion_temperature), which may combine multiple ion species or charge states. Only random motion relative to the charge-state bulk velocity contributes.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_torque_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for a specified ion species and ionization state, retaining the complete torque-vector direction.
NAMES.long:
Torque density for a specified ion species and ionization state is the net angular-momentum transfer rate to that charge-state population per unit volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a toroidal component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,q} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{i,q}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,q}$ is the torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{L}_{i,q}$ is the angular momentum of ion species $i$ in charge state $q$, $\Delta V$ is a volume element, and $t$ is time.

Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, the quantity is the net sum of all applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions. The [toroidal ion charge-state torque density](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density) is its major-radius-weighted toroidal projection, while [thermal ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) restricts the transfer mechanism to collisions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when each resolved component points along the corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Mean bulk-flow velocity vector of ions belonging to one specified ionization charge state, obtained from the first velocity moment of that charge-state population.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state velocity is the mean translational velocity of ions in a specified ionization charge state. It describes the charge-state-resolved bulk flow and is distinct from the charge-state-averaged [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity).

Let $f_Z(\mathbf{v})$ be the velocity distribution function for ions in charge state $Z$, and let $n_Z$ be their number density. The velocity is defined by

$$
\mathbf{u}_Z = \frac{1}{n_Z}\int \mathbf{v}\,f_Z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}, \qquad n_Z = \int f_Z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_Z$ is the charge-state bulk velocity and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity. The vector may be resolved into directional projections, including the [radial ion charge-state velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity), without summing or averaging over other ionization states.
NAMES.sign: Positive components point along the corresponding positive directions of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local number density of ions at a plasma point is the particle number density of a specified ion species, charge state, or population; a species-level quantity without an explicit charge state is summed over all charge states. It is not electric charge density or mass density.
NAMES.long:
Local number density of ions at a plasma point is the particle number density of the specified ion species, charge state, or population. It counts ions as particles and is distinct from electric charge density and mass density. For a species-level quantity without an explicit charge state, the density is summed over all charge states of that species represented in the same population scope.

The local differential definition is:

$$
n_i = \frac{dN_i}{dV}
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $N_i$ is the number of ions in the specified population, and $V$ is physical volume.

For species $s$, the charge-state-summed convention is $n_{i,s} = \sum_Z n_{i,s,Z}$, where $n_{i,s,Z}$ is the ion number density of charge state $Z$ within the same species and population scope. A charge-state-resolved counterpart fixes $Z$ instead of applying this sum; [ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density) denotes such a quantity at its own stated population scope. Population-qualified forms restrict the same density concept, such as [thermal ion density](name:thermal_ion_density) for thermal ions and [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density) for suprathermal ions, while [total ion density](name:total_ion_density) aggregates over ion species and [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) is a spatial average of the local density.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local number density of fast, non-thermal ions of a specified species at a plasma point, summed over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Fast ion density is the local count of suprathermal, non-thermal ions of a specified species per unit volume at a plasma point. It is a population- and species-resolved specialization of [ion_density](name:ion_density), including fast ions while excluding the thermal ion population.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{fast},s} = \sum_Z n_{i,\mathrm{fast},s,Z}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the fast-ion number density for species $s$, $n_{i,\mathrm{fast},s,Z}$ is the corresponding density at charge state $Z$, and each density is expressed in m$^{-3}$. The sum includes all ionic charge states of the specified species.

This quantity differs from [fast_ion_charge_state_density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density), which resolves the fast population by charge state, and from [ion_charge_state_density](name:ion_charge_state_density), which includes both thermal and fast ions at a specified charge state.
