NAMES.name: ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Particle number density of an ion population evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, excluding neutrals and without charge weighting.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of an ion population evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the included ions. The population may be a specific ion species or an aggregate of ion populations; neutral particles are excluded, and ionic charge does not weight the count.

The number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{ion}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N_{\mathrm{ion}}}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $\Delta N_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the number of included ions, and $\Delta V$ is the enclosing volume in m$^{3}$. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density gradients. The broader population-dependent family is defined by [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier), while [total ion density at the internal transport barrier](name:total_ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) is the aggregate over the included ion populations.

NAMES.name: ion_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local particle number density of a specified ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis, with species and charge-state aggregation defined by that ion population; electron and neutral populations are excluded.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density at the magnetic axis is the local number of ions belonging to a specified ion population per physical volume at that location. The ion population may be the aggregate over all ions, a named ion species, an isotope mixture treated as an ion population, or another explicitly defined ionic subset. The magnetic axis is the innermost degenerate closed flux surface of the confined plasma, where the gradient of [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) vanishes.

The defining relation is the limiting local number density of the selected ion population at the magnetic-axis location:

$$
n_{\mathcal{I}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}} n_{\mathcal{I}}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_{\mathcal{I}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the particle number-density field of ion population $\mathcal{I}$ and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position.

This ion-scoped parent does not include electron or neutral populations and does not by itself choose a chemical species, isotope mixture, or aggregate. For a species-level ion density, the per-volume amount is summed over all ionic charge states unless the quantity is explicitly charge-state-resolved; for [total ion density at the magnetic axis](name:total_ion_density_at_magnetic_axis), the selected population is all ion species and charge states. Evaluation at the magnetic axis specifies the locus only and does not imply that the density has an extremum there.

NAMES.name: ion_diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Fickian coefficient for flux-surface-normal redistribution of ion momentum caused by diamagnetic drift, with ion momentum summed over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Diamagnetic ion momentum diffusivity is the Fickian coefficient for the diamagnetic-drift contribution to cross-field redistribution of ion momentum. It applies to the ion population with momentum density aggregated over all ionic charge states, rather than to one selected charge state.

The defining flux-surface-normal closure is

$$
\Gamma_{i,n}^{\mathrm{dia}} = -D_i^{\mathrm{dia}}\frac{\partial \Pi_i}{\partial n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,n}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to the ion momentum flux normal to a magnetic flux surface, $D_i^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this diffusivity, $\Pi_i$ is the charge-state-summed ion momentum density, and $n$ denotes the flux-surface-normal coordinate.

This quantity isolates pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport and excludes collisional viscosity, turbulent mixing, and charge-exchange transport unless they are explicitly included in the defined flux. It is the ion-specific component of [diamagnetic momentum diffusivity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity) and differs from [ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which resolves the ion momentum transport by charge state.

NAMES.name: ion_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective Fickian diffusivity for total-ion particle transport, relating a diffusive flux component to the opposing spatial gradient of charge-state-summed ion number density.
NAMES.long:
The effective ion diffusivity is the coefficient in a Fickian closure for diffusive transport of the total ion population. The total ion population is summed over all ionic charge states; neutral particles and charge-state-resolved transport coefficients are excluded.

For a selected spatial direction $a$, the defining relation is

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(a)} = -D_i^{\mathrm{eff},(a)}\nabla_a n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(a)}$ is the diffusive particle-flux component, $D_i^{\mathrm{eff},(a)}$ is the effective diffusivity, $\nabla_a n_i$ is the physical gradient component of total ion number density in direction $a$, and $n_i$ is that charge-state-summed density. The minus sign specifies transport down the density gradient.

The [radial ion diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient) and [poloidal ion diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_diffusion_coefficient) are directional instances of this parent quantity. Unlike [ion charge-state diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity), this quantity aggregates all ionization states.

NAMES.name: ion_energy
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated energy content associated with an ion population, with qualifying terms specifying the included energy component and population scope.
NAMES.long:
Ion energy is the extensive energy content attributed to a specified ion population. The physical energy component, such as random thermal kinetic energy, is determined by the qualifying terms rather than by this parent name.

For a volume-integrated instance, the defining relation is

$$
E_{\rm ion} = \int_V u_{\rm ion}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $E_{\rm ion}$ is the integrated ion energy, $u_{\rm ion}(\mathbf{r})$ is the corresponding local ion energy density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V$ is the integration volume, and $dV$ is its volume element. The integrated quantity is distinct from [ion kinetic energy density](name:ion_kinetic_energy_density). The representative [thermal ion energy](name:thermal_ion_energy) specializes this parent to random thermal ion motion and excludes nonthermal fast-ion energy.

NAMES.name: ion_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Fickian diffusivity for thermal-energy transport of the ion population, defining the down-gradient part of ion energy flux across or along magnetic field lines.
NAMES.long:
Ion energy diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of ion thermal-energy density. It represents the Fickian part of ion energy transport, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources or sinks.

The defining closure relates the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux to the energy-density gradient:

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,i} = -\chi_{E,i}\nabla w_i
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$ is the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux, $\chi_{E,i}$ is ion energy diffusivity, and $w_i$ is ion thermal-energy density. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport. For an unresolved ion mixture, $w_i$ and the associated flux are summed over the included ion species and charge states; species-resolved quantities such as [ion charge-state energy diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity) retain that resolution. Directional forms include [poloidal ion energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusivity) and [parallel ion energy diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusivity), while [energy diffusivity](name:energy_diffusivity) provides the broader constituent-independent concept.

NAMES.name: ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion energy flux is the signed component of ion energy-flux density normal to an oriented surface, including convective and conductive transport when those channels are in scope.
NAMES.long:
Ion energy flux is the signed component of ion energy-flux density normal to an oriented surface. It gives the rate at which energy carried by a specified ion population crosses the surface per unit area, including convective, conductive, or other channels only when they belong to the stated ion-energy reservoir.

For an oriented surface with chosen unit normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, the scalar ion energy flux $F_{E,i}$ is the normal projection of the ion energy-flux-density vector $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$:

$$
F_{E,i} = \mathbf{q}_{E,i} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$ is the vector density of energy transport for the selected ion population and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ defines the positive normal direction.

Ion energy flux is a species- and charge-state-resolved or aggregated specialization of [energy flux](name:energy_flux). [Total ion energy flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux) aggregates all ion species and charge states, while [parallel ion energy flux](name:parallel_ion_energy_flux) uses the local magnetic-field direction for its projection. The quantity is distinct from ion energy density, a volumetric energy source or sink, and ion velocity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion energy-flux-density vector has a component in the direction of the chosen unit normal to the oriented surface.

NAMES.name: ion_kinetic_energy_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Kinetic energy per unit volume carried by all ion species, including random particle motion and directed bulk-flow motion, summed over ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
The ion kinetic energy density is the local kinetic energy per volume carried by the complete ion population. It includes random particle motion and directed bulk-flow motion, while excluding neutral-particle energy and non-kinetic internal or potential energy.

The defining velocity-space moment is:

$$
u_{i,\mathrm{kin}} = \sum_s \int \frac{1}{2} m_s v^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,\mathrm{d}^3v
$$

where $u_{i,\mathrm{kin}}$ is the ion kinetic energy density, $s$ indexes ion species and charge states, $m_s$ is the ion mass in kg, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is particle speed in m s$^{-1}$, $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution normalized to the species number density, and $\mathrm{d}^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity is summed over the complete ion population rather than resolved by species or charge state. Its volume integral gives the corresponding energy content, related to [ion energy](name:ion_energy); for a thermal population, the random-motion contribution is connected to [ion temperature](name:ion_temperature) through the distribution's second moment.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_diffusivity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Fickian coefficient for flux-surface-normal redistribution of total ion momentum caused specifically by diamagnetic drift, excluding other transport mechanisms.
NAMES.long:
This diffusivity quantifies the diamagnetic-drift contribution to cross-field redistribution of ion momentum, with the ion quantity aggregated over all ionic charge states. It is distinct from the charge-state-resolved coefficient and from the mechanism-unspecified [ion diamagnetic momentum diffusivity](name:ion_diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity).

The Fickian constitutive relation is

$$
\Pi_{i,\mathrm{dia}} = -\rho_i D_{i,\mathrm{mom}}^{\mathrm{dia}} \, \nabla_\perp V_i
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic-drift contribution to ion momentum flux, $\rho_i$ is total ion mass density, $D_{i,\mathrm{mom}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this diffusivity, $\nabla_\perp$ is the gradient normal to magnetic flux surfaces, and $V_i$ is the corresponding ion flow-velocity component. The coefficient describes only the diffusive momentum-transport contribution due to diamagnetic drift; convective and other mechanism-resolved contributions are excluded. Its constitutive sign follows the negative-gradient relation, so outward flux results from an outward-decreasing flow component.

NAMES.name: ion_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion power is the volume-integrated net power coupled to all ion species over the plasma volume, summed over ion species, charge states, and source or sink channels.
NAMES.long:
Ion power is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the ion populations over the plasma volume. It is an all-ion aggregate: contributions are summed over ion species, over the charge states belonging to each species, and over source and sink channels that act on the ion energy balance.

The defining integral is

$$
P_i = \int_{V_\mathrm{plasma}} \sum_s \sum_z \sum_c p_{i,s,z}^{(c)}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_i$ is ion power, $V_\mathrm{plasma}$ is the plasma volume, $s$ indexes ion species, $z$ indexes charge state, $c$ indexes source or sink channels, $p_{i,s,z}^{(c)}$ is the local net ion power density contribution for that species, charge state, and channel, and $dV$ is the volume element.

This quantity is the full ion-channel sum, including direct ion heating, fast-particle energy transfer to ions, collisional exchange that deposits energy in or removes energy from ions, and explicit sink terms. It differs from [total_ion_power](name:total_ion_power), which denotes the ion-species sum for a specified source or sink channel, and from [ion_charge_state_power](name:ion_charge_state_power), which is charge-state-resolved and excludes collisional exchange by definition. The corresponding electron-channel and full-plasma aggregates are [total_electron_power](name:electron_deposited_power) and total_plasma_power.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net energy transfer is into the ion populations.

NAMES.name: ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Isotropic kinetic pressure of the ion population at a plasma location, summed over all charge states and spanning thermal and non-thermal (fast-ion) contributions.
NAMES.long:
Ion pressure is the isotropic kinetic pressure of the ion fluid, defined through the second velocity moment of the ion distribution function. It encompasses both the bulk thermal contribution from ions in local thermodynamic equilibrium and the non-thermal fast-ion contribution from suprathermal particles produced by auxiliary heating. The quantity is summed over all ion charge states present in the plasma.

The total ion pressure decomposes as:

$$
p_i = p_{i,\mathrm{thermal}} + p_{i,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{thermal}}$ is the isotropic thermal pressure from random ion motion and $p_{i,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the contribution from the suprathermal ion distribution, both summed over all charge states.

The thermal component, [thermal_ion_pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure), is inferred from ion temperature and density profiles measured by charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or Thomson scattering. The combined quantity [total_ion_pressure](name:total_ion_pressure) enters radial force balance, beta calculations, and pressure-driven instability analysis; the fast-ion fraction can be dominant during high-power neutral beam or ion cyclotron heating.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion population contributes outward pressure force on a bounding surface element, which holds for any plasma with finite ion thermal energy or non-thermal fast-ion content.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population at a plasma location, summed over all ion species and charge states and excluding the Maxwellian thermal ion contribution.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion pressure is the kinetic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population, defined through the second central velocity moment of the fast-ion distribution function. It is summed over all ion species and all charge states present in that suprathermal population, so it is the charge-state-summed aggregate of [fast-ion charge-state pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure). It excludes the Maxwellian thermal ion contribution represented by [thermal ion pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure).

The tensor is defined as the species and charge-state sum of the second central velocity moment:

$$
\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{\alpha,q} m_\alpha \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}) \otimes (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q})\, f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion pressure tensor, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\alpha$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes charge state, $m_\alpha$ is the ion mass for species $\alpha$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}$ is the mean velocity of the corresponding fast-ion subpopulation, $f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal distribution function whose velocity-space integral gives number density, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\otimes$ denotes the dyadic product.

The tensor may be anisotropic. The scalar fast-ion contribution entering the isotropic [ion pressure](name:ion_pressure) is the trace pressure $p_{\mathrm{fast}}=\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}/3$; for a gyrotropic distribution in the local right-handed field-aligned basis $(\hat{e}_1,\hat{e}_2,\hat{b})$, with $\hat{e}_1 \times \hat{e}_2=\hat{b}$ and $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, this is $p_{\mathrm{fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})/3$. Here $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ and $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ are the normal stresses parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction; related directional quantities include [parallel total fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), [perpendicular total fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure), [parallel fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure), and [perpendicular fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure). The scalar fast-ion contribution combines with the thermal contribution in [total ion pressure](name:total_ion_pressure) when the same population aggregation is used.

NAMES.name: ion_rotation_frequency
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Charge-state-averaged angular velocity vector describing the rotational bulk motion of an ion species, with each component determined by its geometric rotation lever arm.
NAMES.long:
The ion rotation-frequency vector describes the local angular rate and direction of an ion species' bulk rotational motion, averaged over its ionic charge states. It represents rotational motion rather than charged-particle gyrocenter orbit motion.

The rotational part of the bulk velocity is related to the angular rotation-frequency vector by

$$
\mathbf{v}_{i,\mathrm{rot}} = \boldsymbol{\omega}_i \times \mathbf{r}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{i,\mathrm{rot}}$ is the rotational part of the ion bulk velocity, $\boldsymbol{\omega}_i$ is the ion rotation-frequency vector, and $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the rotation axis. The [toroidal ion rotation frequency](name:toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency) is the corresponding charge-state-averaged component, with $\omega_{i,\phi}=v_{i,\phi}/R$. A charge-state-resolved quantity is given by [ion charge state rotation frequency](name:ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\omega}_i$ points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: ion_state_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short: Net local particle production rate per volume for one ion charge state, with positive values for creation and negative values for destruction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net source or sink of particles belonging to a specified ion charge state at a spatial location. It combines all processes that create or remove particles from that charge-state population and is the charge-state-resolved form of the general [particle source rate](name:particle_source_rate).

The source enters the charge-state continuity equation as

$$
\frac{\partial n_q}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_q = S_q
$$

where $n_q$ is the number density of the specified ion charge state, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_q$ is its particle flux, and $S_q$ is this net volumetric source rate. Positive $S_q$ denotes net creation, while negative $S_q$ denotes net destruction. It is local and must be distinguished from the [ion charge-state particle source rate](name:ion_charge_state_particle_source_rate), which is integrated inside an enclosing flux surface.

NAMES.name: ion_torque
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated angular-momentum source vector for the total ion population due to all explicit momentum sources, summed over all ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Ion torque is the net angular-momentum source acting on the entire ion population, obtained by integrating all explicit momentum-source terms — such as neutral beam injection, radio-frequency wave coupling, and collisional momentum exchange — over the plasma volume, with contributions from every ionization charge state summed. Unlike the local [ion torque density](name:ion_torque_density), which quantifies the angular-momentum source per unit volume, ion torque gives the total volumetric integral and carries units of energy (equivalent to N·m).

The ion torque vector $\mathbf{T}_i$ is related to the local torque-density field $\boldsymbol{\tau}_i$ by:

$$
\mathbf{T}_i = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}_i \, dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume over which the integral is evaluated and $\boldsymbol{\tau}_i$ is the volumetric angular-momentum source density summed over all charge states.

In axisymmetric configurations the toroidal projection [toroidal_ion_torque](name:toroidal_ion_torque) is the dominant experimentally relevant component, since toroidal symmetry isolates the contributions that drive toroidal plasma rotation. Collisional subsets can be resolved separately, as in [toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions), which captures the Coulomb-collisional contribution to the thermal ion population. Ion torque is inferred by solving the toroidal angular-momentum transport equation from measured rotation-velocity profiles combined with momentum diffusivity estimates from transport analysis.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal component is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: ion_torque_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Vector rate of external angular-momentum transfer to the combined ion population per unit plasma volume, with internal ion–ion exchanges canceling in the population sum.
NAMES.long:
The ion torque density is the local vector source of angular momentum for the combined ion population. It includes net contributions external to that population, while exchanges among included ion species and charge states cancel.

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_i = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_i}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{external}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_i$ is the ion torque density and $\boldsymbol{\ell}_i$ is the total local angular-momentum density of the included ions. Its toroidal projection is [toroidal ion torque density](name:toroidal_ion_torque_density); a specified species and charge-state contribution is [ion charge-state torque density](name:ion_charge_state_torque_density). The volume integral of the toroidal component gives [toroidal ion torque](name:toroidal_ion_torque).
NAMES.sign: Positive when each vector component points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: ion_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Charge-state-averaged bulk-flow velocity vector of the ion population, defined by the density-weighted first velocity moment and providing geometric and magnetic-field-aligned components.
NAMES.long:
The ion bulk velocity represents the mean directed motion of the ion population after combining its ionization charge states. It is a vector quantity whose geometric components and local magnetic-field-aligned projection are specific resolutions of the same flow.

The charge-state average is defined by

$$
\mathbf{V}_i = \frac{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}\mathbf{V}_{i,Z}}{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_i$ is the charge-state-averaged ion velocity, $n_{i,Z}$ is the number density in charge state $Z$ (m$^{-3}$), and $\mathbf{V}_{i,Z}$ is the bulk velocity of that charge state (m s$^{-1}$). The sum extends over the included ionization charge states.

This quantity includes all included charge states rather than a single selected state, which is represented by [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity). Its field-aligned projection is [parallel ion velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component points along its designated positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$; for a field-aligned projection, positive is along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Particle number density of iron ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over all iron ion charge states and excluding neutral iron.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of iron ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the iron-ion population at that flux-surface location. It is the iron-specific member of the [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) family. Iron has atomic number $Z=26$.

The number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of counted iron ions, and $V$ is volume. The count is summed over all iron ionic charge states and excludes neutral iron. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where reduced cross-field turbulent transport can sustain steep impurity-density gradients, as for [carbon density at the internal transport barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

NAMES.name: iron_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Particle number density of iron ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, summed over all iron ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of iron ions evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local particle count per physical volume at the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces. The magnetic axis is the locus where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes. This is the iron-specific component of [density at magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis).

The on-axis iron density is the limiting value of the charge-state-summed local density field:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}} \sum_{q=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local density of iron charge state $q$, $q$ indexes singly through fully charged iron ions, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position.

The quantity is summed over all iron ionic charge states and is not a charge-state-resolved density or an integrated particle inventory. It uses the same locus as [hydrogen density at magnetic axis](name:hydrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis), but differs in species; [iron density at divertor target](name:iron_density_at_divertor_target) refers instead to the divertor-target location.

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Particle number density of krypton ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over krypton charge states and excluding neutral krypton.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of krypton ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the krypton-ion population at that flux-surface location. The [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) is the parent quantity for this krypton-specific population.

The number density is defined by

$$
n = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n$ is number density, $N$ is the number of particles, and $V$ is volume. The quantity sums all ionized krypton charge states and excludes neutral krypton atoms. It is therefore an elemental ion density, analogous to the [ion density at the internal transport barrier](name:ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), rather than a density for one specified charge state. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep impurity-density gradients.

NAMES.name: krypton_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Number density of krypton ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, the innermost point of the confined plasma where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes.
NAMES.long:
Krypton ($Z = 36$) is a noble-gas impurity that can be seeded into confined plasmas for radiative power exhaust management or employed as a spectroscopic tracer. The krypton number density at the magnetic axis gives the on-axis value of the impurity concentration profile at the innermost nested flux surface, located at coordinates $(R_\mathrm{axis}, Z_\mathrm{axis})$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $\nabla\psi = 0$, with $\psi$ the poloidal magnetic flux. It is the krypton-species instance of the [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis) family.

The on-axis krypton density is inferred from spectrally resolved line-emission diagnostics — such as charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or vacuum-ultraviolet spectroscopy — combined with atomic data for the krypton charge-state distribution, and serves as the inner boundary value of the impurity concentration profile in radial transport analyzes.

Comparing this on-axis value with [krypton_density_at_pedestal](name:krypton_density_at_pedestal_top) and [krypton_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:krypton_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) characterizes the radial accumulation pattern: central peaking indicates the neoclassical inward pinch dominates over turbulent outward diffusion, while a hollow profile signals the reverse. The analogous on-axis density for boron is given by [boron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:boron_density_at_magnetic_axis).

NAMES.name: linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Linear neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the direction-unresolved linear momentum-flux contribution carried by neutral particles in one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It includes convective transport and isotropic pressure, not a poloidal or other directional projection.
NAMES.long:
Linear neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the direction-unresolved linear contribution to the momentum-flux tensor carried by neutral particles restricted to one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It represents transport of linear momentum by the state's mean motion together with the isotropic pressure contribution.

The linear contribution for state $s$ is defined by the convective-plus-isotropic-pressure decomposition:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{lin}}_s = n_s m_s \mathbf{u}_s \otimes \mathbf{u}_s + p_s \mathbf{I}
$$

where $s$ labels the neutral internal state, $n_s$ is its number density, $m_s$ is the particle mass for that state, $\mathbf{u}_s$ is its mean velocity, $p_s$ is its scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and $\otimes$ denotes the dyadic product.

This quantity is not itself a poloidal, radial, toroidal, vertical, or field-parallel component. It is the linear contribution to [neutral internal-state momentum flux] and excludes deviatoric or viscous stress terms not represented by the scalar pressure, as well as angular-momentum flux. Directional component names, for example [poloidal linear neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:poloidal_linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), are obtained by resolving $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{lin}}_s$ along the named direction; poloidal refers to increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the product of the resolved linear-momentum component and the resolved transport direction is positive in the basis used for the component definition.

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Local number density of lithium ions at the internal transport barrier reference radius, where reduced cross-field transport can produce steep impurity density gradients.
NAMES.long:
Lithium density at an internal transport barrier is the local number density of lithium ions on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. Unless a charge state is specified separately, it represents the elemental lithium ion concentration summed over all ionization states, consistent with the broader [density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) family.

The quantity is the sum of charge-state-resolved contributions evaluated at the ITB reference coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$:

$$
n_\mathrm{Li}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_{k=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{k+}}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB})
$$

where $k$ indexes the lithium ionization states (Li$^{1+}$, Li$^{2+}$, Li$^{3+}$) and $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the normalized radial coordinate of the barrier.

Lithium (atomic number $Z = 3$) enters fusion plasmas through pellet injection, evaporation from lithium-coated plasma-facing components, or deliberate wall conditioning. As a low-Z impurity it contributes less radiative cooling than high-Z species, but significant concentrations at the ITB can dilute the fuel ion population. The local value at the barrier is inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy or from inversion of line-integrated visible or soft-X-ray emission measurements.

The corresponding toroidal flow of lithium ions at the same barrier location is given by [toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), and the lithium density adjacent to plasma-facing components is separately described by [lithium_density_at_limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter).

NAMES.name: lithium_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Particle number density of lithium ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, summed over all lithium ionic charge states: Li+, Li2+, and Li3+.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of lithium ions evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local lithium-ion count per physical volume at the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces, summed over all lithium ionic charge states: $\mathrm{Li}^{+}$, $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$, and $\mathrm{Li}^{3+}$. The magnetic axis is the locus where the gradient of [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) vanishes, so this quantity is the central value of the charge-state-summed lithium-ion density field.

The on-axis lithium density is defined by the limiting value of the local charge-state-summed lithium density field at the magnetic-axis position:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}} \sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density field of lithium ions with charge state $q$, $q=1,2,3$ correspond respectively to $\mathrm{Li}^{+}$, $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$, and $\mathrm{Li}^{3+}$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position. For a smooth flux-surface quantity, this is equivalently the value at $\rho=0$ in a flux-coordinate chart $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ whose radial label $\rho$ is zero at the magnetic axis.

The species-level aggregation is a charge-state sum because density is a per-volume amount; it is not a charge-state average, not an electron density, and not an integrated lithium inventory. Neutral lithium atoms are excluded. This is the lithium-specific specialization of [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis); it uses the same charge-state-summed lithium population as [lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary), but the evaluation locus is the magnetic axis rather than the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Toroidal loop voltage at the last closed flux surface, defined by the circulation of electric field that drives inductive and resistive plasma current.
NAMES.long:
The loop voltage is the electromotive force obtained by integrating the electric field around a closed toroidal circuit on the last closed flux surface. It is the net voltage available to drive the plasma current through inductive and resistive electric fields, not the generator or power-supply terminal voltage.

The defining relation is

$$
V_{\rm loop} = \oint_{C} \mathbf{E}\cdot d\boldsymbol{\ell} = -\frac{d\Phi_{\rm pol}}{dt}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric field, $d\boldsymbol{\ell}$ follows the positively oriented toroidal circuit $C$, and $\Phi_{\rm pol}$ is the linked poloidal magnetic flux. Its relationship to the resulting current is represented by [plasma current due to ohmic induction](name:plasma_current_due_to_ohmic_induction) and [toroidal current density](name:toroidal_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electric-field circulation follows the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: lower_bound_charge
NAMES.short: Lower-bound charge is the integer ionization charge number that defines the smallest charge state included in a charge-state interval or bundle. It is a boundary value, not a net, averaged, or representative charge.
NAMES.long:
Lower-bound charge is the integer ionization charge number that defines the smallest charge state included in a charge-state interval for an ion population. It is the lower endpoint of the interval, independent of whether the interval contains one charge state or multiple adjacent charge states.

The charge states included by such an interval are those satisfying:

$$
Z_\mathrm{min} \leq Z \leq Z_\mathrm{max}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{min}$ is the lower-bound charge, $Z$ is an integer ionization charge number, and $Z_\mathrm{max}$ is the matching upper endpoint of the same interval.

This quantity is only the lower boundary of a charge-state range. It is not the net charge of a single particle, not a density-weighted or otherwise averaged charge, and not the nuclear charge of the element. A concrete specialization is the [ion charge-state lower-bound charge](name:ion_charge_state_lower_bound_charge); when $Z_\mathrm{min} = Z_\mathrm{max}$, the interval contains exactly one charge state.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_lower_bound_charge
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Smallest ionization charge number included in an ion charge-state bundle, defining the lower endpoint of its grouped charge-state range.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the lower-bound ionization charge number assigned to an ion charge-state bundle. It identifies the smallest charge state included, independently of whether the bundle contains one state or several adjacent states.

Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the set of ionization charge numbers included in the bundle and let $Z$ denote an ionization charge number:

$$
Z_{\min} = \min_{Z \in \mathcal{S}} Z
$$

The result is the specific lower endpoint of the bundle, not a net charge, representative charge, or charge-state average. It refines [lower-bound charge](name:lower_bound_charge) by restricting that boundary to an ion charge-state bundle and is distinct from the corresponding upper-bound charge.

NAMES.name: magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Vector field whose curl gives the magnetic induction, gage-dependent but physically central to canonical momentum, gyrokinetic, and magnetohydrodynamic formulations of magnetized plasmas.
NAMES.long:
The magnetic vector potential $\mathbf{A}$ is a gage-dependent vector field characterizing the electromagnetic state of a plasma. It enters fundamental physics through the canonical particle momentum $\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v} + q\mathbf{A}$, where $m$ is particle mass and $q$ is particle charge, and it governs inductive electromagnetic effects in both equilibrium and perturbed plasma states.

The defining relation connecting $\mathbf{A}$ to the magnetic induction $\mathbf{B}$ is:

$$
\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic induction. Only the curl of $\mathbf{A}$ is directly physical; the vector potential itself is gage dependent. Its time derivative contributes to the inductive electric field via $\mathbf{E}_\mathrm{ind} = -\partial\mathbf{A}/\partial t$, which is central to Faraday's law in electromagnetic plasma models.

Specific projections serve distinct physical roles. The field-aligned component $A_\parallel = \mathbf{A} \cdot \hat{b}$, where $\hat{b}$ is the equilibrium field unit vector, governs Alfvénic dynamics and is the component retained in gyrokinetic and reduced-MHD formulations; [its normalized perturbed amplitude] is used in eigenmode studies. Cylindrical components in the right-handed $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame — radial, toroidal, and vertical — are natural for equilibrium and MHD calculations, while the poloidal projection in flux coordinates $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$ arises in neoclassical transport analyzes. In vacuum regions, $\mathbf{A}$ is generated solely by external coil currents, with no plasma-current contribution.

NAMES.name: mass_density
NAMES.short: Local plasma mass per unit volume is the charged-particle mass density summed over all charged species and charge states. It is the inertial density used in bulk-fluid momentum and magnetohydrodynamic dynamics.
NAMES.long:
Local plasma mass per unit volume is the local inertial density of the charged plasma. It is an intensive continuum field: its value characterizes the local material state rather than scaling with the size of the volume element.

The defining relation is the sum over charged particle populations:

$$
\rho = \sum_a n_a m_a
$$

where $a$ indexes each charged particle population, $n_a$ is its number density, and $m_a$ is the mass of one particle in that population. For an ion species represented without an explicit charge state, the species contribution is summed over all charge states of that species.

Neutral atoms and molecules are excluded from this charged-plasma mass density. Unlike density-weighted per-particle fields, mass density is additive over constituent populations; charge-state contributions are summed rather than averaged. The charged-plasma momentum density is $\rho \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$, where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the [center of mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), and this quantity is conceptually equivalent to [plasma mass density](name:plasma_mass_density) for the charged plasma.

NAMES.name: momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.short: Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of a specified momentum population, distinct from that population’s bulk flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum for a selected population, momentum component, and transport direction. It is a transport closure quantity, not the population’s actual bulk flow velocity.

For each selected momentum component and transport direction, the convective momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{conv}} P
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum flux, $V_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the momentum convection velocity, and $P$ is the corresponding momentum density. The definition applies componentwise when momentum or transport direction is resolved.

The population may be total plasma, ions aggregated over charge states, a specified ion charge state, or neutral matter. Examples include [ion momentum convection velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity), [ion charge-state momentum convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), [neutral momentum convection velocity](name:neutral_momentum_convection_velocity), and [parallel momentum convection velocity](name:parallel_momentum_convection_velocity). Distinct attributed contributions, such as [diamagnetic momentum convection velocity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity), need not be projections of one physical bulk-flow vector.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated convective momentum flux is in the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported momentum density.

NAMES.name: diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.short: Effective velocity coefficient for diamagnetic, advective, non-diffusive transport of selected momentum populations, components, and transport directions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the diamagnetic contribution to advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum for a selected population, momentum component, and transport direction. It is a transport-closure quantity, not the population’s actual bulk flow velocity.

For the selected momentum component and transport direction, the diamagnetic convective momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{dia}} = V_{\mathrm{dia}} P
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to convective momentum flux, $V_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this convection velocity, and $P$ is the corresponding momentum density.

This quantity isolates the diamagnetic contribution from the total [momentum convection velocity](name:momentum_convection_velocity). A charge-state-resolved realization is the [ion charge-state diamagnetic momentum convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity), while [diamagnetic momentum diffusivity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity) describes the distinct diffusive contribution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated diamagnetic momentum flux is in the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported momentum density.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of the toroidal momentum component of a specified ion charge state due to diamagnetic drift. The momentum component is along the toroidal basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame; this is an effective transport coefficient, not the charge state's diamagnetic drift or bulk-flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of the toroidal momentum component of a specified ion charge state due to diamagnetic drift is the signed effective coefficient multiplying that charge state's toroidal momentum density in a transport closure for flux in the $R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The transported momentum component is along $\hat{\phi}$ in that frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the scalar coefficient is not a toroidal particle velocity.

The defining closure relation is

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{dia}}_{k,\phi}=V^{\mathrm{dia}}_{k,\phi}\,L_{k,\phi}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{dia}}_{k,\phi}$ is the [ion charge state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) for charge state $k$ with flux direction along the $R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $V^{\mathrm{dia}}_{k,\phi}$ is this convection velocity, and $L_{k,\phi}$ is the toroidal momentum density of charge state $k$; the subscript $\phi$ labels the transported momentum component, not the direction of $V^{\mathrm{dia}}_{k,\phi}$.

This coefficient is charge-state-resolved and therefore differs from species-level ion coefficients such as [toroidal ion momentum convection velocity](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity) and [vertical ion momentum convection velocity](name:vertical_ion_momentum_convection_velocity), which are density-weighted means over all charge states rather than coefficients for a single charge state. It is also distinct from [toroidal ion charge state momentum convection velocity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), whose directional token denotes the velocity direction, and from [toroidal ion charge state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), the actual diamagnetic drift velocity component of the charge state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when momentum density directed along $+\hat{\phi}$ for the specified ion charge state gives a diamagnetic momentum flux in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Effective velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum carried by a specified ion species and charge state, distinct from its bulk flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum for a specified ion species and charge state. It is a transport closure quantity, not the actual bulk flow velocity of that ion charge state.

For each selected momentum component and transport direction, the convective momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{conv}} P
$$

where $\Gamma_{P,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum flux, $V_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the momentum convection velocity, and $P$ is the corresponding momentum density. The generic [momentum convection velocity](name:momentum_convection_velocity) uses the same closure relation across momentum populations.

This charge-state-resolved quantity applies to one ion charge state and excludes summation over other charge states. Its vector may be resolved into radial, poloidal, toroidal, vertical, or field-aligned components; unlike [energy convection velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity), it transports momentum rather than energy. It is distinct from the ion charge state's material flow velocity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated convective momentum flux is in the chosen positive transport direction for positive transported momentum density.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective vector velocity at which aggregate ion momentum is advectively transported in plasma fluid models, serving as a closure coefficient distinct from the actual bulk ion flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient in the non-diffusive, advective transport of aggregate ion momentum. It is a transport-closure quantity and is distinct from the material bulk ion velocity, as distinguished from the broader [momentum convection velocity](name:momentum_convection_velocity) framework.

A transport-closure decomposition of ion momentum flux is written as

$$
\mathbf{F}_{p,i} = -D_{p,i}\nabla\mathbf{p}_i + \mathbf{V}_{c,i} \otimes \mathbf{p}_i
$$

where $\mathbf{F}_{p,i}$ is the ion momentum-flux tensor, $D_{p,i}$ is the ion momentum diffusivity, $\mathbf{p}_i$ is ion momentum density, and $\mathbf{V}_{c,i}$ is this convection velocity. The dyadic term represents non-diffusive momentum transport.

The unqualified ion quantity aggregates the ion momentum contribution over all charge states. A species- or charge-state-resolved form, such as [ion charge-state momentum convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), supplies the corresponding resolved convention; unlike [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), this coefficient is not the material flow velocity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when each radial, toroidal, or vertical component points in the corresponding $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for loss of ordered fluid momentum through collisional friction and neoclassical viscosity; the general structural parent for species-, charge-state-, and projection-resolved momentum damping rates.
NAMES.long:
The momentum damping rate $\nu_D$ is the reciprocal relaxation time that quantifies how rapidly ordered fluid momentum is dissipated within a plasma population through inter-species collisional friction and neoclassical viscous stresses. It enters the fluid momentum balance as a linear loss coefficient applied to the local momentum density, capturing the collective effect of Coulomb collisions and drift-driven viscosity acting on any directed flow component.

The defining relation for a fluid momentum component $p$ subject to damping is:

$$
\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\nu_D \, p
$$

where $\nu_D$ is the damping rate and $p$ is the local fluid momentum density. The magnitude of $\nu_D$ depends on plasma collisionality, species masses and charges, and the local magnetic geometry.

This name is the structural parent for species- and projection-resolved variants. In transport models, $\nu_D$ is derived analytically from neoclassical friction-force coefficients or from velocity-space integrals of the collision operator evaluated at the local plasma parameters. Ion-population values are provided by [ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate); charge-state-resolved counterparts are given by [ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate). Directional projections include poloidal_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate, toroidal_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate, parallel_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate, and [radial_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical dissipation of fluid momentum for a specified ion charge state, expressed as a vector whose components quantify the damping rate along distinct geometric projections.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge state momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation timescale at which ordered fluid momentum of a specified ion charge state is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. As a vector, it encodes the direction-dependent damping coefficient along the radial, poloidal, toroidal, and field-parallel geometric projections.

The defining relation for a fluid momentum density component $p_s$ of ion charge state $s$ subject to dissipation is:

$$
\frac{\partial p_s}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\nu_{D,s} \, p_s
$$

where $\nu_{D,s}$ is the charge-state damping rate and $p_s$ is the directed fluid momentum density of the specified charge state. The magnitude of $\nu_{D,s}$ is set by Coulomb collisionality, the charge-state mass and effective charge number, and the local magnetic geometry through neoclassical friction-force coefficients.

This quantity resolves the general [momentum_damping_rate](name:momentum_damping_rate) at the level of an individual ion charge state, in contrast to [ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate), which represents the charge-state-aggregated ion population. Scalar projections along each geometric direction include [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) for the field-aligned component.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical dissipation of bulk ion fluid momentum, expressed as a vector whose components each quantify the damping rate along a distinct geometric projection of the ion velocity.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation timescale at which ordered bulk ion fluid momentum is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. As a vector, it encodes the geometric anisotropy of momentum loss in a magnetized plasma, where the field-aligned and toroidal projections relax through distinct mechanisms compared with the poloidal or radial projections.

In the ion fluid momentum balance the damping contribution enters as:

$$\frac{\partial \mathbf{p}_i}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\boldsymbol{\nu}_D^{\,i} \cdot \mathbf{p}_i$$

where $\mathbf{p}_i = m_i n_i \mathbf{v}_i$ is the ion momentum density, with $m_i$ the ion mass, $n_i$ the number density, and $\mathbf{v}_i$ the bulk ion fluid velocity. The rate $\boldsymbol{\nu}_D^{\,i}$ is applied component-wise and aggregates contributions from all ion charge states.

Component-resolved scalar rates are [radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate), [toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate), [poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate), and [parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate). These are computed from neoclassical transport theory or turbulent-momentum-transport models. This quantity serves as the ion-species-level structural parent described by [momentum_damping_rate](name:momentum_damping_rate), which covers the general multi-species case.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the rate coefficient reduces the magnitude of the corresponding ion momentum component, producing exponential relaxation toward zero ordered flow.

NAMES.name: momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.short: Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of bulk-flow momentum. This generic parent does not specify the transported plasma or neutral population.
NAMES.long:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of bulk-flow momentum. This generic parent does not specify the transported plasma or neutral population; population-qualified standard names identify that population. Each component is a kinematic diagonal coefficient for one named transport direction, not a full viscosity tensor.

For component $\chi_{m,i}$ associated with coordinate $x_i$ along direction $\hat{e}_i$, the diagonal diffusive closure for momentum-density component $M_j$ is

$$
\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{m,i}\,\frac{\partial M_j}{\partial x_i}\qquad\text{(no summation over }i\text{)}
$$

where $\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux in direction $\hat{e}_i$ of momentum component $j$, $\chi_{m,i}$ is the directional momentum diffusion coefficient, $M_j$ is the bulk-flow momentum density component of the same transported population, and $x_i$ is distance along $\hat{e}_i$.

The component basis must be explicit. A radial component is the $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; a toroidal component is the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the same frame. Poloidal, parallel, perpendicular-to-magnetic-field, and flux-surface-normal components are separate named projections; flux-surface-normal is oriented toward increasing flux label.

Population-qualified specializations include [plasma momentum diffusion coefficient](name:plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), [ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), and [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). Scalar specializations include [radial momentum diffusivity](name:radial_momentum_diffusivity) and [ion momentum diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity). This name is the momentum-channel specialization of [diffusion coefficient], and excludes convective momentum transport, external momentum sources, off-diagonal couplings between flux and gradient directions, and the dynamic viscosity-like coefficient obtained by multiplying by mass density.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the diffusive momentum flux is directed opposite to the corresponding gradient of bulk-flow momentum density.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Vector of directional diffusion coefficients governing diffusive transport of bulk-ion momentum in a magnetized plasma, with distinct radial, poloidal, and toroidal components forming the diagonal of the ion momentum diffusivity tensor.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum diffusion coefficient vector collects the anisotropic diagonal components of the bulk-ion momentum diffusivity tensor, each relating the diffusive flux of bulk-ion momentum along a given geometric direction to the local gradient of ion momentum density in that direction. In a gradient-diffusion closure, each directional component $\chi_{\rm mom}$ satisfies the constitutive relation:

$$
\Gamma_{\rm mom} = -\chi_{\rm mom}\,\nabla(m_i n_i v_i)
$$

where $\Gamma_{\rm mom}$ is the diffusive ion momentum flux density, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, and $v_i$ is the bulk ion flow velocity component in the corresponding direction. The three projections are radial_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient, governing cross-flux-surface momentum mixing; poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient, governing transport along the poloidal direction tangent to flux surfaces; and [toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), governing diffusion of toroidal angular momentum. The radial component is the confinement-relevant quantity and is inferred from toroidal momentum balance analyzes or gyrokinetic and fluid turbulence simulations. The scalar analog [ion_momentum_diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity) represents the same physical concept without directional decomposition, while plasma_momentum_diffusivity extends the concept to the full plasma mixture.

NAMES.name: momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short: Vector Fick's-law transport coefficient relating the diffusive momentum flux to the local momentum-density gradient, abstracting over plasma species, neutral populations, charge states, and directional projections in a magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the diffusive momentum flux and the negative local gradient of momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for the fluid momentum balance. Physically, it encapsulates contributions from collisional viscosity, turbulent mixing, charge-exchange friction, and diamagnetic drifts. As a vector quantity, its radial, poloidal, toroidal, parallel, and vertical components capture the strongly anisotropic transport characteristic of magnetized plasma, where diffusivity along magnetic field lines greatly exceeds cross-field values.

The diffusive momentum flux density component along direction $\hat{e}_i$ is

$$
\Gamma_{m,i} = -D_{m,i} \frac{\partial (m n v_i)}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $D_{m,i}$ is the momentum diffusivity component, $m$ is particle mass, $n$ is number density, and $v_i$ is the fluid velocity component along $\hat{e}_i$, making $m n v_i$ the local momentum density.

This parent name abstracts over species-resolved and process-attributed children including plasma_momentum_diffusivity for the total plasma and analogous neutral-population variants; the [radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) is the cross-field specialization and [parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity) is the field-aligned form. Values are inferred from fluid transport simulations by computing the diffusive momentum flux relative to the local momentum-density gradient, or estimated analytically from neoclassical and turbulence theory.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the Fick's-law coefficient relating diffusive momentum flux to the negative gradient of momentum density for a specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the diffusive momentum flux of a specified ion charge state and the negative local gradient of its momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for the fluid momentum balance. It describes directional redistribution of momentum for that charge state.

For transport direction $i$, the diffusive momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{m,i}^{(q)} = -D_{m,i}^{(q)} \frac{\partial\left(\rho_q u_i^{(q)}\right)}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,i}^{(q)}$ is the diffusive momentum flux, $D_{m,i}^{(q)}$ is the corresponding momentum diffusivity, $\rho_q$ is the mass density of the specified ion charge state, $u_i^{(q)}$ is its flow-velocity component, and $x_i$ is the coordinate along the transport direction.

The quantity is general over directional projections, including the cross-flux-surface form represented by [radial ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) and the field-aligned form represented by [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). It is resolved for one ion charge state rather than summed over charge states as in [ion momentum diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity), and is a charge-state-specific instance of [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Diffusion coefficient relating the diffusive ion momentum flux to the local ion momentum density gradient, expressing the rate at which diffusive processes redistribute momentum within the total ion population summed over charge states.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum diffusivity $D_{\mathrm{mom}}^i$ is the effective diffusion coefficient characterizing how diffusive processes redistribute momentum within the total ion population across magnetic flux surfaces. It is the species-summed, charge-state-integrated scalar counterpart of [ion_state_momentum_diffusivity](name:ion_state_momentum_diffusivity), which resolves the same quantity by charge state, and represents the effective-scalar form of the full tensor [momentum_diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity).

The diffusive component of the ion momentum flux density $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{mom},i}$ satisfies:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{mom},i} = -n_i m_i D_{\mathrm{mom}}^i \nabla v_i
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $m_i$ is the ion mass, and $v_i$ is the mean ion fluid velocity.

The ion momentum diffusivity is inferred by fitting a transport model to measured ion rotation profiles, obtained via charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy. Comparing $D_{\mathrm{mom}}^i$ with the ion thermal diffusivity yields the ion-channel Prandtl number, a key indicator of whether momentum and heat are transported by the same underlying turbulent mechanism.

In tokamak core plasmas, values fall in the range 0.1–10 m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, comparable in magnitude to the ion thermal diffusivity under turbulence-dominated conditions and smaller when neoclassical processes dominate. The radial projection is separately quantified by [radial_momentum_diffusivity](name:radial_momentum_diffusivity), while the diamagnetic-drift-driven contribution is captured by [ion_diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity](name:ion_diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: ion_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short: Scalar Fick's-law diffusion coefficient relating the diffusive momentum flux of ions in a specified ion state to the negative local gradient of that ion-state momentum density.
NAMES.long:
Momentum diffusivity for an ion state is the transport coefficient appearing in the diffusive closure of the ion-state-resolved momentum equation, quantifying how collisional, neoclassical, turbulent, and charge-exchange processes redistribute the momentum of the selected ion population. This scalar quantity denotes a single diagonal or otherwise specified transport projection, rather than the full anisotropic momentum-diffusion operator.

For selected ion state $a$ and component $\alpha$, the scalar Fick's-law closure is

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{m,a,\alpha} = -D^{(m)}_{a,\alpha}\frac{\partial (m_a n_a u_{a,\alpha})}{\partial \ell_\alpha}
$$

where $a$ labels the ion state, $\alpha$ labels the selected component, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{m,a,\alpha}$ is the diffusive flux density of the $\alpha$-directed momentum, $D^{(m)}_{a,\alpha}$ is the ion-state momentum diffusivity, $m_a$ is the ion mass, $n_a$ is the ion-state number density, $u_{a,\alpha}$ is the flow velocity component, and $\ell_\alpha$ is distance along the selected transport direction. The product $m_a n_a u_{a,\alpha}$ is the local directed momentum density, and the minus sign makes a nonnegative diffusive coefficient oppose its local gradient.

This name is the ion-state-resolved scalar specialization of [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity). It differs from [ion momentum diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity), which is the effective coefficient in a closure for total ion momentum flux and total ion momentum density after those extensive fields are summed over all ion states; it should not be interpreted as an unqualified sum of state-resolved coefficients. When the ion-state label is an ionization state, it is the scalar state-resolved counterpart of [ion-charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). Direction-specific scalar projections include [radial ion-charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height, and [parallel ion-charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), the projection along the magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: momentum_due_to_hot_tail
NAMES.short: Areal first moment of the momentum-magnitude distribution of pre-quench electrons retained in the suprathermal hot tail after a rapid thermal quench.
NAMES.long:
Hot-tail momentum is the momentum content per unit area of pre-quench electrons that remain in the suprathermal tail during rapid thermal cooling.

The defining first moment is

$$
P_{\mathrm{HT}} = \int_{\mathcal{H}} p\,f_{\mathrm{HT}}(p)\,dp
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{HT}}$ is the hot-tail momentum, $p$ is electron momentum magnitude, $f_{\mathrm{HT}}(p)$ is the differential areal density of retained hot-tail electrons, and $\mathcal{H}$ is the momentum domain occupied by that population.

This quantity is an integrated population moment, not the threshold momentum for runaway generation. The latter is represented by the [runaway-electron critical momentum due to hot-tail generation](name:runaway_electron_critical_momentum_due_to_hot_tail).

NAMES.name: momentum_flux
NAMES.short: Rate of transport of linear momentum per unit area across an oriented surface in the plasma, combining convective, isotropic pressure, and viscous stress contributions from any species or population.
NAMES.long:
The momentum flux describes the rate at which linear momentum crosses a unit area of an oriented surface in the plasma. It encompasses the convective ram-pressure term, the isotropic thermal pressure, and viscous or turbulent stress contributions, and appears as the divergence term in the plasma fluid momentum-balance equation.

The momentum-flux tensor for a single plasma fluid is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi} = \rho \mathbf{v}\mathbf{v} + p\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}
$$

where $\rho$ is the mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ the bulk flow velocity, $p$ the scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}$ the viscous stress tensor. The momentum current through a surface with outward unit normal $\hat{n}$ is $\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}$.

This name is the structural parent for species- and direction-resolved forms. Species-specific instances include [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux), and [plasma momentum flux](name:plasma_momentum_flux), each summed over the relevant population. Directional projections such as [parallel momentum flux] isolate field-aligned transport, while [poloidal momentum flux](name:poloidal_momentum_flux) captures cross-field transport through toroidally symmetric surfaces. The complementary volume source density entering the momentum balance is given by [volumetric plasma momentum source].

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Vector of linear-momentum transport rate per unit area for ions in a specific charge state, with directional projections characterizing charge-state-resolved momentum transport across magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state momentum flux is the vector flux density of linear momentum carried by ions in a single ionization state $z$, combining convective transport from bulk flow and non-convective contributions from pressure and viscous stress. It appears in the charge-state-resolved momentum-balance equation as the flux term whose divergence governs local momentum redistribution across flux surfaces and couples to electromagnetic forces, inter-species friction, and anomalous transport terms.

The component form of the momentum-flux tensor for charge state $z$ is:

$$
\Pi_{z,ij} = m_i n_z v_{z,i} v_{z,j} + p_z \delta_{ij} + \pi_{z,ij}
$$

where $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state $z$, $v_{z,i}$ and $v_{z,j}$ are fluid velocity components, $p_z$ is the scalar pressure, $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta, and $\pi_{z,ij}$ is the viscous stress tensor for that charge state.

Scalar projections onto coordinate axes are resolved in the component names: [radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) for outward transport across flux surfaces, toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux and [poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) for the respective in-surface momentum components, and [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) for field-aligned transport. Summing over all ionization stages recovers the total ion [momentum_flux](name:momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when momentum is transported in the direction of increasing $R$ for the radial component, in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ for the toroidal component, and along the local magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$ for the parallel component.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Vector rate of linear momentum transport per unit area for the total ion population, summed over all ion species and charge states, encompassing convective, pressure, and viscous stress contributions.
NAMES.long:
The ion momentum flux represents the rate at which the total ion population transports linear momentum through a unit area, summed over all ion species and charge states. It combines convective bulk-flow momentum, scalar pressure (isotropic kinetic stress), and viscous or turbulent off-diagonal stress contributions. Its divergence appears in the ion momentum balance equation, governing the forces that drive and redistribute plasma rotation and bulk flows; this quantity is the ion-specific instance of the general [momentum_flux](name:momentum_flux).

The total ion momentum flux density is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion} = \sum_s \left( m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s \mathbf{v}_s + p_s \mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_s \right)
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion species mass, $n_s$ is the number density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the mean fluid velocity, $p_s$ is the scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the unit tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ is the viscous stress tensor for species $s$, with the sum running over all ion species.

Specific resolved components isolate distinct transport channels: [toroidal_ion_momentum_flux](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_flux) quantifies the radial flux of toroidal momentum relevant to rotation drive, [parallel_ion_momentum_flux](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux) captures transport along the magnetic field, and [poloidal_ion_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux) resolves the poloidal channel. The convective contribution can be parameterized through the radial_ion_momentum_effective_convection_velocity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ion momentum is transported in the positive direction of the resolved projection axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with outward (increasing $R$) as positive for radial projections.

NAMES.name: momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: Pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic contribution to momentum flux through an oriented surface, with species, charge state, transported component, and projection left unspecified.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic contribution to momentum-flux density through an oriented reference surface. It leaves the transported momentum component, particle species, charge state, and projection direction unspecified; more specific forms such as [ion charge state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) are instances of this quantity.

The scalar projection of the diamagnetic momentum-flux tensor is defined by

$$
F_{\mathrm{dia}} = \hat{\mathbf n} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{dia}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_p
$$

where $F_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the projected flux, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the oriented unit normal of the reference surface, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic-drift contribution to the momentum-flux tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_p$ identifies the transported momentum component. It is the diamagnetic-drift specialization of [flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and differs from [momentum source due to diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which represents a local balance source rather than transport across a surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the diamagnetic momentum flux is directed through the reference surface along its chosen orientation.
