NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Ion charge state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed cylindrical-R flux density of toroidal linear momentum for one specified ion charge state in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed cylindrical-$R$ flux density of toroidal linear momentum carried by one specified charge state of an ion species and associated with its pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift. The transported momentum is the $\hat{\phi}$ component and the flux direction is $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The diamagnetic contribution is defined as the product of the charge-state toroidal momentum density and the cylindrical-$R$ component of the same charge state's diamagnetic drift velocity:

$$
\Pi_{R\phi,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}} = m_i n_\alpha u_{\phi,\alpha} v_{R,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $\Pi_{R\phi,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this momentum flux, the first tensor index $R$ denotes the flux direction, the second tensor index $\phi$ denotes the toroidal momentum component, $\alpha$ labels the ion charge state, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, $u_{\phi,\alpha}$ is the toroidal flow velocity of that charge state, and $v_{R,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [radial ion charge state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

This quantity is local in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; it is not a flux-surface average, a flux-surface integral, or a flux-surface-normal projection. It is charge-state resolved and excludes contributions to the same $R\phi$ momentum-flux component from non-diamagnetic transport mechanisms. The [radial ion momentum flux at flux surface due to diamagnetic drift](name:radial_ion_momentum_flux_at_flux_surface_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is tied to a magnetic-flux-surface locus, while [toroidal ion charge state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [perpendicular ion charge state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) are velocity components rather than momentum fluxes; perpendicular is relative to the magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when toroidal linear momentum associated with motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ is transported toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: momentum_source
NAMES.short: Directed rate of momentum transfer to or from a plasma population, represented as a source density resolved by species, internal state, or spatial direction.
NAMES.long:
A momentum source density represents the directed transfer of momentum caused by physical processes acting on a plasma population or one of its resolved states. It may retain vector direction or represent a selected component of the momentum-transfer rate.

The area-normalized source is defined by

$$
\mathbf{S}_{p} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src}}$ is the momentum transferred by the source processes, $A$ is the surface over which the source is normalized, and $t$ is time. Concrete variants may resolve a radial component, an internal state, or an ion charge state, as in [radial momentum source](name:radial_momentum_source) and [ion charge-state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source). Population-level quantities may sum the corresponding state-resolved contributions, as for [ion momentum source](name:ion_momentum_source).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Momentum source density for a specified ion charge state gives the net directed momentum transfer into that state, retaining the full vector before directional projection.
NAMES.long:
The momentum source density for a specified ion charge state is the net directed rate of momentum transfer into that state, represented by a physical vector before projection onto a coordinate or magnetic-field direction. It is the charge-state-resolved member of the [momentum source density](name:momentum_source), whereas [ion_momentum_source](name:ion_momentum_source) aggregates the corresponding ion contributions over charge states.

$$
\mathbf{S}_{m,s} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_s}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_s$ is the net momentum transferred to ion charge state $s$, $A$ is the reference area, and $t$ is time.

The state index $s$ identifies one resolved ion charge state; contributions are not summed over charge states. Positive and negative terms represent net momentum addition and removal. Directional forms, such as the [toroidal ion charge-state momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), are projections of this vector. It differs from [ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), which describes momentum transported across a surface rather than locally transferred into the state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a vector component points along its stated positive direction: increasing $R$, $\phi$, or $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, or along the defined positive local magnetic-field direction for a parallel component.

NAMES.name: ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional momentum transfer to the total ion population, summed over all ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Ion momentum source is the area-normalized vector rate of directional momentum transfer to the total ion population, summed over all ion charge states. It retains the direction of the net transfer rather than reducing it to a magnitude.

The charge-state aggregation is

$$
\mathbf{S}_{i} = \sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{i}} \mathbf{S}_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i}$ is the total-ion momentum source vector, $z$ indexes the ion charge states in the set $\mathcal{Z}_{i}$, and $\mathbf{S}_{i,z}$ is the corresponding source for one charge state. The [momentum source](name:momentum_source) defines this same directional momentum-transfer concept at the general species and projection level.

This quantity includes all ion charge states and excludes neutral species. It is distinct from the [ion charge-state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), which resolves one state; its axis and field-aligned projections are components of the same total-ion vector, including the [parallel net ion momentum source](name:parallel_net_ion_momentum_source).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a projected component points along its defined positive direction—$+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; flux-coordinate $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ and field-parallel projections use their stated positive directions.

NAMES.name: neon_density
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Neon particle number density is the count of neon atoms or ions per physical volume, summed over all charge states. Qualifiers may specify spatial treatment, such as volume averaging, without changing the elemental neon species.
NAMES.long:
Neon particle number density is the count of neon atoms or ions per physical volume, summed over all charge states. It represents elemental neon abundance independently of how that abundance is distributed among ionization states or across space.

The charge-state-summed elemental density is defined by

$$
n_\mathrm{Ne}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{q=0}^{10} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Ne},q}}{dV}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the neon particle number density, $q$ is the neon charge-state number, and $N_{\mathrm{Ne},q}$ is the number of neon particles in charge state $q$ in a volume element about position $\mathbf{x}$.

Unless a qualifier states otherwise, `neon_density` denotes the underlying elemental neon number-density quantity and does not specify a spatial averaging operation. A specialization such as [volume-averaged neon density](name:volume_averaged_neon_density) applies a spatial averaging operation to the same charge-state-summed elemental neon density; charge-state-resolved densities for individual neon ionization states are distinct quantities.

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Particle number density of neon ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over ionization states and excluding neutral neon.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of neon ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the neon-ion population at that flux-surface location. Neon has atomic number $Z=10$; unless a charge state is specified separately, all neon ionization states are included and neutral neon is excluded.

The number density is defined by

$$
n = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n$ is number density, $N$ is the number of counted neon ions, and $V$ is volume. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density gradients. This quantity is the neon-specific member of [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier), analogous to [carbon density at the internal transport barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

NAMES.name: neon_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Number density of neon ions at the magnetic axis, the innermost point of the confined plasma where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux vanishes.
NAMES.long:
Neon ($\mathrm{Ne}$, atomic number 10) is a medium-$Z$ noble-gas impurity introduced into magnetically confined plasmas for radiative-mantle seeding and disruption mitigation. Its number density at the magnetic axis is the species-specific realization of [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis) for neon, evaluated at the singular innermost flux-surface point $(R_\mathrm{axis}, Z_\mathrm{axis})$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $\nabla\psi = 0$, with $\psi$ the poloidal magnetic flux.

Because no charge state is resolved, the quantity is summed over all neon ionization states ($\mathrm{Ne}^{1+}$ through $\mathrm{Ne}^{10+}$), representing the total elemental neon ion concentration at the plasma center. In the hot core, neon approaches full ionization, so the on-axis concentration closely tracks the bare-nucleus population and governs central radiative losses via bremsstrahlung and residual line radiation.

The on-axis value is inferred from vacuum-ultraviolet and soft X-ray spectroscopy or from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy on partially stripped neon charge states, supplemented by impurity transport modeling. For context, [nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis) and [argon_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis) give the analogous on-axis concentrations for neighboring noble-gas impurities used in similar seeding applications.

NAMES.name: net_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net ion momentum source is the net force-per-area source for the total ion population, summed over all ion charge states and all contributing momentum-source processes without projection onto a particular direction.
NAMES.long:
Net ion momentum source is the net source that adds or removes momentum from the total ion population as an unprojected vector quantity. Its value is summed over all ion charge states and represents force per area, not a volumetric force density.

The net ion momentum-source vector is defined as the sum of the charge-state-resolved contributions from all contributing momentum-source processes:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion,net}} = \sum_{\zeta}\sum_{\alpha} \mathbf{S}_{i,\zeta}^{(\alpha)}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion,net}}$ is the net ion momentum source, $\zeta$ labels an ion charge state, $\alpha$ labels a contributing momentum-source process, and $\mathbf{S}_{i,\zeta}^{(\alpha)}$ is the momentum source for charge state $\zeta$ due to process $\alpha$.

This quantity is the total-ion, process-summed vector before any directional projection. A directional child such as [parallel net ion momentum source](name:parallel_net_ion_momentum_source) is a projection of this vector along the local magnetic-field direction; it is not an additional process sum separate from the vector definition. Momentum exchanged only between ion charge states cancels in the charge-state-summed total.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a scalar component or projection of $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion,net}}$ points along the positive direction defined for that component or projection.

NAMES.name: neutral_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms and molecules in the unresolved neutral population. Unless a resolved variant is specified, it aggregates over neutral species, thermal and suprathermal populations, internal quantum states, and parent-ion-associated neutral states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms and molecules in the unresolved neutral population. It is a pointwise volumetric particle density, not a flux-surface-averaged or volume-averaged quantity unless an averaging operation is part of the named quantity.

The local aggregate neutral density is defined by the neutral particle count per volume element:

$$
n_0 = \frac{dN_0}{dV} = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathcal{P}_0} n_\alpha
$$

where $N_0$ is the number of neutral particles in the infinitesimal volume element $dV$, $\mathcal{P}_0$ is the set of neutral population classes included by the unresolved quantity, and $n_\alpha$ is the local density of population class $\alpha$.

For the unresolved name, $\mathcal{P}_0$ includes neutral species, thermal and suprathermal kinetic populations, internal quantum states, and parent-ion-associated neutral states that are not otherwise resolved by the standard name. When only thermal and fast kinetic classes are distinguished, the aggregate satisfies $n_0 = n_{0,\mathrm{thermal}} + n_{0,\mathrm{fast}}$, corresponding to [thermal_neutral_density](name:thermal_neutral_density) and [fast_neutral_density](name:fast_neutral_density). It excludes ions, electrons, and any averaging represented by [volume_averaged_density](name:volume_averaged_neutral_species_density).

NAMES.name: fast_neutral_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Suprathermal neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms and molecules in the suprathermal population, summed over neutral species and internal quantum states.
NAMES.long:
Suprathermal neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms and molecules in the suprathermal, nonthermal population. It is the suprathermal component of [neutral density](name:neutral_density), distinct from [thermal neutral density](name:thermal_neutral_density), and is a pointwise volumetric particle density rather than an averaged quantity.

The local suprathermal neutral density is defined by the neutral particle count per volume element:

$$
n_{0,s} = \frac{dN_{0,s}}{dV} = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathcal{P}_{0,s}} n_{\alpha}
$$

where $N_{0,s}$ is the number of suprathermal neutral particles in the infinitesimal volume element $dV$, $\mathcal{P}_{0,s}$ is the set of included suprathermal neutral population classes, and $n_{\alpha}$ is the local density of population class $\alpha$.

The aggregate includes neutral species and internal quantum states represented within the suprathermal population. It excludes locally thermal neutral particles, ions, electrons, and any averaging operation not specified by the standard name.

NAMES.name: neutral_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Fickian diffusion coefficient for neutral particle transport in edge plasma, relating the diffusive neutral particle flux to the local neutral density gradient without specification of a particular transport direction.
NAMES.long:
The neutral diffusion coefficient quantifies the proportionality between the diffusive flux of neutral particles and the spatial gradient of their number density, abstracting over the directional components that resolve transport along specific geometric axes of the torus. In the strongly anisotropic environment of magnetized edge plasmas, neutral particles interact with the background plasma primarily through charge exchange and ionization, making the effective diffusivity a key parameter governing recycling and fueling dynamics.

The constitutive (Fick's law) relation for the diffusive neutral particle flux density $\Gamma_n$ in a given spatial direction is:

$$
\Gamma_n = -D_n \, \nabla n_n
$$

where $D_n$ is the neutral diffusion coefficient and $n_n$ is the local neutral particle number density. The directional components poloidal_neutral_diffusion_coefficient and [radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient) specialize this relation along the poloidal and radial directions respectively, reflecting the geometric anisotropy of the edge region.

Values of $D_n$ are computed from fluid or kinetic neutral transport models that account for charge-exchange mean free paths and collisional momentum transfer with background ions. The analogous energy transport coefficient is described by [poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), and the charge-state-resolved counterpart appears in [poloidal_neutral_state_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: neutral_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral diffusivity is the scalar Fickian particle diffusivity relating the diffusive flux of neutral particles to the spatial gradient of neutral number density. It applies to an isotropic or direction-averaged closure with no resolved preferred direction and is non-negative for passive diffusion.
NAMES.long:
Neutral diffusivity is the scalar Fickian particle diffusivity for neutral particles. It parameterizes the diffusive part of the neutral particle flux caused by gradients of neutral number density when no directional dependence is resolved. It is non-negative for passive diffusion; a negative scalar would represent an anti-diffusive model term rather than this quantity.

The defining Fickian closure is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{n}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_n \nabla n_n
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{n}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive neutral particle flux, $D_n$ is the neutral diffusivity, and $n_n$ is the neutral number density. The leading minus sign makes the diffusive flux point down the neutral density gradient when $D_n \ge 0$.

This scalar quantity excludes tensor and direction-resolved neutral diffusivities; those retain separate projections instead of collapsing the transport to a single isotropic value. It describes particle transport of neutral number density, not diffusion of neutral internal-state energy or charged-particle transport.

NAMES.name: neutral_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral energy diffusivity is the scalar Fickian coefficient for down-gradient transport of thermal energy carried by neutral particles, independent of transport direction or resolved internal state.
NAMES.long:
Neutral energy diffusivity is the scalar local transport coefficient for diffusive smoothing of thermal-energy density carried by neutral particles. It represents only the Fickian, down-gradient part of neutral energy transport, including neutral atoms and molecules when they are treated as an aggregate population.

The defining closure relates the diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux to the gradient of neutral thermal-energy density:

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,n}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{E,n}\nabla w_n
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,n}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux, $\chi_{E,n}$ is the neutral energy diffusivity, and $w_n$ is the neutral thermal-energy density. The minus sign defines down-gradient transport: positive $\chi_{E,n}$ produces flux from larger $w_n$ toward smaller $w_n$.

This quantity is the direction-independent parent of directional variants such as [poloidal neutral energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity). It excludes convective energy transport, explicit source and sink terms, and distinctions between internal states represented by [neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It is distinct from [neutral diffusivity](name:neutral_diffusivity), which describes particle-number transport rather than thermal-energy transport.

NAMES.name: neutral_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral energy flux is the signed energy-flux density carried by neutral atoms and molecules across an oriented surface, summed over neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral energy flux is the signed component of energy-flux density carried by neutral atoms and molecules normal to an oriented surface. It gives the rate at which the neutral energy reservoir crosses unit area, summed over neutral species and internal states.

For an oriented surface with unit normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, the neutral energy flux $F_{E,\mathrm{n}}$ is defined by

$$
F_{E,\mathrm{n}} = \mathbf{q}_{E,\mathrm{n}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,\mathrm{n}}$ is the neutral energy-flux-density vector and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ defines the positive surface-normal direction.

This quantity is the neutral specialization of [energy flux](name:energy_flux). It includes the energy carried by neutral particle transport, including translational and internal-state contributions when present; [neutral particle flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) counts particle transport without weighting by carried energy. Directional projections are represented by [radial neutral energy flux](name:radial_neutral_energy_flux), [poloidal neutral energy flux](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_flux), and [parallel neutral energy flux](name:parallel_neutral_energy_flux), while [neutral internal-state energy flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) restricts the reservoir to a specified internal state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral energy-flux-density vector has a component in the direction of the chosen unit normal to the oriented surface.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective advection velocity for particle transport in a specified internal state, relating that state’s number density to its convective particle flux.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective velocity assigned to particles in a specified internal state for their convective transport. It is the advective coefficient in the convective particle-flux contribution.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a,\mathrm{conv}} = n_a\boldsymbol{v}_{a,\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective particle flux, $n_a$ is the number density of species or internal state $a$, and $\boldsymbol{v}_{a,\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection velocity.

The quantity is independent of any particular species, internal state, coordinate projection, or flux-coordinate direction. The broader [internal state convection velocity](name:internal_state_convection_velocity) provides the corresponding parent context, while [poloidal neutral internal state convection velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity) is a component-specific instance.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component points along the positive direction of its explicitly defined coordinate basis; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, these directions are $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, and $+\hat{Z}$.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Number density of neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state, summed over all velocity populations including thermal and suprathermal neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Number density of neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state $s$, aggregated over all velocity populations. It is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the complete neutral distribution function restricted to state $s$:

$$
n_s = \int f_s(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the phase-space distribution function of neutral particles in internal state $s$ and the integral spans all velocities.

Summing $n_s$ over all internal quantum states recovers the total [neutral_density](name:neutral_density). The thermal-population subset is given by [thermal_neutral_internal_state_density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density), and the fast-population subset by [fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density). This quantity is the neutral-species specialization of [internal_state_density](name:internal_state_density).

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective signed velocity coefficient for convective transport of energy carried by a specified neutral internal state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective velocity associated with convective transport of the energy density carried by one specified neutral internal state. It is the neutral specialization of the [internal-state energy convection velocity](name:internal_state_energy_convection_velocity), with directional realizations remaining applicable to radial, poloidal, or field-aligned transport.

For each resolved transport direction, the convective energy-flux component is defined by

$$
q_{E,\nu}^{\mathrm{conv}} = u_{E,\nu}^{\mathrm{conv}} w_{E,\nu}
$$

where $q_{E,\nu}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective energy-flux component, $u_{E,\nu}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection velocity, $w_{E,\nu}$ is the energy density of the neutral internal state, and $\nu$ identifies that state. The quantity applies to the specified state and does not sum over all neutral states. By contrast, [neutral species energy convection velocity](name:neutral_species_energy_convection_velocity) represents the corresponding energy transport aggregated over a neutral species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective velocity points in the positive orientation assigned to the resolved transport direction, making the convective energy flux positive in that direction.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient multiplying the temperature gradient of neutral particles in one internal state in diffusive thermal-energy transport, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its radial and poloidal component forms.
NAMES.long:
Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar diffusivity that relates Fickian diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in a specified internal state to the temperature gradient of those same particles. It is resolved for one internal state, not summed or averaged over internal states, and is independent of any chosen spatial projection.

The isotropic Fickian contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s} = - n_{n,s} D_{E,n,s} \nabla T_{n,s}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, $n_{n,s}$ is their number density, $D_{E,n,s}$ is this coefficient, and $T_{n,s}$ is their temperature.

The coefficient includes only the Fickian term driven by $\nabla T_{n,s}$ and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, and effective coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. It specializes the [internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) to neutral particles and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [neutral energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

As the direction-agnostic parent, it is distinct from the [radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), where radial denotes the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Signed surface-normal energy flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state, encompassing contributions from kinetic, thermal, and internal-state energy.
NAMES.long:
The neutral internal state energy flux is the signed surface-normal energy flux density transported by neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state (electronic, vibrational, or rotational level). It is the neutral-species restriction of the more general [internal_state_energy_flux](name:internal_state_energy_flux), selecting only uncharged particles and accumulating their directed kinetic, thermal, and internal-state energy contributions.

The flux density is defined as:

$$
q_{n,s} = \hat{n} \cdot \int f_{n,s}(\mathbf{v}) \left( \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + \epsilon_s \right) \mathbf{v} \, d^3v
$$

where $\hat{n}$ is the outward unit normal to the reference surface, $f_{n,s}$ is the velocity distribution of neutrals in internal state $s$, $m$ is the neutral particle mass, $\epsilon_s$ is the energy of internal state $s$, and $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity.

Component-resolved forms are [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) along the poloidal direction and [parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) along the local magnetic field. The analogous number flux without energy weighting is [neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when net energy transport is directed along the outward unit normal $\hat{n}$ to the reference surface.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient is the vector kinematic transport coefficient in Fick's-law down-gradient transport of momentum density carried by neutrals in a specified electronic, vibrational, or rotational state. Its directional children specify the flux and gradient direction, not the transported momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient is the vector kinematic transport coefficient in Fick's-law down-gradient transport of momentum density carried by neutrals occupying a specified electronic, vibrational, or rotational internal state. It is the direction-agnostic parent whose directional members identify the direction of flux and gradient, while the transported quantity remains the full momentum vector of that state-resolved neutral population.

For a diagonal directional member in transport direction $j$, the defining Fick law is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha j} = -D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha j}\,\frac{\partial \mathbf{M}_{\alpha}}{\partial x_j}
$$

where $\alpha$ denotes the specified neutral internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha j}$ is the vector diffusive flux of momentum through surfaces normal to direction $j$, $D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha j}$ is the corresponding diagonal momentum diffusion coefficient, $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$ is the momentum density carried by neutrals in state $\alpha$, and $x_j$ is a coordinate increasing along the flux and gradient direction. The superscript $\mathrm{mom}$ labels momentum transport, not a transported momentum component; the minus sign gives down-gradient transport of each component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$.

This parent covers diagonal directional coefficients only: a directional qualifier selects $j$, the flux and gradient direction, and not a component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$; off-diagonal tensor transport, where a gradient along one direction contributes to flux through another, is outside this standard name. The radial and toroidal directional children use $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the poloidal directional child uses the direction tangent to the poloidal circuit in a meridional plane spanned by $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$.

The defining gradient is the gradient of internal-state momentum density; a form proportional only to a neutral velocity gradient represents the same coefficient only when the state-resolved mass density is uniform or treated outside the gradient. This quantity belongs to the [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity) family, has the same internal-state resolution as [internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient](name:internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), differs from [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) by resolving the neutral population by internal state, and differs from [neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) by transporting momentum rather than energy.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vector flux-limiter coefficient that sets an edge-region, nonnegative componentwise cap on neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a specified internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming bound, without reversing any flux component.
NAMES.long:
Vector flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles occupying a specified internal state over the edge region is the set of directional coefficients used to bound components of the corresponding neutral internal-state momentum-flux density. The internal state may be an electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation state, and the coefficient applies separately to each physical direction used to decompose the momentum-flux vector.

For directional component $k$, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},k}| \le \lambda_k\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},k}|,\qquad 0 \le \lambda_k \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},k}$ is the limited directional component of the neutral internal-state momentum flux over the edge region, $\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},k}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming component whose magnitude defines the bound, $\lambda_k$ is this coefficient component, and $k$ indexes a physical direction rather than the internal state. If a component is specified in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, then $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from $+\hat{Z}$, $Z$ is vertical height, and $k$ may identify an $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ projection; field-aligned components use their explicitly named local directions, such as parallel to the magnetic field.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the realized momentum flux. Because $\lambda_k$ is nonnegative, applying the limiter may reduce or bound a signed momentum-flux component but does not reverse its direction; a nonzero limited component retains the sign of the underlying component to which the cap is applied. This coefficient is not the momentum-flux vector itself and is distinct from limiters for particle flux or energy flux.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Area-normalized vector momentum source for a neutral species in a single resolved internal state is the collisional momentum transfer to that neutral population. It includes charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic collisions.
NAMES.long:
Area-normalized vector momentum source for a neutral species in a single resolved internal state is the collisional momentum transfer to that neutral population after normalization by the transport area. It represents the vector rate at which charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic collisions add momentum to, or remove momentum from, that resolved neutral state.

The defining process decomposition is:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{(p)} = \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{cx}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{ion}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{rec}} + \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{el}}
$$

where \(\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}^{(p)}\) is this momentum source for neutral species \(n\) in internal state \(\alpha\), and the terms on the right are the contributions from charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic collisions, respectively.

The quantity is resolved for one neutral species and one internal state; it is not the state-summed [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source), which is obtained by summing this vector over all resolved internal states of that neutral species. It is the neutral-state analog of the [ion charge-state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), with resolution by internal state rather than ion charge state. A directional component such as the [radial neutral-internal-state momentum source](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) is the projection of this vector onto the corresponding direction; `radial` denotes the \(\hat{R}\) component in the right-handed cylindrical \((R, \phi, Z)\) frame with basis \((\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})\).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a vector component represents momentum transferred to the neutral species in the resolved internal state along the positive basis direction used for that component; in the right-handed cylindrical \((R, \phi, Z)\) frame with basis \((\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})\), the radial, toroidal, and vertical components are positive along \(+\hat{R}\), increasing toroidal angle \(\phi\), and \(+\hat{Z}\), respectively.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Velocity characterizing convective momentum transport by neutral particles in a resolved internal quantum state, forming the bulk-flow coefficient in the neutral internal-state momentum flux equation.
NAMES.long:
The neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity is the fluid velocity at which momentum is transported by bulk convective flow in a neutral particle population that is resolved by internal quantum state (such as a vibrational, rotational, or electronic level). It enters the neutral momentum transport equation as the convective coefficient of the state-resolved momentum flux:

$$
\Pi_{\rm conv,s} = m_n n_s v_{\rm conv,s}
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_s$ is the number density of internal state $s$, and $v_{\rm conv,s}$ is this convection velocity for state $s$.

This is the neutral-species-specific form of the internal-state momentum convection velocity, enabling state-resolved neutral momentum transport to be tracked separately from ionic or electron channels. Its effective counterpart, [effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection), incorporates transport contributions beyond simple bulk advection that enter the convective momentum channel. For comparison, [neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection) describes the corresponding convective velocity for particle (number) transport rather than momentum transport.

NAMES.name: effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective advective drift velocity of neutral particles in a specified internal state for convective momentum transport; it multiplies the population's momentum density to form the convective momentum flux.
NAMES.long:
Effective advective drift velocity of neutral particles in a specified internal state for convective momentum transport is the vector transport coefficient that multiplies the population's momentum-density vector to give the convective momentum-flux tensor. It represents the advective velocity appearing in a momentum-transport closure for that resolved neutral internal-state population.

The convective momentum flux is defined by the outer-product relation

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\alpha} = \boldsymbol{g}_{\alpha} \otimes \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\alpha}$ is the convective momentum-flux tensor of neutral particles in internal state $\alpha$, $\boldsymbol{g}_{\alpha}$ is their momentum-density vector, and $\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}$ is this effective convective momentum velocity.

The effective qualifier means the coefficient is defined by this momentum-flux closure and need not equal the neutral population's microscopic mean particle velocity. It is the momentum-transport analog of [effective neutral internal-state velocity due to convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection), which enters the convective particle-flux relation, and is distinguished from the non-effective counterpart [neutral internal-state momentum velocity due to convection](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection). This name denotes the full vector; [radial effective neutral internal-state momentum velocity due to convection](name:radial_effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection) denotes its cylindrical $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a vector component of $\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}$ is aligned with the positive direction of the corresponding explicitly chosen basis vector.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_number_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Number density of neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state, covering all velocity-distribution subpopulations of the neutral species.
NAMES.long:
The neutral internal state number density $n_0(s)$ is the number of neutral particles per unit volume occupying a specified internal quantum state $s$, where $s$ labels an electronic, vibrational, or rotational level of the neutral atom or molecule.

$$
n_0(s) = \int f_0(\mathbf{v}, s) \, d^3v
$$

where $f_0(\mathbf{v}, s)$ is the phase-space distribution function of neutral particles in state $s$ and $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity. Decomposing by velocity population, [fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density) gives the suprathermal contribution from neutrals with energies well above thermal; [thermal_neutral_internal_state_density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density) covers the Maxwellian subpopulation. Summing $n_0(s)$ over all internal states recovers the species-total neutral number density, as in [thermal_neutral_density](name:thermal_neutral_density) for the thermal subpopulation. This quantity is the neutral-species restriction of [internal_state_number_density](name:internal_state_number_density), which spans charged and neutral particles alike; ionized charge states at any ionization stage are excluded.

NAMES.name: fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Number density of fast neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state.
NAMES.long:
Number density of fast neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state is the local density of neutral atoms or molecules in state $q$ whose velocities belong to the suprathermal neutral population. It is the fast-population contribution to the [neutral internal-state density](name:neutral_internal_state_density) for the same internal state and excludes the thermal neutral population.

It is defined by integrating the internal-state-resolved neutral phase-space density over the fast-neutral region of velocity space:

$$
n_{0,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{fast}}} f_{0,q}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{0,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast neutral internal-state number density, $f_{0,q}$ is the phase-space density of neutral particles in internal quantum state $q$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the velocity-space domain assigned to suprathermal neutrals.

The thermal counterpart is [thermal neutral internal-state density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density). Summing $n_{0,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ over all internal states $q$ gives the [fast neutral density](name:fast_neutral_density).

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Signed surface-normal particle flux density of neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state, giving the net number crossing unit area per unit time.
NAMES.long:
The neutral internal-state particle flux is the surface-normal component of the particle flux vector for neutral atoms or molecules occupying a specified internal quantum state (such as a vibrational, rotational, or electronic level). It quantifies the net number of neutral particles in that state crossing an oriented surface element per unit area per unit time, and specializes [internal_state_particle_flux](name:internal_state_particle_flux) to the neutral-particle subpopulation.

The defining relation for neutral species $\alpha$ in internal state $s$ is:

$$
\Gamma_{\alpha,s} = \int f_{\alpha,s}(\mathbf{v})\, \mathbf{v} \cdot \hat{n} \, d^3v
$$

where $f_{\alpha,s}$ is the velocity distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity, and $\hat{n}$ is the unit normal to the reference surface. Summing $\Gamma_{\alpha,s}$ over all internal states $s$ recovers the total neutral particle flux for species $\alpha$.

Projected onto specific coordinate directions, this quantity yields [radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) and the equivalently defined poloidal and magnetic-field-parallel components. The energy transported by the same state-resolved neutral population is captured by [neutral_internal_state_energy_flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net neutral particle flow is in the direction of $\hat{n}$.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral internal-state power density due to collisions is the net volumetric rate at which collisions transfer energy to or from neutral particles in a specified internal state. It is neutral-specific but not restricted to atomic neutrals.
NAMES.long:
Neutral internal-state power density due to collisions is the net local rate at which collisional interactions transfer energy into or out of the population of neutral particles occupying a specified internal state. The neutral population may be further specialized by species or particle class, but the quantity itself applies to neutral particles as a class.

The net collisional contribution can be written as a sum over collisional channels affecting the specified neutral internal state:

$$
Q_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_c \Delta E_{\alpha c} \, \mathcal{R}_c^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $Q_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the neutral internal-state power density due to collisions for neutral population $n$ and internal state $\alpha$, $\Delta E_{\alpha c}$ is the energy change assigned to that neutral internal state in collisional channel $c$, and $\mathcal{R}_c^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the local occurrence-rate density of that channel.

This quantity is the neutral-particle specialization of [internal-state power density due to collisions](name:internal_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and excludes charged-particle internal-state populations. It is broader than [atomic neutral internal-state power density due to collisions](name:atomic_neutral_internal_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), which restricts the neutral population to atomic neutrals.
NAMES.sign: Positive when collisional interactions add energy to the specified neutral internal-state population.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure contributed by neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state, including thermal and nonthermal velocity-space contributions.
NAMES.long:
Neutral internal-state pressure is the state-resolved scalar kinetic pressure of neutral atoms or molecules occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state. It is a partial pressure, not a sum over all internal states, and can include thermal and nonthermal velocity-space contributions.

For state $a$, the pressure is the one-third trace of the central second velocity-space moment:

$$
p_a = \frac{m_a}{3}\int \lvert\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_a\rvert^2 f_a(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_a$ is the particle mass, $f_a(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of neutrals in state $a$, and $\mathbf{u}_a$ is its mean velocity. The central moment excludes dynamic pressure from directed bulk flow. Thermal and suprathermal contributions may be separated, while [total neutral internal-state pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) combines them. The quantity is a neutral-specific instance of [internal-state pressure](name:internal_state_pressure), and its associated kinetic temperature is [neutral internal-state temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature).

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_source_rate
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Net volumetric particle source rate for a neutral species in a specified internal quantum state, equal to the local creation rate minus loss rate due to collisional and radiative atomic processes.
NAMES.long:
The neutral internal-state source rate is the net volumetric rate at which neutral particles enter or leave a specified internal quantum state — such as an electronic excitation level or, for molecular neutrals, a vibrational or rotational level — due to processes including ionization, recombination, charge exchange, excitation, and de-excitation. It is the neutral-species specialization of [internal_state_source_rate](name:internal_state_source_rate) and the neutral analog of [ion_state_source_rate](name:ion_state_source_rate).

This quantity enters the state-resolved neutral continuity equation:

$$
\frac{\partial n_{n,q}}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot (n_{n,q}\,\mathbf{v}_{n,q}) = S_{n,q}
$$

where $n_{n,q}$ is the number density of neutral particles in internal state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{n,q}$ is their fluid velocity, and $S_{n,q}$ is the net source rate. A negative value indicates net depletion of state $q$ by the dominant atomic processes.

This is a per-state, per-species quantity and is distinct from source rates summed over all internal states or over all neutral species.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_temperature
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Kinetic temperature of neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state, determined from their random translational motion.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the kinetic temperature of neutral particles restricted to one specified internal quantum or excitation state. It characterizes random translational motion, not the energy spacing or population of the internal state.

For an isotropic state-resolved velocity distribution, the energy-equivalent temperature is defined by

$$
T_{n,s} = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle \frac{1}{2}m_n\lvert\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{n,s}\rvert^2 \right\rangle_s
$$

where $T_{n,s}$ is the neutral temperature in state $s$, $m_n$ is the neutral-particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{n,s}$ is the bulk velocity of that state-resolved population, and the brackets denote an average over particles in state $s$.

This is the neutral-species component of [internal_state_temperature](name:internal_state_temperature). It is distinct from [neutral_internal_state_pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure), which also depends on the state-resolved particle density.

NAMES.name: neutral_internal_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy state, given by the first moment of their velocity distribution.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles occupying one specified internal state, such as a quantum or energy state. It retains resolution of that state rather than combining distinct neutral internal states.

The state-resolved bulk velocity is the first velocity moment of the corresponding distribution:

$$
\mathbf{u}_{\alpha} = \frac{\int \mathbf{v}\,f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}{\int f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}$ is the bulk velocity, $\alpha$ identifies the internal state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{\alpha}$ is the velocity distribution for that state.

This is the neutral specialization of [internal_state_velocity](name:internal_state_velocity). Unlike [neutral_velocity](name:neutral_velocity), which may combine or resolve internal states, this quantity is defined for one specified state. The full vector is the parent quantity for projections such as [radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity) and [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a component points along its corresponding positive unit vector $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy state, given by the first moment of their velocity distribution.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles occupying one specified internal state, such as a quantum or energy state. It retains resolution of that state rather than combining distinct neutral internal states.

The state-resolved bulk velocity is the first velocity moment of the corresponding distribution:

$$
\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{bulk}} = \frac{\int \mathbf{v}\,f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}{\int f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{bulk}}$ is the bulk velocity, $\alpha$ identifies the internal state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{\alpha}$ is the velocity distribution for that state.

This quantity is the neutral specialization of [internal-state velocity](name:internal_state_velocity) with the bulk-fluid moment made explicit. The full vector is the parent quantity for component projections such as [vertical bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a component points along its corresponding positive unit vector $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective vector velocity at which neutral particle momentum is advectively transported in edge-plasma fluid models, aggregated over all neutral species and excited states as a transport closure coefficient distinct from the actual neutral particle flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
The neutral momentum convection velocity is the effective bulk vector velocity appearing in the non-diffusive, advective contribution to neutral momentum transport in edge-plasma and scrape-off-layer fluid models. It encapsulates the net effect of charge-exchange, ionization, and recombination reactions on the aggregate neutral momentum balance across all neutral species and excited states, serving as a transport closure coefficient rather than the physical flow speed of any individual neutral population.

In multi-fluid edge-plasma transport frameworks, the total neutral momentum flux is decomposed into a diffusive part proportional to the local momentum-density gradient and a convective (pinch-like) part proportional to the momentum density:

$$
\mathbf{F}_p = -D_p \nabla p_n + \mathbf{V}_c \, p_n
$$

where $D_p$ is the neutral momentum diffusivity and $p_n$ is the neutral momentum density. The convection velocity $\mathbf{V}_c$ (this quantity) drives advective momentum transport independently of the local gradient, functioning as a neutral momentum pinch.

The quantity is computed in fluid neutral transport solvers as a closure derived from atomic physics rate coefficients and the local plasma state. Its directional projections include the radial_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity ($R$ component) and the vertical_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity ($Z$ component) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The analogous charge-state-resolved quantity is [radial_neutral_state_effective_momentum_convection_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity). The parent [momentum_convection_velocity](name:momentum_convection_velocity) establishes the general momentum-flux decomposition framework from which this neutral-species specialization is derived.
NAMES.sign: Positive radial, toroidal, and vertical components correspond to velocity directed in the $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, and $+\hat{Z}$ directions of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, respectively.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vector diffusion coefficient governing diffusive transport of momentum in the neutral particle population, with directional components representing anisotropic momentum diffusivities along the radial, poloidal, and toroidal directions.
NAMES.long:
The neutral momentum diffusion coefficient quantifies the effective diffusivity that drives collisional and turbulent spreading of neutral-particle momentum down local velocity gradients. As a vector quantity, its components represent the diagonal entries of the momentum diffusion tensor for neutrals in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, capturing anisotropy across the radial, poloidal, and toroidal directions independently.

The diffusive neutral momentum flux density along direction $\hat{e}_i$ is governed by:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{diff},i} = -\rho_n \, D_{\mathrm{mom},i} \, \frac{\partial u_{n,i}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\rho_n$ is the neutral mass density, $u_{n,i}$ is the neutral flow velocity component along $\hat{e}_i$, and $D_{\mathrm{mom},i}$ is the corresponding directional component of this coefficient.

In edge plasma modeling, the dominant physical mechanisms determining this diffusivity are charge-exchange with background ions, neutral-neutral collisions, and elastic scattering; the resulting coefficient is strongly anisotropic in realistic magnetic geometries. The [radial_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) gives the cross-field component driving transport across magnetic flux surfaces. For comparison, the analogous momentum diffusivity for the bulk plasma is captured by plasma_momentum_diffusivity, and the toroidal ion channel counterpart is described by toroidal_momentum_diffusivity.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vector diffusion coefficient for bulk neutral-particle momentum, governing anisotropic diffusive redistribution driven by neutral-neutral viscosity and charge-exchange collisions in edge and divertor plasma.
NAMES.long:
Neutral momentum diffusivity is the direction-dependent transport coefficient that relates the diffusive neutral-fluid momentum flux in each spatial direction to the local gradient of neutral momentum density, forming the neutral-particle analog of plasma_momentum_diffusivity. As a vector quantity it encompasses distinct directional components — including [parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), [poloidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), [toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), and [vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity) — reflecting the anisotropy imposed by the magnetic geometry and the varying collisional regimes of edge and divertor regions.

The component $\chi_{n,\mathrm{mom}}$ along a direction $\hat{e}$ enters the neutral fluid momentum balance through the diffusive flux:

$$
\Gamma_{n,\mathrm{mom}} = -\chi_{n,\mathrm{mom}} \, \nabla_{\hat{e}}(m_n n_n u_n)
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number density, and $u_n$ is the neutral fluid velocity component along $\hat{e}$.

The dominant physical mechanisms contributing to neutral momentum diffusivity are neutral-neutral viscous collisions and charge-exchange interactions with background ions; the latter can transfer substantial momentum between the neutral and ion populations and are especially significant in dense regions where charge-exchange mean-free paths are short. This coefficient is computed within fluid-neutral transport models that solve the neutral momentum equation self-consistently alongside the plasma fluid equations.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Rate per unit area at which neutral atoms and molecules transport linear momentum across an oriented surface in the edge plasma, combining convective and isotropic-pressure contributions summed over all neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
The neutral momentum flux describes the rate at which the collective neutral population transports linear momentum across a unit area of an oriented surface in the edge plasma. It captures both the directed convective flow of neutral particles and the isotropic thermal pressure of the neutral gas, aggregated over all neutral species and their internal quantum states.

The neutral momentum-flux tensor $\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n$ is:

$$
\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n = m_n n_n \mathbf{v}_n \mathbf{v}_n + p_n \mathbf{I}
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number density, $\mathbf{v}_n$ is the bulk neutral velocity, $p_n = n_n k_B T_n$ is the neutral thermal pressure with $T_n$ the neutral temperature, and $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor. The divergence of this tensor drives the neutral momentum balance equation and couples neutral dynamics to the ion fluid through charge-exchange and elastic collisions.

This quantity is evaluated within edge fluid or kinetic neutral transport models rather than measured directly. Directional projections include toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux, [poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux), [vertical_neutral_momentum_flux](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux), and [parallel_neutral_momentum_flux](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux) along the local magnetic-field direction. The analogous ion-fluid momentum transport rate is [radial_edge_ion_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_momentum_flux_over_edge_region), while the effective convective transport coefficient for neutral momentum is radial_neutral_effective_momentum_convection_velocity.

NAMES.name: neutral_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Area-normalized vector momentum source density for the neutral population, summed over all neutral internal states, giving the net directed rate of momentum transfer.
NAMES.long:
Area-normalized vector momentum source density for the neutral population is the net directed rate of momentum transfer to all neutral internal states.

The aggregate source is the sum of the contributions from each resolved neutral internal state:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{n}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{N}}\mathbf{S}_{n,a}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{n}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum source density, $\mathcal{N}$ is the set of neutral internal states, and $\mathbf{S}_{n,a}$ is the [neutral internal-state momentum source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) for state $a$. It is the neutral specialization of the general [momentum source](name:momentum_source), and its projections include the [poloidal neutral momentum source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source) and toroidal counterpart.

The quantity is summed over neutral internal states and is not a single-state source. Its vector direction is retained rather than reduced to a magnitude.
NAMES.sign: Positive when each resolved component points along its designated positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, or along the local magnetic-field direction for a parallel projection.

NAMES.name: neutral_source_rate
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Net local volumetric rate of neutral-particle creation minus loss, serving as the source term in the neutral-particle balance.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net local production rate of neutral particles, combining all included creation and loss processes. Positive values denote net neutral-particle creation, while negative values denote net loss.

The net source rate is defined by

$$
S_n = S_{n,\mathrm{create}} - S_{n,\mathrm{loss}}
$$

where $S_n$ is the net neutral-particle source rate, $S_{n,\mathrm{create}}$ is the local volumetric creation rate, and $S_{n,\mathrm{loss}}$ is the local volumetric loss rate. It is the source term in the neutral-particle continuity equation and is distinct from the [particle source rate](name:particle_source_rate) for a general plasma distribution.

This quantity is not restricted to one specified internal quantum state; a state-resolved contribution is represented by the [neutral internal-state source rate](name:neutral_internal_state_source_rate).

NAMES.name: neutral_species_atomic_mass
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Atomic mass of a neutral particle species, identifying its isotope or composition and setting the inertial mass scale for neutral transport and collisional calculations.
NAMES.long:
Atomic mass of a neutral species is the rest-mass scale assigned to an uncharged atom or molecule, determined by its isotope and elemental or molecular composition. It specializes [atomic mass](name:atomic_mass) to neutral species and sets the inertia used in transport, collisional, and momentum relations.

The numerical atomic mass is represented by

$$
m_s = A_s\,u
$$

where $m_s$ is the atomic mass of neutral species $s$, $A_s$ is its dimensionless numerical atomic mass, and $u$ is the unified atomic mass unit, defined as one-twelfth of the mass of a neutral carbon-12 atom.

This quantity applies to neutral atoms and molecules and excludes ionic charge-state effects. It is distinct from [ion atomic mass](name:ion_atomic_mass), which applies to an ion species, and from [ion mass number](name:ion_mass_number), which is the integer nucleon count.
