NAMES.name: parallel_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Projection of the ion energy flux vector onto the local magnetic field direction, giving the field-aligned component of ion thermal and kinetic energy transport.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion energy flux quantifies the rate at which ion energy is transported per unit area along the magnetic field direction $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$. Field-aligned ion transport dominates cross-field transport in the collisional edge and scrape-off layer, making this quantity a key term in the parallel ion energy balance and a primary driver of heat loads at divertor targets.

From Braginskii fluid closure, the parallel energy flux density combines convective and conductive contributions:

$$
q_{\parallel,i} = \frac{5}{2} n_i T_i v_{\parallel,i} - \kappa_{\parallel,i} \nabla_\parallel T_i
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $T_i$ is the ion temperature in energy units, $v_{\parallel,i}$ is the parallel ion fluid velocity, and $\kappa_{\parallel,i}$ is the parallel ion thermal conductivity. The first term represents enthalpy convection and the second is Fourier conduction along the field.

This flux appears as a divergence contribution in the ion energy conservation equation and is the primary carrier of ion thermal energy toward divertor targets in attached plasma regimes. For the charge-state-resolved counterpart, see parallel_ion_state_energy_flux; the species-summed total is [parallel_total_ion_energy_flux](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_flux). The electron analog is [parallel_electron_energy_flux](name:parallel_electron_energy_flux) and the neutral contribution is [parallel_neutral_energy_flux](name:parallel_neutral_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when energy is transported in the direction of the magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective field-aligned convection velocity that advects the parallel component of ion momentum density for a specified ion species, represented by a density-weighted mean over all charge states. Parallel identifies both transported momentum and velocity direction.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion momentum convection velocity is the parallel effective velocity that advects the parallel component of ion momentum density for a specified ion species. The parallel direction follows the local magnetic-field direction, so the velocity direction and transported momentum component coincide. Because this is an intensive coefficient for a species-level quantity, it is represented as the density-weighted mean over all charge states unless a charge-state-resolved quantity is named.

For the parallel ion-momentum component, the advective contribution to its field-aligned flux is

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,\parallel},\parallel} = p_{i,\parallel} V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{i,M,\parallel}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species, $p_{i,\parallel}$ is its parallel momentum density, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,\parallel},\parallel}$ is the field-aligned component of the non-diffusive convective flux, and $V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{i,M,\parallel}$ is this velocity. The parent [ion momentum convection velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity) gives the same closure without selecting the parallel projection. The [parallel ion charge state momentum convection velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) resolves one ionization state, whereas [parallel ion velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity) is the bulk-flow velocity rather than this transport coefficient.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{i,M,\parallel}$ points along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical dissipation of the field-aligned component of bulk ion fluid momentum.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation timescale at which the field-aligned component of ordered bulk ion fluid momentum is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. It quantifies momentum relaxation along the local magnetic-field direction.

In the ion fluid momentum balance, the damping contribution is defined by

$$
\left.\frac{\partial p_{i,\parallel}}{\partial t}\right|_{\rm damp}=-\nu_{D,\parallel}^{\,i}p_{i,\parallel}
$$

where $p_{i,\parallel}=\mathbf{p}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the field-aligned ion momentum density, $\mathbf{p}_i=m_i n_i\mathbf{v}_i$, $m_i$ is ion mass, $n_i$ is ion number density, $\mathbf{v}_i$ is bulk ion velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the local magnetic-field unit vector. The rate aggregates the represented ion species and charge states.

This component is a member of the vector quantity [ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate) and contrasts with the charge-state-resolved [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the rate coefficient reduces the magnitude of the field-aligned ion momentum component, producing exponential relaxation toward zero.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Diffusion coefficient relating the diffusive parallel ion momentum flux to the local parallel ion momentum density gradient, expressing the rate at which diffusive processes redistribute parallel momentum within the total ion population summed over charge states.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion momentum diffusivity $D_{\parallel}^i$ is the effective diffusion coefficient characterizing down-gradient redistribution of the parallel component of momentum within the total ion population summed over all charge states. The parallel component is the signed projection along the unit vector tangent to the magnetic field, so this coefficient isolates the field-aligned channel of ion momentum diffusion. It is the parallel member of [ion momentum diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity).

The diffusive parallel ion momentum flux density $\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom},i}$ satisfies the momentum-density-gradient convention:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom},i} = -D_{\parallel}^i \, \nabla_{\parallel} p_{\parallel i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom},i}$ is the signed flux density of parallel ion momentum along the magnetic-field direction, $p_{\parallel i}$ is the charge-state-summed parallel ion momentum density, and $\nabla_{\parallel}=\hat{b}\cdot\nabla$ is the derivative along the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$. The leading minus sign specifies the down-gradient convention for the diffusive contribution.

This quantity is charge-state aggregated for ions and does not resolve separate ionization states; the charge-state-resolved counterpart is [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). It is directionally distinct from [poloidal ion momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity) and [vertical ion momentum diffusivity](name:vertical_ion_momentum_diffusivity), and it differs from [parallel ion diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_diffusivity), which describes particle-number diffusion rather than momentum diffusion.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged flux density of total-ion linear momentum projected along the local magnetic field and transported across magnetic flux surfaces, summed over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion momentum flux is the flux-surface-averaged flux density of total-ion linear momentum projected along the local magnetic-field direction and transported across magnetic flux surfaces. It is the parallel-momentum projection of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), not a flux directed along the magnetic field; the transport direction is flux-surface normal.

The defining flux-surface average is:

$$
\Pi_{\rho\parallel}^{\mathrm{ion}} = \left\langle \hat{\mathbf n}_{\rho} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{ion}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf b} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the total ion momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\rho}$ is the unit normal toward increasing flux-surface label $\rho$, $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along magnetic field $\mathbf B$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a flux-surface average in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. The ion sum includes convective, pressure, viscous, and turbulent stress contributions over all ion species and charge states. Unlike [poloidal ion momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux), this quantity projects the transported momentum along the magnetic field.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ion momentum projected along the local magnetic field is transported in the outward flux-surface-normal direction toward increasing $\rho$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Charge-state-averaged ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the local magnetic-field direction, using the density-weighted first velocity moment of all included ionization charge states.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion velocity represents the local magnetic-field-aligned component of the charge-state-averaged ion bulk flow. It is the field-aligned resolution of [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity), rather than the velocity of a single ionization charge state.

$$
V_{i,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf V_i=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\frac{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}\mathbf V_{i,Z}}{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}}
$$

Here $V_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion velocity, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathbf V_i$ is the charge-state-averaged ion velocity, $n_{i,Z}$ is the number density of ion charge state $Z$, and $\mathbf V_{i,Z}$ is that charge state's bulk velocity. The sum includes all included ionization charge states. Unlike [parallel ion charge-state velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity), this quantity is not resolved to one selected charge state; it complements geometric components such as [radial ion velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion flow points along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Parallel projection of the gage-dependent magnetic vector potential along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction, retaining its signed component.
NAMES.long:
The parallel component $A_\\parallel$ is the signed projection of the gage-dependent [magnetic vector potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential) $\\mathbf{A}$ onto the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction. It retains the component relevant to field-aligned electromagnetic dynamics and is distinct from the [parallel magnetic field](name:parallel_magnetic_field).

The defining projection is:

$$
A_\\parallel = \\mathbf{A} \\cdot \\hat{b}
$$

where $\\hat{b}$ is the unit vector directed along the local equilibrium magnetic field. Because only the curl of $\\mathbf{A}$ is directly physical, $A_\\parallel$ is gage dependent and changes under a gage transformation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\\mathbf{A}$ has a component in the direction of $\\hat{b}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_net_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Parallel net ion momentum source is the net force-per-area source for the total ion population projected along the local magnetic field. It is summed over all charge states and all contributing physical processes.
NAMES.long:
Parallel net ion momentum source is the net force-per-area source for the total ion population projected along the local magnetic field. It is the field-aligned scalar component of the net vector source and represents the algebraic addition or removal of ion momentum by all contributing physical processes.

The field-aligned projection is defined by

$$
S_{\parallel i}^{\mathrm{net}} = \hat{b} \cdot \mathbf{S}_{i}^{\mathrm{net}}
$$

where $S_{\parallel i}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the parallel net ion momentum source, $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{S}_{i}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the [net ion momentum source](name:net_ion_momentum_source) vector for the total ion population.

The quantity is summed over all charge states of the total ion population; [parallel ion charge-state momentum source](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_source) is the corresponding charge-state-resolved parallel source. The [ion momentum source](name:ion_momentum_source) is the broader ion-momentum-source quantity, whereas this name fixes both net aggregation over contributing processes and projection along $\hat{b}$. The area normalization is the transport-surface area associated with the source term; it is not an area defined along a magnetic field line.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net source adds momentum to the total ion population in the direction of $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel neutral energy flux is the signed energy-flux density carried by neutral atoms and molecules, projected along the local magnetic-field direction and summed over neutral species and states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral energy flux is the scalar projection of the vector energy-flux density carried by neutral particles onto the local magnetic-field direction. It includes convective enthalpy, bulk-flow kinetic-energy, and conductive transport and is the parallel member of [neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux).

With $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$, its fluid expression is:

$$
q_{E,n}^{\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\sum_s\left[n_s\mathbf v_s\left(h_s+\frac{1}{2}m_s|\mathbf v_s|^2\right)-\boldsymbol{\kappa}_s\cdot\nabla T_s\right]
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the dimensionless unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$ (T), $s$ indexes neutral species or internal states, $n_s$ is number density (m$^{-3}$), $\mathbf v_s$ is flow velocity (m s$^{-1}$), $h_s$ is enthalpy per particle (J), $m_s$ is particle mass (kg), $T_s$ is temperature (K), and $\boldsymbol{\kappa}_s$ is the thermal-conductivity tensor. The sum covers all neutral species and states. Unlike [parallel neutral internal state energy flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux), this quantity is not resolved by internal state; unlike [radial neutral energy flux](name:radial_neutral_energy_flux), it is projected along the magnetic field rather than across flux surfaces.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral energy is transported in the direction of the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf B$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Field-line-parallel particle diffusivity for neutral particles in a specified internal state, relating their diffusive particle flux to the gradient of state-resolved number density.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the particle diffusivity of neutral particles resolved to a specified internal state and projected along the local magnetic-field direction. It describes particle-number transport rather than momentum transport or an aggregate over internal states.

The parallel diffusive particle flux is defined by Fick's law:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,s} = -D_{\parallel,s}\nabla_{\parallel} n_s
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,s}$ is the field-line-parallel diffusive particle flux for internal state $s$, $D_{\parallel,s}$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of that state, and $\nabla_{\parallel}=\mathbf{b}\cdot\nabla$ is the derivative along the magnetic-field unit vector $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

This is the directional counterpart of [neutral internal-state diffusivity]; it excludes the separate momentum-transport quantity [parallel neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Field-aligned effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density of a specified neutral internal state, directed along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Field-aligned effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density of a specified neutral internal state is the component of the effective convection velocity parallel to the local magnetic-field vector. It is the field-aligned realization of [neutral internal-state energy convection velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity), complementary to the [radial](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity) and [poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity) realizations.

For the field-aligned direction, the convective energy-flux component is defined by

$$
q_{E,\nu,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = u_{E,\nu,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} w_{E,\nu}
$$

where $q_{E,\nu,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-aligned convective energy-flux component, $u_{E,\nu,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection velocity, $w_{E,\nu}$ is the energy density of the neutral internal state, and $\nu$ identifies that state.

The quantity applies to the specified internal state and does not sum over all neutral states. By contrast, [neutral species energy convection velocity](name:neutral_species_energy_convection_velocity) represents the corresponding energy transport aggregated over a neutral species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective velocity points in the direction of the local magnetic-field vector, making the field-aligned convective energy flux positive in that direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective diagonal diffusivity for neutral-state energy transport along the magnetic field direction, as the parallel component of the neutral internal-state energy diffusivity tensor.
NAMES.long:
The parallel component of the [effective_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity) tensor, expressing the effective Fickian diffusivity for energy transport by neutral particles in a specified internal (atomic or molecular) state along the magnetic field direction.

In a Fick-law energy-flux closure, the field-line-aligned energy flux density for a neutral population in internal state $s$ is:

$$
\Gamma_{E,\parallel} = -D_\parallel \nabla_\parallel \epsilon_s
$$

where $D_\parallel$ is this diffusivity, $\epsilon_s$ is the energy density of the neutral population in state $s$, and $\nabla_\parallel = \hat{b} \cdot \nabla$ is the gradient along the unit magnetic field vector $\hat{b}$.

This parallel diagonal element is distinct from the poloidal diagonal element given by [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). The analogous quantity for ion species resolved by charge state is [parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity). The generic field-line-aligned neutral energy diffusivity without state resolution is [parallel_energy_diffusivity](name:parallel_energy_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Field-parallel energy-flux density carried by neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state.
NAMES.long:
The field-parallel component of neutral internal-state energy flux is the signed energy-flux density carried by neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state. It is the magnetic-field-parallel projection of the [neutral internal state energy flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).

Let $\mathbf{q}_{n,s}$ denote the energy-flux vector carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, and let $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ denote the unit vector along the local magnetic field. The parallel component is defined by

$$
q_{\parallel,n,s}=\mathbf{q}_{n,s}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $q_{\parallel,n,s}$ is the field-parallel flux density, $n$ identifies the neutral population, and $s$ identifies the internal state.

The quantity includes kinetic, thermal, and internal-state energy carried by the specified neutral population, while excluding contributions from other internal states. Its axis projection differs from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral internal-state energy flux points along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the effective advective velocity transporting momentum for a single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma fluid transport, distinct from bulk particle flow. The component is along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
The parallel component of the [neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection) is the effective advective velocity for parallel momentum transport of a single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma fluid transport, distinct from bulk particle flow. The parallel direction is the local magnetic-field direction.

The component is defined by projecting the neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity onto the unit vector along the local magnetic field:

$$
V_{\mathrm{mom},\parallel}^{(n,\alpha)} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{mom}}^{(n,\alpha)} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{mom}}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is the [neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection) for internal state $\alpha$ of neutral species $n$, $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic-field direction, and $V_{\mathrm{mom},\parallel}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is its parallel component.

This quantity is a component of an effective momentum-transport velocity, not the center-of-mass velocity or particle-flow velocity of the neutral state. The same family includes the [radial neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity), the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and the [vertical neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity](name:vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity), the $\hat{Z}$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is distinct from the [parallel neutral internal-state energy convection velocity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity), which transports energy rather than momentum.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective momentum-convection velocity is directed along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity is the coefficient governing down-gradient transport of momentum for neutral particles resolved by internal state. The parallel qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction along the local magnetic field, not a parallel momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity is the coefficient governing down-gradient transport of momentum for neutral particles resolved by internal state. It is the field-aligned directional component of [neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). The parallel qualifier identifies the direction of diffusive momentum flux and of the momentum-density gradient along the local magnetic field, not a projection of the transported momentum onto that direction.

The defining Fick-type relation for the diffusive contribution along the magnetic field is:

$$
\mathbf{F}_{P,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff},(n,s)} = -D_{\parallel}^{(n,s)} \nabla_{\parallel}\mathbf{P}^{(n,s)}
$$

where $\mathbf{F}_{P,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff},(n,s)}$ is the diffusive field-aligned flux of neutral momentum for neutral population $n$ in internal state $s$, $D_{\parallel}^{(n,s)}$ is this diffusivity, $\nabla_{\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\nabla$ is the derivative along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, and $\mathbf{P}^{(n,s)}$ is the neutral momentum-density vector for that population and internal state. The operator $\nabla_{\parallel}$ acts component-wise on the vector momentum density.

The quantity is resolved by internal state and does not aggregate over neutral internal states. It describes momentum transport rather than particle transport, which distinguishes it from [parallel neutral internal-state diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_diffusivity); its state resolution distinguishes it from [parallel neutral momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), and its field-aligned direction distinguishes it from [vertical neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the signed transport rate of magnetic-field-parallel linear momentum carried by neutral particles in one specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the magnetic-field-parallel transport component of linear momentum carried by neutral particles restricted to one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It is a momentum-flux tensor component, not a particle flux or a local momentum source.

For the state-resolved neutral distribution, the parallel component is defined by

$$
\Pi_{\parallel\parallel}^{(s)} = \hat{b} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{b} = \int m_s v_\parallel^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is its momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field, $m_s$ is the mass of a neutral particle in state $s$, $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b}$ is the velocity component along $\hat{b}$, and $f_s$ is the state-resolved velocity distribution.

The parallel direction is the local magnetic-field direction, not the radial, toroidal, or vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This component is the parallel member of the parent [neutral internal-state momentum flux], differs from the [radial](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and [linear](name:linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) internal-state components, and is the state-resolved counterpart of [parallel neutral momentum flux](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when magnetic-field-parallel linear momentum is transported in the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the particle flux of neutral particles in a specified internal state: the signed flux of that state-resolved neutral population along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The parallel component selects the $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ projection of the [neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) vector $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{(s)}$, giving the signed flux density of neutrals in internal state $s$ along the local magnetic-field direction.

The defining relation for neutral species $\alpha$ in internal state $s$ is:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,\alpha s} = \int f_{\alpha s}(\mathbf{v})\, \mathbf{v} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}\, d^3v
$$

where $f_{\alpha s}$ is the velocity distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of the local magnetic field.

For a fixed neutral species $\alpha$, summing $\Gamma_{\parallel,\alpha s}$ over internal states $s$ gives the state-unresolved parallel neutral particle flux for that species; summing over all neutral species and all internal states gives [parallel_neutral_particle_flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux). The matched directional components are [radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) and [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux), while the parallel energy transport carried by the same state-resolved neutral population is [parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net neutral particle flow is in the direction of the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the effective E×B drift velocity assigned to a neutral species in a specified internal state, projected along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
The parallel component of the [effective neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the projection of the assigned drift velocity onto the local magnetic-field direction.

The component is defined from the local electric and magnetic fields by

$$
v_\parallel = \left(\frac{\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $v_\parallel$ is the parallel velocity component, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector in the local magnetic-field direction.

This effective velocity is assigned to the specified neutral internal state for transport attribution; it does not imply direct Lorentz acceleration of neutral particles. For an ideal E×B drift in a region with nonzero magnetic field, $v_\parallel$ is zero because $\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$. It is distinct from the [radial neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), [poloidal neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), and [toroidal neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), which use different projection directions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the assigned velocity points along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal parallel component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor, governing down-gradient redistribution of aggregate neutral momentum along the local magnetic-field direction. The parallel qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal parallel component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor. It parameterizes down-gradient diffusive transport of aggregate neutral momentum density along the local magnetic-field direction. The parallel qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the component of momentum being transported.

The field-aligned component enters a neutral momentum diffusion closure through the vector-valued diffusive flux contribution:

$$
\mathbf{F}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\mathrm{mom}}(\hat{b}) = -\chi_{n,\mathrm{mom},\parallel}\,(\hat{b}\cdot\nabla)\mathbf{g}_n
$$

where $\chi_{n,\mathrm{mom},\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, $\mathbf{F}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\mathrm{mom}}(\hat{b})$ is the diffusive flux through a surface normal to the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$, $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ with $\mathbf{B}$ the magnetic field, and $\mathbf{g}_n=\sum_\alpha m_{n,\alpha} n_{n,\alpha}\mathbf{u}_{n,\alpha}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum density over neutral populations $\alpha$.

Neutral-neutral viscous collisions and charge-exchange interactions with ions may contribute to this coefficient when their net effect is represented as local gradient-driven redistribution. It excludes convective field-aligned transport, pressure contributions, direct momentum source or sink terms from ionization and recombination, and explicit neutral-ion friction terms not represented by the diffusive closure. This diffusive contribution is distinct from the total [parallel neutral momentum flux](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux), and the other diagonal components of [neutral momentum diffusivity](name:neutral_momentum_diffusivity) include [poloidal neutral momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), [toroidal neutral momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), and [vertical neutral momentum diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel neutral momentum flux is the parallel-parallel component of neutral linear-momentum transport, combining convective and isotropic-pressure contributions summed over all neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral momentum flux is the field-aligned, parallel-parallel component of the neutral momentum-flux tensor. It represents transport of neutral momentum through a surface normal to the local magnetic-field direction, aggregated over all neutral species and internal states, and is a directional component of [neutral_momentum_flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux).

$$
\Pi_{n,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}=\sum_s\left[m_s n_s\left(\mathbf v_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right)^2+p_s\right]
$$

Here, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $s$ indexes each neutral species and internal state. The quantities $m_s$, $n_s$, $\mathbf v_s$, and $p_s$ are respectively the particle mass, number density, bulk velocity, and isotropic thermal pressure of state $s$; $\Pi_{n,\parallel}$ is invariant under reversal of $\hat{\mathbf b}$.

The species and internal-state sum distinguishes this quantity from [parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), which resolves one neutral state, and from [parallel_plasma_momentum_flux](name:parallel_plasma_momentum_flux), which describes charged-plasma momentum transport.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_species_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Field-aligned effective velocity for convective transport of a neutral species’ thermal energy, aggregated over all resolved internal states.
NAMES.long:
The neutral species energy convection velocity is the effective advection velocity associated with convective transport of that species’ thermal energy, with all resolved internal states included. Its parallel component is a flux-to-energy-density ratio, not a sum or average of individual neutral-particle velocities.

$$
u_{\parallel,s}^{E} = \frac{\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\sum_{\alpha}\mathbf F_{E,s,\alpha}^{\mathrm{conv}}}{\sum_{\alpha} w_{E,s,\alpha}}$$

where $s$ denotes the neutral species, $\alpha$ indexes its resolved internal states, $\mathbf F_{E,s,\alpha}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective thermal-energy flux, $w_{E,s,\alpha}$ is the corresponding thermal-energy density, and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field $\mathbf B$. The denominator must be nonzero; state-resolved quantities such as [neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity) retain a single internal state rather than this species-level aggregation. This quantity is the field-aligned component of [neutral_species_energy_convection_velocity](name:neutral_species_energy_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aggregated convective thermal-energy flux has a component along the magnetic-field direction $\hat{\mathbf b}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the bulk flow of a neutral particle population, projected along the local magnetic-field direction from its first velocity moment.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral velocity is the component of the bulk flow vector of a selected neutral particle population along the local magnetic-field direction. It is a directional projection of [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity), rather than a random thermal speed.

For position $\mathbf{x}$ and local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, the defining projection is:

$$
V_{n,\parallel}(\mathbf{x}) = \hat{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \mathbf{V}_n(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_n$ and $V_{n,\parallel}$ are velocities expressed in m s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the dimensionless unit vector along the local magnetic field.

The selected neutral population and any state aggregation follow [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity); combining populations gives a density-weighted mean, not an arithmetic mean. This field-aligned projection differs from [poloidal neutral velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_velocity), which follows the poloidal direction, and excludes charged-particle flow.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral bulk-flow projection points along the local magnetic-field direction represented by $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_volume_averaged_runaway_electron_current_density
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Plasma-volume average of the signed conventional current-density component carried by runaway electrons along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the plasma-volume average of the local field-aligned conventional current density carried only by runaway electrons. It selects the magnetic-field-parallel contribution of the runaway-electron current before applying the same volume averaging represented by [volume-averaged runaway-electron current density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_current_density).

$$
\left\langle j_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}} \right\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the local conventional current-density vector of the runaway-electron population, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local unit vector in the magnetic-field direction, $V_p$ is the selected plasma volume, and $dV$ is its volume element. Contributions from thermal electrons, ions, and non-runaway populations are excluded. Because this is conventional current, its direction is opposite to the motion of negatively charged runaway electrons.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the local conventional runaway-electron current component points along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: particle_count
NAMES.short: Particle-count quantity expressing either the number of physical particles in a population or the number represented by each simulated particle marker.
NAMES.long:
Particle-count quantities describe the size of a physical particle population, either as an extensive count or as a representation ratio assigned to simulated markers. The extensive form, [total particle count](name:total_particle_count), is obtained from a phase-space distribution:

$$
N = \int_V \int f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}\,d^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $N$ is the particle count, $V$ is the physical volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity, and $f$ is the particle phase-space distribution. When $N$ physical particles are represented by $N_\mathrm{sim}$ simulated markers, the corresponding [particle-count ratio](name:ratio_of_particle_count_to_simulated_particle_count) is $w = N/N_\mathrm{sim}$ for equal marker weighting. These quantities do not by themselves specify a species, charge state, spatial region, or number density.

NAMES.name: particle_density
NAMES.short: Zeroth velocity-space moment of the particle distribution function, giving the local number density integrated over all energy populations and guiding-center orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
Particle density is the zeroth moment of the phase-space distribution function $f(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v})$ obtained by integrating over all particle velocities:

$$
n(\mathbf{r}) = \int f(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $n$ is the local number density and $f$ is the full distribution function encompassing both thermal and suprathermal populations at position $\mathbf{r}$. This quantity makes no restriction on particle energy or orbital topology, so it includes contributions from all guiding-center orbit classes (trapped, co-passing, and counter-passing) as well as from fast and thermal sub-populations simultaneously.

Decomposing by orbital topology recovers component quantities such as [trapped_density](name:total_trapped_particle_density) and [co_passing_density](name:total_co_passing_particle_density); summing over all particle species (electrons, ions, and neutrals) yields the total_particle_density. For the combined species total on a general-geometry grid, see also total_electron_ion_neutral_particle_number_density.

Computed in kinetic and Monte Carlo models by numerically integrating $f$ over velocity space on a spatial or flux-surface grid. Experimental estimates of orbit-class-resolved components rely on fast-ion diagnostics such as neutral particle analyzers or collective Thomson scattering.
NAMES.sign: Positive for all physical particle distributions, as number density is a non-negative definite quantity by construction.

NAMES.name: fast_particle_density
NAMES.short: Number density of suprathermal particles obtained by integrating the fast-particle distribution over velocity space and combining the applicable guiding-center orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
Fast-particle density is the local number density of suprathermal particles represented by the fast-particle distribution, resolved collectively across the included guiding-center orbit classes. It is a component of the full [particle density](name:particle_density), which also includes other particle populations.

$$
n_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{fast}}} f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle number density, $f_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle phase-space distribution, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the velocity-space domain assigned to the suprathermal population. The quantity includes the orbit-class contributions represented by [trapped fast-particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density), [co-passing fast-particle density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density), and [counter-passing fast-particle density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_density). It excludes thermal particles and is a local density rather than the volume-integrated [total fast-particle count](name:total_fast_particle_count).

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_particle_density
NAMES.short: Number density of suprathermal particles on co-passing orbits, obtained as the zeroth velocity moment over the co-passing region of fast-particle phase space.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing fast-particle density is the local number density of suprathermal particles whose guiding-center parallel velocity follows the bulk plasma current and whose orbits circulate without magnetic mirror reflection. It is the co-passing contribution to the total [fast-particle density](name:fast_particle_density), distinct from trapped and counter-passing contributions.

The density is the zeroth velocity moment of the fast-particle distribution restricted to co-passing orbits:

$$
n_{\mathrm{fast,co}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{r})} f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{fast,co}}$ is the co-passing fast-particle density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution function, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the velocity-space region whose guiding-center orbits are co-passing. The complementary orbit classes are represented by [counter-passing fast-particle density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_density) and [trapped fast-particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density).

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_particle_density
NAMES.short: Number density of fast (suprathermal) particles in the counter-passing orbit class, where guiding-center parallel velocity is directed opposite to the bulk plasma current.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing fast particles are suprathermal ions or electrons whose guiding-center parallel velocity is anti-parallel to the bulk plasma current, executing closed toroidal orbits without magnetic mirror reflection. They are distinct from trapped particles, which undergo mirror reflection on the low-field side of the torus, and from [co_passing_fast_particle_density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density) particles, which travel parallel to the current.

The counter-passing fast-particle density is the velocity-space integral of the fast-particle distribution function $f_\text{fast}$ restricted to counter-passing orbits:

$$
n_\text{fast,cp}(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{v_\parallel < 0} f_\text{fast}(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $v_\parallel$ is the guiding-center parallel velocity and the integration domain covers orbits with $v_\parallel$ anti-parallel to the plasma current direction.

Together with [co_passing_fast_particle_density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density), this quantity partitions the passing component of [fast_particle_density](name:fast_particle_density) by orbit class. The counter-passing population has opposite radial drift-orbit displacement from co-passing particles due to gradient and curvature drifts in the inhomogeneous tokamak field, making this decomposition essential for toroidal momentum balance, fast-particle orbit-loss studies, and neoclassical transport analyzes. The related [counter_passing_density](name:counter_passing_density) covers both thermal and suprathermal counter-passing particles.
NAMES.sign: Positive when counter-passing fast particles are present, with counter-passing defined as guiding-center parallel velocity anti-parallel to the plasma current direction.

NAMES.name: particle_flux
NAMES.short: Directed number of particles crossing a unit oriented surface per unit area per unit time, the general particle-transport flux spanning all species, charge states, and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Particle flux quantifies the directed flow of any plasma or neutral constituent across an oriented reference surface, capturing contributions from bulk convection, diffusion, drift motions, and turbulence. It is the fundamental quantity in the particle continuity equation and applies equally to electrons, ions at any charge state, and neutral atoms or molecules.

For a fluid element with number density $n$ and mean fluid velocity $\mathbf{v}$, the particle flux vector is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma} = n \mathbf{v}
$$

where the surface-normal projection $\Gamma = \boldsymbol{\Gamma} \cdot \hat{n}$ satisfies the continuity equation $\partial n / \partial t + \nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Gamma} = S$, with $S$ the local particle source rate density. In kinetic descriptions, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}$ is the first velocity moment of the distribution function $f(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}, t)$ integrated over all velocities.

Species-resolved specializations include [electron_particle_flux](name:electron_particle_flux) for the electron population, [ion_particle_flux](name:ion_particle_flux) for ions summed over charge states, and [neutral_particle_flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) for neutral atoms and molecules. The net outward particle flux integrated over a closed surface determines the temporal rate of change of [particle_count](name:particle_count) within the enclosed volume.

Particle flux is measured directly by electrostatic probes in the scrape-off layer and inferred from density profile gradients combined with transport modeling across the confined plasma.
NAMES.sign: Positive when particles flow in the direction of the outward surface normal, away from the enclosed plasma volume.

NAMES.name: electron_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Directed number flux of electrons across an oriented surface, including convective, diffusive, drift, and turbulent contributions to electron transport.
NAMES.long:
Electron particle flux quantifies the directed transport of electrons across an oriented reference surface. It is the electron-specific realization of [particle_flux](name:particle_flux).

For an oriented surface, the scalar electron flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_e = \hat{\mathbf n} \cdot \int \mathbf v\, f_e(\mathbf r,\mathbf v,t)\,d^3v
$$

where $f_e$ is the electron distribution function, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity in m/s, $\mathbf r$ is position in m, $t$ is time in s, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the dimensionless unit surface normal. The integral is over all electron velocities.

The flux includes convective, diffusive, drift, and turbulent electron transport. Choosing radial, poloidal, or magnetic-field-aligned orientations gives the corresponding [radial_electron_particle_flux](name:radial_electron_particle_flux), [poloidal_electron_particle_flux](name:poloidal_electron_particle_flux), and [parallel_electron_particle_flux](name:parallel_electron_particle_flux); energy-weighted transport is a distinct quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when electrons cross in the direction of the chosen surface normal.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Full particle flux vector of ions in a specified ionization charge state, giving the directed number flow per unit area per unit time for that charge state resolved independently from all other ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge state particle flux vector characterizes the directed flow of ions in a specific ionization stage $z$ through a unit surface per unit time, treating each charge state as a distinct species in charge-state-resolved multi-fluid transport models. This per-stage resolution is essential for modeling impurity accumulation and fuel-ion evolution in confined plasmas, where ionization and recombination continuously couple adjacent charge states.

The flux vector is defined as the first velocity moment of the charge-state population:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z = n_z \mathbf{v}_z
$$

where $n_z$ is the number density of ions in charge state $z$ and $\mathbf{v}_z$ is the mean fluid velocity of that charge-state population.

Directional projections of this vector yield [radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for cross-field transport across magnetic flux surfaces, [poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for poloidal flow asymmetries, and [parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for field-aligned streaming. The scalar surface-normal analog [ion_state_particle_flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) represents a single-surface projection used in one-dimensional transport approximations.

Charge-state-resolved fluxes are computed in multi-fluid or kinetic transport codes using ionization and recombination rate coefficients from atomic databases. Core plasma values span approximately $10^{18}$–$10^{21}$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, while fluxes near plasma-facing components and divertor targets can exceed $10^{22}$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$.

NAMES.name: ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion particle flux quantifies the directed number flow of ions across an oriented surface, with all charge states aggregated and directional components defined by the surface normal.
NAMES.long:
Ion particle flux quantifies the directed transport of ions across an oriented reference surface. It is the ion-specific realization of [particle_flux](name:particle_flux), with all charge states of the included ion population aggregated rather than resolved independently.

For charge-state index $z$, the ion particle-flux density is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i}=\sum_z n_{i,z}\mathbf{v}_{i,z}=n_i\mathbf{v}_i
$$

where $n_{i,z}$ is the number density in charge state $z$ in m$^{-3}$, $\mathbf{v}_{i,z}$ is its mean velocity in m s$^{-1}$, $n_i=\sum_z n_{i,z}$ is the total ion number density, and $\mathbf{v}_i$ is the density-weighted mean ion velocity. The scalar flux through an oriented surface is $\Gamma_i=\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i\cdot\hat{n}$, where $\hat{n}$ is the unit surface normal.

The aggregate excludes neutral particles and differs from [ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux), which resolves one charge state. Directional projections include [radial_ion_particle_flux](name:radial_ion_particle_flux), [poloidal_ion_particle_flux](name:poloidal_ion_particle_flux), and [parallel_ion_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_particle_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when ions flow in the direction of the outward surface normal.

NAMES.name: neutral_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral particle flux is the net directed number flow of neutral atoms and molecules across an oriented surface, summed over all neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Neutral particle flux is the net directed flow of neutral atoms and molecules across an oriented reference surface, with all included neutral species and internal states aggregated. It is the neutral specialization of [particle_flux](name:particle_flux), while [radial_neutral_particle_flux](name:radial_neutral_particle_flux), [poloidal_neutral_particle_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux), and [parallel_neutral_particle_flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux) are directional projections.

For neutral species and internal-state index $s$, the scalar flux through a surface is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{n}} = \hat{\mathbf{n}} \cdot \sum_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density and $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the mean velocity of constituent $s$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen unit surface normal. The quantity includes convective, diffusive, drift, and turbulent contributions represented in the constituent fluxes.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral particles cross the surface in the direction of the chosen unit normal.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Directed number flux of electrons along the local magnetic-field direction, including convective, diffusive, drift, and turbulent contributions to electron transport.
NAMES.long:
Parallel electron particle flux quantifies the directed transport of electrons along the local magnetic-field direction. It is the field-aligned component of [electron particle flux](name:electron_particle_flux).

For the local magnetic-field unit vector, the scalar flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{e,\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf b} \cdot \int \mathbf v\, f_e(\mathbf r,\mathbf v,t)\,d^3v
$$

where $f_e$ is the electron distribution function, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity in m/s, $\mathbf r$ is position in m, $t$ is time in s, and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the dimensionless unit vector in the direction of the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$. The integral covers all electron velocities.

This quantity counts electron transport rather than transported energy; energy weighting defines [parallel electron energy flux](name:parallel_electron_energy_flux). Its direction-specific projection differs from [radial electron particle flux](name:radial_electron_particle_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when electron motion has a component in the direction of the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Parallel ion charge-state particle flux is the directed number flow of ions in a specified ionization charge state along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state particle flux is the field-aligned component of the particle-flux vector for ions in a specified ionization charge state, resolved independently from other charge states. It describes directed streaming along the local magnetic field rather than aggregation over charge states.

The component is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,z}=\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z\cdot\mathbf{b},\qquad \mathbf{b}=\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|},\qquad \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z=n_z\mathbf{v}_z
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z$ is the particle-flux vector for charge state $z$, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$, $n_z$ is the number density, and $\mathbf{v}_z$ is the mean velocity of that charge-state population.

This quantity is the field-aligned projection of [ion charge-state particle flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux). Unlike [parallel ion particle flux](name:parallel_ion_particle_flux), it retains a specified ionization charge state rather than aggregating over all ion charge states; its poloidal counterpart is [poloidal ion charge-state particle flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the charge-state flux has a component in the direction of the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B$}.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Parallel ion particle flux quantifies the directed number flow of all ion charge states along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion particle flux quantifies the directed transport of ions along the local magnetic-field direction, with all charge states aggregated. It is the parallel component of [ion_particle_flux](name:ion_particle_flux), rather than a charge-state-resolved flux.

For charge-state index $z$, the parallel ion particle-flux density is defined as

$$
\Gamma_{i\parallel}=\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i\cdot\hat{b}=\sum_z n_{i,z}\,\mathbf{v}_{i,z}\cdot\hat{b}
$$

where $n_{i,z}$ is the number density of ions in charge state $z$, $\mathbf{v}_{i,z}$ is their mean velocity, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is the total ion particle-flux vector, and $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. The aggregation includes all included ion charge states and excludes neutrals. It differs from [parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), which resolves one charge state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net ion flow is directed along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel neutral particle flux is the field-aligned component of neutral number flow, summed over all neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral particle flux is the component of the total neutral particle flux along the local magnetic-field direction, with all included neutral species and internal atomic or molecular states aggregated. It is the field-aligned projection of [neutral particle flux](name:neutral_particle_flux), complementing the [radial neutral particle flux](name:radial_neutral_particle_flux).

For neutral species and internal-state index $s$, the field-parallel flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf{b}} \cdot \sum_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of constituent $s$, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is its mean velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector in the direction of the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. The quantity includes all neutral species and states rather than a single state-resolved contribution such as [neutral internal-state particle flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral particles move in the direction of the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}$}.

NAMES.name: particle_pressure
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure of a particle population obtained from the second velocity-space moment of the distribution function, encompassing thermal and nonthermal contributions across all orbit classes and perturbation states.
NAMES.long:
Particle pressure is the scalar mechanical pressure carried by a specified particle population, computed directly from the kinetic distribution function rather than from a fluid closure assumption. It is the parent quantity for orbit-class-resolved and perturbation-resolved variants of kinetic pressure derived from the second moment of the distribution.

The scalar pressure combines the parallel and perpendicular kinetic stress components:

$$
P = \frac{P_\parallel + 2P_\perp}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\int m\,|\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}|^2\,f(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{u}$ is the mean fluid velocity, $f(\mathbf{v})$ is the distribution function, and $P_\parallel$, $P_\perp$ are the pressure components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field. Restricting the velocity-space integral to the co-passing trajectory domain yields [co_passing_particle_pressure](name:co_passing_particle_pressure); evaluating only the fluctuating part of $f$ yields the perturbed variant relevant to turbulence analysis. In kinetic and gyrokinetic transport codes, particle pressure is obtained by numerical quadrature over the phase-space distribution; for Maxwellian populations the expression reduces to $P = nkT$, where $n$ is number density and $T$ is temperature. The fast-particle analog [co_passing_fast_particle_pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) illustrates how orbit-class and population restrictions combine within this hierarchy.

NAMES.name: particle_source_rate
NAMES.short: Net particle production or loss per unit volume generated by a distribution-function source, serving as the continuity-equation source term for a resolved plasma population.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net rate at which a specified or aggregated plasma population is created or removed by a source in its distribution function. It is the particle source term associated with the population's continuity balance.

The local continuity relation is

$$
\frac{\partial n}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Gamma} = S
$$

where $n$ is the population particle density, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}$ is its particle flux, and $S$ is this net source rate. Positive $S$ denotes particle production and negative $S$ denotes particle loss.

The quantity may be resolved by species, ion charge state, population, or aggregation, and may represent a local or flux-surface-averaged source. Charge-state-resolved and charge-state-summed instances are represented by [ion state source rate](name:ion_state_source_rate) and [total ion source rate](name:total_ion_source_rate), while a population-specific instance is [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate). It excludes sources defined solely for energy, momentum, or other non-particle moments.

NAMES.name: ion_particle_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net rate of ion particle production or loss integrated inside the enclosing flux surface, summed over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
The ion particle source rate $\dot{N}_i$ is the net rate at which ion particles are produced or removed inside the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface. It is summed over all ion species and, for each species, all charge states, so it represents the total ion-population source contribution to the enclosed particle balance.

For a monotonic flux-surface label $\rho$, it is defined by the volume integral of the local net ion particle source density:

$$
\dot{N}_i(\rho,t) = \int_{V(\rho)} S_i(\mathbf{x},t)\,dV
$$

where $\dot{N}_i$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $V(\rho)$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the flux surface labeled by $\rho$, $S_i$ has units $\mathrm{m}^{-3}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ has units $\mathrm{s}$, and $dV$ has units $\mathrm{m}^{3}$. The label $\rho$ is a dimensionless monotonic label of nested magnetic flux surfaces.

The integrand is the local ion-specific source density, corresponding to the local [total_ion_source_rate](name:total_ion_source_rate), not the generic all-particle source unless that source has been restricted to ions. The charge-state-resolved enclosed counterpart is [ion_charge_state_particle_source_rate](name:ion_charge_state_particle_source_rate). Processes that only transfer particles among charge states of the same ion population cancel in this charge-state-summed quantity.

This is a source term, not a particle flux: directed transport quantities such as [radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) describe motion across surfaces or in a specified direction, whereas $\dot{N}_i$ accounts for local production, injection, removal, or loss represented by $S_i$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net source terms add ion particles to the volume enclosed by the flux surface.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short: Perpendicular component of the species-summed fast-particle pressure tensor for co-passing guiding-center orbits, formed from velocity components transverse to the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure is the transverse component of the species-summed fast-particle pressure tensor carried by suprathermal particles on co-passing guiding-center orbits. It is complementary to the scalar [co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and the field-aligned [parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure).

The flux-surface-averaged perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse second velocity moment:

$$
P_{\perp,\mathrm{co,fast}}(\psi) = \left\langle \frac{1}{2}\sum_s m_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{co},s}(\mathbf{x})} v_\perp^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes its flux-surface average, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is particle mass, $v_\perp$ is speed transverse to the local magnetic field, $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the distribution function, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{co},s}$ contains only co-passing guiding-center orbits.

The factor one-half accounts for the two perpendicular velocity degrees of freedom. With the same orbit selection, the scalar parent satisfies $P_{\mathrm{co,fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{co,fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{co,fast}})/3$; counter-passing and trapped fast-particle populations are excluded, including the [perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure).

NAMES.name: perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short: Perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure is the field-perpendicular kinetic pressure carried by suprathermal particles on counter-passing guiding-center orbits.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure is the field-perpendicular component of the kinetic pressure tensor contributed by suprathermal particles whose guiding-center orbits are passing and whose parallel motion is opposite to the plasma-current direction. It is the perpendicular-orbit contribution to [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), complementary to the field-aligned [parallel counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure).

The flux-surface-averaged perpendicular pressure is defined by the counter-passing second velocity moment:

$$
P_{\perp,\mathrm{cp,fast}}(\psi) = \left\langle \frac{1}{2}\sum_s m_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s}(\mathbf{x})} v_\perp^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes its flux-surface average, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is particle mass, $v_\perp$ is speed perpendicular to the local magnetic field, $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the fast-particle distribution function, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s}(\mathbf{x})$ contains counter-passing guiding-center orbits at position $\mathbf{x}$.

The orbit selection excludes trapped and co-passing populations. For the same selection, this component combines with the field-aligned component according to $P_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{cp,fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{cp,fast}})/3$, where the scalar trace is [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure).

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Perpendicular fast electron pressure is the gyrotropic pressure moment of the suprathermal electron distribution associated with velocity components perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular fast electron pressure, denoted $p_{\perp,e}^{\mathrm{fast}}$, is the component of the fast-electron pressure tensor transverse to the local magnetic-field direction. It describes the perpendicular kinetic stress of the suprathermal electron population and is distinct from the field-aligned component [parallel_fast_electron_pressure](name:parallel_fast_electron_pressure).

For a gyrotropic fast-electron distribution, the local perpendicular pressure is the second velocity moment of the suprathermal part of the electron distribution function:

$$
p_{\perp,e}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int \frac{1}{2} m_e v_\perp^2 f_e^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m_e$ is the electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is the electron velocity relative to the local mean flow, $v_\perp$ is the magnitude of the component of $\mathbf{v}$ perpendicular to the local magnetic-field unit vector, and $f_e^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal part of the electron distribution function.

This quantity is one transverse gyrotropic pressure component, not the sum over two perpendicular directions and not a flux-surface-normal projection. The scalar [fast_electron_pressure](name:fast_electron_pressure) for a gyrotropic distribution is related by $p_e^{\mathrm{fast}} = (p_{\parallel,e}^{\mathrm{fast}} + 2p_{\perp,e}^{\mathrm{fast}})/3$; for an isotropic suprathermal distribution, $p_{\perp,e}^{\mathrm{fast}} = p_{\parallel,e}^{\mathrm{fast}}$.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: The perpendicular fast-ion charge-state pressure is the field-normal diagonal element of the suprathermal ion pressure tensor for one specified ionization state. It is the transverse second central velocity moment, averaged over the two directions normal to the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular fast-ion charge-state pressure is the field-normal diagonal element of the [fast-ion charge-state pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure) tensor for a specified ion charge state $c$. It represents the second central moment of the suprathermal ion distribution in the two velocity directions transverse to the local magnetic field.

For a charge-state-resolved fast-ion distribution, the scalar perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse peculiar-velocity moment:

$$
p_{\perp,c} = \frac{m_c}{2}\int w_{\perp,c}^2\, f_c(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $p_{\perp,c}$ is the perpendicular fast-ion charge-state pressure, $m_c$ is the ion mass for charge state $c$, $f_c(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$ is the fast-ion distribution function for charge state $c$, $\mathbf{w}_c = \mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_c$ is the peculiar velocity relative to the bulk velocity $\mathbf{u}_c$ of that charge-state population, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $w_{\perp,c}^2 = |\mathbf{w}_c|^2-(\mathbf{w}_c\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}})^2$ is the squared peculiar speed transverse to the magnetic field. The factor $1/2$ makes this the pressure per perpendicular degree of freedom.

This quantity is resolved for one ion charge state and is not summed over charge states. Its difference from the [parallel fast-ion charge-state pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure), $p_{\perp,c}-p_{\parallel,c}$, defines the charge-state-resolved perpendicular–parallel pressure anisotropy.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Perpendicular fast-ion pressure is the component of the suprathermal ion pressure tensor associated with velocity fluctuations transverse to the local magnetic field, summed over all ion species and ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular fast-ion pressure is the component of the suprathermal ion pressure tensor associated with motion transverse to the local magnetic-field direction. It is summed over all ion species and ionization states, forms the charge-state-summed aggregate of [perpendicular fast-ion charge-state pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure), and excludes the Maxwellian thermal-ion contribution described by [fast-ion pressure](name:fast_ion_pressure). Its field-aligned counterpart is [parallel fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure).

The perpendicular component is defined by the transverse second central velocity moment:

$$
P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\alpha,q} m_\alpha \int \left|\left(\mathbf{I}-\hat{\mathbf{b}}\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right)\cdot(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q})\right|^2 f_{\alpha q,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $m_\alpha$ is the species mass in kg, $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha q}$ are particle and mean velocities in m s$^{-1}$, $\alpha$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes ionization state, $f$ is the fast-ion distribution, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local magnetic-field unit vector. For a gyrotropic distribution, this is the common normal stress in the two directions transverse to $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ and satisfies $p_{\mathrm{fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})/3$.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure moment of the suprathermal particle distribution resolved transverse to the local magnetic field; it includes co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped guiding-center orbits.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular fast-particle pressure is the transverse component of the kinetic pressure tensor carried by suprathermal particles. It is the all-orbit contribution to [fast-particle pressure], complementary to the field-aligned [parallel fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure).

The flux-surface-averaged perpendicular pressure is defined by the second velocity moment:

$$
P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}(\psi)=\left\langle \frac{1}{2}\sum_s m_s\int v_\perp^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes its flux-surface average, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is particle mass, $v_\perp$ is velocity perpendicular to the local magnetic field, and $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the distribution function. The factor one-half averages the two perpendicular velocity degrees of freedom. Co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped populations are included; [perpendicular co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) is an orbit-resolved contribution.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Perpendicular (field-normal) component, along a specified local unit vector normal to the magnetic field, of the diamagnetic drift velocity of a specified ion charge state, driven by that state's partial pressure gradient crossed with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular component of the diamagnetic drift velocity for a specified ion charge state is its projection onto a specified local unit vector $\hat{e}_{\perp}$ normal to the magnetic field, with $\hat{e}_{\perp}\cdot\hat{b}=0$. Here $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the local magnetic-field unit vector and $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is the local field magnitude.

The full diamagnetic drift velocity for ion charge state $s$ is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} = -\frac{\nabla p_s \times \mathbf{B}}{q_s n_s B^2}
$$

where $p_s$ is the partial pressure of charge state $s$, $q_s = Z_s e$ is its electric charge with $Z_s$ the charge number and $e$ the elementary charge, $n_s$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field. The perpendicular component is $v_{\mathrm{dia},s,\perp} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s}\cdot\hat{e}_{\perp}$.

This scalar is a projection onto the chosen $\hat{e}_{\perp}$ axis, not the vector projection onto the whole plane normal to $\mathbf{B}$ and not the perpendicular speed. The complementary field-aligned projection is [parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and the cylindrical projections in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame are [radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), [poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), [toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and [vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perpendicular diamagnetic drift points in the $+\hat{e}_{\perp}$ direction.
