NAMES.name: pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short: Pfirsch-Schlueter current density produced by diamagnetic drift in a magnetized plasma, representing the signed field-aligned return current that cancels the divergence of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current.
NAMES.long:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed field-aligned scalar return current associated with the pressure-gradient-driven current described by [current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It enforces charge-current continuity by canceling the divergence of the perpendicular diamagnetic current on a magnetic flux surface in toroidal geometry.

The scalar amplitude $j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is defined by the current-continuity condition

$$
\nabla \cdot \left(j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}\mathbf{b}\right) = -\nabla \cdot \left(\frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p}{B^2}\right)
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is the signed scalar Pfirsch-Schlueter current density due to diamagnetic drift, $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B^2=\mathbf{B}\cdot\mathbf{B}$, and $p$ is the isotropic scalar plasma pressure.

This scalar denotes the amplitude multiplying the magnetic-field unit vector, not an independent vector current and not a cylindrical component. A flux-surface-constant parallel current component not required by the diamagnetic-current divergence is excluded; the component-oriented [parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) denotes the parallel projection of the same field-aligned contribution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional positive charge flows along the local magnetic field direction $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short: Signed field-aligned component of the diamagnetic-driven Pfirsch-Schlüter return-current density that balances perpendicular diamagnetic-current divergence.
NAMES.long:
Signed field-aligned component of the diamagnetic-driven Pfirsch-Schlüter return-current density is the scalar parallel current density that compensates the divergence of the pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular diamagnetic current in toroidal magnetic geometry. The associated return-current vector is $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}^{\mathrm{dia}}\mathbf{b}$, where the direction is constrained to lie along magnetic field lines.

In steady magnetostatic current continuity, the component is defined by the balance:

$$
\nabla \cdot \left(j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}^{\mathrm{dia}}\mathbf{b}\right) = -\nabla \cdot \mathbf{j}_{\perp,\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this signed parallel current-density scalar, $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{j}_{\perp,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the perpendicular diamagnetic current-density vector. For a single-fluid pressure $p$, the diamagnetic drive is represented by $\mathbf{j}_{\perp,\mathrm{dia}}=\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p/|\mathbf{B}|^2$.

The Pfirsch-Schlüter response to diamagnetic-current divergence is field-aligned, so the scalar [Pfirsch-Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) corresponds to this same signed return-current component. The field-line equation determines $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}^{\mathrm{dia}}/|\mathbf{B}|$ up to a flux-surface function; the Pfirsch-Schlüter return-current convention excludes that homogeneous net-current part by setting the flux-surface average of $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}^{\mathrm{dia}}/|\mathbf{B}|$ to zero. This distinguishes the quantity from the perpendicular diamagnetic current that drives it and from broader parallel-current contributions such as [parallel current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current density flows in the direction of the magnetic-field unit vector $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

NAMES.name: plasma_current_due_to_ohmic_induction
NAMES.short: Net plasma electric current generated by the collisional Ohmic response to an inductive electric field, rather than by bootstrap or externally driven non-inductive current.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the total plasma-current contribution produced by the collisional Ohmic response to an inductive electric field. Its drive is changing magnetic flux, equivalently the loop-voltage drive represented by the [loop voltage at the plasma boundary](name:loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary), rather than a pressure-gradient or externally driven non-inductive mechanism.

$$
I_{\rm ohm} = \int_S \mathbf{j}_{\rm ohm}\cdot d\mathbf{S}, \qquad \mathbf{j}_{\rm ohm}=\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\mathbf{E}_{\rm ind}
$$

where $I_{\rm ohm}$ is the Ohmic plasma current, $S$ is an oriented cross-sectional surface, $\mathbf{j}_{\rm ohm}$ is the Ohmic current-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the plasma conductivity tensor, and $\mathbf{E}_{\rm ind}$ is the inductive electric-field vector.

This aggregate quantity includes directional specializations such as the [parallel plasma current due to Ohmic induction](name:parallel_plasma_current_due_to_ohmic_induction) and excludes bootstrap and externally driven current contributions. Its common physical definition is given by [current due to Ohmic induction](name:current_due_to_ohmic_induction).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net Ohmic current crosses the oriented integration surface in the direction of its assigned positive normal.

NAMES.name: plasma_energy
NAMES.short: Plasma energy is the volume-integrated internal kinetic energy carried by all confined electron and ion populations, including thermal and suprathermal particles. It excludes electromagnetic-field, rest-mass, and organized bulk-flow energy.
NAMES.long:
Plasma energy is the volume-integrated internal kinetic energy carried by all confined electron and ion populations, including thermal and suprathermal populations. It is the all-population stored particle energy of the confined plasma, not a thermal-only component.

A pressure-tensor definition gives the stored particle energy without assuming isotropic distributions:

$$
W_\mathrm{p} = \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} \sum_a \frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{P}_a\, dV
$$

where $W_\mathrm{p}$ is the plasma energy, $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $a$ labels the electron, ion, and modeled suprathermal populations included in the confined plasma, $\mathbf{P}_a$ is the pressure tensor of population $a$ in its local mean-flow frame, and $dV$ is the scalar volume element. For isotropic populations this reduces to the pressure-sum relation with energy density $3p_\mathrm{tot}/2$, where $p_\mathrm{tot}=\sum_a p_a$; for a gyrotropic anisotropic population the contribution is $p_{\perp a}+p_{\parallel a}/2$.

This quantity excludes electromagnetic-field energy, electrostatic-field energy, rest-mass energy, and organized macroscopic bulk-flow energy. [Electron energy](name:electron_energy), [thermal plasma energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy), and [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy) are component contributions, while [total plasma energy](name:total_plasma_energy) and [total particle energy] denote the corresponding all-population stored particle-energy concept when the naming emphasizes totality.

NAMES.name: poloidal_center_of_mass_velocity
NAMES.short: Mass-weighted mean poloidal flow of all contributing plasma species, obtained by projecting their barycentric velocity onto the local poloidal direction.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal center-of-mass velocity is the projection of the barycentric bulk velocity of a multicomponent plasma onto the local poloidal direction. It retains the mass weighting of the [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) while selecting the component tangent to the poloidal plane.

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},\theta}=\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\cdot\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\cdot\frac{\sum_s \rho_s\mathbf{v}_s}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

Here $s$ indexes the included species, $\rho_s$ is species mass density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is species fluid velocity, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ is the local poloidal unit vector in the meridional plane. The quantity includes every species represented in the mass-weighted sum and differs from the [parallel center-of-mass velocity](name:parallel_center_of_mass_velocity), which projects onto the magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the barycentric flow points along the direction of increasing poloidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: poloidal_conductivity
NAMES.short: Poloidal conductivity is the local diagonal coefficient relating conductive poloidal current density to poloidal electric field in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
Poloidal conductivity is the poloidal-poloidal diagonal element of the electrical conductivity tensor in the flux-coordinate directions $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\theta$ is the poloidal angle. It is the local coefficient relating the same-direction conductive current response to the [poloidal electric field](name:poloidal_electric_field); the parent [conductivity](name:conductivity) includes all directional coefficients.

The conductivity tensor and its poloidal current component are defined by

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}}=\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\mathbf{E},\qquad J_{\mathrm{cond},\theta}=\sigma_{\theta\theta}E_\theta+\sum_{j\in\{\rho,\phi\}}\sigma_{\theta j}E_j
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive current-density vector, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the conductivity tensor, and $\sigma_{\theta\theta}$ is the poloidal conductivity coefficient. Here $\rho$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ denote the radial, poloidal, and toroidal flux coordinates.

The named quantity is $\sigma_{\theta\theta}$, not the total poloidal conductive current density; off-diagonal coefficients may also contribute to that current. It is the flux-coordinate counterpart of cylindrical directional coefficients such as [radial conductivity](name:radial_conductivity) and [toroidal conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity).

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Poloidal component, along increasing poloidal angle θ in the flux coordinate system (psi, θ, φ), of the electric current density driven by collisional momentum exchange between plasma particle populations. In partially ionized edge and scrape-off-layer plasmas this contribution is commonly dominated by ion-neutral friction.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density due to collisions is the component of the collision-driven electric current density tangent to a magnetic flux surface in the poloidal direction, represented by the unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ along increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux coordinate system $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$. In an axisymmetric plasma this direction lies in the meridional plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The poloidal component is the projection of the collision-driven charged-particle current onto $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$:

$$
j_{\mathrm{coll},\theta} = \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta \cdot \sum_s q_s n_s \mathbf{v}_{s,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$ in C, $n_s$ is its number density in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf{v}_{s,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the part of its mean velocity in m.s$^{-1}$ produced by collisional momentum balance. These velocities follow from collisional friction force densities entering the species momentum equations; in partially ionized edge plasmas the ion-neutral friction $\mathbf{R}_{in}=m_i n_i \nu_{in}(\mathbf{v}_n-\mathbf{v}_i)$ is commonly the dominant such term.

This quantity is inferred rather than measured directly. Transport and edge-plasma analyzes compute it from charged-particle densities and flows, neutral density and flow estimates, collision frequencies, electromagnetic fields, and momentum-balance closures, then project the resulting current onto $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$. Probes, spectroscopy, interferometry, and charge-exchange measurements constrain the inputs, especially in the edge, divertor, and scrape-off layer.

Magnitudes are negligible in hot, weakly neutral core plasma. In the edge and scrape-off layer modeled values commonly span roughly 1-10$^4$ A.m$^{-2}$, and localized divertor or detached-plasma regions can reach higher values where neutral density and relative ion-neutral velocity are large.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collision-driven current density points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux coordinate system $(\psi, \theta, \phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
NAMES.short: Poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the component along the poloidal basis direction, the direction of increasing poloidal angle θ in a flux-coordinate system (ρ, θ, φ), of the electric current-density contribution generated by parallel viscous stress in a magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the component along the poloidal basis direction of the electric current-density contribution generated by parallel viscous stress in a magnetized plasma. The projection is taken along \(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta\), the unit tangent in the direction of increasing poloidal angle \(\theta\) at fixed radial flux label \(\rho\) and toroidal angle \(\phi\) in the flux-coordinate system \((\rho,\theta,\phi)\).

The component is the projection of the parallel-viscosity current-density vector onto that poloidal tangent:

$$
J_{\Pi_\parallel,\theta}
= \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta \cdot \left[
J_{\Pi_\parallel,\parallel}\,\hat{\mathbf{b}}
+ \frac{\mathbf{B} \times (\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel)}{B^2}
\right]
$$

where \(J_{\Pi_\parallel,\theta}\) is the poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity, \(J_{\Pi_\parallel,\parallel}\) is the signed field-aligned projection of the same current-density contribution, \(\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/B\) is the magnetic-field unit vector, \(\mathbf{B}\) is the magnetic field, \(B=|\mathbf{B}|\), \(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel\) is the parallel viscous stress tensor, and \(\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel\) is the corresponding viscous force density. The cross-product term is the perpendicular force-balance drift contribution associated with the parallel-viscous force density.

This quantity is one directional projection of [current density due to parallel viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity). Other projections of the same contribution include [parallel current density due to parallel viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), [radial current density due to parallel viscosity](name:radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) along \(\hat{R}\), [toroidal current density due to parallel viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) along \(\hat{\phi}\), and [vertical current density due to parallel viscosity](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) along \(+\hat{Z}\) in the right-handed cylindrical \((R,\phi,Z)\) frame, where \(R\) is major radius, \(\phi\) is toroidal angle, and \(Z\) is vertical height. It is distinct from [poloidal current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), which uses the perpendicular-viscous stress contribution rather than \(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel\).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current-density contribution points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle \(\theta\) in the flux-coordinate system \((\rho,\theta,\phi)\).

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_viscosity
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the electric current density produced by viscous-stress terms in plasma momentum balance, resolved toward increasing poloidal angle.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density due to viscosity is the poloidal component of the electric current density associated with viscous-stress terms in plasma momentum balance. It represents the charge transport generated by the viscous contribution to species momentum balance.

In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, let $\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ be the unit tangent directed toward increasing poloidal angle. The component is defined by

$$
j_{\mathrm{visc},\theta}=\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta\cdot\mathbf j_{\mathrm{visc}}=\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta\cdot\sum_s q_s n_s\mathbf u_{s,\mathrm{visc}}
$$

where $s$ labels contributing species, $q_s$ is species charge in C, $n_s$ is number density in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf u_{s,\mathrm{visc}}$ is the viscosity-driven velocity contribution. This is the poloidal projection of the parent [current_density_due_to_viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_viscosity), including the viscous channels retained by the momentum closure. Field-aligned and perpendicular branches are represented by [poloidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) and [poloidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the viscous current component points toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the effective electron particle convection velocity, the advective coefficient multiplying electron density in a poloidal particle-transport flux law.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron convection velocity is the effective advective velocity component for electron particle transport in the poloidal direction of a flux coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is a transport coefficient rather than necessarily the microscopic electron fluid velocity, representing directed electron particle transport after diffusive density-gradient transport is separated.

The poloidal electron particle flux is decomposed into diffusive and convective contributions:

$$
\Gamma_{e,\theta} = -D_{e,\theta}\frac{1}{h_\theta}\frac{\partial n_e}{\partial \theta} + n_e v_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\theta}$ is the poloidal electron particle flux, $D_{e,\theta}$ is the poloidal electron particle diffusivity, $n_e$ is electron number density, $v_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this poloidal electron convection velocity, $\theta$ is the poloidal flux coordinate, and $h_\theta$ converts variation in $\theta$ into physical distance. This component specializes the [electron convection velocity] and differs from the [poloidal electron velocity](name:poloidal_electron_velocity), which represents electron-fluid motion rather than an effective transport coefficient. Its species-resolved contrast is the [poloidal ion charge-state convection velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when electron particle convection is directed clockwise around the magnetic axis in the poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, viewed with the machine centerline on the left.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the electron particle diffusion coefficient. It is the poloidal-poloidal diagonal tensor component in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ), where ρ labels magnetic flux surfaces, θ is poloidal angle, and φ is toroidal angle, relating diffusive electron particle flux to the electron density gradient along θ.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal electron diffusion coefficient is the electron particle diffusivity acting along the poloidal direction tangent to increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ on a magnetic flux surface in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ labels magnetic flux surfaces, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle. It is the poloidal-poloidal diagonal component of an anisotropic particle-transport tensor, relating diffusive electron particle flux to the electron density gradient along that poloidal tangent.

For a Fickian closure of the diffusive part of the [poloidal electron particle flux](name:poloidal_electron_particle_flux), the component along the poloidal tangent satisfies:

$$
\Gamma^{e,\mathrm{diff}}_{\theta} = -D^{e}_{\theta\theta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla n_e
$$

where $\Gamma^{e,\mathrm{diff}}_{\theta}$ is the diffusive poloidal component of the electron particle flux density, $D^{e}_{\theta\theta}$ is the poloidal electron diffusion coefficient, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is the unit tangent in the direction of increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$, and $n_e$ is the electron number density. The minus sign expresses the down-gradient convention for positive diffusivity.

This is a particle transport quantity, distinct from electron energy transport such as [poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It excludes convective contributions to the electron particle flux and off-diagonal tensor couplings; radial transport across flux surfaces is represented by [radial_electron_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_electron_diffusion_coefficient), and a non-direction-specific electron particle diffusivity is represented by [electron_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Poloidal electron energy flux is directed electron thermal-energy transport per unit area toward increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates (psi, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron energy flux is the directed flux of electron thermal energy and enthalpy per unit area along the direction of increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates $(\\psi,\\theta,\\phi)$. It is the poloidal projection of the net [electron energy flux](name:electron_energy_flux), including conductive and convective transport.

The defining projection is

$$
q_{e,\\theta} = \\mathbf{q}_e \\cdot \\hat{\\boldsymbol{e}}_\\theta
$$

where $q_{e,\\theta}$ is the poloidal electron energy flux, $\\mathbf{q}_e$ is the electron energy-flux vector, and $\\hat{\\boldsymbol{e}}_\\theta$ is the unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\\theta$ on a surface of constant $\\psi$.

This directional component is distinct from the [radial electron energy flux](name:radial_electron_energy_flux), which is projected along the cylindrical $+R$ direction; together they describe different projections of the parent vector quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron energy flux points toward increasing poloidal angle $\\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\\psi,\\theta,\\phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Poloidal electron particle flux is the signed rate of electron crossings through a unit area normal to increasing poloidal angle, including convective and nonconvective transport.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron particle flux is the component of the [electron particle flux](name:electron_particle_flux) along the local direction of increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. It is the signed rate at which electrons cross a unit area whose normal is tangent to the flux surface in that direction.

The component is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{e,\theta} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_\theta
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\theta}$ is the poloidal electron particle flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the electron particle-flux density vector, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ is the unit tangent to the flux surface oriented toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

This quantity represents particle-number transport rather than electric-current transport and includes convective, drift, diffusive, and turbulent contributions. Unlike [poloidal electron energy flux](name:poloidal_electron_energy_flux), it counts electron crossings rather than transported energy.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net electron particle flow crosses the oriented surface in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Poloidal electron velocity is the component of the electron-fluid bulk flow along the local poloidal direction around a plasma cross-section.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal electron velocity is the component of the electron fluid bulk flow along the local poloidal direction in a plasma cross-section. It represents advective electron motion, rather than random thermal motion or an individual-particle drift.

The projection of the bulk velocity is defined by:

$$
v_{e,\theta}(\mathbf{x},t)=\mathbf{v}_e(\mathbf{x},t)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $v_{e,\theta}$ and $\mathbf{v}_e$ are velocities in m.s$^{-1}$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ is the dimensionless local unit vector in the poloidal direction. This direction lies in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is a projection of [electron_velocity](name:electron_velocity), whose underlying bulk flow is the first velocity-space moment of the electron distribution. It differs from the effective transport quantity [poloidal_electron_convection_velocity](name:poloidal_electron_convection_velocity), which can include contributions beyond the bulk fluid motion.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron bulk flow points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ around the plasma cross-section.

NAMES.name: poloidal_gyrocenter_frequency
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of gyrocenter orbit angular frequency, equal to the signed rate of gyrocenter advance in poloidal angle θ within flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal gyrocenter frequency is the poloidal component of gyrocenter orbit angular frequency in the flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ is a radial flux-surface label, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle. It describes gyrocenter advance after averaging over the fast cyclotron gyration, retaining the slower drift and bounce or transit motion.

It is defined by

$$
\omega_{\theta,gc} = \frac{d\theta_{gc}}{dt}
$$

where $\omega_{\theta,gc}$ is the poloidal gyrocenter angular frequency, $\theta_{gc}$ is the gyrocenter poloidal angle measured in radians, and $t$ is time measured in seconds.

This component is distinct from the [toroidal gyrocenter frequency](name:toroidal_gyrocenter_frequency), which measures advance in $\phi$; together they form the [gyrocenter frequency](name:gyrocenter_frequency). Passing particles can circulate continuously in poloidal angle, whereas trapped particles reverse their poloidal motion during bounce excursions. The fast cyclotron angular frequency is excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the effective convective velocity used for particle transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal component of the effective convective velocity used for particle transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma. It is the poloidal component of the vector defined by [ion charge state convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity), rather than an energy- or momentum-transport velocity.

The associated advective particle flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{adv}} = n_z v_{\mathrm{conv},z}^{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{adv}}$ is the poloidal advective particle flux density, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state $z$, and $v_{\mathrm{conv},z}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is this velocity component. The component is expressed in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The charge state is resolved rather than summed over ionization states. Unqualified convection velocity denotes particle transport; [poloidal ion charge state energy convection velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity) represents the distinct energy-transport channel.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the component points toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal effective Fickian coefficient for particle transport by ions in a specified charge state, relating the diffusive flux tangent to a magnetic flux surface along increasing θ to that charge state’s density gradient in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion charge-state diffusion coefficient is the effective Fickian transport coefficient for one specified ionic charge state, relating its diffusive particle flux in the poloidal direction to the corresponding number-density gradient. The poloidal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface along increasing $\theta$ in a specified flux coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

The poloidal diffusive particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,q}^{\mathrm{diff}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta = -D_{i,q,\theta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta\cdot\nabla n_{i,q}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,q}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle flux of ion charge state $q$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the unit vector tangent to the magnetic flux surface in the direction of increasing $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, $D_{i,q,\theta}$ is this poloidal diffusion coefficient, and $n_{i,q}$ is the number density of that charge state.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over ion charge states. It is the poloidal directional form of the [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient); the [radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) is the corresponding cylindrical $\hat{R}$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The charge-state-specific scope distinguishes it from the [electron diffusion coefficient](name:electron_diffusion_coefficient), which describes electron particle transport.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a positive number-density gradient along increasing $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ drives diffusive particle flux toward decreasing $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the effective velocity convecting energy for one ion charge state along the poloidal direction of flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective poloidal convection velocity for the energy carried by one specified ion charge state. It is the poloidal component of the [ion charge-state energy convection velocity], representing advective rather than diffusive energy transport.

The poloidal convective energy flux is defined by

$$
\mathcal{F}_{E,i,q}^{\theta,\mathrm{conv}} = v_{E,i,q}^{\theta}\,\mathcal{E}_{i,q}
$$

where $\mathcal{F}_{E,i,q}^{\theta,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the poloidal convective energy flux, $v_{E,i,q}^{\theta}$ is this effective velocity, $\mathcal{E}_{i,q}$ is the energy density of ion charge state $q$, and $i$ identifies the ion species. The component is expressed in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with $\theta$ the poloidal coordinate.

This quantity is distinct from the particle-transport velocity [poloidal ion charge-state convection velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) and from the energy diffusivity [poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated convective energy flux is directed toward increasing poloidal coordinate $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the effective convection velocity governing non-diffusive transport of the momentum density of an ion species in a specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion charge-state momentum convection velocity is the poloidal component of the effective velocity vector governing the non-diffusive term in the charge-state-resolved fluid momentum transport equation.

$$
v_{c,\theta}^{(s)} = \hat{\theta} \cdot \mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}
$$

where $\hat{\theta}$ is the unit vector tangent to a flux surface in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the explicitly defined flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, and $\mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ is the effective momentum convection velocity vector for ion charge state $s$.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and is distinct from [ion_momentum_convection_velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity), which represents aggregate ion momentum transport. It is one projection of the [ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) family and is not generally equal to the mean poloidal fluid velocity; the field-aligned counterpart is [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_{c,\theta}^{(s)}$ points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical dissipation of the poloidal fluid-momentum component for a specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation time at which the poloidal component of ordered fluid momentum of a specified ion charge state is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. The poloidal component is the projection tangent to the poloidal angle coordinate $\theta$ in a flux-coordinate system $(\psi,\theta,\phi)$; the orientation of $+\theta$ defines the sign of the momentum component, not a direction for the scalar rate.

The defining relation for the poloidal fluid momentum density component $p_{\theta,s}$ of ion charge state $s$ subject to dissipation is:

$$
\frac{\partial p_{\theta,s}}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\gamma_{\theta,s} \, p_{\theta,s}
$$

where $\gamma_{\theta,s}$ is the poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate and $p_{\theta,s}$ is the poloidal component of ordered fluid momentum density of the specified charge state. For $\gamma_{\theta,s} > 0$, the dissipative term has the opposite sign to $p_{\theta,s}$ and relaxes that component toward zero; its magnitude is set by Coulomb collisionality, the charge-state mass and effective charge number, and local magnetic geometry through neoclassical friction-force coefficients.

This quantity is the poloidal scalar projection of [ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) and resolves the general [momentum damping rate](name:momentum_damping_rate) concept for an individual ion charge state. It differs from [ion momentum damping rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate), which represents a density-weighted mean over all charge states of the ion population; companion charge-state-resolved projections include [radial ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate), [toroidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate), and [parallel ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the kinematic diffusion coefficient for poloidal-arc transport of poloidal momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state. It relates the down-gradient diffusive momentum flux to the gradient along the poloidal arc of that state’s poloidal flow velocity.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the scalar kinematic transport coefficient governing diffusive poloidal-arc transport of poloidal momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state. It represents collisional, neoclassical, and turbulent mixing of that charge state’s poloidal flow and is the poloidal component of charge-state-resolved momentum diffusivity. The poloidal component is tangent to a magnetic flux surface in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ labels flux surfaces and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ major radius and $Z$ vertical height.

In a local Fick-law closure, the poloidal-arc diffusive flux of poloidal momentum for charge state $s$ is:

$$
\Pi_{s,\theta}^{\rm diff} = -m_s n_s \chi_{s,\theta} \frac{\partial v_{s,\theta}}{\partial \ell_\theta}
$$

where $\Pi_{s,\theta}^{\rm diff}$ is the diffusive flux of poloidal momentum along increasing $\theta$, $m_s$ is the ion mass in kilograms, $n_s$ is the charge-state number density in reciprocal cubic meters, $v_{s,\theta}$ is the charge-state mean poloidal velocity component in meters per second, $\ell_\theta$ is arc length along the poloidal direction on the flux surface in meters, and $\chi_{s,\theta}$ is this diffusivity.

This coefficient acts on the gradient of the poloidal flow velocity along the poloidal arc on a flux surface, not on the gradient of total momentum density. It excludes convective momentum transport, residual stress, and external momentum sources, and it is charge-state resolved rather than charge-state summed; the charge-state-summed counterpart is [poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity). It is distinct from [radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which describes cross-flux-surface transport rather than poloidal-arc transport, and from [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) and [toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which refer to other momentum-diffusion components. The minus sign denotes down-gradient diffusion for a non-negative diffusivity.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux is the flux-surface-normal transport rate per unit area of poloidal linear momentum carried by ions in one specified ionization state.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux is the flux-surface-normal transport rate per unit area of the poloidal linear-momentum component carried by ions in one specified ionization state. It is the poloidal projection of the [ion charge-state momentum flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), not particle transport in the poloidal direction.

In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, it is defined by

$$
\Pi_{z,\rho\theta}=\hat{\mathbf n}_{\rho}\cdot\left(m_i n_z\mathbf v_z\mathbf v_z+p_z\mathbf I+\boldsymbol{\pi}_z\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\rho}$ points toward increasing outward flux coordinate $\rho$, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}$ is the unit vector toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, $m_i$ is ion mass, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state $z$, $\mathbf v_z$ is its fluid velocity, $p_z$ is its scalar pressure, $\mathbf I$ is the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_z$ is its viscous stress tensor.

Unlike [radial ion charge-state momentum flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), this quantity resolves the transported momentum along the poloidal direction. Summing over ionization states gives the corresponding charge-state-aggregated poloidal momentum flux.
NAMES.sign: Positive when poloidal momentum in the direction of increasing $\theta$ is transported toward increasing $\rho$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal ion charge-state momentum source is the area-normalized rate of poloidal momentum transfer to or from one ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion charge-state momentum source is the poloidal projection of the area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It represents directional momentum transfer to or from that charge state through the source processes included in the parent [ion charge-state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source).

For ion species $i$ and charge state $z$, the poloidal component is defined by

$$
S_{\theta,i,z} = \mathbf{S}_{i,z} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i,z}$ is the vector [ion charge-state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source), $S_{\theta,i,z}$ is its poloidal component, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is the local poloidal unit vector tangent to a flux surface. The direction follows increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with vectors represented in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is resolved for one charge state and is not summed over charge states. Charge-state summation produces the [poloidal ion momentum source](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_source), while the corresponding toroidal projection is the [toroidal ion charge-state momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the momentum source points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal ion charge-state particle flux is the directed number flow of ions in a specified ionization charge state along the poloidal direction.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion charge-state particle flux is the component of the particle-flux vector for ions in a specified ionization charge state, resolved independently from other charge states. In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, it describes the number crossing a unit surface normal to the poloidal direction per unit time.

The component is defined from the charge-state flux vector as

$$
\Gamma_{z,\theta}=\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta=n_z v_{z,\theta}
$$

where $z$ is the ionization charge state, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z$ is the charge-state particle-flux vector, $\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta$ is the unit tangent in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, $n_z$ is the charge-state number density, and $v_{z,\theta}$ is its mean poloidal velocity. It is a directional component of [ion charge-state particle flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux), unlike [parallel ion charge-state particle flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), which follows the magnetic field.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ions in charge state $z$ flow in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal projection of the mean bulk fluid velocity of ions in a specified ionization charge state, resolved per charge state rather than averaged over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion charge-state velocity is the poloidal projection of the mean bulk fluid velocity of ions in a specified ionization charge state. It is a component of the vector quantity [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), resolved per charge state rather than averaged over all charge states.

Let $f_z(\mathbf{v})$ be the velocity distribution function for ions in charge state $z$, $n_z$ be their number density, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ be the unit tangent at constant flux-surface label $\rho$ and toroidal angle $\phi$ toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the magnetic-flux coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. The poloidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\theta,z} = \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta \cdot \mathbf{u}_z = \frac{1}{n_z}\int (\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta \cdot \mathbf{v})\,f_z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_z$ is the [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity) for charge state $z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ major radius and $Z$ vertical height.

This component is distinct from the [parallel ion charge-state velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity), [radial ion charge-state velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity), and [vertical ion charge-state velocity](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity). It is not the charge-state-averaged [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the charge-state bulk flow has a component along increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the magnetic-flux coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ used to define the projection.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the diamagnetic drift velocity of a specified ion charge state, driven by that state's partial pressure gradient crossed with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the diamagnetic drift velocity for a specified ion charge state is its projection onto the poloidal unit vector $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. The vector $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ lies in the $R$-$Z$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, is tangent to the local magnetic-flux-surface contour, and is oriented so that the ordered triad $(\hat{n}_{\psi}, \hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}, \hat{\phi})$ is right-handed, with $\hat{n}_{\psi}$ pointing toward increasing [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux).

The full diamagnetic drift velocity for ion charge state $s$ is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} = -\frac{\nabla p_s \times \mathbf{B}}{q_s n_s B^2}
$$

where $p_s$ is the partial pressure of charge state $s$, $q_s = Z_s e$ is its electric charge with $Z_s$ the charge number and $e$ the elementary charge, $n_s$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field with magnitude $B$. The poloidal component is $v_{\mathrm{dia},s,\mathrm{pol}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} \cdot \hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$.

This is the signed flux-surface-tangential projection of the full [ion-charge-state diamagnetic drift velocity](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), not the unsigned magnitude of its projection into the $R$-$Z$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. That poloidal-plane vector can also be resolved into the cylindrical projections [radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift); the complementary toroidal cylindrical projection is [toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and the field-aligned projection is [parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the diamagnetic drift points along the magnetic-flux-surface tangent $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ in the $R$-$Z$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $(\hat{n}_{\psi}, \hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}, \hat{\phi})$ is right-handed and $\hat{n}_{\psi}$ points toward increasing poloidal magnetic flux.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective Fickian diffusivity for total-ion particle transport, relating the poloidal diffusive flux component to the opposing poloidal gradient of charge-state-summed ion number density.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion diffusion coefficient is the effective particle diffusivity for total ions moving in the poloidal direction in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. It parameterizes Fickian poloidal mixing of total ion density; the total ion population is summed over all ionic charge states, while neutral particles and charge-state-resolved coefficients are excluded.

For the poloidal direction, the defining relation is

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(\theta)} = -D_{i,\theta}^{\mathrm{eff}}\nabla_\theta n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(\theta)}$ is the poloidal diffusive particle-flux component, $D_{i,\theta}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is this effective diffusivity, $\nabla_\theta n_i$ is the metric-scaled poloidal gradient of total ion number density, and $n_i$ is the charge-state-summed ion number density. The minus sign specifies transport down the density gradient.

This quantity is the poloidal directional instance of the [ion diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient); the [radial ion diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient) represents the corresponding radial component.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical dissipation of the poloidal component of bulk ion fluid momentum along increasing poloidal angle on magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation timescale at which the poloidal component of ordered bulk ion fluid momentum is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. It is the poloidal projection of [ion momentum damping rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate) in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where increasing $\theta$ defines the poloidal direction.

The damping contribution to the poloidal momentum balance is defined by

$$
\left.\frac{\partial p_{i,\mathrm{pol}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}}=-\nu_{i,\mathrm{pol}}p_{i,\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component of bulk ion momentum density, $\nu_{i,\mathrm{pol}}$ is this damping rate, and $\mathbf{p}_i=m_i n_i\mathbf{v}_i$ with $m_i$ the ion mass, $n_i$ the ion number density, and $\mathbf{v}_i$ the bulk ion velocity. The rate aggregates the contributing ion charge states and is distinct from the charge-state-resolved [poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the rate coefficient reduces the magnitude of the poloidal ion momentum component, producing exponential relaxation toward zero ordered flow.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Poloidal ion momentum flux is the flux-surface-averaged outward transport rate per unit area of poloidal linear momentum for all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion momentum flux is the flux-surface-averaged rate per unit area at which the total ion population transports poloidal linear momentum across magnetic flux surfaces, summed over all ion species and charge states. It is the poloidal projection of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), rather than the toroidal projection represented by [toroidal ion momentum flux](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_flux).

In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, the quantity is defined by

$$
\Pi_{\rho\theta}^{\mathrm{ion}}(\rho)=\left\langle \hat{\mathbf n}_{\rho}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{ion}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}\right\rangle_{\rho}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the total ion momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\rho}$ is the unit normal toward increasing flux label $\rho$, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}$ is the poloidal unit direction toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\rho}$ denotes a flux-surface average. The tensor includes convective, pressure, and viscous stress contributions. The quantity is summed over charge states, whereas [poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) resolves one charge state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when poloidal momentum in the direction of increasing $\theta$ is transported toward increasing $\rho$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Poloidal ion momentum source is the net force-per-area source for the total ion population, summed over all ion charge states and projected onto the poloidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion momentum source is the net source that adds or removes momentum from the total ion population through its poloidal component. Its value is summed over all ion charge states and represents force per unit area, not a volumetric force density.

The poloidal component is defined by:

$$
S_\theta = \mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
$$

where $S_\theta$ is the poloidal ion momentum source, $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the net [ion momentum source](name:ion_momentum_source) vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ is the local unit vector in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. The right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame uses $R$ for major radius, $\phi$ for toroidal angle, and $Z$ for vertical height.

The poloidal direction lies in the $(R,Z)$ plane and is distinct from the radial and toroidal directions. Unlike [poloidal ion charge-state momentum source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), this quantity is summed over all ion charge states.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net momentum source points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net ion number flux through unit area per unit time in the poloidal direction, summed over all charge states of a given ion species.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal ion particle flux is the net transport rate of ions across an oriented unit area in the poloidal direction, summed over all ion charge states of a given species. It is the poloidal component of the ion particle-flux vector in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The component is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{\theta,i}=\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta
$$

where $\Gamma_{\theta,i}$ and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ are the scalar and vector ion particle fluxes, respectively, measured in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ is the local unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

This quantity is the poloidal component of [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux), summed over charge states and distinct from [poloidal ion charge-state particle flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), which resolves one ionization state. It is also distinct from [radial ion particle flux](name:radial_ion_particle_flux), directed normal to magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net ion particle-flux vector has a positive projection toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal linear neutral internal-state momentum flux is the component, along increasing poloidal angle θ in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ), of the linear momentum flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal linear neutral internal-state momentum flux is the projection of the linear momentum flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state onto the local poloidal direction. The poloidal direction is tangent to increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with $\rho$ a flux-surface label and $\phi$ the toroidal angle of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The component is defined by projection onto the poloidal unit vector:

$$
\Pi_\theta^{(n,\alpha)} = \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(n,\alpha)} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol e}_\theta
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is the linear momentum flux density carried by neutral particles of species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol e}_\theta$ is the local unit vector in the direction of increasing $\theta$.

The quantity is state resolved: it includes only neutral particles occupying the specified internal quantum state and excludes charged particles, other neutral internal states, and sums over internal states. It denotes transport of linear momentum and is distinct from angular-momentum flux and from radial or toroidal projections of the same flux.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(n,\alpha)}$ has a component in the $+\hat{\boldsymbol e}_\theta$ direction, toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short: Poloidal magnetic flux at the internal transport barrier is the ψ value on the nested magnetic flux surface that marks the barrier location between the magnetic axis and plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the internal transport barrier is the poloidal-flux-function value $\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ on the nested magnetic flux surface identified with the internal transport barrier. An internal transport barrier is a core or mid-radius region of reduced turbulent transport; this quantity gives the barrier location as a poloidal-flux label, not the magnitude of the transport reduction.

The surface-value definition is

$$
\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}} = \psi(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ITB}})
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the magnetic flux surface identified with the internal transport barrier and $\psi(\mathcal{S})$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at a flux surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface) for surface $\mathcal{S}$.

Relative to the axis and boundary references, the normalized poloidal-flux label is $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ITB}} = (\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})/(\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})$, where $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis) and $\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary). Absolute $\psi$ values include an additive reference; direct comparison of $\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ values requires the same additive reference and sign convention, whereas flux differences and normalized labels are unchanged by a common additive offset. This poloidal-flux location is distinct from the [toroidal flux radius at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_flux_radius_at_internal_transport_barrier) and from edge pedestal loci such as the [poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a flux surface outward from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary has $\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}} > 0$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Poloidal projection of the gage-dependent magnetic vector potential along the unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates (psi, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component $A_\theta$ is the projection of the [magnetic vector potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential) $\mathbf{A}$ onto the unit tangent in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\psi,\theta,\phi)$. It is a signed, gage-dependent component of the electromagnetic potential.

The defining projection is:

$$
A_\theta(\psi,\theta,\phi)=\mathbf{A}(\psi,\theta,\phi)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta
$$

where $\mathbf{A}$ is the magnetic vector potential, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the unit tangent toward increasing $\theta$, $\psi$ is the flux label, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The full potential satisfies $\mathbf{B}=\nabla\times\mathbf{A}$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic induction.

Only the curl of $\mathbf{A}$ is gage invariant, so this component depends on the chosen gage. Unlike the [parallel magnetic vector potential](name:parallel_magnetic_vector_potential), it projects onto the flux-coordinate poloidal tangent rather than the magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\mathbf{A}$ points along $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$, toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_momentum_flux
NAMES.short: Rate of transport of poloidal linear momentum per unit area across an oriented surface in the plasma, combining convective, pressure, and stress contributions.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal momentum flux describes the rate at which the poloidal component of linear momentum crosses a unit area of an oriented surface in the plasma. It is the poloidal projection of the momentum current represented by the parent [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux), not a statement that the surface normal is poloidal.

For flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, its defining projection is:

$$
\Pi_{\theta n} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Pi_{\theta n}$ is the poloidal momentum flux, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}$ is the momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}$ is the dimensionless unit vector in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the dimensionless unit normal to the transport surface. For a constant-$\rho$ magnetic flux surface, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is its chosen positive normal and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

The quantity includes convective, pressure, and viscous or turbulent stress contributions. Species-resolved forms such as [poloidal ion momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux) restrict the contributing population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transported momentum points along increasing $\theta$ and crosses the oriented surface in the direction of its positive unit normal $\hat{\mathbf n}$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal neutral energy flux is the signed energy-flux density carried by neutral atoms and molecules along increasing poloidal angle, summed over neutral species and states.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral energy flux is the scalar projection of the vector energy-flux density carried by neutral particles onto the direction of increasing poloidal angle. It represents neutral energy transport along poloidal surfaces and is the poloidal component of [neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux).

In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, a fluid expression for this component is:

$$
q_{E,n}^{(\theta)} = \hat{e}_{\theta} \cdot \sum_s \left[n_s \mathbf{v}_s \left(h_s + \frac{1}{2}m_s|\mathbf{v}_s|^2\right) - \boldsymbol{\kappa}_s \cdot \nabla T_s\right]
$$

where $q_{E,n}^{(\theta)}$ is the poloidal energy-flux density, $\hat{e}_{\theta}$ is the unit direction of increasing $\theta$, and $s$ indexes neutral species or internal states. Here $n_s$ is number density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is velocity, $h_s$ is enthalpy per particle, $m_s$ is particle mass, $T_s$ is temperature, and $\boldsymbol{\kappa}_s$ is the thermal-conductivity tensor. The sum includes neutral convective enthalpy, bulk-flow kinetic energy, and conductive heat transport; ion and electron energy transport are excluded. Unlike [poloidal neutral particle flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux), this quantity weights transport by carried energy, while [radial neutral energy flux](name:radial_neutral_energy_flux) uses the outward flux-surface direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral energy is transported toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the effective convection velocity for particle transport of a specified neutral internal state, serving as the advective coefficient multiplying the state number density in the poloidal direction of flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal projection of [neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_convection_velocity) onto the poloidal direction $\hat{e}_\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ is a flux-surface label, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The associated poloidal particle flux $\Gamma_{\theta,\mathrm{int}}$ for a specified neutral internal state is:

$$
\Gamma_{\theta,\mathrm{int}} = V_{\theta,\mathrm{int}} \, n_\mathrm{int}
$$

where $V_{\theta,\mathrm{int}}$ is this convection velocity component and $n_\mathrm{int}$ is the number density of the specified neutral internal state (an atomic excitation level or molecular state).

This quantity governs particle (number) transport for the specified state and is distinct from [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity), the analogous coefficient in the energy transport equation which multiplies the state energy density rather than the number density. The ionic analog for resolved charge states is [poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the convection is directed toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective poloidal particle diffusivity for neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal state, relating poloidal diffusive flux to that state's physical number-density gradient along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the neutral internal-state diffusion coefficient governs Fickian particle transport of neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal state along the poloidal direction of flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is the proportionality coefficient between the signed poloidal diffusive particle flux and the physical poloidal gradient of that state's number density.

For a neutral internal state $s$, the poloidal Fickian relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\theta,s}\,\frac{1}{h_\theta}\frac{\partial n_s}{\partial \theta}
$$

where $D_{\theta,s}$ is the poloidal neutral internal-state diffusion coefficient, $\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive particle-flux component, $n_s$ is the number density of neutral atoms or molecules in internal state $s$, and $h_\theta = |\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial\theta|_{\rho,\phi}$ is the poloidal metric scale factor for flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The factor $h_\theta^{-1}\partial/\partial\theta$ is the derivative along physical poloidal arc length, not a bare angular derivative.

This coefficient applies only to particle-number diffusion of the specified neutral internal state. It excludes momentum diffusion, energy diffusion, radial diffusion, and off-diagonal transport couplings unless such effects are explicitly represented as part of the effective scalar coefficient.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the poloidal diffusive particle flux is opposite to the physical poloidal gradient of the state number density, with a positive flux component pointing toward increasing poloidal coordinate $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density of a specified neutral internal state, directed along increasing poloidal angle θ in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
Poloidal effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density of a specified neutral internal state is the component of the effective convection velocity along the tangent direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is the poloidal directional realization of the [neutral internal-state energy convection velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity).

For the poloidal transport direction, the convective energy-flux component is defined by

$$
q_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}} = u_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}} w_{E,\nu}
$$

where $q_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the poloidal convective energy-flux component, $u_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this poloidal effective convection velocity, $w_{E,\nu}$ is the energy density of the neutral internal state, and $\nu$ identifies that state.

The quantity applies to the specified state and does not sum over all neutral internal states. It is the poloidal member of the directional set that also includes the [radial neutral internal-state energy convection velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity) and the [field-aligned neutral internal-state energy convection velocity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity); by contrast, [neutral species energy convection velocity](name:neutral_species_energy_convection_velocity) represents the corresponding energy transport aggregated over a neutral species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective velocity points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, making the convective energy flux positive in that direction.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Fick's-law poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient multiplying the poloidal temperature gradient of neutral particles in a specified internal state in diffusive thermal-energy transport. It is internal-state-resolved and represents only the Fickian poloidal contribution.
NAMES.long:
Fick's-law poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar poloidal diffusivity for energy transport by neutral particles in a specified internal state, and is the poloidal component form of the [neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It is resolved for one internal state, not summed or averaged over internal states, and relates only the poloidal projection of the diffusive thermal-energy flux to the poloidal temperature gradient of those same particles.

The poloidal projection is taken along the tangent obtained by increasing the poloidal angle $\theta$ at constant flux coordinate $\rho$ and toroidal angle $\phi$ in a chosen flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The Fickian poloidal contribution is defined by

$$
q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,\theta} = - n_{n,s} D^{\theta}_{E,n,s} \, \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla T_{n,s}
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,\theta}$ is the poloidal component of the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, positive in the direction of increasing $\theta$; $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is the corresponding unit poloidal tangent; $n_{n,s}$ is the number density of those particles; $D^{\theta}_{E,n,s}$ is this coefficient; and $T_{n,s}$ is their temperature.

The coefficient includes only the diagonal Fickian term driven by $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla T_{n,s}$ and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, cross-gradient tensor terms, and effective coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. The factor $n_{n,s}\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla T_{n,s}$ is the temperature-gradient contribution to the poloidal gradient of internal thermal-energy density; an energy-density-gradient form using $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla(n_{n,s}T_{n,s})$ is equivalent only when the density-gradient contribution along the poloidal tangent is absent.

It specializes the [internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) to neutral particles and the poloidal projection. It is distinct from the [radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), where radial denotes the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [poloidal neutral energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal energy-flux density carried by neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of neutral internal-state energy flux is the signed energy-flux density carried by neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state. It is the poloidal projection of the [neutral internal-state energy flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux), selecting the component tangent to a magnetic flux surface along increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed flux label $\rho$ and toroidal angle $\phi$ in a specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The component is defined as:

$$
q_{n,s}^{\theta} = \hat{e}_{\theta} \cdot \int f_{n,s}(\mathbf{v}) \left( \tfrac{1}{2} m v^2 + \epsilon_s \right) \mathbf{v} \, d^3v
$$

where $q_{n,s}^{\theta}$ is this poloidal component, $\hat{e}_{\theta}$ is the unit tangent toward increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$ in the specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, $f_{n,s}$ is the velocity distribution of neutrals in internal state $s$, $m$ is the neutral particle mass, $\epsilon_s$ is the energy of internal state $s$, and $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity.

This quantity uses the same neutral-state energy weighting as the surface-normal parent, but its projection direction is poloidal rather than normal to a reference surface. It is distinct from the [parallel neutral internal-state energy flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) along the local magnetic field. The analogous poloidal number-flux component without energy weighting is [poloidal neutral internal-state particle flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when net energy transport is directed along increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$ in the specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the momentum diffusion coefficient for neutral particles in a resolved neutral-state channel. It governs Fickian redistribution of that state's full momentum vector along the poloidal direction; the qualifier selects the flux and gradient direction, not a transported momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal component of the momentum diffusion coefficient for neutral particles in a resolved neutral-state channel. It is the effective kinematic coefficient governing Fickian redistribution of momentum carried by neutrals along the poloidal direction. The transported quantity is the full momentum vector of the specified neutral internal-state population, not only its poloidal projection.

For neutral internal state $\alpha$, the diagonal Fickian constitutive relation in the poloidal transport direction is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha,\mathrm{pol}} = -D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha,\mathrm{pol}}\,\frac{\partial \mathbf{M}_{\alpha}}{\partial \ell_{\mathrm{pol}}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha,\mathrm{pol}}$ is the vector diffusive flux of momentum through surfaces normal to the poloidal direction, $D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha,\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient, $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$ is the momentum density carried by neutrals in state $\alpha$, and $\ell_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is an arclength coordinate increasing along the poloidal circuit in a meridional plane spanned by $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The minus sign gives down-gradient transport of each component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$.

This member of the [neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) family covers only the diagonal coefficient for poloidal flux driven by a poloidal gradient. It is distinct from the [radial](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) members, which select different flux and gradient directions, and from off-diagonal tensor transport, where a gradient in one direction contributes to momentum flux through another. The qualifier poloidal is not a selector for a transported momentum component.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the particle flux of neutral particles in a specified internal state: the net number crossing unit area per unit time along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component selects the $\hat{\theta}$ projection of the [neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) vector $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{(s)}$, giving the signed number of neutrals in internal state $s$ that cross a unit area oriented normal to $\hat{\theta}$ per unit time.

$$
\Gamma_\theta^{(s)} = n^{(s)} v_\theta^{(s)}
$$

where $n^{(s)}$ is the number density of neutrals in internal state $s$ and $v_\theta^{(s)}$ is their mean fluid velocity projected onto the poloidal unit vector $\hat{\theta}$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, with $\rho$ labeling magnetic flux surfaces and $\theta$ the poloidal angle.

This quantity is internal-state-resolved; summing over all internal states recovers the total [poloidal_neutral_particle_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux). The analogous energy-flux component is [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutrals flow in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.
