NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the bulk fluid velocity for neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or energy state.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal velocity $v_\theta$ of a neutral population in a resolved internal (quantum or energy) state is the projection of the [neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity) vector onto the poloidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
v_\theta = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{n,s}} \cdot \hat{\theta}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{n,s}}$ is the bulk fluid velocity of neutral particles in internal state $s$, $\hat{\theta}$ is the unit vector along the chosen poloidal direction, and $R$, $\phi$, and $Z$ are the major-radius, toroidal-angle, and vertical coordinates.

This quantity is resolved separately for each internal quantum or energy state and is distinct from the state-unresolved [poloidal_neutral_velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_velocity). The [radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity) gives the complementary major-radius component of the same state-resolved neutral flow.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the resolved neutral state population flows in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the effective E×B drift velocity assigned to a neutral species in a specified internal state, projected along the direction of increasing poloidal angle θ in a specified flux-coordinate system (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the [effective neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the projection of the assigned drift velocity onto the poloidal unit direction of the specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

The component is defined from the local electric and magnetic fields by

$$
v_\theta = \left(\frac{\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}\right) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}
$$

where $v_\theta$ is the poloidal velocity component, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ is the unit tangent in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed flux-surface label $\rho$ and toroidal angle $\phi$ in the specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

This effective velocity is assigned to the specified neutral internal state for transport attribution; it does not imply direct Lorentz acceleration of neutral particles. It is distinct from the [radial neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) and [toroidal neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), which use different projection directions. A pure E×B drift has no component along the magnetic-field direction, distinguishing this quantity from the [parallel neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the assigned velocity points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal neutral momentum flux is the poloidal-poloidal component of neutral linear-momentum transport in the edge plasma, combining convective and isotropic-pressure contributions summed over all neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral momentum flux is the poloidal-poloidal component of the [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux) tensor. It represents neutral linear momentum transported through a surface normal to the local poloidal direction in the edge plasma, aggregated over all neutral species and internal states. In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, $theta$ is the poloidal angle and the projection follows the local unit direction $\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ of increasing $\theta$.

For an ideal isotropic neutral fluid, the defining component is:

$$
\Pi_{n,\theta\theta} = \hat{\mathbf e}_\theta \cdot \overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_\theta = m_n n_n v_{n,\theta}^{2} + p_n
$$

where $\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n$ is the neutral momentum-flux tensor, $m_n$ is neutral particle mass in kg, $n_n$ is neutral number density in m$^{-3}$, $v_{n,\theta}$ is the poloidal velocity component in m s$^{-1}$, and $p_n = n_n k_B T_n$ is isotropic neutral pressure; $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant and $T_n$ is neutral temperature. The [poloidal neutral velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_velocity) supplies the associated flow component.

This quantity is summed over neutral species and internal states rather than resolved by species or state. It differs from the [vertical neutral momentum flux](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux) because both tensor projections are poloidal rather than vertical.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states. Its sign distinguishes neutral momentum transfer along and opposite to the local poloidal direction.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states, is the net neutral momentum transfer per unit area resolved along the poloidal direction. It is one projection of the aggregate [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source).

The projection of the aggregate source onto the local positive poloidal unit direction is

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{pol}} = \mathbf{S}_{n}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{pol}} = \sum_{a\in\mathcal{N}} \mathbf{S}_{n,a}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal neutral momentum source, $\mathbf{S}_{n}$ is the aggregate [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source), $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local positive poloidal unit direction in the poloidal plane spanned by the $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$ basis directions of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\mathcal{N}$ is the set of neutral internal states, and $\mathbf{S}_{n,a}$ is the [neutral internal-state momentum source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) for state $a$.

The quantity is summed over neutral internal states and is not a single-state source. It is a signed scalar projection, distinct from the vector aggregate source and from the [radial](name:radial_neutral_momentum_source), [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_source), and [parallel](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_source) neutral momentum-source projections.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net neutral momentum transfer points along the local positive poloidal direction in the poloidal plane spanned by the $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$ basis directions of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the total neutral particle flux density, summed over all neutral species and internal states, giving the net number of neutrals crossing a unit surface area per unit time in the poloidal direction in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal neutral particle flux density is the poloidal projection of the total [neutral_particle_flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) vector, integrated over all neutral species and internal atomic or molecular states. It quantifies the net flow of neutral atoms and molecules per unit area per unit time along the poloidal direction, and is the species-integrated counterpart to [poloidal_neutral_state_particle_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux), which resolves the same quantity for a single specified neutral internal state.

The quantity appears in the neutral particle continuity equation:

$$
\frac{\partial n_n}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_n = S_n
$$

where $n_n$ is the neutral number density, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_n$ is the neutral particle flux vector, and $S_n$ is the net source density from ionization, recombination, and charge exchange. The poloidal component $\Gamma_{n,\theta} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_n \cdot \hat{e}_\theta$ drives neutral transport along the poloidal angle $\theta$.

In the edge plasma, strong poloidal neutral flows arise from recycling at plasma-facing components, charge-exchange momentum transfer with ions, and ionization sinks near the target plates. This flux component is computed within neutral fluid or kinetic transport models covering the scrape-off layer and divertor. The companion quantity [poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux) captures poloidal transport of momentum carried by the same neutral population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutrals flow in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the mean translational flow of a selected neutral-particle population, projected onto the local poloidal direction.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal neutral velocity is the poloidal component of the bulk flow vector of a selected neutral-particle population. It is a directional projection of [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity), rather than a particle flux or momentum flux.

At position $\mathbf r$, it is defined by projecting the first velocity moment onto the local poloidal unit vector:

$$
u_{n,\mathrm{pol}}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}(\mathbf r)\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int \mathbf v\,f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $\mathbf r$ is position in m, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity in m s$^{-1}$, $f_{n,a}$ is the phase-space density, $a$ labels included neutral internal-state or energy subpopulations, $\mathcal A$ is their included set, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the defined local poloidal unit vector. The state-resolved counterpart is [poloidal neutral internal-state velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projected flow points along the defined positive poloidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: power_density
NAMES.short: Net volumetric rate of energy transfer to or from a specified plasma population, energy channel, orbit class, radiation field, or material region.
NAMES.long:
Power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from a designated recipient per unit volume. The recipient may be a plasma population, energy channel, orbit class, radiation field, or material region, as defined by the applicable energy balance.

For a differential volume, the volumetric power density is defined by

$$
p_E = \frac{dE}{dt\,dV}
$$

where $E$ is the energy transferred to the designated recipient, $t$ is time, and $V$ is volume. A flux-surface, spatial, or population average may be applied while retaining the underlying per-volume meaning.

Positive values denote net energy gain by the designated recipient; negative values denote net energy loss. Heating, collisional exchange, radiation, nuclear deposition, particle interactions, and transport-model source or sink terms may contribute according to the qualified balance. [ion charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density) specializes the recipient, while [radiated power density](name:radiated_power_density) specializes the transfer channel and [power density of limiter tile](name:power_density_of_limiter_tile) specializes a material region.

NAMES.name: co_passing_power_density
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for the co-passing orbit population, representing energy transfer to or from particles circulating in the co-current direction.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which kinetic energy is transferred to or from the co-passing orbit population per unit physical volume. Co-passing particles are passing particles that circulate continuously in the co-current direction.

For a flux surface labeled by poloidal magnetic flux $psi$, it is defined as

$$
p_{E,\mathrm{co}}(\psi)=\left\langle\frac{dE_{\mathrm{co}}}{dt\,dV}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the kinetic energy of the co-passing population, $t$ is time, $V$ is physical volume, and the angle brackets denote a flux-surface average. Positive values denote net energy gain by this population; negative values denote net energy loss. Wave-particle interactions, collisions, and particle sources may contribute. The related [counter-passing power density](name:counter_passing_power_density) applies the same energy-transfer definition to the oppositely circulating orbit class, while [power density](name:power_density) is the unqualified parent quantity.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_power_density
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for counter-passing particles, representing energy transfer to or from particles circulating opposite to the plasma-current direction.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which energy is transferred to or from the counter-passing orbit population per unit physical volume. It is the orbit-class specialization of [power density](name:power_density); counter-passing particles are passing particles that circulate opposite to the plasma-current direction, distinct from [co-passing power density](name:co_passing_power_density) and [trapped power density](name:trapped_power_density).

For the underlying local energy balance, volumetric power density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{cp}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{cp}}}{dt\,dV}
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the energy transferred to the counter-passing population, $t$ is time, and $V$ is physical volume. The flux-surface average is applied to this local rate while retaining its per-volume meaning.

Positive values denote net energy gain by the counter-passing population; negative values denote net energy loss. Wave-particle interactions, collisions, and particle sources contribute when they are included in the counter-passing energy balance.

NAMES.name: electron_power_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Net volumetric rate of energy transfer to or from the electron population in the electron energy balance.
NAMES.long:
Electron power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from the electron population per unit volume. It is the scalar source term for the electron recipient in an electron energy balance, including only the source and sink terms assigned to electrons in that balance.

For a differential volume, the electron power density is defined by

$$
p_e = \frac{dE_e}{dt\,dV}
$$

where $E_e$ is the accumulated signed change of electron-population energy produced by the included source and sink terms, $t$ is time, and $V$ is physical volume.

Electron power density specializes [power density](name:power_density) to the electron population. The volume integral of $p_e$ over a specified plasma region gives [electron power](name:electron_power) for the same electron energy balance; power densities for ions, radiation fields, neutrals, or material regions use different recipients.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the included balance terms increase the energy of the electron population.

NAMES.name: ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Ion power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from the ion population per unit volume. It is the scalar source term for the ion recipient in an ion energy transport equation, summed over all ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Ion power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from the ion population per unit volume. It is the scalar source term for the ion recipient in an ion energy transport equation, including only the source and sink mechanisms assigned to that ion-channel balance.

For a differential volume, the ion-channel source term is defined by

$$
S_{E,i} = \frac{\partial^2 E_i}{\partial t\,\partial V}
$$

where $S_{E,i}$ is ion power density, $E_i$ is the energy transferred to the ion population in joules, $t$ is time in seconds, and $V$ is physical volume in cubic meters. In a local ion energy transport equation, $S_{E,i}$ appears separately from the divergence of the ion energy flux, which represents spatial redistribution rather than local transfer to the ion population.

The ion population is the species-level ion recipient; because energy source rate is extensive, this quantity is summed over all ion charge states. It is not a charge-state-resolved source term, which is represented by [ion charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density). When individual ion-channel contributions and their aggregate are both defined, [total ion power density](name:total_ion_power_density) is the sum of the included contributions in the same ion energy transport equation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion population gains energy in the ion energy transport equation.

NAMES.name: power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Signed local rate of collisional energy exchange per unit volume for a specified plasma population, species, charge state, or internal state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for a designated target population. It is positive for energy deposited in the target and negative for energy transferred from it.

$$
P_a^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_a^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the target power density in W m$^{-3}$, $Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate per unit volume from partner population $b$ to target $a$, and the sum includes the collision partners and subpopulations specified by the quantity's aggregation scope.

The target may be a broad population, as in [particle collisional power density](name:particle_power_density_due_to_collisions), or a species, ion charge state, internal state, or electron population. Aggregated electron and ion quantities include the designated contributing species and states, whereas resolved quantities retain only their specified target, as in [ion charge-state collisional power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [internal-state collisional power density](name:internal_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the designated target population gains energy from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for the aggregate electron population, including bulk thermal and suprathermal fast electrons.
NAMES.long:
Electron collisional power density is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for the aggregate electron population, including bulk thermal and suprathermal fast electrons. It combines exchange with all collision partners without resolving the target into an electron subpopulation.

The quantity follows the shared definition of [power density due to collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions):

$$
P_e^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{e\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_e^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the electron collisional power density in W m$^{-3}$, $Q_{e\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the energy-transfer rate per unit volume from collision-partner population $b$ to the aggregate electron target, and the sum includes all specified collision partners and electron subpopulations.

Unlike [fast-electron collisional power density](name:fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), this quantity includes both thermal and suprathermal electron targets. Its volume integral corresponds to [electron collisional power](name:electron_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aggregate electron population gains energy from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed local volumetric Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for the suprathermal electron population, summed over its co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
Fast-electron collisional power density is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for the suprathermal, non-Maxwellian electron population. It includes the kinetic-energy changes of all represented fast-electron orbit classes.

The quantity follows the shared definition of [electron collisional power density](name:electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) for the fast-electron component:

$$
P_{fe}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{fe\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{fe}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-electron collisional power density, $Q_{fe\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the energy-transfer rate from collision-partner population $b$ to the fast-electron target, and the sum includes all specified collision partners. The quantity aggregates the co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped contributions, including [co-passing fast-electron collisional power density](name:co_passing_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) where that component is resolved. It excludes the bulk thermal-electron contribution and therefore forms only the fast-electron part of the aggregate electron quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the fast-electron population gains energy from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Co-passing fast-electron collisional power density is the power density for the kinetic-energy change of the co-passing guiding-center component of the fast-electron distribution caused by Coulomb collisions. It is positive for energy gain by that component and negative for energy loss.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing fast-electron collisional power density is the local rate of change of kinetic energy density of the co-passing-orbit component of the fast-electron distribution caused by Coulomb collisions. The co-passing component is the passing guiding-center subset whose toroidal motion is in the direction of the plasma current; for positive plasma current this is increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the co-passing contribution to the fast-electron collisional energy balance.

The quantity is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator restricted to the co-passing fast-electron orbit class:

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast,co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x})} \frac{1}{2} m_e v^2\, C_{es}[f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}, f_s](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\Omega_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the co-passing part of the fast-electron velocity or guiding-center phase space at that position, the sum is over collision partners $s$, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is speed, $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is normalized so that its velocity-space integral gives fast-electron density, $f_s$ is the distribution of species $s$, and $C_{es}$ is the collision-operator contribution to $\partial f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}/\partial t$ from collisions with $s$. For relativistic fast electrons, the nonrelativistic kinetic-energy weight is replaced by the corresponding relativistic kinetic energy.

The qualifier co-passing restricts the receiving fast-electron component, not the collision partner; collision partners are those included in the sum. It excludes the [counter-passing fast-electron collisional power density](name:counter_passing_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [trapped fast-electron collisional power density](name:trapped_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) receiving components. With a common collision operator and phase-space partition, the co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped components sum to [fast-electron collisional power density](name:fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the kinetic energy of the co-passing-orbit fast-electron component.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Counter-passing fast-electron collisional power density is the local rate of kinetic-energy change of the counter-passing guiding-center component of the suprathermal electron distribution caused by Coulomb collisions with other plasma species. It is the counter-passing orbit-class contribution to the fast-electron collisional energy balance, positive for energy gain by that component and negative for energy loss.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing fast-electron collisional power density is the local rate of change of kinetic energy density of the counter-passing component of the fast-electron distribution caused by Coulomb collisions with other plasma species. It is the counter-passing orbit-class contribution to the fast-electron collisional energy balance. The counter-passing component consists of passing guiding-center states whose bounce-averaged toroidal angular motion is opposite to the plasma-current circulation; the toroidal angle is $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator over the counter-passing part of fast-electron phase space:

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast,counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \int \chi_{\mathrm{counter}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, \frac{1}{2} m_e v^2\, C_{es}[f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}, f_s](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where the sum is over collision partners $s$, $\chi_{\mathrm{counter}}$ is the phase-space indicator equal to one on counter-passing fast-electron guiding-center states and zero elsewhere, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is speed, $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is normalized so that $\int f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}\,d^3v$ gives the local fast-electron density, $f_s$ is the distribution of species $s$, and $C_{es}$ is the Coulomb collision operator giving the collisional time derivative of $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ due to species $s$. The counter-passing restriction is applied by $\chi_{\mathrm{counter}}$; it does not redefine the collision partners. For relativistic fast electrons, the kinetic-energy weight is replaced by the appropriate relativistic kinetic energy.

The orbit-class partition is non-overlapping: [co-passing](name:co_passing_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), counter-passing, and [trapped](name:trapped_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) components sum to [fast-electron collisional power density](name:fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) when the same collision operator and phase-space partition are used. This quantity excludes collisional energy exchange assigned to the thermal-electron population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to the counter-passing fast-electron component.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for ions in a specified charge state, positive for net energy gain and negative for net energy loss.
NAMES.long:
Ion charge-state collisional power density is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for ions in a specified charge state. It includes the contributing thermal and fast ion populations represented by that charge state.

$$
P_{i,z}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{i,z\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{i,z}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional power density for ion population $i$ in charge state $z$, and $Q_{i,z\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the rate of collisional energy transfer from partner population $b$ to that target. The sum covers the collision partners included by the aggregation scope. This is the charge-state-resolved specialization of [power density due to collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions); unlike [fast-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), it is not restricted to fast ions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the specified ion charge state gains energy from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer to fast ions of a specified charge state, aggregated over co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
Fast ion charge state power density due to collisions is the local volumetric rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to or from fast ions of a single, specified charge state. It is the fast-ion-targeted component of [ion charge state power density due to collisions](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The total power density is the sum over the resolved guiding-center orbit classes:

$$
p_{\mathrm{fast},z} = p_{\mathrm{co},z} + p_{\mathrm{counter},z} + p_{\mathrm{trapped},z}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{co},z}$, $p_{\mathrm{counter},z}$, and $p_{\mathrm{trapped},z}$ are the power densities for [co-passing fast ions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), counter-passing fast ions, and [trapped fast ions](name:trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), respectively, and $z$ denotes the specified ion charge state.

The quantity is aggregated over these orbit classes but remains resolved by charge state; it is not summed over charge states.
NAMES.sign: Positive when fast ions of the specified charge state gain net kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer rate for a specified fast-ion charge state, restricted to co-passing particles circulating poloidally with the plasma current.
NAMES.long:
Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer for a specified fast-ion charge state, contributed exclusively by co-passing particles—fast ions whose guiding-center orbits complete full poloidal circuits in the same direction as the plasma current. It is the co-passing-orbit component of [fast-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
P_\mathrm{co} = \int_{\Omega_\mathrm{co}} \dot{E}_z(\mathbf{v})\,f_z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $f_z(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity-distribution function of fast ions in charge state $z$, $\dot{E}_z$ is their Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer rate per particle, and $\Omega_\mathrm{co}$ is the co-passing orbit domain. Summing this quantity with the [counter-passing contribution](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and the trapped-orbit contribution recovers the parent quantity's orbit-class partition.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the co-passing fast-ion charge state gains kinetic energy from Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer rate for a specified fast-ion charge state, restricted to counter-passing particles that circulate poloidally antiparallel to the plasma current.
NAMES.long:
Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer for a specified fast-ion charge state, contributed exclusively by counter-passing particles — fast ions whose guiding-center orbits complete full poloidal circuits antiparallel to the plasma current. It is the counter-passing-orbit component of [fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
P_\mathrm{ctr} = \int_{\Omega_\mathrm{ctr}} \dot{E}_z(\mathbf{v}) \, f_z(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $f_z(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity-distribution function of fast ions in charge state $z$, $\dot{E}_z$ is the Coulomb collisional energy-transfer rate per particle, and $\Omega_\mathrm{ctr}$ denotes the counter-passing orbit domain — passing orbits with parallel velocity antiparallel to the direction of the plasma current.

Summing this quantity with the [co-passing](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [trapped](name:trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) contributions recovers the total fast-ion charge-state collisional power density partitioned by orbit class.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the counter-passing fast-ion charge state gains kinetic energy from Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for the aggregate ion population, including thermal and fast ions.
NAMES.long:
Ion collisional power density is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for the aggregate ion population. It combines energy exchange for the included thermal and fast ion subpopulations.

$$
P_{\mathrm{ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_{a\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the aggregate ion power density, $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of included ion target populations, and $Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate to target population $a$ from partner population $b$. The aggregation includes the contributing ion species, charge states, and orbit classes. This quantity is the ion-population specialization of [power density due to collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions); its thermal and fast components are represented by [thermal ion power density due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [fast ion power density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aggregate ion population gains energy from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net local volumetric power density transferred to the suprathermal fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions, summed over species, charge states, and orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
Fast-ion collisional power density is the aggregate local volumetric rate at which the suprathermal fast-ion population gains or loses kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions with electrons and other plasma constituents. It is the fast-ion component of the total [ion collisional power density](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), complementary to [thermal-ion collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The orbit-aggregated quantity is defined by

$$
Q_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_{o} Q_{\mathrm{fast},o}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-ion collisional power density, $Q_{\mathrm{fast},o}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the contribution from orbit class $o$, and the sum includes co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped fast ions. Species and charge-state contributions are also included in the aggregate.

This quantity excludes collisional energy transfer to the bulk thermal-ion population, which is represented by the corresponding thermal-ion component. Positive values denote net collisional energy gain by the fast-ion population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the fast-ion population gains kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local volumetric Coulomb collisional energy transfer rate to fast ions belonging to the co-passing orbit class, which circulate poloidally in the same direction as the plasma current.
NAMES.long:
The co-passing orbit class consists of fast ions whose guiding-center trajectories complete full poloidal circuits in the same direction as the plasma current, as opposed to trapped particles (which bounce between magnetic mirror points) and counter-passing ions. This quantity isolates the co-passing contribution to the total fast-ion collisional power density, enabling orbit-resolved energy-balance analysis of suprathermal ion populations.

The collisional power density is the energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator restricted to the co-passing velocity-space domain:

$$
P_{\mathrm{cp}} = \int_{\mathrm{co\text{-}passing}} \tfrac{1}{2} m_i v^2 \, C[f_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{cp}}] \, d^3v
$$

where $m_i$ is the fast-ion mass in kg, $v$ is the particle speed in m s$^{-1}$, and $C[f_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{cp}}]$ is the Coulomb collision operator acting on the co-passing portion of the fast-ion distribution function.

Orbit-resolving Fokker-Planck or Monte Carlo kinetic codes evaluate this quantity by partitioning velocity space into co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped regions. Summing these three orbit-class components recovers [fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), the total fast-ion collisional power density. The symmetric companion for the counter-circulating population is [counter_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions); asymmetry between the two arises from anisotropic fast-ion sources such as co-injected neutral beams.
NAMES.sign: Positive when co-passing fast ions gain kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net local volumetric power density transferred by Coulomb collisions to suprathermal fast ions on counter-passing orbits, whose parallel motion is opposite to the plasma-current direction.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing fast-ion collisional power density is the local volumetric rate at which suprathermal fast ions on counter-passing guiding-center orbits gain or lose kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions. It includes the contributing fast-ion species and charge states, while restricting the orbit class to particles circulating opposite to the plasma-current direction.

The charge-state-resolved aggregate is defined by

$$
Q_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_s \sum_z Q_{\mathrm{counter},s,z}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the counter-passing fast-ion collisional power density, $s$ indexes fast-ion species, $z$ indexes their charge states, and $Q_{\mathrm{counter},s,z}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the corresponding contribution.

This quantity is the counter-passing component of [fast-ion collisional power density](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions); the complementary co-passing contribution is [co-passing fast-ion collisional power density](name:co_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions). It excludes trapped and co-passing fast ions from its orbit aggregate.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the counter-passing fast-ion population gains kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: particle_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for a designated particle population, positive for net energy gain and negative for net energy loss.
NAMES.long:
Particle collisional power density is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for a designated particle population. It is the particle-population specialization of [power density due to collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
P_a^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_a^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the power density received by target population $a$, $Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate from partner population $b$ to target $a$, and the sum covers the collision partners and particle subpopulations included by the aggregation scope.

The target may be resolved or aggregated by particle species, charge state, internal state, or orbit class. The [fast-particle collisional power density](name:fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions) is a specific instance, while [particle power due to collisions](name:particle_power_due_to_collisions) is its volume-integrated counterpart.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the designated target particle population gains energy from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Local Coulomb-collisional power density for the complete fast-particle population, summing kinetic-energy exchange over co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped guiding-center orbits.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net local volumetric rate at which Coulomb collisions change the kinetic energy of the complete fast-particle population. It aggregates the contributions from all included charged collision partners and from the co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit classes described by [particle collisional power density](name:particle_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The orbit-class aggregation is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = P_{\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}} + P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} + P_{\mathrm{trapped}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the total fast-particle collisional power density, and the three terms are the corresponding contributions represented by [co-passing fast-particle collisional power density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions), [counter-passing fast-particle collisional power density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions), and [trapped fast-particle collisional power density](name:trapped_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions). Positive values denote net kinetic-energy gain by the fast-particle population; negative values denote net loss.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Local Coulomb-collisional power density changing the kinetic-energy density of fast particles on co-passing guiding-center orbits.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing fast-particle collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions change the kinetic-energy density of fast particles on co-passing guiding-center orbits. It is one orbit-class contribution to the complete [fast-particle collisional power density](name:fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions), including energy exchange with all included charged collision partners.

The orbit-class aggregation is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = P_{\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}} + P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} + P_{\mathrm{trapped}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the complete fast-particle collisional power density, $P_{\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this co-passing contribution, and the other terms are the [counter-passing fast-particle collisional power density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [trapped fast-particle collisional power density](name:trapped_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions). Positive values denote net kinetic-energy gain by the co-passing population; negative values denote net loss.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional power density transferred back to the fast particle population via collisions with electrons, as a 1D radial profile for co-passing particles. Quantifies the energy exchange rate from electrons to suprathermal particles per unit volume.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power density to the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Local Coulomb-collisional power density changing the kinetic-energy density of fast particles on counter-passing guiding-center orbits.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing fast-particle collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions change the kinetic-energy density of fast particles on counter-passing guiding-center orbits. Counter-passing orbits are passing trajectories whose parallel transit is opposite to the reference co-passing direction; this quantity is the collisional source or sink for that orbit class, not its stored kinetic-energy density.

For fast species $a$, the counter-passing contribution is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator restricted to counter-passing phase space:

$$
P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{a\in\mathrm{fast}} \sum_b \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{counter}}} \frac{1}{2} m_a v^2 C_{ab}[f_a,f_b](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the counter-passing fast-particle collisional power density at position $\mathbf{x}$, $m_a$ is the mass of fast species $a$, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is speed, $C_{ab}$ is the Coulomb collision operator giving the collisional time derivative of the fast-species distribution $f_a$ due to charged partner species $b$, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{counter}}$ is the counter-passing region of velocity or guiding-center phase space.

Together with [co-passing fast-particle collisional power density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [trapped fast-particle collisional power density](name:trapped_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions), it forms the orbit-class decomposition of [fast-particle collisional power density](name:fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions): $P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = P_{\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}} + P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} + P_{\mathrm{trapped}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$. The partner sum includes only the charged collision partners represented in the collisional model; a partner-resolved quantity would use the corresponding single partner contribution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the kinetic-energy density of the counter-passing fast-particle population.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional power density transferred to the fast particle electron population from the counter-passing distribution via Coulomb collisions, as a 1D radial profile. Quantifies the energy exchange rate between fast electrons and the electron population.

NAMES.name: power_density_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.short: Local rate at which kinetic energy from suprathermal particles is deposited into the thermal plasma through collisional thermalization.
NAMES.long:
Thermalization power density is the local volumetric rate of kinetic-energy transfer from a fast or suprathermal particle population to the thermal plasma as the particles slow through Coulomb collisions. It represents deposited heating power, rather than the particles’ total kinetic-energy density or their total power before spatial localization.

$$
p_{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\frac{1}{dV}\frac{dE_{\mathrm{transferred}}}{dt}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermalization power density at position $\mathbf{x}$ and time $t$, $dV$ is a differential volume, and $dE_{\mathrm{transferred}}$ is the kinetic energy transferred to the thermal population during time interval $dt$. The concrete particle-channel realization [particle power density due to thermalization](name:particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization) is an instance of this general quantity.

NAMES.name: particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.short: Particle power density due to thermalization is the local volumetric rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy between fast or suprathermal particles and a specified particle population during collisional relaxation toward thermal equilibrium.
NAMES.long:
Particle power density due to thermalization is the local volumetric rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy between fast or suprathermal particles and a specified particle population as the fast particles relax toward thermal equilibrium. It is the particle-population source term associated with collisional thermalization, not a volume-integrated total power.

The local power density is the kinetic-energy moment of the thermalizing part of the collisional operator for the specified particle population:

$$
P_{p,\mathrm{therm}} = \int \frac{1}{2} m_p v^2\, C_{p,\mathrm{therm}}[f] \, d^3v
$$

where $p$ labels the specified particle population, $m_p$ is its particle mass, $v = |\mathbf{v}|$ is particle speed, $f$ denotes the relevant velocity-space distribution functions, and $C_{p,\mathrm{therm}}$ is the Coulomb-collision operator term that transfers kinetic energy through thermalization.

This parent is generic over the affected particle population. The specialization [thermal particle power density due to thermalization](name:thermal_particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization) restricts the affected population to thermal particles; [power density due to thermalization](name:power_density_due_to_thermalization) denotes the corresponding process without the particle-population qualifier. Contributions from direct wave absorption, radiation, ionization energy balance, or transport of already deposited energy are outside this quantity unless they are represented as the same Coulomb thermalization transfer.
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb thermalization increases the kinetic energy of the specified particle population.

NAMES.name: power_due_to_charge_exchange
NAMES.short: Net power transferred to or from a particle population through charge-exchange reactions, in which an ion captures an electron from a neutral atom, interconverting the charged and neutral states and redistributing energy between populations.
NAMES.long:
Charge exchange is a two-body atomic collision process in which an incident ion captures a bound electron from a neutral atom, producing a fast neutral and a new ion. The associated power quantifies the net energy gained or lost by the affected particle population as a result of this electron-transfer mechanism, integrated over the relevant velocity or energy distribution.

The charge-exchange power contribution from a species population can be expressed as:

$$
P_{\mathrm{cx}} = \int E \, n_i \, n_0 \, \langle \sigma v \rangle_{\mathrm{cx}}(E) \, dE
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $n_0$ is the neutral density, $\langle \sigma v \rangle_{\mathrm{cx}}$ is the charge-exchange reaction rate coefficient averaged over the distribution at energy $E$, and the integral spans the relevant energy domain.

In fusion plasmas, charge exchange is a significant energy-loss mechanism for the ion population: fast ions (from neutral beam injection or thermonuclear reactions) exchange charge with cold recycled edge neutrals, becoming energetic neutrals that escape confinement. This ion-channel power is documented in [ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange](name:ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange). The process is quantified using evaluated atomic charge-exchange cross-sections combined with ion and neutral distribution functions from transport modeling or inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the population gains energy through the charge-exchange interaction.

NAMES.name: ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated kinetic-energy transfer rate for a particle population caused by charge-exchange reactions, indicating net energy loss or gain by that population.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net kinetic-energy transfer associated with charge exchange, integrated over the volume occupied by the affected particle population. Charge exchange occurs when an ion captures a bound electron from a neutral particle, producing a neutral particle and a new ion.

The volume-integrated rate is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{CX}} = \int_V q_{\mathrm{CX}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{CX}}$ is the charge-exchange power, $q_{\mathrm{CX}}$ is the local volumetric kinetic-energy transfer rate, $V$ is the integration volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ is position. The quantity is the charge-exchange component of [power due to charge exchange](name:power_due_to_charge_exchange) and excludes energy transfer from other processes.

Positive values denote net kinetic-energy removal from the affected population; negative values denote net kinetic-energy gain. The [fast-ion power due to charge exchange](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange) is a specific instance for confined fast ions.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated kinetic-energy loss rate from the confined fast-ion population due to charge exchange.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated kinetic-energy loss rate from the confined fast-ion population due to charge exchange is the rate at which electron-transfer reactions with neutral particles remove kinetic energy from confined fast ions. The removed energy is not Coulomb energy transfer to plasma particles; it is a loss from the confined fast-ion energy content.

The volume integral is taken over the corresponding local loss-rate density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{CX},f} = \int_V p_{\mathrm{CX},f}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{CX},f}$ is the fast-ion power due to charge exchange, $p_{\mathrm{CX},f}(\mathbf{x})$ is the [fast-ion power density due to charge exchange], $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $V$ is the region over which the confined fast-ion population is defined. Locally, $p_{\mathrm{CX},f}$ is the charge-exchange event-rate density weighted by the kinetic energy removed from the confined fast-ion population per event, summed over all included fast-ion species and charge states.

This quantity excludes Coulomb collisional energy transfer, ionization losses not involving charge exchange, prompt orbit loss, power that was never absorbed into the fast-ion population, and charge-exchange loss assigned solely to thermal ions. It is the fast-ion component of [ion power due to charge exchange](name:ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange) and contributes to the broader [power due to charge exchange](name:power_due_to_charge_exchange); in a fast-ion energy balance written with positive gains, this loss magnitude enters as a sink.

sources.enhanced_context: Power lost from the fast ion distribution due to charge exchange reactions with neutral particles (P_CX). Represents the energy loss channel from the fast ion population via charge exchange neutralization.
sources.leaf_definition: Power loss due to Charge Exchange loss of fast ions
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities (integrated over plasma volume for moments of the distribution, collisional exchange and source terms), for various time slices

NAMES.name: power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated net power transferred to a plasma particle population through Coulomb collisions, abstracting over all source and receiving population combinations without prescribing which species serve as donor or receiver.
NAMES.long:
Coulomb collisions mediate energy exchange between plasma populations — electrons, thermal ions, fast particles, impurity ions, and neutrals — converting differential kinetic energy into thermal energy of the receiving species. This abstract parent captures the general concept of volume-integrated collisional power transfer without specifying which populations participate; every concrete child quantity carries explicit population labels to identify the donor and receiver.

The volume-integrated collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm coll}$ is the local collisional power exchange density and the integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

Concrete population-resolved instances of this quantity include [ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions), which covers the total ion population summed over all species and charge states, and ion_state_power_due_to_collisions, which resolves this to a specified ionization state. Source-resolved variants such as [fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions](name:fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions), [thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions), and [thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) additionally identify the donating population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when net energy is deposited into the specified receiving population (net collisional heating); negative when the receiving population loses energy to others (net collisional cooling).

sources.enhanced_context: Total collisional power (P_fast→e) transferred from the fast (non-Maxwellian) particle population to the bulk electron population via Coulomb collisions, integrated over the plasma volume.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power to the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: electron_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total electron population, aggregating both thermal and fast electron sub-populations without prescribing the thermal or fast character of the receiving electrons.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the complete electron population from Coulomb scattering interactions with all colliding plasma constituents. As a structural abstraction within the [power_due_to_collisions](name:power_due_to_collisions) family, it serves as the all-electron aggregate counterpart to population-resolved forms such as [thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions), which restricts the receiving population to bulk thermal electrons driven by a fast non-Maxwellian source.

The volume-integrated collisional power transferred to electrons is defined as:

$$
P_{e,\rm coll} = \int_V Q_{e,\rm coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{e,\rm coll}$ is the local Coulomb collisional power exchange density into the electron population and $V$ is the confined plasma volume.

In fusion-relevant plasmas this power balance is dominated by energy transfer from fast beam or fusion-born ions to electrons via Coulomb drag, and by thermal ion–electron temperature-equilibration collisions. The source-resolved fast-particle contribution to the full plasma electron population is captured by [fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions](name:fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions), while the local volumetric form underlying this integral is given by [thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when net energy is deposited into the electron population (collisional heating); negative when the electron population transfers net energy to other populations through Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: ion_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total ion population, aggregating both thermal and fast ion sub-populations across all ion species and charge states without prescribing the thermal or fast character of the receiving ions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the complete ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with all colliding plasma constituents. As a structural abstraction within the collisional-power family, it aggregates thermal and fast ion receiving populations across all ion species and charge states without resolving which ion sub-population receives the energy.

The volume-integrated ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm ion,coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm ion,coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm ion,coll}$ is the local [ion power density due to collisions](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) into the aggregate ion receiving population and the integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

The receiving population is charge-state-summed for each ion species and species-summed over the ion population. Collisional exchanges among ion sub-populations contained in this aggregate cancel in the all-ion sum; the retained value is the net transfer between the aggregate ion population and populations outside that aggregate, including the complementary [electron power due to collisions](name:electron_power_due_to_collisions). Population-resolved components include [fast ion power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions), [thermal ion power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions), and the charge-state-resolved [ion-state power due to collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions); [power due to collisions](name:power_due_to_collisions) is the corresponding population-abstract parent.
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net energy into the complete ion population.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total fast-ion population by background ions, summed over all fast-ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the complete fast-ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with background ions. It aggregates all fast-ion species and charge states without resolving the receiving fast-ion subpopulation.

The volume-integrated fast-ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}} = \int_V Q_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}}$ is the local collisional power-exchange density into the aggregate fast-ion population, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $dV$ is the differential volume element, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

This quantity is the fast-ion component of [ion power due to collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions). Its charge-state-resolved counterpart is [fast ion charge state power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), while [thermal ion power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) describes transfer into thermal ions. Internal exchanges among fast-ion species cancel in the summed net value.
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net energy into the complete fast-ion population.

sources.enhanced_context: Total collisional power transferred from the distribution species to the fast ion population, volume-integrated over the plasma. Quantifies fast-ion collisional heating distinct from thermalization to the bulk thermal ion population.

NAMES.name: particle_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred from the fast (non-Maxwellian) particle population to a bulk plasma population, abstracting over all possible receiving populations without prescribing the receiving species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer from the fast (non-Maxwellian) particle population to a receiving bulk plasma population through Coulomb scattering interactions. As a structural abstraction within the [power_due_to_collisions](name:power_due_to_collisions) family, it encompasses all instances in which the fast particle distribution acts as the energy donor, without specifying which bulk species receives the transferred energy.

The volume-integrated collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm fast,\,coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm fast,\,coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm fast,\,coll}$ is the local Coulomb collisional power exchange density from the fast particle population to the receiving population, and the integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

The concrete receiving-population-resolved instance is [fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions](name:fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions), which specifies the bulk electron population as the receiver. Compare with [electron_power_due_to_collisions](name:electron_power_due_to_collisions) and [ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions), which specify the receiving species while remaining agnostic to the donating population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when net energy is deposited into the receiving population by fast particles; negative when the receiving population loses energy to the fast particle population.

NAMES.name: fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred from the fast (non-Maxwellian) particle population to the bulk electron population.
NAMES.long:
Fast particles — such as neutral-beam-injected ions, minority ions accelerated by RF heating, or fusion-born alpha particles — carry a non-Maxwellian velocity distribution well above the thermal speed of the bulk plasma. As they slow down via Coulomb collisions, energy is deposited into both bulk electrons and ions; this quantity captures the total power delivered to the electron channel alone, integrated over the plasma volume.

The governing relation connects this quantity to its local density analog [fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions):

$$
P_{f \to e} = \int_V S_{f \to e}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $S_{f \to e}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local electron-channel collisional power density at position $\mathbf{r}$, and $V$ is the plasma volume. The fraction of fast-particle energy deposited into electrons versus ions is governed by the ratio of the fast particle speed to the critical slowing-down velocity $v_c$; above $v_c$, electron drag dominates.

This quantity is evaluated from kinetic calculations — Monte Carlo orbit-following or Fokker-Planck solvers — that evolve the fast particle distribution function and compute the Coulomb collision operator. In large tokamaks with multi-megawatt injection, the electron channel receives several to tens of megawatts; for fusion-born alpha particles in burning plasmas the contribution scales with the fusion power.

The power received by the thermal electron population from this exchange equals [thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions), and the corresponding ion-channel quantity is [thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when net energy flows from the fast particle population to the electron population via Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: power_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
NAMES.short: Power carried by neutral-beam particles that traverse the plasma without ionization or stopping and exit through the far plasma boundary.
NAMES.long:
The neutral-beam shine-through power is the energy carried per unit time by injected neutral particles that cross the plasma without ionization or another stopping interaction and leave through the far plasma boundary. It includes only the outgoing neutral energy that is not deposited in the plasma.

The defining outward energy-flux integral is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{st}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{far}}} \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{E,n} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the shine-through power, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{E,n}$ is the energy-flux vector carried by the exiting neutral particles, $A_{\mathrm{far}}$ is the far plasma-boundary surface, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is its outward unit normal. It is excluded from the [power absorbed by the plasma from a neutral beam injector](name:absorbed_power_of_neutral_beam_injector).

NAMES.name: radial_center_of_mass_velocity
NAMES.short: Mass-weighted mean radial flow of all contributing plasma species, obtained by projecting their barycentric velocity onto the major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial center-of-mass velocity is the major-radius component of the barycentric bulk velocity of a multicomponent plasma. It retains the mass weighting of the [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) while selecting the local cylindrical radial direction.

The component is defined by

$$
v_R^{\mathrm{cm}} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\left(\mathbf{v}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}\right)}{\rho}
$$

where $s$ indexes included species, $\rho_s$ is species mass density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is species fluid velocity, $\rho=\sum_s\rho_s$ is total mass density, $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the center-of-mass velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the radial unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Only species included in the mass sum contribute; the weighting is by mass density, not particle number. Unlike the [toroidal center-of-mass velocity](name:toroidal_center_of_mass_velocity), this quantity selects the $R$ direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the barycentric velocity points toward increasing $R$, outward from the machine symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_conductivity
NAMES.short: Diagonal radial (R-R) element of the electrical conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius. It is the local material coefficient giving the part of the conductive radial current density driven by the radial electric field; off-diagonal tensor elements may add further coupling to the toroidal and vertical fields.
NAMES.long:
Radial conductivity is the diagonal radial (R-R) element of the electrical conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, whose basis is $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, with $R$ the major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical height. It is a material response coefficient describing how strongly a radial electric field drives radial conductive current, not a signed current or field component.

The quantity is the same-direction projection of the conductivity tensor onto the radial unit vector:

$$
\sigma_R = \hat{R}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\hat{R}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the electrical conductivity tensor, $\hat{R}$ is the radial unit vector directed toward increasing $R$, and $\sigma_R$ is the radial conductivity. In the local generalized Ohm's law the full conductive radial current density is $J_R^{\mathrm{cond}} = \sigma_R E_R + \sigma_{R\phi}E_\phi + \sigma_{RZ}E_Z$; the diagonal element $\sigma_R$ supplies only the $\sigma_R E_R$ term. The relation $J_R^{\mathrm{cond}} = \sigma_R E_R$ holds exactly only when the off-diagonal couplings to $E_\phi$ and $E_Z$ vanish, where $E_R$, $E_\phi$, and $E_Z$ are the radial, toroidal, and vertical electric-field components.

In magnetized plasma the tensor is strongly anisotropic. For a symmetric field-aligned conductivity tensor the radial diagonal element is $\sigma_R = \sigma_\perp + (\sigma_\parallel - \sigma_\perp)\,b_R^2$, where $\sigma_\parallel$ and $\sigma_\perp$ are the parallel and perpendicular conductivities and $b_R$ is the dimensionless $R$ component of the magnetic-field unit vector; the antisymmetric Hall part does not contribute to this same-direction projection. This quantity is distinct from radial current density, radial electric field, and the toroidal and vertical diagonal tensor elements.

NAMES.name: radial_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
NAMES.short: Radial component of the electrical current density generated by anomalous, turbulence-driven transport, projected along the geometric R direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the anomalous current density, $j_{R,\mathrm{anom}}$, is the projection of the full [current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) vector onto the geometric radial direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It is distinguished from the [vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) by its projection direction.

The defining projection is

$$
j_{R,\mathrm{anom}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the anomalous current-density vector and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the geometric radial unit vector. This quantity includes only the anomalous-transport contribution to the radial current density and excludes contributions attributed to other mechanisms, such as parallel viscous stress represented by [radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity](name:radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the anomalous conventional current points in the $+R$ direction, toward increasing major radius, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: Radial projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current-density contribution onto the major-radius direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed major-radius projection of the pressure-gradient-driven current described by [current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It includes the radial projection of the perpendicular diamagnetic drive and any field-aligned closure contribution included in the parent vector.

The projection is defined by

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},R}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}\mathbin{\cdot}\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},R}$ is the radial current-density component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the parent diamagnetic current-density vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the outward major-radius unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It is a signed component rather than the magnitude of the diamagnetic current density; the corresponding toroidal projection is [toroidal current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current-density vector points toward increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short: Radial component of the heat-viscosity-driven current density, projected onto the major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the contribution to the plasma current density arising from heat-viscosity terms in fluid transport theory.
NAMES.long:
Radial current density due to heat viscosity is the major-radius component of the current-density contribution generated by heat-viscosity terms in plasma fluid transport theory. The heat-viscosity contribution is the current density associated with the heat-viscosity part of the stress closure in the fluid-moment equations; this quantity is its projection onto the radial direction.

The radial component is obtained by projecting the heat-viscosity current-density contribution onto the major-radius unit vector:

$$
j_{R,\mathrm{hv}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $j_{R,\mathrm{hv}}$ is the radial current density due to heat viscosity, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density contribution](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is evaluated in transport or fluid-moment modeling from the chosen heat-viscosity closure and the local plasma state, then projected along $\hat{R}$. It is not measured directly; estimates are inferred by combining equilibrium geometry with density, temperature, flow, and current-balance information. It is the radial counterpart of the [parallel](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), [toroidal](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and vertical components of the same heat-viscosity current density.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the heat-viscosity current-density contribution points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia
NAMES.short: Radial component of the electric current density arising from ion-fluid inertial acceleration, projected along increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial projection of the current density due to ion inertia is the electric-current component generated by inertial acceleration terms in the ion-fluid momentum equation. It includes the radial part of the polarization-type current associated with finite ion mass and acceleration.

The radial component is defined by

$$
J_{R,\rm inertia} = \mathbf{J}_{\rm inertia} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\rm inertia}$ is the current density due to ion inertia, $\hat{R}$ is the outward major-radius unit vector, and $J_{R,\rm inertia}$ is the resulting radial component. The underlying current is described by [current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:current_density_due_to_ion_inertia).

This quantity is distinct from the field-aligned [parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia) and the vertical [vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia) components; it is a cylindrical projection, not the component normal to a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion-inertia current points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
