NAMES.name: radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short: Radial component of the electric current density produced by frictional momentum exchange between plasma ions and background neutral particles in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial current density due to ion-neutral friction is the radial projection of [current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), produced by collisional momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral atoms or molecules. It is a signed component along the major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The component is defined by projecting the ion-neutral-friction current-density vector onto the radial unit vector:

$$
j_{R,\mathrm{in}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $j_{R,\mathrm{in}}$ is the radial current-density component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the current-density vector contribution due to ion-neutral friction, and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing $R$.

This quantity is not the ion-neutral friction force density and does not include current-density contributions attributed to ion inertia, pressure-gradient forces, electromagnetic forces, or other collisional mechanisms. It is the same-frame radial counterpart of the [vertical current-density component](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) and is distinct from projections along toroidal, poloidal, field-aligned, or diamagnetic directions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current-density contribution due to ion-neutral friction points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
NAMES.short: Radial component of the electric-current contribution generated by the divergence of perpendicular viscous stress in a magnetized charged plasma.
NAMES.long:
The radial current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the radial projection of the electric-current contribution generated by the divergence of the perpendicular viscous stress tensor. It represents the component along the major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; “perpendicular” identifies the stress mechanism, not the projection direction. It is the radial component of [current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).

The radial component is defined by

$$
J_{R,\perp,\nu}=\hat{R}\cdot\mathbf{J}_{\perp,\nu}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\perp,\nu}$ is the perpendicular-viscosity current-density vector and $\hat{R}$ is the outward radial unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. This quantity is distinct from [radial current density due to viscosity](name:radial_current_density_due_to_viscosity), which includes viscosity mechanisms beyond perpendicular viscosity, and from the toroidal projection [toroidal current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $J_R$ points toward increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame of the effective convective velocity transporting neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective particle-number advection velocity of neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state, projected onto the cylindrical radial direction. The corresponding full vector is [effective neutral internal-state velocity due to convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection).

The radial component is defined by

$$
v_R^{\mathrm{eff}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{eff}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the distribution-function-weighted effective convective velocity and $\hat{R}$ is the outward radial unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This particle-transport velocity is distinct from the [radial effective neutral internal-state momentum velocity due to convection](name:radial_effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection), which characterizes momentum transport.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the velocity component points toward increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_electric_field
NAMES.short: Radial component of the electric field giving the force per unit positive stationary test charge toward increasing major radius.
NAMES.long:
The radial electric field is the component of the [electric field](name:electric_field) vector that gives the force per unit positive stationary test charge along the direction of increasing major radius. It includes electrostatic, inductive, and electromagnetic-wave contributions, like the [vertical electric field](name:vertical_electric_field).

The radial component is defined by

$$
E_R = \mathbf{E} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $E_R$ is the radial electric-field component, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. The projection uses the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is increasing toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Radial means the cylindrical $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ direction and is not synonymous with the normal to a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $E_R$ points toward increasing major radius $R$.

sources.parent_definition: Transport coefficient profiles for various time slices. The transport of particles, energy and momentum is described by diffusion coefficients, D, and convection velocities, v. In 1D (radial) equations, these are defined by the total fluxes of particles, energy and momentum, across a flux surface given by : V' [-D Y' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|^2> + v Y <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>], where Y represents the particles, energy and momentum density, respectively, while V is the volume inside a flux surface, the primes denote derivatives with respect to rho_tor_norm and < X > is the flux surface average of a quantity X. This formulation remains valid when changing simultaneously rho_tor_norm into rho_tor in the gradient terms and in the derivatives denoted by the prime. The average flux stored in the IDS as sibling of D and v is the total flux described above divided by the flux surface area V' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>. Note that the energy flux includes the energy transported by the particle flux, in this form: Q =  V' [- n D (T)' <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|^2> + v (nT) <|grad(rho_tor_norm)|>] + flux_multiplier * T * particle_flux. Fluxes and convection are positive (resp. negative) when outwards i.e. towards the LCFS (resp. inwards i.e.  towards the magnetic axes).

NAMES.name: radial_electron_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Radial component of the electron particle diffusion coefficient. It is the radial-radial diagonal tensor component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height, relating diffusive electron particle flux to the electron density gradient along R.
NAMES.long:
The radial electron diffusion coefficient is the electron particle diffusivity acting along the cylindrical radial direction $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the radial-radial diagonal tensor component of [electron_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_diffusion_coefficient) for Fickian electron particle transport.

In the Fick-law formulation, the contribution of this coefficient to the diffusive radial electron particle flux density satisfies:

$$
\Gamma_{e,R}^{\rm diff} = -D_{e,RR}\,\frac{\partial n_e}{\partial R}
$$

where $D_{e,RR}$ is the radial electron diffusion coefficient, $\Gamma_{e,R}^{\rm diff}$ is the $\hat{R}$ component of the diffusive electron particle flux density, and $n_e$ is the electron number density. The minus sign gives down-gradient diffusion for a positive coefficient.

This is specifically a particle transport quantity, distinct from electron energy transport, which is captured by [radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It denotes the cylindrical radial component; the [poloidal_electron_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_electron_diffusion_coefficient) denotes the component tangent to increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ on a magnetic flux surface in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. A flux-surface-normal diffusivity tied to increasing flux label $\rho$ is a separate geometric projection and is not represented by the cylindrical radial component in general.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Radial electron energy flux is the net electron thermal-energy transport per unit area projected along increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial electron energy flux is the directed flux of electron thermal energy and enthalpy per unit area along the increasing-major-radius direction. It is the radial projection of the net [electron energy flux](name:electron_energy_flux), including conductive and convective contributions.

The radial component is defined by

$$
q_{e,R} = \mathbf{q}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_e$ is the net electron energy flux density, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius, and $q_{e,R}$ is its radial component.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this quantity uses the geometric radial direction and is distinct from the flux-surface-normal [radial total thermal electron energy flux](name:radial_total_thermal_electron_energy_flux). The complementary [poloidal electron energy flux](name:poloidal_electron_energy_flux) resolves the same electron energy-flux vector along the poloidal direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron energy flux points toward increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Net number of electrons crossing a unit area oriented perpendicular to the radial direction per unit time, combining diffusive and convective cross-field transport contributions in the electron density continuity equation.
NAMES.long:
The radial electron particle flux $\Gamma_{e,r}$ is the projection of the electron particle-flux density vector onto the radial direction, quantifying the net cross-field electron transport per unit area per unit time. It combines contributions from collisional diffusion, bulk convective flow, and turbulent fluctuations, and enters directly into the electron continuity equation governing the evolution of the electron density profile.

In 1D transport modeling, the flux is commonly decomposed into diffusive and convective components:

$$
\Gamma_{e,r} = -D_e \frac{\partial n_e}{\partial r} + V_e n_e
$$

where $D_e$ is the radial electron particle diffusion coefficient, $V_e$ is the effective convection velocity (see [radial_electron_convection_velocity](name:radial_electron_convection_velocity)), and $n_e$ is the local electron number density.

This quantity is computed by transport models incorporating measured electron density profiles together with reconstructed or modeled diffusion and convection coefficients. The radial integral of $\Gamma_{e,r}$ must close the global particle balance, including ionization sources and wall recycling. The analogous quantity for individual ion charge states is given by [radial_ion_state_particle_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when electrons flow radially outward, away from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Projection of the electron fluid bulk flow velocity onto the major-radius direction, giving the net electron flow toward or away from the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial electron velocity $v_{e,R}$ is the component of the electron bulk fluid velocity resolved along the major-radius direction $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is measured from the machine symmetry axis. It governs cross-field electron mass transport in the poloidal plane and enters the electron continuity equation through the divergence of the radial particle flux $n_e v_{e,R}$. It is one component of the parent vector [electron_velocity](name:electron_velocity).

The quantity is defined as the first velocity-space moment of the electron distribution function $f_e$ projected onto $\hat{R}$:

$$
v_{e,R} = \frac{1}{n_e} \int v_R \, f_e(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the local electron number density and $v_R$ is the $\hat{R}$-component of a particle velocity $\mathbf{v}$.

Radial electron flow is generally much smaller in magnitude than [parallel_electron_velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity) but is significant for cross-field particle transport, particularly in the edge and scrape-off layer. It is most often inferred from transport analysis using measured density profiles and particle source rates, or derived from fluid simulations. The sibling components [poloidal_electron_velocity](name:poloidal_electron_velocity) and [toroidal_electron_velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity) complete the cylindrical decomposition; the ion analog is [radial_ion_velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron fluid flows in the direction of increasing major radius $R$, i.e., radially outward from the machine symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: radial_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.short: Effective radial advection coefficient for non-diffusive thermal-energy transport, entering the radial convective energy flux independently of the bulk plasma flow speed.
NAMES.long:
The radial energy convection velocity is the effective advection coefficient that parameterizes the radial component of convective thermal-energy transport. It is the radial projection of the more general [energy convection velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity), and it is distinct from the bulk plasma fluid velocity.

The radial convective energy flux for a species is defined by:

$$
Q_{\mathrm{conv},R} = \tfrac{3}{2}\,nT V_{E,R}
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{conv},R}$ is the radial convective energy flux in W m$^{-2}$, $n$ is particle number density in m$^{-3}$, $T$ is temperature expressed as energy in J, and $V_{E,R}$ is the radial energy convection velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The coefficient includes effective drift and pinch contributions and is not a direct fluid-flow measurement. The species-resolved [radial ion energy convection velocity](name:radial_ion_energy_convection_velocity) applies the same radial projection specifically to ion energy transport.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $V_{E,R}$ points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short: Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle-state radial momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction unchanged. Radial denotes the R component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive closures for a neutral-particle state can produce radial momentum-flux densities that exceed the physically realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient regions. A radial flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_R$ bounds the radial component of the neutral-particle-state momentum-flux density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; it caps the permitted magnitude relative to a free-streaming reference while leaving the component sign set by the underlying closure.

The direction-preserving limited radial momentum-flux density can be expressed as:

$$
\Pi_R^{\mathrm{lim}} = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(\Pi_R^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|\Pi_R^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, \alpha_R \Pi_R^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $\Pi_R^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited radial momentum-flux-density component, $\Pi_R^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the unconstrained closure value for the same component, $\Pi_R^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming upper-bound magnitude, and $\alpha_R$ is the radial flux-limiter coefficient. The coefficient itself is a nonnegative scale factor, so directional information resides in $\operatorname{sgn}(\Pi_R^{\mathrm{cl}})$ rather than in $\alpha_R$; values below one impose a stricter cap.

This quantity specializes the [flux-limiter coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient) for the radial neutral-particle-state momentum-flux channel. The [poloidal flux-limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient) and [toroidal flux-limiter coefficient](name:toroidal_flux_limiter_coefficient) are the corresponding resolved-component peers, and the [momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) denotes the transported-quantity-specific parent without selecting the radial component.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial effective Fickian coefficient for particle transport by ions in a specified charge state, relating the diffusive flux in the cylindrical R direction to that charge state’s density gradient in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient is the effective Fickian transport coefficient for one specified ionic charge state, relating its diffusive particle flux in the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ direction to the corresponding number-density gradient in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The radial diffusive particle flux component is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,q,R}\frac{\partial n_{i,q}}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the $\hat{R}$ component of the diffusive particle flux of ion charge state $q$, $D_{i,q,R}$ is this diffusion coefficient, $n_{i,q}$ is the number density of that charge state, and $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Here radial means the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ component, with $R$ the major radius, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical height; it is not a flux-surface-normal projection and not a derivative with respect to a flux coordinate such as $\rho$. The [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) is the direction-unspecified counterpart, and the [poloidal ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) is the corresponding poloidal directional form. The charge-state-specific scope distinguishes this quantity from the [radial electron diffusion coefficient](name:radial_electron_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial component of the effective convection velocity governing non-diffusive transport of the momentum density of an ion species in a specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion charge-state momentum convection velocity is the radial component of the effective velocity that governs non-diffusive transport of momentum density for one ion species and charge state.

It is the $R$-component of the effective velocity vector $\mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ in the charge-state-resolved fluid momentum transport equation:

$$
v_{c,R}^{(s)} = \hat{R} \cdot \mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}
$$

where $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ is the effective momentum convection velocity for charge state $s$.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and is distinct from [radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), which is the transported momentum flux rather than its convection-velocity coefficient. It is the radial component of the [ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) family and is not generally equal to the mean radial fluid velocity of the charge state. Here radial denotes the cylindrical $R$ component, not a flux-surface-normal projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_{c,R}^{(s)}$ points toward increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical dissipation of the radial fluid-momentum component for a specified ion charge state, along increasing major radius R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion charge-state momentum damping rate is the inverse relaxation time $\gamma_{R,s}$ governing the decay of the radial component of ordered fluid momentum density for a specified ion charge state, driven by Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. The radial component is the projection along $\hat{R}$, the direction of increasing major radius $R$, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The defining relation for the radial fluid momentum-density component $p_{R,s}$ of ion charge state $s$ subject to damping is:

$$
\frac{\partial p_{R,s}}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\gamma_{R,s} p_{R,s}
$$

where $\gamma_{R,s}$ is the radial ion charge-state momentum damping rate and $p_{R,s}$ is the radial component of directed fluid momentum density of the specified charge state. The magnitude of $\gamma_{R,s}$ is set by Coulomb collisionality, the charge-state mass and effective charge number, and the local magnetic geometry through neoclassical friction-force coefficients.

This quantity resolves the vector [ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) for the cylindrical radial projection of an individual ion charge state. It differs from [radial ion momentum damping rate](name:radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate), which represents the charge-state-aggregated ion population, and from the sibling scalar projections [poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate), [toroidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate), and [parallel ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate). The radial projection is the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ component, not a flux-surface-normal projection.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the kinematic coefficient for down-gradient cross-flux-surface transport of radial momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the scalar kinematic transport coefficient governing diffusive cross-flux-surface transport of radial momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state. It describes directional redistribution of that charge state's radial momentum.

For radial transport in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the diffusive momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{m,R}^{(q)} = -D_{m,R}^{(q)} \frac{\partial\left(\rho_q u_R^{(q)}\right)}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,R}^{(q)}$ is the radial diffusive momentum flux, $D_{m,R}^{(q)}$ is the radial momentum diffusivity, $\rho_q$ is the mass density of the specified ion charge state, $u_R^{(q)}$ is its radial flow-velocity component, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate. This radial coefficient is a directional member of [ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), distinct from the field-aligned [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) and from the transported flux represented by [radial ion charge-state momentum flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux).

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial ion charge-state momentum flux is the flux-surface-normal transport rate per unit area of radial linear momentum carried by ions in one specified ionization state.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion charge-state momentum flux is the flux-surface-normal transport rate per unit area of the radial linear-momentum component carried by ions in one specified ionization state. It is the radial projection of the [ion charge-state momentum flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), including convective, pressure, and viscous contributions.

$$
\Pi_{z,\psi R}=\hat{\mathbf n}_{\psi}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}_z\cdot\hat{\mathbf R}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_z$ is the momentum-flux tensor for charge state $z$, $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\psi}$ is the outward unit normal to a magnetic flux surface, and $\hat{\mathbf R}$ is the radial unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Unlike [poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), this quantity selects momentum directed along increasing major radius.
NAMES.sign: Positive when radial momentum in the $+\hat{\mathbf R}$ direction is transported outward along $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\psi}$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial ion charge-state particle flux is the directed number flow of ions in a specified ionization charge state across magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion charge-state particle flux is the component of the ion particle-flux vector for a specified ionization charge state normal to magnetic flux surfaces. It resolves that charge state independently rather than aggregating over all ionization stages.

The radial projection is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{z,r}=\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}_r=n_z\,\mathbf v_z\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}_r
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_z$ is the particle-flux vector for charge state $z$, $n_z$ is its number density, $\mathbf v_z$ is its mean velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf n}_r$ is the outward unit normal to the magnetic flux surface. The vector quantity is defined by [ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux); unlike [radial_ion_particle_flux](name:radial_ion_particle_flux), this quantity is not summed over ionization charge states.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ions cross the magnetic flux surface outward, away from the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial component of the mean bulk flow velocity of ions in a specified ionization charge state, resolved per charge state rather than averaged across charge states.
NAMES.long:
Radial component of the mean bulk flow velocity of ions in a specified ionization charge state, obtained by projecting that charge state's velocity moment onto the major-radius direction.

$$
v_{R,z} = \frac{1}{n_z}\int v_R f_z(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{V}_z \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

Here, $z$ identifies the ionization charge state, $f_z(\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity distribution, $n_z$ is its local number density, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v_R$ is its cylindrical radial component, and $\mathbf{V}_z$ is the corresponding bulk velocity vector. The vector parent is [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), while [poloidal ion charge-state velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity) provides the poloidal projection.

This quantity remains resolved for the specified charge state and therefore differs from the charge-state-averaged [radial ion velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion charge-state flow has a component toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial (major-radius) component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the diamagnetic drift velocity of a specified ion charge state, driven by that state's partial pressure gradient crossed with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the diamagnetic drift velocity for a specified ion charge state is its projection onto the major-radius direction $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.

The full diamagnetic drift velocity for ion charge state $s$ is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} = -\frac{\nabla p_s \times \mathbf{B}}{q_s n_s B^2}
$$

where $p_s$ is the partial pressure of charge state $s$, $q_s = Z_s e$ is its electric charge, $n_s$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field. The radial component is $v_{\mathrm{dia},s,R} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} \cdot \hat{R}$.

This component is one projection of [ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift); complementary cylindrical-frame projections are [toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the radial diamagnetic drift points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective Fickian diffusivity for total-ion particle transport, relating the radial diffusive flux across magnetic surfaces to the opposing radial gradient of charge-state-summed ion density.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion diffusion coefficient is the effective particle diffusivity for total ions moving radially across nested magnetic flux surfaces. It parameterizes Fickian radial mixing of charge-state-summed ion density.

For radial transport, the defining relation is

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(r)} = -D_i^{\mathrm{eff},(r)}\nabla_r n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(r)}$ is the radial diffusive particle-flux component, $D_i^{\mathrm{eff},(r)}$ is the radial effective diffusivity, $\nabla_r n_i$ is the radial gradient of total ion number density, and $n_i$ is the ion density summed over all ionic charge states. The minus sign specifies transport down the density gradient.

This is the radial member of the general [ion diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient) family. Neutral particles and charge-state-resolved coefficients, such as the [radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient), are excluded.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical dissipation of the radial component of bulk ion fluid momentum along increasing major radius R.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation timescale at which the radial component of ordered bulk ion fluid momentum is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. It describes damping along the cylindrical radial direction, distinct from field-aligned, poloidal, and toroidal momentum damping.

In the ion fluid momentum balance, its component-wise damping contribution is defined by

$$
\left.\frac{\partial p_{i,R}}{\partial t}\right|_{\rm damp}=-\nu_{D,R}^{\,i}p_{i,R}
$$

where $p_{i,R}$ is the radial component of bulk ion momentum density, and $\nu_{D,R}^{\,i}$ is the radial damping rate. The radial projection is taken along $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with positive direction toward increasing major radius $R$. The rate aggregates the relevant bulk-ion contributions over ion species and charge states. It is a component of [ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate) and complements [parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the rate coefficient reduces the magnitude of the radial ion momentum component, producing exponential relaxation toward zero.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_flux_over_edge_region
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Radial ion momentum flux over the edge region is the total flux of ion radial linear momentum across edge magnetic-flux surfaces, summed over all ion species and charge states. Its positive direction is toward increasing edge radial flux coordinate ρ, outward from the confined plasma.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion momentum flux over the edge region is the radial-radial component of the total ion momentum-flux tensor for ions in the edge plasma. It gives the flux of ion radial linear momentum through surfaces of constant edge radial flux coordinate $\rho$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. The edge region is the outer plasma adjacent to the last closed flux surface, including the pedestal, separatrix vicinity, and scrape-off layer.

The scalar component is defined by projecting the total ion momentum-flux tensor onto the outward normal to the constant-$\rho$ surface:

$$
\Pi_{i,\rho\rho}^{\mathrm{edge}} = \hat{\mathbf n}_\rho \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_i^{\mathrm{edge}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}_\rho
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_i^{\mathrm{edge}}$ is the total ion momentum-flux tensor over the edge region, $\hat{\mathbf n}_\rho$ is the normal vector of magnitude one pointing toward increasing $\rho$, and $\Pi_{i,\rho\rho}^{\mathrm{edge}}$ is the resulting radial-radial scalar component.

The ion population is summed over all ion species and charge states; [radial ion charge-state momentum flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) denotes the corresponding charge-state-resolved quantity. This quantity is distinct from [radial ion particle flux](name:radial_ion_particle_flux), which transports particle number, and from [effective radial ion momentum convection velocity over the edge region], which parameterizes a transport closure rather than the momentum-flux tensor itself.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ion radial linear momentum is transported through surfaces of constant $\rho$ in the direction of increasing edge radial flux coordinate $\rho$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Radial ion momentum source is the net force-per-area source for the total ion population, summed over all ion charge states and projected onto increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion momentum source is the net source that adds or removes momentum from the total ion population through its radial component. Its value is summed over all ion charge states and represents force per unit area, not a volumetric force density.

The radial component is defined by:

$$
S_R = \mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $S_R$ is the radial ion momentum source, $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the net [ion momentum source](name:ion_momentum_source) vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the radial unit vector. The right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame uses $R$ for major radius, $\phi$ for toroidal angle, and $Z$ for vertical height.

The radial direction is the cylindrical major-radius direction, not the normal to a magnetic flux surface. Thus this quantity is the $R$ projection, whereas [toroidal ion momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_source) is the $\phi$ projection of the same total-ion source.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net momentum source points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Radial ion particle flux is the signed component of the net ion particle-flux density along the unit normal to magnetic flux surfaces toward increasing flux coordinate ρ in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ). It gives the number of ions crossing the surface per unit area per unit time and is summed over all ion charge states of the species.
NAMES.long:
Radial ion particle flux is the signed component of the net ion particle-flux density along the unit normal to magnetic flux surfaces toward increasing flux coordinate $\rho$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. It represents particle transport across magnetic flux surfaces and is summed over all ion charge states of a given species.

The flux-surface-normal component is defined by projecting the ion particle-flux vector onto the unit normal in the direction of increasing $\rho$:

$$
\Gamma_{\rho,i} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_\rho
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is the ion particle-flux vector summed over all charge states of the species, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\rho = \nabla\rho/|\nabla\rho|$ is the unit normal to surfaces of constant $\rho$, and $\rho$ labels nested magnetic flux surfaces and increases from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

This quantity is the flux-surface-normal component of [ion_particle_flux](name:ion_particle_flux) for one ion species. It is the charge-state-summed counterpart of [radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), distinct from [parallel_ion_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_particle_flux) along the magnetic-field direction and [poloidal_ion_particle_flux](name:poloidal_ion_particle_flux) tangent to increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ions cross magnetic flux surfaces toward increasing flux coordinate $\rho$, from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short: Cylindrical-radial component of the energy-flux density carried by ions in one resolved charge state, signed according to increasing major radius.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the radial projection of the energy-flux density associated with one specified ion charge state. It retains the net signed energy transport of that state and is the radial component of [ion state energy flux](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux).

$$
\mathcal{F}_{i,q,R}=\boldsymbol{\mathcal{F}}_{i,q}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{F}}_{i,q}$ is the energy-flux-density vector for ion species $i$ in charge state $q$, $\mathcal{F}_{i,q,R}$ is its radial component in W m$^{-2}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector of increasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The quantity is resolved by charge state and is not summed over other ionization states. For a noncircular magnetic flux surface, this cylindrical-radial projection is distinct from a flux-surface-normal projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the associated energy-flux vector has a component in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Charge-state-averaged radial component of the ion bulk-flow velocity, obtained from the density-weighted first velocity moment and directed along the outward major-radius direction.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion velocity represents the radial component of the charge-state-averaged ion bulk flow in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$. It is a geometric component of the full [ion bulk velocity](name:ion_velocity).

The charge-state average is defined by

$$
\mathbf{V}_i = \frac{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}\mathbf{V}_{i,Z}}{\sum_Z n_{i,Z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_i$ is the charge-state-averaged ion velocity, $n_{i,Z}$ is the number density of charge state $Z$ in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf{V}_{i,Z}$ is its bulk velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The radial component is $V_{i,R}=\mathbf{V}_i\cdot\hat{R}$, with $\hat{R}$ directed toward increasing major radius. This quantity includes all included ionization charge states, unlike [radial ion charge-state velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity), which selects one state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion flow component points toward increasing major radius, along $+\hat{R}$.

NAMES.name: radial_magnetic_vector_potential
NAMES.short: R-component of the magnetic vector potential in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where the full potential satisfies the curl relation giving the magnetic induction.
NAMES.long:
The radial component $A_R$ is the projection of the [magnetic_vector_potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential) $\mathbf{A}$ onto the radial direction $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is the vertical height. Like all components of $\mathbf{A}$, this quantity is gage dependent; only the curl of the full vector potential yields a directly physical observable.

The defining projection is:

$$
A_R = \mathbf{A} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\hat{R}$ is the outward radial unit vector. Together with the [vertical_magnetic_vector_potential](name:vertical_magnetic_vector_potential) $A_Z$ and the toroidal component $A_\phi$, it determines the magnetic induction via $\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}$ throughout the domain.

In vacuum regions, $A_R$ is generated solely by external coil currents; the corresponding vacuum-only quantity is [radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential](name:radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential). In plasma-bearing regions, plasma and induced eddy currents add to the coil contribution, making $A_R$ a component of the total field. The radial component is particularly relevant for equilibrium and free-boundary calculations in the poloidal $(R, Z)$ plane, as well as for electromagnetic analysis in wall-adjacent and material-boundary regions where the complete vector potential must be resolved.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $A_R$ points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short: Radial Fick's-law transport coefficient relating the diffusive momentum flux across neighboring magnetic flux surfaces to the negative momentum-density gradient along the outward flux-surface normal.
NAMES.long:
Radial momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the diffusive radial momentum flux and the negative local gradient of momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for the fluid momentum balance. It represents the cross-flux-surface specialization of [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity) and abstracts over the selected plasma species, neutral population, charge state, or momentum component to which the momentum density belongs.

The diffusive radial momentum-flux density is

$$
\Gamma_{m,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{m,r}\frac{\partial p_m}{\partial \ell_r}
$$

where $D_{m,r}$ is the radial momentum diffusivity, $\Gamma_{m,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive momentum-flux density positive outward across magnetic flux surfaces, $p_m$ is the relevant local momentum density, and $\ell_r$ is physical distance measured along the outward flux-surface normal from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary. The minus sign gives down-gradient diffusive transport for positive $D_{m,r}$.

This quantity describes only the diffusive part of radial momentum transport. It excludes convective momentum advection, explicit momentum sources and sinks, and nondiffusive pinch terms unless those effects are deliberately represented as part of an effective Fickian diffusivity; species- and population-resolved relatives include [radial ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), [ion momentum diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity), and [radial neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Fickian diffusivity governing aggregate neutral-particle transport along the cylindrical radial direction, relating radial flux to the neutral number-density gradient.
NAMES.long:
The radial neutral diffusion coefficient is the Fickian diffusivity for the aggregate neutral population, with neutral internal states combined into one particle population. It is the radial component of the directional quantity defined by [neutral_diffusion_coefficient](name:neutral_diffusion_coefficient).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the radial neutral particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,R} = -D_{n,R}\frac{\partial n_n}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,R}$ is the neutral particle flux in the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ direction, $D_{n,R}$ is the radial neutral diffusion coefficient, $n_n$ is the aggregate neutral number density, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate. The coefficient applies to particle transport, not to the separate diffusion of neutral momentum or thermal energy. For passive Fickian diffusion, $D_{n,R}$ is non-negative.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial neutral energy flux is the signed energy-flux density carried by neutral atoms and molecules along the major-radius direction, summed over neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Radial neutral energy flux is the scalar projection of the energy-flux-density vector carried by neutral atoms and molecules onto the cylindrical radial direction in the right-handed $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It represents neutral energy transport along increasing or decreasing major radius, summed over neutral species and internal states.

For radial unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$, the radial flux $F_{E,\mathrm{n},R}$ is defined by

$$
F_{E,\mathrm{n},R} = \mathbf{q}_{E,\mathrm{n}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,\mathrm{n}}$ is the neutral energy-flux-density vector and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

This is the radial specialization of [neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux). Unlike [radial neutral particle flux](name:radial_neutral_particle_flux), it weights neutral transport by the energy carried rather than counting transported particles.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral energy-flux-density vector has a component in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective radial particle diffusivity for neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal state, relating radial diffusive flux to that state’s number-density gradient.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the neutral internal-state diffusion coefficient governs Fickian particle transport of neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal state along the radial direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The radial diffusive flux is defined by

$$
J_R = -D_R \frac{\partial n_s}{\partial R}
$$

where $J_R$ is the radial particle flux, $D_R$ is this radial diffusion coefficient, $n_s$ is the number density of the specified neutral internal state, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate.

This direction-specific quantity is a radial component of [neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient]; its poloidal counterpart is [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient). It applies to the selected internal state rather than an aggregate over all neutral states, as in [radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density of a specified neutral internal state, directed along increasing major radius R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density of a specified neutral internal state is the component of the effective convection velocity along increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is a directional realization of the [neutral internal-state energy convection velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity).

The radial convective energy-flux component is defined by

$$
q_{E,\nu,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = u_{E,\nu,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} w_{E,\nu}
$$

where $q_{E,\nu,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective energy-flux component, $u_{E,\nu,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this radial effective convection velocity, $w_{E,\nu}$ is the energy density of the specified neutral internal state, and $\nu$ identifies that state.

The quantity applies to one specified neutral internal state and does not sum over all neutral states. By contrast, [neutral species energy convection velocity](name:neutral_species_energy_convection_velocity) represents the corresponding energy transport aggregated over a neutral species; [poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity) and [parallel](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity) members resolve the same state-specific coefficient in different directions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective velocity points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, making the radial convective energy flux positive in that direction.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Fick's-law radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient multiplying the R-direction temperature gradient, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of neutral particles in a specified internal state in diffusive thermal-energy transport. It is internal-state-resolved and represents only the Fickian radial contribution.
NAMES.long:
Fick's-law radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar radial diffusivity for energy transport by neutral particles in a specified internal state, and is the radial component form of the [neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). Here radial denotes projection along $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is resolved for one internal state, not summed or averaged over internal states.

The radial Fickian contribution is defined by

$$
q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,R} = - n_{n,s} D_{E,n,s,R} \frac{\partial T_{n,s}}{\partial R}
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,R}$ is the radial component of the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, $n_{n,s}$ is their number density, $D_{E,n,s,R}$ is this coefficient, and $T_{n,s}$ is their temperature.

The coefficient includes only the Fickian term driven by $\partial T_{n,s}/\partial R$ and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, and effective coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. It specializes the [internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) to neutral particles and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [neutral energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient); it is distinct from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a negative radial temperature derivative produces a diffusive thermal-energy flux in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial component of the effective advective velocity transporting momentum for a single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma fluid transport, distinct from bulk particle flow.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the [neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection) is the effective advective velocity for radial momentum transport of a single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma fluid transport.

Its momentum-flux interpretation is given by

$$
u_{r,m}^{\mathrm{mom}} = \frac{\Pi_{rr,m}^{\mathrm{conv}}}{P_{r,m}}
$$

where $u_{r,m}^{\mathrm{mom}}$ is the radial effective convection velocity, $\Pi_{rr,m}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of radial momentum, and $P_{r,m}$ is the radial momentum density for internal state $m$.

The quantity applies to one resolved neutral internal state and is not summed over states. It is an effective momentum-transport velocity and need not equal the [radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity), which describes bulk particle flow; the analogous ion quantity is [radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective convection velocity points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial component of the momentum diffusion coefficient for neutral particles in a resolved neutral-state channel. It governs Fickian redistribution of that state's momentum along the radial direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial component of the momentum diffusion coefficient for neutral particles in a resolved neutral-state channel. It is the effective kinematic coefficient governing Fickian redistribution of momentum carried by neutrals along the radial direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the radial diagonal closure, the defining Fick law is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha R} = -D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha R}\,\frac{\partial \mathbf{M}_{\alpha}}{\partial R}
$$

where $\alpha$ denotes the specified neutral internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha R}$ is the vector diffusive flux of momentum through surfaces normal to $\hat{R}$, $D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha R}$ is the radial neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient, and $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$ is the momentum density carried by neutrals in state $\alpha$. The minus sign gives down-gradient transport of each component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$ with respect to increasing $R$.

This coefficient is a diagonal radial transport coefficient: it couples the gradient along $R$ to the momentum flux through surfaces normal to $\hat{R}$, and off-diagonal tensor terms coupling other gradient directions to radial flux are outside this standard name. The radial qualifier selects the flux and gradient direction, not a component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$; the transported quantity remains the full momentum vector of the state-resolved neutral population. As a diagonal diffusion coefficient in this Fickian closure it is non-negative; the sign of the radial diffusive flux is determined by the gradient and by the explicit minus sign in the defining law.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the signed transport rate of radial linear momentum carried by neutral particles in one specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
The radial neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the radial transport component of linear momentum carried by neutral particles restricted to one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It is a momentum-flux tensor component, not a particle flux or a local momentum source.

For the state-resolved neutral distribution, the radial component is defined by

$$
\Pi_{RR}^{(s)} = \hat{R} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{R} = \int m_s v_R^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is its momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{R}$ is the radial unit vector, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $v_R$ is the cylindrical-radial velocity component, and $f_s$ is the state-resolved velocity distribution.

The radial direction is the $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. This component is the radial member of the parent [neutral internal-state momentum flux] and differs from the field-parallel [parallel neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when radial linear momentum is transported in the direction of increasing $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Major-radius component of the net momentum source for neutral particles occupying one specified internal quantum state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed major-radius component of the net momentum source for neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state. It is the radial projection of the vector quantity [neutral internal state momentum source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source).

$$
S_{m,\sigma,R}=\mathbf{S}_{m,\sigma}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $S_{m,\sigma,R}$ is the radial momentum-source component, $\mathbf{S}_{m,\sigma}$ is the momentum source for internal state $\sigma$, $\sigma$ identifies the resolved neutral internal state, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector in the increasing-$R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The quantity is resolved for one neutral internal state rather than summed over states as in the broader [radial momentum source](name:radial_momentum_source).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the momentum source points in the increasing-$R$ direction.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial component of the particle flux for neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal state, giving the net number crossing a magnetic flux surface per unit area per unit time.
NAMES.long:
The radial component selects the $\hat{\rho}$ projection of the [neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) vector $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{(s)}$, giving the signed number of neutrals in internal state $s$ crossing surfaces of constant minor radius per unit area per unit time:

$$
\Gamma^{(s)}_\rho = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{\rho}
$$

where $\hat{\rho}$ is the outward-pointing unit normal to the magnetic flux surface and $s$ labels the internal quantum state (electronic, vibrational, or rotational level) of the neutral species.

Summing $\Gamma^{(s)}_\rho$ over all internal states $s$ recovers the [radial_neutral_particle_flux](name:radial_neutral_particle_flux). State resolution enables coupling to state-selective atomic and molecular processes such as charge exchange and dissociation in the edge and scrape-off layer.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutrals in state $s$ flow in the direction of increasing minor radius, away from the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial component of the bulk fluid velocity for neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or energy state.
NAMES.long:
The radial velocity $v_R$ of a neutral population in a resolved internal (quantum or energy) state is the projection of the [neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity) vector onto the major-radius direction $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
v_R = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{n,s}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{n,s}}$ is the bulk fluid velocity of the neutral particles occupying the specified internal state $s$ and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector along the major-radius axis.

This quantity is state-resolved: a separate value is defined for each internal level, distinct from the state-averaged neutral fluid velocity. The [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity) gives the complementary poloidal component of the same state-resolved flow. The analogous quantity for ions resolved by charge state is the [radial_ion_charge_state_velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity). The related [radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity) describes the convection velocity that advects momentum for the same resolved neutral state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the resolved neutral state population flows in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial component of the effective E×B drift velocity assigned to a neutral species in a specified internal state, directed along increasing major radius.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the [effective neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the projection of the assigned drift velocity onto the cylindrical major-radius direction.

The component is defined from the local electric and magnetic fields by

$$
v_R = \left(\frac{\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $v_R$ is the radial velocity component, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the major-radius unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This effective velocity is assigned to the specified neutral internal state for transport attribution; it does not imply direct Lorentz acceleration of neutral particles. A pure E×B drift has no parallel component, distinguishing this quantity from the [parallel neutral internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the assigned velocity points toward increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Effective radial diffusivity for momentum transport by the aggregate neutral population, summed over all modeled neutral internal states.
NAMES.long:
The radial neutral momentum diffusion coefficient is the effective coefficient for diffusive transport of neutral-particle momentum across nested magnetic flux surfaces in the radial transport direction. It is the radial component of the [neutral momentum diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) for the aggregate neutral population, summed over modeled internal states.

In a diagonal effective-diffusion closure, the associated constitutive relation is

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,rr} = -\rho_n D_{p,r}\frac{\partial u_{n,r}}{\partial r}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,rr}$ is the radial flux of radial neutral momentum, $\rho_n$ is the total neutral mass density, $D_{p,r}$ is this radial diffusivity, $u_{n,r}$ is the aggregate neutral radial velocity, and $(r,\theta,\phi)$ are radial, poloidal, and toroidal coordinates. The coefficient is distinct from [radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient), which governs particle rather than momentum transport, and from [radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), which resolves a specific neutral internal state.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Radial neutral particle flux is the outward or inward cylindrical-radial component of neutral number flow, summed over all neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Radial neutral particle flux is the cylindrical-radial component of the net directed flow of neutral atoms and molecules across an oriented reference surface, with all included neutral species and internal states aggregated. It is the radial projection of [neutral_particle_flux](name:neutral_particle_flux); [poloidal_neutral_particle_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux) gives the corresponding poloidal projection.

For neutral species and internal-state index $s$, the radial flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{n},R} = \hat{\mathbf{R}} \cdot \sum_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of constituent $s$, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is its mean velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the radial unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity includes the directed convective, diffusive, drift, and turbulent contributions represented in the constituent fluxes. It is distinct from [radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux), which is restricted to one specified internal state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral particle flow has a component in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: radial_particle_convection_velocity
NAMES.short: Effective radial velocity multiplying particle density in the convective part of cross-field transport, positive for transport away from the magnetic axis.
NAMES.long:
The radial particle convection velocity is the effective coefficient of the density-proportional, convective contribution to particle transport across magnetic flux surfaces. It is the radial component of [particle convection velocity] and does not select a particular electron, ion, or neutral species.

The convective radial particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_r^{\mathrm{conv}} = n\,v_r^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_r^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective radial particle flux in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, $n$ is the particle number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_r^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convection velocity in m s$^{-1}$.

This quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport. Species-resolved counterparts, such as [radial electron convection velocity](name:radial_electron_convection_velocity) and [radial ion convection velocity](name:radial_ion_convection_velocity), specify the transported population explicitly.
NAMES.sign: Positive when convective particle transport is directed radially away from the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: radial_total_momentum_source
NAMES.short: Radial component of the total momentum source density, the rate of radial momentum addition per unit volume summed over all included particle species.
NAMES.long:
Radial component of the total momentum source density is the local rate of momentum addition to the total plasma per unit volume, projected onto $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is formed by summing the radial source-density contributions from all particle species included in the total plasma population.

The species aggregation is defined by:

$$
S_{R,\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{I}} S_{R,s} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{I}} \mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{mom},s} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of included particle species, $S_{R,s}$ is the radial [momentum source density](name:radial_momentum_source) for species $s$, $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{mom},s}$ is the momentum source-density vector for species $s$, and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius.

The included-species set defines the total being taken. Pairwise momentum exchange between two members of $\mathcal{I}$ cancels in the species sum and is not a net total source; exchange with a species outside $\mathcal{I}$ or with an external momentum reservoir contributes only through its residual radial source on the included population. For an ion species represented through charge states, this extensive source-density contribution is summed over all charge states before it enters the total; a charge-state-resolved component is represented by [radial ion charge-state momentum source].

This quantity is the source-density counterpart of [radial total momentum](name:radial_total_momentum_source). It is distinct from subset quantities such as [radial neutral momentum source](name:radial_neutral_momentum_source) and from [radial plasma momentum flux], which denotes transport of radial momentum rather than local production.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net total momentum source points in the $+\hat{R}$ direction, toward increasing major radius $R$, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: radial_total_thermal_electron_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Net radial flux density of thermal electron energy across nested magnetic flux surfaces, combining conductive transport with convective enthalpy transport.
NAMES.long:
The radial total thermal electron energy flux is the net flux density of thermal electron energy crossing nested magnetic flux surfaces. It includes conductive transport and convective transport of electron thermal enthalpy, while excluding ion, neutral, and nonthermal-particle energy channels.

The flux is defined by projecting the sum of conductive and enthalpy transports onto the outward surface normal:

$$
q_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{rad}} = \left[\mathbf{q}_{e,\mathrm{cond}} + \left(u_{e,\mathrm{th}} + p_e\right)\mathbf{v}_e\right] \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_\psi
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{e,\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive electron heat-flux vector, $u_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the electron thermal internal-energy density, $p_e$ is electron thermal pressure, $\mathbf{v}_e$ is the electron fluid velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\psi$ is the outward unit normal to the nested magnetic flux surface. The quantity is the electron counterpart of [radial_total_ion_energy_flux](name:radial_total_ion_energy_flux) and is more specifically thermal than [radial_electron_energy_flux](name:radial_electron_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net electron thermal-energy flux is directed away from the magnetic axis across the nested magnetic flux surface.

NAMES.name: rotation_frequency_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short: Angular rotation frequency vector of the species-independent E×B drift, identical for all particle species on a given flux surface and determined entirely by the local electric and magnetic fields.
NAMES.long:
The E×B rotation frequency is the angular rotation rate of the electromagnetic drift driven by $\mathbf{v}_{E\times B} = (\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}) / B^2$, where $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric field and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field. Because this drift velocity depends only on the local fields and not on particle charge or mass, the corresponding rotation frequency is the same for all species on a given flux surface.

For a flux-surface-averaged equilibrium, the toroidal component is related to the electrostatic potential $\Phi$ by:

$$
\omega_{E\times B} = -\frac{\partial \langle \Phi \rangle}{\partial \psi}
$$

where $\langle \Phi \rangle$ is the flux-surface-averaged electrostatic potential and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux. The [toroidal rotation frequency due to E×B drift](name:toroidal_rotation_frequency_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the toroidal projection of this vector, expressed as $v_{E\times B,\phi} / R$ where $R$ is the local major radius.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: runaway_electron_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Runaway-electron convection velocity is the effective vector velocity for advective transport of the runaway-electron population, distinct from gradient-driven diffusive transport. It covers the full vector quantity and any resolved component or projection defined by a more specific name.
NAMES.long:
Runaway-electron convection velocity is the effective vector velocity that represents advective transport of the runaway-electron population in a transport description. It is the coefficient multiplying runaway-electron number density in the convective contribution to the runaway-electron particle flux.

The convective runaway-electron particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{RE,conv}} = n_{\mathrm{RE}}\,\boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{RE,conv}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{RE,conv}}$ is the convective contribution to the runaway-electron particle flux, $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is runaway-electron number density, and $\boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{RE,conv}}$ is the runaway-electron convection velocity.

This quantity excludes gradient-driven diffusive transport, sources, sinks, and loss terms except insofar as they are represented through an effective advective flux. It is not restricted to a single direction; resolved quantities such as the [perpendicular runaway-electron convection velocity](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_convection_velocity) define specific projections of the same runaway-electron advective velocity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component or projection of $\boldsymbol{V}_{\mathrm{RE,conv}}$ points along the positive direction defined for that component or projection.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_runaway_electron_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Signed cross-field component of the effective runaway-electron convection velocity, projected along the outward normal to nested magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the directed transport velocity of runaway electrons across magnetic flux surfaces, isolated from the field-aligned component of the [runaway-electron convection velocity](name:runaway_electron_convection_velocity).

The perpendicular component is defined by

$$
v_{\perp}^{\rm RE} = \mathbf{v}_{\rm RE} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\psi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\rm RE}$ is the effective runaway-electron convection-velocity vector and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\psi}$ is the outward unit normal to nested magnetic flux surfaces. This convective quantity describes directed cross-field transport and excludes diffusive spreading, which is characterized by the [perpendicular runaway-electron diffusivity](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_diffusivity). It contributes to the [perpendicular runaway-electron particle flux](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_particle_flux) together with the runaway-electron density.
NAMES.sign: Positive when runaway-electron convection is directed outward from the magnetic axis toward increasing flux label.

NAMES.name: runaway_electron_critical_electric_field
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Runaway-electron electric-field threshold at which field-aligned acceleration overcomes collisional drag and sustained runaway electron generation becomes possible.
NAMES.long:
The runaway-electron critical electric field is the threshold for the field-aligned electric force to overcome collisional drag on electrons, allowing sustained acceleration into the runaway regime. It is the runaway-electron-specific form of the [critical electric field](name:critical_electric_field); its magnitude-specific representation is the [runaway-electron critical electric-field magnitude](name:runaway_electron_critical_electric_field_magnitude).

In the relativistic collisional threshold model, the field is defined by

$$
E_c = \frac{n_e e^3 \ln\Lambda}{4\pi\epsilon_0^2 m_e c^2}
$$

where $n_e$ is the free-electron number density, $e$ is the elementary charge, $\ln\Lambda$ is the Coulomb logarithm, $\epsilon_0$ is the vacuum permittivity, $m_e$ is the electron rest mass, and $c$ is the speed of light.

This quantity is a positive threshold criterion, not the instantaneous signed parallel electric-field component, runaway-electron current, or runaway-electron generation rate.

NAMES.name: runaway_electron_density
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Number density of runaway electrons in the suprathermal accelerating tail of the electron distribution, excluding the thermal bulk population.
NAMES.long:
Runaway electron density is the local population density of electrons classified as runaway because they occupy the accelerating suprathermal tail of the electron distribution. It excludes electrons belonging to the thermal bulk population.

The density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the runaway-electron distribution:

$$
n_{\mathrm{RE}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{RE}}} f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway electron number density, $f_e$ is the electron phase-space distribution, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the velocity-space domain classified as runaway. The resulting density is distinct from the broader [fast_electron_density](name:fast_electron_density), which need not be restricted to runaway electrons. Its charge-weighted velocity moment contributes to [runaway_electron_current_density](name:runaway_electron_current_density). Spatial averaging and integration produce the [volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density) and [volume_integrated_runaway_electron_density](name:volume_integrated_runaway_electron_density), respectively.
