NAMES.name: thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume deposited in the bulk thermal-electron population through Coulomb collisions with other charged particle populations, acting as a source or sink in the thermal-electron momentum balance.
NAMES.long:
The collisional torque density on the thermal-electron population quantifies how Coulomb collisions between bulk thermal electrons and other charged populations transfer angular momentum locally. It is the collisional angular-momentum source term in the thermal-electron momentum balance, before any additional qualifier selects a projection, a source subpopulation, or a receiving thermal-electron orbit class.

The local collisional torque density is the collisional part of the thermal-electron angular-momentum-density evolution:

$$
\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
=
\left(\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{e,\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{coll}}
=
\sum_{\beta} \boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{e,\mathrm{th}\leftarrow\beta}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this torque density, $\boldsymbol{\ell}_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the angular-momentum density of the bulk thermal-electron population, $\beta$ labels a colliding charged population or subpopulation, and $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{e,\mathrm{th}\leftarrow\beta}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the corresponding Coulomb-collisional transfer to thermal electrons.

This parent quantity is not restricted to a single component, fast-particle orbit class, or receiving-electron orbit class. Resolved forms include the [toroidal thermal-electron collisional torque density](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) for the toroidal projection, the [counter-passing thermal-electron collisional torque density](name:counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) for transfer from counter-passing fast particles, and the [trapped thermal-electron collisional torque density](name:trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) for the trapped-orbit part of the thermal-electron population; the latter two are distinct decompositions and are not members of one common fast-particle orbit-class sum. It is the bulk thermal-electron contribution to the [electron collisional torque density](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and is distinct from the [fast-electron collisional torque density](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a scalar component of $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ acts along the positive direction of the basis vector defining that component; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the toroidal component is positive in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume to thermal electrons from Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local rate per unit volume at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum to the bulk, near-Maxwellian thermal electron population through interactions with counter-passing fast particles.

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,counter}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,counter}}
$$

Here $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,counter}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis, and $\mathbf{f}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,counter}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to thermal electrons by counter-passing fast-particle interactions.

This is the counter-passing contribution to [thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). It retains the full vector transfer; its toroidal projection is represented by [toroidal counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), while [counter-passing thermal ion torque density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) describes the analogous transfer to thermal ions. Non-Coulomb processes are excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the corresponding component of transferred angular momentum points along the positive $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated torque transferred to the bulk thermal electron population through Coulomb collisions with fast particles and other plasma species.
NAMES.long:
The thermal electron collisional torque quantifies the net rate of angular momentum transferred to the bulk (Maxwellian) electron population through Coulomb collisions with other plasma constituents, including ions and suprathermal (fast) particles. It is the thermal-electron branch of [electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:electron_torque_due_to_collisions), complementing [fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions) which captures the non-thermal electron contribution.

The quantity $T_{e_\mathrm{th},\mathrm{coll}}$ enters the toroidal angular momentum balance for the thermal electron fluid:

$$
\frac{\partial L_{e_\mathrm{th},\phi}}{\partial t} = T_{e_\mathrm{th},\mathrm{coll}} + T_{e_\mathrm{th},\mathrm{EM}} + T_{e_\mathrm{th},\nabla p}
$$

where $L_{e_\mathrm{th},\phi}$ is the thermal electron toroidal angular momentum integrated over the plasma volume, $T_{e_\mathrm{th},\mathrm{EM}}$ is the electromagnetic torque contribution, and $T_{e_\mathrm{th},\nabla p}$ is the pressure-gradient torque.

In transport modeling, this torque is evaluated by taking the toroidal moment of the Coulomb collision operator applied to the bulk Maxwellian electron distribution and integrating over the plasma volume. The dominant exchange channels are electron–ion frictional drag and momentum transfer from suprathermal (fast) particles; the fast-particle channel becomes significant when neutral beam injection or auxiliary heating generates substantial non-thermal populations. The toroidal projection of this quantity is given by [toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when angular momentum is transferred to the thermal electron population in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Number density of thermal (Maxwellian) ions of a given species resolved to a specific ionic charge state, excluding fast and suprathermal ion populations.
NAMES.long:
The thermal ion charge state number density is the local number density of ions whose velocity distribution is well approximated by a Maxwellian at the local ion temperature, resolved to a single ionic charge state $Z$. Fast, suprathermal, and runaway ions are excluded from this population.

$$
n_{\mathrm{th},Z}(\mathbf{r}) = \int f_{\mathrm{th},Z}(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{th},Z}$ is the local Maxwellian velocity distribution function for ions with charge state $Z$ at position $\mathbf{r}$.

Summing over all charge states of a given ion species recovers [thermal_ion_density](name:thermal_ion_density). Summing over all species and all charge states yields [total_thermal_ion_density](name:total_thermal_ion_density). The total ion number density for the same charge state, irrespective of the velocity-space population, is [ion_charge_state_density](name:ion_charge_state_density), of which this quantity is the thermal sub-population; the parent aggregate is [ion_charge_state_number_density](name:ion_charge_state_number_density). The complementary charge-state-resolved quantity for fast ions is [fast_ion_charge_state_density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density).

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer to thermal ions of a specified charge state from non-Maxwellian source populations, aggregated over all guiding-center orbit classes of the source particles.
NAMES.long:
Thermal ion charge state power density due to collisions is the local volumetric rate at which non-Maxwellian (fast) particles deposit kinetic energy into thermal ions of a single, specified charge state via Coulomb collisions. It is the thermal-ion-targeted component of [ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The power density $p_{\mathrm{th},i,z}$ is the velocity-space integral of the energy-transfer collision frequency against the non-Maxwellian source distribution $f_s(\mathbf{v})$:

$$
p_{\mathrm{th},i,z} = \int \nu_\epsilon^{(z)}(v)\,\frac{m_s v^2}{2}\,f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\nu_\epsilon^{(z)}(v)$ is the energy-transfer collision frequency from source particles of speed $v$ to thermal ions of charge state $z$, and $m_s$ is the source-particle mass.

Contributions from distinct guiding-center orbit classes of the source particles — co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped — partition this total, as resolved in [co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and its parallel siblings. The quantity is resolved per charge state and not summed over charge states; its volume integral is the [thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when thermal ions of the specified charge state gain net kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric Coulomb-collisional energy-transfer rate received by thermal ions of a specified charge state from the co-passing component of a fast-particle distribution.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions is the local volumetric rate at which co-passing non-Maxwellian fast particles transfer kinetic energy to thermal ions in one specified charge state through Coulomb collisions. It is the co-passing orbit-class component of [thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The power density $p^{\mathrm{co}}_{\mathrm{th},i,z}$ is defined by the energy-transfer collision frequency integrated over the co-passing source distribution:

$$
p^{\mathrm{co}}_{\mathrm{th},i,z} = \int \nu_\epsilon^{(z)}(v)\,\frac{m_s v^2}{2}\,f_s^{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\nu_\epsilon^{(z)}(v)$ is the energy-transfer collision frequency from source particles of speed $v$ to thermal ions of charge state $z$, $m_s$ is the source-particle mass, and $f_s^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the fast-particle distribution restricted to co-passing guiding-center orbits.

Only the co-passing source-orbit contribution is included; counter-passing and trapped contributions are separate, including [counter-passing thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions). The quantity is resolved per charge state rather than summed over charge states, and its volume integral is [thermal ion charge-state power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when thermal ions of the specified charge state gain net kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric Coulomb-collisional energy-transfer rate received by thermal ions of a specified charge state from the counter-passing component of a fast-particle distribution.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions is the local volumetric rate at which a fast-particle population transfers kinetic energy to thermal ions in one specified charge state through Coulomb collisions.

$$
P_{\mathrm{cp}\to i,q}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{\mathrm{cp}} f_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,Q_{\mathrm{f}\to i,q}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{\mathrm{f}}$ is the phase-space distribution of fast particles in the counter-passing orbit class, and $Q_{\mathrm{f}\to i,q}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional kinetic-energy transfer rate from one such particle to thermal ions in charge state $q$. The integration is restricted to counter-passing circulating guiding-center orbits.

This quantity is resolved for one ion charge state and is not summed over charge states. It is distinct from the corresponding [co-passing thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions); aggregation over all source orbit classes gives [thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), while volume integration gives [thermal ion charge-state power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions).

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge state through Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum source associated with Coulomb momentum transfer to a specified thermal ion charge state. Orbit classes and directional components select particular contributions without changing this common physical meaning.

For a selected angular-momentum direction, the torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a} = (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_a
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}$ is the torque density about direction $a$, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the rotation axis, $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to the specified charge state, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the corresponding unit vector. For toroidal angular momentum in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this relation reduces to $R f_\phi$.

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved realization of [ion charge-state torque density due to collisions]; [co-passing thermal ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is one orbit-resolved instance.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the selected angular-momentum transfer is in the positive orientation of its stated axis; for toroidal angular momentum, positive is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Co-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per plasma volume to a specified thermal ion charge state from Coulomb collisions with co-passing particles.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a specified charge state from Coulomb collisions with the co-passing population.

With $\mathrm{co}$ denoting this collision channel, the local torque density is defined by the moment of the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{co}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the local plasma volume, and $\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the collisional force density exerted on the specified thermal ion charge state by co-passing particles. The charge-state selection is retained rather than summed over ionization states. This is the co-passing contribution to [thermal ion charge-state collisional torque density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and differs from the corresponding [counter-passing quantity](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) by the collision-partner orbit class.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Counter-passing collisional torque density is the vector angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge state from Coulomb collisions with counter-passing particles.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a specified charge state from Coulomb collisions with the counter-passing population.

With $\mathrm{cp}$ denoting this collision channel, the local torque density is defined by the moment of the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{cp}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the local plasma volume, and $\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the collisional force density exerted on the specified thermal ion charge state by counter-passing particles. The charge-state selection is retained rather than summed over ionization states. This is the counter-passing contribution to [thermal ion charge-state collisional torque density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and differs from the corresponding [co-passing quantity](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) by the collision-partner orbit class.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local number density of thermal (Maxwellian) ions of a specified species at a plasma point, summed over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Thermal ion density is the local count of Maxwellian ions of a specified species per unit volume at a point in the plasma. It is a population- and species-resolved specialization of [ion_density](name:ion_density).

The charge-state-summed thermal density is defined by

$$
n_i^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_Z \int f_{i,Z}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_i^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal ion number density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $Z$ indexes the ionic charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{i,Z}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal phase-space number density. The sum includes all charge states of the specified species and excludes suprathermal fast ions. The all-species counterpart is [total_thermal_ion_density](name:total_thermal_ion_density), while [thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density) resolves this quantity to one charge state.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_energy
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated internal energy of the thermal-ion population, obtained from its isotropic pressure and excluding fast and suprathermal ions.
NAMES.long:
Thermal-ion energy is the extensive internal-energy content of a thermal-ion population integrated over the plasma volume. It is the thermal component of [ion energy](name:ion_energy), not the energy of directed bulk flow or nonthermal ions.

For an isotropic thermal-ion pressure, the defining relation is

$$
E_{\mathrm{th},i} = \int_V u_{\mathrm{th},i}\,dV = \frac{3}{2}\int_V p_{\mathrm{th},i}\,dV
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the volume-integrated thermal-ion energy, $u_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the thermal-ion internal-energy density, $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the isotropic thermal-ion pressure, and $V$ is the integration volume.

The population scope and aggregation are fixed by qualifying terms; the complete thermal-ion ensemble is represented by [total thermal ion energy](name:total_thermal_ion_energy). Unlike [ion kinetic energy density](name:ion_kinetic_energy_density), this quantity excludes directed bulk-flow energy as well as fast and suprathermal ion energy.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for the aggregate thermal ion population, including contributions from fast-particle orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
Thermal-ion collisional power density is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for the aggregate thermal ion population. It combines energy transfer across the included thermal ion species and charge states, with fast-particle contributions aggregated over the included source-orbit classes.

The defining aggregate is

$$
P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_{a\in\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{th}}}\sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the thermal-ion collisional power density, $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the set of included thermal ion target populations, and $Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional kinetic-energy transfer rate to target population $a$ from partner population $b$.

This quantity is target-population specific: it includes energy gained or lost by thermal ions, not the corresponding fast-ion target power. It is the charge-state-aggregated counterpart of [thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and contributes to [ion power density due to collisions](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions); its volume-integrated counterpart is [thermal ion power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aggregate thermal ion population gains kinetic energy from its collision partners.

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net local volumetric power transferred to the bulk thermal ion population by Coulomb collisions with co-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing thermal-ion collisional power density is the local volumetric rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from co-passing fast particles to the bulk thermal ion population. It is the co-passing contribution to [thermal-ion collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) and includes all contributing thermal-ion species and charge states.

The orbit decomposition is

$$
Q_{\mathrm{th\,ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_o Q_{\mathrm{th\,ion},o}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{th\,ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the total thermal-ion collisional power density, $Q_{\mathrm{th\,ion},o}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the contribution from source-particle orbit class $o$, and $o=\mathrm{co}$ denotes co-passing. Co-passing fast particles are circulating particles whose guiding centers transit poloidally with parallel velocity in the plasma-current direction.

The receiving population is thermal ions; the co-passing qualifier applies to the source particles, not the receiving ions. The quantity is distinct from [co-passing fast-ion collisional power density](name:co_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) and from the charge-state-resolved [co-passing thermal-ion collisional power density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the thermal ion population gains energy through Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Counter-passing thermal-ion collisional power density is the local volumetric rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from counter-passing fast particles to the bulk thermal ion population.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal-ion collisional power density is the local volumetric rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to the bulk thermal ion population from the counter-passing part of a fast-particle distribution. It is summed over receiving ion species and charge states, while the counter-passing qualifier selects the source-particle orbit class.

The orbit-resolved contributions to [thermal-ion collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) satisfy

$$
Q_{\mathrm{th\,ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_o Q_{\mathrm{th\,ion},o}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{th\,ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the total thermal-ion collisional power density, $Q_{\mathrm{th\,ion},o}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the contribution from fast-particle orbit class $o$, and $o$ is counter-passing for this quantity. Counter-passing denotes circulating fast-particle guiding-center orbits moving opposite to the plasma-current direction. The corresponding co-passing contribution is [co-passing thermal-ion power density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), while [thermal-ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) resolves the receiving ions by charge state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the bulk thermal ion population gains energy through Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total thermal-ion population from a fast-particle distribution, summed over all thermal ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the complete thermal-ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with a colliding fast-particle distribution. It aggregates all thermal ion species and charge states without resolving the receiving ion species or charge state.

The volume-integrated thermal-ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm th\,ion,coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm th\,ion,coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm th\,ion,coll}$ is the local collisional power density transferred into the aggregate thermal-ion population and $V$ is the plasma volume. The quantity is the thermal-ion counterpart of [fast ion power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions) and is a population-resolved component of [ion power due to collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions). Charge-state-resolved components include [thermal ion charge-state power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net energy into the complete thermal-ion population.

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Isotropic kinetic pressure of the thermal ion population at a plasma location, summed over all ion species and charge states while excluding non-thermal fast-ion contributions.
NAMES.long:
Thermal ion pressure is the isotropic kinetic pressure of the thermal ion population, defined through the second central velocity moment of the Maxwellian bulk ion distribution function. It is summed over all ion species and all ionization states present in the thermal plasma. It excludes pressure carried by non-thermal fast or suprathermal ions.

For a mixture of thermal ion species and charge states, the defining scalar pressure is:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{thermal}} = \sum_s p_{i,s,\mathrm{thermal}} = \sum_s n_s k_\mathrm{B} T_s
$$

where $s$ labels each thermal ion species and ionization-state population, $p_{i,s,\mathrm{thermal}}$ is the corresponding [thermal ion-state pressure], $n_s$ is the number density of that population, $T_s$ is its thermodynamic temperature, and $k_\mathrm{B}$ is Boltzmann's constant.

This quantity is the charge-state- and species-summed thermal component of [ion_pressure](name:ion_pressure). The corresponding non-thermal contribution is [fast_ion_pressure](name:fast_ion_pressure); their sum gives the ion pressure over the same population scope. In the absence of an additional species qualifier, this quantity has the same physical aggregation scope as [total_thermal_ion_pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure).

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Rate of angular momentum transfer per unit volume deposited in the thermal ion population through Coulomb collisions with charged particle species, acting as a source or sink in the thermal-ion momentum balance.
NAMES.long:
Rate of angular momentum transfer per unit volume deposited in the thermal ion population through Coulomb collisions with charged particle species, acting as a source or sink in the thermal-ion momentum balance. It is the collisional angular-momentum source term for the bulk thermal-ion subset, not the aggregate over all ion populations.

The collisional thermal-ion torque density is the collisional contribution to the rate of change of thermal-ion angular-momentum density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left(\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{i,\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this collisional thermal-ion torque density, $\boldsymbol{\ell}_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the angular-momentum density of the thermal-ion population, and the subscript $\mathrm{coll}$ denotes transfer by Coulomb-collisional momentum exchange with other charged populations.

This quantity specializes the broader [ion torque density due to collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) to bulk thermal ions; [fast ion torque density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) covers the energetic-ion counterpart. As an extensive population quantity it is summed over all thermal-ion charge states. More specific refinements include orbit-class contributions such as [co-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), [counter-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and [trapped thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), as well as the [toroidal thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. By Newton's third law, a collisional exchange between two represented populations contributes equal and opposite terms to their separate torque-density balances.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component of the collisional torque density acts along the positive direction of its named projection; for a toroidal projection this is the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Torque per unit volume transferred to thermal ions by Coulomb collisions with the co-passing fast-particle population, representing the co-passing source-orbit contribution to angular-momentum deposition on bulk thermal ions.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal ion population by Coulomb collisions with co-passing fast particles. It represents the co-passing source-orbit contribution to angular-momentum deposition on thermal ions and is one of the three orbit-class components — co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped — that sum to give the total [thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The defining kinetic moment is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i}^{\mathrm{co}} = R\,m_i \int \mathbf{v}\, C_i^{\mathrm{co}\rightarrow\mathrm{th}}[f_{\mathrm{co}},f_{\mathrm{th},i}]\, d^3v
$$

where $R$ is major radius in m, $m_i$ is the thermal ion mass in kg, $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $C_i^{\mathrm{co}\rightarrow\mathrm{th}}$ is the Coulomb collision operator for momentum transfer from the co-passing fast-particle distribution $f_{\mathrm{co}}$ to the thermal ion distribution $f_{\mathrm{th},i}$, both in s$^3$ m$^{-6}$.

The toroidal projection of this vector is [toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame where $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive toroidal component when angular momentum is transferred in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal ions through Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal-ion population by Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles. It represents the counter-passing source-orbit contribution and is a vector quantity before any directional projection.

The torque density follows from the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{ctr}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{ctr}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{ctr}}$ is the torque density transferred to bulk thermal ions by collisions with counter-passing fast particles, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the toroidal symmetry axis, and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{ctr}}$ is the corresponding collisional force density.

This is the counter-passing source-orbit branch of [thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), not the orbit-class-unresolved collisional torque density. The [toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) quantity is its toroidal projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component of the torque vector points along the corresponding positive basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: thermal_neutral_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Local number density of thermal (Maxwellian) neutral atoms and molecules at a plasma point, summed over all internal quantum states.
NAMES.long:
Thermal neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms or molecules whose velocity distribution is represented by a Maxwellian. It is the thermal component of [neutral density](name:neutral_density), distinct from suprathermal neutral populations.

The density is obtained by summing the thermal populations over the represented neutral species and internal quantum states:

$$
n_{0,\mathrm{th}} = \sum_a \sum_q n_{0,\mathrm{th}}^{(a,q)}
$$

where $n_{0,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal neutral density, $a$ indexes neutral atomic or molecular species, $q$ indexes internal quantum states, and $n_{0,\mathrm{th}}^{(a,q)}$ is the corresponding state-resolved density. The quantity includes all thermal internal states and excludes fast or otherwise non-Maxwellian neutrals; its state-resolved counterpart is [thermal neutral internal-state density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density).

NAMES.name: thermal_neutral_internal_state_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Number density of neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum state within the thermal (Maxwellian) velocity population.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the number density of thermal neutral particles restricted to a specified internal quantum state. It is the thermal contribution to [neutral_internal_state_density](name:neutral_internal_state_density), which includes all neutral velocity populations.

The density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the thermal distribution for state $s$:

$$
n_s^{\mathrm{th}} = \int f_s^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_s^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal neutral density in state $s$, $f_s^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the thermal velocity distribution of neutral particles in that state, and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity.

Only the thermal, Maxwellian population is included; suprathermal neutrals in the same internal state are excluded. Summing over internal states gives the corresponding [thermal_neutral_density](name:thermal_neutral_density).

NAMES.name: thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure of thermal neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state, arising from the local thermal velocity-space component and excluding nonthermal fast-neutral contributions.
NAMES.long:
The thermal neutral internal state pressure is the kinetic pressure associated with neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or excitation state whose velocities belong to the local thermal component of the state-resolved distribution. It is a partial pressure for one internal state, not a sum over all internal states, and excludes suprathermal fast-neutral contributions.

For internal state $a$, the thermal pressure is the one-third trace of the central second velocity-space moment of the thermal subset:

$$
p_{a,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{m_a}{3}\int \lvert\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{a,\mathrm{th}}\rvert^2 f_{a,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_a$ is the particle mass, $f_{a,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of thermal neutrals in state $a$, and $\mathbf{u}_{a,\mathrm{th}}$ is the mean velocity of that thermal subset. The central moment excludes dynamic pressure from directed bulk flow.

The [suprathermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) is the corresponding nonthermal fast-neutral contribution, and [total neutral internal-state pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) combines the thermal and suprathermal contributions for the same internal state. Summing this quantity over internal states gives [thermal neutral pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure). The associated state-resolved kinetic temperature is [neutral internal-state temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature).

NAMES.name: thermal_particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.short: Local volumetric heating rate delivered to thermal particles when fast or suprathermal particles lose kinetic energy through Coulomb thermalization.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the thermal-particle component of [particle power density due to thermalization](name:particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization): the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from a fast or suprathermal population to the specified thermal population.

$$
q_{\mathrm{th}}=\left.\frac{\partial u_{\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{Coulomb\ thermalization}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the transferred power density, in W m$^{-3}$, and $u_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal population's kinetic-energy density. The derivative includes only energy exchange attributable to collisional relaxation toward thermal equilibrium; it excludes direct injection, wave heating, radiation, and other non-thermalization sources. Positive values represent net energy gain by the thermal population.

sources.enhanced_context: Radial source rate of energy density transferred to the thermal particle population due to thermalization of fast (non-thermal) particles, as a 1D profile. Represents the power per unit volume deposited into the thermal background via slowing-down collisions.
sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of energy density within the thermal particle population due to the thermalization of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged source of thermal particles, momentum and energy due to thermalization. Here thermalization refers to non-thermal particles, sufficiently assimilated to the thermal background to be re-categorized as thermal particles. Note that this source may also be negative if thermal particles are being accelerated such that they form a distinct non-thermal contribution, e.g. due run-away of RF interactions.

NAMES.name: thermal_particle_power_due_to_thermalization
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated net power transferred to the thermal particle population as nonthermal particles lose energy and join the thermal background.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net rate of energy transfer to the thermal particle population from the thermalization of nonthermal particles. It represents the global contribution of this process to the thermal-particle energy balance, rather than a local power density or particle source rate.

The volume-integrated power is defined by

$$
P_{\rm th,therm} = \int_{\mathcal{V}} p_{\rm th,therm}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\rm th,therm}$ is the integrated power in W, $p_{\rm th,therm}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local thermalization power density in W m$^{-3}$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathcal{V}$ is the plasma volume.

Positive values represent net energy gain by the thermal particle population; negative values represent net transfer of energy from the thermal population to a nonthermal population. The local counterpart is [thermal particle power density due to thermalization](name:thermal_particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization), while particle-number transfer is represented separately by [total thermal particle source rate](name:total_thermal_particle_source_rate).

sources.enhanced_context: Power input to the thermal particle population due to thermalization of fast particles (volume-integrated). Represents the energy transfer rate as non-thermal particles slow down and join the bulk thermal background.
sources.leaf_definition: Power input to the thermal particle population due to the thermalization of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Volume integrated source of thermal particles, momentum and energy due to thermalization. Here thermalization refers to non-thermal particles, sufficiently assimilated to the thermal background to be re-categorized as thermal particles. Note that this source may also be negative if thermal particles are being accelerated such that they form a distinct non-thermal contribution, e.g. due run-away of RF interactions.

NAMES.name: thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short: Net volumetric rate of particle production or loss from a distribution function source for the thermal population, averaged over flux surfaces and summed over orbit populations.
NAMES.long:
The thermal particle source rate $S_n^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the net rate at which particles enter or leave the thermal population, resolved as a volumetric source and averaged over magnetic flux surfaces. It is the thermal-population component of the general [particle source rate](name:particle_source_rate).

For a flux surface labeled by $\psi$, it is defined by

$$
S_n^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\sum_{o\in\mathcal{O}}\left\langle S_{n,o}^{\mathrm{th}}\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $\mathcal{O}$ is the set of included thermal orbit populations, $S_{n,o}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local net source rate for orbit population $o$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes a flux-surface average. Positive values indicate net transfer into the thermal population; negative values indicate net removal. The sum includes orbit classes such as [trapped thermal particle source rate](name:trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate) and [co-passing thermal particle source rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), rather than isolating one class. Volume integration gives the corresponding [total thermal particle source rate](name:total_thermal_particle_source_rate).

NAMES.name: co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles are added to or removed from the co-passing orbit population. Co-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is in the plasma-current direction.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the co-passing orbit class. Co-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is in the plasma-current direction, so their parallel velocity does not bounce-reverse as for trapped particles.

For a flux surface labeled by the magnetic-flux label $\psi$, it is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\left\langle \mathcal{S}_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}}\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local net source rate for the co-passing thermal orbit population and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes a flux-surface average.

It is the co-passing orbit-class component of the [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), not a sum over [counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) or [trapped](name:trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate) orbit classes. Volume integration gives the corresponding contribution to the [total thermal particle source rate](name:total_thermal_particle_source_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when local processes add thermal particles to the co-passing orbit class.

sources.enhanced_context: Flux-surface-averaged source rate of particle density for the co-passing particle population of the distribution function. Represents the net particle source or sink from wave or collisional processes acting on co-passing particles.
sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of thermal particle density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles are added to or removed from the counter-passing orbit population. Counter-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current direction.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the counter-passing orbit class. Counter-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current direction.

For a flux surface labeled by $\psi$, it is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th,loc}}\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th,loc}}$ is the local net thermal particle source rate restricted to the counter-passing orbit class and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes a flux-surface average.

It is one component of the orbit-class decomposition of the [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate): for a decomposition into trapped, co-passing, and counter-passing thermal populations, $S_n^{\mathrm{th}}=S_{n,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}+S_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}}+S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$. The other corresponding components are the [trapped thermal particle source rate](name:trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate) and the [co-passing thermal particle source rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate); volume integration over the thermal population gives the [total thermal particle source rate](name:total_thermal_particle_source_rate). It describes particle-number balance and is distinct from [counter-passing power density](name:counter_passing_power_density), which describes energy transfer for the same orbit class.
NAMES.sign: Positive when thermal particles are added to the counter-passing orbit class.

sources.enhanced_context: Flux-surface-averaged source rate of thermal particle density for the counter-passing particle population in the Fokker-Planck model. Represents the rate at which particles are added to or removed from the thermal distribution.
sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of thermal particle density

NAMES.name: thermal_plasma_energy
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated stored thermal energy of the confined plasma, equal to 3/2 times the volume integral of the total thermal pressure; the thermal component of total stored plasma energy excluding fast-particle and electromagnetic-field contributions.
NAMES.long:
Thermal plasma energy $W_{th}$ is the internal kinetic energy of the thermal electron and ion populations within the confined plasma. It excludes fast-particle energy and electromagnetic-field energy.

For scalar isotropic thermal pressure, it is defined by

$$
W_{th} = \frac{3}{2} \int_V p_{th}\,dV
$$

where $p_{th}$ is the sum of the thermal electron and ion pressures and $V$ is the confined plasma volume. It is the thermal contribution to [plasma energy](name:plasma_energy).

sources.parent_definition: Thermal plasma energy content = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the thermal pressure

NAMES.name: time_derivative_of_flux_surface_averaged_metric
NAMES.short: Time derivative of the flux-surface averaged metric is the rate of change, at fixed dimensionful toroidal flux radius coordinate, of the radial derivative of enclosed plasma volume. It represents expansion or contraction of the flux-surface volume element used in radial transport equations.
NAMES.long:
Time derivative of the flux-surface averaged metric is the time rate of change, at fixed dimensionful toroidal flux radius coordinate, of the enclosed-volume derivative with respect to that coordinate. The underlying metric is the flux-surface volume element used when conservation laws are written in flux coordinates $(\rho_\mathrm{tor}, \theta, \phi)$.

The quantity $G_{\rho,t}$ is defined by

$$
G_{\rho,t}(\rho_\mathrm{tor}, t) = \left.\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\right|_{\rho_\mathrm{tor}} \left( \frac{\partial V(\rho_\mathrm{tor}, t)}{\partial \rho_\mathrm{tor}} \right)
$$

where $V(\rho_\mathrm{tor}, t)$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the flux surface labeled by the dimensionful toroidal flux radius coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$, and $t$ is time.

This quantity is evaluated at fixed $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ and is distinct from a time derivative at fixed poloidal flux or fixed normalized radius. Transformations between the toroidal-flux-radius convention and poloidal-flux-based radial coordinates involve the [radial derivative of poloidal magnetic flux](name:radial_derivative_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux); time-dependent relabeling of poloidal flux at fixed toroidal flux is a separate quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the flux-surface volume metric $\partial V/\partial \rho_\mathrm{tor}$ increases with time at fixed dimensionful toroidal flux radius coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{tor}$.

sources.enhanced_context: Partial time derivative of the radial derivative of plasma volume with respect to the toroidal flux coordinate (∂(dV/dρ_tor)/∂t). A geometric metric quantity used in 1D transport solvers to account for moving flux surfaces.
sources.leaf_definition: Partial derivative with respect to time of the derivative of the volume with respect to the toroidal flux coordinate
sources.parent_definition: Numerics related to 1D radial solver, for various time slices.

NAMES.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions, density-weighted over charge states and evaluated at the radial location of an internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the density-weighted mean bulk-flow velocity of all argon ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier. Neutral argon is excluded, and the value is not a volume average over the barrier or surrounding plasma.

For argon charge states indexed by $q$, the velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow component along the toroidal unit vector. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\phi$ increasing toroidally. The charge-state aggregation is the same as for [toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the argon-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Argon (Ar).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of argon ions at the magnetic axis, combining all ionization states in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal argon velocity at the magnetic axis is the local bulk-flow component of argon ions projected onto the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It combines Ar+ through Ar18+ and excludes neutral argon; the magnetic axis is where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}}{\sum_{k=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}}$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}$ are toroidal velocities in m.s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{k+}}$ is the local number density in m$^{-3}$, and $(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})$ are the magnetic-axis coordinates in m. The denominator corresponds to the charge-state-summed [argon density at the magnetic axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis); the species and locus semantics parallel [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the charge-state-averaged argon-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, along $+\hat{\phi}$.

sources.enhanced_context: Argon (Ar).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Argon (Ar)

NAMES.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of beryllium ions at the internal transport barrier, combining all beryllium ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal beryllium velocity at the internal transport barrier is the bulk-flow component of the beryllium ion population evaluated at the radial position of the barrier. It combines all beryllium ionization states and excludes neutral beryllium.

The charge-state-averaged velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}} = \frac{\sum_Z n_{\mathrm{Be},Z} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be},Z}}{\sum_Z n_{\mathrm{Be},Z}}
$$

where $Z$ is beryllium charge state, $n_{\mathrm{Be},Z}$ is its ion number density, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be},Z}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow component. It is the internal-transport-barrier counterpart of [toroidal beryllium velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal beryllium velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the beryllium-ion flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Beryllium (Be).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Toroidal beryllium-ion bulk velocity at the magnetic axis, density-weighted over all beryllium ionization states in the right-handed (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal beryllium-ion bulk-flow velocity is the charge-state-aggregated toroidal component of beryllium ion motion evaluated at the magnetic axis. Neutral beryllium is excluded.

$$
V_{phi,\mathrm{Be}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}} V_{phi,\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

Here $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the density of beryllium ions in charge state $z$ at the magnetic axis, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}$ is that charge state's toroidal bulk-flow component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The denominator is the [beryllium ion density at the magnetic axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis), and the sum covers all beryllium ionic charge states.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the beryllium-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Beryllium (Be).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Beryllium (Be)

NAMES.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Toroidal carbon velocity at an internal transport barrier is the signed toroidal component of the carbon impurity-ion fluid velocity in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, evaluated on the barrier flux surface. At species level it is the density-weighted mean over all carbon charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal carbon velocity at an internal transport barrier is the signed toroidal component of the carbon impurity-ion fluid velocity in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, evaluated on the flux surface identified as the internal transport barrier. For the species-level carbon quantity, it is the density-weighted mean over all carbon ion charge states present at that surface.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{C}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C}^{q+}}\,v_{\phi,\mathrm{C}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes carbon ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{C}^{q+}}$ is the local number density of carbon ions in charge state $q+$ at the internal-transport-barrier flux surface, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{C}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding toroidal fluid-velocity component.

This quantity is a local value on the internal-transport-barrier flux surface, not a flux-surface average; a flux-surface-averaged quantity must be named explicitly. It excludes poloidal and cylindrical-radial velocity components, total speed, and charge-state-resolved carbon velocities. The denominator of the aggregation is the [carbon density at the internal transport barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), and the same carbon toroidal velocity evaluated at the magnetic axis is [toroidal carbon velocity at magnetic axis](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the carbon ion fluid velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Carbon (C).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Carbon (C)

NAMES.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the magnetic axis, combining all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The carbon impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis is projected onto the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It represents the density-weighted mean flow of the carbon ion population rather than a simple average of charge-state velocities.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C},q}v_{\phi,\mathrm{C},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C},q}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}}$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{C},q}$ are toroidal velocities in m s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{C},q}$ is the number density in m$^{-3}$, and $q$ indexes carbon ionization states. The quantity includes all carbon ion charge states and excludes neutral carbon. Its boundary counterpart is [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), while the corresponding magnetic-axis quantity for another impurity is [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_center_of_mass_velocity
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the barycentric bulk velocity of a multicomponent plasma, obtained by mass-weighting species velocities in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal center-of-mass velocity is the toroidal component of the barycentric bulk velocity of a multicomponent plasma. It retains the mass weighting of the [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) while selecting the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The toroidal component $V_{cm,\phi}$ is defined by

$$
V_{cm,\phi}=\mathbf{V}_{cm}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}=\frac{\sum_s \rho_s v_{s,\phi}}{\rho}=\frac{\sum_s m_s n_s v_{s,\phi}}{\sum_s m_s n_s}
$$

where $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $s$ indexes included species, $m_s$ is species mass in kg, $n_s$ is number density in m$^{-3}$, $\rho_s=m_s n_s$ is species mass density, $v_{s,\phi}$ is species toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $\rho=\sum_s\rho_s$ is total mass density.

This is a signed projection, not the magnitude of the bulk velocity. It differs from the [radial center-of-mass velocity](name:radial_center_of_mass_velocity) only by the selected spatial direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the barycentric velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Toroidal projection of the collisional angular-momentum source density transferred to co-passing fast electrons.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed toroidal component of the local angular-momentum transfer density delivered to co-passing fast electrons by Coulomb collisions. It is the toroidal component of the vector quantity [co-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}^{e,\mathrm{co}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{e,\mathrm{co}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{e,\mathrm{co}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector transferred to co-passing fast electrons and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity includes Coulomb-collision transfer only and excludes the counter-passing population, which is represented separately by [toroidal counter-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular-momentum source density transferred by Coulomb collisions to co-passing fast ions in a specified ionization state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the local collisional torque density deposited in co-passing fast ions belonging to charge state $q$. It represents angular-momentum transfer per unit volume from Coulomb collisions with background plasma particles.

The toroidal component is defined from the charge-state-resolved collisional torque-density vector:

$$
\tau_{\phi,q}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{q}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{q}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector transferred to ions in charge state $q$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. This is the component of [co-passing fast ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) along the toroidal direction.

The charge state $q$ is retained rather than summed over ionization states, distinguishing this quantity from the charge-state-aggregated [toroidal co-passing fast ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transferred toroidal angular momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit volume from Coulomb collisions to the co-passing fast-ion population.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of the angular-momentum source density deposited in co-passing fast ions by Coulomb collisions. It is the toroidal projection of the vector quantity [co-passing fast ion torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector deposited in the co-passing fast-ion population and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.

The quantity aggregates the included co-passing fast-ion population rather than resolving individual charge states; charge-state resolution is provided by [toroidal co-passing fast ion charge state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Contributions from the counter-passing population are represented separately by [toroidal counter-passing fast ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when collisional angular-momentum transfer to co-passing fast ions is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular-momentum source density transferred by collisions to co-passing thermal ions in a specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the local angular-momentum transfer per volume to co-passing thermal ions in one charge state through collisional momentum exchange. It is the toroidal projection of the corresponding vector quantity, [co-passing thermal ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The component is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,i,Z}^{\mathrm{coll}} = R\,f_{\phi,i,Z}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,i,Z}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal collisional torque density, $R$ is major radius, and $f_{\phi,i,Z}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal collisional force density transferred to the specified ion charge state. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This local component is distinct from the net toroidal torque on the thermal-ion population, which results from integrating the corresponding torque density over volume. Its orbit and population scope must not be conflated with the related [toroidal counter-passing thermal ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional force density points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the local collisional torque density transferred to bulk thermal ions by co-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of angular-momentum transfer to bulk thermal ions from Coulomb collisions with co-passing fast particles. It resolves the corresponding [co-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) in the geometric toroidal direction.

The projection is defined by

$$
\tau_\phi^{\mathrm{co}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the local collisional torque-density vector transferred to thermal ions and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity includes only the co-passing fast-particle contribution and the toroidal projection; it excludes the counter-passing contribution represented by [toroidal counter-passing thermal-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and other torque components.
NAMES.sign: Positive when angular momentum is transferred to the thermal ions in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_torque_density
NAMES.short: Local toroidal angular-momentum source density contributed by passing particles whose parallel motion follows the co-current direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of torque density contributed by the co-passing particle population. It gives the source rate of toroidal angular momentum per unit volume for that orbit class.

The toroidal torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{co}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing toroidal torque density, $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}$ is the toroidal force-density component on co-passing particles. The parent [co-passing torque density](name:co_passing_torque_density) includes the corresponding angular-momentum source without selecting this toroidal component.

This is a local quantity, not a flux-surface average, and is distinct from the [toroidal counter-passing torque density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density), which resolves the opposite passing-orbit branch.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the co-passing force increases toroidal angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_conductivity
NAMES.short: Toroidal conductivity is the local diagonal coefficient relating conductive toroidal current density to toroidal electric field in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal conductivity is the diagonal toroidal (φ-φ) element of the electrical conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame, whose basis is $(\\hat{R}, \\hat{\\phi}, \\hat{Z})$. It is the local coefficient relating the toroidal conductive current-density component to the toroidal electric-field component.

The [conductivity](name:conductivity) tensor is defined by

$$
\\mathbf{J}_{\\mathrm{cond}} = \\boldsymbol{\\sigma}\\cdot\\mathbf{E}, \\qquad J_{\\mathrm{cond},i}=\\sum_j \\sigma_{ij}E_j
$$

where $\\mathbf{J}_{\\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive current-density vector, $\\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, and $\\sigma_{ij}$ is the coefficient coupling electric-field direction $j$ to current direction $i$. Toroidal conductivity is $\\sigma_{\\phi\\phi}$; off-diagonal coefficients can also contribute to the toroidal current through radial or vertical electric fields. It is distinguished from [radial conductivity](name:radial_conductivity) by its toroidal projection.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed projection of the Coulomb-collisional torque-density vector transferred to counter-passing fast electrons onto the toroidal direction.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal collisional torque density is the angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume to counter-passing fast electrons, resolved along the toroidal direction. It is the toroidal component of the parent [counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque density](name:counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Let the parent torque-density vector be $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp,fe}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ and let $\hat{\phi}$ be the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{cp,fe}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp,fe}}^{\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

This component includes angular-momentum transfer caused by Coulomb collisions only and retains the counter-passing fast-electron population scope of the parent quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit volume from Coulomb collisions to fast ions on counter-passing orbits in one specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal angular-momentum source density transferred by Coulomb collisions to fast ions on counter-passing orbits in one specified ionic charge state. It excludes contributions from other orbit classes, thermal ions, and charge-state aggregation.

The toroidal torque density is defined from the collisional force-density component as

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp},q}=R\,\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp},q}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp},q}$ is the collisional force density acting on the specified fast-ion population, and $q$ identifies its charge state. The result is the toroidal projection of the vector [counter-passing fast-ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Charge-state resolution distinguishes this quantity from the aggregated [toroidal counter-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional force on the specified ions has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, producing positive toroidal angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local toroidal component of the collisional angular-momentum source density deposited in counter-passing fast ions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the collisional torque-density vector deposited in counter-passing fast ions. It gives the local source of their toroidal angular momentum.

The component is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque-density vector represented by [counter-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity includes collisional contributions from the counter-passing fast-ion population and excludes other orbit classes and noncollisional mechanisms. It is the charge-state-aggregated counterpart of [toroidal counter-passing fast-ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional angular-momentum source points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal projection of the local torque density transferred to thermal electrons by Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local angular-momentum transfer rate to thermal electrons from counter-passing fast particles through Coulomb collisions, projected onto the geometric toroidal direction. It is a component of the [counter-passing thermal-electron collisional torque density](name:counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\leftarrow cp}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque-density vector transferred to thermal electrons from counter-passing fast particles by Coulomb collisions, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the geometric toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Unlike the broader [toroidal thermal-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), this quantity restricts the fast-particle source to the counter-passing population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transferred torque-density vector projects in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
