NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular-momentum transfer density delivered by collisions to a specified thermal ion charge state from counter-passing particles, obtained from the corresponding vector quantity.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the collisional angular-momentum transfer density delivered to a specified thermal ion charge state by counter-passing particles. It is the component form of the vector [counter-passing thermal ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, the toroidal torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal component of the collisional force density transferred to the specified target population. The quantity includes only the counter-passing collision channel and the specified ion charge state; changing the orbit population produces a distinct quantity such as [toroidal counter-passing fast ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional force density on the specified thermal ion charge state has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal torque density transferred to bulk thermal ions through Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the local angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal ions by Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles. It isolates the toroidal component of the underlying [counter-passing thermal ion torque density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
\tau_\phi^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}
$$

Here $\tau_\phi^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}$ is the corresponding torque-density vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the toroidal direction. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only transfer to bulk thermal ions from the counter-passing fast-particle population is included; electron transfer and co-passing contributions are distinct quantities.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular-momentum source rate per unit volume from counter-passing particles, obtained by applying the major-radius lever arm to their net toroidal force density.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal angular-momentum source rate per unit volume associated with counter-passing particles. Counter-passing particles have guiding-center parallel motion opposite to the plasma-current direction.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the toroidal torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}(R,\phi,Z)=R\,f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}(R,\phi,Z)
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the counter-passing toroidal torque density, $R$ is the major-radius lever arm, and $f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the net toroidal force density on the counter-passing population. The force density is summed over the included particle species and momentum-exchange mechanisms.

This is the toroidal component of [counter_passing_torque_density](name:counter_passing_torque_density), distinguished from the co-passing contribution represented by [toroidal_co_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net toroidal force on the counter-passing population points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Source rate of toroidal angular momentum density contributed by the counter-passing particle population in the distribution function. Represents the flux-surface-averaged toroidal momentum injection or sink rate acting on counter-passing particles.
sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of toroidal angular momentum density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of electrical current density generated by anomalous, turbulence-driven transport in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the anomalous current density is the projection of the full [current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) vector onto the geometric toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

$$
j_{\phi,\mathrm{anom}}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the anomalous current-density vector and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. This projection is distinct from the total [toroidal_current_density](name:toroidal_current_density) and from other components such as the [vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $j_{\phi,\mathrm{anom}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: Toroidal current density due to diamagnetic drift is the projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current density vector onto the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is driven by cross-field gradients of total plasma pressure relative to the magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal current density due to diamagnetic drift is the projection of the diamagnetic drift current density vector onto the toroidal unit direction $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Diamagnetic current is the pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular current produced in a magnetized plasma, so this component isolates the part of that current along the toroidal direction.

For scalar plasma pressure $p$, the toroidal component is defined by

$$
j_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}} = \left(\frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p}{B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the toroidal diamagnetic current density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B^2=\mathbf{B}\cdot\mathbf{B}$, $\nabla p$ is the plasma pressure gradient, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a coordinate projection of [current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), not a flux-surface-normal current or a field-aligned current. The matched projections in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame are [radial_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:radial_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [vertical_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift); the field-aligned component is [parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional positive charge flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the electric current density generated by heat-viscosity terms in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal heat-viscosity current density is the toroidal component of the electric-current contribution generated when heat-viscosity terms in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure drive net charge transport. It is the projection of [current density due to heat viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity) onto the geometric toroidal direction.

The component is defined by

$$
j_{\mathrm{hv},\phi}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}\cdot\hat{\phi}=\sum_s q_s n_s v_{s,\mathrm{hv},\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the heat-viscosity current-density vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$ in C, $n_s$ is its number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{s,\mathrm{hv},\phi}$ is its heat-viscosity-driven toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The projection is taken in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a geometric toroidal projection, distinct from the field-aligned [parallel heat-viscosity current density](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity) and the major-radius [radial heat-viscosity current density](name:radial_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity). It excludes current contributions attributed to other viscous or collisional mechanisms, such as the [toroidal current density due to parallel viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $j_{\mathrm{hv},\phi}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the electric current density arising from ion-fluid inertial acceleration, projected in the increasing-toroidal-angle direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal projection of the [current density due to ion inertia](name:current_density_due_to_ion_inertia) is the electric-current component generated by inertial acceleration terms in the ion-fluid momentum equation. It retains only the toroidal part of the polarization-type current.

The component is defined by

$$
J_{\phi,\mathrm{inertia}} = \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{inertia}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $J_{\phi,\mathrm{inertia}}$ is the toroidal current-density component, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{inertia}}$ is the parent ion-inertia current-density vector, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector. The projection uses the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is a projection of the parent vector, not its magnitude or total current density. It excludes the frictional contribution represented by [toroidal current density due to ion-neutral friction](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) and is distinct from the [radial current density due to ion inertia](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the inertial current-density projection points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the electric current density driven by frictional momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles in a partially ionized plasma.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal current density due to ion-neutral friction is the toroidal projection of the electric current density contribution produced by collisional momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral atoms or molecules. It is a signed component of the full [ion-neutral-friction current density](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) vector.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
j_{\mathrm{in},\phi} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the ion-neutral-friction current-density vector, $j_{\mathrm{in},\phi}$ is its toroidal component, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The toroidal projection is distinct from the [radial current density due to ion-neutral friction](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current-density contribution points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the current density generated when perpendicular viscous stress acts on the charged-particle fluid in a magnetized plasma.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the toroidal projection of the current-density contribution generated by the divergence of the perpendicular viscous stress tensor. It represents the part of the viscosity-driven current directed along the geometric toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
J_{\pi_\perp,\phi} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \mathbf{J}_{\pi_\perp} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B} \times (\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\pi}_\perp)}{B^2}
$$

Here $\mathbf{J}_{\pi_\perp}$ is the full current-density contribution, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $B = |\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_\perp$ is the perpendicular viscous stress tensor. This component is one projection of [current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), complementary to the [radial current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:radial_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $J_{\pi_\perp,\phi}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the effective deuterium–tritium fuel species evaluated at the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the bulk velocity assigned to deuterium–tritium fuel treated as one effective species at the radial location of the internal transport barrier. It describes collective fuel motion rather than the velocity of an individual isotope or charge state.

The component is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{DT}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the effective deuterium–tritium bulk velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [toroidal deuterium velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), this quantity represents the effective deuterium–tritium fuel species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $V_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Fictitious DT single species with mass 2.5, used in some simulations

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the effective deuterium–tritium fuel species evaluated at the magnetic axis.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of deuterium–tritium fuel treated as an effective single species at the magnetic axis, the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces. It represents collective fuel motion rather than speed or an isotope-specific velocity.

The effective velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,DT} = \frac{\rho_D v_{\phi,D} + \rho_T v_{\phi,T}}{\rho_D + \rho_T}
$$

where $\rho_D$ and $\rho_T$ are the deuterium and tritium mass densities, and $v_{\phi,D}$ and $v_{\phi,T}$ are their toroidal bulk-flow velocities in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The isotope-specific [toroidal tritium velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) is therefore not identical to this effective-species value. The quantity excludes poloidal and radial velocity components and differs from the corresponding fuel velocity at the [internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective deuterium–tritium bulk velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Signed deuterium-ion fluid velocity along the geometric toroidal direction, evaluated at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The deuterium-ion toroidal velocity is the projection of the deuterium-ion fluid velocity onto the geometric toroidal direction at the flux-surface radius assigned to the internal transport barrier. Neutral deuterium is excluded. It is the deuterium-specific counterpart of the [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the defining projection is

$$
v_{D,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_D \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_D$ is the deuterium-ion fluid velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and $v_{D,\phi}$ is evaluated at the internal-transport-barrier location.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the deuterium-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of deuterium ion bulk velocity at the magnetic axis, density-weighted over all deuterium ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The deuterium ion velocity at the magnetic axis is the density-weighted mean flow component along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It describes ion motion at the magnetic-axis location and excludes neutral deuterium.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{D}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})=\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{D},q}v_{\phi,\mathrm{D},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{D},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included deuterium ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{D},q}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{D},q}$ is its toroidal velocity component in m s$^{-1}$, and $(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})$ are the major-radius and vertical coordinates of the magnetic axis. The charge-state weighting distinguishes this species quantity from the all-ion [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), while the magnetic-axis locus distinguishes it from [toroidal deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the deuterium ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, namely $+\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Deuterium (D).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Deuterium (D)

NAMES.name: toroidal_electric_field
NAMES.short: Toroidal electric-field component giving the force per unit positive stationary test charge along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal electric field $E_\\phi$ is the electric-force component per unit positive stationary test charge obtained by projecting the local [electric field](name:electric_field) onto the geometric toroidal direction. It includes electrostatic, inductive, and electromagnetic-wave contributions, and is the toroidal counterpart of the [vertical electric field](name:vertical_electric_field).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined by

$$
E_\\phi = \\mathbf{E} \\cdot \\hat{\\phi} = -\\frac{1}{R}\\frac{\\partial \\Phi}{\\partial \\phi} - \\frac{\\partial A_\\phi}{\\partial t}
$$

where $\\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, $\\hat{\\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, $R$ is major radius, $\\Phi$ is electrostatic potential, $A_\\phi$ is the toroidal component of magnetic vector potential, and $t$ is time. The quantity is the geometric toroidal projection rather than a field-parallel or wave-only component; the wave-only counterpart is the [toroidal wave electric field](name:toroidal_wave_electric_field).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $E_\\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Toroidal electron velocity is the component of the electron-fluid bulk flow along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal electron velocity is the component of the electron fluid bulk flow along the local toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It represents advective electron motion, rather than random thermal motion or an individual-particle drift.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, this component is defined by the density-weighted first moment of the electron velocity distribution:

$$
u_{e,\phi}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{u}_e(\mathbf{x})\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}=\frac{1}{n_e(\mathbf{x})}\int [\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}]f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v,\qquad n_e(\mathbf{x})=\int f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{u}_e$ are velocities in m s$^{-1}$, $f_e$ is the electron velocity distribution, $n_e$ is electron number density in m$^{-3}$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector. This is a directional component of [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity); [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity) applies the same projection to ions, while [vertical electron velocity](name:vertical_electron_velocity) uses the vertical direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $u_{e,\phi}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volumetric toroidal torque density deposited in the fast-electron population through Coulomb collisions, the local rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit volume.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal fast-electron collisional torque density is the net rate at which Coulomb scattering transfers toroidal angular momentum per unit volume to the suprathermal electron population. It is the toroidal specialization of [fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

With respect to the toroidal symmetry axis, it is defined from the toroidal collisional force density by

$$
\tau_{\phi,e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}} = R f_{\phi,e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal fast-electron collisional torque density in N m$^{-2}$, $R$ is major radius in m in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $f_{\phi,e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force-density projection on fast electrons in N m$^{-3}$ along $\hat{\phi}$. In this frame, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$ and $Z$ is vertical height.

This density excludes the bulk thermal-electron contribution represented by [thermal-electron torque density due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and is distinct from the volume-integrated [toroidal fast-electron torque due to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions). Orbit-resolved toroidal components distinguish [toroidal co-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), [toroidal counter-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and [toroidal trapped fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional force density on fast electrons has a positive $\hat{\phi}$ projection, i.e. when the angular-momentum transfer is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated toroidal torque transferred to the fast (non-thermal) electron population through Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma.
NAMES.long:
This quantity represents the total toroidal angular momentum per unit time exchanged between the fast (non-thermal) electron population and the thermal plasma constituents via Coulomb collisions, integrated over the entire plasma volume. It measures the net collisional momentum transfer that modifies the toroidal rotation of the fast-electron distribution function.

The volume-integrated toroidal torque is obtained from the angular-momentum moment of the Coulomb collision operator acting on the fast electron distribution:

$$
T_\phi = \int m_e R \, v_\phi \, C[f_{\rm fast}] \, d^3v \, dV
$$

where $m_e$ is the electron mass, $R$ is the major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component, $C$ is the Coulomb collision operator acting on the fast electron distribution function $f_{\rm fast}$, and the integral is taken over both velocity space $d^3v$ and the plasma volume $dV$.

This quantity is evaluated from kinetic modeling of the fast electron distribution function using Fokker-Planck or bounce-averaged solvers. The complementary torque on the thermal electron sub-population is given by [toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions), while [toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions) aggregates collisional torque over all fast particle species. The orbit-resolved local torque density for co-passing fast electrons is available as [toroidal_co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net toroidal torque on fast electrons is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Collisional toroidal angular-momentum source density transferred to fast ions in a specified charge state, summed over all fast-ion orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
The collisional toroidal torque density for fast ions in charge state $q$ quantifies the angular-momentum source per unit volume arising from Coulomb collisions with background plasma particles. It is the toroidal projection of the vector quantity [fast-ion charge-state collisional torque density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

The defining projection is

$$
\tau_{\phi,q}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}_{q}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\cdot\left(\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{f}_{q}^{\mathrm{coll}}\right)
$$

where $q$ labels the specified ionic charge state, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, and $\mathbf{f}_{q}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the total collisional force-density vector transferred to that fast-ion population.

The quantity sums co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit contributions rather than resolving them separately; its orbit-specific components include [toroidal co-passing fast-ion charge-state torque density](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [toroidal counter-passing fast-ion charge-state torque density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the torque vector points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque on fast ions in a selected charge state, equal to the net angular momentum transfer rate about the machine symmetry axis from background plasma species.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal scalar component of the volume-integrated torque vector exerted by Coulomb collisions on fast (suprathermal) ions in a single specified charge state. It represents the net angular momentum transfer rate about the machine toroidal symmetry axis from background plasma species to this charge-state-resolved energetic ion population.

$$
\tau_\phi = \boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll}$ is the charge-state-resolved fast-ion collisional torque vector fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity covers only the suprathermal ion population in one charge state; the thermal-ion charge-state analog is [thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), the total charge-state collisional torque summed over all species is [total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), and the fast-ion toroidal torque summed over all charge states is [toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional angular momentum transfer is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Collisional toroidal torque density for fast ions is the local rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume caused by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.
NAMES.long:
Collisional toroidal torque density for fast ions is the local source density of toroidal angular momentum transferred to or from the fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions. It resolves the collisional torque along the toroidal direction rather than representing the full torque-density vector.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector for fast ions and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The projection is taken in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity aggregates the included fast-ion orbit classes and background collision partners, corresponding to [fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Orbit-resolved quantities such as [toroidal co-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) isolate individual contributions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when collisions increase fast-ion toroidal angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated toroidal angular-momentum transfer to fast particles from the Lorentz force associated with their radial current.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total toroidal torque transferred to the fast-particle population by the electromagnetic force associated with its radial current, integrated over the plasma volume.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$, the radial-current contribution is defined by

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi}=\int_V -R\,j_{R}^{\mathrm{fast}} B_Z\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi}$ is the toroidal torque, $R$ is major radius, $j_{R}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the radial current density carried by fast particles, $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, and $V$ is the plasma volume. Equivalently, the integrand is $R(\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{fast}}\times\mathbf{B})_\phi$ when restricted to the radial-current contribution.

This is a volume-integrated quantity and is distinct from the local [toroidal torque density due to the j-cross-B force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and from collisional torque transfer to fast particles [toroidal fast torque due to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the resulting torque points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Toroidal fast-particle torque due to collisions is the volume-integrated toroidal torque exerted on the fast, non-thermal particle population by Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma. The aggregate includes thermal electrons and all thermal ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal fast-particle torque due to collisions is the volume-integrated toroidal torque exerted on the fast, non-thermal particle population by Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma. It is the component of collisional angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry axis associated with increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The aggregate torque is defined as the plasma-volume integral of the toroidal collisional force density weighted by the major radius:

$$
T_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V R \sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}} f_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}\leftarrow j}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $T_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal fast-particle torque due to collisions, $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a differential volume element, $\mathcal{B}$ is the set of thermal-background collision partners, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}\leftarrow j}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal component of the collisional force density exerted on fast, non-thermal particles by partner $j$.

The set $\mathcal{B}$ contains thermal electrons and every thermal ion species and every charge state of each thermal ion species; the ion part is charge-state-summed. This quantity is the aggregate over those collision partners, not an electron-only or charge-state-resolved contribution; the [thermal-electron collision contribution](name:toroidal_fast_electron_torque_due_to_collisions) and the [thermal-ion charge-state collision contribution](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions) sum to it when defined over the same volume and fast-particle population. The equal-and-opposite collisional angular-momentum transfer to the thermal background is represented by the [thermal-electron](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions) and [thermal-ion](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions) reaction channels.
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb collisions exert a net toroidal force on fast, non-thermal particles in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.short: Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle-state toroidal momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction unchanged. Toroidal denotes the φ component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive closures for a neutral-particle state can produce toroidal momentum-flux densities that exceed the physically realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient regions. A toroidal flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_\phi$ scales that collisionless free-streaming bound for the $\phi$ component of neutral-particle-state momentum-flux density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

A direction-preserving limited toroidal momentum-flux density can be expressed by the harmonic-mean limiter form:

$$
\Pi_\phi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_\phi \, \Pi_\phi^{\mathrm{FS}} \, \Pi_\phi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{\left|\Pi_\phi^{\mathrm{diff}}\right| + \alpha_\phi \, \Pi_\phi^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_\phi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited toroidal momentum-flux density, $\Pi_\phi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the unconstrained diffusive toroidal momentum-flux density for the neutral-particle state, $\Pi_\phi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude, and $\alpha_\phi$ is the toroidal [flux limiter coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient). The coefficient acts as a multiplicative cap on the free-streaming bound; its limiting range is typically $0 \le \alpha_\phi \le 1$, with smaller values imposing a stricter cap.

This quantity is specific to the toroidal $\phi$ component of neutral-particle-state momentum-flux density. It is distinct from the [radial flux limiter coefficient](name:radial_flux_limiter_coefficient) for the $R$ component and from the [poloidal flux limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient); it is also a component-specific child of the broader [momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

NAMES.name: toroidal_gyrocenter_frequency
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the gyrocenter orbit angular frequency, equal to the signed rate of gyrocenter advance in toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal gyrocenter frequency is the toroidal component of gyrocenter orbit angular frequency in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It describes the angular advance of a charged-particle gyrocenter after averaging over its fast cyclotron gyration.

$$
\omega_{\phi,\mathrm{gc}} = \dot{\phi}_{\mathrm{gc}} = \frac{d\phi_{\mathrm{gc}}}{dt}
$$

where $\omega_{\phi,\mathrm{gc}}$ is the toroidal gyrocenter frequency, $\phi_{\mathrm{gc}}$ is the gyrocenter toroidal angle, and $t$ is time. Passing orbits contribute toroidal transit motion, whereas trapped orbits can contribute toroidal precession. This component complements the [poloidal gyrocenter frequency](name:poloidal_gyrocenter_frequency) and belongs to the angular-frequency vector [gyrocenter_frequency](name:gyrocenter_frequency); unlike [toroidal ion rotation frequency](name:toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency), it describes individual gyrocenter orbit motion rather than bulk species rotation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal component of the helium-3 ion fluid velocity evaluated at the radial location identified with the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The helium-3 ion velocity at the internal transport barrier is the density-weighted mean fluid velocity of the helium-3 ion charge states, excluding neutral helium-3. It is evaluated at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier and is not a flux-surface average unless separately specified.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component, $\mathbf{v}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion fluid velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The corresponding species comparison at the same locus is [toroidal deuterium velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), while evaluation at another characteristic location is given by [toroidal helium-3 velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-3 ion velocity has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal bulk-flow velocity of helium-3 ions evaluated at the magnetic axis and projected along the direction of increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local bulk-flow component of the helium-3 ion population at the magnetic axis, rather than the individual thermal speed or the full velocity vector.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, its density-weighted charge-state average is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,3\mathrm{He}}=\left[\frac{\sum_q n_{3\mathrm{He},q}\,\mathbf{v}_{3\mathrm{He},q}}{\sum_q n_{3\mathrm{He},q}}\right]_{\mathrm{axis}}\!\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $q$ indexes helium-3 ionic charge states, $n_{3\mathrm{He},q}$ is the corresponding ion number density, $\mathbf{v}_{3\mathrm{He},q}$ is its fluid velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. Neutral helium-3 is excluded. The species-specific quantity complements the all-ion [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), while [toroidal helium-3 velocity at pedestal top](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top) uses a different radial locus.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-3 ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Helium isotope with 3 nucleons (3He).

NAMES.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk velocity of helium-4 ions, evaluated on the flux surface identified with the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal helium-4 velocity is the density-weighted bulk-flow component of helium-4 ions, evaluated on the flux surface identified with the internal transport barrier. It includes helium-4 ions across their ionization charge states and excludes neutral helium-4.

$$
v_{\phi,4}=\frac{\sum_z n_{4,z}v_{\phi,4,z}}{\sum_z n_{4,z}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,4}$ is the charge-state-averaged helium-4 toroidal velocity, $n_{4,z}$ is the helium-4 ion number density in charge state $z$, and $v_{\phi,4,z}$ is that charge state's toroidal velocity in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The toroidal component is projected along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ and is distinct from the flux-surface-averaged quantity at the plasma boundary and from the analogous [toroidal helium-3 velocity](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the helium-4 ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of hydrogen ions evaluated at the radial location identified with the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion bulk flow projected onto the toroidal direction at the radial location of the internal transport barrier. It describes directed ion motion and excludes neutral-hydrogen motion.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity is evaluated on the flux-surface radius assigned to the internal transport barrier and is the hydrogen counterpart of [toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the hydrogen-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen (H)

NAMES.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal component of hydrogen-ion bulk velocity, averaged over ionization states at the magnetic axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity component in the toroidal direction at the magnetic axis. It includes the hydrogen ion population across its ionization states and excludes neutral hydrogen.

At the magnetic axis, the charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}} V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes hydrogen ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The magnetic axis is the location where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux vanishes. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The same hydrogen-ion quantity at other loci is given by [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). Species-specific counterparts include [toroidal deuterium velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal helium-3 velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the hydrogen-ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the effective convection velocity governing non-diffusive transport of the momentum density of an ion species in a specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion charge-state momentum convection velocity is the $\phi$-component of the effective velocity vector $\mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ appearing in the non-diffusive term of the charge-state-resolved fluid momentum transport equation for ion charge state $s$:

$$
v_{c,\phi}^{(s)} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and $\mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ is the effective momentum convection velocity vector for charge state $s$.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and is distinct from [toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity), which provides the corresponding quantity aggregated over all charge states of a species. It is one projection component of the [ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) vector family. As a transport coefficient in a convection-diffusion closure, it is not in general equal to the mean toroidal fluid velocity of the charge state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_{c,\phi}^{(s)}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical damping of the toroidal fluid-momentum component of a specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation time at which the toroidal component of ordered fluid momentum of a specified ion charge state is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. It isolates the toroidal projection of the direction-dependent damping represented by the [ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).

For toroidal fluid momentum density $p_{\phi,s}$, the dissipative evolution is defined by:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial p_{\phi,s}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{\phi,s} p_{\phi,s}
$$

where $t$ is time, $p_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal fluid momentum density of charge state $s$, the subscript $\phi$ denotes the toroidal component, and $\nu_{\phi,s}$ is the corresponding damping rate.

This quantity remains resolved for one ion charge state and is distinct from the charge-state-aggregated [ion momentum damping rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate). Its toroidal projection complements the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) and [radial ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the kinematic coefficient for down-gradient cross-flux-surface transport of toroidal momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the kinematic transport coefficient governing diffusive cross-flux-surface transport of toroidal momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the toroidal component lies along $\hat{\phi}$.

The diffusive flux of toroidal momentum through a flux surface is defined by

$$
\Pi_{s,\perp\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_s n_s \chi_{s,\phi}\frac{\partial v_{s,\phi}}{\partial x_\perp}
$$

where $\Pi_{s,\perp\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the flux-surface-normal flux of toroidal momentum, $m_s$ is the ion mass in kg, $n_s$ is the number density in m$^{-3}$, $v_{s,\phi}$ is the toroidal flow velocity in m s$^{-1}$, $x_\perp$ is distance normal to the flux surfaces in m, and $\chi_{s,\phi}$ is this diffusivity in m$^2$ s$^{-1}$. The coordinate $x_\perp$ increases toward increasing flux label.

This coefficient is resolved for one ionization state and is not summed over charge states. Toroidal identifies the transported momentum component, not the direction of the flux. It is a directional member of [ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity); [radial ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) resolves the radial momentum component, while [toroidal ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) describes the corresponding bulk-ion quantity.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal ion charge-state momentum flux is the toroidal component of the linear-momentum transport rate per unit area for ions of an ion species in a specified charge state. It is projected along increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal ion charge-state momentum flux is the toroidal component of the charge-state-resolved ion linear-momentum flux for ions of species $a$ in charge state $q$. It is the projection along $\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The toroidal projection is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{a q}^{\phi} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a q}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a q}$ is the vector flux density of linear momentum for ion species $a$ in charge state $q$, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $\Gamma_{a q}^{\phi}$ is the scalar toroidal component. Constitutive decompositions of $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a q}$ may include convective and non-convective stress contributions, but those closure-dependent terms do not change the definition of this component.

This quantity is charge-state resolved, not summed over ionization states. Summing compatible charge-state components over $q$ gives the species-level [toroidal_ion_momentum_flux](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_flux); other directional projections are [radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), [poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), and [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux). Associated transport coefficients, such as [toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) and [toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity), are distinct from the flux itself.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the momentum flux has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular rotation rate of a specified ion charge state, obtained from its toroidal bulk velocity and local major radius.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal angular rotation frequency of one specified ion charge state, rather than a density-weighted average over the ion species' charge states. It is the toroidal component of the charge-state-resolved rotation represented by [ion charge-state rotation frequency](name:ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency).

At a position with major radius $R$, the frequency is defined by

$$
\omega_{\phi,i,q} = \frac{v_{\phi,i,q}}{R}
$$

where $\omega_{\phi,i,q}$ is the toroidal angular rotation frequency, $v_{\phi,i,q}$ is the toroidal component of the bulk velocity of ion species $i$ in charge state $q$, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$. It is the charge-state-resolved counterpart of [toroidal ion rotation frequency](name:toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency), which averages over charge states.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_{\phi,i,q}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the net angular-momentum source density acting on a specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the net torque density acting on a specified ion species in a specified charge state. It represents the local source or sink of toroidal angular momentum, without attribution to a particular transport or collisional mechanism.

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{i,q}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{i,q}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q}$ is the full torque-density vector for ion species $i$ and charge state $q$. The vector parent is [ion charge state torque density](name:ion_charge_state_torque_density).

The quantity is a total over all contributing processes for the specified ion charge state; process-resolved contributions are distinct quantities.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the torque-density vector has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the diamagnetic drift velocity of a specified ion charge state, driven by that state's partial pressure gradient crossed with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the diamagnetic drift velocity for a specified ion charge state is its projection onto the toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

The full diamagnetic drift velocity for ion charge state $s$ is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} = -\frac{\nabla p_s \times \mathbf{B}}{q_s n_s B^2}
$$

where $p_s$ is the partial pressure of charge state $s$, $q_s = Z_s e$ is its electric charge with $Z_s$ the charge number and $e$ the elementary charge, $n_s$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field with magnitude $B$. The toroidal component is $v_{\mathrm{dia},s,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} \cdot \hat{\phi}$.

This is one cylindrical-frame projection of the full ion-charge-state diamagnetic drift velocity; the complementary cylindrical projections are [radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and the field-aligned projection is [parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal diamagnetic drift points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective toroidal convection velocity that advects a chosen component of ion momentum density for a specified ion species, represented as the density-weighted mean over all charge states. The toroidal label names the velocity projection along increasing φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, not the transported momentum component.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion momentum convection velocity is the toroidal effective velocity that advects a chosen component of ion momentum density for a specified ion species. The toroidal direction is the $\phi$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Because this is an intensive coefficient for a species-level quantity, it is represented as the density-weighted mean over all charge states of that species unless a charge-state-resolved quantity is named.

For an ion-momentum component or projection labeled $a$, the toroidal convective contribution to its flux is

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,a},\phi} = p_{i,a}\,V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{i,M,\phi}
$$

where $p_{i,a}$ is the ion momentum density of the selected species for component or projection $a$, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,a},\phi}$ is the $\phi$ component of the non-diffusive convective flux of that momentum density, and $V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{i,M,\phi}$ is this toroidal ion momentum convection velocity. For charge-state index $c$, $V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{i,M,\phi}$ is the density-weighted mean of $V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{i,c,M,\phi}$ over $c$, with weights given by the corresponding charge-state number densities.

The parent [ion momentum convection velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity) denotes the same closure concept without selecting the $\phi$ projection. [Toroidal ion charge state momentum convection velocity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) is the corresponding coefficient for one ion species in one ionization state. This quantity is not the [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity) and is not a flux-surface-normal convection velocity for toroidal momentum; the word toroidal identifies the coefficient projection, not the momentum component being transported.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{i,M,\phi}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical dissipation of the toroidal component of bulk ion fluid momentum along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation timescale at which the toroidal component of ordered bulk ion fluid momentum is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses. It is the toroidal projection of the effective momentum-loss response in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

In the ion fluid momentum balance, its damping contribution is defined by:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial p_{i,\phi}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}}=-\nu_{D,\phi}^{i}p_{i,\phi}
$$

where $t$ is time, $p_{i,\phi}$ is the toroidal component of ordered bulk ion momentum density, and $\nu_{D,\phi}^{i}$ is this damping rate, aggregated over ion species and charge states.

The projection follows $\hat{\phi}$ toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$; $(R,\phi,Z)$ is the right-handed cylindrical frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height. This component belongs to [ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate) and is distinct from the field-aligned [parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate) and the charge-state-resolved [toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the rate coefficient reduces the toroidal ion momentum component, producing exponential relaxation toward zero.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal ion momentum flux is the flux-surface-normal rate of toroidal linear-momentum transport per unit area for all ion species and charge states in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal ion momentum flux is the flux-surface-normal transport rate per unit area of the toroidal component of linear momentum for the total ion population, summed over all ion species and charge states. It is the toroidal projection of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), including convective and stress contributions.

The resolved tensor component is:

$$
\Pi_{\rho\phi} = \hat{\mathbf n}_{\rho} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{ion}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the total ion momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{\mathbf n}_{\rho}$ is the outward unit normal to the magnetic flux surface labeled by the outward-increasing flux label $\rho$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The transported momentum component is toroidal; the transport direction is flux-surface-normal. Unlike [toroidal ion charge-state momentum flux](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), this quantity is aggregated over all ion charge states.
NAMES.sign: Positive when toroidal momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ is transported toward increasing $\rho$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_source
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal ion momentum source is the net force-per-area source for the total ion population, summed over all ion charge states and projected onto increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal ion momentum source is the net source that adds or removes momentum from the total ion population through its toroidal component. Its value is summed over all ion charge states and represents force per unit area, not a volumetric force density.

The toroidal component is defined by:

$$
S_\phi = \mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $S_\phi$ is the toroidal ion momentum source, $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the net [ion momentum source](name:ion_momentum_source) vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame uses $R$ for major radius, $\phi$ for toroidal angle, and $Z$ for vertical height.

The toroidal direction is the geometric toroidal direction, not the poloidal or magnetic-field-parallel direction. This quantity is summed over all ion charge states, unlike the charge-state-resolved [toroidal ion charge-state momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), and it is the $\phi$ projection corresponding to the radial projection in [radial ion momentum source](name:radial_ion_momentum_source).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net momentum source points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular rate of an ion species’ bulk rotational motion, density-weighted over all ionic charge states and distinct from gyrocenter orbit motion.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion rotation frequency is the angular rate of an ion species’ charge-state-averaged bulk rotational motion about the toroidal symmetry axis. It is the toroidal component of [ion rotation frequency](name:ion_rotation_frequency).

The frequency is defined from the toroidal bulk velocity as

$$
\Omega_{\phi,i} = \frac{V_{\phi,i}}{R}
$$

where $\Omega_{\phi,i}$ is the toroidal ion rotation frequency, $V_{\phi,i}$ is the toroidal component of the species’ charge-state-averaged bulk velocity, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The average is density-weighted over all ionic charge states.

This quantity describes fluid rotational motion rather than charged-particle gyrocenter orbit motion. It is distinct from the charge-state-resolved [toroidal ion charge-state rotation frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal bulk velocity points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_torque
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated source of ion angular momentum about the toroidal symmetry axis, obtained as the toroidal component of total ion torque summed over charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal ion torque is the net rate at which explicit momentum sources change the toroidal angular momentum of the total ion population. It is the toroidal component of [ion torque](name:ion_torque), with contributions summed over all ion species and charge states.

The defining volume integral is

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{ion}} = \int_V R\,\mathcal{S}_{\phi,\mathrm{ion}}\,dV
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{ion}}$ is the toroidal ion torque, $R$ is major radius in m, $\mathcal{S}_{\phi,\mathrm{ion}}$ is the toroidal component of the explicit ion momentum-source density in kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-2}$, $dV$ is a volume element in m$^3$, and $V$ is the plasma volume in m$^3$. The quantity is the volume-integrated counterpart of local torque densities such as [toroidal ion charge-state torque density](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density) and excludes momentum transport unless represented as an explicit source.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the explicit sources increase ion angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_torque_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local toroidal torque density on all ion species and charge states, giving the external source rate of ion angular momentum about the symmetry axis with its major-radius moment arm.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion torque density is the local rate at which external processes change the angular momentum of the combined ion population about the symmetry axis. It is the toroidal component of the parent [ion torque density](name:ion_torque_density), summed over ion species and charge states; internal ion–ion exchanges cancel in this aggregate.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, it is defined from the net external ion force density by

$$
\tau_{\phi,i} = R f_{\phi,i} = R\,\mathbf{f}_i \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,i}$ is the toroidal ion torque density, $R$ is major radius in m, $\mathbf{f}_i$ is the external force density on the combined ion population in N m$^{-3}$, $f_{\phi,i}$ is its toroidal component, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. Unlike the broader [toroidal torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density), this quantity is restricted to the ion population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the external torque increases ion angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Charge-state-averaged toroidal component of the ion bulk-flow velocity, obtained from the density-weighted first velocity moment and directed along the toroidal unit vector.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion velocity represents the toroidal component of the charge-state-averaged ion bulk flow in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$. It is a geometric component of the full [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity).

The component is defined by

$$
v_{i,\phi}=\mathbf{V}_i\cdot\hat{\phi}=\frac{\sum_q n_{i,q}v_{i,q,\phi}}{\sum_q n_{i,q}}
$$

where $v_{i,\phi}$ and $v_{i,q,\phi}$ are toroidal velocities in m s$^{-1}$, $\mathbf{V}_i$ is the charge-state-averaged ion velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $n_{i,q}$ is the ion number density in charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and $q$ indexes ionization charge states. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The average includes all included ionization charge states rather than one selected state. The [radial ion velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity) is another geometric component of the same charge-state-averaged flow.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Density-weighted iron-ion bulk-flow velocity along increasing toroidal angle, averaged over all ionization charge states at the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the bulk velocity of ionized iron at the flux-surface locus of the internal transport barrier. It is a density-weighted mean across iron ionization charge states in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ is the ionization charge number, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the number density of iron ions in state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is that state's toroidal bulk-flow component in m.s$^{-1}$. Neutral iron is excluded from the sum.

The internal-transport-barrier value is distinct from the corresponding values at the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [pedestal top](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top), which use different flux-surface loci.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the iron-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Iron (Fe).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Iron (Fe)

NAMES.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron at the magnetic axis, directed along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the charge-state-aggregated toroidal bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the number-density-weighted mean of the iron-ion fluid velocities, excluding neutral iron.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}}(\mathrm{axis}) = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})\,v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}(\mathrm{axis})}
$$

Here $q$ indexes the included positive iron-ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding ion number density, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; the velocity is in m s$^{-1}$ and the density is in m$^{-3}$. The weighting is over charge states, so this is an intensive mean rather than a sum of velocities. It is the magnetic-axis counterpart of [toroidal iron velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and follows the same aggregation principle as [toroidal deuterium velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the iron bulk flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of krypton ions, averaged over charge states at the radial location of an internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the krypton-ion bulk flow evaluated at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier. It includes ionic krypton charge states and excludes neutral krypton.

$$
v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr}} = \\frac{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr},q}}{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ionization states, $n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}$ is the number density of ions in state $q$, and $v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr},q}$ is their toroidal bulk-flow component. The result is the density-weighted mean over all included krypton ionization states, analogous to the corresponding [toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal krypton velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

The toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame, where $\\phi$ increases in the toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the krypton-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Toroidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis, defined as the density-weighted mean over all krypton ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of the krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis is the charge-state-aggregated krypton velocity projected along $\hat{\phi}$. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and the magnetic axis is the innermost closed-flux-surface locus where the gradient of [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) vanishes.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal velocity at this locus is defined by projecting the density-weighted krypton velocity onto the toroidal unit vector:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr},0} =
\left.
\left(
\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}
\right)
\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ionization charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, and the subscript $0$ denotes evaluation at the magnetic axis.

This is an intensive species velocity: krypton charge-state velocities are combined as a density-weighted mean over all ionization states, not as a sum. It is distinct from [flux-surface-averaged toroidal krypton velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_krypton_velocity_at_plasma_boundary) and from local toroidal krypton velocities at the [internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and [pedestal top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the krypton velocity component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal lithium velocity at an internal transport barrier is the signed toroidal component of the lithium ion fluid velocity, evaluated at the barrier flux-surface location. It is the density-weighted mean over Li+ through Li3+ and is positive along increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Density-weighted toroidal lithium velocity at an internal transport barrier is the signed toroidal component of the lithium ion fluid velocity evaluated at the flux-surface location of that barrier. It is an intensive species-level velocity, formed as the density-weighted mean over the lithium ion charge states Li$^{+}$ through Li$^{3+}$.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{ITB}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the density-weighted toroidal lithium velocity at the internal transport barrier, $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the number density of lithium charge state $q+$ at that location, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}^{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the fluid velocity of that charge state at that location, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Neutral lithium atoms are excluded from the aggregation. The value is not a flux-surface average unless explicitly identified as such by a separate quantity, and it is undefined where the summed lithium ion density in the denominator is zero.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted lithium ion velocity has a positive projection on $\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
