NAMES.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal fluid velocity of lithium impurity ions at the magnetic axis, taken as the density-weighted mean over lithium ion charge states Li+, Li2+, and Li3+. Neutral lithium is excluded.
NAMES.long:
Density-weighted toroidal fluid velocity of lithium impurity ions at the magnetic axis is the local toroidal component of the lithium impurity-ion fluid velocity at the magnetic axis. The magnetic axis is the innermost flux-surface locus where the poloidal magnetic flux has an extremum. Because this is an intensive species-level quantity, the charge-state aggregation is the density-weighted mean over lithium ion charge states $\mathrm{Li}^{+}$, $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$, and $\mathrm{Li}^{3+}$; neutral lithium is excluded.

The density-weighted toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the lithium ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is its fluid velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height.

This is a local on-axis value, not a flux-surface average or a boundary value. The analogous local lithium-ion quantities include [toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and [toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted lithium-ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_mhd_mode_number
NAMES.short: Dimensionless integer Fourier harmonic specifying how a linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation varies over one complete toroidal circuit.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal mode number is the integer Fourier harmonic that characterizes the toroidal periodicity of a linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a single toroidal harmonic, the perturbation varies as

$$
\delta X(\phi) = \widetilde{X}_{n_\phi}\exp(i n_\phi \phi)
$$

where $\delta X$ is the perturbed physical quantity, $\widetilde{X}_{n_\phi}$ is its complex Fourier amplitude, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal mode number, and $\phi$ is measured in radians. Periodicity after one toroidal circuit requires $n_\phi$ to be an integer.

The value $n_\phi=0$ denotes an axisymmetric perturbation; nonzero values denote non-axisymmetric structure. It is distinct from the [poloidal mode number](name:poloidal_mode_number), while the radial, poloidal, and toroidal indices together specify the modal branch represented by [mode number](name:mode_number).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the Fourier phase advances as the toroidal angle $\phi$ increases.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of neon ions, averaged over ionic charge states and evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
The neon-ion toroidal velocity is the density-weighted mean flow of all neon ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier; neutral neon is excluded.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included neon ionic charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is its flow-velocity component along the geometric toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This quantity is the toroidal counterpart of the radial-location-specific [toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and uses the same charge-state aggregation convention as the analogous [toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neon-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Neon (Ne)

NAMES.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of neon ions at the magnetic axis, averaged over all neon ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the neon impurity-ion bulk velocity evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the density-weighted mean over all neon ionization states and excludes neutral neon.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}}=\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the charge-state-aggregated neon-ion bulk velocity and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The magnetic axis is the point inside the confined plasma where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes, $\nabla\psi=0$. The analogous quantity at the plasma boundary is [toroidal neon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neon-ion bulk flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the signed transport rate of toroidal linear momentum carried by neutral particles in one specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the toroidal transport component of linear momentum carried by neutral particles restricted to one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It is a momentum-flux tensor component, not a particle flux or a local momentum source.

For the state-resolved neutral distribution, the toroidal component is defined by

$$
\Pi_{\phi\phi}^{(s)} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{\phi} = \int m_s v_\phi^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is its momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component, and $f_s$ is the state-resolved velocity distribution.

The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\phi$ increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$. This component is the toroidal member of the parent [neutral internal-state momentum flux] and differs from the cylindrical-radial [radial neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), the vertical [vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and the field-parallel [parallel neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when toroidal linear momentum is transported in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal flux-limiter coefficient that sets an edge-region, nonnegative cap on the toroidal component of neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a specified internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming bound, without reversing the signed component.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles occupying a specified internal state over the edge region is the directional coefficient used to bound the toroidal component of the corresponding neutral internal-state momentum-flux density. The internal state may be an electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation state, and the toroidal component is the projection along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the toroidal direction, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\phi}| \le \alpha_{\phi}\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\phi}|,\qquad 0 \le \alpha_{\phi} \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\phi}$ is the limited toroidal component of the neutral internal-state momentum flux over the edge region, $\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\phi}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming toroidal component whose magnitude defines the bound, and $\alpha_{\phi}$ is this toroidal limiter coefficient.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the realized momentum flux. Because $\alpha_{\phi}$ is nonnegative, applying the limiter may reduce or bound a signed toroidal momentum-flux component but does not reverse its direction; a nonzero limited component retains the sign of the underlying toroidal component. This scalar coefficient is the toroidal member of the [neutral internal-state momentum-flux limiter coefficient over the edge region](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region), is distinct from the [toroidal neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and is in the same directional family as the [parallel neutral internal-state momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and the [poloidal momentum neutral internal-state flux-limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_momentum_neutral_internal_state_flux_limiter_coefficient).

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_torque_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the angular-momentum source density transferred to the plasma by neutral particles in a specified internal state.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the torque density transferred to the plasma by neutral particles occupying a specified internal state. It is the state-resolved toroidal projection of [neutral internal-state torque density], rather than a sum over all neutral internal states.

$$
\tau_{\phi,s}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\left(\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{f}_s\right)
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the machine symmetry axis, and $\mathbf{f}_s$ is the force density exerted on the plasma by neutrals in internal state $s$.

Summing this state-resolved quantity over all neutral internal states gives [toroidal neutral torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density); it is distinct from the direction-independent [neutral torque density](name:neutral_torque_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the torque points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the effective E cross B drift velocity assigned to a neutral species in a specified internal state, projected along the direction of increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the [effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the projection of the E×B drift vector onto the toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
v_{\phi,E\times B} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}}{B^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $B = |\mathbf{B}|$.

Because neutral particles carry no net charge, they do not experience the Lorentz force directly; this effective drift velocity is assigned within fluid transport formalisms to represent the advection of neutral internal states by local electromagnetic fields. The [poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) provides the complementary poloidal projection of the same drift vector; the corresponding quantity for magnetized ions is [toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_{\phi,E\times B}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal neutral momentum convection velocity is the toroidal projection of the effective velocity that convects aggregate neutral momentum. The toroidal label denotes the velocity component along increasing toroidal angle, not the component of momentum being transported or a particular neutral particle flow.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral momentum convection velocity is the toroidal component of the effective velocity vector that advects neutral momentum in a transport closure for the aggregate neutral population. The toroidal component is the projection along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; toroidal modifies the velocity component, not the momentum component being transported. It is a convection coefficient and need not equal the [toroidal neutral velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity).

The projection defining this component is

$$
u_{\phi,\mathrm{mom}} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is the [neutral momentum convection velocity](name:neutral_momentum_convection_velocity), $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $u_{\phi,\mathrm{mom}}$ is this quantity.

The unqualified neutral population denotes an aggregate over neutral species and internal states; resolved counterparts keep those populations separate. This coefficient belongs to the convective part of the neutral momentum flux and excludes diffusive, viscous, source, sink, and residual terms; it is not the [toroidal neutral momentum flux] itself.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}}$ has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of toroidal momentum carried by one neutral species, aggregated over neutral states. Toroidal denotes the momentum component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, not velocity direction.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral species momentum convection velocity is the flux-surface-normal convection coefficient that multiplies the toroidal momentum density carried by neutrals of one chemical species. The toroidal momentum component is defined along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the coefficient itself is not a velocity directed along $\hat{\phi}$. It is the toroidal component of the [neutral species momentum convection velocity](name:neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity).

The defining relation preserves the total convective flux of toroidal momentum across a magnetic flux surface:

$$
\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = P_{\phi,a} V_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_{s \in a} P_{\phi,s} V_{\phi,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ denotes one neutral chemical species, $s$ runs over its resolved neutral states, $P_{\phi,s}$ and $P_{\phi,a}$ are signed toroidal momentum densities, $V_{\phi,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $V_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ are state-resolved and species-aggregated convection coefficients, and $\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum flux. The state sum excludes other chemical species; this is a local coefficient, not a flux-surface average. The one-species aggregation distinguishes it from the broader [toroidal neutral momentum convection velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $P_{\phi,a}$ have the same sign, with positive toroidal momentum directed toward increasing $\phi$ and positive flux-surface-normal transport directed toward increasing magnetic flux label.

NAMES.name: toroidal_neutral_torque_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the plasma angular-momentum source density produced by neutral–plasma momentum exchange, summed over all neutral internal states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal neutral torque density is the local source of plasma angular momentum about the machine symmetry axis produced by momentum exchange with neutral particles. It is aggregated over all neutral internal states and is distinct from the state-resolved quantity [toroidal neutral internal-state torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_torque_density).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, it is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,n}(R,\phi,Z) = R\sum_s \mathcal{R}_{\phi,n,s}(R,\phi,Z)
$$

where $R$ is major radius in m, $s$ indexes neutral internal states, and $\mathcal{R}_{\phi,n,s}$ is the toroidal component of the momentum-exchange force density from state $s$. The sum gives the neutral contribution to the parent [neutral torque density](name:neutral_torque_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral momentum exchange increases plasma angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Signed nitrogen-ion fluid velocity component along the geometric toroidal direction, evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed nitrogen-ion fluid velocity component along the geometric toroidal direction, evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport barrier.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{N}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the nitrogen-ion fluid velocity and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the geometric toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity represents directed nitrogen-ion flow at the barrier location, not the total speed or radial and poloidal velocity components. It follows the same component definition as [toroidal neon velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), with nitrogen as the species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the nitrogen-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

It is the density-weighted mean over all nitrogen ion charge states.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted nitrogen impurity-ion flow at the magnetic axis is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the oxygen ion bulk velocity, evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport barrier in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. For species-level oxygen, this is the density-weighted mean over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the oxygen ion bulk velocity at an internal transport barrier is the component of the oxygen bulk-flow velocity along the toroidal basis direction at the radial location of the internal transport barrier. The toroidal direction is $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For species-level oxygen, the velocity is the density-weighted mean over all oxygen charge states:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}}) = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})}
$$

where $r_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the radial location of the internal transport barrier, $q$ indexes oxygen charge states, $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is the number density of oxygen charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is its bulk velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle.

This quantity is a local toroidal component at the internal-transport-barrier locus, not a flux-surface average or a boundary value. Same-locus species counterparts include [toroidal carbon velocity at internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), [toroidal xenon velocity at internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), [toroidal nitrogen velocity at internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), and [toroidal deuterium velocity at internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier); the same-species boundary counterpart is [toroidal flux-surface-averaged oxygen velocity at plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted oxygen ion bulk flow is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal bulk velocity of oxygen ions at the magnetic axis, averaged over all oxygen ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the oxygen-ion bulk flow evaluated at the magnetic axis, with contributions from all oxygen ionization states combined as a density-weighted mean.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O},q} V_{\phi,\mathrm{O},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes oxygen ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{O},q}$ is the number density of state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{O},q}$ is its toroidal velocity component in m.s$^{-1}$. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The magnetic axis is the innermost confined-plasma location where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes. Neutral oxygen and other species are excluded. The corresponding boundary quantity is [toroidal oxygen velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted oxygen-ion bulk flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.short: Signed total linear momentum along increasing toroidal angle within a closed flux surface as it approaches the magnetic axis, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total toroidal linear momentum carried by electrons and all ion species within the volume enclosed by a closed magnetic flux surface as that surface approaches the magnetic axis. It is a linear-momentum projection, not toroidal angular momentum.

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\psi\to\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}} \int_{V(\psi)} \sum_s m_s n_s v_{s,\phi}\,dV
$$

Here $P_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the limiting toroidal momentum, $\psi$ is a flux-surface label, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its magnetic-axis value, $V(\psi)$ is the enclosed volume, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, $v_{s,\phi}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and $dV$ is the volume element. The sum includes electrons and ions and excludes neutral species. Its aggregation and projection match [toroidal total plasma momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum), while the corresponding boundary quantity is [toroidal total plasma momentum at plasma boundary](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net enclosed momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_rotation_frequency_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular frequency due to the E-cross-B drift is the species-independent electric-field cross magnetic-field contribution to toroidal motion, equal to its toroidal velocity component divided by local major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal angular frequency due to the E-cross-B drift is the toroidal angular frequency associated with the species-independent drift of a charged particle in crossed electric and magnetic fields. It denotes only the electric-field cross magnetic-field contribution to toroidal motion, not the total toroidal rotation of any species.

The quantity is defined from the drift velocity and the local major radius:

$$
\Omega_E = \frac{v_{E,\phi}}{R}, \qquad \mathbf{v}_E = \frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{B^2}
$$

where $\Omega_E$ is the toroidal angular frequency in inverse seconds, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is the electric-field cross magnetic-field drift velocity in meters per second, $v_{E,\phi}$ is its toroidal component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, $R$ is the local major radius in meters, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric field in volts per meter, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field in tesla, and $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude in tesla. The right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame uses $R$ as major radius, $\phi$ as toroidal angle, and $Z$ as vertical height.

The electric field entering the cross product may include the cylindrical radial component [radial_electric_field](name:radial_electric_field) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; this quantity is the resulting angular frequency, not an electric-field component. It is distinct from total toroidal rotation frequencies such as [toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency](name:toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency) and [toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency), and it excludes charge-state-dependent diamagnetic drift terms represented by quantities such as [toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_{E,\phi}$ is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Toroidal thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate to bulk thermal electrons from Coulomb collisions with fast particles.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local rate per unit volume at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum to the bulk, near-Maxwellian thermal electron population, resolved along the toroidal direction.

$$
\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

Here $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector deposited in thermal electrons, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector. The quantity is the toroidal projection of the [thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions); it excludes torque deposited in fast electrons and contributions from non-Coulomb processes. The [toroidal counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) resolves a specified fast-particle orbit channel.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transferred angular momentum has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the volume-integrated angular-momentum transfer to bulk thermal electrons through Coulomb collisions with other plasma species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the net torque transferred to the bulk thermal electron population by Coulomb collisions. It is the toroidal projection of the volume-integrated [thermal electron collisional torque](name:thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions), including contributions from all specified collisional partners and excluding noncollisional momentum transfer.

The volume-integrated torque is defined from the local [toroidal thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) by

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \tau_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}\,dV
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal collisional torque on thermal electrons, $\tau_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the corresponding local torque density, and $V$ is the integration volume. The toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when collisional angular momentum is transferred to the thermal electrons in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal collisional torque density is the toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge state from Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal collisional torque density is the toroidal component of the rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a specified charge state from Coulomb collisions.

With $\mathrm{coll}$ denoting the collision channel, the local toroidal torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = \left(\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{coll}}\right) \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal torque-density component, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the local plasma volume, $\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density exerted on the specified thermal ion charge state, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector. The charge-state selection is retained rather than summed over ionization states. This is the toroidal component of [thermal ion charge-state collisional torque density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions), distinct from the co-passing contribution [toroidal co-passing thermal-ion collisional torque density](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque on thermal ions of a selected charge state, giving the net rate of toroidal angular momentum transfer to that ion population by collisions.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal projection of the volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque vector [thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), restricted to thermal ions of a selected ionic charge state $Z$. It is defined as:

$$
\tau_\phi(Z) = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}(Z)
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}(Z)$ is the volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque vector for ions in charge state $Z$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector.

This scalar captures the net toroidal angular momentum deposited per unit time into the specified thermal ion charge state by all Coulomb-collisional partners, including fast particles, electrons, and background ion species. It is volume-integrated over the plasma, not a local density; the density-form analog for fast ions is [toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions). For the analogous thermal electron quantity see [toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net collisional angular momentum transfer to the ion charge state is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal ions through Coulomb collisions with other charged populations.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal ion population by Coulomb collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is resolved about the toroidal symmetry axis.

The toroidal torque density is related to the collisional force density by

$$
\tau_\phi = R\,\hat{\phi}\cdot\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_\phi$ is the toroidal torque density, $R$ is the major radius, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the force density transferred to thermal ions by collisions.

This quantity is the toroidal component of [thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), summed over the contributing collision channels and source-orbit classes. It is local and therefore distinct from the volume-integrated [toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions), and from the trapped-population component [toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional force transferred to thermal ions has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net torque about the toroidal symmetry axis transferred to thermal ions by collisional momentum exchange.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net toroidal angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population from colliding particle populations, integrated over the plasma volume. It represents torque about the toroidal symmetry axis rather than a local torque density.

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi,i}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V R\,\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},i}\cdot\hat{\phi}\,dV
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi,i}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the integrated collisional torque, $V$ is the plasma volume, $R$ is major radius in m, $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll},i}$ is the collisional force density on thermal ions in N m$^{-3}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$. The thermal-ion contribution is summed over all represented thermal-ion charge states; its local charge-state-resolved counterpart is [toroidal thermal-ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional force on thermal ions has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, producing positive angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: toroidal_torque_density
NAMES.short: Local toroidal torque density representing the signed source rate of plasma angular momentum about the symmetry axis per unit volume.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local source density of plasma angular momentum about the toroidal symmetry axis, with no restriction to a particular species, charge state, or orbit class.

$$
\tau_\phi(R,\phi,Z)=R f_\phi(R,\phi,Z),\qquad f_\phi=\mathbf{f}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

Here $\tau_\phi$ is the toroidal torque density, $R$ is major radius, $\mathbf{f}$ is the local force density, and $f_\phi$ is its component along the toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Species- or orbit-resolved contributions, such as [toroidal ion torque density](name:toroidal_ion_torque_density) and [toroidal counter-passing torque density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density), are more specific components of this aggregate quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the torque acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_runaway_electron_current
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Total toroidal electric current carried by runaway electrons, obtained by integrating their toroidal current-density component over a poloidal cross-section.
NAMES.long:
Total toroidal runaway-electron current is the net electric current contributed by the runaway-electron population through a poloidal cross-section. It is a global population contribution, distinct from the total plasma current and from local current density.

$$
I_{\mathrm{RE},\phi} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{pol}}} \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\,dS = \int_{S_{\mathrm{pol}}} j_{\mathrm{RE},\phi}\,dS
$$

Here $I_{\mathrm{RE},\phi}$ is the total current, $S_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is a poloidal cross-sectional surface, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the [runaway electron current density](name:runaway_electron_current_density) in A m$^{-2}$, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $dS$ is the surface element in m$^2$. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the runaway-electron current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Density-weighted mean toroidal fluid-velocity component of all tritium ion charge states at the internal transport barrier, directed along increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid-velocity component for all tritium ions at the internal transport barrier. It excludes neutral tritium and aggregates the ionic charge states.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{T}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T},q} v_{\phi,\mathrm{T},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T},q}}
$$

Here $q$ indexes tritium ionic charge states, $n_{\mathrm{T},q}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{T},q}$ is the toroidal fluid-velocity component in m s$^{-1}$. The denominator is the total tritium-ion density, related to [tritium density at the internal transport barrier](name:tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier). The internal transport barrier is the flux-surface location where cross-field transport is locally reduced and kinetic gradients are steep; this quantity is distinct from the corresponding value at the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the density-weighted tritium-ion velocity component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Tritium (T).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tritium (T)

NAMES.name: toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal fluid velocity of the tritium-ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis and resolved in the direction of increasing toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The tritium-ion toroidal velocity is the density-weighted fluid-velocity component of tritium ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes. It describes collective ion motion rather than thermal speed or individual-particle gyro-orbit velocity.

For all tritium ion charge states included in the species definition, the quantity is

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{T}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ is the ionic charge state, $n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}$ is its number density, $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}$ is its fluid velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The corresponding local tritium abundance is given by [tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tritium-ion velocity component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Density-weighted tungsten impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity along increasing toroidal angle, averaged over all ionization charge states at the internal transport barrier.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of the tungsten impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity at the internal transport barrier, with contributions from ionic charge states combined by density weighting.

The charge-state-averaged velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{W}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right)}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ is the tungsten ionic charge state, $n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its number density, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow velocity, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The sum includes all tungsten ionization charge states and excludes neutral tungsten. The corresponding [toroidal tungsten velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) differs only by its spatial locus, while [toroidal iron velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) illustrates the analogous charge-state-averaged quantity for another impurity species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tungsten-ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Tungsten (W).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the tungsten impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at the magnetic axis, the innermost point of the confined plasma where the poloidal magnetic flux gradient vanishes.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component of the tungsten impurity ion bulk flow velocity at the magnetic axis quantifies the net rotation of tungsten ions about the torus axis at the innermost flux surface, where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes ($\nabla\psi = 0$). This on-axis value anchors the full radial toroidal rotation profile and complements the edge measurement given by [toroidal tungsten velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

The toroidal fluid velocity is the first velocity moment of the tungsten ion distribution function $f_W$, summed over all ionization states and projected onto the toroidal direction $\hat{\phi}$:

$$
v_\phi^W = \frac{\int v_\phi \, f_W(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v}{\int f_W(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the individual particle velocity in the $\hat{\phi}$ direction.

Core tungsten rotation is driven by neutral beam injection torque, intrinsic rotation, and radial momentum transport; in H-mode plasmas, on-axis values range roughly $10^4$–$3\times10^5$ m s$^{-1}$, depending on beam torque and intrinsic rotation contributions. Measurement is performed via charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy of tungsten line emission. The analogous quantity for lighter impurity species is [toroidal nitrogen velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), and for the main ion species [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the tungsten ion flow is directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Tungsten (W)

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of xenon ions at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier, averaged over all xenon ionization states.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the toroidal direction at the flux-surface radius assigned to the internal transport barrier. It is averaged over xenon ionic charge states; neutral xenon is excluded.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}}=\frac{\sum_q n_q\left(\mathbf{v}_q\cdot\hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_q}
$$

where $q$ indexes xenon ionization states, $n_q$ is the number density of state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_q$ is its bulk velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical height. The corresponding xenon-ion quantities at the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [pedestal top](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_pedestal_top) use the same aggregation and projection at different radial locations.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the xenon-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Xenon (Xe).
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of xenon ions at the magnetic axis, averaged over all xenon ionization states and signed by the toroidal direction.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the density-weighted mean over all xenon ionization states; neutral xenon is excluded. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

At the magnetic axis, the charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included xenon ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density, $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the resulting mean. This quantity differs from [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), which is not restricted to xenon, and from [toroidal xenon velocity at internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), which is evaluated at another locus.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the xenon-ion flow component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Xenon (Xe)

NAMES.name: torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
NAMES.short: Local collisional transfer rate of angular momentum to a specified plasma population per unit volume, acting as a signed source or sink.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density is the local rate at which collisions transfer angular momentum to or from a specified plasma population per unit volume. It acts as a source or sink in that population’s angular-momentum balance.

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathcal{L}}{\mathrm{d}t\,\mathrm{d}V}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque density, $\mathcal{L}$ is the selected angular-momentum component of the population, $t$ is time, and $V$ is volume. Internal collisional exchange cancels when summed over all participating populations in a closed system, although it can be nonzero for a resolved subpopulation, as illustrated by [electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons). This local quantity is distinct from the volume-integrated [torque due to collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when collisions increase the selected angular-momentum component of the target population in its defined positive direction.

NAMES.name: electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volumetric angular-momentum source in an electron population due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local rate at which electron-electron scattering transfers angular momentum to that population. It vanishes for the complete electron population by self-collision momentum conservation but can be nonzero for resolved electron subpopulations.
NAMES.long:
Volumetric angular-momentum source in an electron population due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local rate at which electron-electron scattering changes the angular momentum carried by that population. It describes only electron-electron collisional exchange and excludes momentum sources from ions, neutrals, waves, or electromagnetic fields. For the complete electron population, the net self-collisional contribution is zero by momentum conservation; for a resolved electron subpopulation, it represents exchange with the rest of the electron distribution.

For a scalar toroidal angular-momentum balance, a common kinetic definition is the velocity-space moment of the electron-electron collision operator in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height:

$$
\tau_{\alpha \leftarrow e} = \int m_e R v_\phi\, C_{\alpha/e}[f_\alpha, f_e] \, d^3v
$$

where $\alpha$ denotes the electron population being followed, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component, $f_\alpha$ and $f_e$ are distribution functions, and $C_{\alpha/e}$ is the Coulomb collision operator giving the rate of change of $f_\alpha$ due to collisions with electrons.

This quantity is usually computed from kinetic or fluid collision models rather than measured directly. In transport modeling it is evaluated from collisional friction terms, momentum-exchange moments of a Fokker-Planck operator, or closures based on electron distribution functions; the [thermal electron specialization](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons) applies when the followed population is the bulk thermal electrons.

For the aggregate electron population, the expected value is zero apart from numerical residuals, because electron-electron collisions redistribute momentum internally. Nonzero values indicate exchange between electron subpopulations, relative drift between parts of the electron distribution, or an intentionally restricted collision operator.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the torque increases electron toroidal angular momentum associated with motion toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Thermal electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local rate of angular-momentum transfer per volume into a selected thermal-electron phase-space region caused only by electron-electron Coulomb collisions. It covers restrictions such as trapped thermal electrons without imposing that restriction itself.
NAMES.long:
Thermal electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local rate at which electron-electron Coulomb collisions transfer angular momentum to a selected thermal-electron recipient phase-space region. It is component-generic and population-generic within thermal electrons: neither a particular angular-momentum component nor an orbit-class restriction is fixed unless a more specific quantity states one.

The corresponding angular-momentum moment of the electron-electron collision operator is

$$
\tau_{\mathcal{P},a}^{ee}(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{\mathcal{P}} L_a(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, C_{ee}[f_e^{\mathrm{rec}}; f_e^{\mathrm{field}}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\tau_{\mathcal{P},a}^{ee}$ is the collisional torque density for recipient region $\mathcal{P}$ and angular-momentum component $a$, $L_a$ is the single-particle angular-momentum component along the positive direction $\hat{\mathbf e}_a$, $f_e^{\mathrm{rec}}$ is the recipient thermal-electron distribution, $f_e^{\mathrm{field}}$ is the electron field-particle distribution, and $C_{ee}$ is the Coulomb collision operator for electron-electron encounters.

The recipient region $\mathcal{P}$ includes only thermal electrons and may represent the complete thermal-electron recipient region or a resolved subset. The [trapped thermal-electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons](name:trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons) is the specialization with $\mathcal{P}$ restricted to trapped thermal electrons. Collision partners are electrons; torque transfer from ions, neutrals, fields, radiation, turbulence, and externally imposed forces is excluded. For an unpartitioned electron set, electron-electron self-collisions conserve total angular momentum, so a nonzero resolved value represents exchange with electron phase space outside $\mathcal{P}$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when electron-electron Coulomb collisions increase the selected thermal-electron angular momentum along the positive direction $\hat{\mathbf e}_a$.

NAMES.name: torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated when a particle-population current interacts with a magnetic field through the Lorentz force.
NAMES.long:
This vector quantity is the torque density transferred to a specified particle population by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with a current contribution.

The defining local relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}=\mathbf{r}\times(\mathbf{J}\times\mathbf{B})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}$ is the torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin, $\mathbf{J}$ is the relevant current density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field. The cross products use the right-hand rule.

The parent covers component projections, orbit-class selections, current closures, and averaging conventions represented by its children. For example, [co-passing J×B torque density](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) selects a passing-particle contribution, whereas [toroidal J×B torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) selects the toroidal component and a flux-surface average.

NAMES.name: co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated when a co-passing-particle current interacts with a magnetic field through the Lorentz force.
NAMES.long:
This vector quantity is the torque density transferred to co-passing particles by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with their current contribution.

The defining local relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{J\times B}=\mathbf{r}\times(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{co}}\times\mathbf{B})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{co}}_{J\times B}$ is the co-passing J-cross-B torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the current-density contribution of co-passing particles, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field. The cross products use the right-hand rule.

This parent fixes the co-passing orbit-class selection. Its children may add component projections or averaging conventions; for example, [toroidal co-passing J-cross-B torque density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) is the flux-surface-averaged $\hat{\phi}$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame of this same co-passing contribution. Counter-passing and trapped-particle contributions are excluded.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated when a particle-population current interacts with a magnetic field through the Lorentz force.
NAMES.long:
This vector quantity is the torque density transferred to a specified particle population by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with a current contribution.

The defining local relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}=\mathbf{r}\times(\mathbf{J}\times\mathbf{B})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}$ is the torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin, $\mathbf{J}$ is the relevant particle-population current density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field. The cross products use the right-hand rule.

This parent covers the component projections, orbit-class selections, current closures, and averaging conventions represented by its children. For example, [co-passing J×B torque density](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) selects a passing-particle contribution, while [toroidal J×B torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) selects the toroidal component and a flux-surface average; [toroidal counter-passing J×B torque density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) combines both selections.
NAMES.sign: Positive when each reported vector component points along its positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source density delivered to co-passing particles by the Lorentz force.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source density delivered to co-passing particles by the Lorentz force. It is the toroidal projection of the [co-passing torque density due to the J cross B force](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{co}}^{J\times B}(\psi)=\left\langle R\left[(J_{\mathrm{co},n}\hat{n}_{\psi})\times\mathbf{B}\right]\cdot\hat{\phi}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $J_{\mathrm{co},n}\hat{n}_{\psi}$ is the co-passing current density normal to that surface, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $R$ is major radius, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The brackets denote an average over the complete flux surface.

The co-passing population consists of passing particle orbits moving in the co-current direction; counter-passing and trapped contributions are excluded and are represented by the [toroidal counter-passing torque density due to the J cross B force](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and [toroidal trapped torque density due to the J cross B force](name:toroidal_trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the Lorentz-force torque on the co-passing population acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ about the symmetry axis.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source density transferred to counter-passing particles by the J cross B force from a flux-surface-normal current. Counter-passing means parallel motion opposite the plasma-current direction.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the torque density transferred to the counter-passing particle population by the magnetic Lorentz force, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. It is the toroidal projection of the vector [counter-passing torque density due to the J cross B force](name:counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).

$$
\left\langle \tau_{\phi,J\times B}^{\mathrm{cp}} \right\rangle_{\psi}
=
\left\langle \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\cdot\left[\mathbf{r}\times\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{n}}^{\mathrm{cp}}\times\mathbf{B}\right)\right]\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

Here, $\tau_{\phi,J\times B}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the local toroidal torque-density component, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector about the torque origin, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{n}}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the counter-passing current-density component normal to the flux surface, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes averaging over the surface labeled by $\psi$.

The counter-passing restriction distinguishes this contribution from the broader [toroidal torque density due to the J cross B force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force); the normal-current restriction is applied before the toroidal projection and surface average.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the torque points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, whose basis satisfies $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

sources.enhanced_context: Toroidal torque density from radial currents, evaluated from the counter-passing particle population of the distribution function and flux-surface averaged. Represents the toroidal momentum source from radial current interactions for counter-passing particles.

NAMES.name: toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated by the Lorentz force, averaged over a magnetic flux surface and projected onto the toroidal direction for a specified particle population.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal component of torque density transferred to a specified particle population by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with its current contribution. The toroidal direction is \(\hat{\phi}\) in the right-handed cylindrical \((R,\phi,Z)\) frame, where \(R\) is major radius, \(\phi\) is toroidal angle, and \(Z\) is vertical height.

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\phi,J\times B}(\psi)=\left\langle\left[\mathbf{r}\times(\mathbf{J}\times\mathbf{B})\right]\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where \(\tau_{\phi,J\times B}\) is the toroidal torque density, \(\mathbf{r}\) is the position vector from the selected torque origin, \(\mathbf{J}\) is the relevant current-density contribution, \(\mathbf{B}\) is the magnetic field, and \(\psi\) labels the magnetic flux surface. The angle brackets denote the flux-surface average; \(\mathbf{r}\), \(\mathbf{J}\), and \(\mathbf{B}\) have units of m, A m\(^{-2}\), and T, respectively.

The quantity is the toroidal, flux-surface-averaged member of the vector [torque density due to J×B force](name:torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) family. Population-resolved contributions, such as [toroidal co-passing J×B torque density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force), provide separate decompositions of this total contribution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projected torque points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle \(\phi\).

NAMES.name: torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
NAMES.short: Torque vector representing the angular momentum per unit time carried away from the plasma by neutral beam particles that traverse the confined plasma without ionization, constituting the beam angular momentum not deposited into the plasma.
NAMES.long:
Neutral beam injection is a primary momentum-input mechanism for magnetically confined plasmas. Shinethrough occurs when a fraction of the injected neutrals fail to ionize along their trajectory through the plasma and exit the far side, carrying with them angular momentum that was never coupled to the plasma fluid. The torque due to neutral beam shinethrough quantifies the corresponding rate of angular momentum loss from this unabsorbed beam fraction.

The total injected beam torque $\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{beam}$ is partitioned between the deposited component and the shinethrough component:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{shinethrough} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{beam} - \boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{deposited}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{deposited}$ is the angular momentum per unit time actually transferred to the plasma ions. The dominant projection in tokamak geometry is the toroidal component tracked by [toroidal torque due to neutral beam shinethrough](name:toroidal_torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough), representing the deficit in angular momentum deposition about the symmetry axis.

Shinethrough is most significant at low plasma densities, high beam energies, or for short beam-plasma path lengths, conditions common during discharge ramp-up or in low-density L-mode operation. It is evaluated by neutral beam deposition codes that integrate beam attenuation along the injection geometry. The shinethrough torque enters the toroidal angular momentum transport equation as a loss term, contrasting with collisional momentum exchange contributions such as [torque due to collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal projection points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of torque carried away by neutral beam particles that traverse the plasma without ionization, representing angular momentum not transferred to the plasma.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal shinethrough torque is the component of angular-momentum loss carried away by neutral beam particles that remain neutral while traversing the plasma and exit without transferring their momentum to the plasma. It is the toroidal component of the parent [torque due to neutral beam shinethrough](name:torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough).

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{sh}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{sh}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the total shinethrough torque vector and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This quantity includes only angular momentum carried away by non-ionized beam neutrals; it excludes momentum deposited by neutrals that ionize and is distinct from local [toroidal torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density) and [toroidal neutral torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: total_co_passing_particle_density
NAMES.short: Number density of co-passing particles integrated over all populations — thermal and suprathermal alike — where co-passing orbits have guiding-center parallel velocity directed along the plasma current.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing particles are those whose guiding-center parallel velocity component is aligned with the plasma current direction, a subset of non-trapped (passing) orbits. The total aggregation sums contributions from both the thermal bulk and any suprathermal (fast) minority populations, yielding the complete co-passing contribution to local number density. This orbit-class-resolved density is distinct from the full particle density, which also includes trapped and counter-passing orbit contributions.

The quantity is defined by integrating the complete particle distribution function over the co-passing partition of velocity space:

$$
n_\text{co} = \int_{\mathcal{D}_\text{co}} f(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $f$ is the distribution function, $\mathbf{r}$ is the spatial position, $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity, and $\mathcal{D}_\text{co}$ restricts integration to orbits with $v_\parallel$ in the plasma-current direction.

This quantity is evaluated from kinetic or drift-kinetic models that resolve $f$ explicitly, available either as a flux-surface-averaged radial profile or as a full poloidal-plane distribution that reveals orbit-class density asymmetries.

Core values in deuterium plasmas lie in the $10^{19}$–$10^{20}$ m$^{-3}$ range, with the co-passing fraction depending on collisionality and the trapped-particle fraction determined by local magnetic geometry.

The suprathermal subset alone is captured by [co_passing_fast_particle_density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density), and the counter-directed analog is [counter_passing_density](name:counter_passing_density). The corresponding pressure moment follows the same decomposition as total_co_passing_particle_pressure, and [co_passing_density](name:total_co_passing_particle_density) is a closely related name for the same aggregate quantity with less explicit notation.

NAMES.name: total_electron_pressure
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure of the entire electron population, defined as the isotropic second velocity-space moment of the electron distribution function and including thermal bulk and suprathermal electron contributions.
NAMES.long:
The electron pressure quantifies the isotropic mechanical stress exerted by the entire electron population and enters the electron momentum equation through the pressure-gradient force $-\nabla p_{e,\mathrm{tot}}$. This total scalar is the trace pressure obtained from the second velocity-space moment of the full electron distribution function.

For a distribution function $f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$ over velocity space at position $\mathbf{x}$, the total scalar electron pressure is defined by the random-kinetic second moment:

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_e}{3}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3_{\mathbf{v}}} \left|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_e(\mathbf{x})\right|^2 f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $m_e$ is the electron mass, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the mean electron flow velocity, and the integral is over the full velocity-space domain. The distribution function is normalized so that $n_e(\mathbf{x})=\int_{\mathbb{R}^3_{\mathbf{v}}} f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}$; for an isotropic Maxwellian full electron population this reduces to $p_{e,\mathrm{tot}}=n_e T_e$, with $T_e$ the electron temperature as particle energy.

The word total fixes the population scope: the moment is taken over all electrons rather than only over a thermal Maxwellian subset. When a population partition is defined, applying the same velocity-space moment to the thermal and suprathermal parts gives the contributions associated with [thermal_electron_pressure](name:thermal_electron_pressure_at_post_sawtooth_crash) and [fast_electron_pressure](name:fast_electron_pressure); their aggregate is this quantity, while ion pressure is excluded. This is the electron-population specialization of the species-agnostic [particle_pressure](name:particle_pressure). Because physical distribution functions are non-negative and the integrand is a squared random speed, $p_{e,\mathrm{tot}}\ge 0$ and is not a signed vector or tensor component.

NAMES.name: total_electron_source_rate
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated rate of net electron production or removal formed by summing the defined electron particle source and sink processes within a plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The total electron source rate $S_e^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the volume-integrated rate at which the total free-electron population is created or removed by particle processes. It is the aggregate net source term for the electron particle balance over the specified plasma volume.

With local source-density components $s_{e,k}(\mathbf{x})$, the total rate is defined by summing the included source and sink processes before integration:

$$
S_e^{\mathrm{tot}} = \int_V \sum_k s_{e,k}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $S_e^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total electron source rate, $s_{e,k}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron source density contributed by process $k$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $V$ is the specified plasma volume. The index $k$ covers the complete defined set of electron particle source and sink processes; positive $s_{e,k}$ denotes electron production and negative $s_{e,k}$ denotes electron removal.

This total quantity is the aggregate member of the [electron source rate](name:electron_source_rate) family. Mechanism-specific, production-only, or subpopulation-specific rates, such as [fast electron source rate](name:fast_electron_source_rate), are separate components rather than this aggregate net rate unless they are the only included term. Transport losses represented only by the divergence of an electron particle flux are excluded unless explicitly treated as particle source or sink processes.

NAMES.name: total_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Gyrotropic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population summed over all charge states, characterized by independent components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The total fast-ion pressure represents the full gyrotropic kinetic stress of the suprathermal ion population, summed over all charge states, as a contribution to the plasma pressure balance. Fast ions — including fusion-born alpha particles, neutral-beam-injected ions, and radio-frequency-accelerated ions — retain pressure anisotropy with $P_\parallel \neq P_\perp$ relative to the local magnetic field because their pitch-angle scattering rate is slow compared with their energy transfer rate to the bulk plasma. The anisotropic structure is fully captured by the two independent scalar components [parallel total fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure) and [perpendicular total fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure).

For a gyrotropic fast-ion distribution, the pressure tensor is:

$$
\overleftrightarrow{P}_\text{fast} = P_{\perp}\,\overleftrightarrow{I} + (P_{\parallel} - P_{\perp})\,\hat{b}\hat{b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel}$ and $P_{\perp}$ are the parallel and perpendicular scalar pressure components, $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\overleftrightarrow{I}$ is the identity tensor.

Fast-ion pressure profiles are obtained from kinetic particle-following or Fokker-Planck solvers that evolve the suprathermal distribution function under collisional slowing-down and pitch-angle scattering. The anisotropic fast-ion stress enters the MHD force balance and can drive pressure-anisotropy-driven instabilities when $P_{\parallel}/P_{\perp}$ departs significantly from unity. The parent quantity [fast_ion_pressure](name:fast_ion_pressure) provides per-charge-state resolution.

In high-performance discharges with strong neutral beam or ion cyclotron resonance heating, fast-ion pressure can reach 10–50% of the total plasma pressure in the core, with anisotropy ratios $P_{\parallel}/P_{\perp}$ ranging from near unity for isotropized distributions to several for strongly beam-like distributions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the fast-ion population exerts compressive kinetic pressure, consistent with the second velocity moment of a non-negative distribution function being positive.

NAMES.name: parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total fast-ion parallel pressure, summed over all fast-ion species and charge states, is the gyrotropic stress component along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The parallel total fast-ion pressure is the principal field-aligned component of the gyrotropic pressure tensor of suprathermal ions, summed over all fast-ion species and charge states. It is one of the two independent components that determine the anisotropic pressure represented by [total fast-ion pressure](name:total_fast_ion_pressure).

It is defined by the projection

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}} = \hat{\mathbf b} \cdot \overleftrightarrow{\mathbf P}_{\mathrm{fast}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel pressure component, $\overleftrightarrow{\mathbf P}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the total fast-ion pressure tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf b} = \mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf B$. The complementary [perpendicular total fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure) describes stress transverse to the field; equality of the two components corresponds to an isotropic fast-ion pressure.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total fast-ion perpendicular pressure, summed over all species, is the component of the suprathermal ion gyrotropic pressure tensor associated with ion motion perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular total fast-ion pressure $P_{\perp,\text{fast}}$ is the principal perpendicular component of the gyrotropic pressure tensor of suprathermal ions, summed over all ion species and charge states. It quantifies the kinetic energy of fast ions stored in the two velocity degrees of freedom transverse to the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. Together with [parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), it fully characterizes the pressure anisotropy of the fast-ion population described by the parent [total_fast_ion_pressure](name:total_fast_ion_pressure) tensor.

The perpendicular pressure is the second velocity moment of the fast-ion distribution function in the plane perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$:

$$
P_{\perp,\text{fast}} = \sum_s \frac{m_s}{2} \int v_\perp^2 \, f_{\text{fast},s}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion mass for species $s$, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed in the plane perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$, and $f_{\text{fast},s}$ is the fast-ion velocity distribution function for species $s$, with the sum running over all fast-ion species.

This quantity is computed from guiding-center kinetic models or Fokker-Planck solvers that evolve the fast-ion distribution function. Preferential perpendicular energization by ion cyclotron resonance heating drives $P_{\perp,\text{fast}} \gg P_{\parallel,\text{fast}}$, while neutral beam injection at oblique angles produces more moderate anisotropy. The charge-state-resolved analog is [perpendicular_fast_ion_state_pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure), and the thermal-ion counterpart is [total_thermal_ion_pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the fast-ion population carries nonzero kinetic energy in degrees of freedom perpendicular to the local magnetic field; this quantity is non-negative for all physically realizable fast-ion distributions.
