NAMES.name: total_fast_particle_count
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated number of suprathermal particles, combining all included fast-particle species and superposed fast-particle distributions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total number of nonthermal or suprathermal particles represented by the included fast-particle distributions over the plasma volume. It is an extensive particle-count measure, not a local density or a count of numerical distribution markers.

$$
N_{\mathrm{fast}} = \int_V n_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the total fast-particle count, $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [fast-particle density](name:fast_particle_density) summed over the included fast-particle species and superposed distributions. The count excludes particles belonging only to the thermal population and is related to the volume-integrated [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy), which weights the same population by kinetic energy.

NAMES.name: total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to an ion charge state by collisions, summing contributions from both thermal and fast ion sub-populations.
NAMES.long:
Total Coulomb-collisional power transferred to ions of a specified species and charge state, integrated over the plasma volume, aggregating contributions from both the thermal and fast (non-Maxwellian) sub-populations.

The total is the sum of its population-resolved components:

$$
P_{\rm coll}^{s,z} = P_{\rm th}^{s,z} + P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}
$$

where $P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$ is the [thermal ion charge state power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions) and $P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}$ is the [fast ion charge state power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), with $s$ denoting the ion species and $z$ the resolved charge state.

This charge-state-resolved total is distinct from [ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions), which aggregates over all charge states and both sub-populations without charge-state resolution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the specified ion charge state is a net recipient of energy from Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the fast (non-Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the fast (non-Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state, obtained by integrating the local Coulomb-collisional energy-exchange rate density over the plasma volume:

$$
P_{\rm coll,fast}^{s,z} = \int Q_{\rm coll,fast}^{s,z}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm coll,fast}^{s,z}$ is the local Coulomb-collisional power density for fast ions of species $s$ in charge state $z$, and $V$ is the plasma volume. Fast ions are those whose velocity distribution departs significantly from a Maxwellian, such as neutral-beam-injected or fusion-born ions undergoing thermalization.

This quantity is the fast-population component of [total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions); summing it with [thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions) recovers the total collisional power for that charge state. Aggregating over all charge states yields [fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when net energy is transferred into the fast ion charge state by Coulomb collisions.

sources.enhanced_context: Total collisional power (volume-integrated) transferred to the fast particle population of a specific ion species charge state, arising from interactions with the modelled non-Maxwellian distribution function.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power to the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the thermal (Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the thermal (Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state, obtained by integrating the local Coulomb-collisional energy-exchange rate density over the plasma volume.

It is defined as the volume integral of the local collisional energy-exchange rate density for that thermal charge-state population:

$$
P_{\rm th}^{s,z} = \int_{V_{\rm p}} q_{\rm th,coll}^{s,z}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$ is the thermal ion charge-state collisional power, $q_{\rm th,coll}^{s,z}$ is the local Coulomb-collisional energy-exchange rate density for thermal ions of species $s$ and charge state $z$, $V_{\rm p}$ is the plasma volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position.

Together with the [fast ion charge state power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), it forms the [total ion charge state power due to collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions) for the same species and charge state through $P_{\rm coll}^{s,z}=P_{\rm th}^{s,z}+P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}$. The aggregate [thermal ion power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) is recovered only after summing over all thermal ion species and charge states, $P_{\rm th}=\sum_s\sum_z P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$; summing only over charge states of one species gives a species-resolved contribution rather than the all-species thermal aggregate.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the specified thermal ion charge state is a net recipient of energy from Coulomb collisions.

NAMES.name: total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state, integrated over the plasma and including both the toroidal projection of the thermal-ion contribution and the summed fast-ion contributions from angular-momentum exchange with co-existing species.
NAMES.long:
Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state is the signed toroidal collisional angular-momentum source for that charge state, integrated over the plasma. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The total torque is the additive thermal-plus-fast scalar contribution:

$$
\tau^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
=
\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
+
\sum_f \tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies the charge state, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [thermal ion charge-state collisional torque](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), $\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its axial projection associated with toroidal angular momentum, $f$ indexes fast-ion sub-populations, and $\tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [toroidal fast ion charge-state collisional torque](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions) for sub-population $f$.

Only torque due to Coulomb-collisional momentum exchange with co-existing charged plasma species is included. This quantity is charge-state resolved, not summed over charge states, and is distinct from the corresponding local [total ion charge-state collisional torque density].
NAMES.sign: Positive when collisions transfer toroidal angular momentum to the specified ion charge state in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: total_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local number density of all represented ions at a plasma point, summed over ion species, ionic charge states, and thermal and non-thermal populations. It is a particle number density, not a charge density or mass density.
NAMES.long:
Total ion density is the local count of all represented ions per physical volume at a plasma point. It is an all-species, all-charge-state, and all-represented-population aggregate specialization of [ion_density](name:ion_density). It is a particle number density, not a charge density or mass density.

The aggregation convention is

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_Z \sum_p n_{i,s,Z,p}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion density, $s$ labels represented ion species, $Z$ labels ionic charge state, $p$ labels represented ion populations such as thermal and non-thermal ions, and $n_{i,s,Z,p}$ is the charge-state- and population-resolved ion density contribution.

Population-qualified species forms restrict the same density concept to a subset: [thermal_ion_density](name:thermal_ion_density) counts Maxwellian ions of a specified species, and [fast_ion_density](name:fast_ion_density) counts suprathermal ions of a specified species. [ion_charge_state_density](name:ion_charge_state_density) resolves a single ionic charge state, while [volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) is a spatial average of ion density rather than the local point value.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_total_ion_density_to_electron_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of total free-ion number density, summed over species and charge states, to the local free-electron number density.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local ratio of total free-ion number density to free-electron number density. It includes thermal and nonthermal ions and counts ions rather than ionic charge.

The ratio is defined by

$$
\mathcal{R}_{i/e} = \frac{n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}{n_e} = \frac{\sum_s \sum_{Z>0} n_{s,Z}}{n_e}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{i/e}$ is the ratio, $s$ indexes ion species, $Z$ is the positive integer charge state, $n_{s,Z}$ is the corresponding ion number density, and $n_e$ is the local [electron density](name:electron_density); the number densities are in m$^{-3}$. The numerator includes the thermal contribution represented by [total thermal ion density](name:total_thermal_ion_density) and all applicable fast-ion contributions, including species-resolved quantities such as [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density).

Neutral particles are excluded. Quasineutrality constrains the charge-weighted sum $n_e \simeq \sum_s \sum_{Z>0} Z n_{s,Z}$, not this unweighted ion count, so the ratio need not equal unity when multicharged ions are present.

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Charge-state-summed number density of all ion species at the internal transport barrier, excluding neutral particles and charge weighting.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total local number density of all included ion populations evaluated at the flux-surface location assigned to the internal transport barrier. It is the aggregate specialization of [ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), rather than the density of a selected species or charge state.

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{total}} = \sum_s \sum_Z n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state $Z$, and both sums include every ion population in the defined ion inventory. The summation counts particles without weighting by ionic charge; neutral particles are excluded. This convention distinguishes the quantity from charge-weighted descriptors such as [charge_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:charge_at_internal_transport_barrier).

NAMES.name: total_ion_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total ion number density at the magnetic axis, where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes, summed over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
The total ion number density at the magnetic axis is the local number density of all ion species, including every ionic charge state. The magnetic axis is the innermost point of the nested closed flux surfaces, defined by a vanishing gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux.

At the magnetic-axis position, the quantity is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}) = \sum_s \sum_Z n_{s,Z}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}})
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position, $s$ indexes ion species, and $Z$ indexes their ionic charge states.

This is the all-ion aggregate of [ion density at magnetic axis](name:ion_density_at_magnetic_axis); it excludes electrons and neutral particles.

NAMES.name: total_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total ion energy flux is the local ion energy-flux-density vector carried by all ion species and charge states, including conductive thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport.
NAMES.long:
Total ion energy flux is the local energy-flux-density vector carried by all ion species and charge states. It represents the rate at which the aggregate ion energy reservoir crosses unit oriented area after projection onto the surface normal, including conductive thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport when those contributions are in scope.

For a multi-species plasma, the aggregate vector $\mathbf{Q}_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is defined as the sum of conductive and convective species contributions:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{s \in \mathrm{ions}} \left(\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{cond}} + \mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}\right)
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species and charge states, $\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive heat-flux vector of species $s$, and $\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective energy-flux vector of species $s$. For an ideal monatomic ion fluid, the enthalpy part of $\mathbf{q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is $(5/2)p_s\mathbf{v}_s$, where $p_s$ is scalar pressure and $\mathbf{v}_s$ is mean flow velocity; bulk-kinetic convection is included only when macroscopic flow energy belongs to the selected ion energy reservoir.

As an extensive flux-density quantity, the aggregate is summed over all ion species and over all charge states of each species; it is not a density-weighted mean. It is local, not a flux-surface average or area-integrated power. Projection onto an oriented surface normal gives a scalar [ion_energy_flux](name:ion_energy_flux), and named aggregate projections include [radial_total_ion_energy_flux](name:radial_total_ion_energy_flux), poloidal_total_ion_energy_flux, and [parallel_total_ion_energy_flux](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_flux). The quantity is distinct from [total_thermal_ion_heat_flux](name:total_thermal_ion_heat_flux), which restricts the transported reservoir to total ion thermal heat, and is an ion contribution to [total_energy_flux](name:total_thermal_ion_heat_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a represented component of the vector carries ion energy in the positive direction of its stated basis vector, projection direction, or oriented surface normal.

NAMES.name: parallel_total_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Parallel total ion energy flux is the field-aligned component of the local ion energy-flux density summed over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel total ion energy flux is the local field-aligned component of the ion energy-flux-density vector carried by all ion species and charge states. It represents aggregate conductive thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport projected along the local magnetic field.

The scalar field-aligned component is defined by

$$
Q_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{tot}}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf Q_i^{\mathrm{tot}},\qquad \hat{\mathbf b}=\frac{\mathbf B}{|\mathbf B|}
$$

where $\mathbf Q_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the aggregate ion energy-flux-density vector, $\mathbf B$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is its unit direction. The quantity is defined where $|\mathbf B|$ is nonzero. It is summed over all ion species and charge states, not density-weighted averaged, and is local rather than flux-surface averaged or area-integrated. It is the field-aligned projection of [total ion energy flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux); its charge-state-resolved counterpart is [parallel ion charge-state energy flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux), while [radial total ion energy flux](name:radial_total_ion_energy_flux) provides the corresponding radial projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aggregate ion energy-flux vector has a component in the direction of the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf B$.

NAMES.name: radial_total_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net local radial component of ion energy flux density carried by all ion species and charge states, combining conductive heat flow with convective enthalpy transport.
NAMES.long:
The radial total ion energy flux is the local radial component of the thermal-energy flux density carried by all ion species and charge states, including conductive heat transport and convective enthalpy transport. It is neither flux-surface averaged nor area-integrated.

The [total ion energy flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux) vector is projected onto the cylindrical radial unit vector:

$$
Q_{i,R}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \hat{\mathbf R}\cdot\sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}}\left(\mathbf q_s+\frac{5}{2}p_s\mathbf v_s\right)
$$

where $Q_{i,R}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the radial flux density, $\hat{\mathbf R}$ is the radial unit vector, $\mathbf q_s$ is the conductive heat-flux vector, $p_s$ is the scalar pressure, and $\mathbf v_s$ is the mean flow velocity of ion species or charge state $s$. The projection uses the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike the [parallel total ion energy flux](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_flux), it is not a field-aligned projection and is not necessarily normal to a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projected ion energy flux is directed toward increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: total_ion_heating_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Cumulative net energy-transfer rate to all ion species enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface, including both heating and cooling contributions.
NAMES.long:
Total ion heating power is the net power coupled to the combined ion population inside a specified magnetic flux surface. It is the volume-integrated form of [total ion power density](name:total_ion_power_density) and the enclosed counterpart of [ion heating power](name:ion_heating_power).

The cumulative quantity is defined by

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{inside}}(\psi)=\int_{V(\psi)} p_i(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{inside}}$ is the enclosed ion heating power, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux label of the specified surface, $V(\psi)$ is the volume inside that surface, $p_i(\mathbf{r})$ is the local net power density coupled to the ion population, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position.

The integration aggregates all included ion species and charge states and represents the cumulative source term for the ion energy balance. It is positive for net ion energy gain and negative for net ion energy loss; it is distinct from the local power density and from a whole-plasma total unless the enclosing surface is the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: total_ion_power
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated net power transferred to the ion population by a specified plasma source or sink, summed over all ion species and positive for net energy gain by ions.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated net power transferred to the ion population by a specified plasma source or sink is the net rate at which that source term changes the energy of ions within the confined plasma. It is source-indexed and species-summed: one value corresponds to one specified source or sink term and aggregates over all ion species.

For a source or sink labeled $s$, the total ion power $P_{i,s}$ is defined by integrating the species-resolved local ion power density over the confined plasma volume:

$$
P_{i,s} = \sum_a \int_{V_c} q_{i,a}^{(s)}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $a$ indexes ion species, $q_{i,a}^{(s)}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local volumetric power density transferred by source term $s$ to ion species $a$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $dV$ is the volume element, and $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume.

Energy transferred directly to electrons is excluded; the electron-channel counterpart is [electron deposited power](name:electron_deposited_power). Sink terms are retained with their sign, so the quantity is distinct from [total ion heating power](name:total_ion_heating_power), which includes only energy gain by ions. Summing $P_{i,s}$ over a complete set of source and sink terms gives the corresponding contribution to [ion power](name:ion_power); [deposited power](name:deposited_power) is the related source-resolved transferred-power concept without the all-ion population restriction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the specified source term transfers net energy to the ion population.

NAMES.name: total_ion_power_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total ion power density is the net local energy-transfer rate to the ion channel, aggregated over all included ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Total ion power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from all included ion species per unit volume. It is the aggregate source term for the ion recipient in an ion energy transport equation, summed over ion charge states and included ion-channel contributions.

For a differential volume, the aggregate ion-channel source term is defined by

$$
S_{E,i}^{\mathrm{total}} = \sum_c \sum_s \sum_Z S_{E,c,s,Z} = \frac{\partial^2 E_i^{\mathrm{total}}}{\partial t\,\partial V}
$$

where $S_{E,i}^{\mathrm{total}}$ is total ion power density, $c$ indexes included ion-energy channels, $s$ indexes ion species, $Z$ indexes charge states, $E_i^{\mathrm{total}}$ is energy transferred to the ion population in joules, $t$ is time in seconds, and $V$ is physical volume in cubic meters. It is the aggregate form of [ion power density](name:ion_power_density), including contributions such as [thermal ion power density](name:thermal_ion_power_density) and fast-ion power density when those channels belong to the same balance. Spatial redistribution by the divergence of ion energy flux is excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aggregate ion population gains energy in the ion energy transport equation.

NAMES.name: total_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total isotropic scalar pressure of the ion fluid at a plasma location, summing thermal and fast (non-thermal) contributions over all charge states of a given ion species.
NAMES.long:
The total ion pressure is the isotropic scalar pressure of the entire ion fluid at a given point in the plasma, combining the Maxwellian thermal bulk and suprathermal fast-ion contributions summed over all charge states of the species. It represents the physically complete ion kinetic pressure entering force-balance and energy-transport equations in multi-fluid and magnetohydrodynamic models.

The total ion pressure decomposes additively as:

$$
P_i = P_{i,\mathrm{th}} + P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal ion pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure) from the Maxwellian bulk, satisfying $P_{i,\mathrm{th}} = n_i k_B T_i$ with $n_i$ the ion number density and $T_i$ the ion temperature, and $P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal fast-ion contribution. The [total thermal ion pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure) isolates the bulk-only term; the [total ion state pressure] provides per-charge-state resolution.

Together with [total electron pressure](name:total_electron_pressure), the total ion pressure contributes to the full plasma pressure $P = P_e + P_i$ appearing in the MHD force-balance $\nabla P = \mathbf{j} \times \mathbf{B}$. Fast-ion contributions can become comparable to or exceed the thermal term during neutral beam injection or ion cyclotron resonance heating. The quantity is inferred by combining ion temperature and density profile diagnostics with energetic-particle measurements and fast-ion transport modeling.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion population has nonzero kinetic energy, which holds for all physical ion populations; scalar ion pressure is an intrinsically non-negative quantity.

NAMES.name: total_ion_source_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Net local production rate of ion particles, summed over all ion species and charge states, with losses represented by a negative contribution.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the net volumetric source term in the continuity balance for the total ion population. It combines ion-particle creation and loss processes while excluding neutral particles from the summed population.

$$
S_{\mathrm{ion}} = \sum_s \sum_Z \left(S^{+}_{s,Z} - S^{-}_{s,Z}\right)
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the total ion source rate, $s$ identifies an ion species, $Z$ identifies its charge state, and $S^{+}_{s,Z}$ and $S^{-}_{s,Z}$ are the corresponding local creation and loss rates. The quantity is the charge-state-summed volumetric counterpart of the parent ion_source_rate, and differs from [ion_particle_source_rate](name:ion_particle_source_rate), which is integrated inside an enclosing flux surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ion-particle creation exceeds ion-particle loss.

NAMES.name: total_neutral_density
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Total neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms and molecules in the fully aggregated neutral population. It explicitly aggregates over neutral species, thermal and suprathermal populations, internal quantum states, and parent-ion-associated neutral states.
NAMES.long:
Total neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms and molecules in the fully aggregated neutral population. It shares the unresolved population scope of [neutral density](name:neutral_density) and makes explicit that neutral species, kinetic-population, internal-state, and parent-ion-associated labels are summed out. It is a pointwise volumetric particle density, not a flux-surface-averaged or volume-averaged quantity unless an averaging operation is part of the named quantity.

The local total neutral density is defined by the total neutral particle count per volume element:

$$
n_0^{\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{dN_0^{\mathrm{tot}}}{dV} = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathcal{P}_0^{\mathrm{tot}}} n_\alpha
$$

where $n_0^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is total neutral density, $N_0^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the number of neutral particles in the infinitesimal volume element $dV$, $\mathcal{P}_0^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the set of non-overlapping neutral population classes included in the total, and $n_\alpha$ is the local density of class $\alpha$.

For this total name, $\mathcal{P}_0^{\mathrm{tot}}$ includes neutral atomic and molecular species, thermal and suprathermal kinetic populations, internal quantum states, and parent-ion-associated neutral states that are not retained as separate labels. For a non-overlapping partition into thermal, suprathermal, and parent-ion-associated components, the population-class sum recovers the sum of those component densities; [thermal neutral density](name:thermal_neutral_density) and [suprathermal neutral density](name:fast_neutral_density) retain the first two kinetic restrictions, while [ion neutral density] retains association with a specified parent ion species. The total excludes ions and electrons; [neutral internal-state density](name:neutral_internal_state_density) retains an internal-state label, and [volume-averaged neutral species density](name:volume_averaged_neutral_species_density) applies an averaging and species resolution not present in this pointwise total.

NAMES.name: total_neutral_internal_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure of all neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or excitation state, combining thermal and nonthermal fast-neutral contributions.
NAMES.long:
The total neutral internal state pressure is the kinetic pressure associated with all neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or excitation state, combining thermal and nonthermal fast-neutral contributions. It is the total-contribution specialization of [neutral internal state pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure).

For the aggregate velocity distribution in state $s$, the scalar pressure is one-third of the pressure-tensor trace:

$$
p_s^{\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{1}{3}\int m_n \lvert\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_s\rvert^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral-particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_s$ is the aggregate mean velocity, and $f_s$ is the distribution of all neutral particles in state $s$. Subtracting the mean flow excludes common bulk-flow dynamic pressure. Unlike [thermal neutral internal state pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure), this quantity includes nonthermal fast-neutral contributions and does not require an isotropic Maxwellian distribution. It remains restricted to the specified internal state and therefore differs from [total neutral pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure), which aggregates over internal states.

NAMES.name: total_neutron_power
NAMES.subject: neutron
NAMES.short: Total kinetic-energy power carried away by fusion-born neutrons, summed over all neutron-producing fusion reaction branches.
NAMES.long:
Total neutron power is the kinetic-energy loss rate carried away from the plasma by fusion-born neutrons. It is the branch-summed form of [neutron power](name:neutron_power), excluding energy transported by charged fusion products and energy deposited within the plasma.

$$
P_n^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_n} \dot{N}_r\,\langle E_{n,r}\rangle
$$

where $P_n^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total neutron power, $\mathcal{R}_n$ is the set of neutron-producing fusion reaction branches, $\dot{N}_r$ is the neutron production rate for branch $r$, and $\langle E_{n,r}\rangle$ is the mean kinetic energy per emitted neutron in that branch. Neutrons are uncharged and therefore are not confined by the magnetic field; their carried-away energy is distinct from plasma-deposited charged-product power.

NAMES.name: total_particle_count
NAMES.short: Total number of particles in the kinetic distribution, obtained by integrating the distribution function over velocity space and the entire plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The total particle count is the global normalization integral of the particle distribution function $f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v})$: it quantifies the total number of particles of the described species present in the plasma at a given instant, summed over all spatial positions within the plasma volume and all velocities in phase space. Being a pure count, it is dimensionless.

The quantity is defined by the phase-space integral

$$
N = \int_V \int f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3v \, d^3x
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector, and $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity. In marker-based kinetic simulations, $N$ reduces to the weighted sum over all simulation markers.

Monitoring $N$ over time provides a particle-conservation diagnostic in kinetic modeling: systematic drift from the initial value indicates numerical particle sources or losses. This quantity is closely related to [total_count](name:total_particle_count), which carries the same physical meaning with a less species-explicit name, and contrasts with [fast_count](name:total_fast_particle_count), which integrates only over the non-thermal sub-population of the distribution. The local spatial counterpart is total_particle_density, whose volume integral recovers $N$.

NAMES.name: total_plasma_energy
NAMES.short: Total internal kinetic energy of the confined plasma, equal to 3/2 times the volume integral of the total kinetic pressure summed over all electron and ion populations, excluding electromagnetic-field and bulk-flow energy.
NAMES.long:
Total plasma energy $W_\mathrm{total}$ is the aggregate internal kinetic energy carried by all confined plasma particles — thermal electrons, thermal ions, and nonthermal fast-particle populations — integrated over the plasma volume. It excludes magnetic-field energy, electrostatic-field energy, rest-mass energy, and macroscopic bulk-flow kinetic energy, making it the fundamental global stored-energy figure of merit for confinement assessment.

The defining relation is:

$$
W_\mathrm{total} = \frac{3}{2} \int p_\mathrm{tot} \, dV
$$

where $p_\mathrm{tot} = p_e + \sum_i p_i$ is the total kinetic pressure summing the electron partial pressure $p_e$ and the ion partial pressures $p_i$ over each species (including fast ions), and the integral extends over the confined plasma volume $V$ enclosed within the last closed flux surface.

It is inferred from diamagnetic loop measurements, which directly probe the total perpendicular stored energy, or from equilibrium reconstruction constrained by external magnetic diagnostics combined with kinetic profile measurements. The global energy confinement time $\tau_E$ is defined by $W_\mathrm{total} = \tau_E P_\mathrm{heat}$, linking this scalar directly to the net [total_plasma_heating_power](name:total_plasma_heating_power) absorbed by the plasma.

Stored plasma energies span from a few kilojoules in small research devices to tens of megajoules in large tokamaks during high-performance H-mode discharges. The integration domain is the [plasma_volume](name:volume_of_flux_surface) bounded by the last closed flux surface. This quantity is distinct from total_energy, which quantifies energy deposited in or extracted from a plasma-facing component rather than energy stored in the plasma itself. The parent quantity [plasma_energy](name:plasma_energy) captures the same aggregate concept without an explicit aggregation qualifier.

NAMES.name: total_plasma_momentum
NAMES.short: Total linear momentum vector of the confined plasma, obtained by integrating the local momentum density over the plasma volume and summing over all particle species (ions and electrons).
NAMES.long:
The total plasma momentum is the vector sum of linear momenta contributed by all plasma constituents — each ion species and the electron population — integrated over the confined plasma volume. It characterizes the bulk directed inertia of the plasma and is the central extensive quantity entering global momentum-balance analyzes, including the response to external torques from neutral beam injection, electromagnetic braking, or viscous redistribution between species.

The defining relation is:

$$
\mathbf{P} = \int \sum_s n_s m_s \mathbf{v}_s \, dV
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of species $s$, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the mean fluid velocity of that species, and the integral extends over the flux-surface-bounded plasma volume. Because $m_i \gg m_e$ for all ion species, the ion contributions overwhelmingly dominate the electron term.

The canonical projected component is [toroidal_total_plasma_momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum), which extracts the $\hat{\phi}$-directed part by integrating the toroidal momentum density over the plasma volume. This quantity is the all-species specialization of [plasma_momentum](name:plasma_momentum) and relates to the intensive flow description through the [center_of_mass_velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), which equals the local momentum density divided by the [total_plasma_mass_density](name:total_plasma_mass_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when each vector component points in the direction of increasing coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame (i.e., the toroidal component is positive in the direction of increasing $\phi$).

NAMES.name: toroidal_total_plasma_momentum
NAMES.short: Total linear momentum of all plasma species projected onto the toroidal direction by integrating their momentum density over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The total toroidal plasma momentum is the integrated linear momentum of all ion species and electrons projected onto the geometric toroidal direction. It is the toroidal component of the [total plasma momentum](name:total_plasma_momentum), not an angular momentum or a local momentum-flux quantity.

$$
P_\phi = \int_{V_p} \left(\sum_s \boldsymbol{\pi}_s\right) \cdot \hat{\phi}\,dV
$$

where $P_\phi$ is the total toroidal momentum, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ is the local linear-momentum density of species $s$, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $dV$ is the volume element. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the integrated linear momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: total_thermal_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total number density of thermal ions, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states and excluding fast nonthermal ions.
NAMES.long:
The thermal-ion density is the local population count of Maxwellian ions, aggregated over all included ion species and ionic charge states. It is the species-aggregated counterpart of [thermal ion density](name:thermal_ion_density).

The defining sum is

$$
n_{\mathrm{th}} = \sum_s \sum_Z n^{\mathrm{th}}_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{th}}$ and $n^{\mathrm{th}}_{s,Z}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, $s$ indexes ion species, and $Z$ indexes ionic charge states. The charge-state-resolved terms correspond to [thermal ion charge-state number density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density). Fast nonthermal ions and neutral particles are excluded.

NAMES.name: total_thermal_ion_energy
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated internal energy of the complete thermal-ion ensemble, obtained from its total isotropic pressure and excluding fast or suprathermal ions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the internal energy stored in the random thermal motion of all confined thermal ions, summed over every ion species and charge state. It is the complete-population specialization of [thermal_ion_energy](name:thermal_ion_energy).

Its defining relation is

$$
U_i = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\rm pl}} p_i(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $U_i$ is the total thermal-ion energy, $p_i(\mathbf{r})$ is the total isotropic thermal-ion pressure, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $dV$ is the volume element, and $V_{\rm pl}$ is the confined plasma volume. The pressure is summed over all thermal ion species and charge states, consistent with [total_thermal_ion_pressure](name:total_thermal_ion_pressure). Fast, suprathermal, and other nonthermal ion populations are excluded.

NAMES.name: total_thermal_ion_heat_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Total thermal ion heat flux is the signed surface-normal flux density of thermal energy carried by ions, summed over all ion species and charge states. It includes conductive heat and convective thermal enthalpy, excluding electron, electromagnetic, fast-ion, and directed bulk kinetic-energy flux.
NAMES.long:
Total thermal ion heat flux is the signed surface-normal flux density of thermal energy carried by ions, summed over all ion species and charge states. It is the ion thermal-heat contribution to energy transport through an oriented surface, formed from conductive thermal heat flow and thermal enthalpy advected by ion particle flow.

The additive definition is the projection of the summed thermal ion heat-flux vector onto the positive normal of the oriented surface:

$$
q_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \hat{\mathbf{n}}_+ \cdot \sum_{s \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}_s} \left( \mathbf{q}_{s,c}^{\mathrm{cond}} + h_{s,c}^{\mathrm{th}}\,\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,c} \right)
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_+$ is the positive unit normal of the oriented surface, $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of thermal ion species, $\mathcal{C}_s$ is the set of charge states included for species $s$, $\mathbf{q}_{s,c}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive thermal heat-flux vector of ion species $s$ in charge state $c$, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,c}$ is its particle-flux-density vector, and $h_{s,c}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is its thermal enthalpy per particle. The thermal enthalpy is defined in the local mean-flow frame; for an ideal monatomic Maxwellian population with no additional internal-state energy, $h_{s,c}^{\mathrm{th}} = 5T_{s,c}/2$, where $T_{s,c}$ is the ion temperature represented as thermal energy per particle.

This quantity is additive over ion populations; charge-state-resolved contributions are summed, not averaged. It excludes electron thermal heat flux, neutral heat flux, fast-ion and other non-thermal particle energy flux, electromagnetic energy flux, and directed bulk kinetic-energy flux. It is therefore the thermal-ion heat part of [total ion energy flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux) and of broader [total energy flux](name:total_thermal_ion_heat_flux), not a synonym for either broader quantity; a [charge-state-resolved ion energy flux](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) identifies one ion species and charge state before this summation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net thermal ion heat flow is directed along the positive normal of the oriented surface.

NAMES.name: total_thermal_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Species- and charge-state-summed isotropic kinetic pressure of the thermal ion population, excluding contributions from fast nonthermal ions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the total isotropic kinetic pressure carried by thermal ions, aggregated over every included ion species and ionic charge state. It retains the thermal-only scope of [thermal_ion_pressure](name:thermal_ion_pressure) while making the total aggregation explicit.

For the thermal ion distributions, the pressure is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{th},i}=\frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_Z m_s\int \left|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{sZ}\right|^2 f_{sZ}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the total thermal-ion pressure, $s$ indexes ion species, $Z$ indexes ionic charge states, $m_s$ is the species mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{sZ}$ is the bulk velocity of a species and charge state, and $f_{sZ}$ is its velocity distribution. It excludes fast-ion pressure and therefore differs from [total_ion_pressure](name:total_ion_pressure), which includes thermal and fast contributions.

NAMES.name: total_thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated thermal particle source rate is the net contribution to the thermal particle balance from particles entering or leaving the thermal population over the specified plasma volume. It is the spatial integral of the local volumetric thermal particle source rate.
NAMES.long:
Total thermal particle source rate is the volume-integrated contribution to the thermal particle balance from particles entering or leaving the thermal background distribution. It is the spatial integral of the local volumetric [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), so it denotes a global particle-count rate rather than a flux-surface-averaged source density.

The total rate is defined by integrating the local source density over the plasma volume:

$$
\dot{N}_{\rm th} = \int_{V_{\rm p}} S_{\rm th}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\rm th}$ is the total thermal particle source rate, $S_{\rm th}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local volumetric thermal particle source rate at position $\mathbf{x}$, $dV$ is the volume element, and $V_{\rm p}$ is the plasma volume included in the global balance.

The integration volume is the physical plasma volume whose thermal particle inventory is being balanced; for a whole-plasma total it is the confined plasma volume. This quantity does not resolve thermal guiding-center orbit classes; orbit-class-resolved volumetric source terms include [co-passing](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), [counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), and [trapped](name:trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate) thermal particle source rates. It counts particles rather than transferred energy; the volume-integrated energy-transfer analog is [thermal particle power due to thermalization](name:thermal_particle_power_due_to_thermalization), and the local energy-transfer-density analog is [thermal particle power density due to thermalization](name:thermal_particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net source adds particles to the thermal population.

sources.enhanced_context: Total particle source rate from a distribution source term, giving the number of particles per unit time injected into the plasma phase space. Used as input to kinetic Fokker-Planck equations for fast particle modelling.
sources.leaf_definition: Particle source rate
sources.parent_definition: Global quantities for various time slices

sources.enhanced_context: Total particle source rate integrated over the plasma volume for a given distribution function in Fokker-Planck modelling. Represents the net rate at which particles enter or leave the distribution due to wave interactions or external particle sources.
sources.leaf_definition: Particle source rate

sources.enhanced_context: Volume-integrated source rate of thermal particles due to thermalization of fast (non-thermal) particles. Represents the net rate at which fast particles are assimilated into the thermal background; can be negative if thermal particles are accelerated into the non-thermal population.
sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of thermal particles due to the thermalization of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Volume integrated source of thermal particles, momentum and energy due to thermalization. Here thermalization refers to non-thermal particles, sufficiently assimilated to the thermal background to be re-categorized as thermal particles. Note that this source may also be negative if thermal particles are being accelerated such that they form a distinct non-thermal contribution, e.g. due run-away of RF interactions.

NAMES.name: total_trapped_particle_density
NAMES.short: Total number density of thermal and non-thermal particles whose guiding-center orbits are magnetically trapped.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the particle number density contributed by the magnetically trapped part of a distribution function, including both thermal and non-thermal particles and excluding passing particles.

At a spatial point, it is defined by the zeroth velocity moment over the trapped region:

$$
n_{\mathrm{trapped}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{trapped}}(\mathbf{x})} f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$ is the particle distribution function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity, and $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{trapped}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the region of velocity space corresponding to magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits. The quantity may be evaluated locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface. The thermal and suprathermal contributions are combined; the suprathermal component alone is represented by [trapped fast particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density), while the unrestricted suprathermal population is represented by [fast particle density](name:fast_particle_density).

sources.enhanced_context: Total particle density (thermal + non-thermal) of the trapped particle population, evaluated as a flux-surface-averaged 1D radial profile from the distribution function. Includes contributions from both thermal and fast trapped particles.
sources.leaf_definition: Density (thermal+non-thermal)
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged profile evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution.

sources.enhanced_context: Total particle density (thermal plus non-thermal) evaluated from the trapped particle part of the distribution function in the 2D poloidal plane. Captures the trapped-particle contribution to plasma density.
sources.leaf_definition: Density (thermal+non-thermal)
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged profile evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution.

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Trapped fast-electron collisional power density is the local rate per unit volume of kinetic-energy change in the trapped guiding-center component caused by Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast-electron collisional power density is the local rate per unit volume at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to the trapped-orbit component of the suprathermal electron distribution. It is the trapped contribution to [fast-electron collisional power density](name:fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), distinct from the [co-passing fast-electron contribution](name:co_passing_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions) and the [counter-passing fast-electron contribution](name:counter_passing_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The quantity is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_s \int \frac{1}{2}m_e v^2\, C_{es}[f_{e,\mathrm{tr}},f_s](\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ indexes collision partners, $m_e$ is the electron mass in kg, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is speed in m/s, $f_{e,\mathrm{tr}}$ and $f_s$ are distribution functions normalized so their velocity integrals give number density, and $C_{es}$ is the collision operator per second. Only the trapped guiding-center component is included; the co-passing and counter-passing components are excluded. For relativistic electrons, the nonrelativistic kinetic-energy factor is replaced by the relativistic kinetic energy.
NAMES.sign: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to the trapped fast-electron component.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional power density transferred to the fast particle population from electron collisions, evaluated using the trapped part of the distribution function in the poloidal plane. Quantifies the collisional energy exchange channel from electrons to fast particles.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power density to the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volumetric torque density deposited in trapped fast electrons through Coulomb collisions, the local rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume.
NAMES.long:
The trapped fast-electron collisional torque density is the net rate at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum per unit volume to suprathermal electrons on trapped guiding-center orbits. It is the trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

It is defined from the collisional force density by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{e,f,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the trapped fast-electron collisional torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is displacement from the torque reference, and $\mathbf{f}_{e,f,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density on trapped fast electrons. For the toroidal specialization, the transfer rate is $R f_\phi$, where $R$ is major radius and $f_\phi$ is the force-density projection onto $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; this is represented by [toroidal trapped-fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

This parent quantity fixes the trapped orbit class but does not select a particular axis projection. It is distinct from the corresponding co-passing and counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque densities, which apply to different passing-orbit populations.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the component being represented points along the corresponding positive basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; for toroidal transfer, positive means $f_\phi$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque density transferred to trapped fast electrons, obtained by applying the major-radius lever arm to the toroidal collisional force density.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal angular-momentum transfer density delivered by Coulomb collisions to the trapped-orbit part of the fast-electron population. It is the toroidal component of [trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:trapped_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The toroidal torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal collisional torque density, $R$ is the major radius, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal component of the collisional force density acting on trapped fast electrons. The quantity excludes torque transferred to other electron orbit classes or particle species.

Its population scope distinguishes it from [toroidal_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), which includes the full fast-electron population.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional torque acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, increasing the trapped fast-electron toroidal angular momentum.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional toroidal torque density (φ-component) transferred to the fast particle population from electron collisions, evaluated from the trapped part of the distribution function. A 1D radial profile of fast particle toroidal momentum source density.

sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer rate for a specified fast-ion charge state, restricted to trapped particles that reverse parallel motion at magnetic mirror points.
NAMES.long:
Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer for a specified fast-ion charge state, contributed exclusively by trapped particles — fast ions whose guiding-center orbits reverse parallel motion at magnetic mirror points rather than complete full poloidal circuits. It is the trapped-orbit component of [fast-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
P_\mathrm{tr} = \int_{\Omega_\mathrm{tr}} \dot{E}_z(\mathbf{v}) f_z(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $f_z(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity-distribution function of fast ions in charge state $z$, $\dot{E}_z$ is their Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer rate per particle, and $\Omega_\mathrm{tr}$ is the trapped-orbit domain in velocity space.

Summing this quantity with the [co-passing contribution](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing contribution](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) recovers the total fast-ion charge-state collisional power density partitioned by orbit class.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the trapped fast-ion charge state gains kinetic energy from Coulomb collisions.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional power density transferred from the trapped fast particle distribution to the fast particle population of a given ion species state, as a 1D radial profile. Represents the fast-to-fast ion energy exchange via Coulomb collisions.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power density to the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional power density transferred to the fast ion population via collisions, evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution function in a 2D poloidal plane profile. Quantifies the rate of energy exchange from trapped particles to fast ions.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power density to the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Trapped fast-ion power density due to collisions is the local Coulomb-collisional rate of kinetic-energy transfer to fast ions on trapped orbits.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast-ion power density due to collisions is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to fast ions on trapped guiding-center orbits per unit volume. A trapped orbit mirror-reflects between magnetic turning points rather than completing a full poloidal transit. This is the trapped-orbit component of [fast-ion power density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), distinct from the [counter-passing fast-ion power density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).

For a fast-ion species, the orbit-restricted collisional power density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{trapped,coll}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \int \chi_{\mathrm{trapped}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,\frac{1}{2}m_i v^2\,C_{\mathrm{coll}}[f_{\mathrm{fast}}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $t$ is time in s, $m_i$ is fast-ion mass in kg, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity in m s$^{-1}$, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$, $f_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion distribution function, $C_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the Coulomb collision operator, $\chi_{\mathrm{trapped}}$ is a dimensionless indicator selecting trapped guiding-center orbits, and $d^3v$ is velocity-space volume. The integral is algebraic: positive values denote net collisional energy gain by trapped fast ions, while negative values denote net collisional energy loss. Contributions from co-passing and counter-passing orbits are excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Radial profile of the collisional power density transferred to the fast ion population of a given ion species, computed from the trapped part of the distribution function. Used in Fokker-Planck modelling of fast particle energy exchange.

sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various ion species

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Collisional torque density for trapped fast ions is the local rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume caused by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species.
NAMES.long:
Collisional torque density for trapped fast ions is the local source density of angular momentum transferred to or from the trapped fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions. It represents the full torque-density vector before any directional projection.

The torque-density vector is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{trapped}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}^{\mathrm{trapped}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{trapped}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}^{\mathrm{trapped}}$ is the angular-momentum density of trapped fast ions, $t$ is time, and the subscript $\mathrm{coll}$ restricts the transfer to Coulomb collisions.

The quantity is the trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), aggregating the included trapped fast ions and background collision partners. It excludes co-passing and counter-passing orbit contributions; [co-passing fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is a separate orbit-class contribution. Its toroidal projection is [toroidal trapped fast-ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when each vector component increases trapped fast-ion angular momentum in the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque density transferred to trapped fast ions, measuring angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry axis.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the angular-momentum transfer rate per unit plasma volume delivered to trapped fast ions by Coulomb collisions with background plasma species. It resolves the parent [trapped fast-ion collisional torque density](name:trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) specifically about the toroidal symmetry axis.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its scalar component. The vectors are expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, with $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ and $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ represented in N.m$^{-2}$.

Only the trapped fast-ion population and Coulomb-collision contribution are included; other orbit classes, ion populations, and collision-independent torque sources are excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional angular-momentum transfer to trapped fast ions points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional toroidal torque density (phi-component) transferred to fast particles via collisions with a given ion species, evaluated from the trapped part of the distribution function on 2D poloidal plane profiles.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque density to the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various ion species

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_particle_density
NAMES.short: Number density of suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits, obtained as the zeroth velocity moment over the trapped region of fast-particle phase space.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast-particle density is the local number density of non-thermal particles whose guiding-center orbits are magnetically trapped and mirror between bounce points. It is the trapped-orbit contribution to the total [fast-particle density](name:fast_particle_density), distinct from the passing contributions.

The density is the zeroth velocity moment of the fast-particle distribution restricted to trapped orbits:

$$
n_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{r})} f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the trapped fast-particle density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution function, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the velocity-space region whose guiding-center orbits are trapped. The complementary passing classes are represented by [co-passing fast-particle density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density) and [counter-passing fast-particle density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_density).

sources.enhanced_context: Fast particle density (n_fast) radial profile computed as a flux-surface-averaged quantity using only the trapped particle portion of the distribution function. Distinguishes fast trapped particle density from thermal and passing contributions.
sources.leaf_definition: Density of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged profile evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution.

sources.enhanced_context: Number density of fast (non-thermal) particles (n_fast) evaluated from the trapped particle part of the distribution function, given as a 2D poloidal plane profile. Represents the trapped fast particle population density.
sources.leaf_definition: Density of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged profile evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution.

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.short: Local Coulomb-collisional power density changing the kinetic-energy density of fast particles on trapped guiding-center orbits.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast-particle collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions change the kinetic-energy density of fast particles in the trapped guiding-center orbit class. It is one orbit-class contribution to the complete [fast-particle collisional power density](name:fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The orbit-class aggregation is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = P_{\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}} + P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} + P_{\mathrm{trapped}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the complete fast-particle collisional power density, $P_{\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ and $P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ are the co-passing and counter-passing contributions, and $P_{\mathrm{trapped}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this trapped-orbit contribution.

The quantity includes Coulomb energy exchange with all included charged collision partners and excludes the co-passing and counter-passing orbit classes represented separately by [counter-passing fast-particle collisional power density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions). Positive values denote net kinetic-energy gain by trapped fast particles; negative values denote net loss.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional power density transferred from the trapped particle distribution to the fast electron population, as a radial profile. Represents the energy exchange rate per unit volume between trapped particles and fast electrons via Coulomb collisions.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power density to the fast particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: trapped_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short: Kinetic pressure moment of the suprathermal particle distribution restricted to trapped guiding-center orbits; it is the flux-surface-averaged trapped-orbit contribution to fast-particle pressure.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast-particle pressure is the scalar trace pressure carried by suprathermal particles on trapped guiding-center orbits. It is the trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-particle pressure], complementary to the field-aligned [parallel trapped fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure) and transverse [perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure).

The flux-surface-averaged pressure is defined by the trapped-particle second velocity moment:

$$
P_{\mathrm{tr,fast}}(\psi) = \left\langle \frac{1}{3}\sum_s m_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s}(\mathbf{x})} v^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes its flux-surface average, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is particle mass in kg, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is particle speed in m s$^{-1}$, $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the distribution function, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s}$ contains only trapped guiding-center orbits. The factor one-third gives the scalar trace; with the same orbit selection, $P_{\mathrm{tr,fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,fast}})/3$. Co-passing and counter-passing populations are excluded.

sources.enhanced_context: Flux-surface-averaged total fast (non-thermal) particle pressure (P_fast) radial profile, computed using only the trapped particle portion of the distribution function. Represents the isotropic pressure contribution from energetic trapped particles.
sources.leaf_definition: Pressure of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged profile evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution.

sources.enhanced_context: Total pressure of fast (non-thermal) particles evaluated from the trapped population, as a 2D profile in the poloidal plane. Captures the fast particle pressure contribution from the trapped fraction of the distribution function.
sources.leaf_definition: Pressure of fast particles
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged profile evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution.

NAMES.name: parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short: Parallel trapped fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned kinetic pressure component carried by suprathermal particles on trapped guiding-center orbits.
NAMES.long:
Parallel trapped fast-particle pressure is the species-summed gyrotropic pressure component parallel to the local magnetic field contributed by suprathermal particles whose guiding-center orbits are magnetically trapped. It is the field-aligned component of [trapped fast-particle pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure), complementary to the transverse [perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure).

The flux-surface-averaged parallel pressure is defined by the trapped-particle second velocity moment:

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,fast}}(\psi) = \left\langle \sum_s m_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s}(\mathbf{x})} v_{\parallel}^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes its flux-surface average, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is particle mass in kg, $v_{\parallel}=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is velocity parallel to the unit magnetic-field direction $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, and $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the distribution function. The domain $\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s}$ contains only trapped guiding-center orbits; co-passing and counter-passing populations are excluded. With the same orbit selection, the parent scalar pressure satisfies $P_{\mathrm{tr,fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,fast}}+2P_{\perpendicular,\mathrm{tr,fast}})/3$.

sources.enhanced_context: Parallel pressure of fast (non-thermal) trapped particles (P_fast,∥), flux-surface-averaged, evaluated from the trapped orbit part of the distribution function. Represents the field-aligned component of the fast particle pressure tensor.
sources.leaf_definition: Pressure of fast particles in the parallel direction
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged profile evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution.

sources.enhanced_context: Parallel pressure of fast (non-thermal) particles (P_fast,∥) evaluated from the trapped particle part of the distribution function, given as a 2D profile in the poloidal plane. Captures the anisotropic fast-particle pressure contribution along the magnetic field.
sources.leaf_definition: Pressure of fast particles in the parallel direction
sources.parent_definition: Flux surface averaged profile evaluated using the trapped particle part of the distribution.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.short: Perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure is the transverse kinetic pressure moment of suprathermal particles on trapped guiding-center orbits, averaged over magnetic flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure is the component of the pressure tensor perpendicular to the magnetic field, carried by suprathermal particles on trapped guiding-center orbits. It complements the field-aligned [parallel trapped fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure).

The flux-surface-averaged perpendicular pressure is defined by

$$
P_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,fast}}(\psi) = \left\langle \frac{1}{2}\sum_s m_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s}(\mathbf{x})} v_\perp^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes its flux-surface average, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is particle mass in kg, $v_\perp$ is perpendicular speed in m s$^{-1}$, $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the distribution function, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{tr},s}$ contains only trapped guiding-center orbits.

With the same orbit selection, the scalar [trapped fast-particle pressure](name:trapped_fast_particle_pressure) satisfies $P_{\mathrm{tr,fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,fast}})/3$. Unlike [perpendicular fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), this quantity excludes co-passing and counter-passing populations.
