NAMES.name: trapped_power_density
NAMES.short: Volumetric energy source rate for the trapped orbit-class particle population, giving the local power density deposited into or extracted from magnetically bouncing particles through heating and collisional processes.
NAMES.long:
Trapped particles are those whose parallel velocity is insufficient to overcome the magnetic mirror force and complete a full poloidal orbit; they execute closed banana orbits between two turning points on a given flux surface. The trapped power density is the net volumetric rate at which energy enters or leaves this orbit-class subpopulation through all active heating and collisional mechanisms.

In a Fokker-Planck kinetic description, the trapped power density is the energy moment of the total distribution-function source operator $S(\mathbf{v})$ restricted to the trapped velocity-space domain:

$$
P_\mathrm{trap} = \int_\mathrm{trap} \frac{m v^2}{2} \, S(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m$ is the particle mass, $v$ is the particle speed, and the integral covers pitch angles satisfying $|v_\parallel/v| < \sqrt{1 - B_\mathrm{min}/B_\mathrm{max}}$, with $B_\mathrm{min}$ and $B_\mathrm{max}$ the minimum and maximum field strength on the flux surface.

This quantity is computed in kinetic transport models that partition velocity space into orbit classes, appearing alongside [co-passing power density](name:co_passing_power_density) and [counter-passing power density](name:counter_passing_power_density) as components of the orbit-resolved local energy budget. Sources include neutral beam injection, ion cyclotron resonance heating, and Coulomb collisions that preferentially populate or drain trapped orbits. The corresponding particle source for the same subpopulation is [trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate](name:trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate), and the total trapped particle number density is [trapped_density](name:total_trapped_particle_density).

sources.enhanced_context: Source rate of energy density contributed by the trapped particle portion of the distribution function. Represents the volumetric energy source term from heating or collisional processes acting on trapped particles in a Fokker-Planck model.
sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of energy density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed local volumetric Coulomb-collisional energy-transfer rate from trapped fast particle populations to the bulk thermal electron population, with positive values denoting net electron heating.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal-electron power density due to collisions is the local rate per unit volume at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from the trapped part of a fast or otherwise non-Maxwellian particle population to the bulk thermal electron population.

The quantity is defined by

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{th};\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_a Q_{e,\mathrm{th}\leftarrow a,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{th};\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the trapped-particle contribution to the [thermal-electron power density due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), $Q_{e,\mathrm{th}\leftarrow a,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate from source population $a$, and $\mathrm{tr}$ denotes the trapped orbit class.

This quantity is the trapped-orbit component of the parent collisional power density and excludes co-passing and counter-passing contributions, such as [co-passing thermal-electron power density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions). Its volume integral contributes to [thermal-electron power due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the bulk thermal electron population gains energy from the trapped collision partners.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional power density (P_coll) transferred from the trapped particle distribution to the thermal electron population, as a 1D radial profile. Represents the collisional energy exchange rate per unit volume between fast/non-Maxwellian trapped particles and bulk electrons.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional power density transferred to the thermal electron population via collisions with the distribution species, evaluated using the trapped part of the distribution function. Given as a 2D profile in the poloidal plane.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional power density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Trapped thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate to the trapped-orbit part of the bulk thermal electron population from Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local rate per unit volume at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum to the trapped-orbit part of the bulk, near-Maxwellian thermal electron population.

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{e,\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

Here $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis, and $\mathbf{f}_{e,\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to trapped thermal electrons.

This quantity is the trapped-orbit component of [thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). It excludes contributions assigned to other electron orbit classes and non-Coulomb processes; its toroidal projection is represented by [toroidal trapped thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions), while [toroidal thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is the corresponding unpartitioned projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the corresponding component of transferred angular momentum points along the positive $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the local collisional angular-momentum transfer density delivered by Coulomb collisions to trapped thermal electrons. The trapped qualifier identifies the receiving orbit class, not the collision partner.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the local collisional angular-momentum transfer density to trapped thermal electrons is the volume density of toroidal angular momentum delivered to that receiving population by Coulomb collisions. The trapped qualifier identifies thermal electrons whose guiding-center orbits are trapped; it does not restrict the collision partner.

The torque density is the major-radius lever arm multiplying the toroidal collisional force-density moment of the trapped thermal-electron distribution:

$$
\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = R(\mathbf{x})\,m_e \int v_\phi\, C_{e,\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{v};\mathbf{x})\, d^3v
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this torque density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $m_e$ is electron mass, $v_\phi$ is the velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$, and $C_{e,\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collision-operator contribution to the evolution of the trapped thermal-electron distribution.

This quantity includes collisional momentum exchange with all collision partners. The electron-electron partner contribution is [toroidal trapped thermal electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons); together with the co-passing and counter-passing thermal-electron orbit-class contributions it forms the orbit-class decomposition of [toroidal thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). It is distinct from the corresponding ion charge-state quantity [toroidal trapped thermal ion charge state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional toroidal force on trapped thermal electrons acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional toroidal torque density (φ-component) transferred to the thermal particle population from the trapped part of the distribution via collisions with electrons, as a flux-surface-averaged 1D radial profile.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Trapped thermal-electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per volume delivered to trapped thermal electrons by electron-electron collisions. It is defined before projection onto any spatial component.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal-electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons is the local vector angular-momentum transfer rate density delivered to trapped thermal electrons by electron-electron Coulomb collisions. It is the full torque-density vector before selecting a spatial projection or component.

The vector is defined from the corresponding collisional force density about the reference origin for angular momentum:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e\to e_{\mathrm{th,tr}}}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{r}(\mathbf{x}) \times \mathbf{f}_{e\to e_{\mathrm{th,tr}}}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from the reference origin to $\mathbf{x}$, and $\mathbf{f}_{e\to e_{\mathrm{th,tr}}}$ is the force density exerted on trapped thermal electrons by electron-electron Coulomb collisions.

The recipient population is restricted to trapped thermal electrons; passing thermal electrons, non-thermal electrons, ions, and torques from interactions other than electron-electron Coulomb collisions are excluded. The [thermal electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons) is the broader population quantity without the trapped-orbit restriction. The [toroidal trapped thermal-electron torque density due to Coulomb collisions with electrons](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons) is the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$ projections are equally valid spatial-component specializations of this vector.
NAMES.sign: Positive when electron-electron Coulomb collisions transfer angular momentum to trapped thermal electrons in the positive sense of the resolved component.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Signed toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to trapped thermal electrons by electron-electron Coulomb collisions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the local torque density transferred to trapped thermal electrons by electron-electron Coulomb collisions. It represents the collisional angular-momentum transfer rate associated with the trapped thermal-electron population.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\tau_\phi = \boldsymbol{\tau} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}$ is the vector torque density defined by [trapped thermal-electron torque density due to electron-electron Coulomb collisions](name:trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons), and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This component excludes the radial and vertical projections and is not the magnitude of the vector torque density.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transferred torque points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with electrons

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer to thermal ions of a specified charge state from the trapped guiding-center orbit class of non-Maxwellian source particles.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions is the local volumetric rate at which trapped non-Maxwellian fast particles transfer kinetic energy to thermal ions in one specified charge state through Coulomb collisions. It is the trapped guiding-center orbit-class component of [thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), the thermal-ion-targeted part of [ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The trapped contribution $p_{\mathrm{th},i,z}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the source-population sum of the velocity-space integral of the energy-transfer collision frequency against the trapped part of each non-Maxwellian source distribution:

$$
p_{\mathrm{th},i,z}^{\mathrm{tr}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathcal{T}_s} \nu_{\epsilon,s}^{(z)}(v)\,\frac{m_s v^2}{2}\,f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $i$ denotes the thermal-ion species, $z$ denotes the specified charge state, $s$ indexes non-Maxwellian source populations, $\mathcal{T}_s$ is the subset of local source-particle velocity space for population $s$ whose guiding-center orbits are trapped, $\nu_{\epsilon,s}^{(z)}(v)$ is the energy-transfer collision frequency from source population $s$ particles of speed $v$ to thermal ions of charge state $z$, $m_s$ is the source-particle mass, and $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the local source-particle velocity distribution.

The co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit-class components partition [thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions); the complementary components are [co-passing thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing thermal ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions). This quantity is resolved per target-ion charge state and not summed over charge states, while the source-particle side is summed over all non-Maxwellian source populations indexed by $s$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when thermal ions of the specified charge state gain net kinetic energy through Coulomb collisions with trapped non-Maxwellian source particles.

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Trapped collisional torque density is the vector angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge state from Coulomb collisions with trapped particles.
NAMES.long:
Trapped collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a specified charge state from Coulomb collisions with the trapped population.

With $\mathrm{tr}$ denoting this collision channel, the local torque density is defined by the moment of the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{tr}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{tr}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the local plasma volume, and $\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the collisional force density exerted on the specified thermal ion charge state by trapped particles. The charge-state selection is retained rather than summed over ionization states. This is the trapped contribution to [thermal ion charge-state collisional torque density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and differs from the corresponding [co-passing quantity](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing quantity](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) by the collision-partner orbit class.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume from Coulomb collisions to trapped thermal ions in a specified charge state, projected in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the collisional torque-density vector delivered to trapped thermal ions in a specified ionic charge state. It represents angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume from Coulomb collisions with background charged species.

The toroidal projection is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}}$ is the [trapped thermal ion charge-state collisional torque density](name:trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions), $q$ identifies the ionic charge state, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity retains only the toroidal projection and remains resolved in ion charge state; it excludes torque transferred to passing or other ion populations and contributions attributed to noncollisional processes. The charge-state-aggregated counterpart is [toroidal trapped thermal ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional toroidal torque density (phi-component, φ) transferred from the trapped particle distribution to a thermal ion charge state. A 2D poloidal-plane profile of momentum exchange via Coulomb collisions.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various states of the ion species (ionisation, energy, excitation, ...)

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Trapped thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed local volumetric rate of kinetic-energy transfer to or from bulk thermal ions through Coulomb collisions with trapped fast particles.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal-ion collisional power density is the local volumetric rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to or from the aggregate thermal ion population through interactions with trapped fast particles. It is the trapped-orbit contribution to [thermal-ion collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The defining trapped-orbit contribution is

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_{a\in\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{th}}} Q_{a\leftarrow\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th,tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this power density, $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the set of included thermal-ion target populations, and $Q_{a\leftarrow\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional kinetic-energy transfer rate to target population $a$ from trapped fast particles.

The target population is aggregated over the included thermal-ion species and charge states. Collisional power received by trapped fast ions is excluded; the charge-state-resolved target contribution is [trapped thermal-ion charge-state power density due to collisions](name:trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), while the corresponding counter-passing contribution is [counter-passing thermal-ion power density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the aggregate thermal ion population gains kinetic energy from collisions with trapped fast particles.

sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various ion species

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Local angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to trapped thermal ions through Coulomb collisions with other charged populations.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per unit volume transferred to the trapped thermal-ion population by Coulomb collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is a vector quantity before any directional projection.

The torque density follows from the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{tr}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{tr}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the torque density transferred to trapped thermal ions, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the toroidal symmetry axis, and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the corresponding collisional force density.

This is the trapped-population branch of [thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions). The [toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) quantity is its toroidal projection, while [trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) resolves the recipient ions by charge state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component of the torque vector points along the corresponding positive basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the collisional torque density transferred to trapped thermal ions, giving angular-momentum deposition per unit volume from charged-particle collisions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the torque density transferred to trapped thermal ions by Coulomb collisions with charged particles represented in the kinetic collision operator.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $\mathcal{T}_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its toroidal component. The quantity is the toroidal component of [trapped thermal ion torque density due to collisions](name:trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), not a torque density resolved by ion charge state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the collisional torque acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various ion species

sources.enhanced_context: Collisional toroidal torque density (phi-component) transferred to the thermal ion population via collisions with the distribution function particles, evaluated from the trapped particle part of the distribution in 2D poloidal profiles.
sources.leaf_definition: Collisional toroidal torque density to the thermal particle population
sources.parent_definition: Collisional exchange with the various ion species

NAMES.name: trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles are added to or removed from the trapped orbit population. Trapped particles have pitch angles that cause their parallel velocity to reverse along a magnetic field line, producing bounce motion between mirror points.
NAMES.long:
Trapped thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the trapped orbit class. Trapped particles have pitch angles that cause their parallel velocity to reverse along a magnetic field line, producing bounce motion between mirror points rather than continuous toroidal circulation. It is the trapped-orbit component of the [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate).

For a magnetic flux surface labeled by $\psi$, it is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{trap}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\left\langle \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{trap}}} \mathcal{S}_{n}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{trap}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the trapped thermal particle source rate, $\Omega_{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the trapped-orbit region of velocity space, $\mathcal{S}_{n}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local kinetic particle source term for thermal particles, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes a flux-surface average.

The quantity excludes source contributions assigned to the co-passing and counter-passing orbit classes. With a consistent orbit decomposition, the sum of this quantity, the [co-passing thermal particle source rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), and the [counter-passing thermal particle source rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) gives the flux-surface-averaged [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate); volume integration of the summed volumetric rate gives the [total thermal particle source rate](name:total_thermal_particle_source_rate).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net source adds thermal particles to the trapped orbit population.

sources.enhanced_context: Source rate of particle density for the trapped particle component of the distribution function, flux-surface averaged. Represents the net rate of particles entering or leaving the trapped phase-space population per unit volume in Fokker-Planck modelling.
sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of thermal particle density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: trapped_torque_density
NAMES.short: Local angular momentum source density per unit volume from the trapped-orbit particle population, giving the full vector contribution of banana-orbit particles to the plasma angular momentum balance from wave, beam, or collisional processes.
NAMES.long:
Trapped-particle torque density is the local rate at which angular momentum is deposited per unit volume by particles on banana (trapped) orbits in a magnetically confined plasma. Trapped particles mirror between their turning points along the field line due to the magnetic gradient and undergo net angular momentum exchange through wave–particle interactions, neutral beam deposition, Coulomb collisions, and the $\mathbf{j} \times \mathbf{B}$ Lorentz force; the resulting volumetric momentum source defines this vector quantity.

The quantity is the first velocity moment of the momentum source operator $Q$ restricted to the trapped phase-space domain:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{trap} = \int m \, \mathbf{v} \, Q[f_\mathrm{trap}] \, d^3v
$$

where $m$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity, and $Q[f_\mathrm{trap}]$ is the net source — collisional, wave-driven, or from external injection — acting on the trapped distribution $f_\mathrm{trap}$.

In tokamak geometry, the toroidal projection is the primary quantity of interest because toroidal angular momentum is approximately conserved in axisymmetric configurations; [toroidal_trapped_torque_density](name:toroidal_trapped_torque_density) quantifies this component. The Lorentz-force contribution is separated in [trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force](name:trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force), and the collisional channel to thermal ions is captured by trapped_thermal_ion_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions. The co-passing counterpart [toroidal_co_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density) carries the passing-orbit share of the total torque balance.
NAMES.sign: Positive when angular momentum is deposited in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_torque_density
NAMES.short: Toroidal trapped torque density is the local rate of change of toroidal angular momentum per physical volume, about the symmetry axis, due to magnetically trapped particles. It equals the major-radius lever arm times their toroidal force density in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal trapped torque density is the local rate of change of toroidal angular momentum per physical volume, about the symmetry axis, due to magnetically trapped particles. It is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation to the local toroidal force density of the trapped population is:

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}} = R f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the toroidal trapped torque density, $R$ is the major-radius lever arm measured from the symmetry axis, and $f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the toroidal component of the trapped-particle force density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The trapped population consists of particles whose pitch and magnetic mirroring cause bounce motion between turning points rather than a full poloidal transit. This quantity excludes the passing-particle contributions represented by [toroidal_co_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density) and [toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density); when the same distribution is partitioned by orbit class, the trapped, co-passing, and counter-passing contributions sum to the corresponding [toroidal_torque_density](name:toroidal_torque_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the trapped-particle toroidal force density is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Source rate of toroidal angular momentum density contributed by the trapped particle fraction of the distribution function. Represents the toroidal momentum injection rate per unit volume from wave or particle source processes acting on trapped particles.
sources.leaf_definition: Source rate of toroidal angular momentum density
sources.parent_definition: Set of flux averaged sources and sinks of particles, momentum and energy included in the Fokker-Planck modelling, related to the various waves or particle source processes affecting the distribution

NAMES.name: trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated when a trapped-particle current interacts with a magnetic field through the Lorentz force.
NAMES.long:
This vector quantity is the torque density transferred to trapped particles by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with their current contribution.

The defining local relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}=\mathbf{r}\times(\mathbf{J}\times\mathbf{B})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}$ is the torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin, $\mathbf{J}$ is the current-density contribution associated with the trapped particles, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field. The cross products follow the right-hand rule.

This quantity selects the trapped-particle contribution within the broader [torque density due to J×B force](name:torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force); it is not itself restricted to a toroidal projection or flux-surface average. The [toroidal trapped J×B torque density](name:toroidal_trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) adds those component and averaging specifications.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source density delivered to trapped particles by the Lorentz force from their current crossing the poloidal magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal angular-momentum source density exerted on trapped particles by the J×B Lorentz force, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. It isolates the trapped-particle contribution and the toroidal component of the torque from the corresponding local quantity [trapped torque density due to J×B force](name:trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).

$$
\left\langle \tau_{\phi,\mathrm{tr}} \right\rangle_\psi = \left\langle R\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}} \times \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pol}}\right) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \right\rangle_\psi
$$

Here $R$ is major radius in meters, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped-particle current density, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal magnetic field, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes a magnetic-flux-surface average. Passing-particle contributions and non-Lorentz-force mechanisms are excluded.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the Lorentz force drives trapped-particle angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

sources.enhanced_context: Toroidal torque density (φ-component) due to radial currents, evaluated using the trapped particle portion of the distribution function, as a flux-surface-averaged 1D radial profile. Represents the angular momentum source in the toroidal direction from trapped particle radial currents.

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Particle number density of tritium ions at the internal transport barrier, the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep radial fuel-ion density gradients to form.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of tritium ions at the internal transport barrier is the local number density of tritium ions on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. The internal transport barrier is a confined-plasma region where effective cross-field transport is locally reduced, allowing steep density gradients to form and persist.

The local tritium-ion density $n_T$ at the ITB reference surface is the zeroth velocity moment of the charge-state-resolved distribution functions:

$$
n_T(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_Z \int f_{T,Z}(\mathbf{v}, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\,d^3v
$$

where $Z$ labels tritium ion charge states, $f_{T,Z}$ is the corresponding velocity distribution, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ identifies the ITB flux surface in coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. This quantity is summed over all tritium ion charge states and excludes neutral tritium. It is the tritium-specific counterpart of [ion density at the internal transport barrier](name:ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and contributes to the species-agnostic [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

NAMES.name: tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Number density of tritium ions at the magnetic axis, the innermost point of the confined plasma where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux vanishes.
NAMES.long:
Tritium density at the magnetic axis is the local number density of tritium ions evaluated at the singular center of the nested closed magnetic flux surfaces. The magnetic axis is the point $(R_{\rm axis}, Z_{\rm axis})$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame — where $R$ is the major radius from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is the vertical height — at which $\nabla\psi = 0$, with $\psi$ the poloidal magnetic flux; this is the species-specific realization of [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis) for the tritium fuel species.

In the hot plasma core, tritium is essentially fully ionized as $T^+$ (charge state +1), so this quantity captures the entire on-axis tritium ion population. It forms the tritium-side complement to [deuterium_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:deuterium_density_at_magnetic_axis) in characterizing the DT fuel mixture at the plasma center; the ratio of the two densities reflects the local fueling balance. The profile boundary value of the same species is given by [tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

On-axis fuel species densities are inferred from charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, neutral beam injection diagnostics, or constrained equilibrium reconstruction supplemented by line-integrated interferometry. In high-performance DT discharges, central ion densities are of order $10^{19}$–$10^{20}$ m$^{-3}$, with the tritium fraction determined by the relative fueling rates of the two fuel isotopes.

NAMES.name: tritium_tritium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion
NAMES.subject: tritium_tritium
NAMES.short: Total neutron production rate from the thermonuclear tritium-tritium reaction branch among Maxwellian bulk tritons, excluding beam-target and beam-beam fast-ion contributions.
NAMES.long:
The total neutron source rate due to thermal fusion is the number of neutrons produced per unit time by the thermal tritium-tritium reaction branch between bulk tritons with locally Maxwellian velocity distributions. It is the tritium-tritium channel member of [neutron source rate due to thermal fusion](name:neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion) and contributes to the channel-summed [total neutron source rate due to thermal fusion](name:total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion).

The tritium-tritium thermal neutron source rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,TT}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int_V 2\,\frac{n_T^2}{2}\,\langle\sigma v\rangle_{TT}(T_T)\,dV
$$

where $S_{n,TT}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the source rate, $V$ is the emitting plasma volume, $n_T$ is the local bulk triton number density, $\langle\sigma v\rangle_{TT}$ is the Maxwellian-averaged tritium-tritium fusion reactivity, $T_T$ is the local triton temperature, and $dV$ is a volume element. The factor of two is the neutron multiplicity of the tritium-tritium branch, while the denominator prevents double counting identical triton pairs.

Only reactions between locally Maxwellian bulk tritons are included; beam-target, beam-beam, fusion-product, and other nonthermal fast-ion contributions are excluded. The deuterium-deuterium channel, including its neutron-producing branch, is a separate contribution described by [deuterium-deuterium neutron source rate due to thermal fusion](name:deuterium_deuterium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion).

NAMES.name: tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Particle number density of tungsten ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes, summed over all positive ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of tungsten ions evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local count of tungsten ions per physical volume at the innermost flux-surface singularity. The magnetic axis is the locus where the gradient of [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) vanishes. This is the tungsten-specific realization of [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis).

The on-axis tungsten density is defined as the limiting local density at the magnetic-axis point:

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}} n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the tungsten-ion number-density field in m$^{-3}$ and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position. The quantity sums tungsten ions over all positive ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten, complementing the corresponding local quantity [tungsten_density](name:tungsten_density).

NAMES.name: upper_bound_charge_number
NAMES.short: Integer upper-bound charge number specifying the highest ionization state included in a grouped set of ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
An upper-bound charge number is the largest ionic charge number represented in a defined group of ionization states. It sets the upper endpoint of the group's integer charge-state range, as in the concrete [ion upper-bound charge number](name:ion_upper_bound_charge_number).

Let $S$ be the set of charge numbers included in the group and let $Z$ denote an individual ionization charge number. The upper bound is defined by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{upper}} = \max\{Z \mid Z \in S\}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{upper}}$ is the maximum included charge number and $S$ is the charge-state set.

This quantity identifies a range boundary, not an average charge or the charge of a single unspecified ion. The corresponding lower endpoint is represented by the [ion charge-state lower-bound charge](name:ion_charge_state_lower_bound_charge), while an averaged charge is represented by the [ion charge-state average charge number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number).

NAMES.name: ion_upper_bound_charge_number
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Maximum charge number of the ionization states grouped into an ion charge-state bundle, setting the upper end of the bundle's integer charge-state range.
NAMES.long:
The ion upper-bound charge number $Z_\mathrm{max}$ is the largest ionization charge number included in a grouped ion charge-state bundle. The charge number equals the count of electrons removed from the neutral atom and takes non-negative integer values.

Together with [ion_charge_state_lower_bound_charge](name:ion_charge_state_lower_bound_charge), it defines the closed integer interval $[Z_\mathrm{min}, Z_\mathrm{max}]$ of ionization states aggregated into the bundle. The concentration-weighted mean over this interval is given by [ion_charge_state_average_charge_number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number).

This quantity is the ion-subject specialization of [upper_bound_charge_number](name:upper_bound_charge_number), restricting the concept to ionic species. It excludes neutral atoms ($Z = 0$) and fully stripped nuclei are included only when the bundle range extends to the atomic number of the element.

NAMES.name: velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: The velocity due to diamagnetic drift is a signed scalar component of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid velocity contribution for a charged plasma population, charge state, or charged internal state. It is the projection of the diamagnetic drift vector onto a specified component direction, not a guiding-center particle drift.
NAMES.long:
The velocity due to diamagnetic drift is a signed scalar component of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid velocity contribution for a charged plasma population, charge state, or charged internal state. It is the projection of the population diamagnetic-drift vector onto a selected component direction and represents a fluid moment flow, not the guiding-center drift of individual particles.

For a charged population $\alpha$ and component unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_c$, the defining scalar component is:

$$
v_{\ast \alpha,c} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_c
$$

where $p_\alpha$ is the partial pressure of population $\alpha$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is the number density, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_c$ is the unit vector in the selected component direction.

Specific component qualifiers determine $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_c$: radial, toroidal, and vertical components project onto $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$ in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; a parallel component projects along $\mathbf{B}$; a [diamagnetic component](name:diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) projects along the local diamagnetic-drift direction; and a flux-surface-normal component projects toward increasing flux label. Because velocity is intensive, a species-level value that is not charge-state resolved is the density-weighted mean over all charge states, $v_{\ast s,c}=(\sum_z n_{sz}v_{\ast sz,c})/(\sum_z n_{sz})$; it is not summed over charge states. Charge-state-resolved members include [parallel ion charge-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [ion charge-state diamagnetic velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). The direct electromagnetic definition is restricted to populations with nonzero signed charge and does not define a neutral-population drift for $q_\alpha=0$; it excludes [velocity due to E-cross-B drift](name:velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), polarization drift, curvature drift, and imposed parallel flow.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the pressure-gradient diamagnetic drift vector has a positive projection onto the positive component direction $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_c$.

NAMES.name: diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: The diamagnetic velocity due to diamagnetic drift is a signed scalar component of the pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular drift of a plasma population. It is the projection of the diamagnetic-drift velocity vector onto the local diamagnetic direction set by the magnetic field crossed with the population pressure gradient.
NAMES.long:
The diamagnetic velocity due to diamagnetic drift is a signed scalar component of the pressure-gradient-driven perpendicular drift of a plasma population. It is the projection of the population diamagnetic-drift velocity vector onto the local diamagnetic direction defined by the magnetic field crossed with the population pressure gradient, perpendicular to both $\mathbf{B}$ and $\nabla p_s$.

The signed component for population $s$ is defined by:

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia},s} = \mathbf{v}_{\ast s}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia},s},\qquad
\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia},s} = \frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_s}{|\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_s|}
$$

where $v_{\mathrm{dia},s}$ is the signed scalar component, $\mathbf{v}_{\ast s}$ is the population diamagnetic-drift velocity vector in meters per second, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{dia},s}$ is the unit diamagnetic direction, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field vector in teslas, $p_s$ is the population pressure in pascals, and $\nabla p_s$ is the population pressure gradient in pascals per meter.

This scalar is the diamagnetic-direction projection of [velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), not a direction-independent speed. Bulk-plasma and charge-state-resolved counterparts, such as [plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), use the pressure and drift velocity of their stated population. When $\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_s=\mathbf{0}$, the diamagnetic direction is undefined and the pressure-gradient diamagnetic component is zero.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projected diamagnetic-drift velocity points along $\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_s$.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: The specified component of charge-state-resolved ion velocity due to diamagnetic drift is the signed projection of the charge state's pressure-gradient drift onto an explicitly defined positive direction.
NAMES.long:
The specified component of charge-state-resolved ion velocity due to diamagnetic drift is the signed scalar projection of the diamagnetic drift velocity for one ionization state of an ion species. The drift is generated by that charge state's partial-pressure gradient in the local magnetic field and is distinct from the total fluid velocity.

For an ionized charge state $c$ with charge number $Z_c>0$ and specified positive unit direction $\hat{\mathbf{a}}$, the component is defined by

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia},c}^{(a)} = \hat{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},c} = \hat{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p_c}{Z_c e\, n_c\, B^2}
$$

where $v_{\mathrm{dia},c}^{(a)}$ is the signed scalar component, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},c}$ is the vector diamagnetic drift velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{a}}$ is the specified positive unit direction, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, $p_c$ is the charge-state partial pressure, $\nabla p_c$ is its spatial gradient, $n_c$ is the charge-state number density, and $e$ is the elementary charge.

This quantity is charge-state resolved; no sum or density-weighted mean over ionization states is implied. It includes only the diamagnetic contribution from $\nabla p_c$ and excludes electric-field, curvature, polarization, collisional, and parallel-flow velocity contributions. The scalar is not a speed and has a defined value only after $\hat{\mathbf{a}}$ is specified. The concrete family members define common choices of $\hat{\mathbf{a}}$: [radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) uses $+\hat{R}$, [toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) uses $+\hat{\phi}$, and [vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) uses $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; [parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) uses the local magnetic-field direction; [perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is defined relative to the magnetic-field direction and is not a flux-surface-normal projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot(\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p_c)>0$.

NAMES.name: velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short: Velocity due to E cross B drift is the nonnegative magnitude of the drift velocity produced by crossed local electric and magnetic fields in a magnetized plasma; it is a speed, not a signed projection along a named axis. For magnetized charged species this drift is independent of particle mass and charge sign.
NAMES.long:
Velocity due to E cross B drift is the nonnegative magnitude of the drift velocity arising from crossed electric and magnetic fields in a magnetized plasma. Because the underlying drift depends only on the local field ratio, it is identical for all magnetized charged species regardless of particle mass or charge sign, and the drift by itself carries no net current.

The defining relation is:

$$
v_{E\times B} = \frac{|\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}|}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector. The underlying drift vector $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|^2$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$ and has no component along the magnetic-field direction; consequently any parallel projection of this drift vanishes identically.

This quantity is the speed of the drift and is therefore nonnegative; it must not be confused with signed axis-resolved projections of the drift vector, such as the toroidal projection for a specific ion charge state in [toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) or the parallel projection for a neutral internal state in [parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). Population-resolved counterparts of the same drift family are provided for individual ion charge states in [ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), for internal states in [internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), and for neutral-species internal states in [neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Velocity due to E cross B drift for a specified ion charge state is the guiding-center drift vector produced by crossed local electric and magnetic fields, independent of ion mass and charge.
NAMES.long:
Velocity due to E cross B drift for a specified ion charge state is the guiding-center drift vector produced by local crossed electric and magnetic fields in a magnetized plasma. It is common to all magnetized charged species at the same position, although this name resolves it to one ion charge state.

The defining relation is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{E\times B} = \frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector. The resulting vector is perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$, and its magnitude is the parent [velocity due to E cross B drift](name:velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).

This vector quantity must be distinguished from its signed axis projections, including the [radial ion charge-state velocity due to E cross B drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) and [toroidal ion charge-state velocity due to E cross B drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). The ion charge-state resolution identifies the represented population but does not introduce mass- or charge-dependent variation in the drift itself.

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the E×B guiding-center drift velocity for a specified ion charge state, signed along increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal component of the E×B drift velocity for an ion charge state is the signed projection of the cross-field guiding-center drift onto the poloidal direction. It is independent of ion mass and charge at a fixed position and is a component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).

The defining projection is

$$
v_{E\times B,\theta} = \left(\frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol e}_\theta
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\boldsymbol e}_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. The associated geometric decomposition uses the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The [radial ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the corresponding major-radius projection. This quantity differs from the [poloidal ion charge-state diamagnetic drift velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) because its mechanism is electric-field cross magnetic-field drift rather than pressure-gradient drift.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projected velocity points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Radial component of the E×B guiding-center drift velocity for a specified ion charge state, projected along increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial component of the E×B guiding-center drift velocity for a specified ion charge state is the projection of the local electric-field drift onto the major-radius direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is one component of the full vector quantity [ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).

The component is defined by projecting the E×B drift onto $\hat{R}$:

$$
v_{E \times B,R}^{(q)} = \hat{R} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $v_{E \times B,R}^{(q)}$ is the radial component for ion charge state $q$, $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric field, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field.

Radial denotes the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ component and is not a projection along the normal to a magnetic flux surface. At fixed electromagnetic fields the E×B guiding-center drift is independent of ion mass and charge, so the charge-state label selects the ion charge-state population rather than changing the drift formula.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the E×B drift has a component in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the E×B guiding-center drift velocity for a specified ion charge state in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal component is the projection of the E×B guiding-center drift velocity for a specified ion charge state onto the toroidal direction. It is the component of the full vector quantity [ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) along increasing toroidal angle.

The drift velocity and its toroidal projection are defined by

$$
\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}=\frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2},\qquad v_{E\times B,\phi}=\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The E×B drift is independent of ion mass and charge at a fixed position. This quantity excludes the pressure-gradient contribution represented by the [toroidal ion charge-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift); its radial counterpart is the [radial ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projected velocity points along $+\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vertical Z-component of the bulk fluid velocity of neutral particles in a single resolved internal quantum state, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical projection of [bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), giving the $\hat{Z}$ component of the mean fluid velocity for a neutral species resolved into one specific internal state (electronic, vibrational, or rotational level).

It is defined as:

$$
v_Z^{\text{neut,state}} = \mathbf{v}_{\text{bulk,neut,state}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\text{bulk,neut,state}}$ is the first velocity moment of the neutral distribution function for that internal state, normalized by the state number density, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is state-resolved: each internal state contributes its own fluid velocity, and these do not in general equal one another. The species-level vertical neutral velocity — aggregated over all internal states — is given by [vertical_neutral_velocity](name:vertical_neutral_velocity). The corresponding vertical momentum-flux density for the state is given by [vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux](name:vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral bulk flow is directed in the $+Z$ direction (increasing vertical height).

NAMES.name: vertical_conductivity
NAMES.short: Vertical conductivity is the diagonal vertical (Z-Z) element of the electrical conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the local material coefficient giving the same-direction conductive vertical current density driven by the vertical electric field.
NAMES.long:
Vertical conductivity is the diagonal vertical (Z-Z) element of the electrical conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, whose basis is $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the local material coefficient giving the same-direction part of the conductive vertical current-density component driven by the vertical electric-field component.

For the diagonal vertical response, the defining component relation is:

$$
J_{Z,\mathrm{diag}}^\mathrm{cond} = \sigma_Z E_Z
$$

where $J_{Z,\mathrm{diag}}^\mathrm{cond}$ is the same-direction conductive contribution to the vertical current-density component, $E_Z$ is the vertical electric-field component, and $\sigma_Z$ is the vertical conductivity. Equivalently, $\sigma_Z = \hat{Z}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\hat{Z}$, where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the electrical conductivity tensor.

This quantity is only the vertical diagonal tensor element. In the full tensor relation, the conductive vertical current-density component may also contain off-diagonal terms driven by $E_R$ or $E_\phi$; those cross-direction responses, including Hall terms, are outside the scope of vertical conductivity. It is distinct from [vertical_current_density](name:vertical_current_density), which is a current-density component rather than a material response coefficient. Matched cylindrical diagonal conductivity components are [radial_conductivity](name:radial_conductivity) and [toroidal_conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity).

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the electrical current density generated by anomalous, turbulence-driven transport, projected along the geometric Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical component of the anomalous current density, $j_{Z,\mathrm{anom}}$, is the projection of the full [current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) vector onto the geometric vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It is distinguished from the [radial_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:radial_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) by its projection direction.

The defining projection is

$$
j_{Z,\mathrm{anom}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the anomalous current-density vector and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the geometric vertical unit vector.

This quantity includes only the anomalous-transport contribution to the [vertical_current_density](name:vertical_current_density); the contribution due to ion-fluid inertia is represented separately by [vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the anomalous conventional current points in the $+Z$ direction, vertically upward, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: Vertical current density produced by diamagnetic drift in a magnetized plasma, projected onto the Z direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical current density due to diamagnetic drift is the cylindrical-$Z$ projection, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of the pressure-gradient-driven current described by [current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It is a signed component along the vertical basis direction $\hat{Z}$, not a magnitude of the diamagnetic current density.

For scalar pressure $p$, the vertical component is defined by projecting the diamagnetic current density onto $\hat{Z}$:

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},Z} = \left(\frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p}{B^2}\right) \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},Z}$ is the vertical current density due to diamagnetic drift, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B^2=\mathbf{B}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ is the squared magnetic-field magnitude, $\nabla p$ is the plasma pressure gradient, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is the vertical component of the same diamagnetic-drift current vector whose cylindrical-$R$ and toroidal projections are [radial_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:radial_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes field-aligned return currents such as [pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and does not represent a vertical particle flux.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the diamagnetic drift current density has a component in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the electric current density arising from ion-fluid inertial acceleration, projected along the Z direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical projection of the current density due to ion inertia is the electric-current component generated by inertial acceleration terms in the ion-fluid momentum equation. It includes the $Z$ component of the polarization-type current associated with finite ion mass and time-dependent or convective ion-fluid acceleration, taken along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The vertical component is the projection of the ion-inertia current density vector onto $\hat{Z}$:

$$
J_{Z,\mathrm{inertia}} = \hat{Z}\cdot \left(\frac{m_i n_i}{B^2}\mathbf{B}\times \frac{d_i\mathbf{v}_i}{dt}\right)
$$

where $J_{Z,\mathrm{inertia}}$ is the vertical projection, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, $\mathbf{v}_i$ is the ion-fluid velocity, and $d_i/dt=\partial/\partial t+\mathbf{v}_i\cdot\nabla$ is the ion convective derivative.

This quantity is the $Z$ projection of [current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), not the full vector, its magnitude, or its divergence. The matched right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ components are [radial_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), [toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), and this vertical projection; the field-aligned projection is [parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia). It excludes turbulent or anomalous-transport contributions such as [vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion-inertia current density points in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
NAMES.short: Vertical current density due to parallel viscosity is the +Z component of the current-density contribution from parallel viscous stress in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical current density due to parallel viscosity is the component along the vertical basis direction of the electric current-density contribution generated by parallel viscous stress in a magnetized plasma. The projection is taken from the full [current-density contribution](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), not from a scalar viscosity coefficient.

The contribution and its vertical projection are defined by

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\Pi_\parallel}=\frac{(\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel)\times\mathbf{B}}{B^2},\qquad J_{\Pi_\parallel,Z}=\mathbf{J}_{\Pi_\parallel}\cdot\hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\Pi_\parallel}$ is the full current-density contribution, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel$ is the parallel viscous stress tensor, $\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel$ is its viscous force density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector. The vertical projection is distinct from the [toroidal current-density projection](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) and from contributions due to other viscous-stress components.

The basis is the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $J_{\Pi_\parallel,Z}$ points along the $+Z$ direction.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the current density due to perpendicular viscous stress, projected along Z (vertical height) in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and φ is toroidal angle.
NAMES.long:
The vertical current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the $\hat{Z}$ projection of the plasma current-density contribution associated with the divergence of the perpendicular viscous stress tensor. It represents the part of the [perpendicular-viscosity current density](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity) directed along vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal angle.

The vertical component is defined by projecting the perpendicular-viscosity drift-current contribution onto $\hat{Z}$:

$$
j_{\pi_\perp,Z} = \hat{Z} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B} \times (\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\pi}_\perp)}{B^2}
$$

where $j_{\pi_\perp,Z}$ is the vertical component, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B = |\mathbf{B}|$, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}_\perp$ is the perpendicular viscous stress tensor.

This scalar is one cylindrical component of the full vector, alongside the [radial](name:radial_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity) and [toroidal](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity) components in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is distinct from the [vertical current density due to parallel viscosity](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), from a projection along the magnetic field, and from a flux-surface-normal projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perpendicular-viscosity current-density component points in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_electric_field
NAMES.short: Z-component of the electric field vector in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, giving the vertical electric force per unit positive charge at a plasma location.
NAMES.long:
The vertical electric field $E_Z$ is the projection of the electric field vector $\mathbf{E}$ onto the $Z$-axis of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z$ increases vertically upward from the device midplane. It governs vertical charged-particle acceleration and contributes to plasma drifts and currents in the poloidal cross-section, particularly in complex-geometry edge regions near X-points and divertor targets.

The field decomposes into electrostatic and inductive contributions:

$$
E_Z = -\frac{\partial \Phi}{\partial Z} - \frac{\partial A_Z}{\partial t}
$$

where $\Phi$ is the electrostatic potential and $A_Z$ is the $Z$-component of the magnetic vector potential $\mathbf{A}$.

In edge and scrape-off-layer transport modeling, $E_Z$ is evaluated at discrete spatial locations covering the full poloidal cross-section with realistic boundary geometry. It couples to [vertical_current_density](name:vertical_current_density) through the [vertical_conductivity](name:vertical_conductivity) tensor element via Ohm's law, and is one component of the full [electric_field](name:electric_field) vector. The radial and poloidal components together determine the $\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}$ drift that transports plasma across field lines.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $E_Z$ points in the direction of increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Vertical electron velocity is the component of the electron-fluid bulk flow along the vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical electron velocity is the component of the electron fluid bulk flow along the vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height. It represents advective electron motion, rather than random thermal motion or an individual-particle drift.

The vertical projection of the bulk velocity is defined by:

$$
v_{e,Z}(\mathbf{x},t)=\mathbf{v}_e(\mathbf{x},t)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $v_{e,Z}$ and $\mathbf{v}_e$ are velocities in m.s$^{-1}$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $t$ is time in s, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the dimensionless vertical unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a projection of [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), whose underlying bulk flow is the first velocity-space moment of the electron distribution. It applies only to electrons and is distinct from [vertical ion velocity](name:vertical_ion_velocity), which describes ion flow.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron bulk flow points in the direction of increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the effective convection velocity governing non-diffusive transport of the momentum density of an ion species in a specified charge state.
NAMES.long:
The vertical ion charge-state momentum convection velocity is the $Z$-component of the effective velocity vector $mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ appearing in the non-diffusive term of the charge-state-resolved fluid momentum transport equation for ion charge state $s$.

$$
v_{c,Z}^{(s)} = hat{Z} \cdot \mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}
$$

where $\hat{Z}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing vertical coordinate $Z$ and $\mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ is the effective momentum convection velocity vector for charge state $s$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and is distinct from [vertical ion momentum convection velocity](name:vertical_ion_momentum_convection_velocity), which provides the corresponding quantity aggregated over all charge states of an ion species. It is the vertical member of the [ion charge-state momentum convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) family and is not generally equal to the mean vertical fluid velocity of the charge state.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_{c,Z}^{(s)}$ points in the direction of increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Vertical ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the kinematic diffusion coefficient for vertical transport of vertical momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It relates the down-gradient diffusive momentum flux to the local vertical gradient of that state’s vertical momentum density.
NAMES.long:
Vertical ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the scalar kinematic transport coefficient governing diffusive vertical transport of vertical momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state. The vertical direction is the $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It represents collisional, turbulent, or effective redistribution of vertical momentum when that redistribution is modeled by a local down-gradient Fick's-law closure.

For the vertical direction, the diffusive vertical momentum flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{m,Z}^{(q)} = -D_{m,Z}^{(q)} \frac{\partial\left(\rho_q u_Z^{(q)}\right)}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,Z}^{(q)}$ is the diffusive flux of vertical momentum along increasing $Z$, $D_{m,Z}^{(q)}$ is the vertical ion charge-state momentum diffusivity, $\rho_q$ is the mass density of the specified ion charge state, $u_Z^{(q)}$ is its vertical flow-velocity component, and $Z$ is vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The quantity is resolved for one ionization state rather than summed over charge states as in [ion momentum diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity), and is a charge-state-specific directional instance of [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity). It is the vertical member of the directional family that also includes [radial ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), [poloidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), [toroidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), and [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity).
