NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Vertical ion charge-state momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of vertical linear momentum carried by ions in one specified ionization state.
NAMES.long:
Vertical ion charge-state momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the vertical linear-momentum component carried by ions of species $a$ in charge state $q$. It is the vertical projection of the [ion charge-state momentum flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) through a surface normal to the vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

For a surface normal to increasing $Z$, the charge-state-resolved vertical momentum flux is:

$$
\Pi_{a,q,ZZ}=m_a n_{a,q}v_{a,q,Z}^{2}+p_{a,q}+\pi_{a,q,ZZ}
$$

where $m_a$ is the ion mass, $n_{a,q}$ is the number density, $v_{a,q,Z}$ is the vertical velocity component, $p_{a,q}$ is the scalar pressure, and $\pi_{a,q,ZZ}$ is the vertical-normal component of viscous stress.

This quantity is resolved for one ionization state and therefore differs from [vertical ion momentum flux](name:vertical_ion_momentum_flux), which sums over ion charge states. It is the vertical counterpart of [radial ion charge-state momentum flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when vertical linear momentum is transported through a surface whose normal points in the direction of increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Vertical projection of the mean bulk fluid velocity of ions in a specified ionization charge state, resolved per charge state rather than averaged over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
Vertical ion charge-state velocity is the vertical projection of the mean bulk fluid velocity of ions in a specified ionization charge state. It is the $Z$ component of [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity), with the charge state resolved explicitly.

$$
v_{i,Z}^{(q)} = \frac{1}{n_i^{(q)}} \int v_Z f_i^{(q)}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

Here $i$ labels the ion species, $q$ labels the selected ionization charge state, $f_i^{(q)}$ is its velocity distribution, $n_i^{(q)}$ is its number density, and $v_Z$ is the particle-velocity component along the vertical direction. Unlike [vertical ion velocity](name:vertical_ion_velocity), this quantity is not averaged over charge states; [poloidal ion charge-state velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity) resolves the corresponding poloidal component.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the selected ion charge-state flow has a component in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Vertical component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the diamagnetic drift velocity of a specified ion charge state, driven by its partial pressure gradient crossed with the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The vertical component of the diamagnetic drift velocity for a specified ion charge state is its projection onto the vertical unit vector $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height.

The full diamagnetic drift velocity for ion charge state $s$ is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} = -\frac{\nabla p_s \times \mathbf{B}}{q_s n_s B^2}
$$

where $p_s$ is the partial pressure of charge state $s$, $q_s = Z_s e$ is its electric charge, $Z_s$ is its charge number, $e$ is the elementary charge, $n_s$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field with magnitude $B$. The vertical component is $v_{\mathrm{dia},s,Z} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},s} \cdot \hat{Z}$.

This component is a projection of [ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift); the corresponding major-radius projection is [radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It excludes drift contributions from mechanisms other than diamagnetic pressure-gradient drift.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the vertical diamagnetic drift points in the direction of increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the E×B guiding-center drift velocity for a specified ion charge state, projected in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical component of the E×B guiding-center drift velocity for a specified ion charge state is the projection of the local electric-field drift onto the vertical direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It is one component of the [full ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), not a diamagnetic-drift contribution.

The defining relation is

$$
v_Z = \left(\frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf Z}
$$

where $v_Z$ is the vertical velocity component, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf Z}$ is the vertical unit vector. The E×B drift is independent of ion mass and charge value at a given position; the specified charge state identifies the ion population. The corresponding [radial ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) uses the same vector with the radial projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $v_Z$ points in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective coefficient governing down-gradient transport of the total ion population’s vertical momentum along the vertical Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical ion momentum diffusivity $D_Z^i$ is the effective coefficient characterizing down-gradient redistribution of the vertical component of momentum within the total ion population summed over all charge states. It is the vertical-direction component of [ion momentum diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The vertical diffusive momentum-flux density is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{ZZ} = -\rho_i D_Z^i \frac{\partial v_{i,Z}}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{ZZ}$ is the flux density of vertical ion momentum in the vertical direction, $\rho_i$ is total ion mass density in kg m$^{-3}$, $v_{i,Z}$ is the mass-weighted mean vertical ion-fluid velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $Z$ is vertical height in m. The minus sign makes the diffusive flux oppose the vertical velocity gradient.

This coefficient is charge-state summed and is distinct from [vertical ion charge state momentum diffusivity](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which resolves one ion charge state. Its cylindrical vertical direction also distinguishes it from the poloidal transport represented by [poloidal ion momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Vertical ion momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the vertical component of linear momentum for the total ion population through a surface whose normal is parallel to the Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, summed over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
Vertical ion momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the vertical component of linear momentum for the total ion population through a surface whose normal is parallel to the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height, summed over all ion species and charge states. It is the $Z$-momentum, $Z$-normal projection of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), including convective, scalar-pressure, and viscous or turbulent stress contributions.

The $ZZ$ component of the ion momentum-flux tensor gives this quantity:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{ion},ZZ} = \hat{\mathbf{Z}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}} = \sum_s \left( m_s n_s v_{s,Z}^2 + p_s + \pi_{s,ZZ} \right)
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{ion},ZZ}$ is the vertical ion momentum flux, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\mathrm{ion}$ is the [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux) tensor, $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$, $m_s$ is the ion mass of population $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, $v_{s,Z}$ is its vertical mean-fluid velocity component, $p_s$ is its scalar pressure, and $\pi_{s,ZZ}$ is its viscous or turbulent stress component, with the sum running over all ion species and charge states.

This quantity is the total-ion, charge-state-summed counterpart of the charge-state-resolved [vertical ion charge-state momentum flux](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux). It differs from [toroidal ion momentum flux](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_flux), [poloidal ion momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux), and [parallel ion momentum flux](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux) by resolving both the transported momentum component and the surface-normal direction along $Z$ rather than along toroidal, poloidal, field-aligned, or flux-surface-normal projections.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ion linear momentum in the $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is transported across a surface whose normal points in the $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction.

NAMES.name: vertical_ion_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Vertical (Z) projection of the charge-state-averaged ion bulk fluid velocity, capturing the mean ion flow component along the height axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The vertical component of the ion bulk fluid velocity, $v_{i,Z}$, is the projection of the charge-state-averaged mean ion flow velocity $\mathbf{v}_i$ onto the $\hat{Z}$ axis of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ coordinate frame, where $Z$ is the height measured along the machine symmetry axis. It quantifies the net vertical directed motion of the ion fluid at each plasma location and is a component of the parent [ion_velocity](name:ion_velocity) vector.

The quantity arises as the $\hat{Z}$-projection of the first velocity-space moment of the ion distribution function $f_i$:

$$
v_{i,Z} = \frac{1}{n_i} \int v_Z \, f_i(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $n_i$ is the local ion number density and $v_Z$ is the particle velocity component along $\hat{Z}$.

In tokamak edge and divertor plasmas, vertical ion flows arise from the poloidal component of $E \times B$ and diamagnetic drifts, poloidal rotation, and parallel transport projected onto $\hat{Z}$ by the local magnetic-field geometry. This component is particularly relevant in diverted configurations where poloidal field lines carry ion flow toward or away from the divertor targets. The convective contribution to vertical ion momentum transport is captured by [vertical_ion_momentum_convection_velocity](name:vertical_ion_momentum_convection_velocity), and the charge-state-resolved analog is vertical_ion_state_momentum_convection_velocity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion bulk flow is directed in the $+Z$ direction, upward along the machine height axis.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the effective advective velocity transporting momentum for a single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma fluid transport, distinct from bulk particle flow. The component is along Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where Z is vertical height.
NAMES.long:
The vertical component of the [neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection) is the effective advective velocity for vertical momentum transport of a single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma fluid transport, distinct from bulk particle flow. The vertical direction is the $\hat{Z}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height.

The component is defined by projecting the neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity onto $\hat{Z}$:

$$
V_{\mathrm{mom},Z}^{(n,\alpha)} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{mom}}^{(n,\alpha)} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{mom}}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is the [neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection) for internal state $\alpha$ of neutral species $n$, and $V_{\mathrm{mom},Z}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is its vertical component.

This quantity is a component of an effective momentum-transport velocity, not the center-of-mass velocity or particle-flow velocity of the neutral state. The same family includes the [radial neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity), the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and the [parallel neutral internal-state momentum convection velocity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity), the component along the magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective momentum-convection velocity is directed toward increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vertical neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity is the coefficient governing down-gradient transport of momentum for neutral particles resolved by internal state. The vertical qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction along Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, not a vertical momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Vertical neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity is the coefficient governing down-gradient transport of momentum for neutral particles resolved by internal state. It is the vertical directional component of [neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). The vertical qualifier identifies the direction of diffusive momentum flux and of the momentum-density gradient along the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height, not a projection of the transported momentum onto that direction.

The defining Fick-type relation for the diffusive contribution along the vertical direction is:

$$
\mathbf{F}_{P,Z}^{\mathrm{diff},(n,s)} = -D_{Z}^{(n,s)} \nabla_Z \mathbf{P}^{(n,s)}
$$

where $\mathbf{F}_{P,Z}^{\mathrm{diff},(n,s)}$ is the diffusive vertical flux of neutral momentum for neutral population $n$ in internal state $s$, $D_Z^{(n,s)}$ is this diffusivity, $\nabla_Z=\hat{\mathbf{Z}}\cdot\nabla=\partial/\partial Z$ is the derivative along the vertical basis direction, and $\mathbf{P}^{(n,s)}$ is the neutral momentum-density vector for that population and internal state. The operator $\nabla_Z$ acts component-wise on the vector momentum density.

The quantity is resolved by internal state and does not aggregate over neutral internal states. It describes momentum transport rather than particle transport, which distinguishes it from [vertical neutral internal-state diffusivity]; its state resolution distinguishes it from [vertical neutral momentum diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity), and its vertical direction distinguishes it from [parallel neutral internal-state momentum diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vertical transport rate of vertical linear momentum carried by neutral particles in one specified internal state. It is the vertical-vertical component of the neutral momentum-flux tensor for that state.
NAMES.long:
The vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vertical transport component of linear momentum carried by neutral particles restricted to one specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It is the $ZZ$ component of the state-resolved momentum-flux tensor, not a particle flux or a local momentum source.

For the state-resolved neutral distribution, the vertical component is defined by

$$
\Pi_{ZZ}^{(s)} = \hat{Z} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{Z} = \int m_s v_Z^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is its momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $m_s$ is the mass of a neutral particle in state $s$, $v_Z=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{Z}$ is the vertical velocity component, and $f_s$ is the state-resolved velocity distribution.

The vertical direction is the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; it is not the radial, toroidal, or magnetic-field-parallel direction. As a diagonal $ZZ$ tensor component formed from $v_Z^2$, this quantity is nonnegative for any nonnegative state-resolved velocity distribution.

This component is the vertical member of the parent [neutral internal-state momentum flux], differs from the [radial](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), [parallel](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and [linear](name:linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) internal-state components, and is the state-resolved counterpart of [vertical neutral momentum flux](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux).

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vertical neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal vertical component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor, governing down-gradient redistribution of aggregate neutral momentum density along Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. The vertical qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.
NAMES.long:
Vertical neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal vertical component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor. It parameterizes down-gradient diffusive transport of aggregate neutral momentum density along the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The vertical qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.

For a diagonal Fick's-law closure, the vertical diffusive flux of a neutral momentum-density component is

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\alpha Z} = -D^{(n)}_{m,Z}\,\frac{\partial P_{n,\alpha}}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the transported momentum component, $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\alpha Z}$ is the vertical diffusive flux of that momentum component, $D^{(n)}_{m,Z}$ is the vertical neutral momentum diffusivity, $P_{n,\alpha}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum density component, and $Z$ is vertical height. The minus sign denotes down-gradient diffusion: for positive diffusivity, the diffusive flux is directed from larger toward smaller aggregate neutral momentum density along $Z$.

This coefficient applies to the aggregate neutral population represented by the neutral momentum-density field. It does not denote a diffusivity for a particular transported momentum component, and it is distinct from off-diagonal tensor components or convective transport of neutral momentum.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vertical neutral momentum flux is the vertical-vertical component of neutral linear-momentum transport in the edge plasma, combining convective and isotropic-pressure contributions summed over all neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
Vertical neutral momentum flux is the vertical-vertical component of the [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux) tensor. It represents neutral linear momentum transported across a surface normal to the vertical direction in the edge plasma, combining directed convection and isotropic pressure summed over all neutral species and internal states.

For neutral species and internal states indexed by $s$, the defining component is:

$$
\Pi_{n,ZZ} = \hat{\mathbf{Z}}\cdot\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
= \sum_s \left(m_s n_s v_{s,Z}^{\,2}+p_s\right)
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$; $m_s$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_s$ is its number density, $v_{s,Z}$ is its vertical velocity component, and $p_s$ is its isotropic pressure.

The sum is not resolved by internal state, unlike [vertical neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux). Its vertical projection is distinct from [poloidal neutral momentum flux](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux), which uses the local poloidal direction.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Mass-weighted vertical component of the neutral-species center-of-mass flow in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the vertical component of the mass-weighted fluid velocity of the neutral-species population. It describes the bulk neutral flow and is distinct from the effective velocity used to represent momentum transport.

$$
v_{\mathrm{cm},Z}^{(n)} = \frac{\sum_{s\in n} \rho_s v_{s,Z}}{\sum_{s\in n} \rho_s}
$$

where $\rho_s$ is the mass density of neutral species $s$ in kg m$^{-3}$, $v_{s,Z}$ is its velocity component along $\hat{Z}$ in m s$^{-1}$, and $n$ denotes the included neutral-species population. The component is taken in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ radial, $\phi$ toroidal, and $Z$ vertical. The definition follows the mass-weighted [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), whereas [vertical neutral-species momentum-convection velocity](name:vertical_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity) denotes a distinct transport-closure quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral center-of-mass velocity points in the direction of increasing $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Signed vertical component of the E×B drift velocity assigned to a specified internal state of a neutral species.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the signed projection along the vertical direction of the E×B drift velocity for a specified neutral-species internal state. It is the vertical component of the vector quantity [neutral-species internal-state E×B drift velocity](name:neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), not the drift speed or full vector.

The component is defined by projecting the crossed-field drift onto the vertical axis:

$$
v_Z = \left(\frac{\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}}{B^2}\right) \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $v_Z$ is the vertical velocity component, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $B = |\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The quantity is specific to the stated internal state and contains no aggregation over other neutral species or internal states.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the drift velocity points in the direction of increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_species
NAMES.short: Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of vertical momentum carried by one neutral species, aggregated over neutral states. Vertical denotes the momentum component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, not velocity direction.
NAMES.long:
Vertical neutral species momentum convection velocity is the flux-surface-normal convection coefficient that multiplies the vertical momentum density carried by neutrals of one chemical species. The vertical momentum component is defined along $hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the coefficient itself is not a velocity directed along $hat{Z}$. It is the vertical component of the [neutral species momentum convection velocity](name:neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity).

The defining relation preserves the total convective flux of vertical momentum across a magnetic flux surface:

$$
\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = P_{Z,a} V_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_{s \in a} P_{Z,s} V_{Z,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ denotes one neutral chemical species, $s$ runs over its resolved neutral states, $P_{Z,s}$ and $P_{Z,a}$ are signed vertical momentum densities, $V_{Z,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $V_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ are state-resolved and species-aggregated convection coefficients, and $\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum flux. The state sum excludes other chemical species and this local coefficient is not a flux-surface average. Unlike [vertical neutral velocity](name:vertical_neutral_velocity), it is defined by momentum transport.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\Gamma_{Z,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $P_{Z,a}$ have the same sign, with positive vertical momentum directed toward increasing $Z$ and positive flux-surface-normal transport directed toward increasing magnetic flux label.

NAMES.name: vertical_neutral_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the bulk fluid velocity of a neutral particle population, averaged over all neutral internal quantum and energy states.
NAMES.long:
Vertical neutral velocity is the vertical component of the bulk drift vector of a neutral particle population. It represents convective neutral motion after averaging over particle velocities and over all populated neutral internal quantum and energy states.

The component is defined from the parent [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) by

$$
v_{n,Z} = \mathbf{v}_n \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_n$ is the state-averaged neutral bulk velocity, $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $v_{n,Z}$ is its signed vertical component. The quantity is defined where the neutral population has nonzero density.

This quantity aggregates the neutral internal states; it is distinct from the state-resolved [vertical bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). It complements directional components such as parallel neutral velocity, which is projected along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral bulk flow points toward increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short: Effective kinematic coefficient governing down-gradient transport of the plasma’s vertical momentum component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the effective kinematic momentum diffusivity associated with the vertical component of plasma momentum. The vertical component is defined along $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a scalar down-gradient closure, the diffusive flux of vertical momentum is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_Z = -\rho D_Z \nabla u_Z
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_Z$ is the flux vector of vertical momentum, $\rho$ is mass density, $D_Z$ is this diffusivity, $u_Z$ is vertical velocity, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport.

The subscript $Z$ identifies the transported momentum component, not necessarily the direction in which the flux crosses a surface. This aggregate plasma quantity is distinct from the species-resolved [vertical ion momentum diffusivity](name:vertical_ion_momentum_diffusivity) and [vertical neutral momentum diffusivity](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_argon_density
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged number density of argon ions over the confined plasma volume, summed over all ionization stages.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged argon ion number density is the spatial mean of the local [argon ion density](name:argon_density) throughout the confined plasma volume, including contributions from every argon ionization stage. It is distinct from a local or charge-state-resolved density.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{Ar}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}}\int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\mathrm{d}V$ is a volume element, and $n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local argon ion density. The local density is charge-state summed, $n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}(\mathbf{r})$, where $q$ is the argon ionization stage. This quantity provides the argon-density numerator for the impurity concentration ratio [ratio of volume-averaged argon density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Deuterium-tritium density is the volume-averaged ion number density of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium as one effective species.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-tritium density is the volume-averaged ion number density of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium ions as one effective species. It is obtained from the local [deuterium-tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density), which is summed over all ion charge states.

The defining volume average is

$$
\bar n_{DT} = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{DT}\,dV
$$

where $\bar n_{DT}$ and $n_{DT}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, $V$ is the specified averaging volume in m$^{3}$, and $dV$ is its volume element. The local density satisfies $n_{DT}=n_D+n_T$, with $n_D$ and $n_T$ the corresponding charge-state-summed deuterium and tritium ion densities.

The quantity includes only deuterium and tritium fuel ions represented by the effective pseudo-species; neutral atoms and molecules, reaction products, and impurity ions are excluded. Unlike the [line-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density), it uses a volume measure rather than a line-of-sight average, and it supplies the numerator of the [ratio of volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_hydrogen_density
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma, giving the mean H+ concentration across the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged hydrogen density quantifies the mean concentration of ionized protium throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatial average of the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density), rather than its value at a particular position.

$$
\overline{n}_H = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_H(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_H$ is the volume-averaged hydrogen density, $n_H(\mathbf{r})$ is the local ionized-protium density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, and $dV$ is a volume element. The average includes ionized protium throughout $V_p$ and excludes neutral atomic hydrogen and other isotopes. Unlike [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), it averages over the full plasma volume. Its isotope fraction relative to all hydrogenic fuel is represented by [the volume-averaged hydrogen-density fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density).

sources.parent_definition: Hydrogen

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged charge number of the dominant ionization state for a given ion species, representing the global mean ionization level integrated over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged ion charge $\langle Z_\mathrm{ion} \rangle$ is the spatial mean of the dominant-state charge number for a given ion species across the confined plasma volume. It is the volume-averaging transformation of ion_charge, compressing a spatially varying ionization profile into a single global scalar that tracks the mean ionization level of each species.

$$
\langle Z_\mathrm{ion} \rangle = \frac{1}{V} \int Z_\mathrm{ion}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $V$ is the confined plasma volume and $Z_\mathrm{ion}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local dominant-state ion charge number of the species at position $\mathbf{r}$.

This quantity is particularly relevant during plasma initiation and current ramp-up, when gas breakdown and ionization fronts cause the mean charge state to evolve dynamically from near-neutral to partially or fully ionized conditions. The volume average captures this global ionization progression as a single time-evolving scalar for each species present.

Unlike ion_species_charge, which is the density-weighted average over all occupied charge states of a species, this quantity reflects only the dominant ionization state. For the density-weighted mean-squared charge relevant to resistivity and impurity transport, see [effective_charge](name:effective_charge); the corresponding volumetric ion number density is given by [volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion carries net positive electric charge, as holds for all ionized plasma species with at least one electron removed.

sources.enhanced_context: Structure containing the volume-averaged ion charge (Z_ion) of the dominant ionization state for each ion species during the plasma initiation phase. Tracks mean ionization level as the plasma breaks down and current ramps up.
sources.leaf_definition: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed), volume averaged over plasma radius
sources.parent_definition: Quantities related to the different ion species, in the sense of isonuclear or isomolecular sequences

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Volume average of the local density-weighted mean charge number of an ion charge-state bundle over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged mean charge number of an ion charge-state bundle is the volume integral of the local density-weighted mean charge number $\bar{Z}(\mathbf{r})$ normalized by the confined plasma volume $V$:

$$
\langle \bar{Z} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V} \int_V \bar{Z}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $\bar{Z}(\mathbf{r})$ is the [ion charge state average charge number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number) — the local density-weighted mean charge number over all charge states in the bundle at position $\mathbf{r}$ — and $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last-closed flux surface.

This quantity condenses the radial $\bar{Z}$ profile into a single global representative value for transport and power-balance analyzes. It is distinguished from [volume averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge) by its explicit resolution of the charge-state bundle dimension rather than representing only the dominant ionization state.

sources.enhanced_context: Concentration-weighted mean charge number (⟨Z⟩) of an ion charge-state bundle, volume-averaged over the plasma radius. Computed as Σ(Z·x_z) over all charge states within the bundle; scalar complement to the radial profile z_average_1d.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged number density of ions of a specified species over the confined plasma volume, summed over all ionic charge states.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged ion density is the mean number density of ions of a specified species throughout the confined plasma volume. It is a volume-integrated specialization of [ion_density](name:ion_density), rather than a density evaluated at one plasma point.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_i = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_i(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $\overline{n}_i$ is the volume-averaged density, $n_i(\mathbf{r})$ is the local density of the specified ion species, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $V$ is the confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface. The species density is summed over all ionic charge states and excludes neutral particles. The all-species counterpart is [volume-averaged total ion density](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_density).

sources.enhanced_context: Volume-averaged ion density (⟨ni⟩) for a specific ion species, averaged over the plasma volume up to the last closed flux surface (LCFS). A global scalar characterising the bulk ion content of the confined plasma.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_neon_density
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Volume average of the charge-state-summed neon number density throughout the plasma, giving the mean elemental neon content independent of local spatial variation.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged neon density is the mean elemental neon number density over the plasma volume. It includes neutral neon and all neon ionization states, extending the local definition of [neon density](name:neon_density) to a spatial average.

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Ne}} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local neon number density summed over all ionization states. The volume integral represents the total neon inventory divided by the plasma volume. This quantity provides the numerator in the [neon abundance ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which additionally normalizes it to the volume-averaged electron density.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_runaway_electron_density
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Mean number density of runaway electrons over the confined plasma volume, obtained by averaging the local suprathermal population that remains in the accelerating tail.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged runaway electron density is the spatial mean of the local runaway-electron population over the confined plasma volume. Runaway electrons are suprathermal electrons whose momentum makes collisional slowing-down ineffective compared with continued electromagnetic acceleration, as described by [runaway_electron_density](name:runaway_electron_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{RE} = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\overline{n}_\mathrm{RE}$ is the volume-averaged runaway electron density, $n_\mathrm{RE}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local runaway electron density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the physical volume element.

This quantity averages the local density rather than reporting the total runaway-electron count; the latter is obtained by multiplying the average by $V_\mathrm{p}$. It includes the full confined plasma volume and excludes regions outside that volume.

sources.enhanced_context: Volume-averaged number density of runaway electrons (n_RE). A key global scalar characterising the runaway electron population generated by Dreicer, avalanche, hot tail, Compton, or tritium mechanisms during disruptions.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_density
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged total ion number density over the confined plasma volume, summing all ion species and charge states and including thermal and non-thermal ion populations.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged total ion density is the aggregate ion number density averaged over the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. It includes all ion species, resolved charge states, and thermal and non-thermal ion populations; it excludes electrons and neutral particles.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{i,\mathrm{total}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{i,\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the volume-averaged density, $n_{i,\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [total ion density](name:total_ion_density) in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^3$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume element. This is a density average, not the total ion inventory. Unlike [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), it aggregates all ion species rather than one selected species.

sources.enhanced_context: Total ion density (ni,total) as a volume average, summed over all ion species. Represents the overall ion particle content per unit volume for global plasma characterization.
sources.leaf_definition: Value
sources.parent_definition: Total ion density (sum over species)

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Particle number density of xenon ions at the internal transport barrier, the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep radial impurity-density gradients to form; summed over all xenon ion charge states and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of xenon ions at the internal transport barrier is the local xenon-ion particle density, summed over all xenon ion charge states, on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. The internal transport barrier is a confined-plasma flux-surface region where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep radial impurity-density gradients to form. Xenon (atomic number $Z = 54$) is a high-$Z$ noble-gas impurity species.

The charge-state-summed xenon-ion density at the barrier reference surface is the sum of zeroth velocity moments of the xenon ion distribution functions:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_{q=1}^{54} \int f_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v}, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\, d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the elemental xenon ion number density, $q$ is the xenon ion charge number, $f_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the distribution function of xenon ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the scalar flux-surface label identifying the internal-transport-barrier reference surface. The range $q=1,\ldots,54$ spans all positive xenon ion charge states and excludes neutral xenon atoms.

At the species level this per-volume particle amount is charge-state-summed: charge-state-resolved xenon ion densities are distinct populations, and summing them over all positive charge states recovers this elemental density. It is the xenon-specific instance of [density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and the barrier-local counterpart of [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), distinct from [electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and from other noble-gas impurity densities at the same locus.

NAMES.name: xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Particle number density of xenon ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes, summed over all xenon ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of xenon ions evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at the innermost point of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces, summed over all xenon ionization states. The magnetic axis is the locus where the gradient of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes.

The on-axis xenon density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}} \sum_{q=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the number density of xenon ions in charge state $q$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $q$ is the positive ionic charge state, and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position. Neutral xenon is excluded. This is the xenon-specific realization of [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis), using the same locus convention as [carbon density at the magnetic axis](name:carbon_density_at_magnetic_axis).

NAMES.name: bulk_plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
NAMES.short: Mass-weighted bulk-plasma velocity contribution from charged-species pressure gradients through diamagnetic drift, retaining the vector direction rather than only its magnitude.
NAMES.long:
The bulk-plasma velocity due to diamagnetic drift is the mass-weighted center-of-mass velocity contribution obtained by combining charged-species diamagnetic drifts driven by their pressure gradients. It is a vector contribution, not the full plasma flow, a charge-weighted drift, or a direction-independent speed.

The defining bulk-plasma contribution is

$$
\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia,bulk}} = \frac{1}{\rho}\sum_s \rho_s \frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p_s}{q_s n_s B^2}
$$

where $\rho$ is the total charged-species mass density, $\rho_s$ is the mass density of species $s$, $p_s$ is its scalar pressure, $q_s$ is its signed particle charge, $n_s$ is its number density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $B$ is its magnitude.

The sum includes the charged species represented in the bulk-plasma definition and excludes neutral-species flows. A signed projected component is represented by [plasma velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), whereas [bulk-plasma velocity due to diamagnetic drift magnitude](name:bulk_plasma_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift_magnitude) omits direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component points along its declared positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_current_density
NAMES.short: Counter-passing current density is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux carried by the counter-passing orbit class across all included particle populations, including associated back-current contributions.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing current density $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux associated with particles in the counter-passing orbit class. It represents signed charge transport assigned to this orbit class, including associated back-current contributions.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the orbit-resolved distribution functions:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_s q_s \int \mathbf{v}\, f_{s,\mathrm{cp}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes included charged species, $q_s$ is species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,\mathrm{cp}}$ is the distribution contribution assigned to the counter-passing class.

The counter-passing class consists of circulating guiding-center orbits directed opposite the reference plasma-current direction. Its charge and velocity weighting distinguishes it from [counter-passing density](name:counter_passing_density), while its orbit restriction distinguishes it from the full [current density](name:current_density) and from [fast current density](name:fast_current_density). Component quantities inherit the positive direction of their defining basis vector or unit vector.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the stated component or scalar projection of $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is aligned with the positive direction of its defining basis vector or unit vector.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_current_density
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal current density from the counter-passing orbit class, encompassing contributions from all particle populations and including back-current drag from thermal electrons and ions.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing particles complete full poloidal circuits in the direction opposing the plasma current and contribute a net toroidal current density whose sign is generally opposite to the driven current. This quantity captures the $\hat{\phi}$ projection of that current, integrated over the full counter-passing portion of the distribution function and flux-surface averaged, including the back-current response of thermal electrons and ions to collisional momentum exchange. The companion quantity [toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density) isolates the fast-particle contribution alone and excludes these back-current terms.

The flux-surface-averaged toroidal current density is defined as:

$$
\langle J_\phi^{\mathrm{cp}} \rangle = \left\langle \int_{\mathrm{cp}} \sum_s q_s\, v_\phi\, f_s(\mathbf{v})\, d^3v \right\rangle_{\!\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component, $f_s$ is the distribution function restricted to the counter-passing orbit domain, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes the flux-surface average.

This quantity is evaluated in kinetic transport simulations that classify particle orbits by guiding-center topology. Together with co-passing and [toroidal_trapped_current_density](name:toroidal_trapped_current_density) contributions, it provides a complete orbit-class decomposition of the total driven toroidal current density. It is the toroidal projection of the full vector counter_passing_current_density.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: deuterium_deuterium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion
NAMES.subject: deuterium_deuterium
NAMES.short: Total neutron count rate from deuterium-deuterium beam-beam fusion reactions, counting neutrons from the D-D branch when both reacting deuterons are nonthermal ions generated by neutral beam injection.
NAMES.long:
The D-D beam-beam neutron flux counts the rate at which neutrons are emitted through the neutron-producing branch of deuterium-deuterium fusion when both reacting deuterons are nonthermal fast ions generated by neutral beam injection. It is the volume-integrated neutron-count component of [neutron flux due to beam-beam fusion](name:neutron_flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion), distinct from the D-T channel represented by [deuterium-tritium neutron flux due to beam-beam fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion) and from beam-thermal production.

$$
\dot{N}_{n}^{\mathrm{DD,bb}} = \int_{V} \nu_{\mathrm{DD}}^{(n)} R_{\mathrm{DD}}^{\mathrm{bb}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

Here $\dot{N}_{n}^{\mathrm{DD,bb}}$ is the total neutron count rate, $R_{\mathrm{DD}}^{\mathrm{bb}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local beam-beam D-D reaction rate density, $\nu_{\mathrm{DD}}^{(n)}$ is the neutron multiplicity of the included branch, $V$ is the active plasma volume, and $\mathbf{r}$ is position. The non-neutron-producing D-D branch is excluded. Unlike the local [deuterium-deuterium fusion emissivity](name:deuterium_deuterium_emissivity_due_to_fusion), this quantity is integrated over volume.

NAMES.name: deuterium_deuterium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion
NAMES.subject: deuterium_deuterium
NAMES.short: Deuterium-deuterium beam-thermal neutron emission is the global neutron production rate from fusion between a fast beam deuteron and a thermal plasma deuteron.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-deuterium beam-thermal neutron emission is the global production rate of neutrons from the neutron-producing D-D fusion reaction. One reactant is a neutral-beam-injected fast deuteron and the other is a thermal plasma deuteron.

For resolved beam-deuteron and thermal-deuteron velocity distributions, the neutron emission rate is defined by:

$$
\Phi_n^{\mathrm{DD,BT}} = \int_V \int \int f_D^{\mathrm{beam}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v}_b) f_D^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v}_t) \sigma_{DD}(v_{\mathrm{rel}}) v_{\mathrm{rel}} Y_{DD}(v_{\mathrm{rel}}) \, d^3v_b \, d^3v_t \, dV
$$

where $\Phi_n^{\mathrm{DD,BT}}$ is the global D-D beam-thermal neutron emission rate, $V$ is the plasma volume, $f_D^{\mathrm{beam}}$ and $f_D^{\mathrm{th}}$ are velocity-space density distributions, $\sigma_{DD}$ is the D-D fusion cross-section, $v_{\mathrm{rel}}=|\mathbf{v}_b-\mathbf{v}_t|$ is the relative speed, and $Y_{DD}$ is the neutron yield per reaction, including the neutron-branching fraction.

This is the D-D channel contribution to [neutron flux due to beam-thermal fusion](name:neutron_flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion). It excludes D-T beam-thermal reactions, thermal-thermal and beam-beam fusion, and non-fusion neutron sources; the corresponding D-T channel is [deuterium-tritium neutron flux due to beam-thermal fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion).

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Total neutron count rate from deuterium-tritium beam-beam fusion reactions, counting neutrons from the D-T branch when both reacting fuel ions are nonthermal and generated by neutral beam injection.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the volume-integrated neutron count rate from deuterium-tritium fusion reactions between a nonthermal fast deuteron and a nonthermal fast triton generated by neutral beam injection. It counts neutrons from the D-T reaction branch.

$$
\dot{N}_{n}^{\mathrm{DT,bb}} = \int_{V} \nu_{\mathrm{DT}}^{(n)}(\mathbf{r})\,R_{\mathrm{DT}}^{\mathrm{bb}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

Here $\dot{N}_{n}^{\mathrm{DT,bb}}$ is the total D-T beam-beam neutron count rate, $R_{\mathrm{DT}}^{\mathrm{bb}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local reaction rate density for fast deuterons and fast tritons, $\nu_{\mathrm{DT}}^{(n)}$ is the neutron multiplicity of the reaction branch, $V$ is the active plasma volume, and $\mathbf{r}$ is position.

This channel-specific quantity resolves the aggregate [neutron flux due to beam-beam fusion](name:neutron_flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion), alongside the [deuterium-deuterium neutron flux due to beam-beam fusion](name:deuterium_deuterium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion). It excludes beam-thermal and thermonuclear fusion reactions.

NAMES.name: deuterium_tritium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion
NAMES.subject: deuterium_tritium
NAMES.short: Deuterium-tritium beam-thermal neutron emission is the global production rate of neutrons from the neutron-producing fusion branch between a fast beam isotope and a thermal counterpart.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium-tritium beam-thermal neutron emission is the global production rate of neutrons from fusion reactions in which a fast beam deuteron reacts with a thermal triton or a fast beam triton reacts with a thermal deuteron. It is integrated over the plasma volume and restricted to the neutron-producing deuterium-tritium reaction channel.

For resolved beam-ion and thermal-ion velocity distributions, the emission rate is defined by:

$$
\Phi_n^{\mathrm{DT,BT}} = \sum_{(a,b)\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DT}}} \int_V \int \int f_a^{\mathrm{beam}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v}_a) f_b^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v}_b) \sigma_{ab}(v_{\mathrm{rel}}) v_{\mathrm{rel}} Y_{ab}(v_{\mathrm{rel}}) \, d^3v_a \, d^3v_b \, dV
$$

where $\Phi_n^{\mathrm{DT,BT}}$ is the deuterium-tritium beam-thermal neutron emission rate, $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the set of ordered deuterium-tritium beam-thermal reactant pairs, $f_a^{\mathrm{beam}}$ and $f_b^{\mathrm{th}}$ are velocity-space density distributions, $\sigma_{ab}$ is the fusion cross section, $v_{\mathrm{rel}}=|\mathbf{v}_a-\mathbf{v}_b|$ is relative speed, and $Y_{ab}$ is neutron yield per reaction.

This is the deuterium-tritium component of [neutron flux due to beam-thermal fusion](name:neutron_flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion). It includes both ordered beam-thermal reactant assignments and excludes beam-beam reactions, including [deuterium-tritium neutron flux due to beam-beam fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_beam_fusion), as well as deuterium-deuterium reactions represented by [deuterium-deuterium neutron flux due to beam-thermal fusion](name:deuterium_deuterium_neutron_flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion). The quantity counts emitted neutrons rather than reaction events, so the neutron yield is included.

NAMES.name: diamagnetic_current_density
NAMES.short: Diamagnetic current density is the scalar magnitude of the vector density of conventional electric charge flux associated with pressure-gradient diamagnetic drift in a magnetized plasma. It is the magnitude of the diamagnetic-drift current-density vector, not a radial, poloidal, toroidal, vertical, or field-aligned projection.
NAMES.long:
Diamagnetic current density $J_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the scalar magnitude of the vector density of conventional electric charge flux associated with pressure-gradient diamagnetic drift in a magnetized plasma. It is the magnitude of [current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), a contribution to [current density](name:current_density), and represents no resolved direction of its own.

For an isotropic scalar pressure, the defining magnetized-fluid relation is the magnitude of the diamagnetic-drift current-density vector:

$$
J_{\mathrm{dia}} = \left|\frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p}{B^2}\right|
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, $p$ is the total scalar plasma pressure over the included plasma populations, and $\nabla p$ is its spatial gradient. The vector inside the magnitude is the pressure-gradient contribution [current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

This scalar is distinct from signed components or projections of the same vector contribution, such as [radial_diamagnetic_current_density](name:radial_diamagnetic_current_density), [poloidal_diamagnetic_current_density](name:poloidal_diamagnetic_current_density), and [toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, radial, toroidal, and vertical projections are along $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ respectively; in a flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, a poloidal projection is along increasing $\theta$. The neoclassical return current represented by [pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) and the heat-viscosity-driven contribution [diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity](name:diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity) are separate quantities.

NAMES.name: poloidal_diamagnetic_current_density
NAMES.short: Poloidal diamagnetic current density is the signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current-density vector along the poloidal direction.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal diamagnetic current density is the signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current-density vector along the local poloidal direction. Its magnitude is not the scalar magnitude represented by [diamagnetic_current_density](name:diamagnetic_current_density).

For an isotropic scalar pressure, the defining relation is

$$
J_{\mathrm{dia},\theta}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}=\left(\frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p}{B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, $p$ is the total scalar plasma pressure, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is the unit direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux coordinate $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. This component is distinct from the [radial_diamagnetic_current_density](name:radial_diamagnetic_current_density) and other directional projections.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the diamagnetic current-density vector points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: radial_diamagnetic_current_density
NAMES.short: Radial component of the diamagnetic current density, obtained by projecting the magnetic-field–pressure-gradient drift current onto the radial direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The radial diamagnetic current density is the projection of the total [diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) onto the local radial direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It arises from the differential ion and electron guiding-center drifts produced by a pressure gradient in a magnetized plasma.

The radial component is defined by projecting the diamagnetic current-density vector:

$$
j_R = \mathbf{j}_\mathrm{dia} \cdot \hat{R} = \left(\frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p}{B^2}\right) \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $j_R$ and $\mathbf{j}_\mathrm{dia}$ are current densities, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $p$ is the total scalar plasma pressure, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude, and $\hat{R}$ is the radial unit vector. The quantity is the radial projection only; it excludes non-diamagnetic current contributions and differs from the [vertical diamagnetic current density](name:vertical_diamagnetic_current_density) through its projection axis. The radial direction is the increasing-major-radius direction, not generally the normal to a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $j_R$ points in the $+R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the diffusive thermal energy flux of the electron population to the local electron temperature gradient, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its radial and poloidal component forms.
NAMES.long:
The electron energy diffusion coefficient $D_{e,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by the electron population, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the diffusive electron heat flux and the local electron temperature gradient. It is the electron-species-resolved instance of the parent [energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective or $E \times B$ drift contributions to the total electron heat flux.

The defining relation for the diffusive electron heat flux $\mathbf{Q}_{e,\mathrm{diff}}$ is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{e,\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,E} \, \nabla T_e
$$

where $D_{e,E}$ is the electron energy diffusion coefficient and $T_e$ is the local electron temperature. In a magnetized plasma $D_{e,E}$ is strongly anisotropic; cross-field radial values govern electron energy confinement while values along field lines are many orders of magnitude larger.

Directional projections of this coefficient include [radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient), which governs cross-field energy confinement, and [poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient), which captures transport along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The analogous coefficient for the ion population is given by [ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the effective electron energy diffusion coefficient governing Fick's-law diffusive transport of electron thermal energy along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The poloidal electron energy diffusion coefficient $D_{e,\theta}^{E}$ is the poloidal projection of the effective thermal diffusivity for the electron energy channel, quantifying how efficiently electron heat is transported along the poloidal direction in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ by gradient-driven diffusion. It is the poloidal component form of [electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective, advective, or $E \times B$ drift contributions to the total electron heat flux.

The defining local Fick's-law relation for the diffusive poloidal electron heat flux is:

$$
q_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}} = - n_e D_{e,\theta}^{E} \nabla_{\theta} T_e
$$

where $q_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the physical heat-flux component tangent to increasing poloidal coordinate $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, $n_e$ is the electron number density, $D_{e,\theta}^{E}$ is the poloidal electron energy diffusion coefficient, $T_e$ is the local electron temperature expressed as energy per particle, and $\nabla_{\theta} T_e$ is the temperature gradient per unit length along the same poloidal direction. The minus sign denotes down-gradient diffusion, so the diffusive heat-flux component is opposite to the local temperature-gradient component for a positive coefficient.

Directional members of this family are distinguished by the direction of the heat-flux projection and temperature-gradient component, not by a change of transported species or energy channel. The companion [radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is a different directional member of the same electron-energy diffusion-coefficient family. The closely related [poloidal_electron_energy_diffusivity](name:poloidal_electron_energy_diffusivity) denotes the corresponding poloidal effective thermal diffusivity; the present coefficient is identified by the Fick's-law heat-flux closure above, in which electron density multiplies the coefficient.

NAMES.name: radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Radial component of the effective electron energy diffusion coefficient governing Fick's-law diffusive transport of electron thermal energy along the radial direction in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
The radial electron energy diffusion coefficient $D_{e,\rho}^{E}$ is the radial projection of the effective thermal diffusivity for the electron energy channel, quantifying how efficiently electron heat is transported along the radial direction in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$. It is the radial component of [electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and applies only to diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by electrons.

The defining Fickian closure for the radial diffusive electron thermal-energy flux $q_{e,\rho}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is:

$$
q_{e,\rho}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -n_e D_{e,\rho}^{E}\frac{\partial T_e}{\partial l_\rho}
$$

where $q_{e,\rho}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial component of the diffusive electron thermal-energy flux, $n_e$ is electron number density, $D_{e,\rho}^{E}$ is this coefficient, $T_e$ is electron temperature expressed as energy per electron, and $l_\rho$ is physical distance along increasing $\rho$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

This coefficient excludes convective, pinch, and $E \times B$ advective contributions to the electron energy flux. The poloidal component is [poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient), [radial_electron_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_electron_diffusion_coefficient) relates electron particle flux rather than electron energy flux to its driving gradient, and the analogous ion-channel coefficient is [radial_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: fast_current_density
NAMES.short: Fast current density is the conventional electric charge flux density carried by suprathermal particles, partitioned into circulating and magnetically trapped orbit classes.
NAMES.long:
Fast current density is the electric current density contributed by fast (suprathermal) charged particles. It is the shared parent for orbit-resolved contributions from co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped guiding-center populations.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the fast distribution, resolved over orbit classes:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\sum_C\sum_s q_s\int \mathbf{v}\,f_{s,C}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle current density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $C$ indexes the orbit classes, $s$ indexes particle species, $q_s$ is species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,C}$ is the fast-particle velocity-space distribution restricted to class $C$.

The orbit-resolved quantities [co-passing fast current density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density), [counter-passing fast current density](name:counter_passing_fast_current_density), and [trapped fast current density](name:trapped_fast_current_density) represent the corresponding contributions. This quantity excludes non-fast particle contributions and displacement-current density, while [current density](name:current_density) includes all charged-particle contributions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a scalar projection of the fast-particle current density is aligned with the positive direction of its defining basis vector or unit vector.

NAMES.name: co_passing_fast_current_density
NAMES.short: Co-passing fast current density is the electric current density contributed by fast (suprathermal) particles whose guiding-center orbits carry sufficient parallel energy to circulate continuously around the torus in the co-current direction.
NAMES.long:
Co-passing fast current density is the portion of [fast_current_density](name:fast_current_density) arising from fast (suprathermal) particles whose guiding-center orbits have sufficient parallel energy to pass untrapped around the torus in the same toroidal direction as the plasma current, without being reflected into banana orbits by the magnetic mirror force.

It is one of three orbit-class contributions to the total fast current density:

$$
j_\mathrm{fast} = j_\mathrm{co\text{-}pass} + j_\mathrm{ctr\text{-}pass} + j_\mathrm{trap}
$$

where $j_\mathrm{ctr\text{-}pass}$ is the [counter_passing_fast_current_density](name:counter_passing_fast_current_density) from particles traveling counter to the plasma current, and $j_\mathrm{trap}$ is the [trapped_fast_current_density](name:trapped_fast_current_density) from particles executing banana orbits on the low-field side. The toroidal projection of this quantity is given by [toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the conventional current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: counter_passing_fast_current_density
NAMES.short: Counter-passing fast current density is the electric current density contributed by fast (suprathermal) particles whose guiding-center orbits carry sufficient parallel energy to circulate continuously around the torus in the counter-current direction.
NAMES.long:
Counter-passing fast current density is the portion of [fast_current_density](name:fast_current_density) arising from fast (suprathermal) particles whose guiding-center orbits have sufficient parallel energy to pass untrapped around the torus in the direction counter to the plasma current, excluding thermal back-current contributions from electrons and thermal ions.

These counter-passing particles form one of the three guiding-center orbit classes that partition the fast current density:

$$
j_\mathrm{fast} = j_\mathrm{co\text{-}pass} + j_\mathrm{ctr\text{-}pass} + j_\mathrm{trap}
$$

where $j_\mathrm{co\text{-}pass}$ is [co_passing_fast_current_density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density), $j_\mathrm{ctr\text{-}pass}$ is this quantity, and $j_\mathrm{trap}$ is [trapped_fast_current_density](name:trapped_fast_current_density). The toroidal projection of this vector is given by [toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the conventional current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of electric current density carried by fast particles on co-passing, untrapped guiding-center orbits, averaged over a magnetic flux surface and expressed along the φ direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It excludes compensating thermal-electron and thermal-ion back currents.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of electric current density carried by fast particles on co-passing, untrapped guiding-center orbits is the contribution to the flux-surface-averaged toroidal current density from the fast-particle distribution restricted to that orbit class. The toroidal component is the signed projection along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. A co-passing orbit is a passing orbit for which the guiding-center parallel velocity remains directed along the equilibrium magnetic-field direction.

The distribution-function definition for the flux-surface average is:

$$
\langle J_{\phi,\mathrm{fast,co}} \rangle = \left\langle \sum_s q_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{co}}} v_\phi\, f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes an average over a magnetic flux surface, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $q_s$ is the electric charge of species $s$, $v_\phi$ is the signed toroidal velocity component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle velocity-space distribution for species $s$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing region of velocity space.

Only current carried directly by fast particles is included. Compensating return currents in thermal electrons and thermal ions arising from momentum exchange with fast particles are excluded. Together with the [toroidal counter-passing fast-particle current density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density) and the [toroidal trapped fast-particle current density](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density), this contribution forms the [toroidal fast-particle current density](name:toroidal_fast_particle_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the co-passing fast-particle current is directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal current density carried by fast particles on counter-passing guiding-center orbits, excluding thermal back-current contributions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the toroidal electric-current-density component carried by the fast-particle counter-passing orbit class. These suprathermal particles circulate continuously around the torus opposite to the plasma-current direction; thermal electron and ion back-current contributions are excluded.

$$
J_{\phi,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\psi)=\left\langle\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{\phi}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

Here $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the current-density vector from fast counter-passing particles, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\psi$ labels the flux surface, and angle brackets denote its flux-surface average. It is the toroidal component of [counter_passing_fast_current_density](name:counter_passing_fast_current_density), whereas [toroidal_counter_passing_current_density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_current_density) includes all counter-passing contributions; [toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density) represents the opposite orbit direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal current-density component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
