NAMES.name: trapped_fast_current_density
NAMES.short: Trapped fast current density is the electric current density contributed by fast (suprathermal) particles whose guiding-center orbits lack the parallel energy to circulate freely around the torus, instead executing banana orbits between mirror-reflection points on the low-field side.
NAMES.long:
Trapped fast current density is the portion of [fast_current_density](name:fast_current_density) arising from fast (suprathermal) particles whose guiding-center orbits have insufficient parallel energy to overcome the magnetic mirror force, causing them to execute banana orbits between turning points on the low-field side rather than passing untrapped around the torus.

The trapped component $j_\mathrm{trap}$ completes the orbit-class decomposition

$$
j_\mathrm{fast} = j_\mathrm{co\text{-}pass} + j_\mathrm{ctr\text{-}pass} + j_\mathrm{trap}
$$

where $j_\mathrm{co\text{-}pass}$ is [co_passing_fast_current_density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density) from co-circulating fast particles and $j_\mathrm{ctr\text{-}pass}$ is [counter_passing_fast_current_density](name:counter_passing_fast_current_density) from counter-circulating fast particles. Trapped particles contribute a net current through the toroidal projection of their banana-orbit drift velocity. This quantity excludes compensating return-current contributions from thermal electrons and thermal ions; the toroidal component is [toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the conventional current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of electric current density carried by magnetically trapped fast particles, excluding compensating electron and thermal-ion return-current contributions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the local toroidal projection of the electric current density carried directly by fast particles whose guiding-center orbits are trapped by magnetic-mirror reflection. It is the toroidal component of [trapped_fast_current_density](name:trapped_fast_current_density), resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
J_{\phi}^{\mathrm{tf}} = \sum_s q_s n_s^{\mathrm{tf}} u_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{tf}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of trapped fast species $s$ in coulombs, $n_s^{\mathrm{tf}}$ is its local number density in m$^{-3}$, and $u_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{tf}}$ is its mean toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The sum includes only the trapped fast population; compensating electron and thermal-ion return-current contributions are excluded. It is distinct from the broader [toroidal_fast_particle_current_density](name:toroidal_fast_particle_current_density) and from the co-passing contribution [toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $J_{\phi}^{\mathrm{tf}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: fast_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Local number density of the suprathermal (non-thermal) electron population, forming the fast-electron fraction of the total electron density and distinct from the bulk thermal electron component.
NAMES.long:
The fast electron density $n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ quantifies the number of suprathermal electrons per unit volume — electrons whose energies lie substantially above the bulk Maxwellian distribution. Fast electrons arise through wave-particle interactions during electron cyclotron or lower hybrid heating, inductive electric field acceleration, or rapid MHD events such as sawtooth crashes that eject energetic electrons from the core region.

The total [electron density](name:electron_density) $n_e$ decomposes as:

$$
n_e = n_{e,\mathrm{th}} + n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal electron number density and $n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is this quantity.

The fast electron population is inferred from hard X-ray bremsstrahlung emission diagnostics, suprathermal electron cyclotron emission radiometry, or kinetic transport models that resolve the non-Maxwellian high-energy tail of the electron distribution function. In edge and scrape-off layer plasmas, fast electrons transported from the core contribute to energy deposition on plasma-facing components. The [runaway electron density](name:runaway_electron_density) is a distinct sub-population of fast electrons continuously accelerated by the parallel inductive electric field and represents an extreme tail of this quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when suprathermal electrons are present in the plasma volume element; as a number density this quantity is non-negative everywhere.

NAMES.name: fast_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Gyrotropic kinetic pressure of the suprathermal (fast) neutral particle population, decomposing into components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field direction, summed over all internal quantum states of the neutral species.
NAMES.long:
The fast neutral pressure characterizes the second-order velocity moment of the suprathermal neutral distribution function projected onto the two principal axes defined by the local magnetic field. Unlike magnetized ions, fast neutrals are insensitive to the magnetic force directly, yet they retain an anisotropic pressure signature inherited from their birth mechanism — charge exchange between fast ions and cold neutrals, or direct neutral beam injection — producing unequal stress along and across the magnetic field direction.

The gyrotropic pressure tensor for the fast neutral population is:

$$
\mathbf{P}_{\rm fn} = P_{\perp,\rm fn}\,\mathbf{I} + (P_{\parallel,\rm fn} - P_{\perp,\rm fn})\,\hat{b}\hat{b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel,\rm fn}$ is the [parallel fast neutral pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure) along the magnetic field unit vector $\hat{b}$, $P_{\perp,\rm fn}$ is the [perpendicular fast neutral pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure) across $\hat{b}$, and $\mathbf{I}$ is the unit tensor. The equivalent isotropic scalar pressure is $p_{\rm fn} = (P_{\parallel,\rm fn} + 2P_{\perp,\rm fn})/3$. State-resolved analogs are captured in [parallel_fast_neutral_state_pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure) and [perpendicular_fast_neutral_state_pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure). This quantity is distinct from the thermal [neutral_pressure](name:neutral_pressure) measured by vacuum gages, which represents the isotropic equilibrium cold-gas limit.

In high-power neutral beam injection scenarios the fast neutral pressure can reach a few percent of the total plasma pressure in the core; it is inferred from neutral particle analyzer energy spectra combined with distribution-function modeling or Monte Carlo fast-particle transport codes.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the fast neutral population exerts compressive outward normal stress on a control surface, consistent with a non-negative phase-space distribution function.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Gyrotropic kinetic pressure of the suprathermal fast-neutral population along the local magnetic field, summed over all internal quantum states.
NAMES.long:
Parallel fast neutral pressure is the scalar field-aligned component of the kinetic pressure tensor of suprathermal neutral particles. It represents the random kinetic stress associated with neutral motion parallel to the local magnetic field, summed over all internal quantum states.

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fn}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf P_{\mathrm{fn}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fn}}$ is the parallel fast neutral pressure, $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{fn}}$ is the fast-neutral kinetic pressure tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.

This quantity is the field-aligned component of [fast neutral pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure) and, together with [perpendicular fast neutral pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure), defines its gyrotropic decomposition. The state-resolved counterpart [parallel fast neutral internal-state pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure) separates contributions by internal neutral state.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Gyrotropic kinetic pressure of the suprathermal fast-neutral population perpendicular to the local magnetic field, summed over all internal quantum states.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular fast neutral pressure is the scalar field-perpendicular component of the kinetic pressure tensor of suprathermal neutral particles. It represents the random kinetic stress associated with neutral motion in the two directions perpendicular to the local magnetic field direction, after summing over all internal quantum states of the neutral population.

For a gyrotropic fast-neutral distribution, this component is defined by the second velocity moment perpendicular to $\hat{b}$:

$$
P_{\perp,\mathrm{fn}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{\alpha} \frac{m_{\alpha}}{2} \int v_{\perp}^{2} f_{\mathrm{fn},\alpha}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fn}}$ has unit Pa, $\alpha$ labels internal quantum or excitation states, $m_{\alpha}$ is the neutral particle mass for state $\alpha$, $f_{\mathrm{fn},\alpha}$ is the suprathermal neutral velocity distribution for that state, $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field unit vector, and $v_{\perp}=|\mathbf{v}-(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|$. The factor $1/2$ averages the kinetic stress over the two perpendicular velocity degrees of freedom.

This quantity is the internal-state-summed counterpart of [perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure), so $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fn}}=\sum_{\alpha}P_{\perp,\mathrm{fn},\alpha}$. Together with [parallel_fast_neutral_pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure), it determines the gyrotropic [fast_neutral_pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure) tensor; the equivalent isotropic scalar pressure is $p_{\mathrm{fn}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fn}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{fn}})/3$. It is distinct from [neutral_pressure](name:neutral_pressure), which denotes the isotropic thermal neutral-gas pressure rather than a suprathermal anisotropic pressure component.

NAMES.name: fast_particle_energy
NAMES.short: Fast particle energy is a gyrokinetic volume-integrated kinetic-energy moment of the suprathermal particle distribution, including both parallel and perpendicular motion.
NAMES.long:
Fast particle energy is a gyrokinetic velocity-space energy moment assigned to the fast-particle population through a kinetic-energy weight and integrated over the plasma volume. It is the fast-population specialization of [particle energy](name:particle_energy), rather than a local energy density.

The total fast-particle kinetic energy is defined by

$$
E_{\mathrm{fast}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathcal{V}_p} \int \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2 f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\,d^3x
$$

where $s$ indexes the included fast species, $\mathcal{V}_p$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity in m s$^{-1}$, $m_s$ is particle mass in kg, and $f_s$ is the fast-particle phase-space distribution. The quantity excludes bulk thermal energy unless that population is explicitly classified as fast. Its directional decompositions are [parallel fast-particle energy](name:parallel_fast_particle_energy) and [perpendicular fast-particle energy](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_energy), whose sum equals the total under the same species and volume scope.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_particle_energy
NAMES.short: Parallel fast-particle energy is the part of the suprathermal particle kinetic energy associated with motion parallel to the local magnetic field, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Parallel fast-particle energy is the part of the kinetic energy of the suprathermal particle population associated with motion parallel to the local magnetic field. It complements [perpendicular fast-particle energy](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_energy) within the total [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy).

It is defined by

$$
W_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_{\mathcal{V}} \int \frac{1}{2} m v_\parallel^2 f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\,d^3r
$$

where $\mathcal{V}$ is the plasma volume, $f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})$ is the fast-particle phase-space distribution, $m$ is particle mass, and $v_\parallel$ is the velocity component parallel to the local magnetic field. For a gyrotropic distribution, the corresponding energy density is one-half the parallel pressure, so this quantity is the volume integral of that parallel energy density, summed over the included fast-particle species.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local temperature gradient, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its radial and poloidal component forms.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in a specified charge state $z$, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the density-normalized diffusive ion heat flux for that charge state and the local ion temperature gradient for the same charge state. It is the charge-state-resolved specialization of the [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective, advective, or $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat flux.

The defining relation for the density-normalized diffusive energy flux of charge state $z$ is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E}\,\nabla T_{i,z}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,z,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their [number density](name:ion_charge_state_number_density), and $T_{i,z}$ is their [temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature). The minus sign denotes transport down the local temperature gradient.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not an aggregation over charge states. The corresponding charge-state-aggregated [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is a density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states. Directional children include [radial_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient], for the component associated with $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, and [poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient], for the poloidal component.

NAMES.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Dimensionless vector flux-limiter coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on momentum-flux density for a specified ion charge state, applied component-by-component in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures.
NAMES.long:
The ion charge-state momentum coefficient is the charge-state-resolved ion specialization of [momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), providing one dimensionless limiter factor per spatial transport direction for momentum flux attributed to a specific ion charge state in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures.

Each vector component $\alpha_s$ bounds the corresponding directional momentum-flux density through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_s \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_s \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux estimate for charge state $s$, and $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming reference scale with $m_s$ the ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the thermal speed. When $|\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_s \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm\alpha_s \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

The vector components provide separate limiter factors for each spatial direction; the [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) is the scalar projection onto the magnetic-field direction. The neutral-particle analog is [neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). Each component is intrinsically non-negative.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Dimensionless parallel ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming bound on field-aligned momentum transport for a specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge state in the field-aligned direction. It is the parallel component of the vector quantity [ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

If $\Pi_{\parallel}$ is the modeled parallel momentum flux and $\Pi_{\parallel,\mathrm{fs}}$ is its collisionless free-streaming reference bound, the limiter constrains their magnitudes according to

$$
|\Pi_{\parallel}| \leq \alpha_{\parallel}|\Pi_{\parallel,\mathrm{fs}}|
$$

where $\alpha_{\parallel}$ is this coefficient and the parallel direction is tangent to the magnetic field. The coefficient limits the magnitude of the modeled flux; it does not define the flux direction or its sign. The corresponding axis-specific quantity for poloidal transport is the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), while the ion-species aggregate is the [parallel ion momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

NAMES.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Dimensionless poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming bound on poloidal momentum transport for a specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge state in the poloidal direction. It is the poloidal component of the vector quantity [ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

The coefficient $lpha_{s,\box{pol}}$ bounds the poloidal momentum-flux density through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \, \Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive poloidal momentum-flux estimate for charge state $s$, and $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming reference scale with $m_s$ the ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the thermal speed. When $|\Pi_{s,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}} \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm\alpha_{s,\mathrm{pol}}\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

The poloidal component is distinct from the [parallel ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which projects onto the magnetic-field direction, and from the [toroidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which applies in the geometric toroidal direction. The coefficient is intrinsically non-negative; the sign of the limited poloidal momentum flux is inherited from the reference poloidal momentum-flux estimate.

NAMES.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Dimensionless toroidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming bound on toroidal momentum transport for a specified ion charge state.
NAMES.long:
The toroidal ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge state in the geometric toroidal direction. It is the toroidal component of the vector quantity [ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

If $\Pi_{\phi}$ is the modeled toroidal momentum flux and $\Pi_{\phi,\mathrm{fs}}$ is its collisionless free-streaming reference bound, the limiter constrains their magnitudes according to

$$
|\Pi_{\phi}| \leq \alpha_{\phi}|\Pi_{\phi,\mathrm{fs}}|
$$

where $\alpha_{\phi}$ is this coefficient and the toroidal direction is the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The coefficient limits the magnitude of the modeled flux; it does not define the flux direction or its sign. The corresponding axis-specific quantity for poloidal transport is the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

NAMES.name: ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized diffusive thermal energy flux of the ion population to the local ion temperature gradient, aggregated as a density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states and serving as the direction-agnostic parent over radial and poloidal component forms.
NAMES.long:
The ion energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by the ion population, providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the density-normalized diffusive ion heat flux and the local ion temperature gradient. It is the ion-population specialization of the general [energy diffusion coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is distinct from convective or $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat flux. As an intensive species-level coefficient, the total-ion value is the density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states; [ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) denotes the corresponding coefficient for a specified ion charge state.

The defining Fickian relation for the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}} = - n_i D_{i,E} \nabla T_i
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux, $n_i$ is the total ion number density, $D_{i,E}$ is the ion energy diffusion coefficient, $T_i$ is the total-ion temperature expressed as thermal energy per ion, and $\nabla T_i$ is its spatial gradient. For ion species and charge-state components indexed by $a$, $n_i = \sum_a n_a$, $T_i = \sum_a n_a T_a / n_i$, and the intensive aggregation convention for component coefficients $D_{a,E}$ is $D_{i,E} = \sum_a n_a D_{a,E}/n_i$. The leading minus sign encodes down-gradient Fickian diffusion: for positive $D_{i,E}$, the diffusive flux points opposite to $\nabla T_i$.

This name is direction-agnostic. [Radial ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) denotes the cylindrical $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and [poloidal ion energy diffusion coefficient] denotes the projection tangent to the poloidal direction in the $(R, Z)$ cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is distinct from [energy diffusivity](name:energy_diffusivity), which uses a thermal-energy-density gradient rather than the ion-temperature gradient, and from effective diffusivity names that combine diffusive and convective heat transport.

NAMES.name: radial_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Radial cross-field diffusion coefficient for thermal energy carried by the total ion population, summed over all ion species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
The radial ion energy diffusion coefficient is the Fick's-law proportionality coefficient for cross-field transport of thermal energy carried by the total ion population. It aggregates all ion species and charge states.

The radial diffusive thermal-energy flux is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,E,r}\frac{\partial w_{i,E}}{\partial r}
$$

where $D_{i,E,r}$ is this radial diffusion coefficient, $\Gamma_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive thermal-energy flux density, $w_{i,E}$ is the total ion thermal-energy density, and $r$ is the radial transport coordinate. The minus sign denotes transport down the thermal-energy-density gradient.

This quantity is the radial component of [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient), not the energy flux itself. It differs from the charge-state-resolved [radial thermal ion charge state energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and excludes electron thermal-energy transport, described by the [radial electron energy diffusion coefficient](name:radial_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: magnetic_shear_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short: Normalized logarithmic derivative of the safety factor with respect to normalized toroidal flux radius, evaluated at the internal transport barrier location.
NAMES.long:
The magnetic shear at the internal transport barrier is the normalized logarithmic derivative of the safety factor $q$ with respect to the normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_{tor}$, evaluated at the radial position of the internal transport barrier. The sign and magnitude of this quantity govern the stability of microinstabilities at the barrier, with reversed (negative) shear strongly associated with ITB formation in advanced tokamak scenarios.

The defining relation is:

$$
s = \frac{\rho_{tor}}{q} \frac{dq}{d\rho_{tor}}
$$

where $q$ is the safety factor — the number of toroidal field-line transits per single poloidal circuit — and $\rho_{tor}$ is the normalized toroidal flux radius, equal to zero at the magnetic axis and unity at the last closed flux surface.

The safety-factor profile needed to evaluate this quantity is obtained from equilibrium reconstruction, often constrained by motional Stark effect polarimetry or Faraday rotation measurements resolving the internal $q$-profile. The full radial context is provided by the [magnetic shear](name:magnetic_shear_at_pedestal_top) profile; analogous point evaluations are defined at [the magnetic axis](name:magnetic_shear_at_magnetic_axis) and [the pedestal top](name:magnetic_shear_at_pedestal_top).

In reversed-shear configurations the value is negative near the $q$-minimum, commonly ranging from $-2$ to $0$; in conventional positive-shear ITB scenarios values are small and positive, in the range $0$ to $1$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the safety factor $q$ increases with the normalized toroidal flux radius $\rho_{tor}$, i.e., when $dq/d\rho_{tor} > 0$.

NAMES.name: neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Fick's-law diffusion coefficient for thermal energy transport of the aggregated neutral particle population, serving as the direction-agnostic parent over its radial and poloidal component forms.
NAMES.long:
The neutral energy diffusion coefficient characterizes the proportionality between the diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux and the spatial gradient of neutral thermal energy density in an edge plasma. As neutrals carry no charge and are unaffected by the magnetic field, their transport is not constrained to field lines, yet the coefficient remains directionally resolved in toroidal geometry where radial and poloidal pathways represent physically distinct transport channels.

The Fickian closure takes the form:

$$
\mathbf{q}_n^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_n^E \, \nabla\!\left(\tfrac{3}{2} n_n T_n\right)
$$

where $n_n$ is the neutral number density, $T_n$ is the neutral temperature, $\frac{3}{2} n_n T_n$ is the neutral thermal energy density, and $D_n^E$ is in m$^2$ s$^{-1}$.

In edge transport models the coefficient is resolved into directional components: [radial_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) governs cross-field energy transport across magnetic flux surfaces, while [poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) governs transport in the poloidal direction. This quantity aggregates over all neutral charge states; for state-resolved treatment see [poloidal_neutral_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). The analogous coefficient for the ion population is poloidal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient.

NAMES.name: poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Poloidal-direction diffusion coefficient governing the diffusive transport of neutral particle thermal energy in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The poloidal neutral energy diffusion coefficient $D_\mathrm{pol}$ quantifies how neutral particle thermal energy spreads in the poloidal direction through diffusive processes in the edge plasma and scrape-off layer. It is the poloidal projection of the full [neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), isolating the poloidal directional contribution from the general tensor in the anisotropic geometry of the divertor region.

The neutral energy transport equation relates the poloidal diffusive energy flux $q^\mathrm{E}_\mathrm{pol}$ to the local gradient of thermal energy density through:

$$
q^\mathrm{E}_\mathrm{pol} = -D_\mathrm{pol} \, \nabla_\mathrm{pol} w_n
$$

where $w_n = \tfrac{3}{2} n_n T_n$ is the neutral thermal energy density, $n_n$ is the neutral particle number density, and $T_n$ is the neutral temperature.

This coefficient is computed within neutral transport models that resolve atomic and molecular processes in the divertor and scrape-off layer, ranging from fluid moment closures to kinetic Monte Carlo treatments of neutral atoms and molecules.

The particle-transport (not energy) counterpart is poloidal_neutral_diffusion_coefficient. The charge-state-resolved energy analog is [poloidal_neutral_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), and the equivalent quantity for ion species is poloidal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient.

NAMES.name: radial_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Fickian diffusion coefficient for radial transport of thermal energy by the aggregated neutral particle population in an edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The radial neutral energy diffusion coefficient characterizes the proportionality between the radial diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux and the major-radius gradient of neutral thermal-energy density in an edge plasma. Neutral transport is not constrained to magnetic-field lines, and this coefficient is the radial component of the directionally resolved neutral transport.

The Fickian closure is

$$
q_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{n,R}^{E}\frac{\partial}{\partial R}\left(\frac{3}{2}n_n T_n\right)
$$

where $q_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive neutral thermal-energy flux, $D_{n,R}^{E}$ is this radial diffusion coefficient, $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $n_n$ is neutral number density, and $T_n$ is neutral temperature.

This coefficient is the radial component of the parent [neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and applies to the aggregated neutral population. Directional comparison is provided by the [poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), while state-resolved transport is represented by [radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Fick's-law diffusion coefficient for field-aligned particle transport of the total ion population, relating the parallel ion flux to the gradient of ion number density along the magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion diffusivity $D_{\parallel,i}$ quantifies how efficiently ions diffuse along magnetic field lines via Fick's-law particle transport. It is the field-aligned component of the full [ion_diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_diffusivity) and enters the parallel ion particle continuity equation as the principal diffusive term; in magnetized fusion plasmas, parallel transport coefficients exceed their cross-field counterparts by several orders of magnitude.

The defining Fick's-law relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,i} = -D_{\parallel,i} \, \nabla_\parallel n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,i}$ is the field-aligned ion particle flux density, $n_i$ is the total ion number density summed over charge states, and the parallel gradient $\nabla_\parallel = \hat{b} \cdot \nabla$ is taken along the unit magnetic field vector $\hat{b}$.

This quantity covers the total ion species without charge-state resolution; the charge-state-resolved analog is [parallel_ion_charge_state_diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_diffusivity), which provides species- and charge-state-specific transport coefficients. It complements [parallel_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity) for momentum transport along field lines and [parallel_neutral_state_diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_diffusivity) for the neutral species counterpart. Values span from classical Braginskii-limit estimates in high-density collisional edge regimes to anomalously enhanced levels driven by plasma turbulence.

NAMES.name: parallel_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Signed component of the total magnetic induction resolved along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction, distinguishing field-aligned strength from cylindrical-axis projections.
NAMES.long:
The parallel magnetic field $B_\\parallel$ is the component of the total [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) resolved along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction. It represents field-aligned magnetic strength rather than a projection onto a fixed cylindrical axis.

The defining projection is

$$
B_\\parallel = \\mathbf{B} \\cdot \\hat{\\mathbf{b}}_0, \\qquad \\hat{\\mathbf{b}}_0 = \\frac{\\mathbf{B}_0}{|\\mathbf{B}_0|}
$$

where $\\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic induction, $\\mathbf{B}_0$ is the local equilibrium magnetic induction, and $\\hat{\\mathbf{b}}_0$ is the corresponding field-line unit vector. This total-field component is distinct from the [parallel wave magnetic field](name:parallel_wave_magnetic_field), which is restricted to an oscillatory wave perturbation, and from the [parallel magnetic vector potential](name:parallel_magnetic_vector_potential), which projects a different physical quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the total magnetic induction points along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_vorticity
NAMES.short: Parallel vorticity is the projection of the plasma bulk-flow curl onto the local magnetic-field direction, measuring signed rotation in the perpendicular plane.
NAMES.long:
Parallel vorticity is the component of plasma vorticity along the local magnetic-field direction. It measures the signed local rotation of the bulk plasma flow in the plane perpendicular to that field.

The defining relation is:

$$
\omega_\parallel = \boldsymbol{\omega}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b} = (\nabla\times\mathbf v)\cdot\frac{\mathbf B}{|\mathbf B|}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is plasma vorticity, $\mathbf v$ is the bulk velocity, $\mathbf B$ is the local magnetic field, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is its unit vector, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. The velocity is expressed in m s$^{-1}$, and $\omega_\parallel$ is expressed in s$^{-1}$.

This is the field-aligned projection of [vorticity](name:vorticity), distinct from the fixed-axis projection [toroidal_vorticity](name:toroidal_vorticity) and from the field-aligned bulk velocity [parallel_center_of_mass_velocity](name:parallel_center_of_mass_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the local vorticity has a positive projection along the defined magnetic-field vector $\mathbf B$.

NAMES.name: pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short: Pfirsch-Schlueter current density is the vector flux density of conventional electric charge, equal to electric current per unit area normal to the flow, for the neoclassical return current that restores current continuity when the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current is divergent in toroidal magnetic geometry. It denotes the full vector before scalar projection.
NAMES.long:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux associated with the neoclassical return current in toroidal magnetic confinement geometry. It restores local current continuity when the pressure-gradient [diamagnetic_current_density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) has finite divergence caused by magnetic-field inhomogeneity. It is a contribution to [current_density](name:current_density) and varies around a magnetic flux surface while remaining predominantly aligned with the magnetic field.

The defining continuity relation for the pressure-gradient part of the current is:

$$
\nabla\cdot\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}+\frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p}{B^2}\right)=0
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch-Schlueter current density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, and $p$ is the total scalar plasma pressure. The term $\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p/B^2$ is the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current density, so the equation states that the Pfirsch-Schlueter return current closes its divergence. In the field-aligned neoclassical representation, the vector is reconstructed from the parallel amplitude as $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}=j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}\mathbf{b}$ with $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$; scalar component names are projections of this vector.

This quantity excludes bootstrap_current_density, Ohmic current density, externally driven current density, and the diamagnetic current density itself, although these may enter the total current balance. The generic name denotes the unprojected vector; related projections include [parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) along $\mathbf{b}$, [poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) along increasing $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ labels flux surfaces, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and [radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), [toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), and [vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) along $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the stated scalar component or projection of $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is aligned with the positive direction of the basis vector or unit vector defining that component or projection.

NAMES.name: parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the Pfirsch-Schlüter neoclassical current density is the signed field-aligned return-current density that restores current continuity for divergent pressure-gradient diamagnetic current.
NAMES.long:
Parallel component of the Pfirsch-Schlüter neoclassical current density is the signed projection of the local [Pfirsch-Schlüter current density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) onto the local magnetic-field direction. It is the field-aligned neoclassical return-current contribution associated with the finite divergence of pressure-gradient diamagnetic current in toroidal magnetic geometry.

The defining projection is:

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}} = \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}\cdot\mathbf{b}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}$ is the parallel component, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch-Schlüter current-density vector, and $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, with $B$ its magnitude.

This quantity excludes the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current itself, bootstrap current, Ohmic current, and externally driven current. Unlike the [toroidal Pfirsch-Schlüter current density](name:toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), it is projected along the magnetic field rather than onto the geometric toroidal direction.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the Pfirsch-Schlüter current density has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short: Poloidal component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter neoclassical current density is the signed return-current projection tangent to a flux surface toward increasing poloidal angle.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter neoclassical current density is the signed projection of the local [Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) onto the poloidal tangent of a magnetic flux surface. It is the poloidal part of the neoclassical return current that restores continuity for divergent pressure-gradient diamagnetic current.

The defining projection is:

$$
J_{\mathrm{PS},\theta}=\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch-Schlueter current-density vector and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}$ is the unit tangent to a flux surface directed toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$; $\rho$ labels flux surfaces and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

This component is a projection of the full return-current vector, distinct from the field-aligned [parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) and major-radius [radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density). It excludes the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current itself and other current contributions such as bootstrap and externally driven currents.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the Pfirsch-Schlueter current has a component in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short: Radial component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter neoclassical current density is the signed projection of the return-current vector onto increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter neoclassical current density is the signed projection of the local [Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) vector onto the cylindrical radial direction. It is the major-radius component of the neoclassical return current that restores continuity for the divergent pressure-gradient diamagnetic current.

The radial projection is defined by

$$
J_{\mathrm{PS},R}=\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch-Schlueter current-density vector, $J_{\mathrm{PS},R}$ is its radial component, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a projection of the full return-current vector, not the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current itself. Its decomposition is distinct from the [toroidal Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) and the [parallel Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current-density vector has a component toward increasing major radius $R$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short: Toroidal component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter neoclassical current density is the signed return-current projection in the geometric toroidal direction, restoring local current continuity.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter neoclassical current density is the signed projection of the local [Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) onto the geometric toroidal direction. It is the toroidal part of the neoclassical return current associated with the divergence of pressure-gradient diamagnetic current.

The defining projection is:

$$
J_{\mathrm{PS},\phi}=\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch-Schlueter current-density vector and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. This component is distinct from the [poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) and [radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) projections, and excludes the diamagnetic current itself.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the Pfirsch-Schlueter current has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
NAMES.subject: pfirsch_schlueter
NAMES.short: Vertical component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter neoclassical current density is the signed projection of the local Pfirsch-Schlueter current-density vector onto +Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, contributing to the return current that restores current continuity for divergent pressure-gradient diamagnetic current.
NAMES.long:
Vertical component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter neoclassical current density is the signed projection of the local [Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) vector onto the $+\hat{Z}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is the vertical contribution to the neoclassical return current that restores current continuity when the pressure-gradient [diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) has finite divergence in toroidal magnetic geometry. The underlying vector is a contribution to [current density](name:current_density) and is predominantly aligned with the magnetic field before this scalar projection is taken.

The component is defined by the vector projection:

$$
J_{\mathrm{PS},Z} = \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}\cdot\hat{Z}
$$

where $J_{\mathrm{PS},Z}$ is the vertical Pfirsch-Schlueter current density, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the [Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a component of the Pfirsch-Schlueter return current, not the [diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) whose divergence it closes, and it excludes bootstrap, Ohmic, and externally driven current-density contributions. It is distinct from the cylindrical co-projections [radial Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) and [toroidal Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density), and from the [poloidal Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) and [parallel Pfirsch-Schlueter current density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density). The token `vertical` denotes projection along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; it is not a flux-surface-normal projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the Pfirsch-Schlueter current-density vector has a component in the direction of increasing $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: poloidal_current_density
NAMES.short: Poloidal current density is the signed conventional charge flux per unit area projected along increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
NAMES.long:
Poloidal current density is the signed conventional charge flux per unit area represented by the component of [current density](name:current_density) tangent to increasing poloidal angle.

The defining projection is:

$$
J_{\mathrm{pol}}(\rho,\theta,\phi)=\mathbf{J}(\rho,\theta,\phi)\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}$ is the conventional current-density vector, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\theta}$ is the unit tangent to increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, and $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ are flux coordinates. These coordinates are embedded in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity includes all charged-particle contributions unless a narrower qualifier is specified. It is distinct from [poloidal total current density](name:poloidal_total_current_density), which specifies an aggregated current contribution, and from [poloidal current density due to ion-neutral friction](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), which isolates one driving process.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the current-density vector is aligned with the unit tangent to increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: poloidal_vorticity
NAMES.short: Poloidal vorticity is the signed projection of the plasma bulk-flow curl onto the direction of increasing poloidal angle on a magnetic flux surface.
NAMES.long:
Poloidal vorticity is the component of plasma vorticity tangent to a magnetic flux surface in the direction of increasing poloidal angle. It measures the signed local rotation rate of the bulk plasma flow about that poloidal direction.

The defining relation is:

$$
\omega_\theta = \boldsymbol{\omega} \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_\theta = (\nabla \times \mathbf v) \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_\theta
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is the plasma vorticity, $\mathbf v$ is the bulk plasma velocity, $\nabla \times$ is the spatial curl operator, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_\theta$ is the unit vector tangent to the flux surface toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

Poloidal vorticity is a directional component of [vorticity](name:vorticity), distinct from the toroidal component represented by [toroidal_vorticity](name:toroidal_vorticity). It is not the magnitude of the vorticity vector and does not represent the cylindrical radial or toroidal projection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the plasma vorticity has a component in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

NAMES.name: radial_vorticity
NAMES.short: Radial vorticity is the component of the plasma bulk-flow curl along the outward major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial vorticity is the component of the plasma vorticity vector along the outward major-radius direction. It measures the signed local rotation rate of the bulk plasma flow about that direction and is a directional projection of [vorticity](name:vorticity).

The defining relation is:

$$
\omega_R = \hat{\mathbf R}\cdot\boldsymbol{\omega} = \hat{\mathbf R}\cdot(\nabla\times\mathbf v)
$$

where $\omega_R$ is radial vorticity in s$^{-1}$, $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is the vorticity vector in s$^{-1}$, $\hat{\mathbf R}$ is the outward unit vector, $\nabla$ is the spatial differential operator, and $\mathbf v$ is the bulk plasma velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The vectors are expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical coordinate.

This quantity is derived from the full velocity field, not the radial velocity itself, such as [radial_plasma_velocity](name:radial_plasma_velocity). It differs from the [toroidal_vorticity](name:toroidal_vorticity) projection because the two describe rotation about different directions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the bulk-flow rotation follows the right-hand sense about the outward $+\hat{\mathbf R}$ direction.

NAMES.name: runaway_electron_current_density
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Runaway electron current density is the vector charge flux per unit area carried by suprathermal electrons beyond the collisional drag limit.
NAMES.long:
Runaway electron current density $\mathbf{J}_{\rm RE}$ characterizes the conventional charge transport carried by the runaway-electron population, a suprathermal electron population extending beyond the collisional drag limit. It is a component of the total [current density](name:current_density), distinct from the current carried by non-runaway populations.

The current density is the first velocity moment of the runaway-electron distribution:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\rm RE}(\mathbf{x}) = q_e \int_{\mathcal{R}} \mathbf{v}\, f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $q_e$ is the electron charge, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $f_e$ is the runaway-electron phase-space number density, and $\mathcal{R}$ is the velocity-space subset classified as beyond the collisional drag limit. The general vector quantity includes both the field-aligned form represented by [parallel runaway electron current density](name:parallel_runaway_electron_current_density) and spatial averages such as [volume averaged runaway electron current density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component of the conventional current points along the positive direction of that component; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the toroidal component is positive toward increasing $\phi$.

NAMES.name: parallel_runaway_electron_current_density
NAMES.subject: runaway_electron
NAMES.short: Parallel runaway electron current density is the field-aligned charge flux per unit area carried by suprathermal electrons beyond the collisional drag limit.
NAMES.long:
Parallel runaway electron current density $J_{\rm RE,\parallel}$ characterizes the field-aligned conventional charge transport carried by the runaway-electron population, a suprathermal electron population extending beyond the collisional drag limit. It is the field-aligned projection of [runaway electron current density](name:runaway_electron_current_density).

The parallel current density is the first velocity moment of the runaway-electron distribution projected onto the magnetic-field direction:

$$
J_{\rm RE,\parallel}(\mathbf{x}) = q_e \int_{\mathcal{R}} (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}) f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $q_e$ is the electron charge, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field unit vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $f_e$ is the runaway-electron phase-space number density, $\mathcal{R}$ is the velocity-space subset classified as beyond the collisional drag limit, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The integration includes only the runaway-electron population and excludes current carried by non-runaway populations. It therefore differs from [co-passing fast current density](name:co_passing_fast_current_density), which is selected by an orbit class rather than the runaway criterion. The related [runaway electron density](name:runaway_electron_density) describes the carrier abundance rather than its charge transport.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local thermal Maxwellian population, excluding fast and suprathermal electron contributions.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the local thermal Maxwellian population is the local continuum count density of electrons not bound to atoms, molecules, or ions. It excludes fast and suprathermal electron populations.

For a representative physical volume surrounding the point, the defining ratio is:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{N_{e,\mathrm{th}}}{V}
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal electron density, expressed in m$^{-3}$, $N_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the number of thermal electrons in the representative volume, and $V$ is that physical volume. The continuum value applies to volumes small on macroscopic plasma scales but large enough to contain many particles.

This component is distinct from the unqualified [electron_density](name:electron_density), which includes the local free-electron population without a population qualifier, and from [fast_electron_density](name:fast_electron_density). When those are the only components, the [total_electron_density](name:total_electron_density) is their sum.

NAMES.name: thermal_electron_energy
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Volume-integrated thermal energy content of the electron population, excluding fast suprathermal electrons and non-electron plasma populations.
NAMES.long:
Volume-integrated thermal energy content of the electron population is the total kinetic energy carried by bulk thermal electrons throughout the confined plasma. It is an extensive energy content, not a power or energy-transfer rate, and excludes fast suprathermal electrons and non-electron populations.

The defining relation is

$$
E_{e,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_\mathrm{plasma}} p_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $E_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the integrated thermal electron energy, $p_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local thermal electron pressure, $V_\mathrm{plasma}$ is the confined plasma volume, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position. This quantity is the thermal-electron component of [electron energy](name:electron_energy); unlike [thermal plasma energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy), it excludes thermal-ion energy.

sources.parent_definition: Thermal electron plasma energy content = 3/2 * integral over the plasma volume of the thermal electron pressure

NAMES.name: thermal_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Thermal neutral pressure is the isotropic kinetic pressure from random thermal motion of neutral particles about their mean flow, aggregated over unresolved internal states.
NAMES.long:
Thermal neutral pressure is the scalar kinetic pressure of the thermal neutral-particle population. It is the isotropic part of the central second velocity moment about the mean thermal-neutral flow and includes neutral internal states unless pressure is explicitly resolved by state.

For the thermal neutral distribution function $f_{n,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})$, the pressure tensor and scalar pressure are defined by:

$$
\mathbf{P}_{n,\mathrm{th}} = m_n \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{n,\mathrm{th}})(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{n,\mathrm{th}}) f_{n,\mathrm{th}}\,d^3v,\qquad p_{n,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{n,\mathrm{th}}
$$

where $m_n$ is neutral particle mass in kg, $\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{u}_{n,\mathrm{th}}$ are particle and mean-flow velocities in m s$^{-1}$, and $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the tensor trace.

Unlike [neutral pressure](name:neutral_pressure), this quantity excludes the suprathermal contribution represented by [fast neutral pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure). A selected internal-state contribution is represented by [thermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure), while [total neutral pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure) includes both thermal and fast populations.

NAMES.name: toroidal_flux_radius_at_internal_transport_barrier
NAMES.short: Toroidal flux radius at the internal transport barrier is a non-negative effective minor-radius label for the magnetic flux surface at that barrier.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal flux radius at the internal transport barrier is a non-negative, radius-like label for the magnetic flux surface at the internal transport barrier. It is the value of the [toroidal flux radius](name:toroidal_flux_radius) coordinate at that transport barrier and represents an effective minor-radius scale rather than a cylindrical major-radius coordinate.

The barrier coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor},\mathrm{ITB}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},\mathrm{ITB}}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the internal transport barrier, $B_0$ is the reference toroidal magnetic field, and ITB denotes evaluation at the barrier. The principal square root is used.

This quantity is a dimensional toroidal-flux radial coordinate at an internal transport barrier and is distinct from [toroidal flux radius at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_flux_radius_at_plasma_boundary), which defines the outer boundary value.

sources.enhanced_context: Toroidal flux coordinate (ρ_tor) at the radial position of an internal transport barrier (ITB), defined as the square root of the toroidal magnetic flux divided by π times the reference toroidal field B0.
sources.leaf_definition: Toroidal flux coordinate. rho_tor = sqrt(b_flux_tor/(pi*b0)) ~ sqrt(pi*r^2*b0/(pi*b0)) ~ r [m]. The toroidal field used in its definition is indicated under global_quantities/b0
sources.parent_definition: Radial position at which physics quantities are evaluated

NAMES.name: toroidal_vorticity
NAMES.short: Toroidal vorticity is the toroidal component of the curl of plasma bulk velocity, measuring local rotation about the toroidal direction.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal vorticity is the component of the plasma vorticity vector along the toroidal direction. It measures the signed local rotation of the bulk plasma flow in the poloidal plane and is a directional projection of [vorticity](name:vorticity).

The defining relation is:

$$
\omega_\phi = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\omega} = \hat{\phi} \cdot (\nabla \times \mathbf{v})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is the plasma vorticity, $\mathbf{v}$ is the bulk plasma velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, this projection is distinct from [vertical_vorticity](name:vertical_vorticity) and other directional components.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\omega_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: total_current_density
NAMES.short: Net electric current density summing all current-carrying mechanisms — ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions — over all plasma species, before specialization to any geometric or magnetic-field projection direction.
NAMES.long:
Total current density is the net conventional charge flux per unit area at a plasma point, formed by aggregating all current-carrying processes — ohmic induction, bootstrap, and externally driven currents — over all resolved species and charge states. It generalizes [current_density](name:current_density) to represent the full sum of current mechanisms appearing in transport and edge-plasma models, serving as the common physical basis for directional projections.

The aggregate satisfies:

$$
J_\mathrm{total} = J_\mathrm{ohmic} + J_\mathrm{bootstrap} + J_\mathrm{drive}
$$

where $J_\mathrm{ohmic}$ is the ohmic inductive contribution driven by loop voltage, $J_\mathrm{bootstrap}$ is the pressure-gradient-driven neoclassical component, and $J_\mathrm{drive}$ collects all external current-drive sources, each in A m$^{-2}$.

Directional projections specialize this parent for specific transport and edge modeling contexts: the field-aligned (parallel) component governs current balance in transport equations, while poloidal, radial, and vertical projections appear in edge models where cross-field charge transport matters — the radial projection is particularly relevant alongside other edge transport quantities such as [radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). Vertical and toroidal components are resolved along $\hat{Z}$ and $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.
NAMES.sign: Positive when conventional current flows in the positive direction of the chosen projection coordinate — in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ for toroidal projections, along $+\hat{Z}$ for vertical projections, outward along the flux-surface normal for radial projections, or aligned with the reference magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$ for the parallel projection.

NAMES.name: parallel_total_current_density
NAMES.short: Parallel total current density is the flux-surface-averaged field-aligned component of the aggregated total current density vector, normalized by the signed reference toroidal magnetic field, combining ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions over all plasma species and charge states.
NAMES.long:
The parallel total current density is the component of the aggregated current-density vector [total_current_density](name:total_current_density) resolved along the magnetic-field direction, with the transport convention that the field-aligned projection is flux-surface averaged and divided by the signed reference toroidal magnetic field. It combines ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions over all plasma species and charge states.

The defining convention is:

$$
J_{\parallel,\mathrm{total}} = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{J}_\mathrm{total}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle}{B_0}
$$

where $J_{\parallel,\mathrm{total}}$ is this quantity, $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{total}$ is the aggregated total current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B_0$ is the signed reference toroidal magnetic field, and $\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes a magnetic-flux-surface average.

This scalar is distinct from a pointwise local projection $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{total}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ because the magnetic-field projection is averaged over a flux surface before normalization by $B_0$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\left\langle \mathbf{J}_\mathrm{total}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle$ has the same sign as the signed reference toroidal magnetic field $B_0$, with $B_0$ positive when the reference toroidal magnetic field points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

NAMES.name: total_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the complete local population, equal to the sum of thermal and fast-electron densities.
NAMES.long:
Number density of free electrons per physical volume for the complete local free-electron population is the local continuum count density of electrons not bound to atoms, molecules, or ions. It explicitly aggregates the thermal and fast-electron components rather than selecting one population.

For a representative physical volume, the total density is defined by:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_a n_{e,a} = n_{e,\mathrm{thermal}} + n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total free-electron density, $n_{e,a}$ is the density of included population $a$, and the final equality applies when thermal and fast electrons are the complete population decomposition.

This local aggregate is distinct from the unqualified [electron density](name:electron_density) only in making the population sum explicit, and from [thermal electron density](name:thermal_electron_density), which excludes fast electrons. Spatially averaged electron densities are excluded.

NAMES.name: total_neutral_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Total neutral pressure is the scalar kinetic pressure of the complete neutral population, combining thermal and fast particles across all internal states.
NAMES.long:
Total neutral pressure is the scalar kinetic pressure of the complete neutral-particle population. It combines thermal and fast neutral populations and includes all unresolved internal quantum states, rather than selecting one population or state.

For the total neutral distribution function $f_n(mathbf{x},mathbf{v})$, the pressure tensor and scalar pressure are defined by:

$$
\mathbf{P}_n = m_n \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_n)(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_n) f_n(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v,\qquad p_n = \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_n
$$

where $m_n$ is neutral particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $n_n=\int f_n\,d^3v$ is total neutral number density, and $\mathbf{u}_n=n_n^{-1}\int\mathbf{v}f_n\,d^3v$ is the total mean neutral flow velocity. Thus, the central moment includes both random motion and relative streaming between included populations. It is the aggregate counterpart of [neutral pressure](name:neutral_pressure), whereas [thermal neutral pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure) excludes the fast population and [neutral internal state pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure) selects a specified internal state.

NAMES.name: total_plasma_mass_density
NAMES.short: Local plasma mass per unit volume obtained by summing electrons, main ions, and impurity charge states while excluding neutral atoms and molecules.
NAMES.long:
The total plasma mass density is the local plasma mass per unit volume obtained by summing the mass contributions of all charged plasma species. It is the equilibrium total represented by [plasma mass density](name:plasma_mass_density) and supplies the inertial term in the MHD momentum balance.

In the equilibrium description, it is defined by:

$$
\rho = \sum_s m_s n_s
$$

where $\rho$ is the total plasma mass density, $m_s$ is the particle mass in kg, $n_s$ is the number density in m$^{-3}$, and $s$ indexes electrons, main-ion isotopes, and impurity charge states.

The total refers to summation over species at one location, not spatial integration or volume averaging. Neutral atoms and molecules are excluded. This equilibrium quantity is distinct from the first-order perturbation represented by [perturbed plasma mass density](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density) and is physically equivalent to the more generic [mass density](name:mass_density).

NAMES.name: trapped_current_density
NAMES.short: Trapped current density is the electric current density carried by particles on trapped banana orbits in toroidal confinement geometry, encompassing both the direct fast-particle trapped contribution and the collisional drag back-currents induced in the thermal electron and ion populations.
NAMES.long:
Trapped current density is the portion of the total [current_density](name:current_density) arising from particles on trapped guiding-center orbits — those that execute closed banana orbits bouncing between magnetic mirror points along the field line rather than completing full toroidal transits. It encompasses both the current carried directly by energetic trapped particles and the collisional drag back-current they induce in the co-existing thermal electron and ion populations.

The vector quantity follows the species-resolved definition:

$$
\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{trap} = \sum_s q_s n_s^\mathrm{trap} \mathbf{u}_s^\mathrm{trap}
$$

where $q_s$ is the species charge, $n_s^\mathrm{trap}$ is the trapped-particle number density, and $\mathbf{u}_s^\mathrm{trap}$ is the mean flow velocity of trapped species $s$.

This quantity differs from [trapped_fast_current_density](name:trapped_fast_current_density), which excludes the thermal drag back-current and retains only the fast-particle contribution. The [toroidal_trapped_current_density](name:toroidal_trapped_current_density) is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal projection of this vector.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the conventional current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

NAMES.name: toroidal_trapped_current_density
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal current density carried by trapped particles, including direct fast-particle current and collisional drag back-current.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the current density associated with trapped particle orbits, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. It includes the direct contribution from trapped fast particles and the compensating collisional drag current induced in thermal electron and ion populations. It is the toroidal projection of [trapped current density](name:trapped_current_density), not the total plasma current.

$$
J_{\\phi,\\mathrm{trap}}(\\psi)=\\left\\langle\\mathbf{J}_{\\mathrm{trap}}\\cdot\\hat{\\phi}\\right\\rangle_{\\psi}
$$

Here $\\mathbf{J}_{\\mathrm{trap}}$ is the trapped-particle current-density vector, $\\hat{\\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame, and $\\langle\\cdot\\rangle_{\\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average at flux label $\\psi$.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal current-density component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

NAMES.name: vertical_current_density
NAMES.short: Vertical current density is the conventional charge flux per unit area projected onto the geometric vertical direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Vertical current density is the vertical component of the conventional charge-flux density represented by the [current density](name:current_density) vector. It describes signed charge transport along the geometric vertical direction.

The defining projection is:

$$
J_Z(R,\phi,Z,t)=\mathbf{J}(R,\phi,Z,t)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}$ is the full current-density vector, $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the unit vector along increasing vertical height, $R$ is major radius in meters, $\phi$ is toroidal angle in radians, $Z$ is vertical height in meters, and $t$ is time in seconds.

This quantity includes the charged-particle contributions represented by current density and excludes displacement-current density. It is a component of the vector quantity, not the electric current through a specified surface; the explicitly aggregated [vertical total current density](name:vertical_total_current_density) is a distinct total-current variant.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the conventional charge flux has a component in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

NAMES.name: vertical_vorticity
NAMES.short: Vertical vorticity is the Z-component of the curl of plasma bulk velocity in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measuring local rotation about the vertical axis.
NAMES.long:
Vertical vorticity is the component of the plasma vorticity vector along the vertical direction. It measures the signed local rotation of the bulk plasma flow in the horizontal plane and is one directional projection of [vorticity](name:vorticity).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the defining relation is:

$$
\omega_Z = \boldsymbol{\omega}\cdot\hat{Z} = (\nabla\times\mathbf{v})\cdot\hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}$ is the local bulk plasma velocity in m/s, $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is the vorticity vector in s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector. Here $R$ is major radius in m, $\phi$ is toroidal angle in radians, and $Z$ is vertical height in m.

The related [toroidal vorticity](name:toroidal_vorticity) projects the same vorticity vector onto $\hat{\phi}$ instead. The major-radius-scaled quantity [vertical vorticity divided by major radius](name:ratio_of_vertical_vorticity_to_major_radius) is distinct because it includes an additional inverse-length factor.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the bulk velocity field rotates in the right-hand sense about the positive vertical direction $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_beryllium_density
NAMES.subject: beryllium
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged number density of beryllium impurity ions over the confined plasma volume, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral beryllium atoms.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged beryllium ion number density quantifies the mean beryllium impurity content throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the volume average of the local [beryllium ion number density](name:beryllium_density), rather than a value at a particular position or along a diagnostic chord.

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{Be} = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{Be}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the local number density of beryllium ions with charge state $z+$, with $z=1$ through $4$. Neutral beryllium is excluded. The resulting global quantity is distinct from the [line-averaged beryllium density](name:line_averaged_beryllium_density) and provides the numerator for the [ratio of volume-averaged beryllium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_beryllium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_boron_density
NAMES.subject: boron
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged boron density is the elemental boron number density integrated over the plasma volume and divided by that volume, including every boron charge state.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged boron density is the elemental boron particle density averaged over the plasma volume, with neutral boron and every ionic charge state included.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_B = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_B(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_B$ is the volume-averaged quantity, $V_p$ is the plasma volume, $n_B(\mathbf{r})$ is the local [boron density](name:boron_density), and $\mathbf{r}$ specifies position. The local density includes all boron charge states through $n_B=\sum_{Z=0}^{5}n_{B,Z}$, where $Z$ is the ionic charge state and $n_{B,Z}$ is the density in that state.

This is a global volume average, distinct from the local boron density and from the [ratio of volume-averaged boron density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_boron_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which expresses the same boron content relative to the electron population.
