NAMES.name: volume_averaged_carbon_density
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Plasma-volume mean of the total number density of elemental carbon, summed over neutral carbon and all ionic charge states through fully stripped C6+.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged carbon density is the plasma-volume mean of the total number density of elemental carbon, encompassing neutral carbon atoms and all ionic charge states from singly ionized C+ through fully stripped C6+.

The volume average of the local [carbon density](name:carbon_density) is defined by

$$
\langle n_C \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_C(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_C(\mathbf{r})$ is the local total carbon number density in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the plasma volume in m$^{3}$, $dV$ is the volume element, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position. The local density includes the sum over all carbon charge states before the volume average is taken.

This quantity represents a volume average over the specified plasma volume and is distinct from [line-averaged carbon density](name:line_averaged_carbon_density), which averages along a plasma chord.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_deuterium_density
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Deuterium ion density averaged over the plasma volume is the mean local number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium ion density averaged over the plasma volume is the mean local number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is the charge-state-summed spatial average of the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_D = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_D(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_D$ is the volume-averaged deuterium density, $V$ is the specified plasma-volume domain, and $n_D(\mathbf{r})$ is the local deuterium density at position $\mathbf{r}$. The local density is summed over positive ionization states and excludes neutral atoms, molecular deuterium, and non-deuterium species.

This quantity averages over the specified plasma volume rather than along a chord; the latter is represented by [line-averaged deuterium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_effective_charge
NAMES.short: The volume average of the effective ionic charge Zeff over the plasma, providing a single global scalar characterization of bulk impurity content.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged effective charge is the plasma-volume mean of the local effective charge $Z_\text{eff}$, a dimensionless parameter quantifying how multi-charged impurity species elevate the mean-square ionic charge above the pure-hydrogen baseline. It is derived from the local [effective_charge](name:effective_charge) profile by integrating over the confined plasma volume $V$.

The local effective charge is defined by the ionic-density-weighted charge ratio

$$
Z_\text{eff}(\mathbf{r}) = \frac{\sum_i n_i(\mathbf{r}) \, Z_i^2}{n_e(\mathbf{r})}
$$

where $n_i$ is the number density of the $i$-th ion species, $Z_i$ is the corresponding atomic charge number, and $n_e = \sum_i n_i Z_i$ is the electron density imposed by quasi-neutrality. The volume-averaged quantity integrates this local value over the confined plasma volume.

This global scalar is inferred from continuum bremsstrahlung spectroscopy, where radiated power scales as $P_\text{brem} \propto n_e^2 Z_\text{eff} T_e^{1/2}$, or from impurity density profiles measured by charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy. The [line_averaged_effective_charge](name:line_averaged_effective_charge) provides an alternative single-chord diagnostic proxy, while [effective_charge_at_limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter) gives the boundary value. A pure deuterium plasma has $Z_\text{eff} = 1$; moderate impurity levels in tokamak operation yield values in the range 1.2–4, with values above 3 indicating substantial high-$Z$ contamination.
NAMES.sign: Positive for any physical plasma composition, since all ion densities $n_i$ and charge numbers $Z_i$ entering the defining sum are non-negative.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron number density averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, providing the primary global scalar for discharge density characterization and density feedback control.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged electron density $\langle n_e \rangle$ is the mean of the local electron number density integrated over the plasma volume $V$ bounded by the last closed flux surface (LCFS). It compresses the full radial electron density profile into a single global scalar that quantifies the total electron content of the discharge, serving as a primary parameter in confinement characterization and fueling control.

The defining relation is:

$$
\langle n_e \rangle = \frac{1}{V} \int_V n_e(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $n_e(\mathbf{r})$ is the local [electron density] and $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the LCFS.

Multi-channel interferometry estimates $\langle n_e \rangle$ directly by combining line-integrated electron density measurements from multiple viewing chords spanning different minor-radius positions. Profile diagnostics such as Thomson scattering and reflectometry constrain the spatial distribution, while equilibrium reconstruction provides the LCFS boundary geometry that defines $V$.

Representative values in H-mode tokamak discharges span $0.3$–$1.5 \times 10^{20}$ m$^{-3}$, with the volume average lying below the on-axis peak for centrally-peaked profiles. Together with [volume_averaged_electron_temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature) and [volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), it forms the set of global scalar parameters entering energy confinement scaling laws and Greenwald density-limit assessments.
NAMES.sign: Positive when electrons are present within the plasma volume.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless argon ion concentration given by the ratio of charge-state-summed, volume-averaged argon-ion density to volume-averaged electron density.
NAMES.long:
Argon ion concentration is the relative abundance of confined argon ions measured against the electron population. It includes argon ions summed over all ionization stages and excludes neutral argon.

$$
C_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}} \rangle}{\langle n_e \rangle}
$$

where $C_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon ion concentration, $\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}} \rangle$ is the [volume-averaged argon-ion number density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), and $\langle n_e \rangle$ is the [volume-averaged electron number density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) over the confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface. This is a ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the local argon-to-electron density ratio. It is distinct from [argon_density](name:argon_density), which gives the local or averaged argon-ion density before normalization to the electron population.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged deuterium-ion number density divided by volume-averaged electron number density, giving the electron-density-normalized deuterium abundance over the same plasma volume. Deuterium ions are summed over all positive atomic ion charge states.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged deuterium-ion number density divided by volume-averaged electron number density is the electron-density-normalized deuterium abundance over a specified plasma volume. The numerator is the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), formed from [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) summed over all positive atomic ion charge states of deuterium; it excludes neutral atoms, molecules, and deuterium bound in non-ion populations.

The ratio is defined as the quotient of volume averages over the same volume:

$$
f_{D,V} = \frac{\langle n_D \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{D,V}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_D \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and $V$ is the common averaging volume.

This quantity is a quotient of two volume-averaged densities, not the volume average of the pointwise ratio $n_D/n_e$. For non-negative number densities and positive $\langle n_e \rangle_V$, the ratio is non-negative; it is not the fraction of deuterium among all fuel nuclei and does not represent the absolute deuterium particle inventory.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless abundance ratio of the volume-averaged deuterium-tritium fuel-ion density to the volume-averaged electron number density.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the abundance ratio of the combined deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species to electrons, with both densities averaged over the same plasma volume. The numerator corresponds to the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density).

$$
\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{DT}/e} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{DT}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the local number density of deuterium and tritium fuel ions treated as one combined species, $n_e$ is the local electron number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes a volume average over the common plasma volume $V$. The deuterium-tritium ion density is summed over the relevant ionic charge states; this ratio is the ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of a local density ratio.

NAMES.name: time_derivative_of_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Rate of change of the electron number density averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the temporal rate of change of [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). It describes the evolution of the global density measure rather than the local density derivative or a directed particle flux.

The defining relation is

$$
\frac{d\langle n_e\rangle}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left[\frac{1}{V(t)}\int_{V(t)} n_e(\mathbf{x},t)\,dV\right]
$$

where $n_e(\mathbf{x},t)$ is the local electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $V(t)$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\langle n_e\rangle$ denotes the volume average. The derivative includes changes in the local density and, when the boundary moves, changes in the averaging volume.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Mean random kinetic energy of the electron population expressed as an energy-equivalent temperature, averaged uniformly over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged electron temperature is the second-moment measure of the random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population, averaged uniformly over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface. It is the volume-averaged counterpart of [electron_temperature](name:electron_temperature) and the volume analog of [line_averaged_electron_temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature).

The defining volume average is

$$
T_{e,V} = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $T_{e,V}$ is the volume-averaged temperature, $T_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron temperature at position $\mathbf{x}$, $V$ is the confined plasma volume, and $dV$ is the differential volume element.

The average is geometric rather than density-weighted. It excludes directed-flow energy and is distinct from [thermal_electron_energy](name:thermal_electron_energy), which uses the density-weighted integral of the local electron temperature.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_helium_3_density
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged helium-3 ion number density is the mean charged-ion population over the confined plasma volume, summed over singly ionized and fully stripped states and excluding neutral atoms.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged helium-3 ion number density is the spatial mean of the charged helium-3 ion population throughout the confined plasma volume. It is derived from the local [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density), rather than representing a density at one location.

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,d^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion density summed over singly ionized and fully stripped states. Neutral helium-3 atoms are excluded. The [line-averaged helium-3 density](name:line_averaged_helium_3_density) instead averages the same local quantity along a specified path.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Ratio of volume-averaged helium-3 density to volume-averaged electron density is the confined-plasma-volume composition ratio formed after averaging each density over the same volume. Helium-3 density is the charged helium-3 ion number density summed over all charge states and excludes neutral atoms.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of volume-averaged helium-3 density to volume-averaged electron density is the composition ratio obtained by dividing the confined-plasma-volume average of helium-3 ion number density by the corresponding average electron number density. The helium-3 ion density in the numerator is summed over all charged ionization states of helium-3 and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms.

The ratio is defined with both averages taken over the same confined plasma volume before division:

$$
r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e} =
\frac{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e}$ is this ratio, $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density summed over all charged ionization states, $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position, and $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume.

This quantity is a ratio of two independently averaged densities, not the confined-volume average of the local ratio $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}/n_e$. Its numerator is [volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), its denominator is [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and closely related composition ratios include [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density) and [ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_helium_4_density
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged number density of helium-4 ions over the confined plasma volume, providing a global measure of fusion-ash concentration in deuterium-tritium plasmas.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged helium-4 ion number density quantifies the mean concentration of fusion-ash ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the global counterpart of the local [helium-4 ion density](name:helium_4_density) and is distinct from the chord mean [line-averaged helium-4 density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density).

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^4\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local helium-4 ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position.

The helium-4 ion population is summed over all ionic charge states, while neutral helium is excluded. Its ratio to the volume-averaged electron density is defined by [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: Ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density is the confined-plasma-volume composition ratio of helium-4 ion number density, summed over all charge states, to electron number density. Neutral helium atoms are excluded, and both densities are volume averaged before division.
NAMES.long:
Ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron density is the confined-plasma-volume composition ratio of helium-4 ion number density to electron number density. The helium-4 density in the numerator is summed over all charge states of helium-4 ions before volume averaging; neutral helium-4 atoms are excluded.

The ratio is defined from independent volume averages over the confined plasma volume:

$$
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}, \qquad \langle n_s\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{conf}}\int_{V_\mathrm{conf}} n_s(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ is this composition ratio, $\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged helium-4 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $V_\mathrm{conf}$ is the confined plasma volume, and $dV$ is an element of plasma volume. For $s={}^4\mathrm{He}$, $n_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-4 ion number density summed over all charge states; for $s=e$, it is the local electron number density.

The denominator and numerator are averaged independently, so this quantity is not the volume average of the local ratio $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}/n_e$. In a quasi-neutral plasma with fully stripped helium-4 ions, $2 f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ is the fraction of the electron charge balance supplied by helium-4 ions. The analogous isotope composition ratio is [ratio of volume-averaged helium-3 density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_ion_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged temperature of a specified ion species over the confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged ion temperature is the temperature of a specified ion species averaged over the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle T_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_{\rm LCFS}}\int_{V_{\rm LCFS}} T_i(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $T_i(\mathbf{r})$ is the local temperature of the specified ion species, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $dV$ is the volume element, and $V_{\rm LCFS}$ is the confined volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. The local quantity being averaged is [ion temperature](name:ion_temperature). This species-resolved average does not density-weight or sum temperatures across different ion species; that combined quantity is represented by [volume-averaged total ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_iron_density
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged iron density is the total number density of iron ions, summed over Fe1+ through Fe26+ and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged iron density is the total number density of iron ions, aggregated over all iron charge states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ and averaged throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatially averaged form of [iron_density](name:iron_density), not a charge-state-resolved quantity.

The volume-averaged density is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{p}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{p}}} \left(\sum_{z=1}^{26} n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})\right)\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the volume-averaged iron density in m$^{-3}$, $V_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the confined plasma volume in m$^{3}$, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local density of iron charge state $z$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $dV$ is a volume element.

Neutral iron is excluded, and the result does not preserve the distribution among charge states. It differs from [volume_averaged_ion_density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) through its fixed iron-species scope and from [iron_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:iron_density_at_magnetic_axis) because it represents a volume average rather than a local axis value.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_krypton_density
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Number density of krypton, volume-averaged over the plasma, summed over neutral krypton and all ionized charge states through fully stripped Kr36+.
NAMES.long:
Number density of krypton, volume-averaged over the plasma, summed over neutral krypton and all ionized charge states through fully stripped Kr$^{36+}$.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} \left(\sum_{q=0}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}}^{(q)}(\mathbf{r})\right) d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}^{(q)}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local number density of krypton in charge state $q$; $q=0$ denotes neutral krypton and $q=36$ denotes fully stripped krypton.

Unlike the local [krypton density](name:krypton_density), this quantity includes neutral krypton and applies a plasma-volume average. It is an absolute elemental density, distinct from the normalized abundance in the [volume-averaged krypton-to-electron density ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_krypton_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_lithium_density
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged total number density of lithium ions, summed over all charge states from Li+ through fully stripped Li3+, within the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
This is the volume average of lithium ion number density, summed over all ionization stages from Li+ through fully stripped Li3+, throughout the confined plasma. Neutral lithium is excluded. The quantity provides a global measure of lithium impurity content rather than a local or boundary value.

The volume average is defined as

$$
\overline{n}_{Li} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{Li}\,dV
$$

where $n_{Li}$ is the local lithium-ion number density, $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the physical volume element. Unlike the boundary value [flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary), this quantity averages over the full confined volume. Its electron-normalized counterpart is the [ratio of volume-averaged lithium density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_lithium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_nitrogen_density
NAMES.subject: nitrogen
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged nitrogen density is the plasma-volume mean of nitrogen nuclei number density, with neutral and all ionized charge states included.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged nitrogen density is the plasma-volume mean of the local number density of nitrogen atomic nuclei. It is a species-level density, so neutral nitrogen and every ionized charge state contribute to the average; the local quantity is [nitrogen density](name:nitrogen_density).

The volume average and charge-state aggregation are defined by

$$
\overline{n}_N = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_N(\mathbf{r})\,dV, \qquad n_N(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{z=0}^{7} n_{\mathrm{N}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\overline{n}_N$ and $n_{\mathrm{N}^{z+}}$ are number densities in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $z$ is the nitrogen charge-state index from neutral nitrogen ($z=0$) through fully stripped nitrogen ($z=7$).

The average is over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. Unlike [line-averaged nitrogen density](name:line_averaged_nitrogen_density), it weights volume elements rather than points along a specified chord.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_oxygen_density
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged oxygen density is the spatial mean of the local oxygen number density, summed over all charge states from neutral O0 through fully stripped O8+, over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged oxygen density is the volume mean of the local oxygen number density—summed over all charge states from neutral O$^0$ through fully stripped O$^{8+}$—within the confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface. It characterizes the total oxygen impurity inventory per confined plasma volume, independent of how that oxygen is distributed inside the boundary.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{O} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} \int_{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} n_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{r})\, dV
$$

where $\langle n_\mathrm{O} \rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged oxygen density, $V_\mathrm{LCFS}$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, $dV$ is a volume element, and $n_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density), with $n_\mathrm{O}=\sum_{Z=0}^{8} n_{\mathrm{O}^{Z+}}$.

This quantity differs from [line_averaged_oxygen_density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density), which is a chord mean rather than a confined-volume mean. It is a charge-state-summed species density and must not be interpreted as an ionic-only density that excludes neutral oxygen.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, with all included species and charge states contributing by number density and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged total ion temperature is the volume average of the local density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\int_V T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV}{\int_V dV}
$$

where $V$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is its differential volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local quantity defined by [total_ion_temperature](name:total_ion_temperature). Species and charge-state density weighting is performed locally before the volume averaging. Unlike [line_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity averages over volume rather than along a plasma chord.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_tritium_density
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged number density of tritium ions over the confined plasma volume, obtained from the local charge-state-summed fuel-ion density.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged tritium ion number density quantifies the mean concentration of hydrogen-3 fuel ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the spatial average of the local [tritium_density](name:tritium_density), rather than a chord average such as [line_averaged_tritium_density](name:line_averaged_tritium_density).

$$
\overline{n}_T = \frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_T\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_T$ is the volume-averaged tritium ion number density, $n_T$ is the local tritium ion number density, $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume element. The tritium ion density is summed over all ionic charge states and excludes neutral tritium. This quantity provides the tritium-density basis for volume-averaged isotopic ratios and is distinct from the local boundary value [tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
NAMES.short: The ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density measures volume-averaged tritium abundance relative to the volume-averaged free-electron population, with tritium ions summed over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
The ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density is the volume-mean tritium-ion number density normalized by the volume-mean free-electron number density. The tritium density in the numerator is the tritium-ion number density summed over all charge states.

The defining ratio uses separately volume-averaged densities over the same plasma volume:

$$
f_{T/e,V} =
\frac{\langle n_T\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V},
\qquad
\langle n_s\rangle_V =
\frac{\int_{\Omega} n_s(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\int_{\Omega} dV}
$$

where $f_{T/e,V}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_T\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $\Omega$ is the plasma volume common to both averages, and $n_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density being averaged.

The numerator contains only the tritium contribution; deuterium, other hydrogen isotopes, helium ash, and impurity ions are excluded from $\langle n_T\rangle_V$, although their ion charge can contribute to $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ in a quasi-neutral plasma. This quantity is the ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio $n_T/n_e$, and it has no built-in reference to a peak-density time or other temporal extremum.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_tungsten_density
NAMES.subject: tungsten
NAMES.short: Volume-averaged number density of positively charged tungsten ions within the plasma enclosed by the last closed flux surface, summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
Volume-averaged tungsten-ion density is the spatial mean of the local charge-state-summed density [tungsten-ion density](name:tungsten_density) over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface. It includes all positive tungsten ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local tungsten-ion density, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the enclosed plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position, and $dV$ is the volume element. The local density is the sum of the densities of all tungsten charge states from W$^{1+}$ through W$^{74+}$.

This quantity is distinct from the boundary [flux-surface-averaged tungsten density](name:flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary) and from the impurity-abundance [ratio of volume-averaged tungsten density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density), which is normalized to electron density.

NAMES.name: volume_averaged_xenon_density
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Number density of xenon ions averaged over the full plasma volume, including all charged xenon ionization states and excluding neutral xenon.
NAMES.long:
The volume-averaged xenon ion number density is the plasma-wide mean of the local [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which sums xenon ions from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral atoms.

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the volume-averaged xenon ion density, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local xenon ion density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_p$ is the full plasma volume, and $dV$ is the physical volume element. The averaging is over the plasma volume rather than along a measurement chord or at a single locus. The resulting global impurity-content measure can be compared with electron content through the [ratio of volume-averaged xenon density to volume-averaged electron density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_xenon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

NAMES.name: density_at_outboard_midplane
NAMES.short: Particle number density of a specified plasma species at the outboard midplane is the local particle count per volume for that species at the low-field-side intersection of a magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane.
NAMES.long:
Particle number density of a specified plasma species at the outboard midplane is the local particle count per physical volume for that species at the fixed outboard-midplane locus of the selected magnetic flux surface. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height, this locus is the larger-$R$ crossing of that flux surface with the equatorial midplane.

The local density is defined by the differential particle count evaluated at the outboard-midplane position:

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{omp}}) = \left.\frac{dN_s}{dV}\right|_{\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{omp}}}
$$

where $N_s$ is the particle number of species $s$, $V$ is physical volume, and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{omp}}$ is the outboard-midplane point on the selected magnetic flux surface.

The species label is the abstraction axis of this parent quantity; the evaluation position is always the outboard midplane. For a species not resolved by charge state, this per-volume amount is summed over all charge states. Species-specific standard names, such as [electron density at the outboard midplane](name:electron_density_at_outboard_midplane), instantiate the same fixed-locus quantity for a particular population. This is a local value, not a flux-surface average, line average, or volume average.

NAMES.name: electron_density_at_outboard_midplane
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron particle number density at the low-field-side intersection of a magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane.
NAMES.long:
Electron number density at the outboard midplane is the local density of the electron population at the low-field-side intersection of a specified magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane. It is the electron-specific member of [density_at_outboard_midplane](name:density_at_outboard_midplane).

At that location, the density is defined by the zeroth velocity-space moment

$$
n_e(R,\phi,Z)=\int f_e(R,\phi,Z,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_e$ is electron number density, $f_e$ is the electron velocity-distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. The position is described in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This quantity counts electrons only and is distinct from total particle density and from electron density evaluated at the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: normalized_collisionality
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of a specified interspecies collision frequency to the characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce frequency used for the plasma population.
NAMES.long:
This collisionality measures the strength of interspecies collisional relaxation relative to collisionless motion along magnetic-field trajectories.

$$
\nu_{ab}^{*} = \frac{\nu_{ab}}{\omega_{\mathrm{char}}}
$$

where $\nu_{ab}$ is the collision frequency between species $a$ and $b$, and $\omega_{\mathrm{char}}$ is the relevant characteristic streaming, transit, or bounce angular frequency; both quantities have reciprocal-time units.

The denominator must be interpreted according to the selected orbit or motion class, so this quantity is distinct from the collision frequency itself. It generalizes the population-specific [electron collisionality](name:electron_collisionality) and complements [collisionality at the pedestal top](name:collisionality_at_pedestal_top) when the characteristic frequency is evaluated there.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalised collisionality (ν*) between pairs of particle species in a local gyrokinetic simulation. Represents the ratio of the inter-species collision frequency to a characteristic transit frequency, governing collisional coupling and neoclassical effects.
sources.leaf_definition: Normalised collisionality between two species
sources.parent_definition: Collisions related quantities

NAMES.name: normalized_debye_length
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of the multispecies Debye shielding length to the positive reference length used by the gyrokinetic formulation.
NAMES.long:
The multispecies Debye shielding length is the electrostatic screening scale produced by the combined response of all charged species. This quantity expresses that scale relative to the positive reference length selected for the gyrokinetic formulation.

$$
\lambda_{D,\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{1}{L_{\mathrm{ref}}}\left(\sum_s \frac{n_s q_s^2}{\epsilon_0 k_B T_s}\right)^{-1/2}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of species $s$, $q_s$ is its particle charge, $T_s$ is its thermodynamic temperature, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, $\epsilon_0$ is the vacuum permittivity, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the gyrokinetic reference length. The sum includes the charged species contributing to quasistatic Debye shielding and excludes neutral populations. The underlying shielding length also enters the [Coulomb logarithm](name:coulomb_logarithm); this normalized quantity is not a species-specific screening length.

sources.leaf_definition: Debye length computed from the reference quantities (see detailed documentation at the root of the IDS)

NAMES.name: normalized_effective_particle_energy
NAMES.short: Normalized effective particle energy is the ratio of a species effective particle-energy coordinate to the positive species reference thermal-energy scale.
NAMES.long:
Normalized effective particle energy is the ratio of a species effective particle-energy coordinate to the positive species reference thermal-energy scale. It is a dimensionless velocity-space coordinate for the effective single-particle energy relative to that species reference, not an independent temperature, mass, or charge ratio.

The normalization is

$$
\bar{\mathcal{E}}_s = \frac{\mathcal{E}^{*}_{\mathrm{eff},s}}{E_{\mathrm{th,ref},s}}
$$

where $\bar{\mathcal{E}}_s$ is the normalized effective particle energy, $s$ labels the particle species, $\mathcal{E}^{*}_{\mathrm{eff},s}$ is the effective particle-energy coordinate for that species expressed on a scale compatible with the denominator, and $E_{\mathrm{th,ref},s} > 0$ is the species reference thermal-energy scale. If the reference is specified by a species reference temperature $T_{\mathrm{ref},s}$, the corresponding denominator is $E_{\mathrm{th,ref},s}=k_B T_{\mathrm{ref},s}$; the same reference temperature appears in [ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_reference_particle_temperature](name:ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_reference_particle_temperature).

It is distinguished from [effective_particle_energy](name:effective_particle_energy), which denotes the effective-energy coordinate without requiring this particular species thermal normalization. If the effective particle energy contains an additive effective-potential term $U_{\mathrm{eff},s}$, its normalized contribution is $U_{\mathrm{eff},s}/E_{\mathrm{th,ref},s}$; with the same denominator this is normalized_particle_effective_potential. The detailed split of the effective energy into kinetic and potential terms and the choice of potential-energy zero are not fixed by this name.

NAMES.name: derivative_with_respect_to_poloidal_angle_of_normalized_effective_particle_energy
NAMES.short: Poloidal-angle derivative of the normalized effective particle-energy coordinate, resolving its variation around a magnetic flux surface at fixed flux-surface and toroidal coordinates.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the directional variation of the normalized effective particle-energy coordinate as position advances in poloidal angle. It resolves a specific poloidal derivative rather than the energy coordinate itself or its complete gradient.

Using flux coordinates $(\psi,\theta,\phi)$, it is defined as

$$
\mathcal{E}_\theta = \left.\frac{\partial \mathcal{E}}{\partial \theta}\right|_{\psi,\phi}
$$

where $\mathcal{E}_\theta$ is the poloidal-angle derivative, $\mathcal{E}$ is [normalized effective particle energy](name:normalized_effective_particle_energy), $\theta$ is poloidal angle, $\psi$ is the flux-surface label, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle.

The normalized coordinate relates [effective particle energy](name:effective_particle_energy) to a positive species reference thermal-energy scale. The derivative is evaluated at fixed $\psi$ and $\phi$ and may be positive, negative, or zero; when centrifugal contributions are included in the effective energy, it describes their poloidal variation relevant to species density behavior.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalised effective potential energy gradient determining the poloidal variation of the background density of a species in a local gyrokinetic simulation. Accounts for centrifugal effects on density distribution along the flux surface.

NAMES.name: normalized_energy_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Gyro-Bohm-normalized turbulent energy-flux contribution from the perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential is the dimensionless flux-surface-normal energy transport channel caused by δA∥ magnetic flutter in a rotating-frame gyrokinetic description.
NAMES.long:
Gyro-Bohm-normalized turbulent energy-flux contribution from the perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential is the dimensionless signed flux-surface-normal transport of gyrocenter energy caused by magnetic flutter from $\delta A_\parallel$ in a rotating-frame gyrokinetic description. Gyrocenters streaming along field-line perturbations associated with $\delta A_\parallel$ carry energy across neighboring magnetic flux surfaces.

The normalized channel is the energy moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution coupled to the $\delta A_\parallel$ magnetic-flutter velocity, divided by the positive gyro-Bohm reference energy flux:

$$
\widehat{Q}_{A_\parallel}
=
\frac{1}{Q_\mathrm{gB}}
\left\langle
\sum_s \int d^3v \; \mathcal{E}_s \, \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta f_s^{*} v_{\psi,A_\parallel,s}\right]
\right\rangle
$$

where $\widehat{Q}_{A_\parallel}$ is this normalized energy-flux contribution, $Q_\mathrm{gB}$ is the gyro-Bohm reference energy flux, $s$ indexes species, $d^3v$ denotes integration over velocity space, $\mathcal{E}_s$ is the gyrocenter energy for species $s$, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, $v_{\psi,A_\parallel,s}$ is the flux-surface-normal magnetic-flutter velocity generated by $\delta A_\parallel$, and $\langle\cdots\rangle$ denotes the turbulence and magnetic-flux-surface averaging that defines the scalar flux. For complex spectral amplitudes, the product is the real part of the complex-conjugate correlation. The reference flux has the gyro-Bohm form $Q_\mathrm{gB}=n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}v_{\mathrm{th,ref}}(\rho_\mathrm{ref}/L_\mathrm{ref})^2$, where $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is a reference density, $T_\mathrm{ref}$ is a reference temperature, $v_{\mathrm{th,ref}}$ is a reference thermal speed, $\rho_\mathrm{ref}$ is a reference gyroradius, and $L_\mathrm{ref}$ is a reference gradient scale length.

This quantity identifies only the $\delta A_\parallel$ field-channel contribution to gyrocenter-energy transport; it is not the total turbulent energy flux, the [particle-flux counterpart](name:normalized_particle_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential), the [parallel-momentum-flux counterpart](name:normalized_parallel_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential), or electromagnetic Poynting flux. It is distinct from the electrostatic $\delta\phi$ and compressional magnetic $\delta B_\parallel$ energy-flux channels; resolving or summing perpendicular-wavevector content changes the aggregation, not the underlying channel. The [flux-surface-resolved gyrocenter energy-flux counterpart](name:normalized_radial_gyrocenter_energy_flux_at_flux_surface_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential) retains the local flux-surface dependence before the same channel is aggregated. The normalized magnitude is interpreted relative to $Q_\mathrm{gB}$, so a magnitude near unity denotes an $A_\parallel$ channel comparable to the gyro-Bohm reference scale.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed-parallel-vector-potential contribution carries gyrocenter energy in the flux-surface-normal direction toward increasing flux coordinate $\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$ (normalized toroidal-flux radius).

NAMES.name: normalized_frequency_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode
NAMES.short: Dimensionless real oscillation frequency of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized by the positive reference angular frequency for the same perpendicular wavevector.
NAMES.long:
The quantity is the real oscillation-frequency component of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode in the local flux-tube approximation. It is evaluated for a specified wavevector perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field.

The normalized frequency is defined by

$$
\omega_{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{\operatorname{Re}(\omega)}{\omega_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\omega$ is the complex eigenfrequency and $\omega_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference angular frequency used for the same eigenvalue problem.

Together with the [normalized linear growth rate](name:normalized_linear_growth_rate_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode), this quantity specifies the real and imaginary components of the normalized complex eigenfrequency. Its sign follows the temporal Fourier and wave-propagation convention used to define $\omega$.

NAMES.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Two-component vector of the normalized pressure moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, with components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field, each normalized to a reference thermal pressure.
NAMES.long:
The normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is a vector quantity collecting the dimensionless parallel and perpendicular thermal-pressure responses of the non-equilibrium part of the gyrocenter distribution function $\delta f_s$ for a single plasma species, normalized to a reference thermal pressure $p_{\mathrm{ref}} = n_{\mathrm{ref}} T_{\mathrm{ref}}$. It generalizes the scalar gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure to the full anisotropic pressure decomposition along and across the local magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$.

The two components are defined as velocity-space integrals:

$$
\hat{p}_{\parallel/\perp,\,s} = \frac{m_s}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int w_{\parallel/\perp}\, \delta f_s\, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, the weight $w_\parallel = v_\parallel^2$ defines the parallel component (see parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) and $w_\perp = v_\perp^2/2$ defines the perpendicular gyrotropic component (see [perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure)), with $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ the velocity projections along and across $\hat{b}$ respectively.

This vector is computed in gyrokinetic simulations as part of the velocity-space moment hierarchy characterizing pressure anisotropy driven by electromagnetic fluctuations. Gyroaveraged variants incorporating finite-Larmor-radius corrections are provided by perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_gyroaveraged_pressure and parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_gyroaveraged_pressure.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function increases the respective pressure moment above the equilibrium reference value.

NAMES.name: normalized_linear_growth_rate_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode
NAMES.short: Dimensionless imaginary part of the complex linear gyrokinetic eigenmode frequency, divided by the positive reference angular frequency, at a specified wavevector perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field in the local flux-tube approximation. Positive values represent exponential growth and negative values represent damping.
NAMES.long:
Dimensionless imaginary part of the complex linear gyrokinetic eigenmode frequency, divided by the positive reference angular frequency, is the normalized temporal growth rate of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode at a specified wavevector perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field in the local flux-tube approximation. It identifies the exponential amplitude change of that eigenmode in linear gyrokinetic theory.

The defining normalization is

$$
\gamma_\mathrm{norm} = \frac{\operatorname{Im}\omega}{\omega_\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $\omega$ is the complex eigenfrequency for time dependence $\exp(-i\omega t)$ and $\omega_\mathrm{ref}>0$ is the reference angular frequency used for the normalized eigenfrequency. When the reference angular frequency is written as $v_{\mathrm{th,ref}}/L_\mathrm{ref}$, this is equivalently $\gamma_\mathrm{norm}=\gamma L_\mathrm{ref}/v_{\mathrm{th,ref}}$, with $\gamma=\operatorname{Im}\omega$, $v_{\mathrm{th,ref}}$ the reference thermal speed, and $L_\mathrm{ref}$ the reference length scale.

This quantity is for one linear gyrokinetic eigenmode at one specified perpendicular wavevector, not for a spectrum-averaged rate, nonlinear turbulent growth, or finite-amplitude envelope evolution. It is the imaginary-part counterpart to the [normalized_frequency_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode](name:normalized_frequency_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode), which uses the real part of the same $\omega$; the eigenmode-specific scope distinguishes it from [normalized_growth_rate](name:normalized_linear_growth_rate_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode), which does not by itself require a linear gyrokinetic eigenvalue.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the eigenmode amplitude increases exponentially with time.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalised growth rate (γ) of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode for a given wavevector in the local flux-tube geometry. Quantifies the exponential growth of micro-instabilities such as ITG, TEM, or ETG modes.

NAMES.name: normalized_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Gyro-Bohm-normalized parallel component of the toroidal momentum flux driven by perturbed parallel magnetic-field fluctuations in gyrokinetic turbulence.
NAMES.long:
Normalized parallel momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel magnetic field is the dimensionless, parallel-velocity-weighted electromagnetic contribution to turbulent radial transport of toroidal angular momentum.

The normalized quantity is defined by

$$
\widehat{\Pi}_{\phi,\parallel}^{\delta B_\parallel} = \frac{\Pi_{\phi,\parallel}^{\delta B_\parallel}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{GB}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi,\parallel}^{\delta B_\parallel}$ is the toroidal momentum flux in the parallel velocity-space channel driven by the perturbed parallel magnetic field, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{GB}}$ is the gyro-Bohm reference momentum-flux scale. The perturbation $\delta B_\parallel$ is the magnetic-field-magnitude fluctuation along the equilibrium magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$.

This is the parallel component of the aggregate [momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel magnetic field](name:normalized_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field), complementary to the [normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel magnetic field](name:normalized_perpendicular_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field). It excludes contributions attributed to the electrostatic potential and the perturbed parallel vector potential, including the [normalized parallel momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential](name:normalized_parallel_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential). The normalization follows the gyrokinetic reference based on outboard-midplane electron density and temperature.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the toroidal angular momentum flux is directed outward across magnetic flux surfaces, away from the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_mass
NAMES.short: Dimensionless ratio of a species’ particle mass to a positive reference mass, preserving relative inertial scales in normalized kinetic equations.
NAMES.long:
This quantity expresses the inertial mass of one particle of a specified species relative to a strictly positive reference mass. It is the normalized counterpart of [particle mass](name:particle_mass), rather than an independent mass or mass density.

The normalized particle mass is defined by

$$
\bar{m}_s = \frac{m_s}{m_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$ and $m_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference mass used by the normalization. The result preserves the relative inertial ordering of species while removing the mass scale from normalized equations of motion.

The reference mass must be kept fixed when comparing normalized masses; changing it rescales all such ratios by the same factor. This quantity excludes mass associated with a population or volume and does not represent a mass density.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalised mass of a particle species in a local gyrokinetic simulation, expressed in units of the reference mass. Sets the species inertia entering the gyrokinetic equations and is used to determine the gyroradius and cyclotron frequency ratios.
sources.leaf_definition: Normalised mass
sources.parent_definition: Set of species (including electrons) used in the calculation and related quantities

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Normalized gyrotropic pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components parallel and perpendicular to the background magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The normalized particle perturbed pressure is a gyrotropic vector quantity representing the pressure fluctuation of the physical particle population in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components parallel and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, each expressed dimensionlessly as a ratio to a reference thermal pressure $p_\mathrm{ref}$.

For species $s$, the parallel and perpendicular components are the second velocity-space moments of the perturbed particle distribution function $\delta f_s$:

$$
\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} = \frac{m_s}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\parallel^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v, \qquad \hat{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{m_s}{2 \, p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\perp^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are velocities parallel and perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$, and $p_\mathrm{ref} = n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}$ is evaluated at the outboard midplane.

Unlike the corresponding [gyroaveraged gyrocenter perturbed pressure], this quantity is built from the full particle distribution function, implicitly incorporating finite-Larmor-radius corrections through the particle-to-gyrocenter coordinate transformation. The isotropic scalar parent particle_perturbed_pressure is recovered as the trace average $\hat{p}_s = (\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} + 2\hat{p}_{\perp,s})/3$. The [parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure) and [perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure) components together encode the pressure anisotropy of the eigenmode, with the ratio $\hat{p}_{\parallel,s}/\hat{p}_{\perp,s}$ quantifying deviation from local thermodynamic equilibrium relevant to mirror-mode and fire-hose stability.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the species pressure perturbation corresponds to a local increase above the equilibrium background pressure.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless form of the perturbed current density vector, obtained by normalizing the deviation of current density from its equilibrium value to characterize finite-Larmor-radius current responses in gyrokinetic turbulence.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed current density is the dimensionless vector representation of the deviation of current density from its equilibrium value, derived as a charge-weighted velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function $\delta f$. Normalization by a reference current scale renders the quantity independent of bulk plasma parameters and enables direct comparison of fluctuation amplitudes across different equilibrium configurations.

The normalization follows the gyrokinetic moment convention:

$$
\widetilde{\mathbf{J}} = \frac{\delta \mathbf{J}}{n_\mathrm{ref}\, e\, v_\mathrm{th,ref}}
$$

where $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is a reference number density, $e$ is the elementary charge, and $v_\mathrm{th,ref}$ is a reference thermal velocity. Finite-Larmor-radius effects enter through Bessel-function weighting of the velocity-space integrals, capturing the off-diagonal current response at wave scales comparable to the ion gyroradius.

The parallel projection of this vector, [parallel_normalized_perturbed_current_density](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_current_density), is the component most directly relevant to electromagnetic coupling in gyrokinetic eigenmode calculations. The dimensional counterpart [perturbed_current_density](name:perturbed_current_density) provides the species-resolved current deviation in physical units, to which this quantity reduces upon application of the inverse normalization scale.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Dimensionless vector form of the magnetic-field perturbation, obtained by dividing the deviation of the magnetic field from its equilibrium reference value by the equilibrium field magnitude.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed magnetic field $\delta\hat{\mathbf{B}}$ is the pointwise dimensionless ratio of the magnetic-field deviation from the equilibrium background to the equilibrium field magnitude.

$$
\delta\hat{\mathbf{B}} = \frac{\delta\mathbf{B}}{B_0}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{B} - \mathbf{B}_0$ is the fluctuating component of the total magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}_0$ is the equilibrium background field, and $B_0 = |\mathbf{B}_0|$ is the equilibrium field magnitude used as the normalizing scale. This normalization is standard in gyrokinetic formulations for representing electromagnetic fluctuations in dimensionless form.

This quantity is the dimensionless counterpart of [perturbed_magnetic_field](name:perturbed_magnetic_field). Its [parallel projection](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_magnetic_field) along the equilibrium field direction isolates the compressional electromagnetic fluctuation channel, in which perturbations alter the local field strength rather than only bending field lines.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Dimensionless total isotropic pressure moment of the perturbed particle distribution function for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized by the equilibrium species reference pressure.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed pressure is the dimensionless isotropic trace of the pressure tensor perturbation carried by the particle distribution function for a single plasma species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. It captures the second velocity-space moment of the non-equilibrium part $\delta f_s$ combined symmetrically over parallel and perpendicular velocity directions and normalized to the equilibrium reference pressure. As the undifferentiated total, it is the parent abstraction for its directional decompositions; see [perturbed_pressure](name:perturbed_pressure) for the species-agnostic scalar concept.

The normalized total pressure moment is:

$$
\tilde{p}_s = \frac{1}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int \frac{m_s}{3}\left(v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2\right) \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ is the velocity component along the equilibrium magnetic field, $v_\perp^2 = v_{\perp 1}^2 + v_{\perp 2}^2$ is the squared perpendicular speed summed over the two gyrophase directions, and $p_\mathrm{ref} = n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference pressure. The factor $1/3$ imposes the isotropic trace average $\tilde{p}_s = (\tilde{p}_\parallel + 2\tilde{p}_\perp)/3$.

This moment is computed in local linear gyrokinetic solvers as part of the perturbed-moment hierarchy. Its perpendicular projection is the [perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure) and the parallel particle-frame component is [parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure); the corresponding gyrocenter-frame parent is parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure. For linear eigenmodes the quantity is generally complex-valued, with phase set by the eigenmode normalization convention; reported magnitudes are normalization-dependent.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the velocity-space moment of the perturbed particle distribution yields a net pressure enhancement above the equilibrium reference pressure.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
NAMES.short: Normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the dimensionless total pressure response of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, formed from parallel and perpendicular pressure moments weighted by the first-order Bessel function evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument and normalized to the equilibrium species pressure.
NAMES.long:
Normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the dimensionless total pressure response of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, formed from parallel and perpendicular pressure moments weighted by the first-order Bessel function evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument and normalized to the equilibrium species pressure. It is a species-resolved complex amplitude representing the finite-Larmor-radius part of the gyrocenter pressure response.

For species $s$, it is defined by the sum of the first-order Bessel-weighted parallel and perpendicular pressure moments divided by the equilibrium species pressure:

$$
\widehat{P}^{(J_1)}_s = \frac{P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)} + P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)}}{p_s}, \qquad P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)} = \int d^3v\, m_s v_\parallel^2 J_1(\lambda_s)\widetilde{F}_{g,s}, \qquad P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)} = \int d^3v\, m_s \frac{v_\perp^2}{2} J_1(\lambda_s)\widetilde{F}_{g,s}
$$

where $P_{\parallel s}^{(J_1)}$ and $P_{\perp s}^{(J_1)}$ are pressure-moment amplitudes with pressure units, $p_s=n_sT_s$ is the equilibrium species pressure when $T_s$ is expressed as energy per particle, $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are velocities parallel and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\widetilde{F}_{g,s}$ is the perturbation amplitude of the gyrocenter distribution. The first-order Bessel function $J_1$ is evaluated on the gyroaveraging argument $\lambda_s=k_\perp v_\perp/\Omega_s$, with $k_\perp$ the magnitude of the wave vector perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field and $\Omega_s=|q_s|B/m_s$ the positive cyclotron-frequency magnitude.

The total moment is the sum of parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1 and [perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1](name:perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1). It is a gyrocenter-distribution moment with explicit $J_1(\lambda_s)$ weighting; it is distinct from [normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure), which lacks this Bessel-1 weighting, and from particle-distribution pressure perturbations such as [normalized_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_perturbed_pressure) and [normalized_total_particle_perturbed_pressure_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode](name:normalized_total_particle_perturbed_pressure_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode). Because $J_1(0)=0$, this member vanishes at zero gyroaveraging argument.

In a linear eigenmode, $\widetilde{F}_{g,s}$ is the complex coefficient multiplying the chosen harmonic phase factor. This moment inherits the same arbitrary global amplitude and phase normalization as the eigenmode; changing the reference phase multiplies all perturbation amplitudes by the same complex factor, so its sign and phase are defined only relative to that reference.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Vector of the dimensionless perturbed electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence, normalized by a reference electromagnetic scale, whose parallel projection drives magnetic-flutter transport across flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed vector potential is the fluctuating electromagnetic vector potential $\delta\mathbf{A}$ in gyrokinetic plasma turbulence, rendered dimensionless by dividing by a reference scale $B_\text{ref} \rho_\text{ref}$, where $B_\text{ref}$ is a reference magnetic-field strength and $\rho_\text{ref}$ is a reference ion gyroradius. In tokamak geometry the dominant electromagnetic degree of freedom is the component aligned with the equilibrium field $\hat{b}$, which enters the gyrocenter equations of motion through the parallel canonical momentum $p_\parallel - q_s \delta A_\parallel / c$, where $q_s$ is the species charge and $c$ is the speed of light (Gaussian units).

The normalized parallel projection $\tilde{A}_\parallel$ is determined self-consistently by the gyrokinetic parallel Ampère equation:

$$
-\nabla_\perp^2 \tilde{A}_\parallel = \frac{\beta_\text{ref}}{2} \sum_s q_s \int v_\parallel \tilde{f}_s \, d^3v
$$

where $\beta_\text{ref}$ is the reference plasma beta, $v_\parallel$ is the particle velocity component parallel to $\hat{b}$, and $\tilde{f}_s$ is the normalized perturbed distribution function.

The child [parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential) provides the scalar parallel projection and directly governs the magnetic-flutter energy transport quantified by normalized_energy_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential and the momentum transport described by momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential. This normalized vector is the dimensionless counterpart of the dimensional [perturbed_vector_potential](name:perturbed_vector_potential).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\delta A_\parallel$ is aligned with the equilibrium magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$, i.e., in the direction of increasing arc length along the field line.

NAMES.name: normalized_radial_gyrocenter_energy_flux_at_flux_surface_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Gyro-Bohm-normalized radial gyrocenter energy flux at a flux surface, with radial meaning the R component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, due to perturbed parallel vector-potential fluctuations.
NAMES.long:
Gyro-Bohm-normalized radial gyrocenter energy flux at a flux surface due to the perturbed parallel vector potential is the dimensionless contribution to gyrocenter energy transport from the magnetic-flutter velocity generated by $\delta A_\parallel$. The radial component is the $R$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the flux surface is a magnetic surface labeled by the flux coordinate $\psi$. It isolates this electromagnetic channel from electrostatic transport and from the contribution associated with the perturbed parallel magnetic field.

For a spectral representation, the aggregate species-summed contribution is defined by the flux-surface and time average of the energy-weighted gyrocenter perturbation contracted with the $\delta A_\parallel$ radial-flutter velocity:

$$
Q_{A_\parallel}^{\mathrm{norm}} =
\frac{1}{Q_\mathrm{gB}}
\left\langle
\sum_s \sum_{\mathbf{k}_\perp}
\operatorname{Re}\!\left[
\int d^3v\, \frac{m_s v^2}{2}\,
\delta f_{s,\mathbf{k}_\perp}^{*}\,
v_{R,s,\mathbf{k}_\perp}^{(A_\parallel)}
\right]
\right\rangle_{\psi,t}
$$

where $Q_{A_\parallel}^{\mathrm{norm}}$ is this normalized flux, $Q_\mathrm{gB}=n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}v_{\mathrm{th},\mathrm{ref}}(\rho_\mathrm{ref}/a_\mathrm{ref})^2$ is the positive gyro-Bohm reference energy flux, $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference particle density, $T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference thermal energy per particle, $v_{\mathrm{th},\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference thermal speed, $\rho_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference gyroradius, and $a_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference minor radius. The index $s$ labels kinetic species, $\mathbf{k}_\perp$ labels perpendicular-to-the-magnetic-field wave-number components, $\delta f_{s,\mathbf{k}_\perp}$ is the corresponding perturbed gyrocenter distribution, $v_{R,s,\mathbf{k}_\perp}^{(A_\parallel)}$ is the $R$ component of the magnetic-flutter velocity associated with $\delta A_\parallel$, $\operatorname{Re}$ selects the in-phase flux-carrying part of the bilinear product, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi,t}$ denotes averaging on the magnetic flux surface labeled by $\psi$ and over the turbulence time interval.

The wave-number sum denotes the aggregate flux at the flux surface rather than a mode-resolved contribution. The quantity includes only the $\delta A_\parallel$ part of the radial magnetic-flutter transport channel, excluding electrostatic $E\times B$ energy flux, magnetic-compression transport from $\delta B_\parallel$, and field-energy terms not carried by gyrocenter kinetic energy. If the gyrocenter variables are expressed in a rotating plasma reference frame, both factors in the bilinear product are interpreted in that same reference frame.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net gyrocenter energy flux component is in the $+\hat{R}$ direction, away from the machine symmetry axis, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: normalized_time
NAMES.short: Dimensionless gyrokinetic time coordinate formed by dividing physical elapsed time by a positive reference thermal transit time.
NAMES.long:
This quantity parameterizes gyrokinetic evolution using a thermal transit-time scale rather than physical time. It is a coordinate, not a frequency, growth rate, or elapsed-time measurement in physical units.

The normalized time is defined by

$$
t_* = \frac{t}{\tau_{\mathrm{th}}}
$$

where $t$ is physical elapsed time from the selected time origin and $\tau_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the positive reference thermal transit time for the specified gyrokinetic system.

The reference time fixes the normalization convention; changing it changes the numerical coordinate without changing the underlying evolution. This quantity is distinct from [normalized frequency of a gyrokinetic eigenmode](name:normalized_frequency_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode), which describes a spectral frequency normalized to a reference scale.

sources.parent_definition: Non-linear simulation

NAMES.name: normalized_total_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Normalized toroidal momentum flux from the perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence, restricted to the parallel velocity-space channel. Total denotes aggregation over species and fluctuation contributions within that channel.
NAMES.long:
Normalized toroidal momentum flux from the perturbed parallel electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence, restricted to the parallel velocity-space channel, is the gyro-Bohm-normalized flux-surface-normal transport of toroidal angular momentum associated with magnetic-flutter correlations from $\delta A_\parallel$. Toroidal angular momentum is referenced to motion in the direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The normalized total parallel-channel contribution is defined by the aggregate gyrokinetic flux moment normalized by the gyro-Bohm momentum-flux scale:

$$
\widehat{\Pi}^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\phi,\delta A_\parallel;\parallel}
=
\frac{1}{\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}}
\sum_s \sum_{\mathbf{k}}
\left\langle
\int m_s R v_\parallel b_\phi\,
v^{\mathrm{fl}}_{\chi,\delta A_\parallel}\,
\delta f_{s,\mathbf{k}}\,d^3v
\right\rangle
$$

where $s$ labels species, $\mathbf{k}$ labels fluctuation-wavevector contributions, $m_s$ is species mass, $v_\parallel$ is gyrocenter velocity parallel to the magnetic field, $b_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the magnetic-field unit vector, $v^{\mathrm{fl}}_{\chi,\delta A_\parallel}$ is the flux-surface-normal magnetic-flutter velocity produced by $\delta A_\parallel$ for magnetic-flux label $\chi$, $\delta f_{s,\mathbf{k}}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution contribution, and angle brackets denote the flux-surface and turbulence average. The gyro-Bohm scale is $\Pi_{\mathrm{gB}}=n_{\mathrm{ref}}T_{\mathrm{ref}}R_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}/a_{\mathrm{ref}})^2$, with $n_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference density, $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference temperature, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference major radius, $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference gyroradius, and $a_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the reference minor radius.

This quantity has the same parallel velocity-space projection as the [normalized parallel momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential](name:normalized_parallel_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential), while the word total denotes aggregation over species and fluctuation contributions within that projection. It excludes the [normalized perpendicular momentum flux due to the perturbed parallel vector potential](name:normalized_perpendicular_momentum_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential), whose velocity-space projection is perpendicular to the magnetic-field direction, and is not the algebraic sum of the parallel and perpendicular projections.
NAMES.sign: Positive when toroidal angular momentum for motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ is transported in the flux-surface-normal direction toward increasing magnetic-flux label in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: normalized_total_particle_perturbed_pressure_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode
NAMES.short: The normalized total perturbed particle pressure of a gyrokinetic eigenmode is the second velocity-space moment of the perturbed particle distribution, scaled by the equilibrium species pressure. It is the sum of the normalized parallel and perpendicular particle pressure perturbations under the same eigenmode amplitude and phase convention.
NAMES.long:
The normalized total perturbed particle pressure of a gyrokinetic eigenmode is the second velocity-space moment of the perturbed particle distribution, scaled by the equilibrium species pressure. It combines kinetic-pressure perturbations from velocity components parallel and perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$ and is a perturbation moment of a linear eigenmode, not an equilibrium thermodynamic pressure.

The defining particle moment and component decomposition are:

$$
\hat{p}_{\mathrm{part},s} = \frac{\delta p_{\parallel,\mathrm{part},s}+\delta p_{\perp,\mathrm{part},s}}{p_{0s}} = \frac{m_s\int v_\parallel^2\,\delta f_{\mathrm{part},s}\,d^3v + m_s\int \frac{v_\perp^2}{2}\,\delta f_{\mathrm{part},s}\,d^3v}{p_{0s}} = \hat{p}_{\parallel,\mathrm{part},s}+\hat{p}_{\perp,\mathrm{part},s}, \qquad p_{0s}=n_{0s}T_{0s}
$$

where $s$ labels the species, $\delta f_{\mathrm{part},s}$ is the perturbed particle distribution for that species, $m_s$ is the species particle mass in kilograms, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are the velocity components parallel and perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}_0$ in meters per second, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The two velocity integrals define $\delta p_{\parallel,\mathrm{part},s}$ and $\delta p_{\perp,\mathrm{part},s}$, the parallel and perpendicular particle pressure perturbations in pascals; $p_{0s}$ is the equilibrium species pressure in pascals, $n_{0s}$ is the equilibrium number density in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, and $T_{0s}$ is the equilibrium temperature expressed as energy per particle in joules. If $T_{0s}$ is represented in electronvolts, $p_{0s}=n_{0s}eT_{0s}$ with $e$ the elementary charge.

The total moment is exactly the sum of the component moments [parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure) and [perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure); it is not an additional closure variable. It is the particle-representation member of [normalized_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_perturbed_pressure). It differs from [normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) because that moment is formed from the perturbed gyrocenter distribution before the gyrocenter-to-particle mapping; normalized_gyroaveraged_pressure denotes the related gyroaveraged pressure response.

A linear eigenmode may be multiplied by an arbitrary complex constant, so comparisons of this moment require the same eigenmode normalization and phase convention as its component pressure moments and related perturbed eigenmode quantities.
NAMES.sign: Positive when, under the chosen common eigenmode phase convention, the real particle pressure perturbation moment increases the particle pressure relative to the equilibrium species pressure.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Normalized parallel pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed physical-particle distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, representing its parallel thermal-energy fluctuation relative to a reference pressure.
NAMES.long:
The parallel normalized particle perturbed pressure is a dimensionless complex eigenmode moment of the perturbed physical-particle distribution function. It represents the fluctuation of thermal energy associated with random particle motion parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field.

For species $s$, its defining velocity-space moment is

$$
\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} = \frac{m_s}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\parallel^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ is the velocity component parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The reference pressure is $p_\mathrm{ref}=n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}$, with $n_\mathrm{ref}$ the reference particle number density and $T_\mathrm{ref}$ the reference thermal temperature.

This quantity is the parallel component of the [normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure). Together with the [perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure), it describes pressure anisotropy and is distinct from the isotropic trace represented by [normalized perturbed pressure](name:normalized_perturbed_pressure).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the pressure perturbation corresponds to a local increase above the equilibrium background pressure.
