NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless parallel component of the perturbed current density, obtained as a parallel-velocity-weighted moment of the perturbed distribution function in gyrokinetic theory and normalized to a reference current scale.
NAMES.long:
The parallel normalized perturbed current density is the projection of the [normalized_perturbed_current_density](name:normalized_perturbed_current_density) vector along the equilibrium magnetic field direction. It characterizes how perturbations to the particle or gyrocenter distribution function $\delta f$ drive parallel current fluctuations relative to equilibrium, with normalization by a reference current density yielding a dimensionless measure of the parallel current response strength.

The general defining moment takes the form:

$$
\tilde{j}_\parallel = \frac{\sum_s q_s \int v_\parallel \, \delta f_s \, d^3v}{j_\text{ref}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $v_\parallel$ is the velocity component along the background magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed distribution function for species $s$, and $j_\text{ref}$ is a reference current density set by the gyrokinetic normalization. Finite-Larmor-radius corrections to this moment arise through Bessel-function weighting of the velocity-space integral; [parallel_normalized_perturbed_current_density_bessel_1](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_current_density_bessel_1) isolates the J1-weighted contribution that enters the electromagnetic response through the perturbed parallel vector potential.

This quantity enters the parallel component of Ampere's law in gyrokinetic field equations, coupling the plasma current response to electromagnetic field perturbations. It is evaluated from gyrocenter or particle distribution functions in linear eigenmode analyzes and nonlinear turbulence simulations.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed parallel current flows in the direction of the background magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_current_density_bessel_1
NAMES.short: Dimensionless finite-Larmor-radius contribution to the field-aligned perturbed current-density moment of a gyrocenter distribution, weighted by the first-order Bessel function.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the dimensionless finite-Larmor-radius contribution to the parallel perturbed current-density moment of a gyrocenter distribution. It is the Bessel-weighted component associated with the first-order gyroaveraging response and refines the full [parallel normalized perturbed current density](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_current_density).

A defining normalized moment is

$$
\mathcal{J}_{\parallel,\mathrm{FLR}}^{(1)} = \frac{1}{j_{\mathrm{ref}}} \sum_s q_s \int d^3v\, v_\parallel J_1(k_\perp\rho_s)\,\delta f_s
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$ in C, $v_\parallel$ is its velocity along the local magnetic field in m/s, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space measure, $J_1$ is the dimensionless first-order Bessel function, $k_\perp$ is the perpendicular wavenumber in m$^{-1}$, $\rho_s$ is the species gyroradius in m, and $j_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference current-density scale in A/m$^2$.

This component retains only the $J_1$-weighted finite-Larmor-radius contribution; it is not the complete parallel response or the unrestricted vector quantity [normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the charge-weighted moment is directed along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Signed dimensionless component of a magnetic-field perturbation along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction, identifying compressional fluctuations.
NAMES.long:
The parallel normalized perturbed magnetic field is the component of the magnetic-field perturbation aligned with the local equilibrium field, scaled by the equilibrium field magnitude. It describes compressional magnetic fluctuations rather than perturbations that only bend field lines.

$$
\delta \hat{B}_{\parallel} = \frac{\delta \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{b}_0}{B_0}
$$

where $\delta \mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed magnetic-field vector, $\mathbf{B}_0$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, $B_0 = |\mathbf{B}_0|$ is its magnitude, and $\mathbf{b}_0 = \mathbf{B}_0/B_0$ is the equilibrium field-line unit vector. This is the parallel projection of the [normalized perturbed magnetic field](name:normalized_perturbed_magnetic_field). For a complex mode representation, taking the modulus yields the phase-independent [parallel normalized perturbed magnetic field amplitude](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_magnetic_field_amplitude).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbation has a component in the direction of the local equilibrium magnetic field.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_magnetic_field_amplitude
NAMES.short: Phase-independent magnitude of a complex normalized parallel magnetic-field perturbation, representing the strength of compressional fluctuations.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the phase-independent magnitude of the magnetic-field perturbation aligned with the local equilibrium magnetic field. It represents compressional magnetic fluctuations and does not retain the sign or phase of the underlying perturbation.

$$
A_{\u005cparallel B} = \frac{\left|\widetilde{\u005cdelta\mathbf{B}} \u005ccdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}_0\right|}{B_0}
$$

where $A_{\parallel B}$ is the normalized amplitude, $\widetilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}$ is the complex perturbed magnetic-field coefficient, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_0$ is the unit vector along the equilibrium magnetic field, and $B_0$ is its magnitude. Unlike the signed [parallel normalized perturbed magnetic field](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_magnetic_field), this modulus is invariant under a change of perturbation phase and is non-negative. It is distinct from the amplitude of the parallel perturbed vector potential, which describes a different electromagnetic field quantity.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Dimensionless field-aligned component of the perturbed electromagnetic vector potential in gyrokinetic turbulence, retaining its signed or complex value rather than its modulus.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the parallel projection of the fluctuating electromagnetic vector potential, normalized consistently with the [normalized perturbed vector potential](name:normalized_perturbed_vector_potential). It represents the field-aligned electromagnetic fluctuation itself rather than its amplitude.

$$
a_\parallel = \frac{\delta\mathbf{A}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}}{B_{\mathrm{ref}}\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}} = \frac{\delta A_\parallel}{B_{\mathrm{ref}}\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{A}$ is the perturbed electromagnetic vector potential, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the equilibrium magnetic field, $\delta A_\parallel$ is its field-aligned projection, $B_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is a reference magnetic-field strength, and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is a reference length.

The value retains the signed real component or complex eigenfunction coefficient and is distinct from the modulus defined by [parallel normalized perturbed vector potential amplitude](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential_amplitude). Its value depends on the selected electromagnetic gage and, for a linear eigenmode, on the arbitrary overall eigenfunction phase.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential_amplitude
NAMES.short: Modulus of the complex normalized perturbed vector-potential component parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field for a gyrokinetic mode.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the non-negative amplitude of the normalized perturbed electromagnetic vector potential projected parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field. It describes the magnitude of the field-aligned electromagnetic fluctuation without retaining its phase or signed complex value.

For a specified gyrokinetic mode, the amplitude is defined by

$$
\mathcal{A}_{\parallel,\mathrm{amp}} = \left|\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}_\parallel\right|
$$

where $\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}_\parallel$ is the complex normalized perturbed vector-potential eigenfunction parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field, and $|\cdot|$ denotes its complex modulus.

This quantity is the modulus of [parallel normalized perturbed vector potential](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_vector_potential), so it excludes the phase information and signed or complex value retained by that parent quantity. It is distinct from [parallel normalized perturbed magnetic field amplitude](name:parallel_normalized_perturbed_magnetic_field_amplitude), which represents a magnetic-field fluctuation rather than a vector-potential fluctuation.

NAMES.name: parity_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode
NAMES.short: Dimensionless symmetry label of a gyrokinetic eigenmode's perturbed eigenfunction under reflection of poloidal angle about the outboard midplane.
NAMES.long:
Parity of a gyrokinetic eigenmode is the discrete symmetry class of its perturbed eigenfunction under reflection across the outboard-midplane poloidal coordinate. It distinguishes even and odd mode structure and does not describe the equilibrium field.

The defining relation is

$$
\widetilde{f}(\rho,-\theta,\phi)=\mathcal{P}\,\widetilde{f}(\rho,\theta,\phi), \qquad \mathcal{P}\in\{+1,-1\}
$$

where $\widetilde{f}$ is a perturbed eigenfunction component, $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ are flux coordinates, $\theta=0$ is the outboard midplane, and $\mathcal{P}$ is the parity label. The value $+1$ denotes even symmetry and $-1$ denotes odd symmetry. The more specific [perturbed parity of a gyrokinetic eigenmode](name:perturbed_parity_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode) is an instance of this shared eigenmode-symmetry definition.

NAMES.name: particle_charge
NAMES.short: Particle charge is the signed charge number assigned to a particle species, defining the direction and relative strength of that species' coupling to electric and magnetic fields.
NAMES.long:
Particle charge is the signed charge number assigned to a particle species, identifying the electric charge carried by one particle of that species for electromagnetic coupling. It determines the sign and relative strength with which the species responds to electric and magnetic fields.

For a resolved charge state, particle charge denotes the charge of that state. For a species represented as an aggregate over ionization states, it denotes the density-weighted mean over all charge states; it is not a charge-state population, number density, or electric current. A [normalized particle charge](name:normalized_particle_charge) is a particular normalized representation of this same signed charge concept, rather than a different physical property.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the particle carries electric charge with the same sign as a proton.

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_charge
NAMES.short: Dimensionless charge number of a particle species, obtained by dividing its physical charge by the positive reference charge used for normalization.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized form of [particle charge](name:particle_charge) for a particle species. It preserves the sign of the physical charge and expresses its magnitude relative to a common positive reference charge.

The normalized charge is defined by

$$
q_{\rm n} = \frac{q}{q_{\rm ref}}
$$

where $q$ is the species' physical electric charge and $q_{\rm ref}$ is the strictly positive reference charge, both expressed in the same charge units.

The result is dimensionless and is used as the charge-coupling coefficient in normalized electromagnetic and electrostatic equations. Its sign distinguishes positive and negative charge, while its magnitude gives the charge relative to the selected reference.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalised charge of a particle species in a local gyrokinetic simulation, expressed in units of the reference charge. Specifies the electromagnetic coupling strength of each species in the gyrokinetic equations.
sources.leaf_definition: Normalised charge
sources.parent_definition: Set of species (including electrons) used in the calculation and related quantities

NAMES.name: particle_energy
NAMES.short: Energy-like measure of particle motion in velocity space, combining parallel and perpendicular kinetic-energy contributions for distribution-based plasma quantities.
NAMES.long:
Particle energy denotes the kinetic-energy content or energy coordinate associated with a species' velocity-space distribution. It is based on both parallel and perpendicular motion and can characterize an ordering coordinate, a distribution moment, or a response of a perturbed distribution.

The underlying single-particle kinetic energy is

$$
E = \frac{1}{2}m\left(v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2\right)
$$

where $E$ is particle kinetic energy, $m$ is particle mass, and $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are the velocity components parallel and perpendicular to the local magnetic field. Distribution-based quantities use this energy or an equivalent velocity-space weighting; [fast_particle_energy](name:fast_particle_energy) represents a fast-population moment, while [perturbed_particle_energy](name:perturbed_particle_energy) represents the corresponding response of a perturbed distribution. An effective coordinate may additionally be scaled by a positive reference energy, as in [effective_particle_energy](name:effective_particle_energy). A moment of a perturbed distribution may be signed even though the underlying single-particle kinetic energy is nonnegative.

NAMES.name: particle_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Particle-flux contribution to turbulent cross-field transport associated with the perturbed vector-potential component parallel to the magnetic field. It fixes the transported quantity as particles and the mechanism as parallel-vector-potential fluctuations without fixing a projection or normalization.
NAMES.long:
Particle flux due to perturbed parallel vector potential is the mechanism-resolved contribution to turbulent particle transport arising from the component of the perturbed vector potential parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field, commonly denoted $\delta A_\parallel$. The transported quantity is particle number; the mechanism qualifier selects the perturbed-parallel-vector-potential part of the turbulent flux.

This family-level quantity does not by itself prescribe a transport projection, flux label, averaging operation, or scaling. A specialized quantity supplies those additional qualifiers; for example, [normalized particle flux due to perturbed parallel vector potential](name:normalized_particle_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential) is a scaled member of this same mechanism-resolved particle-flux family.

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential
NAMES.short: Dimensionless gyro-Bohm-normalized contribution to turbulent radial particle transport produced by fluctuations of the perturbed parallel vector potential.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the normalized magnetic-flutter contribution to turbulent radial particle transport caused by fluctuations of the perturbed parallel vector potential. It isolates this electromagnetic channel from other contributions to the total turbulent particle flux.

$$
\widehat{\Gamma}_{r,A_\parallel}=\frac{\Gamma_{r,A_\parallel}}{\Gamma_{\rm GB}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{r,A_\parallel}$ is the radial particle-flux contribution attributed to the perturbed parallel vector potential, and $\Gamma_{\rm GB}$ is the positive reference gyro-Bohm particle-flux scale. The normalized result is dimensionless and corresponds to the related unnormalized [particle-flux contribution](name:particle_flux_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).

It excludes particle transport produced by electrostatic fluctuations, collisional processes, or other electromagnetic perturbation channels unless they are included in the defined parent contribution.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the net particle transport is outward, toward increasing distance from the magnetic axis.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Dimensionless perpendicular gyrotropic pressure moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is the second velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function $\delta f_s$, integrated with the perpendicular kinetic-energy weight and normalized by a reference thermal pressure $p_{\mathrm{ref}} = n_{\mathrm{ref}} T_{\mathrm{ref}}$. It characterizes the perturbation to the gyrotropic pressure component in the plane orthogonal to the background magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$ for a given linear gyrokinetic eigenmode.

The defining velocity-space integral is:

$$
\delta \tilde{p}_{\perp} = \frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int \frac{m_s v_{\perp}^2}{2} \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass, $v_{\perp}$ is the gyrocenter speed perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}_0$, and $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function. The absence of the $J_0(k_{\perp} \rho_s)$ gyroaveraging factor distinguishes this moment from normalized_perpendicular_gyroaveraged_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure, where $k_{\perp}$ is the perpendicular wavenumber and $\rho_s$ is the species Larmor radius.

This moment is computed in local delta-f flux-tube gyrokinetic simulations as part of the linear eigenmode structure. It is the second (perpendicular) entry of the ordered component pair in [normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure), complementing parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure which carries the parallel component. Together these two moments fully characterize the gyrotropic pressure response of each kinetic species to the eigenmode perturbation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter distribution contributes a net increase in perpendicular thermal pressure relative to the local equilibrium value.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalised perpendicular pressure (p⊥) moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Represents the perpendicular thermal pressure perturbation associated with the eigenmode.
sources.leaf_definition: Normalised perpendicular temperature

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
NAMES.short: Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the dimensionless velocity-space moment of a species' perturbed distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, weighted by the perpendicular speed squared times the total speed squared and normalized to the unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment of the same species.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy is the perpendicular member of the particle perturbed-energy moment family for a species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its velocity-space weight is the perpendicular speed squared multiplied by the total speed squared, and the reference normalization is the corresponding unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment.

The quantity is defined as the ratio of the weighted perturbed moment to the unperturbed reference moment:

$$
M_{\perp E,s} = \frac{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\displaystyle\int \tfrac{1}{2} m_s v^2\, v^2\, f_{0,s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction, $v_\parallel$ is the particle speed parallel to the local magnetic-field direction, $v^2 = v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2$ is the total particle speed squared, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution of the eigenmode, $f_{0,s}$ is the unperturbed (equilibrium) particle distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The denominator is the unperturbed total-speed-squared energy moment shared by the parent [normalized particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) and its parallel counterpart, so the parallel and perpendicular members are directly comparable.

This scalar is the perpendicular entry of the [normalized particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) decomposition and is paired with the [parallel normalized particle perturbed energy] evaluated with the same perturbed distribution and normalization. It is distinct from the [perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure), whose weight is the perpendicular speed squared alone: the energy moment retains the additional total-speed-squared factor. Because a linear eigenmode carries an arbitrary complex amplitude, only comparisons made under the same eigenmode amplitude and phase convention are physically meaningful.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the velocity-space integral of $\tfrac{1}{2} m_s v_\perp^2 v^2\,\delta f_s$ is positive under the chosen eigenmode phase convention.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalised gyrokinetic moment of the perturbed particle distribution corresponding to the integral of 0.5·m·v⊥²·v² over velocity space. Related to the perpendicular energy-weighted pressure moment in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode.

sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalised) of the perturbed distribution function of particles

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Normalized perpendicular pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, representing its perpendicular thermal-energy fluctuation relative to a reference pressure.
NAMES.long:
The perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure is a dimensionless complex eigenmode moment of the perturbed particle distribution function. It represents the fluctuation of thermal energy associated with random particle motion perpendicular to the background magnetic field and is the perpendicular component of the [normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure).

For species $s$, it is defined by the perpendicular second velocity-space moment:

$$
\hat{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{m_s}{2p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\perp^2\,\delta f_s\,d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\perp$ is the speed perpendicular to the background magnetic field, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $p_\mathrm{ref}$ is a positive reference thermal pressure. The perpendicular and [parallel normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure) components together describe the gyrotropic pressure perturbation.

Unlike the [perpendicular normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure), this moment is formed from the physical particle distribution and includes finite-Larmor-radius effects associated with the particle-to-gyrocenter transformation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perpendicular pressure perturbation represents a local increase in perpendicular thermal energy relative to the equilibrium background.

sources.parent_definition: Moments (normalised) of the perturbed distribution function of particles

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure
NAMES.short: Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure is a dimensionless gyrotropic perpendicular pressure moment of a perturbed particle or gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to the species reference thermal pressure.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure is the dimensionless gyrotropic perpendicular pressure moment of a perturbed particle or gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to the species reference thermal pressure. It represents the part of the perturbed pressure tensor associated with kinetic energy perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic-field direction.

For species $s$, the normalized perpendicular moment is defined by

$$
\tilde{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{ref},s}} \int \varepsilon_{\perp,s}\,\delta f_s\,d\Lambda_s
$$

where $\tilde{p}_{\perp,s}$ is the perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure, $p_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ is the species reference thermal pressure, $\varepsilon_{\perp,s}$ is the particle or gyrocenter kinetic energy associated with motion perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed distribution-function amplitude, and $d\Lambda_s$ is the local velocity-space or gyrocenter velocity-space measure for that distribution.

This quantity is the perpendicular member of the gyrotropic pressure-moment pair; the companion member is [parallel normalized perturbed pressure]. When formed from the same distribution and normalization, the scalar trace pressure perturbation [normalized perturbed pressure](name:normalized_perturbed_pressure) is related by $\tilde{p}_s = (\tilde{p}_{\parallel,s} + 2\tilde{p}_{\perp,s})/3$. For complex linear eigenmodes this quantity is a complex amplitude whose overall phase follows the eigenmode normalization; relative phases, ratios, and magnitudes within the same normalization carry the invariant information.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perpendicular pressure perturbation is an enhancement of the equilibrium perpendicular thermal pressure.

NAMES.name: perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1
NAMES.short: Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the perpendicular pressure moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure and weighted by the first-order Bessel function J1.
NAMES.long:
Perpendicular normalized perturbed pressure Bessel-1 is the perpendicular kinetic-pressure moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, normalized to a reference thermal pressure and weighted by the first-order Bessel function. It is the perpendicular projection of the Bessel-1 normalized perturbed pressure moment, associated with particle kinetic energy perpendicular to the background magnetic field.

The normalized moment is defined by

$$
\hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1} = \frac{1}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \frac{m v_\perp^2}{2}\, J_1\!\left(k_\perp \rho(v_\perp)\right)\, \delta f_\mathrm{gc}(\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\hat{\delta p}_{\perp,J_1}$ is the normalized perpendicular Bessel-1 pressure perturbation, $p_\mathrm{ref}=n_\mathrm{ref}T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference thermal pressure, $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference density, $T_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference temperature expressed as particle energy, $m$ is the species mass, $v_\perp$ is the particle speed perpendicular to the background magnetic field, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel function, $k_\perp$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude, $\rho(v_\perp)$ is the velocity-dependent gyroradius, $\delta f_\mathrm{gc}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity is the perpendicular pressure-tensor projection of [normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1](name:normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1); the complementary field-aligned projection is parallel_normalized_perturbed_pressure_bessel_1. It differs from [perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_perturbed_pressure) by the first-order Bessel weighting and from [perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) by representing the Bessel-1 finite-Larmor-radius contribution rather than the unweighted gyrocenter moment.
NAMES.sign: Positive when, after the eigenmode phase has been fixed by the chosen reference perturbation, the real part of the defining Bessel-weighted perpendicular kinetic-pressure moment represents an excess over the equilibrium gyrocenter distribution.

NAMES.name: shearing_rate_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short: Shearing rate due to E×B drift is a signed measure of differential advection by the E×B flow across neighboring magnetic flux surfaces. It is formed from the flux-surface-normal variation of a selected E×B flow quantity scaled by a positive reference rate, without fixing the component or the reference normalization.
NAMES.long:
Shearing rate due to $E \times B$ drift is a signed scalar measure of how neighboring magnetic flux surfaces are differentially advected by the $E \times B$ flow. It characterizes the shear of that drift flow across flux surfaces, with the physical gradient scaled by a positive reference rate.

The scaled shearing rate is locally defined by

$$
\hat{\gamma}_E = \frac{1}{\Omega_\mathrm{ref}} \frac{\partial u_{E\times B}}{\partial \ell_n}
$$

where $\hat{\gamma}_E$ is the scaled shearing rate, $u_{E\times B}$ is the selected component or equivalent scalar flow speed of $\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}$, $\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}=\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}/B^2$, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field with magnitude $B$, $\ell_n$ is distance along the flux-surface-normal direction, positive toward increasing chosen flux-surface label, and $\Omega_\mathrm{ref}$ is a positive reference rate with the same dimensions as $\partial u_{E\times B}/\partial \ell_n$.

This quantity does not by itself specify the flow component, the flux-surface label, or the reference rate. More specific quantities may fix those choices, for example [normalized shearing rate due to $E \times B$ drift](name:normalized_shearing_rate_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). It is distinct from the $E \times B$ drift velocity because it is a gradient of that flow, and distinct from turbulence growth rates because it describes differential advection rather than temporal amplification.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $u_{E\times B}$ increases as $\ell_n$ increases toward increasing chosen flux-surface label.

NAMES.name: normalized_shearing_rate_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.short: Normalized shearing rate due to E×B drift is the flux-surface-radius derivative of the toroidal E×B drift velocity, normalized by the gyro-Bohm reference rate set by the reference sound speed over the reference minor radius.
NAMES.long:
Normalized shearing rate due to E×B drift is the dimensionless measure of how rapidly the toroidal component of the E×B drift velocity varies across neighboring flux surfaces, expressed relative to the gyro-Bohm reference rate. It is the gyro-Bohm-normalized counterpart of [shearing_rate_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:shearing_rate_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).

With a flux-surface minor-radius coordinate $r = a_\mathrm{ref}\,\rho$, it is defined as

$$
\hat{\gamma}_{E\times B} = \frac{a_\mathrm{ref}}{c_\mathrm{ref}}\,\frac{\partial u_{\phi,E\times B}}{\partial r} = \frac{\partial}{\partial \rho}\!\left(\frac{u_{\phi,E\times B}}{c_\mathrm{ref}}\right)
$$

where $u_{\phi,E\times B}$ is the toroidal component of the E×B drift velocity in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame in m s$^{-1}$, $c_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference sound speed in m s$^{-1}$, $a_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference minor radius in m, and $\rho$ is the normalized flux-surface minor-radius coordinate increasing from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

The shear is taken of the toroidal drift velocity $u_{\phi,E\times B}$ itself, not of the associated angular rotation frequency. The angular quantity [toroidal_rotation_frequency_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:toroidal_rotation_frequency_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the same drift divided by the local major radius $R$; because $R$ varies across a flux surface, the radial derivative of that angular frequency differs from this velocity-based shear. The derivative is with respect to the flux-surface coordinate $\rho$, not along the major-radius coordinate $R$; a uniform toroidal E×B drift gives zero shearing rate, since only variation between neighboring flux surfaces contributes.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $u_{\phi,E\times B}$, taken positive in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, increases with increasing normalized flux-surface minor-radius coordinate $\rho$.

NAMES.name: temperature_at_outboard_midplane
NAMES.short: Temperature at the outboard midplane is the scalar kinetic temperature of a specified plasma particle population at the low-field-side equatorial intersection of a chosen magnetic flux surface. It represents the local random kinetic energy of that population, independent of species-specific specialization.
NAMES.long:
Temperature at the outboard midplane is the scalar kinetic temperature of a specified plasma particle population evaluated where a chosen magnetic flux surface intersects the low-field-side equatorial plane. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height, this is the midplane intersection on the larger-$R$ side of the magnetic axis.

The energy-equivalent scalar temperature for population $a$ is defined from the local pressure tensor by:

$$
T_a = \frac{\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_a}{3 n_a}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_a$ is the pressure tensor, $n_a$ is the number density, and both are evaluated locally at the outboard midplane. For an isotropic velocity distribution this is equivalently two thirds of the mean random kinetic energy per particle.

This parent quantity is population-generic; species-specific instances, such as [electron temperature at outboard midplane](name:electron_temperature_at_outboard_midplane), use the same outboard-midplane locus and scalar kinetic-temperature definition. It is distinct from a flux-surface average, a volume average, or a temperature evaluated at any other midplane or radial location.

NAMES.name: electron_temperature_at_outboard_midplane
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Kinetic temperature of the bulk electron population at the low-field-side intersection of a chosen magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane.
NAMES.long:
The electron temperature at the outboard midplane is the local energy-equivalent kinetic temperature of the bulk electron population at the low-field-side equatorial intersection of a chosen magnetic flux surface. It is the electron-specific component of [temperature at outboard midplane](name:temperature_at_outboard_midplane).

For an isotropic electron velocity distribution, the energy-equivalent temperature is defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}} \right\rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature, and $\left\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}} \right\rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron, with both expressed on the same energy scale.

This quantity is local to the outboard-midplane intersection and is not a field-line average, flux-surface average, or value at the plasma boundary.

sources.enhanced_context: Electron temperature (Te) at the outboard equatorial midplane of the local flux surface, used as the normalizing reference temperature for a local gyrokinetic simulation. Sets the energy scale for the normalised gyrokinetic description.
sources.leaf_definition: Electron temperature at outboard equatorial midplane of the flux surface (angle_pol = 0)

NAMES.name: gyrocenter_current_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Gyrocenter current density is the vector flux density of conventional electric charge represented by gyrocenter motion, equal to electric current per unit area normal to the flow.
NAMES.long:
Gyrocenter current density $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{gc}}$ is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux associated with gyrocenter motion. It represents signed charge transport contributed by gyrocenter dynamics to the [current density](name:current_density) quantity.

The charge-weighted first velocity moment of the gyrocenter distributions is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{R},t) = \sum_s q_s \int \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}} f_{\mathrm{gc},s}(\mathbf{R},\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}},t)\,d^3v_{\mathrm{gc}}
$$

where $\mathbf{R}$ is gyrocenter position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes charged species, $q_s$ is species charge, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}}$ is gyrocenter velocity, and $f_{\mathrm{gc},s}$ is the gyrocenter distribution function.

This parent quantity does not select an equilibrium or perturbed contribution; [perturbed gyrocenter current density](name:perturbed_gyrocenter_current_density) is the corresponding fluctuation. It is distinct from particle-number flux and from a scalar electric current obtained by integrating a current-density component through a specified surface.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the stated component or scalar projection of $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{gc}}$ is aligned with the positive direction of its defining basis vector or unit vector.

NAMES.name: perturbed_gyrocenter_current_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Perturbed gyrocenter current density is the charge-transport fluctuation associated with gyrocenter motion, obtained from the charge-weighted first velocity moment of perturbed gyrocenter distributions.
NAMES.long:
The perturbed gyrocenter current density is the fluctuating charge transport carried by gyrocenters in gyrokinetic theory. It is the perturbation of [gyrocenter current density](name:gyrocenter_current_density), distinct from a particle-space current perturbation such as [perturbed particle current density](name:perturbed_particle_current_density).

The underlying charge-weighted first-moment relation is

$$
\delta \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{gy}} = \sum_s q_s \int \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gy}}\,\delta f_{\mathrm{gy},s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ indexes species, $q_s$ is the signed species charge, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gy}}$ is gyrocenter velocity, $\delta f_{\mathrm{gy},s}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

A reference current-density scale may be applied to this moment to form a dimensionless representation, as in [normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density). The quantity is not restricted to a particular directional projection and excludes the instantaneous gyromotion contribution.

NAMES.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Dimensionless vector of the normalized gyrocenter current-density perturbation, equal to the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function divided by a reference current-density scale.
NAMES.long:
The normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density is the dimensionless vector form of the gyrocenter current-density perturbation in gyrokinetic theory, obtained by normalizing [perturbed_gyrocenter_current_density](name:perturbed_gyrocenter_current_density) to a reference current-density scale $J_\mathrm{ref}$.

$$
\tilde{\mathbf{J}} = \frac{1}{J_\mathrm{ref}} \sum_s q_s \int \mathbf{v}\, \delta f_s\, d^3v
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, and the integral is over velocity space. For a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode the result is generally complex, carrying both amplitude and phase. The vector decomposes along the background magnetic-field direction; the field-aligned projection is documented in [parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density). This quantity is structurally analogous to [normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density) (zeroth moment) and [normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) (second moment), differing in the velocity weight and charge weighting.

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Dimensionless field-aligned component of the charge-weighted first velocity moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution, normalized to a reference current-density scale.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the parallel component of the normalized gyrocenter current-density perturbation. It represents the charge-weighted first moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution along the local magnetic-field direction and is the field-aligned component of [normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).

$$
J_{parallel,g}^{(s)} = \frac{q_s}{J_{\rm ref}} \int v_\parallel\,\delta g_s\,d^3v
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $v_\parallel$ is its velocity along the local magnetic field, $\delta g_s$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $J_{\rm ref}$ is the reference current-density scale. The underlying unnormalized moment is the corresponding [perturbed gyrocenter current density](name:perturbed_gyrocenter_current_density). For a linear eigenmode, the quantity may be complex, with its phase defined by the eigenmode convention.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter current density points along the local magnetic field.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_electrostatic_potential
NAMES.short: Dimensionless complex eigenfunction for the normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation of a gyrokinetic mode.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed electrostatic potential is the dimensionless complex eigenfunction describing the scalar electric-potential part of a first-order gyrokinetic electromagnetic perturbation. Unlike the unnormalized [perturbed electrostatic potential](name:perturbed_electrostatic_potential), it is expressed relative to a reference potential scale and excludes the inductive vector-potential contribution.

$$
\widehat{\phi} = \frac{\widetilde{\phi}}{\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\widehat{\phi}$ is the normalized eigenfunction, $\widetilde{\phi}$ is the complex perturbed electrostatic potential in volts, and $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference potential in volts. The normalization convention is part of the eigenmode definition. The representative child [normalized perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude](name:normalized_perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude) is the modulus $|\widehat{\phi}|$ and therefore omits the perturbation phase.

NAMES.name: normalized_perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude
NAMES.short: Normalized perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the modulus of the complex normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation eigenfunction for a gyrokinetic mode. It retains the phase-independent amplitude while discarding the arbitrary complex phase.
NAMES.long:
Normalized perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the modulus of the complex normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation eigenfunction for a gyrokinetic mode. It represents the phase-independent strength of the electrostatic potential component of the mode and excludes the arbitrary complex phase of the eigenfunction.

For a complex [normalized perturbed electrostatic potential](name:normalized_perturbed_electrostatic_potential) eigenfunction $\delta\hat{\phi}$, the amplitude $A_{\phi_N}$ is defined by its complex modulus:

$$
A_{\phi_N} = |\delta\hat{\phi}| = \sqrt{\left(\operatorname{Re}\delta\hat{\phi}\right)^2 + \left(\operatorname{Im}\delta\hat{\phi}\right)^2}
$$

where $\operatorname{Re}\delta\hat{\phi}$ and $\operatorname{Im}\delta\hat{\phi}$ are the real and imaginary parts of the same normalized eigenfunction, and $A_{\phi_N}$ is the corresponding dimensionless amplitude.

This quantity is not the complex eigenfunction itself and contains no phase information. Its value is non-negative and depends on the normalization chosen for $\delta\hat{\phi}$, so it denotes relative mode structure within that normalization rather than an independently fixed absolute scale.

NAMES.name: normalized_wave_vector
NAMES.short: Dimensionless gyrokinetic wave vector formed by multiplying each component of the local fluctuation wave vector by a reference gyroradius, characterizing fluctuation scales relative to the ion Larmor radius.
NAMES.long:
The normalized wave vector is the dimensionless counterpart of the local fluctuation wave vector $\mathbf{k}$ in gyrokinetic theory. Each component is obtained by multiplying the corresponding physical wave-vector component by a reference gyroradius $\rho_\mathrm{ref}$, the thermal gyroradius of a reference ion species:

$$
\hat{\mathbf{k}} = \rho_\mathrm{ref}\,\mathbf{k}
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the wave vector of a fluctuation. A component of order unity indicates structure on gyroradius scales in that direction. In gyrokinetic turbulence the fluctuation spectrum is strongly anisotropic: perpendicular components (across magnetic-field lines) are of order unity, whereas the [parallel normalized wave vector](name:parallel_normalized_wave_vector) along the equilibrium field is much smaller, consistent with the gyrokinetic ordering $k_\parallel \rho_\mathrm{ref} \ll k_\perp \rho_\mathrm{ref}$. This quantity generalizes over all projections; for the specific field-aligned projection see the [parallel normalized wave vector](name:parallel_normalized_wave_vector).

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_wave_vector
NAMES.short: Dimensionless field-aligned wave-number component obtained by scaling the local parallel wave number by a positive reference gyroradius.
NAMES.long:
The parallel normalized wave-vector component is the projection of a local fluctuation wave vector onto the magnetic-field direction, expressed relative to a reference gyroradius. It describes phase variation along field lines and is the field-aligned component of the [normalized wave vector](name:normalized_wave_vector).

It is defined by

$$
k_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{norm}} = \rho_{\mathrm{ref}} k_{\parallel} = \rho_{\mathrm{ref}}\,\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $k_{\parallel}$ is the parallel wave number in inverse meters, $\mathbf{k}$ is the local wave vector in inverse meters, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local magnetic-field unit vector, and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is a positive reference gyroradius in meters. The quantity is dimensionless; it excludes perpendicular wave-vector projections, which describe variation across the magnetic field.

NAMES.name: particle_current_density
NAMES.short: Particle current density is the dimensionless scalar projection of the flux density of conventional electric charge carried by particle motion, obtained from a charge-weighted first velocity moment of particle distribution functions and normalized by a positive reference scale.
NAMES.long:
Particle current density $\tilde{J}_{\mathrm{part},\hat{\mathbf{e}}}$ is the dimensionless scalar projection of the particle contribution to [current density](name:current_density). It represents conventional charge transport carried by charged particles along a defining positive unit direction $\hat{\mathbf{e}}$, rather than the full current-density vector.

For a represented set of charged species, the normalized scalar particle current density is defined by the projected charge-weighted first velocity moment of the particle distribution functions:

$$
\tilde{J}_{\mathrm{part},\hat{\mathbf{e}}}(\mathbf{x},t;\mathcal{S}) = \frac{1}{J_{\mathrm{ref}}} \sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} q_s \int (\hat{\mathbf{e}}\cdot\mathbf{v})\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $\mathcal{S}$ is the represented species set, $s$ indexes charged species, $q_s$ is species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the particle velocity-space distribution function, and $J_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference current-density scale used for the dimensionless normalization. For a species-resolved quantity, $\mathcal{S}$ contains that species; for a summed particle contribution, it contains all included charged species.

This quantity excludes displacement-current density and is a scalar component or projection, not the vector [current density](name:current_density) itself. A [perturbed particle current density](name:perturbed_particle_current_density) applies the same particle-moment definition to the perturbed distribution or perturbed particle response. It is distinct from [gyrocenter current density](name:gyrocenter_current_density), because transformations between particle and gyrocenter variables can introduce finite-gyroradius, magnetization, or polarization contributions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the charge-weighted particle flux projects along the positive direction of the defining unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}$.

NAMES.name: perturbed_particle_current_density
NAMES.short: Perturbed current density computed as a velocity-space moment of the species-resolved perturbed particle distribution function, including polarization drift contributions absent from the gyrocenter-frame analog.
NAMES.long:
The particle perturbed current density is the fluctuation component of the electric current density for a given plasma species, obtained by integrating the perturbed particle distribution function $\delta f_s$ over velocity space weighted by charge and velocity:

$$
\delta \mathbf{J}_s = q_s \int \mathbf{v} \, \delta f_s(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v}, t) \, d^3v
$$

where $q_s$ is the species charge and the integral runs over all of velocity space.

In gyrokinetic theory, this particle-frame current density differs fundamentally from the gyrocenter-frame current density because the coordinate transformation between guiding-center and particle frames introduces polarization drift contributions. These contributions become significant at finite perpendicular wavenumber $k_\perp \rho_s \gtrsim 1$ (where $\rho_s$ is the species thermal Larmor radius) and are essential for satisfying the quasi-neutrality constraint and recovering the correct electromagnetic plasma response. The gyrocenter current density systematically underestimates the true current unless these polarization terms are restored.

This quantity is related to [particle_current_density](name:particle_current_density) through the linearized decomposition $\mathbf{J}_s = \mathbf{J}_{s,0} + \delta \mathbf{J}_s$, where $\mathbf{J}_{s,0}$ is the equilibrium species current. The [normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density) provides the dimensionless form used as standard output in gyrokinetic eigenmode analyzes, while [parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density) gives the projection along the magnetic field direction.

NAMES.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless vector of the species-resolved fluctuating particle current-density moment, formed from the perturbed distribution and normalized to a positive reference current-density scale.
NAMES.long:
The normalized perturbed particle current density is the dimensionless, species-resolved fluctuation obtained from the charge-weighted first velocity-space moment of the perturbed particle distribution. It represents the particle-frame electric-current perturbation described by the [perturbed particle current density](name:perturbed_particle_current_density), distinct from the corresponding gyrocenter moment.

For species $s$, the normalized quantity is defined by

$$
\widehat{\delta \mathbf{J}}_s = \frac{q_s \int \mathbf{v}\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{J_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $J_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is a positive reference current-density scale.

The vector retains the full particle-frame current-density moment; a resolved member such as [parallel normalized particle perturbed current density](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density) is one directional component. Particle-frame contributions, including polarization-drift effects when present, are not replaced by the gyrocenter approximation represented by [normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).

NAMES.name: parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_current_density
NAMES.short: Normalized parallel current density moment of the perturbed particle distribution function for a gyrokinetic eigenmode, capturing the species-resolved parallel current in the particle frame including polarization drift contributions absent from the gyrocenter-frame analog.
NAMES.long:
The normalized parallel current density moment of the perturbed particle distribution function characterizes the net parallel current carried by a plasma species in response to a gyrokinetic eigenmode perturbation, evaluated in the particle frame. Unlike the corresponding gyrocenter moment, it incorporates the polarization drift correction that converts between the guiding-center and full-particle representations of the perturbed distribution.

The moment is the first parallel velocity moment of the perturbed distribution, normalized to a gyro-Bohm reference current density:

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{norm}} = q_s \int v_\parallel \, \delta f_s \, d^3v \Big/ j_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the species charge, $v_\parallel = \mathbf{v} \cdot \hat{b}$ is the particle velocity component along the unit vector $\hat{b}$ parallel to the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution function, and $j_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the gyro-Bohm reference current density. The difference between this moment and [parallel normalized gyrocenter current density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density) arises precisely from the polarization correction relating particle and gyrocenter phase-space coordinates.

This quantity is computed from linear gyrokinetic eigenmode solutions at a specified perpendicular wavevector $\mathbf{k}_\perp$ and enters the parallel Ampere equation, governing electromagnetic mode structure relevant to microtearing modes and kinetic Alfvén waves. It belongs to the same particle-frame moment hierarchy as [parallel normalized particle perturbed pressure](name:parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure) and [parallel normalized particle perturbed heat flux].
NAMES.sign: Positive when the parallel current flows in the direction of the equilibrium magnetic field $\hat{b}$ (i.e., parallel to $\mathbf{B}_0$).

NAMES.name: perturbed_gyrocenter_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Dimensionless zeroth velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function for a plasma species, giving the gyrocenter density response to a fluctuation before finite-Larmor-radius averaging.
NAMES.long:
The gyrocenter perturbed density is the unweighted (zeroth) velocity-space integral of the deviation $\delta f_g(\mathbf{R}, v_\parallel, \mu)$ of the gyrocenter distribution function from its equilibrium background, normalized to a positive reference number density $n_{\rm ref}$.

$$
\delta \tilde{n}_g = \frac{1}{n_{\rm ref}} \int \delta f_g \, d^3v
$$

where the integral is over the full gyrocenter velocity space, $v_\parallel$ is the velocity parallel to the background magnetic field, and $\mu$ is the magnetic moment. The quantity is evaluated at the gyrocenter position $\mathbf{R}$ and does not incorporate the finite-Larmor-radius corrections that arise when transforming back to particle coordinates; it therefore differs from the particle density perturbation by gyroaveraging terms of order $(k_\perp \rho)^2$, where $k_\perp$ is the perpendicular wavenumber and $\rho$ is the thermal Larmor radius. It represents the perturbation to the background [gyrocenter_density](name:gyrocenter_density). The concrete normalized instance resolved for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode is [normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density).

NAMES.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density
NAMES.subject: gyrocenter
NAMES.short: Normalized gyrocenter perturbed density is the species-resolved zeroth velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution divided by a positive reference density. It is the before-finite-Larmor-radius gyrocenter-density fluctuation response, distinct from a gyroaveraged particle-density perturbation.
NAMES.long:
Normalized gyrocenter perturbed density is the species-resolved zeroth velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution divided by a positive reference density. It is the before-finite-Larmor-radius [gyrocenter density](name:gyrocenter_density) fluctuation response; the normalization removes the scale of the reference density while preserving perturbation amplitude and phase.

For magnetic moment $\mu = m_s v_\perp^2/(2B)$, the normalized moment is defined by:

$$
\widehat{n}_{gc,s} = \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{ref},s}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \int_{0}^{\infty} \delta f_{gc,s}(v_\parallel,\mu)\,\frac{2\pi B}{m_s}\,d\mu\,dv_\parallel
$$

where $\widehat{n}_{gc,s}$ is the normalized gyrocenter perturbed density for species $s$, $n_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ is the positive reference number density for that species, $\delta f_{gc,s}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution with respect to ordinary velocity-space volume, $B$ is the local magnetic-field magnitude, $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ is velocity parallel to the magnetic field, $v_\perp$ is speed perpendicular to the magnetic field, and $\mu$ is magnetic moment. The factor $2\pi B/m_s$ is the gyroangle-integrated velocity-space Jacobian for this definition of $\mu$.

For a species represented by multiple charge states, the perturbed gyrocenter-density numerator and the reference density are charge-state-summed before the ratio is formed. This quantity excludes any Bessel-function or finite-Larmor-radius weighting inside the velocity-space integral; that weighted moment is the [normalized gyrocenter gyroaveraged density]. The dimensional numerator of the ratio is the unnormalized gyrocenter-density perturbation; the related [perturbed gyrocenter density](name:perturbed_gyrocenter_density) denotes a dimensionless gyrocenter-density perturbation in the same family. The [normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure) is the corresponding perturbed pressure moment. For complex perturbation amplitudes, the integral is taken over the complex amplitude; the arbitrary overall mode phase is external to the definition.
NAMES.sign: Positive when, for a real perturbation amplitude, the velocity-space integral of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution gives an excess gyrocenter density relative to the positive reference density.

sources.enhanced_context: Normalised density moment (δn) of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Captures the gyrocenter density response associated with microinstabilities such as ITG, ETG, or TEM modes.

NAMES.name: radial_derivative_of_elongation_of_flux_surface
NAMES.short: Radial rate of change of the flux surface elongation kappa with respect to normalized minor radius, measuring how rapidly the poloidal cross-section aspect ratio varies across nested flux surfaces.
NAMES.long:
The radial derivative of flux surface elongation quantifies how the vertical-to-horizontal shape of nested toroidal magnetic surfaces changes as a function of radial position. The flux surface elongation $\kappa$ equals the ratio of the vertical to horizontal semi-axis of the poloidal cross-section, so its radial derivative captures the rate at which flux surfaces become more (or less) vertically elongated moving outward from the magnetic axis.

The quantity is defined as:

$$
\frac{d\kappa}{d\hat{r}}
$$

where $\kappa$ is the [elongation of the flux surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface) and $\hat{r}$ is the normalized minor radius running from 0 at the magnetic axis to 1 at the plasma boundary. Both $\kappa$ and $\hat{r}$ are dimensionless, so the derivative is also dimensionless.

This derivative is a required geometric input to local gyrokinetic flux-tube simulations, entering the metric coefficients that govern field-line curvature and grad-$B$ drift terms within the flux-tube domain. It belongs to the broader family of radial flux surface shape coefficient derivatives that also includes the [radial derivative of flux surface shape coefficient](name:radial_derivative_of_elongation_of_flux_surface). In plasmas with significant edge shaping, this quantity grows in magnitude toward the separatrix, while remaining near zero for nearly circular flux surfaces where $\kappa \approx 1$ throughout the minor radius.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the elongation $\kappa$ increases with increasing normalized minor radius $\hat{r}$, corresponding to flux surfaces that become more vertically elongated toward the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: reference_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Magnetic field at a specified reference major radius, generalizing the equilibrium field vector whose resolved components provide common reference values for turbulence quantities.
NAMES.long:
The reference magnetic field designates the equilibrium magnetic-field vector evaluated at a prescribed reference major radius. It generalizes the resolved components of that vector, including the [toroidal reference magnetic field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field), and is a reference specialization of the [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field).

The reference evaluation is represented by

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ref}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}(R_{\mathrm{ref}})
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference magnetic-field vector, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equilibrium magnetic-field vector, and $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the prescribed reference major radius measured in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Perturbation-only fields and fields defined exclusively by external coils are outside this equilibrium reference quantity.
NAMES.sign: Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ref}}$ points along its corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: toroidal_reference_magnetic_field
NAMES.short: Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at the reference point whose major radius is the reference major radius, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Toroidal reference magnetic field is the signed toroidal component of the equilibrium magnetic field at a specified reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The reference point has major radius equal to the [reference major radius](name:reference_major_radius).

The defining projection is:

$$
B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \cdot \hat{\phi}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}})
$$

where $B_{\phi,\mathrm{ref}}$ is the toroidal reference magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ref}}=(R_{\mathrm{ref}},\phi_{\mathrm{ref}},Z_{\mathrm{ref}})$ is the full reference point in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference major radius, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing $\phi$. For an axisymmetric equilibrium, the value is independent of $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$.

This quantity is the reference-location specialization of [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field). It is distinct from [toroidal magnetic field at magnetic axis](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_magnetic_axis), from the magnetic-field magnitude, and from [toroidal vacuum magnetic field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $B_\phi$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

NAMES.name: flux_surface_averaged_effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary
NAMES.short: Flux-surface average of the ion-mixture effective charge over the entire plasma-boundary surface, distinct from the local boundary value.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the ion-mixture effective charge over the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed flux surface. It summarizes the charge composition across the complete boundary surface rather than at a single location.

$$
\left\langle Z_{\mathrm{eff}} \right\rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi_b} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}\,d\ell/B_p}{\oint_{\psi_b} d\ell/B_p}, \qquad Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{n_e}
$$

Here $\psi_b$ labels the plasma-boundary flux surface, $d\ell$ is poloidal arc length, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, $n_i$ and $Z_i$ are the number density and charge number of ion population $i$, and $n_e$ is the electron number density. The linked [effective charge at the plasma boundary](name:effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary) denotes the corresponding local boundary quantity; this entry denotes its flux-surface average.

NAMES.name: ratio_of_line_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_line_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
NAMES.short: Line-averaged hydrogen density divided by line-averaged total hydrogenic density, giving the line-averaged protium fraction among hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions along the same line.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged hydrogen density divided by line-averaged total hydrogenic density is the isotope fraction of the line-averaged hydrogenic ion density contributed by hydrogen (protium). It is formed from hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion number densities averaged along the same line.

The fraction $f_H$ is defined from path-length averages along line $C$:

$$
f_H = \frac{\overline{n}_H}{\overline{n}_H + \overline{n}_D + \overline{n}_T} = \frac{\frac{1}{L_C}\int_C n_H(l)\,dl}{\frac{1}{L_C}\int_C \left[n_H(l)+n_D(l)+n_T(l)\right] \, dl}
$$

where $L_C$ is the path length of $C$, $l$ is distance along $C$, $n_H$, $n_D$, and $n_T$ are the local hydrogen (protium), deuterium, and tritium ion number densities, and the overbar denotes the corresponding line-averaged density along the same line.

The numerator is the [line-averaged hydrogen density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density), and the denominator is the sum of the line-averaged hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion densities along the same line. Hydrogenic density includes only hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ions, with each isotope density summed over all ion charge states; neutral atoms, molecules, electrons, and non-hydrogenic ions are excluded. For non-negative isotope densities and a nonzero denominator, $0 \le f_H \le 1$; this line-averaged isotope fraction is distinct from the corresponding [volume-averaged isotope fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density).

NAMES.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
NAMES.short: Dimensionless hydrogen-isotope fraction equal to the volume-averaged protium-ion density divided by the volume-averaged density of all hydrogenic ions.
NAMES.long:
This quantity is the fraction of the hydrogenic ion population attributable to protium, evaluated from volume-averaged densities over the same plasma volume. The numerator is the [volume-averaged hydrogen density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator includes the corresponding hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion populations.

$$
f_H = \frac{\overline{n}_H}{\overline{n}_H + \overline{n}_D + \overline{n}_T}
$$

Here $f_H$ is the hydrogen-isotope fraction; $\overline{n}_H$, $\overline{n}_D$, and $\overline{n}_T$ are the volume-averaged densities of protium, deuterium, and tritium ions, respectively. The quantity is a ratio of separately volume-averaged densities, not a local isotope fraction or a fraction restricted to a single charge state.
